senses.en: to accept rules, a law, an agreement, a decision, etc. and obey them/it
senses.zh: 遵守， 遵循( 规章制度等) :

ex.en: Members must abide by the rules of the club.
ex.zh: 会员必须遵守俱乐部的规定。

senses.en: to have a lot of sth; to contain a lot of sth

ex.en: The rivers there abound in/with fish.
ex.zh: 那里的江河盛产鱼。

senses.en: to agree to or allow sth that sb has asked for, often after you have opposed it for a while

ex.en: The government acceded to public pressure to review the tax.
ex.zh: 政府在公众的压力下同意检讨税项。

senses.en: to know where sb/sth is or what has happened to them, especially after an accident or a natural disaster
senses.zh: (尤指在事故或自然灾害之后)了解，查明:

ex.en: All the people who were working in the building have now been accounted for.
ex.zh: 所有当时在大楼中工作的人现在都有了下落。

ex.en: There are three files that I can’t account for.
ex.zh: 有三份文件我找不到。

senses.en: to explain how or why sth happened; to be the explanation for sth
senses.zh: 解释；说明； 是…的说明:

ex.en: How do you account for the fact that the box has disappeared?
ex.zh: 箱子不见了你如何解释？

ex.en: Poor hygiene may have accounted for the increase in cases of the disease.
ex.zh: 宪生状况差可能是这种病例增多的原因。

senses.en: to be a particular part of sth; to be a particular amount

ex.en: Car crime accounted for 28% of all reported offences.
ex.zh: 汽车犯罪占所有举报的罪行的28%。

ex.en: Wages account for less than half of the budget.
ex.zh: 工资占预算开支不到一半。

senses.en: to keep a record of how the money in your care will be spent or has been spent
senses.zh: 说明钱财的使用； 报账:

ex.en: Every penny of the funds is accounted for.
ex.zh: 基金中每一分钱的使用都报清楚。

senses.en: to consider particular facts or circumstances when you are making a decision about sth, especially when you are calculating the cost of sth
senses.zh: (尤指计算成本等时)考虑到，顾及(细节或环境):

ex.en: The cost of the film and the processing were all accounted for in the calculation of the cost of the service.
ex.zh: 胶片和冲洗的费用均计算在服务成本中。

senses.en: to make sb/yourself familiar with sth; to become used to sth

ex.en: It shouldn’t take long to accustom your students to working in groups.
ex.zh: 你的学生应该很快就会习惯分组学习的。

ex.en: It took a while for her eyes to accustom themselves to the dark.
ex.zh: 她的眼睛过了一会儿才适应了黑暗。

senses.en: to have a strong desire for sb/sth or to do sth

ex.en: I was aching for home.
ex.zh: 我巴不得回家。

senses.en: to make sb/yourself familiar with or aware of sth
senses.zh: (使自己或他人)熟悉某事物，了解某事物:

ex.en: He decided to take his son along and acquaint him with the business.
ex.zh: 他决定带上儿子，让他了解一下生意。

senses.en: to perform a particular role or function
senses.zh: 充当某角色；担任某工作；起…作用:

ex.en: Will you act as interpreter for us?
ex.zh: 你给我们当翻译好吗？

ex.en: Large fines act as a deterrent to motorists.
ex.zh: 高额罚款是对开车的人的制约。

senses.en: if sb acts for you or acts on behalf of you, they deal with your affairs for you, for example by representing you in a court of law,or by doing your duty when you are not able to
senses.zh: 代表某人(办理事情、出庭、担任职务等):

ex.en: Do you have a solicitor acting for you?
ex.zh: 你有代理律师吗？

ex.en: The Prince was acting on behalf of the Queen.
ex.zh: 当时王子代表女王作出行动。

senses.en: to do sth as a result of advice, information, instructions,etc. that you have received
senses.zh: 根据(建议、信息、指示等)行事:

ex.en: The police were acting on information from a member of the public.
ex.zh: 警察根据一个老百姓的报告采取行动。

ex.en: I was just acting on instructions.
ex.zh: 我只不过是奉命行事。

senses.en: to have an effect on sth
senses.zh: 对某事物产生作用(或影响):

ex.en: The drug acts on the central nervous system.
ex.zh: 这药对中枢神经系统产生影响。

senses.en: to perform a story or events that have happened or might happen, as if you are performing a play
senses.zh: 将故事(或往事、可能发生的事)表演出来:

ex.en: The teacher read a story and the children acted it out.
ex.zh: 老师讲了个故事，孩子们把它表演出来。

ex.en: She acted out her fantasies of pop stardom in front of her bedroom mirror.
ex.zh: 她对着…室镜子模拟自己幻想成为流行歌星的样子。

senses.en: to make sb annoyed by behaving badly, trying to get attention, etc.
senses.zh: 做出恼人(或引人注意等)的行为:

ex.en: The kids have been acting up all day.
ex.zh: 孩子们闹了一整天了。

senses.en: if a machine or part of the body acts up, it does not work properly

ex.en: The car’s acting up again.
ex.zh: 汽车又坏了。

ex.en: My ankle is acting up (= is painful and causing problems).
ex.zh: 我的脚踝犯病了。

senses.en: to include sth with sth else; to put sth into sth else or between two things

ex.en: Send me the new figures when the additional costs have been added in.
ex.zh: 算进外加成本后再把新数目给我。

ex.en: I’ve added in two extra paragraphs.
ex.zh: 我另外插进了两段。

senses.en: to build an extra room or rooms on to a house or other building

ex.en: They decided to add on rather than move.
ex.zh: 他们决计扩建一下房子，不搬走了。

senses.en: a thing that is added to or included with sth else

ex.en: The catalogue advertised add-ons such as extra memory and software.
ex.zh: 目录册宣传说有额外的内存和软件等附带产品。

ex.en: add-on products/pockets/units
ex.zh: 外加的产品/口袋/单元

senses.en: to increase the size, amount, number,etc. of sth
senses.zh: 使(数量等)增加；使(规模)扩大:

ex.en: Taking the children with us would only add to our problems.
ex.zh: 带着孩子只会给我们添乱。

ex.en: Music playing in the background added to the atmosphere.
ex.zh: 背景音乐渲染气氛。

senses.en: to come together to produce sth; to join two or more things, numbers, etc. together to produce sth

ex.en: The games, the dancing and the good food all added together to make a memorable occasion.
ex.zh: 游戏、舞蹈和美餐组成了这一难以忘怀的时刻。

ex.en: When all the different factors are added together, I can understand her decision.
ex.zh: 考虑到种种因素，我能够理解她的决定。

senses.en: to seem reasonable; to make sense; to have all the different parts agreeing with each other
senses.zh: 合乎情理；有道理；各部份协调一致:

ex.en: There are things in her story that just don’t add up.
ex.zh: 她的叙述有些地方根本不吻合。

ex.en: Now that I know where she was last night, it’s all beginning to add up.
ex.zh: 我知道了她昨晚的去处，一切就开始说得通。

senses.en: to calculate the total of two or more numbers or amounts

ex.en: I never could add up.
ex.zh: 我从来不会计算账目。

ex.en: She’s very good at adding up in her head.
ex.zh: 她很会心算。

senses.en: () to show sth; to have a particular meaning or result

ex.en: His evidence didn’t really add up to very much (= gave us very little information).
ex.zh: 他的证词实际上说明不了什么问题。

ex.en: All in all, it adds up to a pretty desperate situation.
ex.zh: 从各方面来看，这意味着情势相当危急。

senses.en: to think about a problem or a situation and decide how you are going to deal with it
senses.zh: 想法解决问题(或处理事情等) :

ex.en: We must address ourselves to the problem of traffic pollution.
ex.zh: 我们必须着手解决交通污染的问题。

senses.en: to act in the way that a particular law, rule or set of instructions says that you should; to follow or support a particular opinion or set of beliefs
senses.zh: 坚持，遵守，遵循(法律、规章、指示、信念等):

ex.en: They have adhered strictly to the terms of the treaty.
ex.zh: 他们严格遵守了条约的条款。

ex.en: He found the diet very difficult to adhere to.
ex.zh: 他觉得很难坚持这种规定饮食。

senses.en: to show that sth such as an explanation or an answer is possible; to allow sth to happen
senses.zh: 容许，有…可能(指解释、回答等) :

ex.en: The situation admits of only one explanation.
ex.zh: 这一状况只可能有一种解释。

senses.en: to make you feel happy or healthy
senses.zh: 使高兴(或健康)；适合某人:

ex.en: You look great! Marriage obviously agrees with you.
ex.zh: 你容光焕发啊！结婚显然对你有益。

ex.en: Mushrooms don’t agree with me (= they make me feel ill/sick).
ex.zh: 我吃了蘑菇就会不舒服。

senses.en: to approve of sth, especially a policy or a belief
senses.zh: 同意，赞成(尤指政策或信仰):

ex.en: I don’t agree with capital punishment.
ex.zh: 我不赞成死刑。

senses.en: to try to achieve sth; to have sth as your aim
senses.zh: 力求达到；努力取得；以…为目标:

ex.en: She’s aiming at a sports scholarship.
ex.zh: 她在争取获得一项体育奖学金。

ex.en: We need to aim at increasing exports.
ex.zh: 我们要努力增加出口。

senses.en: to have sth as an aim or purpose

ex.en: The new scheme is aimed at reducing unemployment.
ex.zh: 新计划旨在减低失业率。

senses.en: to notice sb/sth suddenly; to find or think of sth by chance
senses.zh: 突然注意到；偶然发现(或想到):

ex.en: My eye alighted on an old book.
ex.zh: 我的目光突然落到了一本旧书上。

ex.en: He finally alighted on a solution.
ex.zh: 他最后偶然想到了解决方法。

senses.en: to publicly support a person, a group of people or a set of opinions
senses.zh: 公开支持(某人、集体或观点) :

ex.en: The senator aligned himself with the critics of the proposed reforms.
ex.zh: 这位参议员公开支持对拟议的改革提出批评的人。

senses.en: to include sth when you are calculating sth or planning sth
senses.zh: 将…计算在内；考虑到； 估计到:

ex.en: Add an extra ten minutes to your journey time to allow for the traffic.
ex.zh: 考虑到交通，你的行程得额外多预算十分钟。

ex.en: I ’ ve bought a large size to allow for the fact that it may shrink in the wash.
ex.zh: 估计到衣服可能会缩水，我买了件大号的。

senses.en: to show that sth such as an explanation or an answer is possible; to make sth possible
senses.zh: 容许(解释、回答等)；使有可能:

ex.en: The facts allow of only one explanation.
ex.zh: 这些事实只可能有一种解释。

senses.en: to mention sb/sth indirectly or in a few words
senses.zh: 间接(或略微)提到；暗指；影射:

ex.en: He hated his mother’s way of alluding to Jean but never actually saying her name.
ex.zh: 他不喜欢母亲拐弯抹角从不指名地提及琼。

senses.en: to add up to sth; to result in a final total of sth

ex.en: The cost of the trip amounted to well over ￡500.
ex.zh: 这次旅行花费远远超过了500 英镑。

ex.en: The money I pay in tax and insurance contributions amounts to about 40% of my salary.
ex.zh: 交税和保险费用掉我工资的40%左右。

senses.en: to be equal to or the same as sth

ex.en: What they did amounted to a breach of contract.
ex.zh: 他们这样做等同于违约。

ex.en: It doesn’t matter whether I pay or my husband pays — it amounts to the same thing in the end.
ex.zh: 我付钱或我丈夫付钱无关紧要─最终反正都是一回事。

senses.en: to try to obtain sth without asking for it directly

ex.en: She’s angling for an invitation to the party.
ex.zh: 她婉转地让别人邀请她参加聚会。

senses.en: to defend yourself against sth bad that sb has said about you

ex.en: It’s not fair to criticize without giving her the chance to answer back.
ex.zh: 批评她而不给她机会辩白是不公平的。

senses.en: to speak on behalf of sb and say what they will do or what they think
senses.zh: 代表…讲话； 代表…的意见:

ex.en: I can’t answer for my colleagues, but I can manage a meeting next week.
ex.zh: 我不能代表同事们的意见，但我可以在下个星期会面。

senses.en: to say that you are certain that sb has a particular quality or can be trusted or relied on
senses.zh: 担保，保证(某人的品质等):

ex.en: I can answer for her honesty.
ex.zh: 我可以担保她为人诚实。

senses.en: to have to explain your actions to sb or show that they are right or reasonable

ex.en: You will answer to me for any damage to the car.
ex.zh: 汽车有任何损坏我都找你负责。

ex.en: If anything happens to her, you’ll have me to answer to.
ex.zh: 她如果出了任何事，你都得向我交待。

senses.en: to make a serious and urgent request for sth or for sth to be done

ex.en: The government has appealed for calm.
ex.zh: 政府呼吁保持镇静。

ex.en: The police appealed for witnesses to come forward.
ex.zh: 警方呼吁目击者挺身而出。

senses.en: to try to persuade sb to do sth by reminding them that it is a good, reasonable thing to do
to belong to sth; to be connected with sth
senses.zh: 属于，涉及，关系到(某事物) :

ex.en: the duties appertaining to the post
ex.zh: 这一职位的责任

senses.en: [NOTE]This verb is usually only used in written English.
senses.zh: 这个动词通常只用于书面语。

senses.en: to tell or inform sb of sth
senses.zh: 将某事通知某人；向某人告知某事:

ex.en: We were fully apprised of the situation.
ex.zh: 我们完全获悉当时的情况。

senses.en: to persuade sb to do sth by giving them a large number of reasons why they should do it

ex.en: I managed to argue him into going back home to talk to his parents.
ex.zh: 我终于说服他回家去和父母对话。

senses.en: to discuss all the details of an idea, a plan, etc., often in an excited or angry way, until you reach a decision
senses.zh: 彻底辩论(常指激烈辩论之后作出决定):

ex.en: I’m sure they’ll manage to argue out any differences that arise.
ex.zh: 我相信他们会把出现的分歧辩个明白。

senses.en: to persuade sb not to do sth by giving them a large number of reasons why they should not do it

ex.en: I argued her out of her crazy idea.
ex.zh: 我说服她放弃了荒唐的想法。

senses.en: to disagree with what sb says;to say or show that sth is not right
senses.zh: 不同意(说法)；不承认(表述)；表示(某事)不正确:

ex.en: ‘It’s cold today, isn’t it?’ ‘I can’t argue with you there!(= I agree with you).’
ex.zh: “今天很冷，对吧？”“ 的确很冷！ ”

ex.en: It’s a lovely jacket — and you couldn’t argue with the price.
ex.zh: 这件短上衣很不错─而且价格也合适。

senses.en: to agree on sth or to find sth after discussing and thinking about it
senses.zh: 达成(协议)；作出(决议等)；得出(结论等):

ex.en: They had both arrived at the same conclusion.
ex.zh: 他俩得出了同样的结论。

ex.en: It didn’t take long to arrive at a decision.
ex.zh: 没过多久便作出了决定。

senses.en: to behave in a silly or annoying way and waste time instead of doing what you are supposed to be doing

ex.en: Stop arsing about and give me my bag back.
ex.zh: 别胡闹了，把我的包还给我。

senses.en: to consider, perhaps wrongly,that sth has been written, painted, spoken or created by a particular person
senses.zh: 以为某项作品(或说话) 出自某人:

ex.en: This play is usually ascribed to Shakespeare.
ex.zh: 这个剧本通常被认为是莎士比亚创作的。

senses.en: to consider that sth is caused by a particular person or thing

ex.en: He ascribed his exhaustion to the heat and an unfamiliar diet.
ex.zh: 他认为自己疲乏是由于炎热和不适应饮食。

senses.en: to consider that a person or a thing has a particular quality

ex.en: I am reluctant to ascribe supernatural powers to a fortune teller.
ex.zh: 我不太相信算命的人有超自然力。

ex.en: The government ascribe great importance to these policies.
ex.zh: 政府十分重视这些政策。

senses.en: to ask for news about sb and how they are, etc.

ex.en: Did she ask after me in her letter?
ex.zh: 她在信中问起我了吗？

senses.en: to ask sb if they would like to go with you to an event or activity
senses.zh: 邀某人做伴；请某人同行:

ex.en: Jane and Ed are going to a movie tonight, and they’ve asked me along.
ex.zh: 简和埃德今晚要去看电影，还邀我同去。

senses.en: to ask a number of different people in order to find out sth

ex.en: I don’t know if there’s any work, but I’ll ask around for you.
ex.zh: 我不知道有没有工作，不过我会帮你打听打听。

senses.en: to invite sb to come back to your house with you for a drink,etc. when you are both out together
senses.zh: 邀请(一起外出的人)回到家里来:

ex.en: I asked him back for a coffee.
ex.zh: 我邀请他回我家来喝杯咖啡。

senses.en: to say that you want to see or speak to sb
senses.zh: 要求与某人见面(或对话):

ex.en: There’s somebody at the door asking for Pete.
ex.zh: 门外有人要见皮特。

senses.en: to invite sb to come into the room or building that you are in, especially your home

ex.en: Aren’t you going to ask me in? It’s cold out here.
ex.zh: 你不请我进去吗？外面很冷。

ex.en: She asked me into her office for a chat.
ex.zh: 她请我进她的办公室聊聊。

senses.en: to invite sb to go out with you, especially when you would like a romantic relationship with them
senses.zh: 请…外出约会(尤指为建立恋爱关系):

ex.en: Has he asked you out yet?
ex.zh: 他约你外出了吗？

senses.en: to invite sb to come and visit you in your home

ex.en: She’s asked me round for dinner.
ex.zh: 她请我去她家吃饭。

senses.en: to have a strong desire to gain or achieve sth
senses.zh: 渴望得到某事物；有志成就某事:

ex.en: He’s never really aspired to great wealth.
ex.zh: 他从未真正渴求过致富。

senses.en: to be involved with or spend a lot of time with sb or with a group of people,especially people that sb else does not approve of
senses.zh: 与(尤指不受欢迎的人)密切交往；和…混在一起:

ex.en: I don’t like the people you associate with.
ex.zh: 我不喜欢你交往的人。

senses.en: to say that you agree with sb or with their ideas

ex.en: It was unreasonable to expect the Democrats to associate themselves with spending cuts and tax increases.
ex.zh: 期望民主派赞同削减开支和加税是不合理的。

senses.en: to deal with or take responsibility for sth; to give practical help and care to sb who needs it

ex.en: I have some urgent business to attend to.
ex.zh: 我有一些急事要处理。

ex.en: () Are you being attended to?
ex.zh: 有人接待你吗？

senses.en: to consider, perhaps wrongly, that sth has been written, painted,spoken or created by a particular person
senses.zh: 以为某项作品(或说话)出自某人:

ex.en: This painting is usually attributed to Goya.
ex.zh: 据一般相信，这幅画是戈雅的作品。

senses.en: to consider that sth is caused by a particular person or thing

ex.en: His success can be largely attributed to hard work.
ex.zh: 他的成功可以说主要是靠勤奋。

ex.en: She said she was not going to attribute blame or seek revenge for what had happened.
ex.zh: 她说她不会为所发生的事进行谴责或寻求报复。

senses.en: to sell sth at an auction, especially sth that sb no longer needs or wants
senses.zh: 拍卖掉(尤指不再需要的东西):

ex.en: The house and all its contents will be auctioned off next week.
ex.zh: 下星期将拍卖掉这所房子和里面的所有东西。

senses.en: to make use of sth; to take advantage of sth, usually to improve your situation

ex.en: Guests are encouraged to avail themselves of all the hotel’s services.
ex.zh: 旅馆鼓励旅客充分利用各种服务。

ex.en: I’d like to avail myself of this opportunity to thank you all.
ex.zh: 我想藉此机会感谢大家。

senses.en: to result in a fair or equal amount over a period of time or after several occasions
senses.zh: 达到平均；结果公平；持平:

ex.en: Sometimes I do the cooking and sometimes my flatmate does. It averages out over a month (= results in us each doing the same amount of cooking).
ex.zh: 有时我做饭，有时同住的人做饭。一个月下来我们做饭的次数一样多。

senses.en: to have a particular amount as the average over a period of time

ex.en: The time she spends practising the piano averages out at about an hour a day.
ex.zh: 她练钢琴的时间是平均每天大约一小时。

senses.en: to become aware of sth and its possible results; to realize or understand sth
senses.zh: 察觉到；意识到；醒悟到；明白到:

ex.en: They finally awoke to the full extent of the problem.
ex.zh: 他们最终彻底认识到问题的严重程度。

ex.en: I suddenly awoke to the fact that I had the answer in front of me.
ex.zh: 我突然发觉答案就摆在我面前。

senses.en: to become aware of sth, or to make sb become aware of sth, and its possible results
senses.zh: (使)察觉到， 意识到， 醒悟到:

ex.en: People are gradually awakening to their rights.
ex.zh: 人们正逐渐意识到自己的权利。

ex.en: The public has been awakened to the full horror of the situation.
ex.zh: 公众完全意识到了这一状况的可怕程度。

senses.en: to move backwards away from sb/sth frightening or unpleasant

ex.en: He stepped forward and she backed away in alarm.
ex.zh: 他向前跨了一步，她惊慌地退避开。

ex.en: The child backed away from the dog nervously.
ex.zh: 孩子紧张地后退躲避那条狗。

senses.en: to avoid doing sth unpleasant or difficult; to show that you no longer support an action or an idea
senses.zh: 退缩；背弃(某行动或想法):

ex.en: We will not back away from tough measures.
ex.zh: 我们不会手软的。

ex.en: The union has backed away from calling a strike.
ex.zh: 工会放弃了号召罢工。

senses.en: to take back a claim or a demand that you have made, or sth that you have said, usually because sb forces you to
senses.zh: (被迫)收回(声明、言论等)；放弃(要求、主张等):

ex.en: Neither of them will back down on this issue.
ex.zh: 他俩在此问题上都不会让步的。

ex.en: His critics were forced to back down.
ex.zh: 批评他的人被迫偃旗息鼓了。

senses.en: () to stop threatening or annoying sb

ex.en: Back off and let me make my own decisions.
ex.zh: 别烦我了，让我自己做决定吧。

ex.en: The press have agreed to back off and leave the couple alone.
ex.zh: 新闻界同意不再打扰这对夫妻。

senses.en: to move away from sb/sth frightening or unpleasant

ex.en: As the head teacher approached the children backed off.
ex.zh: 校长过来时，孩子们闪开了。

senses.en: to decide not to continue to do sth or support an idea, in order to avoid a difficult or unpleasant situation
senses.zh: 放弃(某事)；不再支持(某想法):

ex.en: The government backed off in the face of strong opposition.
ex.zh: 政府在强烈的反对下退却了。

ex.en: He refused to back off from his earlier statement.
ex.zh: 他不肯撤回先前的声明。

senses.en: to decide not to do sth that you had agreed or promised to do
senses.zh: 退出；放弃(同意或答应做的事):

ex.en: Everything’s arranged. It’s too late to back out now.
ex.zh: 一切都安排好了。现在打退堂鼓为时太晚。

ex.en: There’s still time to back out of selling the house.
ex.zh: 现在决定不卖房子还来得及。

senses.en: to move backwards a short distance, especially in a vehicle; to make sb/sth move backwards a short distance

ex.en: You can back up another two metres or so.
ex.zh: 你可以再退两米左右。

ex.en: Jeff backed the van up and drove off quickly.
ex.zh: 杰夫倒了倒车，然后飞快地开走。

senses.en: to say or show that what sb says is true
senses.zh: 证明某人(所言属实)；证实(某人所言):

ex.en: If I tell my parents I was with you, will you back me up?
ex.zh: 假若我对父母说我当时和你在一起，你肯为我作证吗？

ex.en: His version of events is not backed up by the evidence.
ex.zh: 他对事情的陈述证据不足。

senses.zh: (通常用作形容词) music that supports the main singer or player in popular music or jazz(流行音乐或爵士乐的)伴奏，伴唱:

ex.en: a backup singer for Stevie Wonder
ex.zh: 史蒂维·旺德的伴唱歌手

ex.en: She once sang backup for Madonna.
ex.zh: 她曾经为麦当娜伴唱。

senses.en: ) to make a copy of a file, a program, etc. that can be used if the original one is lost or damaged
senses.zh: 给(文件、程序等)做备份；备份:

ex.en: We back up all the files every night.
ex.zh: 我们每晚都给所有文件做备份。

senses.en: [U] support or help that you can use in order to do sth

ex.en: military backup
ex.zh: 军事援助

ex.en: They have a huge back-up team.
ex.zh: 他们有一支庞大的后援队伍。

senses.en: [C] a second piece of equipment, set of plans, person, etc. that can replace another if necessary
senses.zh: 备用器械(或计划、人员等)；后备:

ex.en: He’s our back-up if another player isn’t available.
ex.zh: 如果我们其他队员无法上场，就由他替补。

ex.en: the back-up plan
ex.zh: 备用计划

senses.en: [C] () a copy of a file, program, etc.for use in case the original is lost or damaged

ex.en: Have you kept a backup of this file?
ex.zh: 你把这文件备份了吗？

ex.en: a backup disk
ex.zh: 备份磁盘

senses.en: to put sth, usually large amounts of sth, into a bag or bags
senses.zh: 把(常指大量的东西)装进袋子:

ex.en: The vegetables are bagged up on the farm and then sent out to the shop.
ex.zh: 蔬菜在农场装袋后送到商店。

senses.en: ) to stop doing sth or taking part in sth because it is difficult or unpleasant

ex.en: The actor who was supposed to be playing the part bailed out.
ex.zh: 原计划饰演这个角色的演员不干了。

senses.en: to throw water out of a boat with a container or with your hands

ex.en: The boat will sink unless we bail out.
ex.zh: 我们若不排水，船就要沉。

ex.en: They started bailing the boat out.
ex.zh: 他们动手把船里的水舀出去。

senses.en: to pay sb’s bail (= the money that sb accused of a crime has to pay if they do not appear at their trial) for them, so that they can be set free until their trial
to rescue sb/sth from difficulties,especially financial difficulties
senses.zh: 帮助…脱离(财政等)困境；(从困境中)拯救…:

ex.en: The government has refused to bail the company out again.
ex.zh: 政府拒绝再次帮助该公司渡过难关。

senses.en: an act of giving financial help to a company, economy, etc.to save it from failing

ex.en: government/bank bailouts
ex.zh: 政府财政援助；银行应急贷款

ex.en: a bailout package
ex.zh: 财政援助计划

senses.en: to compare the value or importance of one plan, argument, etc. against another
senses.zh: 将(两计划、论点等)进行比较；权衡(两事物的)重要性:

ex.en: You must balance the high salary against the long working hours.
ex.zh: 你必须权衡高工资和长工时两者的利弊。

senses.en: to spoil sth; to do sth very badly
something that has been done very badly

ex.en: I made a real balls-up of my exams.
ex.zh: 我考试考得一塌煳涂。

senses.en: to form a group and act together in order to achieve sth, etc.

ex.en: We need to band together to fight these reforms.
ex.zh: 我们要齐心协力与这些变革作斗争。

senses.en: to wrap a bandage (= a long narrow strip of material) around a part of the body that is injured
senses.zh: 为某人包扎伤口；包扎(受伤部位) :

ex.en: Joe bandaged me up until the doctor came.
ex.zh: 乔在医生到来之前用绷带包扎着我的伤口。

ex.en: I didn’t see the burns because her fingers were all bandaged up.
ex.zh: 我没有看见烧伤，因为她的手指缠满了绷带。

senses.en: to move around noisily

ex.en: We could hear them banging about upstairs, moving things.
ex.zh: 我们能听到他们在楼上轰隆隆地来回挪动东西。

senses.en: () to hit sth repeatedly with lots of force or energy

ex.en: She picked up the hammer and began banging away with enthusiasm.
ex.zh: 她拿起锤子便用力敲打起来。

senses.en: to work very hard at sth

ex.en: She banged away all day at her assignment.
ex.zh: 她一整天都在埋头写作业。

senses.en: to put sth down quickly and with a lot of force so that it makes a loud noise

ex.en: He banged his fist down on the table.
ex.zh: 他砰地一拳砸在桌子上。

ex.en: He banged the phone down (= ended the telephone conversation) before I could explain.
ex.zh: 我还没来得及解释，他就啪地挂断了电话。

senses.en: to crash into or hit sb/sth violently, usually by mistake

ex.en: He ran around the corner and banged into an old lady who was coming the other way.
ex.zh: 他从拐角处跑出来，一下子撞了迎面走来的一位老太太。

senses.en: to talk or write a lot or in a boring way about sth

ex.en: Pat is always banging on about politics.
ex.zh: 帕特总是没完没了地谈论政治。

ex.en: She keeps banging on about how wonderful her son is.
ex.zh: 她逢人便说她的儿子有多优秀。

senses.en: to play music very loudly

ex.en: He banged out the tune on the piano.
ex.zh: 他在钢琴上轰鸣地弹奏那首曲子。

senses.en: to write sth very quickly and without taking much care
senses.zh: 匆匆写出；(写文章等)粗制漤造:

ex.en: She was banging out four novels a year.
ex.zh: 她一年赶写了四部小说。

senses.en: to damage or injure sb/sth, especially by hitting sth else
senses.zh: 撞伤某人(或身体部位)；碰坏:

ex.en: I banged up my knee when I fell off the bike.
ex.zh: 我从自行车上摔下来磕破了膝盖。

senses.en: to be locked up or put in prison

ex.en: He was banged up in a Singapore jail for six months.
ex.zh: 他在新加坡一座监狱里关押了六个月。

senses.en: to rely on sb/sth; to be confident that sth will happen
senses.zh: 依靠； 指望；对…有信心:

ex.en: I’m banking on your help.
ex.zh: 我还得靠你帮忙呢。

ex.en: I’m banking on you to help me.
ex.zh: 我还得靠你帮忙呢。

senses.en: to form into a large pile; to make sth form a large pile

ex.en: The snow had banked up on either side of the road.
ex.zh: 路的两旁尽是积雪。

senses.en: to give away sth valuable or important in exchange for sth less valuable or important

ex.en: The leaders refused to bargain away the freedom of their people.
ex.zh: 领导人不肯以牺牲人民的自由做交易。

senses.en: to expect or be prepared to do sth; to expect sth to happen or sb to do sth
senses.zh: 预料到(某事)；预备(做某事)；料想到(某事发生或某人做某事):

ex.en: We hadn’t bargained for such bad weather.
ex.zh: 我们没预料到如此恶劣的天气。

ex.en: I hadn’t bargained on taking the kids with us.
ex.zh: 我没打算让孩子们和我们同去。

senses.en: [NOTE]These phrasal verbs are usually used in negative sentences.
senses.zh: 这些短语动词通常用于否定句。

senses.en: to enter a place or join a group of people quickly and rudely, without being asked

ex.en: Sorry to barge in, but…
ex.zh: 抱歉冒昧打扰，可是…

ex.en: She barged in on our meeting without knocking.
ex.zh: 我们开会时她不敲门就闯了进来。

senses.en: to interrupt what sb is doing or saying, especially when you have not been invited to join in

ex.en: As soon as I paused for breath, Bart barged in.
ex.zh: 我刚停下来喘口气，巴特便抢过了话头。

ex.en: You can’t just come barging into our conversation!
ex.zh: 你不能冒冒失失地打断我们的谈话！

senses.en: to shout sth loudly

ex.en: She barked out instructions to her secretary.
ex.zh: 她扯着嗓子对秘书发号施令。

senses.en: to put up a line of objects at the entrance to a room or building, so that nobody can get in or out,usually to protect or defend yourself or sb else
senses.zh: (堵住入口)让自己(或别人)躲在(…)里面:

ex.en: The police were called when he barricaded himself in.
ex.zh: 他躲进去时有人叫来了警察。

ex.en: They barricaded themselves inside their house.
ex.zh: 他们把自己关在屋子里。

senses.en: to use or have an idea, an experience, etc.as the point from which sth can be developed
senses.zh: 以概念(或经验等)为…的基础(或根据):

ex.en: The novel is based on a true story.
ex.zh: 这部小说是根据一件真事创作的。

ex.en: She is basing the prosecution case on the evidence of two witnesses.
ex.zh: 她是依照两名目击者的证词提起诉讼的。

senses.en: to hit or strike sb/sth and treat them/it in a rough way

ex.en: The mugger had bashed her about.
ex.zh: 行兇抢劫者对她拳打脚踢。

senses.en: to work very hard at sth for a period of time
senses.zh: 持续努力地做，持之以囱地做(某事):

ex.en: I bashed away at the article without a break from 11 until 6.
ex.zh: 我从11点到6点钟一刻不停地写那篇文章。

senses.en: to destroy sth and make it fall by hitting it violently

ex.en: The firefighters had to bash the door down.
ex.zh: 消防员当时要把门撞倒。

senses.en: to break or destroy sth by hitting it violently

ex.en: The window had been bashed in.
ex.zh: 窗户打碎了。

senses.en: to continue working hard at sth

ex.en: Let’s bash on.
ex.zh: 咱们加把劲吧。

ex.en: I’d better bash on with my work.
ex.zh: 我最好继续努力工作。

senses.en: to write sth very quickly, without taking much care
senses.zh: 匆匆地写；(写文章等)粗制漤造:

ex.en: I don’t do drafts of articles. I just bash them out.
ex.zh: 我写文章不打草稿，随便一写就完事了。

senses.en: to attack sb violently
to talk about or discuss plans or ideas, etc. before you decide what to do
senses.zh: 讨论(想法、计划等)的可行性:

ex.en: We’re just batting some ideas around.
ex.zh: 我们只不过是在讨论一些想法。

senses.en: to fasten sth firmly in order to prevent damage by storms or winds
senses.zh: 固定某物(以防风暴危害) :

ex.en: They managed to batten down the shutters and doors before the hurricane hit.
ex.zh: 他们赶在飓风到来之前钉牢了百叶窗和门。

senses.en: to prepare for difficult times ahead
senses.zh: 为应付困难做准备；未雨绸缪:

ex.en: Businesses are battening down the hatches and preparing for a difficult year.
ex.zh: 各公司都在为困难的一年做准备。

senses.en: to hit sth repeatedly until it breaks and falls down

ex.en: The only way to get in was to batter the door down.
ex.zh: 想进去只能把门砸开。

senses.en: to be unwilling to do sth or to get involved in sth because it is difficult, dangerous, expensive, etc.

ex.en: He baulked at the idea of telling his parents where he was going.
ex.zh: 他不愿告诉父母自己要去哪里。

senses.en: to speak angrily to sb because they have done sth wrong

ex.en: My boss bawled me out for being late.
ex.zh: 我迟到， 给老板训斥了一顿。

senses.en: [usually sing.] () an act of speaking angrily to sb because they have done sth wrong
to try to get or obtain sth

ex.en: Several people in the office are after the same job.
ex.zh: 办公室里有几个人想做同一件工作。

ex.en: She’s being too nice. I wonder what she’s after.
ex.zh: 她表现得好过了头。我不知道她图的是什么。

senses.en: to be busy doing sth

ex.en: He’s been at his essay all night.
ex.zh: 他整整一夜都在写文章。

senses.en: to behave badly; to argue or fight

ex.en: The kids are at it again.
ex.zh: 孩子们又闹起来了。

senses.en: to not be at home, especially when you are on holiday/vacation or on a business trip

ex.en: We’ll be away for the month of August.
ex.zh: 我们八月份要外出度假。

ex.en: He’s away on business at the moment.
ex.zh: 他出差了。

senses.en: to give sb your support

ex.en: Don’t forget that we’re behind you all the way.
ex.zh: 别忘了我们始终支持你。

senses.en: to be late doing sth, such as paying a bill, your rent, etc.

ex.en: We’re behind with the mortgage repayments.
ex.zh: 我们没有按时偿还按揭贷款。

ex.en: I’m behind with my college assignments.
ex.zh: 我没依时完成大学作业。

senses.en: to treat sb severely or unfairly

ex.en: He’s been really down on me lately.
ex.zh: 他最近特别和我过不去。

senses.en: to be the responsibility of sb; to be sb’s fault
senses.zh: 是某人的责任；是某人的错:

ex.en: It’s down to you to help them now.
ex.zh: 现在该你帮助他们了。

senses.en: to have or catch an illness

ex.en: Gill’s down with flu.
ex.zh: 吉尔得了流感。

senses.en: to be in fashion

ex.en: Miniskirts are in this season.
ex.zh: 本季度流行超短裙。

senses.en: to be elected to a political position

ex.en: The Democrats are in for another term.
ex.zh: 民主党获选连任。

senses.en: to be going to experience sth soon, especially sth unpleasant
senses.zh: 即将面临(尤指令人不快的事):

ex.en: She’s in for a shock.
ex.zh: 她就要碰上一件震惊的事了。

ex.en: It looks like we’re in for a storm.
ex.zh: 我们好像要遇到暴风雨了。

senses.en: to have a share in or knowledge of sth; to be or become involved in sth

ex.en: Are you in on the secret?
ex.zh: 你知道这个秘密吗？

ex.en: I’d like to be in on the deal.
ex.zh: 我很想加入这桩交易。

senses.en: to be (very) friendly with sb and likely to get an advantage from the friendship
senses.zh: 同某人关系密切(可从中获益)

senses.en: to have a taste for or an interest in sth

ex.en: Are you into jazz music?
ex.zh: 你喜欢爵士乐吗？

ex.en: He’s been into trains since he was a small boy.
ex.zh: 他从小就很喜欢火车。

senses.en: to leave; to go, especially in a hurry

ex.en: I must be off.
ex.zh: 我必须走了。

senses.en: to have gone bad and not be fit to eat or drink

ex.en: This milk is off.
ex.zh: 牛奶坏了。

senses.en: to have a particular amount of sth

ex.en: How are we off for coffee (= how much have we got)?
ex.zh: 我们有多少咖啡？

senses.en: (of an event, a show, a performance, etc.
senses.zh: 活动、演出、表演等) to be happening; to take place进行中:

ex.en: Is the party still on?
ex.zh: 聚会还没散吗？

senses.en: (of a performer
senses.zh: 演员) to be on the stage; to perform在台上；演出:

ex.en: Who’s on next?
ex.zh: 下面该谁上台？

ex.en: We’re on after the support band.
ex.zh: 我们在伴奏响起之后上台。

senses.en: (of food
senses.zh: 食物) to be cooking在烹调中:

ex.en: Are the potatoes on?
ex.zh: 土豆烧上了吗？

senses.en: to talk about sth, often in a boring way; to mean sth

ex.en: He’s always on about how much money he earns.
ex.zh: 他总爱唠叨他赚多少钱。

ex.en: What are you on about? (= I don’t really understand).
ex.zh: 你究竟是什么意思？

senses.en: to try to persuade sb to do sth by talking about it very often and in an annoying way

ex.en: I’ve been on at my husband to go to the doctor, but he won’t.
ex.zh: 我不断地劝我丈夫去看医生，可他就是不去。

senses.en: to become aware that sb has done sth wrong or illegal and be trying to catch them
senses.zh: 捕捉，缉捕(犯错或违法者):

ex.en: The police aren’t onto us yet.
ex.zh: 警方还没有发觉要捉拿我们。

senses.en: to talk to sb about sth, especially to complain about sth or ask them to do sth
senses.zh: 和某人谈(某事)；(尤指)向某人抱怨，要求某人(做某事):

ex.en: I’ve been onto the council about the noise.
ex.zh: 我已经和委员会谈过噪音的问题了。

senses.en: to have stopped work as a protest and be on strike

ex.en: The postal workers are still out.
ex.zh: 邮政工人还在罢工。

senses.en: to be no longer in prison

ex.en: I’ve heard Smith’s out now.
ex.zh: 我听说史密斯出狱了。

senses.en: to no longer be in fashion

ex.en: Black is out this year.
ex.zh: 今年不时兴黑色。

senses.en: to be trying very hard to do sth or to get sth

ex.en: He’s out for revenge.
ex.zh: 他企图进行报复。

ex.en: Everyone’s just out for what they can get these days (= they are trying to get things for themselves).
ex.zh: 如今每个人都只顾图谋私利。

senses.en: to have used up a supply of sth and have nothing left

ex.en: We’re out of sugar.
ex.zh: 我们的糖吃完了。

senses.en: to have returned to your usual state of happiness after the end of a relationship
senses.zh: (和某人关系结束后)恢复心情:

ex.en: It was hard at first, but I’m over him now.
ex.zh: 和他分手之初很难过，可我熬过来了。

senses.en: used to show that you think sb is so old that they can no longer do anything useful or interesting

ex.en: The children laughed at him and said he was past it.
ex.zh: 孩子们嘲笑他，说他年老不中用了。

senses.en: to be connected to sb on the telephone

ex.en: You’re through now.
ex.zh: 您的电话接通了。

ex.en: You’re through to the manager now.
ex.zh: 您可以和经理通话了。

senses.en: to be awake

ex.en: You’re up early.
ex.zh: 你醒得真早。

ex.en: I’ve been up all night.
ex.zh: 我彻夜未眠。

senses.en: (of the wind, the sea, etc.
senses.zh: 风、海等) to increase in strength or become violent增强；变得猛烈； 水势(变得) 兇猛:

ex.en: In the morning the wind was up and we got ready for a day’s sailing.
ex.zh: 早晨风力增强了，我们为一天的航行作好了准备。

senses.en: , ) (of a drink, a meal,etc.
senses.zh: 饮料、饭菜等) to be ready准备好；预备好:

ex.en: Tea’s up! Come and get it.
ex.zh: 茶沏好了！来用吧。

senses.en: to be facing problems or difficulties

ex.en: We’re up against tough competition.
ex.zh: 我们面临着激烈的竞争。

ex.en: With three players injured, they were really up against it (= in a difficult situation).
ex.zh: 三名队员受了伤，他们的处境实在艰难。

senses.en: to appear in court or before a judge

ex.en: He’s up before the judge tomorrow.
ex.zh: 他明天出庭受审。

senses.en: to be considered for sth, especially as a candidate for a job, in an election, etc.
senses.zh: 为(职位或选举等的)候选人:

ex.en: She’s up for promotion.
ex.zh: 她可能升职。

senses.en: to be for sb to buy
() to be ready to take part in an activity
to be sb’s responsibility or duty

ex.en: It’s up to you to make sure the house is kept tidy.
ex.zh: 保持房屋整洁是你的责任。

senses.en: to be left to sb to decide

ex.en: ‘Shall we go out?’ ‘It’s up to you.’
ex.zh: “ 我们出去好吗？”“你来决定吧。

senses.en: used as a greeting to mean ‘how are you?’,‘what have you been doing?’, etc.
to be going to happen very soon

ex.en: The election is almost upon us.
ex.zh: 选举很快就要开始了。

senses.en: ) to move towards sb/sth in a determined or threatening way

ex.en: A crowd of journalists bore down on the minister.
ex.zh: 一群记者冲向部长。

ex.en: A hurricane is bearing down on central America.
ex.zh: 飓风向中美洲袭来。

senses.en: ) to press or push on sb/sth

ex.en: ( )The government has announced it will bear down on (= deal strictly with) inflation.
ex.zh: 政府宣布将严加遏制通货膨胀。

senses.en: ( ) to be connected with sb/sth; to have an effect on sb/sth
senses.zh: 和… 有关； 涉及； 对… 有影响:

ex.en: This decision bears directly on our everyday lives.
ex.zh: 这一决定直接影响我们的日常生活。

senses.en: [NOTE]This verb is mainly used in written English.
senses.zh: 这个动词主要用于书面语。

senses.en: to show that sth is true or that what sb says is true; to support sb/sth
senses.zh: 证实； 为… 作证； 支持:

ex.en: I always said she’d do well. John will bear me out on this.
ex.zh: 我总是说她会做好的。约翰会证实这一点。

ex.en: John will bear out what I say.
ex.zh: 约翰会证实我的话。

senses.en: to remain cheerful and in control in a difficult situation

ex.en: ‘How is your mother?’ ‘She’s bearing up very well.’
ex.zh: “你母亲好吗？”“她很硬朗。”

ex.en: ‘How are you?’ ‘Oh, bearing up.’
ex.zh: “你怎么样了？”“还挺得住。

senses.en: to be patient with sb

ex.en: If you’ll just bear with me for a moment, I’ll try to find her.
ex.zh: 你如果能给我一点时间，我会尽力找她的。

ex.en: She’s under a lot of strain. Just bear with her.
ex.zh: 她承受着很大的压力。对她要有耐心。

senses.en: to make sb move backwards away from sth

ex.en: She was beaten back by the flames.
ex.zh: 火焰迫使她退了回去。

ex.en: They tried to beat the enemy forces back.
ex.zh: 他们试图把敌军击退。

senses.en: to persuade sb to reduce theprice of sth; to get sb to accept a lower price forsth

ex.en: Chris tried to beat them down to a lower price.
ex.zh: 克里斯设法让他们降价。

senses.en: to hit sth hard, often manytimes, until it falls down

ex.en: The police had to beat the door down.
ex.zh: 警察不得不把门撞开。

senses.en: to make sth flatter or lower byhitting it hard, usually with sth flat
senses.zh: (用平展的工具)把…拍平，把…打下去:

ex.en: I used a spade to beat down the mud until it was flat and hard.
ex.zh: 我用铁锹把泥土拍得又平又硬实。

ex.en: Two women tried to beat down the flames on his back.
ex.zh: 两个女子试图把他后背上的火焰扑打灭。

senses.en: to drive sb/sth back or awayby fighting

ex.en: They beat off an attack by the rebel army.
ex.zh: 他们击退了叛军的进攻。

ex.en: He tried to beat the thugs off with a stick.
ex.zh: 他想用棍子打走那些流氓。

senses.en: to hit or kick sbrepeatedly
to produce a rhythm by hittingsth such as a drum repeatedly
to achieve sth orreach a place before sb else

ex.en: Beckham beat everyone else to the ball.
ex.zh: 贝克汉姆超过了所有的人先得到球。

ex.en: Book now before somebody else beats you to it!
ex.zh: 别人还没预订之前赶紧捷足先登吧！

senses.en: to hit or kick sb repeatedly

ex.en: Her husband used to beat her up.
ex.zh: 她的丈夫过去常对她大打出手。

ex.en: The gang went round beating up old ladies.
ex.zh: 这伙匪徒四处殴打老妇。

senses.en: [usually before noun] ()old or damaged

ex.en: He drives a beat-up old van.
ex.zh: 他开一辆破破烂烂的旧货车。

senses.en: to blame yourself for sth; to criticize yourself

ex.en: If we don’t succeed the first time, we shouldn’t beat ourselves up, but try again.
ex.zh: 第一次不成功，我们不应该自责，而要再次努力。

senses.en: to attack sb physically or with words
senses.zh: 攻击某人(身体)；(言语上)攻击某人:

ex.en: Of course it’s not OK to beat up on your wife.
ex.zh: 打妻子当然不对。

ex.en: He was accused of beating up on the President in the press.
ex.zh: 有人指责他在报章上攻击总统。

senses.en: to work very hard at sth

ex.en: She’s been beavering away at her homework for hours.
ex.zh: 她连续几个小时都在忙着写作业。

senses.en: to happen to sb/sth

ex.en: I wonder what became of the people who lived next door.
ex.zh: 我不知道原来住隔壁的人怎么样了。

ex.en: What will become of us if I lose my job?
ex.zh: 如果我丢了工作，我们会怎么样？

senses.en: to lie down to go to sleep somewhere you do not normally sleep

ex.en: Young people bedded down in doorways.
ex.zh: 年轻人睡在各家门口。

senses.en: to make sth bigger, stronger, more interesting, etc.
senses.zh: 使较大(或强壮、有意思等)；加强…:

ex.en: Security has been beefed up.
ex.zh: 安全措施已经加强了。

ex.en: The company has been trying to beef up its image.
ex.zh: 公司一直致力于改善形象。

senses.en: [only before noun] improved;made bigger, stronger, more interesting, etc.

ex.en: beefed-up security
ex.zh: 强化的安全措施

senses.en: to ask to be excused from sth; to say that you cannot do sth that you are expected or have promised to do
senses.zh: 推辞(要求或已答应做的事)；反悔:

ex.en: She was asked to work the weekend shift but she tried to beg off.
ex.zh: 有人让她周末轮值，可她竭力推辞。

ex.en: He begged off visiting his grandparents.
ex.zh: 他把看祖父母的事推掉了。

senses.en: to feel sure that sb/sth exists

ex.en: Do you believe in ghosts?
ex.zh: 你相信有鬼吗？

ex.en: I believe in God.
ex.zh: 我相信有上帝。

senses.en: to have confidence in sb/sth, to feel sure that they/it will be successful or achieve sth
senses.zh: 信赖；信任；相信某人(或事情)会成功:

ex.en: My parents always believed in me.
ex.zh: 我父母始终对我抱有信心。

ex.en: I have to believe in a product before I can sell it.
ex.zh: 我必须对产品有把握才能出售。

senses.en: to feel that sth is right or valuable; to approve of sth
senses.zh: 认为某事对(或有价值)；赞成:

ex.en: Do you believe in capital punishment?
ex.zh: 你赞成死刑吗？

ex.en: She doesn’t believe in running risks.
ex.zh: 她不主张冒险。

senses.en: to accept that sb is capable of a particular action, etc., especially a bad or immoral one
senses.zh: 相信某人做出(尤指坏事或不道德的事) :

senses.en: (not used in the progressive tenses
to be the property of sb; to be owned by sb

ex.en: The house belonged to my cousin.
ex.zh: 这所房子是我表兄的。

ex.en: That land belongs to the golf club.
ex.zh: 那片地归高尔夫俱乐部所有。

senses.en: to be part of a particular group or system
senses.zh: 是(某族类或纲目)的一部份；属于:

ex.en: Rattlesnakes belong to the viper family.
ex.zh: 响尾蛇属于蛇科。

ex.en: These three turtles all belong to one species.
ex.zh: 这三种龟均属同一物种。

senses.en: to drink sth quickly

ex.en: He belted down his beer.
ex.zh: 他把啤酒一饮而尽。

senses.en: ) used to tell sb not very politely to be quiet

ex.en: Belt up, will you?
ex.zh: 你安静点行不行？

senses.en: to lean down

ex.en: He bent down and kissed her on the cheek.
ex.zh: 他低下头吻了她的面颊。

senses.en: to lean over; to bend from the waist

ex.en: Bend over and touch your toes.
ex.zh: 弯下腰触摸你的脚指。

ex.en: He was bending over his desk, writing.
ex.zh: 他正伏案写字。

senses.en: to do everything you can or make a great effort to do sth, especially to help sb
senses.zh: 尽一切努力，竭力(做某事、帮助某人):

ex.en: We bend over backwards to be fair to all the children.
ex.zh: 我们尽力公平对待所有的孩子。

senses.en: to rely on sth or on sb doing sth and expect it to happen
senses.zh: 相信；对…有把握；指望(某人做某事) :

ex.en: ‘Do you think she’ll come?’ ‘I wouldn’t bet on it (= I don’t think it is very likely).
ex.zh: “你觉得她会来吗？”“难说。”

ex.en: Don’t bet on me still being here when you get back!
ex.zh: 别以为你回来的时候我还会在这里！

senses.en: to describe sb/sth in a particular way; to advertise sb/sth as sth

ex.en: Some patients are receiving what has been billed as a revolutionary treatment.
ex.zh: 有些病人正在接受所谓的革命性治疗。

ex.en: The concert was billed as ‘A Night of Magic’.
ex.zh: 这场音乐会被宣传成“魅力之夜”。

senses.en: to warn sb that they will have to appear in court if they break the law again
senses.zh: 令某人具结保证(不再违法):

ex.en: He was bound over to keep the peace.
ex.zh: 他被责令具保不再闹事。

senses.en: to force sb to do sth by making them promise to do it or making it part of a legal document
senses.zh: 迫使(某人)许诺(某事)；(用法律文书)约束:

senses.en: to tie a long thin piece of fabric around sth to protect it

ex.en: She bound up his wounds with bandages.
ex.zh: 她用绷带把他的伤口包扎好。

senses.en: to be very busy with sth;to be very interested or involved in sth

ex.en: He’s too bound up in his work to have much time for his children.
ex.zh: 他工作太忙，没有多少时间留给孩子。

senses.en: closely connected with sth

ex.en: The history of the company is closely bound up with the history of the Grant family.
ex.zh: 公司的历史与克灵顿家族的历史密切相关。

senses.en: to try to bite sth

ex.en: The dog bit at the boy’s hand.
ex.zh: 狗想去咬男孩的手。

senses.en: to react when sb has harmed you and try to harm or criticize them

ex.en: If you criticize him, he’ll bite back.
ex.zh: 你若批评他，他会反驳的。

senses.en: to cut or press into the surface of sth

ex.en: The collar bit into his neck.
ex.zh: 他的衣领勒脖子了。

senses.en: to have an unpleasant effect on sth, especially by making it smaller
senses.zh: 产生不良影响；(尤指)使缩小；压缩:

ex.en: The recession is biting into our profits.
ex.zh: 经济衰退对我们的收益产生负面影响。

senses.en: to cut sth off by biting it

ex.en: She bit off a piece of chocolate.
ex.zh: 她咬下一块巧克力。

ex.en: His finger had been bitten off by a dog.
ex.zh: 他的手指让狗咬了。

senses.en: to shout at sb or speak to them angrily, often for no good reason

ex.en: I only asked him when the work would be finished and he almost bit my head off.
ex.zh: 我只是问了问什么时候能把活干完，他就冲我大喊大叫。

senses.en: to try to do too much or sth that is too difficult for you
senses.zh: 想一口吃成胖子；不自量力:

ex.en: This time he’s bitten off more than he can chew.
ex.zh: 这一次他胃口太大， 难以应付了。

senses.en: to lose consciousness or lose your memory for a short time
senses.zh: 暂时失去知觉(或记忆) ； 晕眩； 昏厥:

ex.en: The pain hit him and he blacked out.
ex.zh: 他疼得昏了过去。

senses.en: a temporary loss of consciousness or of memory
senses.zh: 暂时失去知觉(或记忆)；晕眩:

ex.en: When did you start having these blackouts?
ex.zh: 你何时开始有这些短暂昏厥的？

senses.en: to deliberately forget sth unpleasant
senses.zh: 刻意忘记某事；抹去…的记忆:

ex.en: Your childhood may have been difficult but you can’t just blank it out.
ex.zh: 一个人的童年或许艰难，但不能就从记忆中抹去。

senses.en: to cover sth written or printed, for example, with black ink so that it cannot be read
senses.zh: 把(书写或印刷文字)掩盖，遮盖:

ex.en: All the names in the report had been blanked out.
ex.zh: 报告中所有的名字都已涂掉。

senses.en: to kill sb or remove sth or break it apart violently,for example with a gun, explosives, etc.
senses.zh: 击毙，炸死(某人)；打掉，炸开(某物):

ex.en: They have blasted away the side of this beautiful valley to make a road.
ex.zh: 他们炸掉了这美丽的峡谷的一侧以便修路。

ex.en: ( ) This theory has been blasted away by the new evidence.
ex.zh: 这个理论给新的证据推翻了。

senses.en: [U] the moment when a spacecraft leaves the ground

ex.en: Blast-off will be in 30 seconds.
ex.zh: 离发射时间还有30 秒钟。

senses.en: (in cooking
senses.zh: 烹饪) to add another substance to sth and mix them together把…调入:

ex.en: Heat the butter gently and then blend in a little flour.
ex.zh: 把黄油稍稍加热，然后调入少许麵粉。

senses.en: to make a substance mix with another so that you cannot see where one ends and the other starts

ex.en: Blend the eyeshadow in with your fingers.
ex.zh: 用手指把眼影揉进去。

ex.en: He blended in the charcoal lines to make the picture look softer.
ex.zh: 他加了些炭笔线条使画面显得柔和些。

senses.en: to look or sound so similar to sth that it is difficult for anyone to see or hear it separately

ex.en: The animals can become almost invisible by blending into the long grass.
ex.zh: 这些动物藏在长草中几乎难以辨认。

ex.en: The new development should blend into its surroundings.
ex.zh: 新开发区应该和周围环境协调一致。

senses.en: to become fat; to gain weight
to clear sth from the eyes by blinking (= closing and opening your eyes quickly)
senses.zh: 眨眼分散泪水(或挤掉脏东西):

ex.en: He blinked away a tear.
ex.zh: 他眨掉眼泪。

senses.en: to try to control your tears

ex.en: I found myself blinking back tears during his speech.
ex.zh: 他演讲的时候我觉得我在尽力克制着不流泪。

senses.en: to stop a vehicle from being driven away by parking too close to it
senses.zh: (紧挨着停靠车辆)把某人或另一辆车困住:

ex.en: You’re blocking that Mini in.
ex.zh: 你挡住那辆迷你牌汽车了。

ex.en: Somebody had parked in front of me, blocking me in.
ex.zh: 有人把车停在我前面，把我困住了。

senses.en: to close a road or another place by placing a barrier across it to stop sb/sth going in or coming out

ex.en: The police blocked the street off.
ex.zh: 警察把这条街道封锁了。

ex.en: The pipe had been blocked off to prevent further leaks.
ex.zh: 管道堵上了，以免再渗漏。

senses.en: ) to reserve a period of time for a particular activity

ex.en: Thursday afternoons are blocked off for sports.
ex.zh: 星期四下午定为体育运动时间。

senses.en: to stop light or noise from coming in; to cover or hide sth
senses.zh: 挡住，遮住(光线或声音)；覆盖；隐藏:

ex.en: The trees blocked out much of the sunlight.
ex.zh: 树木挡住了大部份的阳光。

ex.en: ( ) I’m so used to the traffic noise now I just block it out (= I don’t hear it).
ex.zh: 我很适应汽车的噪音，现在不把它当回事了。

senses.en: to avoid remembering sb/sth or thinking about sb/sth, especially sth unpleasant
senses.zh: 刻意忘记，不去想(尤指令人不快的人或事物)；(从脑海中)抹去:

ex.en: He tried to block the incident out of his mind.
ex.zh: 他试图把那件事从记忆中抹去。

senses.en: to fill sth such as a hole completely so that nothing can get through it

ex.en: All the windows had been blocked up.
ex.zh: 所有的窗户都封死了。

senses.en: completely full; not clear

ex.en: I’ve got a blocked-up nose.
ex.zh: 我的鼻子塞住了。

senses.en: to avoid remembering sb/sth or thinking about sb/sth, especially sth unpleasant
senses.zh: 刻意忘记，不去想(尤指令人不快的人或事物):

ex.en: He wanted to blot out the memory.
ex.zh: 他想抹去那段记忆。

senses.en: to stop light or noise coming in; to cover or hide sth
senses.zh: 挡住，遮住(光线或声音)；掩盖； 隐藏:

ex.en: Dark clouds were blotting out the sun.
ex.zh: 乌云渐渐遮住太阳。

senses.en: to be moved or carried away by the force of the wind or by sb’s breath; to move in this way

ex.en: It was so windy the tent nearly blew away!
ex.zh: 风大得把帐篷都快颳走了！

ex.en: A sudden breeze blew his newspaper away.
ex.zh: 突如其来的一阵风颳跑了他的报纸。

senses.en: () to impress sb a lot;to surprise or please sb
senses.zh: 给某人留下深刻印象；使某人惊喜(或高兴):

ex.en: I saw her performance on Broadway last year and it just blew me away.
ex.zh: 我去年在百老汇看过她的演出，印象十分深刻。

senses.en: , , ) to defeat sb easily

ex.en: Mitchell blew away the other runners.
ex.zh: 米切尔轻而易举地赢了其他赛跑选手。

senses.en: to kill sb or remove or destroy sth with explosives or with a gun

ex.en: He threatened to blow us away.
ex.zh: 他威胁说要把我们枪毙。

ex.en: They blew his kneecaps away (= by shooting them).
ex.zh: 他们开枪打碎了他的膝盖。

senses.en: to arrive somewhere where you are not expected

ex.en: Look who’s just blown in!
ex.zh: 看，谁来了！

ex.en: Have you heard who’s just blown into town?
ex.zh: 你听说谁刚到城里来了吗？

senses.en: to impress or surprise sb very much
senses.zh: 给某人留下深刻印象；使某人十分惊愕:

ex.en: When I first heard the song, it blew my socks off.
ex.zh: 我初次听到这首歌时就被深深打动了。

senses.en: to decide not to do sth you should do or were planning to do
senses.zh: 推掉(应该做的事)；取消(原计划):

ex.en: Jessica blew off her classes on Friday afternoon to go shopping.
ex.zh: 杰西卡逃掉了星期五下午的课去逛商店了。

senses.en: to disappoint sb by not meeting them as arranged; to end a relationship with sb

ex.en: We were supposed to go out yesterday, but he blew me off.
ex.zh: 我们说好昨天出去的，可他让我空等了一场。

senses.en: an occasion when a tyre bursts on a vehicle while it is being driven
an occasion when oil or gas suddenly escapes from an oil well
,) a large meal at which people eat too much
to defeat sb easily

ex.en: The home team blew out the Suns by 30 points.
ex.zh: 主队以30 分的优势把太阳队一举打败。

senses.en: to explode; to be destroyed by an explosion

ex.en: The bomb blew up as experts tried to defuse it.
ex.zh: 专家们试图拆除引信时炸弹爆炸了。

ex.en: The car blew up when it hit the wall.
ex.zh: 汽车撞墙后炸毁了。

senses.en: ) an explosion
) an occasion when sb becomes very angry; an argument

ex.en: The tensions between them ended in a big blow-up.
ex.zh: 他们之间的紧张关系最终使他们大吵一场。

senses.en: to kill sb or destroy sth with a bomb or an explosion

ex.en: The hijackers threatened to blow the plane up.
ex.zh: 劫机者威胁说要炸掉飞机。

ex.en: A judge in Italy was blown up by a car bomb last week.
ex.zh: 上个星期一名法官在意大利被汽车炸弹炸死了。

senses.en: to make sth larger

ex.en: What a lovely photo! Why don’t you have it blown up?
ex.zh: 多可爱的照片！你为什么不把它放大呢？

senses.en: [only before noun] that you can fill with air or gas
to lie and pretend in order to deceive sb
to lie and deceive sb in order to get out of a difficult situation,especially when they suspect you are not being honest
senses.zh: (即使受到怀疑) 继续蒙混过关:

ex.en: If he asks any difficult questions, you’ll have to bluff it out.
ex.zh: 他要是出难题，你就只能蒙混了。

ex.en: I know everything so there’s no point trying to bluff it out.
ex.zh: 我什么都知道了，所以不必再蒙骗下去。

senses.en: to deceive sb in order to get sth from them
senses.zh: 哄骗某人交出；从某人处骗得

senses.en: to move about a place in an awkward or uncertain way, knocking into things

ex.en: He blundered about in the dark, feeling for the light switch.
ex.zh: 他摸黑撞来撞去找电灯开关。

ex.en: I blundered around the flat, trying to be quiet.
ex.zh: 我在公寓里磕磕绊绊，尽力保持安静。

senses.en: to walk into sb/sth because you are awkward or unable to see

ex.en: She blundered into a tree.
ex.zh: 她撞到了一棵树上。

senses.en: to accidentally find yourself in a difficult or dangerous place or situation

ex.en: She blundered into a dangerous area of the city after losing her way.
ex.zh: 她迷路之后不知怎么就到了城市的危险地带。

ex.en: He had innocently blundered into a private dispute.
ex.zh: 他稀里煳涂地卷入了一场私人纠纷。

senses.en: to say sth suddenly and without thinking carefully

ex.en: ‘There’s been an accident,’ she blurted out.
ex.zh: “出事了。”她脱口而出。

ex.en: He found himself blurting out the whole story to her.
ex.zh: 他随口就把这件事全告诉了她。

senses.en: to cover a window or a door with boards

ex.en: All the windows had been boarded up.
ex.zh: 所有的窗户都用木板钉上了。

senses.en: to come to the surface quickly

ex.en: She dived in and bobbed up a few seconds later in the middle of the pool.
ex.zh: 她潜入水中，几秒钟后在游泳池中央猛地钻出水面。

senses.en: to appear suddenly

ex.en: She bobbed up from behind the fence.
ex.zh: 她突然从篱笆后面钻出来。

senses.en: to be unable to make progress

ex.en: The bill bogged down after being passed by Congress.
ex.zh: 议案在国会通过之后很难推行。

senses.en: to be/get stuck in mud or wet ground; to become stuck in sth and unable to make progress
senses.zh: 陷进烂泥(或泥沼)；受到阻碍；无法前进:

ex.en: The car got bogged down in the mud.
ex.zh: 汽车陷入了烂泥中。

senses.en: to be unable to make progress in an activity

ex.en: Don’t get bogged down in details.
ex.zh: 不要拘泥于细节问题。

ex.en: I’m rather bogged down (with work) at the moment.
ex.zh: 我现在被(工作)拖住了。

senses.en: used to tell sb rudely to go away

ex.en: Bog off, I’m trying to sleep!
ex.zh: 一边去，我要睡觉！

senses.en: to make a liquid less in quantity by boiling it
to heat a liquid or some food until it boils

ex.en: I’ll boil the kettle up again and we’ll have a cup of tea.
ex.zh: 我烧壶开水，咱们泡茶喝。

senses.en: to confuse or change sth; to spoil sth
to support or encourage sb;to make sth better or stronger
senses.zh: 支持，鼓励(某人)；改善，加强(某事物):

ex.en: He tried to bolster up their morale.
ex.zh: 他尽力鼓舞他们的士气。

ex.en: The high interest rates helped to bolster up the economy.
ex.zh: 高利率使经济更稳健。

senses.en: to eat sth very quickly

ex.en: I had to bolt down my breakfast.
ex.zh: 我只好匆匆吃完早饭。

senses.en: to move very fast, usually in a vehicle
to fail very badly

ex.en: The movie bombed out at the box office.
ex.zh: 这部电影一点儿也不卖座。

senses.en: to study sth; to look again at sth you already know

ex.en: I must bone up on my French before we go to Paris.
ex.zh: 我们去巴黎之前我一定得把法语捡起来。

senses.en: to arrive at a hotel and arrange to have a room

ex.en: They booked in (at the St Francis Hotel) using a false name.
ex.zh: 他们(在圣富兰西斯旅馆)用假名办理了住宿手续。

ex.en: She booked into a hotel in the centre of Boston.
ex.zh: 她在波士顿市中心的一家旅馆办理了住宿手续。

senses.en: to reserve a room at a hotel,etc. for sb
senses.zh: 为别人(或自己)预订(旅馆房间等):

ex.en: I’ve booked us in at the Plaza.
ex.zh: 我在广场大酒店预订了房间。

ex.en: The hotel I was booked into was awful.
ex.zh: 我预订的那家旅馆很糟糕。

senses.en: to reserve a place, for example on a trip or a course

ex.en: I booked up for the course months in advance.
ex.zh: 我提前几个月就报名要听这门课了。

senses.en: to say sth in a loud deep voice

ex.en: She boomed out instructions through a loudhailer.
ex.zh: 她用扩音器深沉有力地发出指示。

ex.en: A voice boomed out:‘Nobody move!’
ex.zh: 有人低沉地说：“全都不许动！”

senses.en: to force sb to leave a place, job,school, club, etc.
senses.zh: 迫使某人离开(处所、工作、学校等)；赶走；解雇；开除:

ex.en: I’ll have to boot you out soon — I want to lock up.
ex.zh: 过会儿我就得赶你走了─ 我想关门了。

ex.en: The manager booted him out of the team.
ex.zh: 经理把他赶出这个队。

senses.en: to share a border with another country or region; to be next to a place
senses.zh: 与(另一个国家或地区)接壤；挨着:

ex.en: Many states bordering on the EU are eager to join.
ex.zh: 多个和欧盟接壤的国家急于加入。

ex.en: Their garden borders on the River Severn.
ex.zh: 他们的园子在塞文河沿岸。

senses.en: to come close to being sth

ex.en: Her self-confidence borders on arrogance.
ex.zh: 她自信得近乎傲慢。

ex.en: Our task borders on the impossible.
ex.zh: 我们的任务几乎难以完成。

senses.en: to tell sb what to do in a forceful or unpleasant way

ex.en: He’s always bossing his wife around.
ex.zh: 他总是对妻子指手画脚。

senses.en: to spoil sth by doing it badly; to do sth badly
senses.zh: 把东西弄坏；把事情搞糟:

ex.en: Instead of fixing my computer, he’s botched it up completely.
ex.zh: 他不但没有修好我的计算机，反而把它彻底弄坏了。

senses.en: a piece of work that is badly done
senses.zh: 搞坏了的东西；办砸了的事

senses.en: to suddenly decide not to do sth because you are too frightened
senses.zh: (因恐惧而)突然放弃原打算；临阵退缩:

ex.en: I bottled out of phoning him at the last minute.
ex.zh: 我在最后时刻决定不敢给他打电话。

senses.en: to keep your feelings, especially sadness or anger, hidden and not tell other people how you are feeling

ex.en: Tell someone how you’re feeling, instead of bottling it all up.
ex.zh: 找人说说你的感受，不要一味地压抑自己。

senses.en: to discuss sth with other people

ex.en: We’re bouncing some new ideas around.
ex.zh: 我们正在讨论一些新想法。

senses.en: () to recover well after you have been ill/sick or had a difficult time
senses.zh: 恢复健康； 重整旗鼓:

ex.en: No matter what happens, she always bounces back very quickly.
ex.zh: 无论发生什么事，她总能很快地振作起来。

senses.en: to make or force sb to do sth quickly without giving them time to think about it

ex.en: I felt I’d been bounced into supporting a proposal I didn’t really agree with.
ex.zh: 我觉得迫于压力才支持了一项自己并非真正同意的提案。

senses.en: [NOTE]This phrasal verb is often used in the passive.
senses.zh: 这个短语动词常用于被动语态。

senses.en: to tell sb else your ideas to find out what they think about them
senses.zh: (把想法)告诉(某人以试探其反应):

ex.en: We were able to share problems and bounce ideas off each other.
ex.zh: 我们能够共同探讨问题并相互交流思想。

senses.en: to stop doing an activity or a job that you have been doing successfully,often for a long time
senses.zh: 退出，告别(成功的事业等):

ex.en: After thirty years in politics, he feels it is time to bow out.
ex.zh: 从政三十年之后，他觉得是时候退出政坛了。

ex.en: Smith will bow out of professional football at the end of the season.
ex.zh: 史密斯将于本赛季末告别职业足球。

senses.en: to agree unwillingly to do sth or to accept sth that sb else wants you to
senses.zh: 勉强同意做(或接受某事)；屈从于:

ex.en: The government eventually bowed to public pressure.
ex.zh: 政府终于在公众的压力下让步了。

senses.en: to surprise or impress sb a lot; to affect sb deeply
senses.zh: 使某人惊叹；让某人印象深刻；深刻影响:

ex.en: We were bowled over by the news.
ex.zh: 我们对这个消息感到震惊。

ex.en: Philip bowled us all over by deciding to go into advertising.
ex.zh: 菲利普决定从事广告业，让我们全都大为吃惊。

senses.en: to prevent sb from doing what they want, especially by creating rules or other difficulties
senses.zh: 给某人设框框；使窒碍难行:

ex.en: The President was unable to act because the Democrats were boxing him in.
ex.zh: 总统受到民主党的阻拦无法展开工作。

ex.en: She was boxed in by rules and regulations.
ex.zh: 她给规章制度框住了脚。

senses.en: to prevent a person or a vehicle from moving by surrounding them/it with other people or vehicles

ex.en: You can’t park here — you’re boxing that car in!
ex.zh: 你不能在这里停车─ 你挡了那辆车的路！

ex.en: He couldn’t overtake the leader because he was boxed in by the other runners.
ex.zh: 他没法超过领先的人，因为其他赛跑运动员把他的路堵住了。

senses.en: to put sth in a box or boxes

ex.en: She boxed up all the old baby clothes to send to her niece.
ex.zh: 她把所有的旧婴儿服都装箱寄给姪女。

senses.en: to begin to do a new job or an activity that you do not usually do
senses.zh: 涉足新工作；拓展新业务:

ex.en: The company is branching out into Europe.
ex.zh: 公司正在开拓欧洲业务。

senses.en: to behave in a confident way as if you are not ashamed or embarrassed about sth you have done, even though you should be
[sing.] an act of separating from a larger group/state, etc.
to lose control of your feelings and start crying

ex.en: As she drove away, I just broke down and wept.
ex.zh: 她开车离开时， 我不禁失声痛哭。

senses.en: [C] an occasion when a vehicle or a machine stops working
senses.zh: (车辆或机器的)故障， 损坏:

ex.en: We had a breakdown on the way home.
ex.zh: 我们的车在回家的路上抛锚了。

ex.en: a breakdown truck
ex.zh: 救险车

senses.en: [C] [U] a failure of talks, a marriage, law and order, etc.
senses.zh: (谈判、婚姻的)破裂，失败；(治安的)瘫痪:

ex.en: a breakdown in communication
ex.zh: 通信中断

ex.en: They were both responsible for the breakdown of their marriage.
ex.zh: 他们双方对婚姻的破裂都负有责任。

senses.en: [C]a period of mental illness when sb becomes tired, depressed and unable to lead a normal life
[C,usually sing.] detailed information or figures that are the results of dividing sth into its parts to explain it more clearly

ex.en: Get me a breakdown of how the money was spent.
ex.zh: 给我看一下这笔钱使用情况的细目。

senses.en: [U] the act of dividing a substance into its parts in a chemical process
[usually before noun]
(of a vehicle or a machine
senses.zh: 车辆或机器) not working 抛锚的；出故障的:

ex.en: a broken-down car
ex.zh: 抛锚的汽车

senses.en: in a poor condition

ex.en: a broken-down wall
ex.zh: 剥落的墙壁

senses.en: to destroy or remove sth,especially a problem or an attitude or opinion that sb has
senses.zh: 破除，消除(尤指问题、思想等):

senses.en: to enter a building illegally or by force
senses.zh: 非法(或强行)进入；破门而入:

ex.en: Somebody broke in last night and stole the PC and video.
ex.zh: 昨晚有人闯进屋里偷走了电脑和录像机。

ex.en: The firefighters had to break in to rescue them.
ex.zh: 消防队员得破门而入营救他们。

senses.en: an entry into a building using force, usually illegally
senses.zh: 破门而入；闯入；(非法的)强行进入:

ex.en: There has been a series of breakins in the area.
ex.zh: 这个地区发生了一连串的闯入房屋案。

senses.en: to train a person so that they get used to a new job or situation; to train a horse so that you can ride it
senses.zh: 让新来者适应(新工作或环境)；训练(马匹) :

ex.en: We try to break newcomers in gently.
ex.zh: 我们尝试让新来者慢慢融入整体。

ex.en: The horses hadn’t been broken in.
ex.zh: 那些马还没训练好。

senses.en: ) (in the past) to prepare the engine of a new car for normal use by driving it slowly and carefully
to enter a building, open a car,etc. illegally and by force

ex.en: A thief can break into a car in under ten seconds.
ex.zh: 窃贼十秒钟之内就能把车撬开。

ex.en: Three houses in our street have been broken into this week.
ex.zh: 我们这条街本周有三家被盗。

senses.en: to stop speaking or stop doing sth suddenly before you have finished

ex.en: He broke off abruptly in the middle of a sentence.
ex.zh: 他一句话说了一半就突然停住口。

ex.en: We had to break off our holiday and return home immediately.
ex.zh: 我们不得不中止休假立刻回家。

senses.en: to end sth such as a relationship

ex.en: They’ve broken off their engagement.
ex.zh: 他们解除了婚约。

ex.en: Britain threatened to break off diplomatic relations.
ex.zh: 英国威胁说要断绝外交关系。

senses.en: an escape from prison
the start of sth or the sudden appearance of sth unpleasant or violent
senses.zh: 爆发；突然发生；突然出现:

ex.en: the outbreak of war
ex.zh: 战争的爆发

ex.en: an outbreak of food poisoning
ex.zh: 食物中毒事件

senses.en: to get sth ready to be used, eaten,drunk, etc.
senses.zh: 预备好，准备好(用品、食物、饮料等):

ex.en: That’s wonderful news! Let’s break out the champagne!
ex.zh: 真是个好消息！咱们准备香槟酒吧！

senses.en: to suddenly become covered in sth such as sweat

ex.en: He broke out in a cold sweat at the thought of the trial.
ex.zh: 他一想到审判就冒出一身冷汗。

ex.en: My skin has broken out in an itchy rash.
ex.zh: 我的皮肤上突然长出一片让人发痒的皮疹。

senses.en: to achieve your first important success in sth; to make an important or new discovery
senses.zh: 获得初次重要成功； 作出新的重大发现； 突破:

ex.en: Glenn Close broke through as a star with ‘Fatal Attraction’.
ex.zh: 格伦·克洛斯因影片《致命的诱惑》崭露头角成为明星。

ex.en: Scientists believe they have broken through in their fight against the disease.
ex.zh: 科学家认为他们在对抗这一疾病的研究中已经有所突破。

senses.en: an important discovery or development; sb’s first important success in sth
senses.zh: 重大发现(或进展)；突破；初次重要成功:

ex.en: an important breakthrough in the negotiations
ex.zh: 谈判中的重大突破

ex.en: Jo was only 19 when he got his breakthrough as a DJ.
ex.zh: 乔作为流行音乐节目主持人崭露头角的时候只有19岁。

senses.en: to make a way through a barrier using force

ex.en: He ran towards the barrier in an attempt to break through.
ex.zh: 他向栅栏冲去，想把它撞破。

ex.en: Demonstrators tried to break through the police cordon.
ex.zh: 示威群众试图冲破警方的封锁线。

senses.en: to end a relationship with sb

ex.en: Rob and I broke up last week.
ex.zh: 我和罗布上个星期吹了。

ex.en: She’s just broken up with her boyfriend.
ex.zh: 她刚刚和男朋友分手。

senses.en: [C] [U] the ending of a marriage or a relationship

ex.en: He moved away after the break-up of his marriage.
ex.zh: 他离婚之后就搬走了。

ex.en: marriage break-up
ex.zh: 婚姻破裂

senses.en: to make sth that is rather boring,such as a period of time or a pattern, more interesting by adding sth different to it
senses.zh: 给(乏味的事物)增添趣味；调剂(生活等):

ex.en: I break up my day by going for a walk in the afternoon.
ex.zh: 我下午散步，调节一天的生活。

ex.en: Drawings were used to break up the page.
ex.zh: 页面用了插画。

senses.en: to end your connection or relationship with sb/sth because you no longer agree with them
senses.zh: (因分歧)离开某人，离开某事物；终止与…的关系:

ex.en: Nick broke with his father to set up his own firm.
ex.zh: 尼克不再跟着父亲，办起自己的公司。

senses.en: to reject sth such as a tradition or the past and decide to do sth different

ex.en: The prince broke with tradition by going to study abroad.
ex.zh: 王子破除传统去国外读书。

ex.en: The new directors are eager to break with the past.
ex.zh: 新董事们急于废除过去的东西。

senses.en: to take air into your lungs through your nose or mouth

ex.en: Breathe in through your nose as you stretch up.
ex.zh: 举起手臂时用鼻子吸气。

ex.en: He breathed in deeply and then spoke.
ex.zh: 他深吸一口气之后开始讲话。

senses.en: to fill sth with life, energy or enthusiasm
to send air out of your lungs through your nose or mouth

ex.en: Breathe out slowly through your mouth as you stand up.
ex.zh: 站起时用口慢慢呼气。

senses.en: to arrive somewhere or enter a place in a casual,cheerful and confident way
senses.zh: 轻盈而自信地走(到某处)；飘然而至:

ex.en: She breezed in at eleven and greeted everyone with a smile.
ex.zh: 十一点时她一阵风似的飘进来，向大家微笑。

ex.en: He breezed into the office and announced he was leaving.
ex.zh: 他潇洒自如地走进办公室宣布他要走了。

senses.en: to succeed in doing sth very easily

ex.en: She breezed through the first exam.
ex.zh: 她轻松地通过了第一次考试。

senses.en: to prepare a hot drink of tea or coffee

ex.en: Come into the kitchen while I brew up.
ex.zh: 我煮咖啡时你到厨房来吧。

ex.en: I’ll brew up a fresh pot of tea when they arrive.
ex.zh: 他们到来时我来沏壶新茶。

senses.en: an act of making a drink of tea; the drink that you make
senses.zh: 沏茶；沏好的茶；煮好的咖啡

senses.en: to fill in or block an opening with bricks

ex.en: The fireplace had been bricked in some years before.
ex.zh: 壁炉几年前用砖封上了。

ex.en: Somebody had bricked up all the doors and windows.
ex.zh: 有人把所有的门窗用砖堵住了。

senses.en: to make sth more interesting,exciting or attractive
senses.zh: 使更加有趣(或令人兴奋、有吸引力):

ex.en: I’ve brought some flowers to brighten the place up a bit.
ex.zh: 我带来一些花，把这里装点一下。

ex.en: Brighten up your bedroom with a few posters.
ex.zh: 挂几张印刷画让你的寝室亮丽生色。

senses.en: to make sth happen

ex.en: What has brought about this change?
ex.zh: 是什么引起了这一转变？

ex.en: His nervous breakdown was brought about by stress.
ex.zh: 他神经崩溃是压力所致。

senses.en: to bring sb/sth somewhere with you

ex.en: Can I bring my sister along to the party?
ex.zh: 我能带妹妹来参加聚会吗？

ex.en: She brought some CDs along.
ex.zh: 她随身带了些激光唱片。

senses.en: to return sb to a place;to take sb home
senses.zh: 把某人送回(某处)；送某人回家:

ex.en: I’ll bring you back again after the party.
ex.zh: 聚会结束后我再把你送回去。

ex.en: She tried to bring him back (= to make him return) to the matter in hand.
ex.zh: 她尽量让他回到手头的事情上来。

senses.en: to put sb back in their old job or position
senses.zh: 恢复某人的工作(或职位):

ex.en: United have brought back their old manager.
ex.zh: 联队重新起用从前的经理。

senses.en: to present sb for judgement; to present sth to sb/sth for discussion or a decision
senses.zh: 把某人提交法庭审判；将…提交讨论:

ex.en: Children should not be brought before a court.
ex.zh: 不应该让儿童在法庭受审。

ex.en: The case was brought before the judge.
ex.zh: 这个案子提交给了法官审理。

senses.en: to depress sb; to make sb unhappy

ex.en: Spending New Year alone brought me right down.
ex.zh: 独自一人过新年让我闷闷不乐。

senses.en: to take sb/sth from a higher to a lower level
senses.zh: 使下落； 使降低位置:

ex.en: They brought all the boxes down from the attic.
ex.zh: 他们从阁楼搬下了所有箱子。

senses.en: to make sb/sth fall to the ground

ex.en: He was brought down in the penalty area.
ex.zh: 他在罚球区被撞倒。

ex.en: Their plane was brought down by a violent storm.
ex.zh: 他们的飞机遇到强烈风暴坠毁了。

senses.en: to make a government,a leader, etc. lose power or be defeated
senses.zh: 使(政府、领导人等)倒台；打倒:

ex.en: The scandal brought the government down.
ex.zh: 这件丑闻导致了政府垮台。

senses.en: to make sth unpleasant happen to sb as a result of your actions
senses.zh: 给某人带来(不愉快的事)；给某人招惹某事；连累:

ex.en: He had brought nothing but trouble down on the family.
ex.zh: 他尽给家里添乱。

senses.en: to finish or mark the end of sth
senses.zh: 落下帷幕；结束；标志着…的终结:

ex.en: Her decision to retire brought down the curtain on a glittering 30-year career.
ex.zh: 她退休的决定给她30 年辉煌的职业生涯画上了句号。

senses.en: to give birth to sb

ex.en: She brought forth a son.
ex.zh: 她生了个儿子。

senses.en: to move sth to an earlier date or time

ex.en: We’ll have to bring the date of the final game forward.
ex.zh: 我们得把决赛日期提前。

senses.en: to suggest a subject, an idea, etc. for discussion

ex.en: She brought forward proposals for a new school building.
ex.zh: 她提出了建新校舍的建议。

senses.en: () to move a total from the bottom of one page or column of numbers to the top of the next page
senses.zh: 把账目转入次页；转下页

senses.en: to make or earn money for sb

ex.en: How much is she bringing in every month?
ex.zh: 她每月挣多少钱？

ex.en: His job only brought him in a small income.
ex.zh: 他的工作收入微薄。

senses.en: to take sb/sth into a room, a house, an office, etc.

ex.en: Could you bring in another chair?
ex.zh: 请再搬张椅子进来好吗？

ex.en: Bring him in!
ex.zh: 把他带进来！

senses.en: to attract sb/sth to a place or a business

ex.en: The visitor centre is bringing in more and more people.
ex.zh: 游客中心吸引着越来越多的人。

senses.en: to mention or include sth

ex.en: She brought in other evidence to support her argument.
ex.zh: 她引用其他证据来支持她的论点。

senses.en: to take sb/sth into a place

ex.en: Bring that chair into the dining room.
ex.zh: 把那张椅子搬到餐厅吧。

senses.en: to include or mention sb/sth in a discussion, conversation,etc.
senses.zh: 将…包括在(讨论、谈话等)中；让某人参加；提及:

ex.en: Why do you always have to bring Pete into it (= mention Pete when we are discussing sth)?
ex.zh: 你怎么张口闭口就是皮特？

ex.en: I knew you’d manage to bring football into the conversation!
ex.zh: 我就知道你最后会把话题转到足球上的！

senses.en: to attract sb/sth to a place or business

ex.en: The advertising campaign should bring more people into the bookshops.
ex.zh: 这场广告运动将会吸引更多的人去书店的。

senses.en: to manage to do sth difficult successfully
to help sb to develop or improve when they are learning to do sth
senses.zh: 帮助(学习者)进步；提高(学习者)的水平:

ex.en: We need to bring on the young players quickly.
ex.zh: 我们得帮年轻队员赶快提高水平。

ex.en: There’s no time to bring employees along gradually.
ex.zh: 没有时间按部就班地培训雇员。

senses.en: to be responsible for sth unpleasant that happens to sb/yourself

ex.en: You’ve brought shame on the whole family!
ex.zh: 你使全家人蒙羞！

ex.en: Don’t blame me! You’ve brought this on yourself.
ex.zh: 别埋怨我！这都怪你自己。

senses.en: to help sb to be more confident and less shy

ex.en: He’s good at bringing out nervous interviewees.
ex.zh: 他善于帮助接受面试的人克服紧张心理。

senses.en: to produce or publish sth

ex.en: They’re bringing out a new sports car this year.
ex.zh: 他们今年要推出一款新跑车。

ex.en: How many albums have the band brought out?
ex.zh: 这个乐队出了多少张专辑？

senses.en: to make a particular quality easier to see, taste,or notice

ex.en: That dress brings out the colour of your eyes.
ex.zh: 那件连衣裙衬托出你眼睛的颜色。

senses.en: to make sb’s skin be covered in sth such as sweat or spots

ex.en: Tomatoes bring me out in a rash.
ex.zh: 我吃西红柿过敏。

senses.en: to take or bring sb/sth to a particular place, especially sb’s home

ex.en: When your sister gets back from New York, bring her over to see us.
ex.zh: 你妹妹从纽约回来就带她来看看我们吧。

ex.en: Bring your chair over and sit with us!
ex.zh: 把椅子搬过来和我们一块儿坐！

senses.en: to bring sb/sth to sb’s home

ex.en: I’ll bring the papers round to your house this evening.
ex.zh: 我今晚把文件送到你家。

senses.en: to direct a conversation,a discussion, etc. so that you are talking about the subject you want to talk about

ex.en: He always brings the conversation round to football.
ex.zh: 他总是把话题转到足球上。

senses.en: to help two people or groups to end a quarrel; to unite two people or groups
senses.zh: 使双方言和；使和好如初；使团结:

ex.en: The crisis brought the family closer together.
ex.zh: 这场危机使一家人关系更融洽。

senses.en: to introduce two people who have never met; to help two people come together socially
senses.zh: 介绍两人认识；让两人交往:

ex.en: It was me who brought them together.
ex.zh: 是我给他们牵的线。

senses.en: to collect a group of people or objects together in one place

ex.en: This exhibition brings together many artists’ work.
ex.zh: 展览会汇集了多位艺术家的作品。

senses.en: to care for a child until he or she is grown up

ex.en: She was brought up by her aunt.
ex.zh: 她是由姨妈带大的。

ex.en: I was brought up (=I grew up) on a farm.
ex.zh: 我是在农场长大的。

senses.en: to teach your child a particular way to behave, etc.

ex.en: They brought their children up very strictly.
ex.zh: 他们对孩子的家桝很严。

ex.en: We were brought up to be polite and do what we were told.
ex.zh: 从小家里就要求我们讲礼貌和听话。

senses.en: [sing.] [U] the way in which a child is cared for and taught, especially by parents,while he or she is growing up
to move sb/sth to a higher place, especially up the stairs
senses.zh: 将…带(或移)到(较高的位置，尤指楼上)；举起；抬起:

ex.en: Breakfast was brought up to our room.
ex.zh: 早餐送到了我们的房间。

ex.en: Callum is downstairs. Shall I bring him up?
ex.zh: 卡勒姆在楼下。要不要把他带上来？

senses.en: to make sth appear on a computer screen
senses.zh: 使显示在计算机屏幕上；调出:

ex.en: Can you bring that file up on screen?
ex.zh: 你把文件调出来好吗？

senses.en: to make sb realize sth or face sth and deal with it

ex.en: This case brings us up against the problem of punishment in schools.
ex.zh: 这件事使我们直面学校体罚的问题。

senses.en: to help sb/sth to reach an acceptable level or standard

ex.en: They have now brought the football ground up to the required safety standards.
ex.zh: 他们现在把足球场修整得符合规定的安全标准了。

senses.en: to be covered in sth; to have or contain a large number or amount of sth

ex.en: a roof bristling with TV aerials
ex.zh: 布满电视天线的楼顶

ex.en: The staff bristle with efficiency.
ex.zh: 全体职员工作效率很高。

senses.en: to look through a book, a magazine, etc. in a casual way, without reading everything

ex.en: She browsed through the newspaper while she waited.
ex.zh: 她一边等一边翻阅报纸。

senses.en: to touch sb/sth lightly when you move close to them/it

ex.en: A cat brushed against his leg.
ex.zh: 一只猫蹭了他的腿。

ex.en: He brushed by/past me and ran out.
ex.zh: 他和我擦肩而过，跑了出去。

senses.en: to push sb/sth to one side
senses.zh: 把某人(或某物) 推到一边:

ex.en: She brushed a strand of hair aside.
ex.zh: 她把一缕头发抹到耳旁。

senses.en: to refuse to listen to sb/sth or treat them/it as important

ex.en: He brushed my protests aside and paid the bill.
ex.zh: 他不理会我的反对把账结了。

ex.en: Every time I try to explain, you brush me aside.
ex.zh: 每次我要解释，你都不理我。

senses.en: to remove sth from a surface with a brush, your hand, etc.

ex.en: She brushed a stray hair away from her face.
ex.zh: 她拂开脸上的一缕散发。

senses.en: to clean sb/yourself by brushing their/your clothes with your hand, especially after they/you have fallen
senses.zh: 掸乾净某人/自己(尤指摔跤后拂去衣服上的灰尘) :

ex.en: She stood up and brushed herself down.
ex.zh: 她站起来把身上的灰尘拍掉。

senses.en: to clean sth by brushing it thoroughly

ex.en: Brush your coat down to get the mud off.
ex.zh: 把你外套上的泥刷乾净。

ex.en: The children were taught how to brush down their ponies.
ex.zh: 有人桝孩子们如何把他们的小马刷乾净。

senses.en: to refuse to listen to sb; to ignore sb in a rude or unkind way

ex.en: He tried to explain to her, but she brushed him off impatiently.
ex.zh: 他试图向她解释，可她不耐烦地不搭理他。

senses.en: rude or unkind behaviour that shows you do not want to be friendly

ex.en: to give sb the brush-off
ex.zh: 不理睬某人

senses.en: to clean sb/yourself by brushing their/your clothes quickly with your hand
senses.zh: 掸净某人/自己(拂去衣服上的灰尘)

senses.en: to brush sth, especially hair,thoroughly to remove knots or to make it straighter

ex.en: She brushed out her hair, washed her face and got into bed.
ex.zh: 她把头发梳开，洗脸，然后上床了。

senses.en: to study or practise sth in order to get back the skill or knowledge that you had in the past but have not used for some time
senses.zh: 重温，复习(生疏了的技术或知识):

ex.en: I need to brush up my computer skills.
ex.zh: 我需要捡起我的计算机技术。

ex.en: You should brush up on your French before you go to France.
ex.zh: 你去法国之前得温习一下法语。

senses.en: to be full of excitement,enthusiasm, ideas, etc.
senses.zh: 充满，充溢着(兴奋、热情、某想法等) :

ex.en: They were bubbling over with excitement.
ex.zh: 他们兴奋不已。

senses.en: used to tell sb to hurry up

ex.en: Buck up! We’ll be late.
ex.zh: 快点！我们要迟到了。

senses.en: to become, or to make sb, more cheerful

ex.en: Buck up! There’s no school tomorrow!
ex.zh: 高兴点！ 明天不用上学了！

ex.en: He bucked up when I said he could go.
ex.zh: 我说他可以走了，他便来了精神。

senses.en: to start behaving in a more acceptable way, so that work gets done better, etc.
to rain heavily

ex.en: It bucketed down all day.
ex.zh: 大雨下了一整天。

senses.en: to start working or doing sth in a serious or determined way

ex.en: He tried to buckle down to some work/study.
ex.zh: 他努力静下心来认真工作/学习。

senses.en: to become friendly with sb or work closely with another person

ex.en: She buddied up to Laura, hoping to get to know her brother.
ex.zh: 她和劳拉来往， 希望结识她的哥哥。

ex.en: I asked to get buddied up with an experienced diver.
ex.zh: 我要求和有经验的潜水员搭档。

senses.en: to move up; to make more room for sb else

ex.en: Budge up a bit! I’d like to sit down too.
ex.zh: 动动身！我也想坐下。

senses.en: to plan to save or provide an amount of money for a particular purpose
senses.zh: 预先计划…所需的费用；预算…的费用:

ex.en: Don’t forget to budget for the cost of textbooks.
ex.zh: 别忘了划出课本的费用。

senses.en: to leave in a hurry

ex.en: I picked up my pay and then bugged out.
ex.zh: 我领了工资就赶快离开。

senses.en: to waste time doing stupid or unimportant things; to behave in a silly way

ex.en: Stop buggering about and let’s get on with it.
ex.zh: 别晃荡了，我们继续干正事吧。

senses.en: to go away

ex.en: Bugger off and leave me alone.
ex.zh: 走开，别管我。

ex.en: Clive’s buggered off to the pub with Julie.
ex.zh: 克莱夫和朱莉去酒馆了。

senses.en: to spoil sth; to do sth badly

ex.en: I’m not going to let her bugger things up for me.
ex.zh: 我不会让她把我的事情搞糟。

senses.en: to create sth, basing it on a particular thing, person, idea, etc.

ex.en: The story is built around the adventures of 12 knights.
ex.zh: 故事围绕着12位骑士的历险展开。

senses.en: to make sth a fixed and permanent part of a system, a plan,etc.
senses.zh: 使…成为(体系、计划等的)组成部份:

ex.en: Safeguards against fraud are built into the system.
ex.zh: 该系统设置了防伪措施。

senses.en: to make sth a fixed and permanent part of sth larger
senses.zh: 把…建造在…里；使…固定(于较大的物件):

ex.en: The flash is built into the camera.
ex.zh: 闪光灯在照相机里。

ex.en: This dishwasher can be built in.
ex.zh: 这款洗碗机可以是嵌入式的。

senses.en: [only before noun] forming a fixed part of a larger structure
senses.zh: 固定在…中的；内置的；嵌入式的:

ex.en: a built-in cupboard
ex.zh: 壁橱

ex.en: The camera has a builtin flash.
ex.zh: 这架照相机有内置闪光灯。

senses.en: [only before noun] existing as an essential part of sth/sb

ex.en: the inbuilt survival instinct of animals
ex.zh: 动物与生俱来的生存本能

senses.en: to develop further from sth that you have already achieved

ex.en: We need to build on last year’s success.
ex.zh: 我们要在去年成功的基础上努力。

ex.en: This course builds on existing skills.
ex.zh: 这门课需要以所掌握的技能为基础。

senses.en: to add sth such as an extra room to an existing building

ex.en: They had built on a large extension at the back of the house.
ex.zh: 他们在房子后部进行了大规模扩建。

senses.en: to become greater, stronger or larger in number

ex.en: Queues of traffic are building up after the accident.
ex.zh: 车祸之后来往车辆排起的长龙越来越长。

ex.en: I could feel the anger building up inside me.
ex.zh: 我感觉到心头火起。

senses.en: [sing.] [U] an increase in the amount, strength or number of sth
senses.zh: 增长； 增加； 增强:

ex.en: a build-up of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere
ex.zh: 大气中二氧化碳的增加

senses.en: to gradually prepare yourself for sth such as a race or competition

ex.en: Start gently and build up to the more strenuous exercises.
ex.zh: 开始时慢点，逐渐过渡到较强的锻炼。

ex.en: Build up slowly until you can jog for 30 minutes.
ex.zh: 慢慢地增加时间，直到能跑上30 分钟。

senses.en: to make sb healthier or stronger
senses.zh: 增强…的体质；使更加强壮:

ex.en: She gave me lots of vitamins and minerals to build me up.
ex.zh: 她让我服用很多维生素和矿物质以使我更健康。

senses.en: to speak about sb/sth with great enthusiasm, often praising them more than they deserve
[usually before noun]
covered with many houses or buildings

ex.en: The speed limit is lower in built-up areas.
ex.zh: 在楼房林立的地区最高限速要低一些。

senses.en: built-up shoes, boots, or heels have extra height added
senses.zh: (鞋子、靴子、鞋跟)增高的；(后跟)埝高的

senses.en: to increase in size or weight; to make sb/sth increase in size or weight

ex.en: Griswold had bulked up for this match and won easily.
ex.zh: 格里斯沃尔德为这次比赛增加了体重，结果轻松地赢了。

ex.en: Local businesses are helping to bulk up school computer labs (= provide more computers).
