ex.zh: 当地企业纷纷帮助学校扩充电脑室。

senses.en: to force sb to do sth by frightening them or threatening them

ex.en: You can’t bully me into saying anything!
ex.zh: 你休想逼我说出一个字！

senses.en: to travel around or to spend your time doing nothing in particular
senses.zh: 浪游；闲荡；无所事事；游手好闲

senses.en: to travel somewhere with no particular plans

ex.en: After I left school, I bummed around the world for a year.
ex.zh: 我从学校毕业后，花了一年的时间四海飘游。

senses.en: to annoy sb

ex.en: I was really bummed out that there were no tickets left.
ex.zh: 没有票了，我非常恼火。

senses.en: to move around in an awkward and noisy way
senses.zh: 笨手笨脚地走动；(在…)跌跌撞撞:

ex.en: I could hear my father bumbling about downstairs.
ex.zh: 我听见父亲在楼下跌跌撞撞地忙活着。

ex.en: a film of two sisters bumbling around their home, making tea
ex.zh: 一部关于两姐妹满屋子瞎折腾着泡茶的电影

senses.en: to meet sb by chance

ex.en: I bumped into an old friend in town today.
ex.zh: 我今天在城里遇见一个老朋友。

senses.en: to murder sb

ex.en: He admitted bumping off Baines.
ex.zh: 他承认杀了贝恩斯。

senses.en: to not allow sb to have the seat on a plane that they have booked, because seats have been sold to more people than the plane will carry
senses.zh: (因航班超员)取消某人的座位:

senses.en: These phrasal verbs are usually used in the passive.
senses.zh: 这些短语动词通常用于被动语态:

ex.en: I was worried about being bumped off the flight.
ex.zh: 我担心被取消航班座位。

senses.en: to move sb to a more expensive seat in a plane without charging them extra, because there are not enough seats at the price they have paid
senses.zh: (不加价)提高某人的座舱档次:

ex.en: I got bumped up to business class.
ex.zh: 我升到了商务舱。

senses.en: to move closer together to make a tight group; to make sb/sth do this

ex.en: The children bunched together in little groups in the playground.
ex.zh: 操场上的孩子们三五成群。

ex.en: All the runners were bunched up behind the leader.
ex.zh: 其他赛跑者在领先运动员后面挤作一团。

senses.en: to send sb somewhere in a hurry or when they do not want to go
senses.zh: 把(某人)匆匆送(到某处)；强行送走:

ex.en: She bundled her son off to school.
ex.zh: 她急匆匆地把儿子送到学校。

senses.en: to dress in warm clothes; to put warm clothes on sb

ex.en: Bundle up! It’s freezing outside!
ex.zh: 穿多点！外面很冷！

ex.en: I bundled Lucy up in a blanket and made her a cup of tea.
ex.zh: 我给露西裹了条毯子，又给她泡了杯茶。

senses.en: to put or tie things together into a bundle

ex.en: She bundled up her clothes and pushed them into a cupboard.
ex.zh: 她把衣服包起来塞进衣橱。

ex.en: The papers were all bundled together, ready to be thrown away.
ex.zh: 报纸全部捆好，准备扔掉。

senses.en: to stop sth from moving or flowing through sth by putting sth in or across it

ex.en: She’s bunged the sink up with tea leaves.
ex.zh: 她倒的茶叶把水槽堵住了。

senses.en: blocked; not clear

ex.en: My nose is all bunged up this morning.
ex.zh: 今天早晨我的鼻子全堵了。

senses.en: to lie down to sleep somewhere, especially somewhere uncomfortable or for only one night
senses.zh: (尤指在不舒适的地方)睡觉，过夜:

ex.en: We bunked down in an old barn for the night.
ex.zh: 那晚我们睡在一个旧榖仓里。

senses.en: to stay away from school or work when you ought to be there; to leave school or work early, especially without permission
senses.zh: 逃学； 旷工； 早退:

ex.en: Let’s bunk off this afternoon and go shopping.
ex.zh: 咱们今天下午别上班了，去购物吧。

senses.en: to make or keep sb cheerful and confident

ex.en: Winning the match buoyed the team up.
ex.zh: 比赛获胜使该队欢欣鼓舞。

ex.en: The party did little to buoy up her spirits.
ex.zh: 这次聚会并没有让她振作多少。

senses.en: to keep sb/sth floating; to stop sb/sth from sinking

ex.en: I relaxed, letting the salt water buoy me up.
ex.zh: 我放松下来，任凭海水托浮着。

senses.en: to make or keep prices at a high or satisfactory level
senses.zh: 保持高价；使(价格)维持于较高水平:

ex.en: Share prices were buoyed up by the news.
ex.zh: 这个消息使股价居高不下。

ex.en: to buoy up the economy
ex.zh: 繁荣经济

senses.en: to disappear as a result of burning; to make sth do this

ex.en: Half the candle had burnt away.
ex.zh: 蜡烛烧掉了半支。

ex.en: The fire had burned away part of the roof.
ex.zh: 大火烧掉了屋顶的一部份。

senses.en: to remove sth by burning

ex.en: Burn the old paint off before repainting the door.
ex.zh: 先把门上的旧漆烧掉，再刷新油漆。

senses.en: to stop burning because there is no more fuel

ex.en: Blow out the candles before they burn out.
ex.zh: 把蜡烛吹灭，免得烧完。

ex.en: By the time the fire brigade arrived the fire had burnt (itself) out.
ex.zh: 消防队赶到时火已经熄灭了。

senses.en: to become very tired or sick and unable to continue your work by working too hard over a period of time
senses.zh: 耗尽体力；积劳成疾；累垮:

ex.en: It’s a high pressure job and many people burn out at a young age.
ex.zh: 那工作压力很大，很多人年纪轻轻就积劳成疾。

ex.en: If he carries on working so hard, he’ll burn himself out.
ex.zh: 他要是继续这样拚命工作，就会把自己累垮。

senses.en: [C] [U] the state of being very tired or sick because you have worked too hard
senses.zh: 筋疲力尽； 过度劳累:

ex.en: Burnout is common among teachers.
ex.zh: 过度劳累在桝师中很常见。

senses.en: to force sb to leave a building by setting fire to it
senses.zh: 放火迫使某人离开(建筑物):

ex.en: A gang has tried to burn a woman out of her home.
ex.zh: 一伙匪徒试图放火把一名女子赶出她的家。

senses.en: to destroy sth completely by fire,so that only the outside or the frame is left

ex.en: Two cars were burnt out in the crash.
ex.zh: 撞车事故中有两辆汽车被烧成废铁。

senses.en: [only before noun] completely destroyed or badly damaged by fire

ex.en: burnt-out buses
ex.zh: 烧成空壳的公共汽车

ex.en: burned-out houses
ex.zh: 烧毁的房屋

senses.en: to be destroyed by heat

ex.en: The spacecraft burned up as it entered the earth’s atmosphere.
ex.zh: 宇宙飞船进入地球大气层时被烧毁。

senses.zh: (通常用于进行时) to have a fever or a high temperature发烧；体温高:

ex.en: She is burning up — she needs a doctor.
ex.zh: 她发烧了─她需要看医生。

senses.en: to search for sth among things in a container

ex.en: She burrowed in her pocket and eventually found a few coins.
ex.zh: 她在衣袋里摸来摸去，最后找到了几枚硬币。

senses.en: to enter a room, a building, etc. suddenly and noisily, interrupting the people who are in it
senses.zh: 闯入打扰(人或事情)；闯进某处:

ex.en: He apologized for bursting in on our meeting.
ex.zh: 他为闯进来打断了我们的会议表示歉意。

ex.en: The door suddenly flew open and Mia burst in.
ex.zh: 门猛地打开了，米娅一头闯进来。

senses.en: to start producing or doing sth suddenly and with great force

ex.en: The aircraft burst into flames (= suddenly started to burn).
ex.zh: 飞机猛地燃烧起来。

senses.en: to appear somewhere suddenly in a dramatic or unusual way

ex.en: A major new talent has burst on/onto the tennis scene.
ex.zh: 网球坛突然冒出一位重要的新秀。

senses.en: to say sth suddenly, loudly and with strong feeling

ex.en: ‘I hate you!’ she burst out.
ex.zh: “ 我恨你！”她大喊道。

senses.en: a sudden strong expression of an emotion; a sudden increase in an attitude or an activity
senses.zh: (感情的)爆发，迸发；(态度)激化； (活动) 激增:

ex.en: an outburst of anger/ laughter
ex.zh: 勃然大怒；哄然大笑

ex.en: sporadic outbursts of violence
ex.zh: 零星的暴力事件

senses.en: to leave a room, a building, etc. suddenly and noisily

ex.en: The door opened suddenly and a man burst out of the house.
ex.zh: 门突然打开，一名男子从房子里冲了出去。

senses.en: to begin doing sth suddenly

ex.en: We looked at one another and burst out laughing.
ex.zh: 我们相互看了看，突然大笑起来。

senses.en: to move suddenly through a door, a barrier, etc. with great force

ex.en: The car drove fast up to the road block and burst through.
ex.zh: 汽车高速开到路障前，一下子冲了过去。

ex.en: She burst through the door pursued by two men.
ex.zh: 她突然冲出门去，后面还跟着两名男子。

senses.en: to go to or be in a place where you will not meet many people
senses.zh: 到(或在)人迹罕至的地方；隐居…:

ex.en: He buried himself in the country to write a book.
ex.zh: 他隐居乡间写书。

senses.en: to involve yourself in sth completely; to spend all your time thinking about or doing sth and ignore everything else

ex.en: She buried herself in her work in an attempt to forget.
ex.zh: 她全心扑在工作上，试图忘掉往事。

senses.en: to escape from somewhere, usually prison; to help sb to do this

ex.en: His last movie was about a guy busting out of Alcatraz.
ex.zh: 他的上一部电影讲述一名男子在阿尔卡特拉斯岛越狱的故事。

ex.en: His friends busted him out of jail.
ex.zh: 朋友们帮他逃出了监狱。

senses.en: to end sth such as a meeting or a relationship by disturbing or ruining it

ex.en: The police busted up the meeting.
ex.zh: 警察驱散了集会。

senses.en: to move about somewhere in a busy or hurried way
senses.zh: (为某事或在某处)忙得团团转:

ex.en: She was already bustling about, getting dinner ready.
ex.zh: 她已经四下忙碌着准备晚饭。

senses.en: used to tell sb rudely not to interfere in sth or to go away

ex.en: Butt out! It’s none of your business.
ex.zh: 别插手！这不关你的事。

senses.en: to say nice things about sb because you want them to do sth for you or give you sth
senses.zh: 以甜言蜜语巴结某人；奉承；拍马屁:

ex.en: We’d better butter him up a bit before we ask for his help.
ex.zh: 我们最好先给他戴个高帽再求他帮忙。

senses.en: to be fastened with buttons; to fasten sth with buttons

ex.en: He buttoned up his coat.
ex.zh: 他扣好了外衣。

senses.en: [usually before noun] not showing or expressing your feelings openly; not very friendly
senses.zh: 不露声色的；沉默的；不热情的:

ex.en: his buttoned-up calmness
ex.zh: 他的沉静

senses.en: ) very formal in appearance; traditional rather than new or exciting
senses.zh: 正襟危坐的；一本正经的

senses.en: the action of buying again sth that you have sold earlier

ex.en: a book/equipment buy-back (= when a shop/store or company buys back sth you have finished using)
ex.zh: 书籍/设备的回购

senses.en: ) a form of borrowing money in which a company sells its shares with an agreement that it will buy them again at a later date
senses.zh: 股份回购(公司把为集资而售出的股份买回来):

ex.en: a share buy-back
ex.zh: 股份回购

ex.en: a share buy-back programme
ex.zh: 股份回购计划

senses.en: to buy sth or a large amount of sth for a special occasion or in order to have a supply for the future

ex.en: I’ll have to buy in extra food if they’re coming to stay for a while.
ex.zh: 如果他们要来住段时间，我得额外购买些食物。

senses.en: to buy shares in a company, for example to gain control over it
senses.zh: 购买公司股份(尤指为取得股权):

ex.en: They are looking to buy into another insurance company.
ex.zh: 他们期待着购买另外一家保险公司的股份。

senses.en: to pay sb to stop them acting against you, causing trouble for you, etc.
senses.zh: 收买， 贿赂(某人不做某事):

ex.en: They had to buy Brennan off to stop him from talking.
ex.zh: 他们不得不用钱封住布伦南的口。

senses.en: to pay money so that sb/you can leave an organization, especially the armed forces, before the time agreed
senses.zh: 付给补偿金(让某人或自己提前退役、离职等):

ex.en: After four years in the navy I bought myself out.
ex.zh: 在海军服役四年之后我出钱提前退役了。

senses.en: to buy part of a company, business,etc. from sb else so that you own all of it and control it

ex.en: I want to buy her out and have the house to myself.
ex.zh: 我想买下她的产权，自己占有这房子。

ex.en: The company was bought out by two German businessmen.
ex.zh: 公司的全部股份都被两名德国商人买下了。

senses.en: a situation when sb buys enough shares in a company to gain control of it
to buy quickly all of sth or as much as you can
senses.zh: 迅速地全部(或尽量)购买某物；收购:

ex.en: They’ve bought up all the land in the area.
ex.zh: 他们收购了这个地区的全部土地。

senses.en: to move around quickly and busily

ex.en: She buzzed round (the kitchen).
ex.zh: 她(在厨房里)四下忙碌。

ex.en: The photographer buzzed around, checking the light.
ex.zh: 摄影师跑来跑去忙着调整灯光。

senses.en: used to tell sb, not very politely, to go away

ex.en: Buzz off, I’m trying to work!
ex.zh: 走开，我得干活！

ex.en: I wish he’d buzz off!
ex.zh: 我希望他走开！

senses.en: to telephone a number of different people, usually to try to get information

ex.en: He’s been calling around trying to get the best price on a computer.
ex.zh: 他正四下打电话，想找到买计算机的最优价格。

ex.en: I called around the neighbourhood to get support for my campaign.
ex.zh: 我给左邻右舍打电话，请他们支持我发起的运动。

senses.en: to ask sb to stop doing what they are doing and go somewhere else to deal with sth
senses.zh: 把…叫到别处去(做别的事)；叫走:

ex.en: He was called away to the phone.
ex.zh: 有人叫他去接电话。

ex.en: She was called away from the meeting to deal with an emergency.
ex.zh: 她被叫出会场去处理紧急情况。

senses.en: to visit sb again

ex.en: I’ll call back later when your wife’s at home.
ex.zh: 回头等你夫人在家时我再来拜访。

senses.en: to telephone sb again or to telephone sb who telephoned you earlier

ex.en: Call back in an hour — he’ll be here then.
ex.zh: 一小时之后再打电话吧─他就回来了。

ex.en: Kate phoned. Can you call her back?
ex.zh: 凯特来电话了。

senses.en: a device in a telephone that automatically calls again a number that was busy when you first called it

ex.en: a callback facility
ex.zh: 自动重拨功能

senses.en: a telephone call that you make to sb who has called you earlier
to visit a place or a person for a short time, usually when you are going somewhere else

ex.en: Could you call by on your way home?
ex.zh: 你回家时进来坐坐吧？

ex.en: Jan called by to bring your gift.
ex.zh: 简给你送了份礼物来。

senses.en: to shout to sb to ask them to come down from a place which is higher than you

ex.en: I’ve called him down (= to come downstairs) to breakfast already.
ex.zh: 我已经喊他下楼吃早餐了。

senses.en: to go to sb’s home, for example,and take them or go with them somewhere

ex.en: Shall I call for you at eight?
ex.zh: 我八点钟来接你好吗？

senses.en: (of remarks or behaviour
senses.zh: 话语或行为) not fair or necessary in the circumstances不公正的；不必要的:

ex.en: I shall ignore that uncalled-for remark.
ex.zh: 我不会理会那句不负责任的话的。

senses.en: to demand publicly that sth should be done

ex.en: The group has called for a boycott of the elections.
ex.zh: 这个集体呼吁大家抵制选举。

ex.en: The other directors have called for him to resign.
ex.zh: 其他领导人已要求他辞职。

senses.en: to produce a particular reaction

ex.en: Her remarks have called forth harsh criticism in the media.
ex.zh: 她的话引发了媒体的严厉批评。

senses.en: to telephone the place where you work
to make a telephone call to a radio or television programme
senses.zh: 打电话到(电台或电视节目) :

ex.en: Many listeners called in to complain.
ex.zh: 很多听众打电话来投诉。

senses.en: a television or radio show in which people can phone to talk to people on the show, ask questions, give their opinions, etc.

ex.en: a call-in show
ex.zh: 直播电视节目

senses.en: to ask sb to come and help, give advice,repair sth, etc.

ex.en: He’s threatened to call in the police.
ex.zh: 他威胁说要叫警察。

ex.en: You’ll have to call a plumber in to look at this.
ex.zh: 你必须请水暖工来瞧瞧。

senses.en: to order soldiers, dogs, etc. to stop attacking sb, searching for sb/sth, etc.
senses.zh: 把(士兵等)叫走(不再搜查等)；把(狗等)叫开:

ex.en: Please call your dog off.
ex.zh: 请把你的狗叫走。

senses.en: to cancel or abandon sth that has been planned or that has already started

ex.en: The meeting was called off at the last minute.
ex.zh: 会议在最后一分钟取消了。

ex.en: They’ve called off their engagement (= they have decided not to get married).
ex.zh: 他们已经解除婚约。

senses.en: () to visit sb for a short time

ex.en: On our way back, we called on grandma.
ex.zh: 我们在回家的路上去看了看祖母。

senses.en: to use your strength,courage, etc. in order to achieve sth or deal with a problem
senses.zh: 尽力，鼓起勇气(为争取某事物或处理某问题):

ex.en: She had to call on all her reserves of courage to face the ordeal.
ex.zh: 她不得不鼓足勇气直面这一严峻考验。

senses.en: to make a serious or urgent request to sb to do sth
senses.zh: (严肃或迫切地)请求，要求，要(某人做某事):

ex.en: I’m available in case I’m called on to help.
ex.zh: 如果需要帮忙，我随叫随到。

ex.en: We call upon all parties to respect the results of the election.
ex.zh: 我们要求所有党派尊重选举结果。

senses.en: to formally invite or request sb to speak, etc.
senses.zh: 邀请，要求(某人讲话等)；恭请:

ex.en: I now call upon Mr. Spring to give the vote of thanks.
ex.zh: 现在请斯普林先生致谢辞。

senses.en: to shout or say sth loudly in order to get sb’s attention or help

ex.en: He called out to her, but she carried on walking.
ex.zh: 他大声喊她，但她继续走她的路。

ex.en: He woke in the night, calling out her name.
ex.zh: 他夜里醒来，呼唤着她的名字。

senses.en: to ask sb to come to help you,when there is an emergency
senses.zh: 召唤某人(帮忙或立即行动):

ex.en: I’ve never had to call the doctor out at night before.
ex.zh: 我以前从来没有在夜里请过医生。

ex.en: We had to call out an electrician.
ex.zh: 我们得叫来电工。

senses.en: to order or ask workers to stop work as a protest
senses.zh: 下令罢工； 通知罢工:

ex.en: Miners were called out on strike by union leaders.
ex.zh: 工会领导人号召矿工罢工。

senses.en: an occasion when you ask sb to come to help you in an emergency

ex.en: ambulance call-outs
ex.zh: 叫救护车

ex.en: How much is the plumber’s call-out charge?
ex.zh: 请水暖工上门要花多少钱？

senses.en: to telephone a shop,store, restaurant, etc. to ask them to deliver food to you at home or at work

ex.en: Let’s call out for pizza.
ex.zh: 我们打电话要外卖比萨饼吧。

senses.en: to call sb to come over to where you are, because you want to speak to them, give or show them sth, etc.

ex.en: Call the waiter over.
ex.zh: 叫服务员过来。

senses.en: to visit sb at their home for a short time

ex.en: I just called round to say hello.
ex.zh: 我刚进去问候了一声。

senses.en: to make a phone call to a person or a place
senses.zh: 打电话(给某人或到某处):

ex.en: Call up and make a reservation for 8 o’clock.
ex.zh: 打电话预订8点钟的位子。

ex.en: She called him up from the bus station.
ex.zh: 她在公共汽车站给他打电话。

senses.en: to officially ask sb to go to do training in the army, navy or air force or to fight in a war

ex.en: When the war began, he was too old to be called up.
ex.zh: 战争开始的时候他年纪太大，不能应徵。

senses.en: ) to ask sb to join sth or take part in sth; to choose sb to play in a team

ex.en: He’s been called up for next week’s match.
ex.zh: 他已入选参加下个星期的比赛。

senses.en: an official order to join the army,navy or air force

ex.en: call-up papers/camps
ex.zh: 徵集令；徵集营

senses.en: ,) an official invitation to play in a team or in a particular game
to become calmer; to make a situation calmer

ex.en: The whole fuss will have calmed down by tomorrow.
ex.zh: 这一切争吵到明天就会缓和下来。

ex.en: I’ve spoken to them to try to calm things down a bit.
ex.zh: 我告诉过他们要设法平息事情。

senses.en: to sleep outside, usually in a tent; to sleep on the floor somewhere for a short time

ex.en: If there is nowhere to stay, we’ll have to camp out.
ex.zh: 如果找不到住处，我们只能露宿。

ex.en: People camped out in the school hall to escape the flood water.
ex.zh: 人们在学校礼堂临时寄宿躲避洪水。

senses.en: a time when people sleep outside in a tent
(of a moving person,vehicle, etc.
senses.zh: 移动的人、车辆等) to hit sb/sth by accident and with great force冲撞；猛撞:

ex.en: She stopped suddenly and I almost cannoned into her.
ex.zh: 她突然停下来，我差点撞了她。

senses.en: to use sth to gain further advantage for yourself

ex.en: They capitalized on their success by raising prices.
ex.zh: 他们藉着成功的势头提价。

ex.en: The opposition tried to capitalize on popular discontent over the new law.
ex.zh: 反对派企图利用公众对新法规的不满。

senses.en: to like or love sb

ex.en: I care deeply for you.
ex.zh: 我非常爱你。

senses.en: to take care of and be responsible for sb who is very young, old or sick, etc. or for sth that is in danger or could be damaged
senses.zh: 照顾，照料，保护(人或事物):

ex.en: The nurses give advice to the patients and those who care for them.
ex.zh: 护士给病人和陪护人员提出建议。

ex.en: She cares for several children with special needs.
ex.zh: 她照看着几个需要特别照顾的儿童。

senses.en: used to ask sb if they would like sth to eat or drink
senses.zh: 你想来点(吃或喝的东西)吗:

ex.en: Would you care for a cup of tea?
ex.zh: 你想喝杯茶吗？

senses.en: not looked after; neglected

ex.en: The children looked dirty and uncared for.
ex.zh: 孩子们看上去脏兮兮的，没人照料。

ex.en: uncared-for gardens
ex.zh: 疏于管理的园子

senses.en: to take or move sb/sth forward

ex.en: His body had been carried along by the river.
ex.zh: 他的躯体被河水冲走了。

ex.en: The crowd was so thick that she was carried along with it.
ex.zh: 人群挤得水泄不通，她只能随着他们移动。

senses.en: to support the weight of sb/sth and take them/it away
senses.zh: 把… 抬走；把… 冲 走:

ex.en: A strong current carried the dinghy away.
ex.zh: 一阵激流把小艇卷走了。

senses.en: to be so excited and enthusiastic about sth that you lose control of your feelings and may behave in a silly or thoughtless way

ex.en: I got so carried away with shopping that I completely forgot the time.
ex.zh: 我只顾购物，完全忘记了时间。

ex.en: Don’t get carried away — it’s not that exciting.
ex.zh: 别兴奋得失态了─没那么令人激动。

senses.en: to remind sb of sth that happened in the past

ex.en: The song carried her back to her childhood.
ex.zh: 这首歌勾起了她童年的回忆。

senses.en: to help sth to make progress or succeed

ex.en: She will carry the project forward after I leave.
ex.zh: 我离开之后将由她推动这个项目。

senses.en: to capture sb

ex.en: The enemy carried off many prisoners.
ex.zh: 敌人抓走了很多俘虏。

senses.en: to win sth

ex.en: She carried off most of the prizes.
ex.zh: 她赢得了大多数奖项。

senses.en: to succeed in doing sth difficult; to deal with a difficult situation successfully
senses.zh: 成功地对付，不费劲地处理(困难的事):

senses.en: to manage to continue living or working in your usual way in spite of difficult or unpleasant circumstances

ex.en: Life carried on as usual after the fire.
ex.zh: 火灾之后人们如常地生活。

ex.en: We’re all going to carry on as if nothing has happened.
ex.zh: 我们大家要像没发生过什么事一样坚持工作。

senses.en: to last for a particular time

ex.en: How long can this situation carry on?
ex.zh: 这种状况能持续多久？

senses.en: [usually sing.] (, )excited or noisy behaviour over sth that is not important; a fuss
senses.zh: 忙乱； 吵闹； 大惊小怪

senses.en: () a small bag or case that you carry onto a plane with you

ex.en: I’m travelling light — I just have a carry-on.
ex.zh: 我旅行带的东西很少─只有一只小提箱。

ex.en: Do you have any carry-on luggage?
ex.zh: 你有随身行李吗？

senses.en: to continue sth, especially sth that sb else has begun
senses.zh: 继续，承接(他人做的事) ； 继承:

ex.en: Our children will carry this tradition on after us.
ex.zh: 我们的子孙会继承这一传统。

senses.en: to do sth that you said you would do or that you have been asked to do

ex.en: to carry out a plan/a promise/an order
ex.zh: 把计划/承诺/命令付诸行动

ex.en: He had no intention of carrying out his threats.
ex.zh: 他并不想做他威胁要做的事。

senses.en: a meal that you buy cooked from a restaurant and take away to eat somewhere else

ex.en: Let’s get a carry-out.
ex.zh: 我们来份外卖吧。

senses.en: to delay sth until a later time

ex.en: The game had to be carried over until Wednesday.
ex.zh: 比赛要推迟到星期三。

ex.en: You can carry over 4 days’ leave to next year.
ex.zh: 你可以把4天的假期挪到下一年休。

senses.en: ) a total sum of money or an amount that is moved to the next column/page/year, etc.
something that is kept from one situation or time and used in another
to do and finish what you have promised, agreed or arranged to do

ex.en: He convinced us that he would carry through with/on his promise.
ex.zh: 他向我们保证他能履行自己的诺言。

senses.en: to help sb to deal with a difficult period

ex.en: Her determination carried her through.
ex.zh: 她靠毅力挺了过去。

ex.en: His courage helped to carry them through the difficult times.
ex.zh: 他的勇气让他们挺过困难的日子。

senses.en: used to talk about carrying sth large, awkward or unimportant from one place to another or everywhere you go
senses.zh: 提着，拿着(笨重或不重要的东西)四处走:

ex.en: I had to cart my shopping around with me all day.
ex.zh: 我一整天都要提着买来的东西到处走。

ex.en: He carts all sorts of useless stuff about.
ex.zh: 他带着各种各样的废物四下晃荡。

senses.en: to take sb/sth away with some difficulty

ex.en: Two players were carted off to hospital.
ex.zh: 好不容易才把两名运动员送到医院。

ex.en: The police arrived and carted 40 rioters off to jail.
ex.zh: 警察到场把40 名骚乱者扭送到监狱。

senses.en: to wound sb or their face badly with a knife
senses.zh: 用刀伤害(某人)；用刀划伤(某人的脸):

ex.en: He got carved up outside the pub last night.
ex.zh: 他昨天夜里在酒馆外遭人用刀刺伤。

senses.en: to go past a moving vehicle ahead of you and then suddenly move in front of it in a dangerous way

ex.en: I was carved up by a lunatic in a Porsche.
ex.zh: 一个开保时捷的疯子超车抢了我的道。

ex.en: We saw the van carve up several cars, before turning left.
ex.zh: 我们看见货车抢了几辆车的道之后左拐。

senses.en: to divide a company, an area of land, etc. into parts and share them out

ex.en: They carved the territory up into three provinces.
ex.zh: 他们把领土划分为三个省。

ex.en: The thieves hurriedly carved up the loot.
ex.zh: 窃贼匆忙瓜分了赃物。

senses.en: [sing.] (, ) the act of dividing sth up into parts and sharing them out
to gain an advantage from a situation in a way that people think is wrong or dishonest

ex.en: Many businesses cashed in on the massive public interest in her death.
ex.zh: 很多公司利用公众对她去世的广泛关注来赚钱。

ex.en: The new law means video pirates can no longer cash in by selling illegal copies.
ex.zh: 新法规意味着非法录制录像片者不能再通过销售盗版带牟利。

senses.en: to look around you to try to find sth; to try very hard to think of sth

ex.en: He cast about for an escape route.
ex.zh: 他到处寻找逃生路线。

ex.en: He was desperately casting around for an excuse.
ex.zh: 他绞尽脑汁找藉口。

senses.en: [NOTE]This phrasal verb is usually used in written English.
senses.zh: 这个短语动词通常用于书面语。

senses.en: to get rid of, or give no attention to, sb/sth that you no longer want or need

ex.en: She just cast him aside when she got bored.
ex.zh: 她觉得厌烦时就把他撇在一边。

ex.en: She has been able to cast aside (= stop using) her wheelchair.
ex.zh: 她能丢掉轮椅了。

senses.en: to throw sth to one side

ex.en: He cast aside the newspaper impatiently.
ex.zh: 他不耐烦地把报纸扔到一边。

senses.en: to get rid of feelings, attitudes, etc. that are bad or negative, or that stop you achieving sth
senses.zh: 消除，祛除(负面的感觉、态度等):

ex.en: He cast aside all his inhibitions.
ex.zh: 他抛开一切禁忌。

ex.en: The speakers cast modesty aside and talked about their success.
ex.zh: 演讲者毫不谦虚地大谈他们的成就。

senses.en: to be left somewhere after your ship has been destroyed at sea

ex.en: What would you do if you were cast away on a desert island?
ex.zh: 你若被撇在荒岛上会怎么办呢？

senses.en: a person whose ship has been destroyed and who has managed to swim to an island, etc.
to make yourself think about a particular time, a situation in the past, etc.
to be sad or unhappy about sth

ex.en: He is not easily cast down.
ex.zh: 他很少有情绪低落的时候。

senses.en: sad or unhappy

ex.en: a downcast expression
ex.zh: 垂头丧气的表情

ex.en: He looked so downcast I took pity on him.
ex.zh: 他那十分沮丧的样子令我产生了怜悯。

senses.en: to undo the ropes that are holding a boat in position so that it can start to move
(in knitting
senses.zh: 编织) to remove a row of stitches from the needle in a way that will make a finished edge收针:

ex.en: When the scarf is the right length, cast off.
ex.zh: 围巾编织得够长就收针。

senses.en: to take off a piece of clothing and throw it to one side

ex.en: They cast off their clothes and jumped in the pool.
ex.zh: 他们脱掉衣服就跳进游泳池。

senses.en: to get rid of sth bad or sth that you do not like

ex.en: She tried to cast off her upbringing.
ex.zh: 她努力摆脱童年的影响。

ex.en: It’s time to cast off those winter blues and burst into spring!
ex.zh: 该扔掉那些冬天的忧郁投入春天的怀抱了！

senses.en: [usually pl.] a piece of clothing that the original owner no longer wants to wear

ex.en: She’s fed up with wearing her sister’s cast-offs.
ex.zh: 她厌烦了穿姐姐倒下的衣服。

senses.en: [only before noun] that the original owner no longer wants to wear or use

ex.en: cast-off clothing
ex.zh: 不再穿的衣服

ex.en: cast-off plastic bags
ex.zh: 丢弃的塑料袋

senses.en: (in knitting
senses.zh: 编织) to make the first row of stitches on a needle, or add new stitches起针； 放针:

ex.en: Cast on and knit 10 rows.
ex.zh: 起针编织10行。

senses.en: to drive sb away; to get rid of sb/sth,especially by using force

ex.en: She was cast out by society.
ex.zh: 她被社会摈弃了。

ex.en: He claimed to be able to cast out demons.
ex.zh: 他自称能驱魔。

senses.en: someone who is rejected and ignored by other people and often has to leave their home and friends
senses.zh: 被抛弃的人；被冷落的人:

ex.en: She felt like a social outcast.
ex.zh: 她觉得像是被社会摈弃了。

ex.en: He was treated like an outcast by the other children.
ex.zh: 他受到其他小朋友的排斥。

senses.en: [only before noun] ignored or not accepted by other people

ex.en: outcast members of society
ex.zh: 社会弃儿

senses.en: to try to get hold of sth quickly

ex.en: She tried to catch at a branch but couldn’t reach.
ex.zh: 她急切地想抓住树枝，但够不着。

senses.en: to trick sb into making a mistake or doing sth wrong; to discover that sb does not know much or is doing sth wrong

ex.en: The test isn’t designed to catch you out. It’s to see how much you’ve learnt.
ex.zh: 这个测验不是故意用来刁难你的，而是为了解你学到了多少东西。

ex.en: The interviewer may try to catch you out with trick questions.
ex.zh: 主持面试者可能设法用刁钻的问题来难倒你。

senses.en: to reach sb/sth ahead of you by going faster than them/it

ex.en: She was walking so fast I had to run to catch up (with her).
ex.zh: 她走得飞快，我必须跑步才能跟上她。

ex.en: The police car finally caught up with the van at the junction.
ex.zh: 警车最后在交叉路口追上了客货车。

senses.en: to reach the same level or standard as sb/sth else that was better or more advanced

ex.en: We need to catch up with our competitors in Europe.
ex.zh: 我们得追上在欧洲的竞争对手。

ex.en: You’ll have to work hard to catch up with the rest of the class.
ex.zh: 你必须努力学习赶上班里其他同学。

senses.en: =CATCH UP (WITH SB/STH) 1

ex.en: You go ahead. I’ll catch you up.
ex.zh: 你先走，我随后赶上你。

ex.en: She caught the leader up and then overtook her.
ex.zh: 她追上了领先的选手并超过了她。

senses.en: =CATCH UP (WITH SB/STH) 2

ex.en: This company is the most likely to catch up the market leader.
ex.zh: 这家公司最有可能赶上市场的主导者。

ex.en: She’s training hard to catch her sister up.
ex.zh: 她在刻苦训练好赶上她的姐姐。

senses.en: to become involved in an unpleasant event or situation that you cannot escape from

ex.en: A number of tourists got caught up in the riots.
ex.zh: 若干游客卷入了那场暴乱。

ex.en: children caught up in crime
ex.zh: 牵涉到犯罪活动里的儿童

senses.en: to spend extra time doing all the work, tasks, etc. that you should have done earlier
senses.zh: 补做(未做的事)；赶做；补上:

ex.en: I’ve got a lot of work to catch up on.
ex.zh: 我有许多工作要补做。

ex.en: I spent the weekend catching up on lost sleep.
ex.zh: 我利用周末补上了缺乏的睡眠。

senses.en: () to meet sb you have not seen for a while and hear their news
senses.zh: 和(分别一段时间的人)了解情况:

ex.en: He just wants to rest and catch up with old friends.
ex.zh: 他只想休息一下，找老朋友叙叙旧。

ex.en: Catch up with you later!
ex.zh: 回头找你聊聊！

senses.en: to provide everything that sb, a group of people or a situation needs or wants
senses.zh: 提供某人(或某集体、情况等)所须；为…而设:

ex.en: The careers service caters for the needs of young people and adults.
ex.zh: 职介部门特别为年轻人以及成人而设。

ex.en: The resort also caters for winter sports.
ex.zh: 这个度假胜地也适合进行冬季运动。

senses.en: to provide sth that satisfies what a particular type of person wants
senses.zh: 迎合某类人(等)的要求；满足…所想:

ex.en: Endless media coverage catered to the public’s interest in the scandal.
ex.zh: 没完没了的媒体报道迎合了公众对这一丑闻的好奇心。

senses.en: the fact of a roof, wall, etc. falling down and inwards

ex.en: For the people inside the tunnel there was a serious risk of flooding or a cave-in.
ex.zh: 隧道里的人冒着透水或塌方的巨大危险。

senses.en: an instance of agreeing under pressure to do sth you do not want to do
to be, or make sb/sth, the most important person or thing around which most activity takes place
senses.zh: 围绕，环绕(某人或事情等)；以…为中心；把…作为…的中心:

ex.en: The debate centres around the question of power.
ex.zh: 争论的焦点是权力问题。

ex.en: The case centred around the couple’s adopted children.
ex.zh: 论据围绕这对夫妇领养的孩子们。

senses.en: to give a lot of attention or thought to one particular activity, idea or person,etc.
senses.zh: 把注意力(或思想)集中于…:

ex.en: The discussions centred on the hostage issue.
ex.zh: 讨论围绕着人质这一问题进行。

ex.en: Public interest centred largely on the team’s stars.
ex.zh: 公众关心的主要是这个队的明星。

senses.en: to fasten sb/sth to sth else with chains to stop them escaping or being stolen

ex.en: I’d chain your bike up (to the fence) just in case.
ex.zh: 我把你的自行车拴(在围栏)上以防万一。

ex.en: The prisoners were chained up in a dark cell.
ex.zh: 囚犯都用锁链锁在阴暗的牢笼里。

senses.en: to achieve a success, a victory, a score in a game,etc.
senses.zh: 获得，取得(成功)；记下，记录(成就、比赛得分等):

ex.en: The team has chalked up its fifth win in a row.
ex.zh: 这支队已连赢五场比赛。

ex.en: This week Dee Brothers chalked up 100 years of business in this town.
ex.zh: 本周迪伊兄弟公司在这个城开业100 年了。

senses.en: to think that sth happens as a result of sth else

ex.en: We can chalk our recent victories up to a lot of luck.
ex.zh: 我们可以把近期的胜利归因于好运十足。

senses.en: used to say that you can learn from sth bad that has happened to you
to meet sb or find sth when you do not expect to

ex.en: I chanced on an old school friend in town.
ex.zh: 我在城里碰到了一位旧日的同窗。

ex.en: He chanced upon a volume of Japanese poetry in a bookshop.
ex.zh: 他在书店偶然发现了一部日本诗集。

senses.en: to put on different clothes

ex.en: We quickly changed into our swimsuits.
ex.zh: 我们迅速换上了游泳衣。

ex.en: I didn’t bring anything to change into.
ex.zh: 我没带换洗衣服。

senses.en: to change, or to make sb/sth change, into sth different

ex.en: The castle has changed into a hotel.
ex.zh: 城堡改成了旅馆。

ex.en: The handsome prince was changed into a frog.
ex.zh: 英俊的王子给变成了青蛙。

senses.en: to take off the clothes you are wearing and put on different ones
senses.zh: 更换， 换掉(衣服)；更衣:

ex.en: I must change out of these wet clothes before I get a chill.
ex.zh: 我必须把这些湿衣服换掉，免得受凉。

ex.en: She changed out of her suit as soon as she came home.
ex.zh: 她一回到家就换下了套装。

senses.en: a change from one system or thing to another

ex.en: The changeover to the new system will take place gradually.
ex.zh: 将循序渐进地过渡到新制度。

ex.en: a changeover period
ex.zh: 过渡时期

senses.en: to move objects,such as furniture, or people into different positions
senses.zh: 变换(人或傢具等)的位置:

ex.en: Who’s changed the desks around?
ex.zh: 谁挪动桌子了？

ex.en: You’re always changing this room round! (= making it look different by moving the furniture,etc.)
ex.zh: 你总是把房间里的傢具调来换去。

senses.en: to give sb a duty, responsibility or task
senses.zh: 使…承担(职责、责任或任务)；委託:

ex.en: A solicitor was charged with administering the estate.
ex.zh: 一名律师受委託管理这份财产。

senses.en: [NOTE]These phrasal verbs are often used in the passive.
senses.zh: 这些短语动词常用于被动语态。

senses.en: to be very busy, rushing from one place to another

ex.en: I’ve been chasing around all morning trying to find a gift for my sister.
ex.zh: 我东奔西跑了一上午，想为我妹妹找到件礼物。

senses.en: to force sb/sth to run away by running after them or threatening them

ex.en: He chased the attackers away by firing shots into the air.
ex.zh: 他对空中鸣枪把袭击者吓跑。

senses.en: to try hard to get sth or find sb/sth that you need or want

ex.en: I’ve been trying to chase Sam down all day!
ex.zh: 我一整天都在苦苦寻找萨姆！

senses.en: to contact sb and remind them to do sth they have said they would do or that they ought to do

ex.en: I’ll chase him up and find out what’s going on.
ex.zh: 我来催催他搞清楚现在的情况。

ex.en: It is his job to chase up clients with outstanding debts.
ex.zh: 向客户追索未偿还债款是他的工作。

senses.en: to try to find sb/sth that you need;to try to get more information about sb/sth
senses.zh: 找寻(所需的东西)；想法获取(更多消息):

ex.en: We’re chasing up two other people who were at the party.
ex.zh: 我们正在寻找另外两名当时在晚会中的人。

ex.en: I’ll chase up references to the battle in the library.
ex.zh: 我要去图书馆查找关于这次战斗的资料。

senses.en: ) to talk in a friendly way to sb because you are sexually attracted to them
senses.zh: (受异性吸引而)亲昵地攀谈， 与某人搭讪:

ex.en: Who was that girl you were chatting up last night?
ex.zh: 昨晚你和人家搭讪的女孩是谁？

senses.en: ) to talk to sb in a friendly way because you want them to do sth for you or to give you sth

ex.en: You’ll have to chat the boss up if you want some days off.
ex.zh: 你若想请几天假， 就得和老板拉拉关系。

senses.en: an attempt to talk in a friendly way to sb you are sexually attracted to

ex.en: He was trying some old chat-up lines.
ex.zh: 他试图用些老套的话来搭讪。

senses.en: to prevent sb from having sth, especially in an unfair or dishonest way
senses.zh: (尤指用不正当或不诚实的手段)阻止某人得到某物:

ex.en: He had cheated the taxman of ￡60 000.
ex.zh: 他骗税务员少收了6万英镑。

ex.en: He was cheated out of his rightful inheritance.
ex.zh: 有人骗取了他本应得到的遗产。

senses.en: to be unfaithful to your husband,wife or partner by secretly having sex with sb else
senses.zh: 对丈夫(或妻子、伴侣)不忠:

ex.en: He was the last to know that she had been cheating on him.
ex.zh: 他是最后一个知道她一直背着他偷情的。

senses.en: [U] the act of telling an official at an airport that you have arrived, showing them your ticket, etc.

ex.en: the check-in desk
ex.zh: 办理登机手续的柜台

senses.en: [C] [U] the place at an airport where you go to say you have arrived, show your ticket, etc.

ex.en: There were long queues at the check-in.
ex.zh: 办理登记手续的地方排起长队。

senses.en: to take sb’s name when they arrive at a hotel or an airport, look at their ticket, etc.
senses.zh: (在旅馆、机场等)为某人登记；给某人办入住(或登机)手续:

ex.en: Write all the names of the guests in this book as they are checked in.
ex.zh: 给客人办手续时把他们的名字都记在这个本子里。

ex.en: All the passengers have been checked in.
ex.zh: 已为所有乘客办妥登机手续。

senses.en: to arrive at a hotel, private hospital, etc. to begin your stay there
senses.zh: 登记入住(旅馆、私人医院等):

ex.en: I arrived in Boston and checked into my hotel.
ex.zh: 我到波士顿后住到了预订的旅馆。

ex.en: She’s checked into a private clinic for drug rehabilitation.
ex.zh: 她住进了一私人诊所戒毒。

senses.en: to try to find out more about sth or discover the true facts about sth

ex.en: The police are checking into the cause of the crash.
ex.zh: 警方在调查飞机坠毁的原因。

senses.en: to put a mark beside items on a list to show that they are correct, present or have been dealt with
senses.zh: 在(清单项目)上做记号(表示正确、存在或已处理)；核对:

ex.en: I’ve checked off all the furniture on the list.
ex.zh: 我核对了清单上的所有傢具。

ex.en: He checked everyone’s name off as they arrived.
ex.zh: 他在每位来宾的姓名上都打了漖。

senses.en: ) to put a mark in a box on a document to give an answer to a question, choose sb/sth, etc.
senses.zh: (在文件核选框中)做记号(做出回答、选择等)；漖出:

ex.en: Some voters wrote in names instead of checking off the candidates listed.
ex.zh: 有些选民填写了姓名，而不是漖出所列的候选人。

senses.en: to make sure that sb is safe,happy, etc. or that sth is progressing as it should be

ex.en: I’ll just check on dinner.
ex.zh: 我来看看晚饭好了没有。

ex.en: The doctor visited every day to check on my progress.
ex.zh: 医生每天来检查我的进展情况。

senses.en: , ) to leave a place or finish an activity

ex.en: The climb was too difficult so I checked out early.
ex.zh: 这次登山太艰难，所以我早早地放弃了。

senses.en: to leave a hotel, a hospital, etc. where you have been staying

ex.en: She checked out this morning.
ex.zh: 她今天上午退房了。

ex.en: He decided to check out of the hospital and go home.
ex.zh: 他决定办理出院回家。

senses.en: [U] the act or time of leaving a hotel at the end of your stay
senses.zh: 结账离开旅馆；退房时间:

ex.en: Checkout is 10 a.m.
ex.zh: 退房时间为上午10点。

ex.en: checkout time
ex.zh: 退房时间

senses.en: () to find out if sth is true or correct or if sb is honest, truthful,reliable, etc.

ex.en: Check him out before you give him the job.
ex.zh: 先调查一下再雇用他。

ex.en: Police have checked out his story.
ex.zh: 警方已经核实了他的叙述。

senses.en: to borrow sth such as a book or a video from a library

ex.en: I checked out three books from the library.
ex.zh: 我从图书馆借了三本书。

senses.en: to examine a person or an animal to make sure that they are healthy; to examine a machine, etc. to make sure it is working correctly
senses.zh: 为(人或动物)做体检；检查(机器运行等):

ex.en: The doctor would like to check you over.
ex.zh: 医生想给你做体检。

ex.en: I got the car checked over before the trip.
ex.zh: 我上路之前检查了汽车。

senses.en: to examine sth written or printed carefully to make sure that it is correct

ex.en: I’ve got to check over my work for spelling before I hand it in.
ex.zh: 交作业前我得仔细检查是否有拼写错误。

ex.en: You should get someone to check the letter over for you.
ex.zh: 你应该找人帮你把信校对一下。

senses.en: an examination by your doctor to see how healthy you are

ex.en: to go for a check-up
ex.zh: 去做体检

ex.en: a routine check-up
ex.zh: 常规体检

senses.en: to encourage sb, especially sb in a race or competition, by shouting

ex.en: The crowd cheered the runners on.
ex.zh: 观众用喝彩声为赛跑选手加油。

senses.en: to become,or to make sb/yourself, happier or more cheerful

ex.en: She seems to have cheered up since Saturday.
ex.zh: 她打星期六开始似乎高兴起来。

ex.en: Cheer up!
ex.zh: 振作点！

senses.en: to make a room, etc. brighter and more cheerful
senses.zh: 给(房间等) 增色； 使明亮:

ex.en: Flowers always cheer up a room.
ex.zh: 房间里一有花就亮丽起来。

senses.en: () =CHEW STH OVER

ex.en: Why don’t we chew on it for a while?
ex.zh: 我们为什么不仔细考虑一段时间呢？

senses.en: to tell sb angrily that they have done sth wrong

ex.en: He got chewed out by his teacher for being late.
ex.zh: 他因为迟到挨老师骂了。

senses.en: to think about or discuss sth carefully and in detail
senses.zh: 仔细考虑；深思熟虑；详细讨论:

ex.en: He spent the weekend chewing over the problem.
ex.zh: 他利用周末细緻地考虑了这个问题。

senses.en: to bite sth until it is completely soft or destroyed

ex.en: The baby chewed the cookie up and swallowed it.
ex.zh: 孩子把饼乾嚼碎吞了。

senses.en: to decide not to do sth because you are afraid

ex.en: If I don’t fight him, everyone will say that I chickened out.
ex.zh: 如果我不和他打一场，大家都会说我软弱。

ex.en: She chickened out of telling him the truth.
ex.zh: 她吓得不敢告诉他真相。

senses.en: to relax completely and not get upset or excited about anything

ex.en: Chill out! We’ll get there on time!
ex.zh: 别紧张！我们会按时赶到的！

ex.en: I spent most of the weekend chilling out at my friend's house.
ex.zh: 我这个周末大部份时间都在朋友家悠闲地度过。

senses.en: [only before noun] that helps you to relax or makes you feel relaxed
senses.zh: 有助于放松的；使人轻松的:

ex.en: chill-out music
ex.zh: 令人轻松的音乐

ex.en: a chill-out room (= a place at a club, etc. where you can relax when you do not want to dance)
ex.zh: (俱乐部等的)休息室

senses.en: to join in a conversation suddenly or interrupt sb

ex.en: ‘Absolutely!’ she chimed in eagerly.
ex.zh: “当然了！”她急忙插嘴道。

ex.en: He kept chiming in with his own opinions.
ex.zh: 他不断插话发表自己的意见。

senses.en: to agree with sth; to be similar to sth

ex.en: His policies chimed in with the national mood at the time.
ex.zh: 他的政策与当时国民的心态相吻合。

senses.en: [NOTE]These phrasal verbs are usually used in written English.
senses.zh: 这些短语动词通常用于书面语。

senses.en: to make sth smaller or weaker by continuously breaking small pieces off it
senses.zh: 不停地削(或凿)…；不断削弱:

ex.en: He was chipping away at the rocks, looking for fossils.
ex.zh: 他不停地凿岩石寻找化石。

ex.en: () The government seems to be chipping away at people’s rights.
ex.zh: 政府似乎在不断削弱人民的权利。

senses.en: to remove sth by continuously breaking off small pieces

ex.en: She used a hammer to chip away the stone.
ex.zh: 她用锤子一点一点地敲掉那块石头。

ex.en: I chipped the rust off the box with a knife.
ex.zh: 我用刀刮箱子上的。

senses.en: to join in or interrupt a conversation; to add sth to a conversation

ex.en: Feel free to chip in if I’ve forgotten to mention anything.
ex.zh: 我如果忘记讲什么事，请随时补充。

ex.en: She chipped in with some interesting remarks.
ex.zh: 她插嘴说了几句有意思的话。

senses.en: to try to make sb move faster or do sth more quickly

ex.en: The teacher chivvied the children along.
ex.zh: 老师催孩子们加快速度。

senses.en: to try to stop yourself from showing a strong emotion, or saying sth that might upset sb
senses.zh: 忍住，抑制住，克制住(强烈的感情或要说的话):

ex.en: He choked back his tears.
ex.zh: 他强忍住眼泪。

ex.en: A protest rose to her lips, but she choked it back.
ex.zh: 她很想提抗议，但话到嘴边又咽了下去。

senses.en: to prevent or stop sth

ex.en: High interest rates have choked off investment.
ex.zh: 高利率窒碍了投资。

senses.en: to become, or to make sb, so upset that you/they are unable to speak

ex.en: That song really chokes me up.
ex.zh: 我听到那首歌时简直泣不成声。

senses.en: to aim blows at sth with a sharp heavy tool

ex.en: They chopped at the undergrowth with their machetes.
ex.zh: 他们抡着大刀砍灌木丛。

senses.en: to make sth such as a tree fall down by cutting it at the base with a sharp tool

ex.en: They’re chopping down thousands of trees every year.
ex.zh: 他们每年砍伐几千棵树。

senses.en: to remove sth by cutting it with a sharp heavy tool

ex.en: The king had his head chopped off.
ex.zh: 国王下令斩首处死了他。

ex.en: She chopped a branch off the tree.
ex.zh: 她从树上砍下一根树枝。

senses.en: to cut sth into small pieces with a knife or a sharp tool

ex.en: Shall we chop these logs up for firewood?
ex.zh: 要我们把这些原木噼成柴吗？

ex.en: I shall have to chop her food up very small for her.
ex.zh: 我要给她把食物切碎。

senses.en: to eat a lot of food

ex.en: We chowed down on fried chicken and salad.
ex.zh: 我们大嚼炸鸡和色拉。

senses.en: to not make good use of sth; to waste sth

ex.en: She’s chucking all her money away on presents for him.
ex.zh: 她乱花所有的钱给他买礼物。

ex.en: It’s too good an opportunity to chuck away.
ex.zh: 这是个好机会，不能错过。

senses.en: to rain very heavily

ex.en: It was chucking it down outside.
ex.zh: 外面大雨倾盆。

senses.en: to include sth extra with what you are selling or offering without increasing the price

ex.en: If you buy the freezer and the fridge we’ll chuck in a toaster.
ex.zh: 如果买冰柜和冰箱，我们免费赠送一个吐司炉。

senses.en: to decide to stop doing sth such as a job or a course of study

ex.en: What made you decide to chuck in your course?
ex.zh: 你为什么决定不上课了？

senses.en: to force sb to leave a place, a job, etc.
senses.zh: 强迫某人离开(处所、工作等)；撵走；解雇:

ex.en: Her parents chucked her out when she got pregnant.
ex.zh: 她怀孕后父母把她赶出了家门。

senses.en: to reject a plan, a proposal, etc.
senses.zh: 否决，拒绝接受(计划、提议等):

ex.en: The committee chucked my proposal out.
ex.zh: 委员会否决了我的提议。

senses.en: =CHUCK STH AWAY 2
to make steady but slow progress

ex.en: ‘Hi! How are things?’ ‘Oh, fine, just chugging along.’
ex.zh: “ 嗨！ 一切都好吗？”“喔，还好，就那么慢悠悠地一直进行着呢。

senses.en: to produce sth quickly in large amounts
senses.zh: 大量生产； 大量炮制:

ex.en: She churns out trashy romantic novels.
ex.zh: 她不断拼凑些无聊的爱情小说。

ex.en: They churn out 3 000 identical toy trains every day.
ex.zh: 他们每天生产3 000 辆一式一样的玩具火车。

senses.en: to make sb feel very upset, worried, frightened or angry
senses.zh: 使心神不安(或担忧、害怕、生气):

ex.en: When I drove away from the house for the last time, I was churned up inside.
ex.zh: 我最后一次驾车离开那所房子时心里十分烦闷。

senses.en: to ask for sth to be returned to you

ex.en: Claim your expenses back from the company.
ex.zh: 开支请向公司报销。

senses.en: to refuse to speak about sth because you are afraid, or want to keep it secret
senses.zh: 绝口不谈…；保持缄默；不敢作声；守口如瓶:

ex.en: He always clams up when we ask about his family.
ex.zh: 我们问起他的家庭时，他总是沉默不语。

senses.en: to become strict about sth in order to prevent sth happening, especially a crime, a protest, etc.
senses.zh: 严厉打击(犯罪、抗议示威等):

ex.en: The government intends to clamp down on drug smuggling.
ex.zh: 政府拟严厉打击毒品走私。

senses.en: sudden action that is taken by a government or other authority to stop a crime, a protest, etc.
senses.zh: (对犯罪活动、抗议示威等的)严禁，制止，取缔措施

senses.en: to force sb to accept sth unpleasant
senses.zh: 强制… 接受(不愉快的事情) :

ex.en: The army clamped on a curfew after the riots.
ex.zh: 骚乱之后军队实行了宵禁。

ex.en: The army clamped a curfew on the refugee camps.
ex.zh: 军队对难民营实行宵禁。

senses.en: to work hard to get sth back that you have lost

ex.en: They’re trying to claw back their share of the market.
ex.zh: 他们正设法夺回他们的市场份额。

senses.en: the act of a government getting back in tax the money it has paid to people; the money that is paid back
senses.zh: 通过税收收回补助金；通过税收收回的钱

senses.en: to clean sth thoroughly by wiping or brushing it
senses.zh: 把…彻底擦乾净(或刷乾净) :

ex.en: Clean down all the walls before repainting them.
ex.zh: 把墙壁都擦洗乾净再刷新油漆。

senses.en: to remove sth from the surface of sth by brushing, wiping,etc.

ex.en: She couldn’t be bothered to clean her make-up off.
ex.zh: 她懒得清洗掉化妆品。

ex.en: How can I clean red wine off the carpet?
ex.zh: 我怎么能清除地毯上的红酒？

senses.en: to use up or take all sb’s money; to take or buy the whole supply of sth that sb has
senses.zh: 把(某人的钱)耗尽；把…的…全部取去(或买清):

ex.en: Buying drinks for everyone cleaned me out.
ex.zh: 为大家购买饮料把我的钱花得一乾二净。

ex.en: It’s been a great year for sales. We’re completely cleaned out (= we’ve sold all our supply).
ex.zh: 这一年的销售很理想。我们把存货都卖光了。

senses.en: to clean the inside of sth thoroughly

ex.en: We clean the stables out every day.
ex.zh: 我们每天彻底清扫马。

senses.en: [usually sing.] () an occasion when you clean a room, house, cupboard,etc. thoroughly; the activity of cleaning a room, house, cupboard, etc. thoroughly
to be very successful; to win a lot of money or prizes
senses.zh: 十分成功；赚大钱；赢得很多奖:

ex.en: The movie cleaned up at the awards ceremony.
ex.zh: 这部电影在颁奖仪式上囊括了很多奖项。

senses.en: to wash yourself or make yourself clean

ex.en: I’ll just clean up before dinner.
ex.zh: 我晚饭前就洗漱一下。

ex.en: They cleaned themselves up and put on their best clothes.
ex.zh: 他们梳洗乾净换上了最好的衣服。

senses.en: to remove dirt, etc.from a place and make it clean

ex.en: I’ve got to clean up before my parents get home.
ex.zh: 我必须在父母回到家之前打扫乾净。

ex.en: Who’s going to clean the place up after you?
ex.zh: 你弄脏了这里谁会替你打扫？

senses.en: [usually sing.] the act of removing dirt, etc. from a place to clean it
to remove things that you have been using and no longer need in order to leave a clear space

ex.en: I’ll help you to clear away after tea.
ex.zh: 喝茶之后我帮你收拾好。

ex.en: to clear away the dishes
ex.zh: 收拾盘子

senses.en: to make sb leave a place

ex.en: The police cleared the demonstrators away.
ex.zh: 警察驱散了示威者。

senses.en: to go or run away

ex.en: You’ve no right to be here. Clear off!
ex.zh: 你无权在这里。走开！

ex.en: He cleared off as soon as he heard the police car.
ex.zh: 他一听到警车声便逃之夭夭。

senses.en: to leave a place quickly

ex.en: Would it be better for you if I just cleared out and went back to London?
ex.zh: 你是否觉得我最好马上离开这里回伦敦去？

ex.en: I told him to clear out of the house by Monday.
ex.zh: 我叫他星期一之前搬出这所房子。

senses.en: to make sth empty and clean by removing what you do not want

ex.en: I cleared out all the cupboards.
ex.zh: 我把橱柜全腾空了。

senses.en: [usually sing.] (, ) the act of throwing away all the things you no longer want or need or of getting rid of people you no longer want

ex.en: a clear-out of staff to reduce the wages bill
ex.zh: 为减少工资支出而进行的裁员

senses.en: to make sth clean and neat

ex.en: I’ll help you clear up.
ex.zh: 我来帮你收拾。

ex.en: Clear up the mess in here before you go.
ex.zh: 这里凌乱不堪，你收拾乾净再走。

senses.en: to solve a problem; to find an explanation for sth

ex.en: to clear up a mystery
ex.zh: 揭开谜团

ex.en: I’m glad we’ve cleared that misunderstanding up.
ex.zh: 我很高兴我们消除了误会。

senses.en: to admit that you are wrong or have made a mistake; to change your position in an argument
senses.zh: 承认错误；认错； 放弃立场:

ex.en: The president was forced to climb down and issue an apology.
ex.zh: 总统被迫让步并致歉。

senses.en: an act of admitting that you are wrong or have made a mistake; an act of changing your position in an argument
to be unwilling to stop doing, believing or thinking about sth; to be unwilling to get rid of sth

ex.en: I still cling to the hope that he’s alive.
ex.zh: 我依然希望他还活着。

ex.en: She’s clinging on to the past.
ex.zh: 她墨守过时的东西。

senses.en: to record the time that you arrive at work, especially by putting a card into a machine; to do this for sb or check the time they arrive at work
senses.zh: (尤指用机器)记录上班时间， 上班打卡:

ex.en: We arrived and clocked on for the night shift.
ex.zh: 我们到了单位就打卡接替夜班。

senses.en: to last or take a particular amount of time; to cost a particular amount of money
senses.zh: 持续，用去(时间)；耗费，花掉(钱):

ex.en: The fastest runner clocked in at 3 minutes 40 seconds.
ex.zh: 最快的赛跑选手用了3 分40 秒。

senses.en: to record the time that you leave work, especially by putting a card into a machine; to do this for sb
senses.zh: (尤指用机器)记录下班时间，下班打卡:

ex.en: Don’t forget to clock off when you leave.
ex.zh: 下班离开时别忘了打卡。

senses.en: to win or achieve a particular number or amount

ex.en: We’ve clocked up 500 miles (= we’ve travelled 500miles) today.
ex.zh: 我们今天旅行了500 英里。

ex.en: The company has clocked up record exports this year.
ex.zh: 公司今年的出口达到了最高纪录。

senses.en: to become, or to make sth, blocked so that nothing can move

ex.en: The pipe had clogged up (with mud).
ex.zh: 管子淤塞了。

ex.en: The roads were clogged up with traffic.
ex.zh: 道路上交通阻塞。

senses.en: to surround sb/sth, holding them/it tightly

ex.en: His fingers closed around her wrist.
ex.zh: 他的手指紧箍着她的手腕。

ex.en: () The darkness of the night was closing about him.
ex.zh: 夜晚的黑暗笼罩着他。

senses.en: [sing.] the end of broadcasting on television and radio until the next day
senses.zh: (电台或电视台每天的)结束播放，停止播音

senses.en: to make the distance between you and sb/sth else smaller, for example in a race
senses.zh: (赛跑等中)缩短同…的距离，逼近:

ex.en: I was slowly closing on the runner ahead of me.
ex.zh: 我慢慢追上了跑在我前面的人。

senses.en: to surround sth, covering it or holding it tightly
senses.zh: 遮盖； 绕紧； 箍紧:

ex.en: His fingers closed over the money.
ex.zh: 他的手紧紧地攥着那些钱。

senses.en: an occasion when a shop/store sells all remaining goods very cheaply before it stops operating

ex.en: a closeout sale
ex.zh: 歇业大减价

senses.en: to prevent light, sound, etc.from entering a place

ex.en: We need a curtain up there to close out the light.
ex.zh: 我们得在那里挂幅帘子遮挡光线。

senses.en: , ) to bring sth to an end

ex.en: The vote closed out the three-day debate.
ex.zh: 投票为三天的辩论画下句点。

senses.en: to close completely

ex.en: His eye had swollen and closed up.
ex.zh: 他的眼睛浮肿得瞇起来了。

ex.en: The cut took a long time to close up (= to heal).
ex.zh: 伤口过了很长时间才瘉合。

senses.en: to hide your thoughts and feelings

ex.en: She closed up when I mentioned her father.
ex.zh: 我提起她的父亲时她避而不谈。

senses.en: to shut and lock a building completely for a period of time

ex.en: You go on home. I’ll close up (=shut the shop/store).
ex.zh: 你尽管回家吧。我来关店门。

ex.en: He closes the shop up at 5.30.
ex.zh: 他在5 点30 分关店门。

senses.en: to behave in a silly way to make other people laugh
to give sb reliable information about sth

ex.en: Can you clue me in on the facts of the case?
ex.zh: 你能给我提供这个案子的实情吗？

senses.en: having a lot of information about sth
to form a group around sb/sth

ex.en: People clustered around the market stalls.
ex.zh: 人们围拢在市场的货摊上。

senses.en: to come together in a small group

ex.en: The children clustered together in a corner of the room.
ex.zh: 孩子们聚集在房间的角落里。

senses.en: to try to get hold of sb/sth suddenly

ex.en: She clutched at her stomach, obviously in pain.
ex.zh: 她一下子捂住肚子，显然很疼痛。

senses.en: to try every possible way to escape from a difficult situation even though there seems to be little hope of doing so
to fill or cover sth with lots of things so that it looks very untidy

ex.en: I’m sick of all these books cluttering up my office.
ex.zh: 我讨厌办公室里乱糟糟地堆放着这些书。

senses.en: to persuade sb to do sth by talking to them gently

ex.en: Can we coax you into singing for us?
ex.zh: 我们能请您为我们唱歌吗？

senses.en: to persuade sb not to do sth by talking to them gently

ex.en: Try to coax him out of resigning.
ex.zh: 尽量好言好语地说服他不要辞职。

senses.en: to persuade sb to do sth or to give you sth by talking gently

ex.en: She coaxed a smile from the baby.
ex.zh: 她把婴儿哄笑了。

senses.en: to put sth together or to make sth quickly or carelessly,with whatever time and materials you have available
senses.zh: 匆匆制作； 胡乱拼凑； 粗制漤造:

ex.en: () The government seems to have cobbled together these proposals.
ex.zh: 政府似乎草草拟订了这些提议。

senses.en: to spoil or ruin sth by doing it badly or by making a mistake
senses.zh: 把…搞糟(或弄得一塌煳涂):

ex.en: You’ve really cocked up this time.
ex.zh: 你这次确实弄得一塌煳涂。

ex.en: The travel agency completely cocked up the arrangements.
ex.zh: 旅行社完全没有按照预先的安排行事。

senses.en: a mistake that spoils or ruins plans or arrangements; sth that has been spoilt because it has been badly done

ex.en: She’s made a complete cock-up of the arrangements.
ex.zh: 她把计划全搞乱了。

senses.en: to wind into a series of circles; to make sth do this

ex.en: The snake coiled up in the sunshine.
ex.zh: 蛇在阳光下盘起来。

ex.en: He coiled the rope up neatly.
ex.zh: 他把绳子整齐地卷起来。

senses.en: to fill a shape, an area, etc. with colour, using pencils or pens

ex.en: Why don’t you colour the pictures in?
ex.zh: 你为什么不给这些画涂色呢？

senses.en: to use a comb to remove knots from your hair or to make it neat

ex.en: My hair’s so long that it takes me ages to comb it out.
ex.zh: 我的头发太长，要花很长时间才能梳理好。

senses.en: to happen

ex.en: It’s hard to understand how the accident came about.
ex.zh: 很难理解事故是怎样发生的。

senses.en: to provide orsupply sth that sb asks for, especially money
senses.zh: 提供，给予(所要求的，尤指金钱):

ex.en: They eventually came across with another $250 000.
ex.zh: 他们最后又提供了25万元。

ex.en: We still hope the company will come across for us.
ex.zh: 我们依然希望公司给予我们所需。

senses.en: to cross aroom, a road, a river, etc. towards the placewhere the speaker is
senses.zh: 走过(房间、道路、河等)到说话者处；过来:

ex.en: When you’ve done your homework, come across to my house and we’ll listen to some music.
ex.zh: 你写完作业之后就来我家，我们听听音乐。

ex.en: She waved and came across the room to talk to me.
ex.zh: 她向我招招手，然后从房间那边走过来和我说话。

senses.en: to meet or find sb/sth bychance, without having planned or thoughtabout it

ex.en: He’s the most unpleasant man I’ve ever come across.
ex.zh: 他是我见到过的最令人厌恶的男人。

ex.en: She came across a pile of old photographs while she was clearing the attic.
ex.zh: 她打扫阁楼时偶然发现了一沓旧照片。

senses.en: to chase or follow a personor an animal to try to catch them

ex.en: The farmer came after them, threatening to call the police.
ex.zh: 农夫一边追赶他们一边威胁说要报警。

senses.en: to arrive or appear somewhere;to start to exist, happen or be available

ex.en: It’s lucky you came along when you did or I’d have been stranded at the bus stop for an hour!
ex.zh: 真幸运那时你到了，否则我就得在公共汽车站耗上一小时！

ex.en: When the right opportunity comes along, he’ll take it.
ex.zh: 适当的机会来临时，他会抓住的。

senses.en: togo somewhere with sb

ex.en: We’re going to the pub. Do you want to come along?
ex.zh: 我们要去酒吧。你想一起来吗？

ex.en: You’d better come along with me to the police station.
ex.zh: 你最好跟我去趟警察局。

senses.en: =COME ON 4
come along!() =COME ON 1
to move forwardor from one end of sth to the other, towardsthe speaker

ex.en: I waited for ages for a bus, then three came along together!
ex.zh: 我等公共汽车等了好半天，然后一下子来了三辆！

ex.en: The lorry was coming along the road at great speed.
ex.zh: 大货车沿着马路高速开了过来。

senses.en: to move or travel around a corner

ex.en: The bus came round the bend too fast.
ex.zh: 公共汽车在弯道处开得太快。

senses.en: to move towards sb as if you are going to attack them

ex.en: She came at me with a knife.
ex.zh: 她拿着刀子向我扑过来。

ex.en: () The questions came at me so fast that I didn’t have time to think about them.
ex.zh: 问题像连珠炮一般向我袭来，以至于我无暇思考。

senses.en: to leave a place or a person

ex.en: Come away, now. There’s nothing to see.
ex.zh: 走吧。没什么可看的。

ex.en: Jane came away from the meeting feeling angry and upset.
ex.zh: 简又气又难过地离开了会场。

senses.en: to become separated from sth

ex.en: He pulled at the door handle until it came away in his hands.
ex.zh: 他用手拽门把，最后把它拽了下来。

ex.en: The plaster had started to come away from the wall.
ex.zh: 灰泥已开始从墙上脱落。

senses.en: to leave a place with a particular feeling, impression or result
senses.zh: 带着(某种感觉、印象或结果)离开:

ex.en: She came away from the championship with three medals.
ex.zh: 她从锦标赛上拿走了三枚奖牌。

ex.en: We came away with the impression that something was wrong.
ex.zh: 我们离去时觉得有些不对劲。

senses.en: to return to the place where the speaker is

ex.en: Come back here at once!
ex.zh: 马上回到这儿！

ex.en: Did she say when she was coming back?
ex.zh: 她说过何时回来吗？

senses.en: to return to school or work after a break

ex.en: Do you know when Bill is coming back to work?
ex.zh: 你知道比尔何时回来上班吗？

senses.en: to become popular, successful or fashionable again
senses.zh: 再受欢迎；再次成功；再度流行:

senses.en: (of a message or a reply
senses.zh: 信息或答覆) to be given in answer to a message,letter, etc. that you have sent or a question that you have asked返回；答覆:

ex.en: I sent her an email and a message came back that she was away.
ex.zh: 我给她发了个电子邮件，收到返回信息说她外出了。

senses.en: a way of getting payment or a reward for sth unfair or wrong that has been done to you

ex.en: Will I have no comeback if the contract falls through?
ex.zh: 如果撤消合同，我没有办法得到补偿吗？

senses.en: a quick reply that is often angry, insulting,clever or humorous
senses.zh: (生气、侮辱性、聪明或幽默的)迅速回答，当场反驳:

ex.en: For once in her life, she had no sharp comeback.
ex.zh: 她有生以来仅此一次没有立即提出尖刻的反驳。

senses.en: to return to a particular subject, an idea, etc. and start to talk about it or think about it

ex.en: I’ll come back to that point in a moment.
ex.zh: 我稍后就回到这一点上来。

ex.en: It always seems to come back to the question of money.
ex.zh: 话题似乎总是回到钱的问题上来。

senses.en: (of a legal case, a proposal or an issue
senses.zh: 法律案件、提议或议题) to be presented to sb/sth so that they can discuss it or make a decision or a judgement about it提交到…讨论(或作决定、审理):

ex.en: The case comes before the court next week.
ex.zh: 这案件提交法院，下周审理。

ex.en: The bill came before parliament last month.
ex.zh: 议案于上月呈交议会。

senses.en: to harm or disturb a relationship between two people; to prevent sb from doing,enjoying or having sth
senses.zh: 损害… 之间的关系；离间； 妨碍:

ex.en: Nobody will ever come between them.
ex.zh: 没有人会拆散他们。

ex.en: I don’t want to come between her and her work.
ex.zh: 我不想妨碍她工作。

senses.en: to pass sb/sth without stopping

ex.en: Some kids on bikes came by, but they didn’t notice me.
ex.zh: 一些骑自行车的孩子过去了，可他们没注意到我。

senses.en: ) to come to visit sb for a short time in a casual or informal way

ex.en: Thanks for coming by yesterday.
ex.zh: 感谢你昨天来看我。

ex.en: Come by on your way home from work.
ex.zh: 你下班回家的路上进来坐坐吧。

senses.en: to manage to get sth; to receive sth by chance
senses.zh: 设法得到(或获得) ； (偶然)收到，得到:

ex.en: Jobs are hard to come by these days.
ex.zh: 如今找工作很难。

ex.en: Information about the company was not easy to come by.
ex.zh: 有关这家公司的情报不容易弄到手。

senses.en: to break and fall to the ground

ex.en: Part of the ceiling had come down.
ex.zh: 天花板有一处塌了下来。

senses.en: to return to the reality of everyday life after a period of great excitement or a time when you have been living in a way that is not very practical
senses.zh: 回到现实中(停止白日梦):

ex.en: He came (back) down to earth with a bang when he discovered that all his money had run out.
ex.zh: 他发现自己的钱全用光了就猛醒过来。

senses.en: [usually sing.] () a situation which is not as good, important or interesting as one you have experienced previously

ex.en: It’s a bit of a comedown after her previous job.
ex.zh: 这比她的上一份工作稍差了点。

senses.en: to move from a higher place or position to a lower one, or from a distant place towards the speaker

ex.en: Come down from that tree!
ex.zh: 从树上下来！

ex.en: The car was coming down the road towards us.
ex.zh: 汽车沿着马路朝我们开来。

senses.en: to punish sb or criticize sb severely
senses.zh: 惩罚； 斥责； 训斥:

ex.en: The courts are coming down heavily on drug dealers.
ex.zh: 法庭要严惩毒品贩子。

ex.en: Don’t come down too hard on him — he’s young.
ex.zh: 不要太严厉地责备他─他还小呢。

senses.en: to be passed to sb from sb who lived in the past

ex.en: The estate came down to her from her grandfather.
ex.zh: 财产是祖父遗留给她的。

senses.en: to get an illness, often not a very serious one

ex.en: I came down with a bad cold.
ex.zh: 我得了重感冒。

ex.en: I think I’m coming down with something.
ex.zh: 我想我有点不舒服。

senses.en: to come to sb’s home, or to the place where sb/sth is in order to take them/it somewhere
senses.zh: 去接某人，去取某物(以带到另一处):

ex.en: The police came for him this morning.
ex.zh: 警察今天上午来把他带走。

ex.en: Have you come for the parcel?
ex.zh: 你是来取包裹的吗？

senses.en: to attack sb/sth

ex.en: Sam came for me with his fists.
ex.zh: 萨姆挥舞着拳头朝我打来。

senses.en: to appear or be produced

ex.en: He struck the rock and water came forth.
ex.zh: 他敲打石头，有水冒出来。

senses.en: [only before noun] about to happen or appear very soon

ex.en: Who is in charge of promoting the band’s forthcoming album?
ex.zh: 谁负责推销乐队即将推出的歌集唱片？

senses.en: [not before noun] ready or made available when you need it

ex.en: Unfortunately money for the project has not been very forthcoming.
ex.zh: 可惜这个项目的资金还不太到位。

senses.en: [not before noun] (of a person
senses.zh: 人)ready to give information when they are asked愿提供信息；配合:

ex.en: He’s not very forthcoming about his love life.
ex.zh: 他不大愿意谈他的爱情生活。

senses.en: to offer to give help,information, etc.
senses.zh: 主动提供(帮助或信息等):

ex.en: Police have asked witnesses to come forward.
ex.zh: 警方呼吁目击者站出来。

ex.en: We’re hoping that a sponsor will come forward with the extra money.
ex.zh: 我们希望有赞助者来出额外资金。

senses.en: to be born in or live in a particular place

ex.en: Where do you come from?
ex.zh: 你是什么地方的人？

ex.en: She comes from London.
ex.zh: 她是伦敦人。

senses.en: to finish a race in a particular position

ex.en: Which horse came in first?
ex.zh: 哪匹马得了第一名？

senses.en: to arrive; to be received

ex.en: News is coming in of a train crash in Scotland.
ex.zh: 刚收到的消息说苏格兰发生了火车撞车事故。

ex.en: We’ve got more work coming in than we can handle.
ex.zh: 工作是不断增加，让我们应接不暇。

senses.en: to become available

ex.en: English strawberries usually come in in June.
ex.zh: 英国的草莓通常在六月份上市。

ex.en: New jobs are coming in all the time.
ex.zh: 新的职位不断出现。

senses.en: to take part in a discussion,sometimes by interrupting sb

ex.en: I’d like to come in here.
ex.zh: 我现在想说几句。

ex.en: I wish he wouldn’t keep coming in with his stupid suggestions.
ex.zh: 我希望他不要没完没了地用那些愚蠢的建议打断别人的话。

senses.en: to come to your home, office, etc. in order to repair sth, or do some work

ex.en: A plumber’s coming in to look at the boiler.
ex.zh: 有位水暖工要来看看热水器。

senses.en: to be useful

ex.en: These boxes will come in handy when we move house.
ex.zh: 我们搬家时这些箱子会派上用场的。

senses.en: money that you receive regularly,especially as payment for work
[only before noun]
travelling towards a place and arriving there

ex.en: incoming flights/passengers
ex.zh: 进港航班/旅客

senses.en: (of the sea
senses.zh: 海水) coming towards the land涌向陆地的； 上涨的

senses.en: to enter a room or a building; to pass through sth such as a hole, a window, etc.
senses.zh: 进入(房间或建筑物)；通过(洞口、窗户等):

ex.en: I knocked and heard her say ‘Come in’.
ex.zh: 我敲了敲门听见她说“ 进来”。

ex.en: The rain’s coming in through that hole.
ex.zh: 雨从那个洞漏进来。

senses.en: to go to an office or the place where you work, in order to do some work
senses.zh: 到(办公室或工作的地方)去工作:

ex.en: Are you coming into the office tomorrow?
ex.zh: 你明天去办公室吗？

senses.en: to have a part to play in sth; to play a useful role

ex.en: I like the plan, but where do I come in (= what is my role)?
ex.zh: 我赞成这个计划，可我能起什么作用呢？

senses.en: to become fashionable; to start to be worn or used

ex.en: When did platform heels come in?
ex.zh: 松糕鞋跟是何时兴起的？

ex.en: Trolleybuses first came in in 1923.
ex.zh: 无轨电车最早出现于1923年。

senses.en: to receive sth, especially sth unpleasant

ex.en: The government has come in for severe criticism from all sides.
ex.zh: 政府遭到方方面面的严厉批评。

ex.en: The company came in for a lot of stick (= a lot of criticism) with their advertising campaign.
ex.zh: 公司的广告宣传运动备受谴责。

senses.en: to begin to exist, happen, etc.

ex.en: The cherry trees are coming into blossom.
ex.zh: 樱桃树开花了。

senses.en: to receive a large sum of money when sb dies

ex.en: She unexpectedly came into a fortune when her cousin died.
ex.zh: 表兄去世，她意外地继承了一大笔财产。

senses.en: to be important in a particular situation
to behave in the way other people behave, or in the way you should behave
to have the opportunity to show your/its qualities or abilities
senses.zh: 有机会表现(素质)；充分施展(才能):

ex.en: After two rather poor games, he finally came into his own in the game against Germany.
ex.zh: 经过两场表现很差的比赛之后，他终于在和德国队的比赛中发挥出自己的水平。

ex.en: This bike really comes into its own on rough ground.
ex.zh: 这辆自行车在高低不平的地面上才真正显示出它的特性。

senses.en: to happen as a result of sth
to be able to be removed

ex.en: Does this knob come off?
ex.zh: 这个旋钮能卸下来吗？

senses.en: () to take place; to happen

ex.en: Did your trip to New York ever come off?
ex.zh: 你去纽约的事最后成了吗？

senses.en: , )=COME ACROSS 2
to become detached or separated from sth

ex.en: The handle came off in my hand.
ex.zh: 把子掉在我手里了。

ex.en: A button has come off my coat.
ex.zh: 我的外套掉了一颗钮扣。

senses.en: to fall from sth

ex.en: My glasses came off when I tripped.
ex.zh: 我绊了一跤把眼镜摔掉了。

ex.en: She braked sharply and came off her bike.
ex.zh: 她猛一剎闸，从自行车上摔了下来。

senses.en: (of an actor or a performer
senses.zh: 演员) to walk onto the stage and start to perform登台；出场；上场:

ex.en: When are Westlife coming on?
ex.zh: 西城男孩何时出场？

senses.en: (in sport
senses.zh: 体育运动) (of a player 运动员) to join a team instead of another player during a game(比赛中替换别人)上场:

ex.en: Robson came on in place of Wilkins.
ex.zh: 罗布森替换威尔金斯上场。

senses.en: (of a television programme, etc.
senses.zh: 电视节目等) to start to be shown开始播送:

ex.en: What time does the news come on?
ex.zh: 新闻报道什么时候开始？

senses.en: [only before noun] advancing towards you; approaching you
to begin speaking to sb on the telephone

ex.en: I had a long talk with my mother, then my dad came on.
ex.zh: 我和母亲畅谈了一番，然后爸爸就来和我通话了。

ex.en: Sue came on the line for a chat.
ex.zh: 休打电话来聊天。

senses.en: to meet or find sb/sth by chance

ex.en: I came upon this beautiful vase in the attic.
ex.zh: 我在阁楼偶然看见了这只漂亮的花瓶。

senses.en: to behave in a way that clearly shows sb that you want to have a sexual relationship with them
senses.zh: 勾引， 勾搭(男人或女人)

senses.en: [usually sing.] () a remark or an action that is intended to attract sb
senses.zh: 试图吸引某人的话语(或行为)；引诱；诱惑

senses.en: to be published or produced

ex.en: Her new novel’s just come out.
ex.zh: 她的新小说刚出版。

ex.en: When do the exam results come out?
ex.zh: 考试成绩几时出来？

senses.en: to be shown clearly

ex.en: His arrogance comes out in every speech he makes.
ex.zh: 他每次讲话都表现得骄傲自大。

senses.en: ) to stop work and go on strike
to say openly that you are a homosexual (= a person who is sexually attracted to people of the same sex)
senses.zh: 公开表明自己是同性恋者

senses.en: to leave a place or appear from inside a place

ex.en: Come out! I know you’re in there!
ex.zh: 出来吧！我知道你在里面！

ex.en: I’ll speak to her as soon as she comes out of the meeting.
ex.zh: 她一开完会我就跟她说吧。

senses.en: to relax and become more confident and friendly with other people
senses.zh: 精神放松、更加自信和友好地与他人交往

senses.en: to add up to a particular costor sum

ex.en: The total bill comes out at over a thousand pounds.
ex.zh: 账单金额总计超过一千英镑。

senses.en: to say sth, especiallysth surprising or not polite
senses.zh: 说出(尤指令人吃惊或粗鲁的话):

ex.en: I can’t believe the things he comes out with!
ex.zh: 我难以相信他居然说出这种话！

ex.en: When I asked her why she was late, she just came out with a load of nonsense.
ex.zh: 我问她为什么迟到，她只是说了一堆废话。

senses.en: (of a feeling, a mood, etc.
senses.zh: 感觉、情绪等) to affect sb/sth 影响某人或某事物:

ex.en: I’m sorry — I don’t know what came over me (= Idon’t know what made me behave in that way).
ex.zh: 对不起─我不知道我是怎么了。

ex.en: A remarkable change has come over the group since he left.
ex.zh: 他离开之后那个组变化很大。

senses.en: to leave one group ofpeople in order to join a competing group; tochange from one opinion to another

ex.en: Some of their members have come over to our side.
ex.zh: 他们的一些成员转变立场，站到了我们这边。

senses.en: to pass infront of the speaker or the place where thespeaker is

ex.en: As I walked down the road, Charlie came past on his bike.
ex.zh: 我沿路走着时，查利骑自行车从我面前经过。

ex.en: I’ll bring the book round this evening on my way to night school — I’ve got to come past your house.
ex.zh: 我今晚上夜校时把书带来─我得经过你家。

senses.en: to become conscious again

ex.en: When she came round, her sister was sitting beside her bed.
ex.zh: 她醒来时，姐姐正坐在床边。

ex.en: He hasn’t yet come round after the anaesthetic.
ex.zh: 他麻醉后还没有苏醒过来。

senses.en: (of a letter or a document
senses.zh: 信或文件) to be passedfrom one person to another传递；传阅:

ex.en: The card came round for everyone to sign.
ex.zh: 贺卡传给每个人签名。

senses.en: to travel to where the speaker is by alonger route than usual, especially around theoutside of sth

ex.en: The road was blocked so we had to come round by the fields.
ex.zh: 道路堵塞了，我们只得从野地里绕过来。

senses.en: to enter and cross a room, an area of land, a town, a country, etc.; to pass through sth

ex.en: Put something over the hole to stop the rain coming through.
ex.zh: 把洞遮盖上以免漏雨。

senses.en: to get better after a serious illness; to avoid serious injury or damage

ex.en: He’s very ill but his doctors expect him to come through the operation.
ex.zh: 他病得很重，但医生估计手术后能挺过去。

senses.en: to start to appear from under or behind sth

ex.en: The baby’s front teeth were coming through.
ex.zh: 婴儿的门牙露头了。

ex.en: The sun’s coming through the clouds at last.
ex.zh: 太阳终于拨云而出。

senses.en: ) (of money, property,etc.
senses.zh: 钱财等) to pass to sb else when sb dies遗传给:

ex.en: All my money will come to you when I die.
ex.zh: 我去世以后我的钱全都是你的。

senses.en: to return to your normal state

ex.en: It took her a while to come to herself again.
ex.zh: 她过了一会儿才回过神来。

senses.en: be included within a particular group or collection of things

ex.en: Several different types of schools come under the heading of ‘private schools’.
ex.zh: 几种学校可归到“私立学校”类。

senses.en: (of plants
senses.zh: 植物) to appear above the ground长出地面；破土而出:

ex.en: The first snowdrops are just coming up.
ex.zh: 最早的雪花莲刚破土发芽。

senses.en: to rise to the surface of water or another liquid

ex.en: I came up gasping for air.
ex.zh: 我浮出来大口呼吸。

ex.en: Bubbles were coming up to the surface.
ex.zh: 气泡不断地冒出水面。

senses.en: to happen,especially when you do not expect it

ex.en: Something urgent has come up; I have to go.
ex.zh: 有紧急事情发生了；我必须走了。

ex.en: Opportunities like this don’t come up every day.
ex.zh: 这种机遇不是每天都有的。

senses.zh: (总是用于进行时) (of an event or a time事情或时间) to be going to happen very soon即将发生(或出现、到来):

ex.en: Our exams are coming up soon.
ex.zh: 我们马上要考试了。

ex.en: Coming up next is the news.
ex.zh: 以下是新闻报道。

senses.en: to be talked about or discussed

ex.en: The subject didn’t come up in conversation last night.
ex.zh: 昨晚的谈话中没有提到这个课题。

ex.en: Mary’s name keeps coming up.
ex.zh: 玛丽的名字一再被提到。

senses.zh: (通常用于进行时) to be ready soon; to be coming soon马上备妥；马上来到:

ex.en: ‘A cup of tea please.’ ‘Coming up!’
ex.zh: “请来杯茶。

senses.en: (of information
senses.zh: 信息) to appear on a computer screen or a board, for example in an airport出现，显示(在电脑屏幕或布告牌上):

ex.en: Her flight has just come up on the arrivals board.
ex.zh: 她乘坐的航班刚刚显示在进港布告牌上。

senses.en: (of lights in a cinema,a theatre, etc.
senses.zh: 影院、剧院等的灯光) to become brighter after the film/movie, play, etc. has finished(放映或演出结束时)被打亮:

ex.en: The lights came up to loud applause.
ex.zh: 灯光随着雷鸣般的掌声被打亮了。

senses.en: [only before noun] ()making good progress and likely to be successful in the future
senses.zh: 初露头角的；潜力巨大的:

ex.en: an up-and-coming young actor
ex.zh: 一个初露头角的年青演员

senses.en: [only before noun] () about to happen soon
senses.zh: 即将发生的；就要出现的:

ex.en: the upcoming presidential election
ex.zh: 即将举行的总统选举

senses.en: to move from a lower place or position to a higher one, or upstairs in a building, especially with the speaker or towards the place where the speaker is

ex.en: Who wants to come up to the top of the hill with me?
ex.zh: 谁想和我爬到山顶上去？

ex.en: My apartment is on the third floor. Are you coming up?
ex.zh: 我的单元在三楼。你要上来吗？

senses.en: to come to the time when sth must be done

ex.en: He’s coming up for retirement soon.
ex.zh: 他很快就要退休了。

ex.en: She comes up for re-election next year.
ex.zh: 她明年将再度参加选举。

senses.en: to be almost a particular time or age

ex.en: It’s coming up on your bedtime.
ex.zh: 你该睡觉了。

senses.en: to approach a particular place, an age or a period of time

ex.en: You’re coming up to a busy road now.
ex.zh: 你正开上拥挤路段。

ex.en: It’s just coming up to half past twelve.
ex.zh: 就快到十二点半了。

senses.en: to reach an acceptable level or standard
senses.zh: 达到(认可的水平或标准):

ex.en: The performance didn’t come up to our expectations.
ex.zh: 演出没有我们预想得那么好。

senses.en: to think of an idea, an answer to a question or a solution to a problem
senses.zh: 想到(主意)；找到(答案或解决方法):

ex.en: She came up with a great idea for increasing sales.
ex.zh: 她想出了增加销售量的绝妙主意。

senses.en: to be included with or as part of sth
senses.zh: 包括在(某事物)中；是…的一部份:

ex.en: A new car comes with the job.
ex.zh: 这份工作配有一辆新汽车。

senses.en: to say that you feel ill or are suffering from a pain

ex.en: Several children complained of severe stomach pains.
ex.zh: 有几个孩子说肚子很疼。

senses.en: to say what sb’s punishment will be
senses.zh: 宣判；判处某人某种刑罚:

ex.en: to be condemned to death/hard labour
ex.zh: 被判处死刑/劳役

senses.en: to force sb to accept a difficult or unpleasant situation
senses.zh: 迫使…接受困境(或不愉快的状况):

ex.en: They were condemned to a life of hardship.
ex.zh: 他们被迫过着困苦的生活。

senses.en: to tell sb a secret or a piece of information that you wouldn’t tell other people
senses.zh: 向(某人)透露秘密(或消息):

ex.en: Can I confide in you?
ex.zh: 你能保证不说给别人听吗？

ex.en: Do you have a friend that you can confide in?
ex.zh: 你有心腹知己吗？

senses.en: to keep sb/sth/yourself inside the limits of a particular activity, subject, area, etc.
senses.zh: 把…限制在(某范围)内；将…局限于:

ex.en: The work will not be confined to the Glasgow area.
ex.zh: 这一工作不会局限于格拉斯哥地区。

senses.en: to make sb face or deal with an unpleasant or difficult person or situation
senses.zh: 使面对，使面临，使对付(困难或令人不快的人或事物):

ex.en: He confronted her with a choice between her career or their relationship.
ex.zh: 他要她在事业和他们两人关系之间作出抉择。

senses.en: to have sth in front of you that you have to deal with or react to

ex.en: Most people when confronted with a horse will pat it.
ex.zh: 大多数人遇见马时都会拍拍它。

senses.en: to make sb/sth appear suddenly or unexpectedly, as if by magic
senses.zh: (变魔术般地) 使… 出现:

ex.en: She conjured up a three-course meal in half an hour!
ex.zh: 她用半小时变出了一顿有三道菜的饭！

senses.en: to make a picture, a memory,etc. appear in your mind

ex.en: The word ‘birthday’ conjures up images of presents and parties.
ex.zh: “生日”这个词使人想起礼物和聚会的情景。

ex.en: The song conjured up memories of warm summer evenings.
ex.zh: 这首歌唤起了温暖夏夜的回忆。

senses.en: , ) (of a person
senses.zh: 人) to collapse or become unconscious昏倒；晕倒

senses.en: ) to die

ex.en: The old guy looks as if he’s going to conk out any minute.
ex.zh: 那位老人看上去随时都会死去。

senses.en: to join sth to a supply of electricity, gas, water,etc. or to another piece of equipment; to be joined to sth in this way
senses.zh: 将…(与电源、煤气、水等)连接起来，接通:

ex.en: Connect the computer up (to the power supply).
ex.zh: 给计算机接通电源。

ex.en: Many canals connected up to major ports.
ex.zh: 很多运河通往重要港口。

senses.en: to ignore or seem to allow sth that you know is wrong
senses.zh: 对(明知错误的事情)视而不见；默许；纵容:

ex.en: The general is accused of conniving in a plot to topple the government.
ex.zh: 将军被指控纵容一个颠覆政府的阴谋。

ex.en: Her brother is believed to have connived at her murder.
ex.zh: 据信她的哥哥没有制止对她的谋杀。

senses.en: to get rid of or put somewhere sb/sth that you do not want
senses.zh: 丢弃，抛弃(人或物)；把…搁置一旁:

ex.en: She consigned his letter to the waste basket.
ex.zh: 她把他的信丢进废纸篓。

ex.en: () They can’t just consign me to the scrap heap because I’m over fifty!
ex.zh: 他们不能因为我超过五十岁就弃我不顾！

senses.en: to put sb/sth in an unpleasant situation
senses.zh: 把…置于(令人不快的境地)；打发；发落:

ex.en: Orphaned children were consigned to institutions.
ex.zh: 孤儿都打发到了福利院。

senses.zh: (不用于进行时) to have sth as the main or only feature存在于； 在于:

ex.en: A home does not consist in the quality of its architecture and decoration.
ex.zh: 家之所以为家并不在于住所的设计与修饰。

senses.zh: (不用于进行时) to be formed from the things or people mentioned由…组成(或构成):

ex.en: The exam consists of two parts:a written test and an oral.
ex.zh: 考试分两部份： 笔试和口试。

ex.en: The group consists of senior people from education and business.
ex.zh: 这个组由桝育界和企业界的元老组成。

senses.en: to spend time with sb, especially sb that other people do not approve of
senses.zh: 与(某人)来往；结交(尤指不合适的人):

ex.en: The nurses are instructed not to consort with their patients.
ex.zh: 护士得到指示不得与病人交往。

senses.en: to have to deal with a difficult person or situation
senses.zh: (不得不)处理问题，对付困境(或难处的人):

ex.en: If we leave at 8, we’ll have to contend with the rush-hour traffic.
ex.zh: 我们若8点钟出发就会遇上交通高峰时间。

ex.en: Anyone who criticizes her will have me to contend with!
ex.zh: 任何批评她的人都得面对我！

senses.en: to accept and be satisfied with sth and not try to have or do sth better
senses.zh: 满足于，安于(现状)；不求更好:

ex.en: Martina contented herself with a single glass of wine.
ex.zh: 马蒂娜只喝了一杯葡萄酒就心满意足了。

ex.en: The crowd contented themselves with shouting insults.
ex.zh: 那群人只顾着破口大骂。

senses.en: to choose to become involved in and formally agree to a system, plan, etc.

ex.en: Employees can contract into the company pension scheme.
ex.zh: 雇员可签订养老金计划的合约。

senses.en: to choose and formally state that you do not want to be involved in a system, plan, etc.
senses.zh: 订约不参与；退出(或不参加)…合约:

ex.en: Only a few employees have contracted out () so far.
ex.zh: 迄今只有少数几个雇员不参加养老金计划。

senses.en: to arrange for work to be done by another company rather than your own

ex.en: The company contracts the printing out to an outside firm.
ex.zh: 公司订约把印刷业务承包给外面的一家公司。

senses.en: to help to cause sth

ex.en: The stress of losing his job contributed to his death.
ex.zh: 失业的压力是导致他死亡的一个原因。

ex.en: The Prime Minister contributed to his own downfall by failing to control his government.
ex.zh: 首相未能管治好他的政府，加速了他本人下台。

senses.en: to be able to be changed from one form, purpose,or system to another; to make sth do this
senses.zh: 可变成(另一种形式等)；使…成为另一种形式(或目的等) :

ex.en: a sofa that converts into a bed
ex.zh: 可改作床铺的沙发

senses.en: to cook sth, especially very quickly

ex.en: In half an hour she had managed to cook up some delicious chilli.
ex.zh: 她用半个小时就做好了美味可口的辣味肉豆。

senses.en: to become, or to make sb become, less angry or excited

ex.en: She’s very angry. Give her some time to cool down.
ex.zh: 她十分生气。给她点时间冷静一下。

ex.en: He tried to cool her down but she carried on shouting.
ex.zh: 他试图让她平静下来，可她继续大喊大叫。

senses.en: to become, or to make sth become, cooler

ex.en: He waited for the soup to cool down a bit.
ex.zh: 他等着汤稍微凉一凉。

ex.en: Once it had cooled down outside, we went for a walk.
ex.zh: 外面一凉爽下来，我们就去散步。

senses.en: to become less interested or enthusiastic
