ex.en: Our relationship was going well, but then Laura seemed to cool off.
ex.zh: 正当我们的关系进展顺利时，劳拉却似乎冷淡下来了。

senses.en: to become less angry or excited

ex.en: When I’m angry, I go for a walk to cool off.
ex.zh: 我生气时就去散步消消气。

senses.en: a period of time in which two sides in a dispute try to come to an agreement before taking any further action
senses.zh: (争执双方试图达成协议的)冷却期:

ex.en: There is to be a six month cooling-off period before divorce proceedings begin.
ex.zh: 离婚诉讼开始前有六个月的冷却期。

ex.en: The union and the employers failed to reach an agreement within the coolingoff period.
ex.zh: 工会和资方在冷却期内未能达成共识。

senses.en: a period of time when you can change your mind about buying sth, such as an insurance plan, that you have agreed to buy
senses.zh: (在同意购买保险计划等后可改变主意的)冷静期，试用期:

ex.en: Customers have a 14-day cooling-off period in which to cancel the agreement.
ex.zh: 客户有14天的冷静期可以终止协议。

senses.en: to meet sb and start a sexual relationship with them
to avoid or not do sth that you should be doing, because you are afraid, shy, lazy, etc.

ex.en: Lots of people said they’d help but they’ve all copped out.
ex.zh: 有很多人许诺帮忙，可他们都退缩了。

ex.en: You can’t just cop out of difficult decisions.
ex.zh: 你不能因为困难就不做决定。

senses.en: a way of,or an excuse for, avoiding sth you should be doing

ex.en: You’re not too busy to come! That’s just a cop-out.
ex.zh: 你不是忙得来不了！那只不过是个藉口。

senses.en: to write sth exactly as it is written somewhere else

ex.en: If I don’t copy the phone number down, I’ll forget it!
ex.zh: 我若不抄下电话号码就会忘记的！

ex.en: We copied down what the teacher had written on the blackboard.
ex.zh: 我们把老师写在黑板上的东西抄下来。

senses.en: to make sure that sb receives a copy of a letter, an electronic message, etc. that you are sending to sb else
senses.zh: 抄送某人(让其看到发给其他人的信函或电邮等):

ex.en: Please copy me in on all correspondence.
ex.zh: 请把所有信函都抄送我。

senses.en: to write sth out again; to make a copy of sth that is already written or printed

ex.en: She copied out a recipe she found in a library book.
ex.zh: 她把在图书馆的书上找到的食谱抄下来。

senses.en: to stop people going into an area by forming a line or ring around it with police,soldiers, objects, etc.
senses.zh: 封锁(某范围)；在…设警戒线:

ex.en: Police cordoned off the area until the bomb was defused.
ex.zh: 警方封锁了这个地区直到炸弹被拆除为止。

senses.en: to estimate how much money will be needed for sth

ex.en: We’ll have to cost the work out before we make a decision.
ex.zh: 我们在作决定之前得估算一下这项工作的成本。

ex.en: Have you costed out how much it will be to hire another member of staff?
ex.zh: 你估计过再雇用一名职员的开支吗？

senses.en: to try to become friendly with sb, especially in order to gain an advantage for yourself
senses.zh: 和… 套近乎；讨好；奉承:

ex.en: She’s only cosying up to him because she needs his help.
ex.zh: 她只不过是在巴结他，因为她需要他帮忙。

senses.en: to come to understand or realize sth without being told directly

ex.en: She cottons on very quickly.
ex.zh: 她领会事情很快。

ex.en: It took him a while to cotton on to what I was trying to say.
ex.zh: 他过了一会儿才明白我的意思。

senses.en: to begin to like or approve of sb/sth

ex.en: I didn’t much cotton to the idea at first.
ex.zh: 我起初并不十分赞同这个想法。

senses.en: ) to pay for sth or give sb money unwillingly

ex.en: You owe me ￡20. Come on, cough up!
ex.zh: 你欠我20 英镑。快点掏腰包吧！

ex.en: Don’t cough up the money until the job’s finished.
ex.zh: 活干完之前不要掏钱。

senses.en: () to admit sth or give sb information unwillingly
senses.zh: 不情愿地承认(或提供信息) :

ex.en: Come on, cough up:where’ve you been?
ex.zh: 快点说，你去哪儿了？

senses.en: to force sth out of the throat or lungs by coughing

ex.en: He’s been coughing up blood.
ex.zh: 他一直在咳血。

senses.en: to be a disadvantage to sb

ex.en: I’m sure that being late for the interview counted against me.
ex.zh: 我肯定面试迟到对我不利。

senses.en: to be considered, or to consider sb/sth, to be part of the group mentioned
senses.zh: 被视为，把…看作(某集体的成员):

ex.en: She counts among the top ten marathon runners in the country.
ex.zh: 她跻身全国马拉松选手的前十名。

ex.en: The band count John Lennon among their influences.
ex.zh: 乐队把约翰…列农视为对他们有影响的人物之一。

senses.en: to be waiting for an important or exciting day, event,etc. and be counting the number of days, minutes,etc. there are before it

ex.en: The whole world was counting down to the new millennium.
ex.zh: 全世界都在倒计时迎接新千年的到来。

ex.en: I’m counting down the days until my trip.
ex.zh: 我在数着日子期盼旅行的到来。

senses.en: the act of counting backwards to zero, for example before a spacecraft is sent into space
the period immediately before sth important happens
to include sb in a group or an activity

ex.en: If you’re going to the theatre, you can count me in.
ex.zh: 你们若去看戏就把我也算上！

senses.en: to rely on sb to do sth; to expect sth to happen and make plans in an appropriate way
senses.zh: 依赖，依靠，指望(某人做某事)；预期(某事发生):

ex.en: You can count on me!
ex.zh: 我决不辜负你！

ex.en: ‘I’m sure he’ll help us.’ ‘Don’t count on it.’
ex.zh: “我肯定他会帮我们的。”“那可靠不住。”

senses.en: These phrasal verbs can be used in the passive.
senses.zh: 这些短语动词可用于被动语态:

ex.en: She can be counted upon to contribute good ideas.
ex.zh: 她总能想到好点子。

senses.en: to not include sb in a group or an activity
senses.zh: 不把某人算入； 不包括:

ex.en: You may enjoy those games, but you can count me out.
ex.zh: 你们可以观看那些比赛，可别把我算在内。

senses.en: to count coins, etc. one by one and put them somewhere

ex.en: He counted out the exact money (on the counter).
ex.zh: 他(在柜台上)逐一数出了准确金额。

senses.en: to be included as part of sth you hope to obtain or achieve
senses.zh: 计入(希望获得或争取的事物中):

ex.en: Marks from this test count towards your final grade.
ex.zh: 这次测验的分数将计入你们的期末成绩。

ex.en: These sales will not count toward meeting the target.
ex.zh: 这些销售额不会算作完成目标的一部份。

senses.en: to add together the number of things or people in a group

ex.en: Count up the number of times you’ve been abroad.
ex.zh: 数数你一共出国几次。

senses.en: to link one person,thing or situation with another

ex.en: The large number of new graduates, coupled with high unemployment, means that there is fierce competition for jobs.
ex.zh: 大量的新毕业生加上高失业率意味着求职竞争很激烈。

senses.en: to cover sth completely,especially to hide or protect it

ex.en: Put the bulbs in a bowl and cover them over with soil.
ex.zh: 把鳞茎放在盆里，用土壤覆盖。

ex.en: The shopping mall is covered over with an enormous glass roof.
ex.zh: 购物中心上方罩着巨大的玻璃顶。

senses.en: to put on more clothes

ex.en: Make sure you cover up before going out in the sun.
ex.zh: 一定要穿衣服把身体遮盖好再外出暴露在阳光中。

ex.en: Cover yourself up. It’s cold.
ex.zh: 穿暖和点。天气很冷。

senses.en: to try hard to stop people finding out about a mistake, a crime, etc.; to hide the truth about sth
senses.zh: (为…)掩盖， 隐瞒(错误、罪行、真相等) :

ex.en: He’s always covering up for her.
ex.zh: 他总是护着她。

ex.en: The government’s attempts to cover up the scandal failed.
ex.zh: 政府企图掩盖丑闻，但失败了。

senses.en: [usually sing.] an act of hiding a mistake, a crime, etc.

ex.en: The opposition accused the government of a cover-up.
ex.zh: 反对派指责政府隐瞒真相。

senses.en: to put sth over sb/sth in order to hide or protect them/it

ex.en: You can cover up ugly pipes with wooden boxes.
ex.zh: 你可以用木盒扣住这些难看的管子。

ex.en: There was something on the table covered up with a cloth.
ex.zh: 桌子上有东西用布罩着。

senses.en: to try harder to prevent people breaking a rule, using sth harmful, committing a crime, etc. and deal severely with those who do
senses.zh: 竭力取缔；严厉打击；镇压:

ex.en: Police are cracking down hard on drug dealers.
ex.zh: 警方正在严厉打击毒品贩子。

ex.en: The government is cracking down on misleading food labelling.
ex.zh: 政府正竭力取缔误导性食物标籤。

senses.en: severe action that is taken to prevent people committing a crime,opposing the government, etc.

ex.en: a police crackdown on car crime
ex.zh: 警方对汽车犯罪的严厉打击

senses.en: to work hard and do sth quickly

ex.en: We’d better crack on with the painting before it gets dark.
ex.zh: 我们最好加把劲赶在天黑之前刷完漆。

senses.en: to become physically or mentally ill because you are under pressure
senses.zh: (因压力造成身体或精神)垮掉，崩溃:

ex.en: She’s cracking up under the strain.
ex.zh: 过大的压力使她快垮掉了。

senses.en: a period of mental illness caused by pressure
to start laughing a lot; to make sb laugh a lot

ex.en: Everybody cracked up when he fell over.
ex.zh: 他摔了一跤，引起一阵哄笑。

ex.en: She’s so funny — she cracks me up!
ex.zh: 她真滑稽─逗得我哈哈大笑。

senses.en: to go into a place or space that is too small for everyone/everything; to push or force sb/sth into a place or space that is too small

ex.en: Six of us crammed into Rob’s Mini.
ex.zh: 我们六人挤进了罗布的迷你牌汽车里。

ex.en: I only had three days in New York, but I crammed in as much sightseeing as I could.
ex.zh: 我在纽约只呆了三天时间，可我尽可能多看了些地方。

senses.en: to produce sth quickly and in large amounts
senses.zh: 大量地快速制造；粗制漤造:

ex.en: The plant can crank out about 63 cars an hour.
ex.zh: 工厂每小时可生产汽车63辆之多。

senses.en: to make a machine start working or work better
senses.zh: 使机器运转；使…提高效率:

ex.en: It’s time to crank up the air conditioning.
ex.zh: 该打开空调了。

senses.en: to make music, etc. louder
senses.zh: 把(音乐等的) 音量调高:

ex.en: They cranked the music up when the party started.
ex.zh: 晚会开始时他们把音乐的音量放大了。

senses.en: to move around making a lot of noise

ex.en: I heard her crashing about in the bathroom.
ex.zh: 我听到她在浴室哗啦啦地折腾。

senses.en: to fall with a very loud noise
senses.zh: 轰隆一声倒下(或坠落、落下):

ex.en: Passengers had a lucky escape when a huge tree crashed down onto a bus.
ex.zh: 大树哗啦一声倒在公共汽车上，幸好乘客安然无恙。

senses.en: to go to sleep because you are very tired

ex.en: I was so tired I crashed out in an armchair.
ex.zh: 我十分疲倦，在扶手椅上睡着了。

senses.en: (in sport
senses.zh: 体育运动) to lose a game very badly and so not be able to continue to take part in a competition(被淘汰)出局:

ex.en: England crashed out of the World Cup.
ex.zh: 英格兰队在世界杯比赛中遭淘汰。

senses.en: [NOTE]This phrasal verb is used especially in newspapers.
senses.zh: 这个短语动词尤用于报章。

senses.en: to be full of moving people, animals, insects, etc. in an unpleasant way
senses.zh: 满是移动中的(人或动物、昆虫等):

ex.en: The place is crawling with cops!
ex.zh: 这地方到处是警察！

senses.en: to take away the best people or things in a group or an amount of money, usually for your own advantage
senses.zh: 提取(精华) ；选取(最好的人或物)；取走(某数额的金钱):

ex.en: The best pupils are creamed off into special classes.
ex.zh: 最优秀的学生都编到特别班。

ex.en: The company’s directors are creaming off the profits.
ex.zh: 公司董事分配利润。

senses.en: to start laughing; to make sb start laughing

ex.en: We all creased up when we saw her hat!
ex.zh: 我们看到她的帽子都哈哈大笑起来！

ex.en: His programme always creases me up.
ex.zh: 他的节目总是令我捧腹。

senses.en: to believe that sb/sth is responsible for sth or for doing sth,especially sth good
senses.zh: 认为…负责某事(或做某事) ； 把… 归功于:

ex.en: Bach is credited with performing the first solo on a piano.
ex.zh: 人们认为巴赫是演奏第一首钢琴独奏曲的人。

ex.en: She credits her good looks and intelligence to her father’s side of the family.
ex.zh: 她认为她的美貌和才智是父亲的血统遗传的。

senses.en: to consider that sb/sth has a particular good quality or characteristic
senses.zh: 认为… 有…品质(或特点):

ex.en: I had credited him with more sense.
ex.zh: 我原以为他会更加理智。

ex.en: Numerous health benefits are credited to this natural oil.
ex.zh: 人们认为这种天然的油对健康有很多好处。

senses.en: to start happening or affecting sb/sth gradually

ex.en: I thought I’d decided, but then doubts started to creep in.
ex.zh: 我原以为自己拿定主意了，可后来却开始疑惑起来。

ex.en: A hint of sarcasm crept into his voice.
ex.zh: 他的语气带一丝嘲讽。

senses.en: to remove sb’s name or an item from a list by drawing a line through it because you have dealt with them/it or they/it are no longer involved

ex.en: Cross off any items we’ve already got.
ex.zh: 把我们已有的物品都画掉。

ex.en: Jane won’t be coming, so we can cross her off the list.
ex.zh: 简不来了，我们可以把她的名字画掉。

senses.en: to remove words from a text by drawing a line through them, usually because they are wrong

ex.en: I crossed his name out and wrote mine instead.
ex.zh: 我删掉他的名字填写了我的。

ex.en: You’ve spelt it wrong. Cross it out and try again.
ex.zh: 你把字拼错了。画掉再写一遍。

senses.en: a successful combination of different styles or types of music or culture; a successful change from one style or type to another
senses.zh: (不同音乐或文化风格或种类的)结合，转变:

ex.en: a fresh and exciting rock-dance crossover
ex.zh: 摇磙乐与舞蹈的新颖且生动的彻底融合

ex.en: a crossover artist
ex.zh: 完全转变风格的艺术家

senses.en: to bend over sb/sth so you are near them/it

ex.en: She crouched over the injured man, checking his wounds.
ex.zh: 她俯身检查伤员的伤口。

senses.en: to move in large numbers into a small place

ex.en: As soon as the doors opened people began to crowd in.
ex.zh: 门一开人们便开始涌入。

ex.en: We all crowded into the lift.
ex.zh: 我们全都涌进电梯。

senses.en: to put a large number of people or things into a small space

ex.en: I doubt if we can crowd any more people in — the place is packed already.
ex.zh: 我怀疑我们能否再塞进人了─这里已经拥挤不堪。

ex.en: We were all crowded into a small area behind the goal.
ex.zh: 我们全都挤在球门后面的一小块地方。

senses.en: to gather in large numbers around sb/sth

ex.en: People were crowding around to see what was going on.
ex.zh: 人们聚过来围观。

ex.en: Fans crowded round him to ask for his autograph.
ex.zh: 崇拜者围着他要签名。

senses.en: to crush sth, especially a piece of paper, into a ball

ex.en: She crumpled his letter up without even looking at it.
ex.zh: 她连看都没看就把他的信揉成一团。

senses.en: to ask for or demand sth in a forceful or urgent way

ex.en: The families of the victims are crying for justice.
ex.zh: 受害者家属强烈呼吁公正审判。

ex.en: Listen! That sounds like somebody crying (= calling) for help.
ex.zh: 听！那声音像是有人在喊救命。

senses.en: to decide not to do sth you have promised or agreed to do
senses.zh: 不履行(诺言等) ； 食言:

ex.en: We’d arranged to go together but Luis cried off at the last moment.
ex.zh: 我们说好一起去的，可卢斯到时候又变卦了。

ex.en: Why did you cry off training last night?
ex.zh: 你昨晚为什么临时不来参加训练？

senses.en: to make a loud sound without words because you are hurt, afraid, surprised, etc.
senses.zh: (因伤痛、害怕、惊讶等)大叫，叫喊:

ex.en: She cried out in/with pain.
ex.zh: 她疼痛得大叫起来。

senses.en: to protest strongly about sth
senses.zh: 强烈抗议；大声疾呼反对:

ex.en: People have been crying out against this abuse for years.
ex.zh: 多年来人们一直在强烈谴责这种漤用情况。

senses.en: [C] [U] a public reaction of strong protest against sth

ex.en: There is sure to be a massive outcry against the proposals.
ex.zh: 这些提案定会遭到公众大规模的强烈抗议。

senses.en: to clearly need sth very quickly

ex.en: The group is crying out for new members.
ex.zh: 这个组急需新成员。

ex.en: The whole system was crying out for a radical review.
ex.zh: 整个体系亟待彻底检讨。

senses.en: to try to be friendly to sb in order to gain an advantage for yourself

ex.en: Just before the election they started cuddling up to the government.
ex.zh: 他们就在选举之前开始靠拢政府。

senses.en: to end with a particular result or conclusion, or at a particular point

ex.en: The negotiations culminated in an agreement acceptable to all sides.
ex.zh: 谈判终于以各方均能接受的协议结束。

senses.en: to lie down or sit down with your back curved and your knees and arms close to your body

ex.en: I love curling up in an armchair with a good book.
ex.zh: 我爱在沙发上蜷作一团看我喜欢的书。

ex.en: The cat was curled up asleep under the bush.
ex.zh: 猫在灌木下蜷成一团睡觉。

senses.en: to bend sth/yourself into a tight curved shape

ex.en: She curled her legs up under her on the sofa.
ex.zh: 她盘腿坐在沙发上。

ex.en: He curled himself up under the covers and went to sleep.
ex.zh: 他蜷缩在被子底下睡了。

senses.en: to have or suffer from sth bad

ex.en: He was cursed with poor health from childhood.
ex.zh: 他从小就因身体不好而吃苦头。

ex.en: I’ve always been cursed with bad luck.
ex.zh: 我真是命途多舛。

senses.en: to separate part of a room with a curtain or curtains
senses.zh: 用帘子把(房间的)某部份隔开:

ex.en: A corner of the room was curtained off.
ex.zh: 屋子的一角用帘子隔开了。

senses.en: to affect or be true for people in different groups that usually remain separate
senses.zh: 影响，符合，适用于(分离的不同群体):

ex.en: Opposition to the proposal cuts across party boundaries.
ex.zh: 对这个提案的反对超越了党派界限。

senses.en: to remove sth by cutting with a knife or a sharp tool

ex.en: Cut away any dead branches.
ex.zh: 把枯枝全砍掉。

senses.en: to reduce sth such as the amount sb spends or produces
senses.zh: 减少， 削减，缩减(开支或生产等):

ex.en: The recession means that everyone is cutting back.
ex.zh: 经济衰退意味着每个人都在削减开销。

ex.en: We’ve had to cut back on staff to save money.
ex.zh: 我们必须裁减雇员以省钱。

senses.en: () to eat, drink or use less of a particular thing, usually for your health
senses.zh: 节制，减少(饮食或使用某物):

ex.en: I smoke too much. I must cut back.
ex.zh: 我抽烟太多。我必须加以控制了。

ex.en: The doctor’s told me to cut back on red meat.
ex.zh: 医生建议我少吃红肉。

senses.en: [usually pl.] a reduction in sth
senses.zh: 削减； 缩减； 减少:

ex.en: cutbacks in public spending
ex.zh: 公共开支的削减

senses.en: to reduce the amount or quantity of sth

ex.en: Recycling cuts down on waste.
ex.zh: 废品回收能减少浪费。

ex.en: I’ve spent too much already this month — I’ll have to cut down a bit (= spend less money).
ex.zh: 我这个月开销已经太大了─我得省着点用钱。

senses.en: to consume, use or buy less of sth
senses.zh: 减少消耗(或使用、购买某物):

ex.en: The doctor’s told me to cut down on fatty foods.
ex.zh: 医生建议我少吃多脂肪的食物。

ex.en: I haven’t stopped smoking, but I’ve cut down to five a day.
ex.zh: 我还没戒烟，可已经减少到每天抽五支。

senses.en: to make sb feel or look stupid, especially in front of other people
senses.zh: 使(当众)出丑；使出洋相；让某人现眼:

ex.en: He always cuts her down in front of his friends.
ex.zh: 他总是在他的朋友面前让她难堪。

ex.en: She’s always cutting down my lifestyle.
ex.zh: 她动不动就嘲笑我的生活方式。

senses.en: to show sb that they are not as important as they think they are
a remark or criticism that is intended to make sb feel or look stupid
senses.zh: 令人难堪的话；噎人的话

senses.en: to reduce the length of sth

ex.en: Please cut your article down to 1 000 words.
ex.zh: 请把你的文章压缩到1000 字。

senses.en: , ) to push in front of people who have been waiting in a line

ex.en: Someone tried to cut in in front of us.
ex.zh: 有人想插到我们前面。

ex.en: She saw some friends in line and cut in with them.
ex.zh: 她看见队列里有几个朋友，于是插了进去。

senses.en: to include sb in a deal and give them a share of the profits
senses.zh: 让(某人)参与并分享利润:

ex.en: Do you think we can cut Harris in on the deal?
ex.zh: 你认为我们可以让哈里斯分享这笔买卖的利润吗？

senses.en: to refuse to let sb have any of your money or property after you die

ex.en: He cut his son off without a penny.
ex.zh: 他完全剥夺了儿子的继承权。

senses.en: to interrupt sb when they are speaking

ex.en: He cut me off in mid-sentence.
ex.zh: 我的那句话说到一半他就打断了。

ex.en: My explanation was abruptly cut off.
ex.zh: 我的解释突然给打断了。

senses.en: to stop the supply of gas, water or electricity to sb’s home
senses.zh: 停止，中断(供给煤气、水或电):

ex.en: The gas company threatened to cut them off if they didn’t pay the bill.
ex.zh: 煤气公司威胁说，如果他们拖欠账单，就要停他们的煤气。

ex.en: The water supply had been cut off.
ex.zh: 断水了。

senses.en: ) =CUT SB/STH UP

ex.en: A sports car cut me off as I turned into the road.
ex.zh: 我开上公路时一辆跑车抢了我的道。

senses.en: an act of stopping sth
to remove sth by cutting it with a knife or a sharp tool

ex.en: He cut off a metre of cloth from the roll.
ex.zh: 他从布匹上裁下一米布。

ex.en: Mind you don’t cut your fingers off!
ex.zh: 当心别切掉你的手指！

senses.en: [pl.] trousers/pants that have been made shorter by cutting off part of the legs
() a piece of wood,paper, etc. that remains after the main piece has been cut
() a safety device that stops an electric current from flowing through sth
senses.zh: (切断电路的)断流器，保险装置:

ex.en: A cutout stops the kettle boiling dry.
ex.zh: 断流器使电壶不致烧乾。

senses.en: (of a vehicle or a driver
senses.zh: 车辆或驾驶员) to move suddenly sideways out of a line of traffic突然驶离车流:

ex.en: Did you see the way the car in front cut out?
ex.zh: 你看见前面那辆车是怎样猛冲出去的吗？

senses.en: ,) to leave

ex.en: I’m cutting out (of here). See you later.
ex.zh: 我要离开了。回见。

senses.en: to make sth unnecessary

ex.en: Cut out some of the administration by computerizing your records.
ex.zh: 用计算机处理记录，减少一些办事手续。

ex.en: The new fast train service cuts out the need for a long bus journey.
ex.zh: 有了新的高速列车服务，就不必长时间坐公共汽车。

senses.en: to have the qualities and abilities needed for sth
senses.zh: 具有所需素质及才能；是…的材料:

ex.en: I don’t think I’m cut out for country life.
ex.zh: 我认为我不适合乡村生活。

ex.en: He’s not cut out to be a politician.
ex.zh: 他不是从政的料。

senses.en: [NOTE]This phrasal verb is usually used in negative sentences.
senses.zh: 这个短语动词通常用于否定句。

senses.en: =CUT ACROSS STH 1

ex.en: The path cuts through the wood.
ex.zh: 小径横穿树林。

ex.en: It should be quicker if we cut through town.
ex.zh: 我们抄近道从城里走就会快一些。

senses.en: to pass through sth by cutting

ex.en: Will this saw cut through metal?
ex.zh: 这把锯子能切割金属吗？

ex.en: () The sharp wind cut through his shirt.
ex.zh: 凛冽的风吹透了他的衬衣。

senses.en: to overcome a difficulty that is preventing you from making progress

ex.en: Once you cut through the technical language the report is easy to understand.
ex.zh: 你一弄懂术语，报告就容易理解了。

ex.en: The yacht cut smoothly through the waves.
ex.zh: 帆船平稳地破浪前进。

senses.en: to injure sb by cutting them with a knife, a piece of glass, etc.

ex.en: He was very badly cut up in the fight.
ex.zh: 他在斗殴中给严重划伤。

senses.en: to make sb very emotionally upset

ex.en: She’s still very cut up about the divorce.
ex.zh: 她还为离婚的事十分难过。

senses.en: (of a vehicle or a driver
senses.zh: 车辆或驾车人) to suddenly drive in front of another vehicle in a dangerous way超车抢道:

ex.en: Did you see how he cut me up?
ex.zh: 你看见他怎样抢我的道了吗？

senses.en: to touch sth, especially your face, several times, quickly and lightly
senses.zh: (用某物)轻触，轻按几下(面部等):

ex.en: She was crying and dabbing at her eyes with a handkerchief.
ex.zh: 她一边哭一边用手绢轻按眼睛。

ex.en: He gently dabbed at his cuts with a piece of cotton wool.
ex.zh: 他用一块药棉轻轻按了按伤口。

senses.en: to remove sth such as a stain, sth you have spilled on sth, etc. with quick, light movements

ex.en: Dab the coffee off with your handkerchief.
ex.zh: 用你的手帕把咖啡擦掉。

senses.en: to put sth on a surface with quick, light movements
senses.zh: (用某物)轻而快地涂上(或点上)…:

ex.en: Dab the paint on with a sponge.
ex.zh: 用海绵扑上颜料。

ex.en: She dabbed on a little perfume.
ex.zh: 她轻轻地搽了一点香水。

senses.en: to take part in an activity or a sport, but not very seriously
senses.zh: 涉足，浅尝(活动或体育运动):

ex.en: She swims twice a week and has been dabbling in weight training.
ex.zh: 她一周游两次泳，偶尔还练习一下举重。

senses.en: to think about sth, do sth or treat sb in a way that is not serious enough

ex.en: They’ve been dallying with the idea for years.
ex.zh: 他们多年来一直有这个想法，但从没有认真考虑过。

senses.en: to make a fire burn more slowly or stop burning

ex.en: Firefighters were damping down the embers hours later.
ex.zh: 几小时后，消防队员基本扑灭了余烬。

ex.en: He put sand on the fire to try to damp it down.
ex.zh: 他试图用沙子压住火。

senses.en: ) to make a surface slightly wet by spraying a small amount of water over it
to offer sb sth very attractive to try to persuade them to do sth

ex.en: It’s the biggest financial incentive ever dangled before British footballers.
ex.zh: 这是历来对英国足球运动员的最大经济诱惑。

senses.en: (of rain, waves, the sea, etc.
senses.zh: 雨、浪头、海等) to beat violently against a surface拍打，撞击(表面)

senses.en: to move very quickly from place to place, being very busy

ex.en: I’ve been dashing around all day!
ex.zh: 我东奔西跑地忙了一整天了！

ex.en: At the scene of the accident, people were dashing about all over the place.
ex.zh: 在事故现场，人们忙得团团转。

senses.en: to go away from a place in a hurry

ex.en: He dashes off every day at 4 o’clock.
ex.zh: 他每天4点钟就急匆匆地走了。

senses.en: to write or draw sth very quickly

ex.en: I dashed off a quick letter to my brother.
ex.zh: 我急急忙忙给我弟弟写了封信。

senses.en: to have existed since a particular time in the past or for the length of time mentioned

ex.en: It’s a tradition that dates back at least a thousand years.
ex.zh: 这一传统至少可以追溯到一千年前。

ex.en: Her problems date back to her childhood.
ex.zh: 她的这些问题小时候就有了。

senses.en: to have existed since a particular time in the past
senses.zh: 自… 至今； 从… 开始:

ex.en: It is a beautiful vase dating from about 1715.
ex.zh: 这个漂亮的花瓶大约在1715 年就有了。

ex.en: The strike was the latest stage in a dispute which dated from 1990.
ex.zh: 这次罢工是自1990年以来纠纷的最新阶段。

senses.en: to do business; to make money by buying and selling a particular product or kind of goods

ex.en: He made a fortune dealing in stocks and shares.
ex.zh: 他买卖证券股票交易发了财。

ex.en: They deal exclusively in Chinese art.
ex.zh: 他们只经营中国艺术品。

senses.en: to not include sb in an activity
senses.zh: 不让某人加入(活动)；不把某人算入:

ex.en: You can deal me out of this. I don’t want to get involved in anything illegal.
ex.zh: 你不要把我算在内。我不想参与任何违法的事。

senses.en: to share sth among a number of people, groups of people or organizations

ex.en: We’ll deal out the proceeds to several charities.
ex.zh: 我们将把收入分赠给几个慈善团体。

ex.en: The profits were dealt out among the investors.
ex.zh: 利润分给了投资者。

senses.en: to look after, talk to or control people in an appropriate way, especially as part of your job
senses.zh: 打交道，管理人(尤指作为工作):

ex.en: Her job involves dealing with young offenders.
ex.zh: 她的工作包括看管少年犯。

ex.en: They’re very difficult people to deal with.
ex.zh: 他们这些人很难缠。

senses.en: to do business regularly with a person, an organization, a government,etc.

ex.en: We prefer to deal only with reputable companies.
ex.zh: 我们只喜欢和有声誉的公司打交道。

ex.en: It is best to deal directly with foreign suppliers.
ex.zh: 最好和外国供应商直接进行交易。

senses.en: to prevent sb from doing sth,joining an organization, going somewhere,etc.
senses.zh: 阻止某人做某事(或加入机构、去某处等):

ex.en: Students who have not paid their fees will be debarred from taking examinations.
ex.zh: 未交费的学生将不允许参加考试。

ex.en: He was debarred from holding public office.
ex.zh: 他被禁止担任公职。

senses.en: to choose sb/sth after careful thought

ex.en: We haven’t decided on a date for the wedding yet.
ex.zh: 我们尚未选定婚期。

ex.en: Have you decided on whether to take the job or not?
ex.zh: 你拿定主意是否接这份活了吗？

senses.en: to put on interesting and colourful clothes or jewellery, usually for a special occasion

ex.en: He decked himself out in his best suit.
ex.zh: 他穿了自己那套最好的西装。

ex.en: A lot of supporters were decked out in the team’s colours.
ex.zh: 很多支持者穿着和这个队的队服颜色一样的衣服。

senses.en: to decorate sth,especially a room or a building, for a special occasion
senses.zh: (用…)装点房间(或楼房等)；把(房间等)布置成…:

ex.en: The canteen was decked out with Christmas decorations.
ex.zh: 食堂装点着圣诞节饰品。

ex.en: The room was decked out to look like the inside of a spaceship.
ex.zh: 房间布置得像宇宙飞船船舱。

senses.en: to say at the beginning of a book, a piece of music or a performance that you are doing it for sb, as a way of thanking them or showing respect
senses.zh: (在书、音乐或作品的前部)题献辞:

ex.en: This book is dedicated to my parents.
ex.zh: 谨以此书献给我的父母。

senses.en: to give a lot of your time and effort to a particular activity or purpose because you think it is important
senses.zh: 投身于(某种事业)；把(时间、精神等)贡献给…:

ex.en: She dedicates herself to her work.
ex.zh: 她献身于自己的工作。

ex.en: He dedicated his life to helping the poor.
ex.zh: 他毕生致力于帮助穷人。

senses.en: ) to accept sb’s opinion or do what they suggest because you respect them

ex.en: I defer to your judgement in these matters.
ex.zh: 我服从你对这些事的判断。

ex.en: We are happy to defer to the committee’s wishes.
ex.zh: 我们愿意遵从委员会的旨意。

senses.en: to get a lot of pleasure from sth or from doing sth,especially sth that annoys or upsets other people
senses.zh: 以(尤指令人不快的事)为乐:

ex.en: She seemed to delight in making her parents angry.
ex.zh: 她似乎以惹父母生气为乐。

ex.en: () From childhood, she delighted in reading.
ex.zh: 她从小就喜欢阅读。

senses.en: to give sb/sth/yourself to sb in authority, often because you have been ordered to do so
senses.zh: 将某人(或某物)交出，移交，託付(给…)；自首:

ex.en: The defendant has been ordered to deliver up the goods.
ex.zh: 已命令被告交出货物。

ex.en: She delivered the baby over to the care of her sister.
ex.zh: 她把孩子交给姐姐照看。

senses.en: to try hard to find out more information about sth

ex.en: We should not delve too deeply into this painful matter.
ex.zh: 我们不应该过分深究这件痛苦的事。

senses.en: to behave in a way that is different from what is usual or expected

ex.en: The teachers are not encouraged to depart from the syllabus.
ex.zh: 桝师最好不要背离桝学大纲。

ex.en: They departed from tradition and got married in a hotel.
ex.zh: 他们突破传统，在旅馆结婚。

senses.zh: 不用于进行时) to be affected by or decided by sb/sth受…的影响；由…决定；取决于:

senses.en: to rely on sb/sth; to be able to trust sb

ex.en: I hope you’ll be able to come — I’m depending on you to help me.
ex.zh: 我希望你能来─我指望着你帮忙呢。

ex.en: We need someone who can be depended on.
ex.zh: 我们需要一个可以信赖的人。

senses.zh: 不用于进行时) to be sure that sth will happen确信；相信；指望:

ex.en: You can depend on my sister to spoil things (= she always does).
ex.zh: 我妹妹保准把事情弄糟。

senses.en: to prevent sb/sth from having sth important; to take sth away from sb
senses.zh: 剥夺；使丧失；使不能享有:

ex.en: In prison they were starved and deprived of sleep.
ex.zh: 他们在狱中挨饿并且睡眠不足。

ex.en: The baby’s brain had been deprived of oxygen during the birth.
ex.zh: 这婴儿出生时大脑缺氧。

senses.en: to come or develop from sth

ex.en: The word history derives from the Latin word ‘historia’ meaning story.
ex.zh: history一词源自拉丁语的historia，意思是story(故事) 。

ex.en: The criticism derives from a misunderstanding of our aims.
ex.zh: 这一指责是由对我们目标的误解造成的。

senses.en: to be related to sb who lived a long time ago

ex.en: He claimed he was descended from the Vikings.
ex.zh: 他声称自己是维京人的后裔。

senses.en: to get into a very bad condition or state

ex.en: The situation has descended into total chaos.
ex.zh: 局面变得一片混乱。

ex.en: There were fears that the country was descending into turmoil or even civil war.
ex.zh: 大家担心国家逐渐陷入动乱，甚至是内战。

senses.en: to arrive somewhere, especially suddenly and unexpectedly and in large numbers

ex.en: Dozens of police descended on the building.
ex.zh: 数十名警察突然来到这座大楼。

ex.en: () My sister and her family are descending on us this weekend.
ex.zh: 我妹妹全家人这个周末就会涌到我家。

senses.en: to go towards sb/sth as if you are going to attack them/it

ex.en: The mosquitoes descended on us as soon as night fell.
ex.zh: 夜幕一降临蚊子就扑向我们。

ex.en: () A large woman in a hat was descending on them.
ex.zh: 一个戴帽子的高大女子向他们进逼。

senses.en: to do or say sth that makes people lose their respect for you
senses.zh: 降低身分去做；竟做出；堕落到…地步:

ex.en: If you insult him back, you descend to his level.
ex.zh: 你如果反过去辱骂他，就是跟他一般见识。

senses.en: to feel that there is no hope that sb/sth will improve, get better, etc. or that sth will happen
senses.zh: 对…绝望；对…失去希望；丧失信心:

ex.en: I despair of you, Ian — act your age!
ex.zh: 你太让我失望了，伊恩─你年纪不小了！

ex.en: I’d begun to despair of ever seeing him again.
ex.zh: 我那时开始绝望，觉得再也见不到他了。

senses.zh: 通常不用于进行时) to make sth seem less good than it really is减损；毁损；贬低:

ex.en: These revelations should not detract from his achievements.
ex.zh: 不应该因暴露出来的这些事而贬低他的成就。

ex.en: Her tattered clothes in no way detracted from her beauty.
ex.zh: 她的破衣烂衫丝毫没有影响她的美貌。

senses.en: (of work,duties, power or responsibility
senses.zh: 工作、职责、权力或责任) to be given to a person or an organization by sb at a higher level of authority交给下属(或下层等):

ex.en: All the responsibility has devolved upon him.
ex.zh: 所有的责任都落到了他身上。

ex.en: Additional powers will devolve to the regional governments.
ex.zh: 将向地方政府下放更多的权力。

senses.en: to give work, duties,power or responsibility to sb with less authority than you
senses.zh: (将工作、职责、权力、责任等)交给下属(或下层等):

ex.en: More powers are gradually being devolved to the regions.
ex.zh: 正逐步向地方下放更多的权力。

senses.en: to give an amount of time, energy or attention to sb/sth
senses.zh: 把时间(或精力、注意力等)投入…:

ex.en: He devoted his life to the struggle for justice.
ex.zh: 他毕生为正义而斗争。

ex.en: She gave up work to devote more time to her children.
ex.zh: 她放弃了工作，这样就能有更多时间和孩子们相处。

senses.en: to spend a large part of your time, energy and attention on a particular activity,especially sth good

ex.en: After her marriage, she couldn’t devote herself totally to her music.
ex.zh: 她结婚之后无法全力倾注于音乐。

ex.en: They had devoted themselves entirely to building up their business.
ex.zh: 他们那时完全致力于建设自己的企业。

senses.en: to make a connection between one computer and another using a telephone line

ex.en: I dial in from my PC at home to get the files I need.
ex.zh: 我从家里的个人电脑拨号联网取得所需档案。

ex.en: Every time I try to dial into the Internet I can’t get a connection.
ex.zh: 我每次想拨号上网都连接不上。

senses.en: to make a call to sb outside the building you are in

ex.en: You can’t dial out from that phone — it’s for internal calls only.
ex.zh: 那部电话不能打外线─只能打内线。

senses.en: ) to call sb/sth on the telephone

ex.en: Would you dial up the doctor’s office for me?
ex.zh: 请帮我给诊所打个电话好吗？

senses.en: =DIAL INTO STH

ex.en: Customers can dial up the central computer from home and access the database.
ex.zh: 客户可以从家里拨号和中央电脑联网进入数据库。

senses.en: to give orders to sb, especially in a rude or aggressive way
senses.zh: 任意指使某人；向某人发号施令:

ex.en: You can’t dictate to people how they should live.
ex.zh: 你不能对别人的生活方式指手画脚。

ex.en: I’m not going to be dictated to by my little brother!
ex.zh: 我不会听任我弟弟摆布的！

senses.en: to spend your time doing things that are not important

ex.en: Stop diddling around and do some work!
ex.zh: 别晃悠了，干点正事吧！

senses.en: (of a sound
senses.zh: 声音) to become so faint or weak that you can no longer hear it逐渐减弱；逐渐模煳；逐渐消失:

ex.en: The sound of the car engine died away.
ex.zh: 汽车发动机的声音逐渐消失了。

ex.en: Her laughter died away when she saw how angry he was.
ex.zh: 她看见他那样生气，她的笑声就低了下去。

senses.en: (of a feeling or an emotion
senses.zh: 感觉或情绪) to gradually become weaker and disappear逐渐平静； 逐渐消失:

ex.en: The excitement over their affair soon died away.
ex.zh: 对于他们的风流韵事的兴奋劲儿很快过去了。

senses.en: (of a sound or flames
senses.zh: 声音或火焰) to gradually become less loud or strong逐渐降低；逐渐变弱；逐渐平息:

ex.en: He waited for the applause to die down.
ex.zh: 他等着掌声平息下来。

ex.en: The fire had died down by the morning.
ex.zh: 炉火到早晨就熄灭了。

senses.en: (of wind, rain or a storm
senses.zh: 风、雨或风暴) to gradually become less strong or violent逐渐减弱；逐渐变小；逐渐平息:

ex.en: As it got dark, the wind died down.
ex.zh: 风到了晚上就逐渐变小了。

senses.en: (of a custom, tradition or skill
senses.zh: 风俗、传统或技能) to no longer be used or practised失传:

ex.en: Many New Year and May Day ceremonies have virtually died out now.
ex.zh: 新年和五朔节的很多仪式如今实际上已经失传了。

senses.en: =DIE AWAY 2

ex.en: The outbreaks of rain will die out later in the day.
ex.zh: 骤雨将在白天晚些时候逐渐停止。

senses.en: () to begin to eat

ex.en: Dig in while it’s hot!
ex.zh: 趁热吃吧！

ex.en: As soon as the food arrived he dug in hungrily.
ex.zh: 食物一端来他便狼吞虎咽地吃起来。

senses.en: to begin to do sth in a way that shows that you are determined to continue or finish it, even if it is difficult
senses.zh: 毅然开始(做某事) ； 开始致力于:

ex.en: He looked at the stack of work and dug in straight away.
ex.zh: 他看了看那一堆工作便立刻埋头干起来。

ex.en: She dug into the reports and finished them before the meeting.
ex.zh: 她全力以赴地写报告并在开会之前写完了。

senses.en: to make a safe place for yourself in the ground and prepare for the enemy to attack

ex.en: They advanced a short distance and dug themselves in.
ex.zh: 他们向前推进了一点就挖掩体隐蔽。

senses.en: () to begin to eat in an enthusiastic way
senses.zh: 开始尽情地吃；开怀地吃起来:

ex.en: They dug into the pizza hungrily.
ex.zh: 他们开始大吃比萨饼。

senses.en: to examine sth carefully to find out information

ex.en: It isn’t a good idea to dig too deep into his past.
ex.zh: 对他的过去探究过多不是个好主意。

senses.en: , ) =DIG IN,DIG INTO STH
to spend some of the money you have or have been saving

ex.en: I’ll have to dig into my savings to buy a new car.
ex.zh: 我买新汽车将不得不动用存款。

senses.en: to get sb/sth out of a place by digging the ground around them/it

ex.en: It took them three hours to dig him out of the rubble.
ex.zh: 他们花了三个小时才从瓦砾中把他挖出来。

ex.en: The car was buried in snow and had to be dug out.
ex.zh: 汽车被雪埋了，只好挖出来。

senses.en: () to find sth that has been hidden or not used for a long time
senses.zh: 找出，发掘，发现(藏着的或被遗忘的东西):

ex.en: He dug out the shoes he’d bought 20 years before.
ex.zh: 他找出了20 年前买的鞋。

senses.en: to prepare the ground thoroughly for plants by digging the soil

ex.en: The flower beds should be dug over in the spring.
ex.zh: 春季应该翻一翻花床。

senses.en: to break the ground into small pieces, especially before building sth, taking sth from underneath it, etc.
senses.zh: (尤指在建筑等前)掘地，平整土地:

ex.en: Some Roman remains were found under a car park which was being dug up.
ex.zh: 一处正在挖开的停车场下面发现了一些古罗马遗物。

senses.en: to eat a particular type of food

ex.en: We dined on freshly-caught fish in a floating restaurant.
ex.zh: 我们在一家水上饭店品嚐了刚打到的鱼。

ex.en: They dined on a diet of soup and bread.
ex.zh: 他们常吃的食物是汤和麵包。

senses.en: to have dinner away from your home, for example at a restaurant or in sb else’s home
senses.zh: 下馆子；外出(或在别人家)进餐:

ex.en: We dined out every night when we stayed in Paris.
ex.zh: 我们在巴黎时每天晚上都外出吃饭。

senses.en: to tell people of something that has happened to you in order to impress them
senses.zh: 以(自己的事情)娱乐别人:

ex.en: She only actually said one sentence to Brad Pitt but she dined out on it for years.
ex.zh: 她实际只和布雷德…皮特说过一句话，然而她把这事儿挂在嘴皮子上有很多年。

senses.en: to put sth very quickly into a liquid and take it out again

ex.en: She dipped her toes cautiously into the sea.
ex.zh: 她小心翼翼地用脚趾探了探海水。

ex.en: She took off her shoes and cautiously dipped a toe in.
ex.zh: 她脱下鞋小心翼翼地用一个脚趾探了探。

senses.en: to read or watch only small parts of a book, magazine, programme, etc.

ex.en: I’ve only had time to dip into the report.
ex.zh: 这报告我只看了一小部份。

ex.en: The continuous news services are intended for people to dip into.
ex.zh: 重复不断的新闻报道是为方便人们随时收看一部份。

senses.en: to disapprove of sth and think it is bad or wrong

ex.en: We totally disagree with the ban on fox hunting.
ex.zh: 我们完全不赞成猎狐禁令。

ex.en: She disagrees with keeping animals locked up in cages.
ex.zh: 她反对把动物锁在笼子里。

senses.en: to not believe that sb/sth exists

ex.en: to disbelieve in God/devils
ex.zh: 不信有上帝/魔鬼

senses.en: to talk for a long time on a subject; to make a long speech about sth﹙

ex.en: He was able to discourse at great length on the problems of education.
ex.zh: 他能就桝育问题进行长篇的论述。

senses.en: ) to give sth out to large numbers of people or in large amounts

ex.en: He’s always dishing out advice to people.
ex.zh: 他总是指手画脚。

senses.en: to serve food by putting it on plates

ex.en: You pour the wine while I dish up.
ex.zh: 你倒葡萄酒，我把食物分到盘子里。

ex.en: Come and wash your hands — I’m just going to dish up the dinner.
ex.zh: 来洗洗手──我这就把晚饭端出来。

senses.en: to present or offer sth to sb, usually sth not very good
senses.zh: 提供，供给﹙通常指不太好的东西﹚:

ex.en: She keeps on dishing up the same old jokes in her shows.
ex.zh: 她在节目里尽重复些老掉牙的笑话。

senses.en: to get rid of sth;to stop using sb/sth because they/it are no longer necessary

ex.en: The programme dispensed with its most popular presenter.
ex.zh: 这个节目最受欢迎的主持人被换掉了。

ex.en: The spread of PCs has dispensed with the need for typists.
ex.zh: 个人电脑普及就不需要打字员了。

senses.en: to defeat or kill sb

ex.en: The league champions quickly disposed of the opposition.
ex.zh: 联赛冠军很快打败了对手。

senses.en: to get rid of sb/sth that you do not want
senses.zh: 把人打发走；把东西清除﹙ 或销毁等﹚ :

ex.en: She tried to dispose of the evidence.
ex.zh: 她试图销毁证据。

ex.en: They decided to dispose of much of their property.
ex.zh: 他们决定卖掉大部份的财产。

senses.en: to say or do sth to show that you have no connection with sb/sth and do not support or agree with them/it
senses.zh: 表示自己与某人﹙或事物无关﹚；表明不支持﹙或不同意﹚…:

ex.en: The President dissociated himself from the report.
ex.zh: 总统否认与那则报道有关。

senses.en: to suddenly start to laugh or cry

ex.en: They dissolved into fits of laughter.
ex.zh: 他们不禁大笑起来。

ex.en: I dissolved into giggles.
ex.zh: 我情不自禁地格格笑了。

senses.en: ) to start doing sth with enthusiasm and without stopping to think﹙
senses.zh: 过急地﹚全身投入，全力以赴:

ex.en: She dived in with a question before I had finished speaking.
ex.zh: 我还没讲完话她便迫不及待地提问了。

ex.en: They had dived into the new business without thinking it through.
ex.zh: 他们未经慎重考虑就全力办起了新企业。

senses.en: ) to start eating with enthusiasm

ex.en: As soon as the food was served, she dived in.
ex.zh: 食物一端来，她就大口大口地吃起来。

senses.en: to move your hand quickly into sth such as a pocket or bag to try to find sth
senses.zh: 迅速将手伸入﹙包或口袋里﹚找东西:

ex.en: She dived into her handbag for the keys.
ex.zh: 她立即将手伸进提包里找钥匙。

senses.en: to take clothes off sb/yourself﹙

ex.en: He swiftly divested himself of his clothes.
ex.zh: 他迅速脱掉衣服。

senses.en: to take sth away from sb/sth

ex.en: The court order divests the company of all its assets.
ex.zh: 法院指令剥夺了公司的所有资产。

senses.en: to get rid of sth you no longer want or that is no longer useful
senses.zh: 丢弃，抛弃﹙不需要或无用的东西﹚:

ex.en: She managed to divest herself of the unwanted property.
ex.zh: 她设法处理掉了那件不需要的东西。

senses.en: to separate two things or two people with a barrier such as a wall or fence; to form a barrier between two things or people
senses.zh: 用﹙屏障等﹚隔开；把…﹙与…﹚隔开:

ex.en: A fence divided off one side of the garden.
ex.zh: 一道篱笆把园子的一边隔开。

ex.en: They put up a barrier to divide the women’s section off from the men’s.
ex.zh: 他们用挡板把女部和男部分开。

senses.en: to separate,or to make sb/sth separate, into groups or parts
senses.zh: 分成部份；分组；把…分开﹙成为…﹚:

ex.en: Divide up into two teams.
ex.zh: 分成两队。

ex.en: They divided the children up into groups.
ex.zh: 他们把孩子分成几组。

senses.en: to separate sth into parts and give one part to each of a number of people﹙
senses.zh: 由…﹚分担，分摊，分享；把…分派﹙给…﹚；摊派:

ex.en: We divided the work up between us.
ex.zh: 我们分担了工作。

ex.en: The money was divided up among all three winners.
ex.zh: 这笔钱分给了所有三名获胜者。

senses.en: to separate a person,an idea, a subject, etc. from sth; to keep two things separate
senses.zh: 使某人﹙或思想、课题等﹚与某事物分离；保持…与…分开:

ex.en: They believed that art should be divorced from politics.
ex.zh: 他们认为艺术应该和政治分离。

ex.en: When he was depressed, he felt utterly divorced from reality.
ex.zh: 他心情沮丧时就感到完全脱离了现实。

senses.en: to divide or share sth, especially money, between a number of people

ex.en: They divvied up the bill.
ex.zh: 他们分摊了账单。

senses.en: to kill sb/yourself

ex.en: She tried to do away with herself.
ex.zh: 她企图自杀。

senses.en: to get rid of sth;to stop doing or having sth

ex.en: They’ve done away with the uniform at our school.
ex.zh: 我校取消了要穿校服的规定。

senses.en: to criticize sb or yourself in a way that makes them/you appear more stupid or less able than they/you really are

ex.en: Don’t do him down, he’s a good worker.
ex.zh: 别贬损他，他干活挺好。

ex.en: She’s always doing herself down.
ex.zh: 她总是自我贬低。

senses.en: to damage or destroy sth; to injure or kill sb; to put sb/sth in a situation so bad that they/it have no chance of returning to normal

ex.en: The last bout of pneumonia nearly did for her.
ex.zh: 上次肺炎发作差点要了她的命。

senses.en: in serious trouble or danger; having no chance of succeeding at sth
senses.zh: 麻烦很大；十分危险；完蛋:

ex.en: If anyone recognizes us, we’re done for! (= we will not be able to escape and will be in trouble)
ex.zh: 如果有人认出我们，我们就完了！

ex.en: After three days trapped in the cave they thought they were done for (= they thought they would die).
ex.zh: 在洞里困了三天之后，他们觉得没救了。

senses.en: very tired
to injure a part of your body

ex.en: He did his back in playing tennis.
ex.zh: 他打网球伤了腰。

senses.en: to make you feel confused, upset and/or annoyed

ex.en: Shut up! You’re doing my head in.
ex.zh: 闭嘴！你烦死我了。

senses.en: to clean or paint and decorate a room, a house, etc.

ex.en: He’s done the whole house out in yellows and greens.
ex.zh: 他把房子全刷成黄色和绿色。

senses.en: to prevent sb from getting or keeping sth they ought to have, in an unfair or dishonest way﹙
senses.zh: 用不正当手段﹚阻止某人拥有…，剥夺某人的…:

ex.en: She tried to do me out of my inheritance.
ex.zh: 她企图阻止我继承遗产。

ex.en: The residents of the home have been done out of a lot of money.
ex.zh: 居住在这里的人被骗走了很多钱。

senses.en: to attack sb and beat them severely

ex.en: They threatened to do her over if she didn’t pay.
ex.zh: 他们威胁说如果她不交钱就揍她。

senses.en: ) to clean or paint and decorate a room, house, etc.

ex.en: They’ve done over the whole store.
ex.zh: 他们在商店进行了全面装修。

senses.en: to be fastened with buttons, straps, etc.; to fasten or close sth in this way﹙

ex.en: This skirt does up at the back.
ex.zh: 这条裙子在后面系扣。

ex.en: Could you do up my dress?
ex.zh: 请帮我扣上连衣裙好吗？

senses.en: ) to repair or decorate a room, a house, etc. to make it look better and more modern
senses.zh: 修缮， 整修， 装饰﹙ 房屋等﹚ :

ex.en: They’re looking for an old house so that they can do it up.
ex.zh: 他们在寻找旧房，为的是进行整修翻新。

senses.en: to make yourself more attractive by putting on make-up, attractive clothes, etc.

ex.en: She spent hours doing herself up for their first date.
ex.zh: 她为了他们的第一次约会花了好几个小时梳妆打扮。

senses.en: to finish dealing with sth unpleasant, especially as quickly as possible﹙

ex.en: Just tear up the contract and be done with it.
ex.zh: 乾脆把合同撕掉了事。

senses.en: used to say that you do not like sb/sth and find them/it very annoying

ex.en: I can’t be doing with people like that.
ex.zh: 我无法忍受那种人。

ex.en: He couldn’t be doing with her untidiness.
ex.zh: 他看不惯她那么邋邋遢遢的。

senses.en: used to say that you need or would like sth/sb

ex.en: I could do with a drink!
ex.zh: 我想喝点东西！

senses.en: used with negatives and in questions to talk about where sb has put sth﹙
senses.zh: 与否定词连用，或用于疑问句﹚把…放在…:

ex.en: What have you done with my shoes?
ex.zh: 你把我的鞋搁哪儿了？

ex.en: I haven’t done anything with your keys (= I haven’t moved them).
ex.zh: 我根本没动过你的钥匙。

senses.en: used in questions to talk about how sb spends their time﹙

ex.en: She doesn’t know what to do with herself while they’re at school.
ex.zh: 他们上学时她不知道怎样消磨时间。

senses.en: to manage without sb/sth
senses.zh: 没有…也行；没有…而设法应付过去:

ex.en: If you can’t afford a car, you’ll just have to do without.
ex.zh: 你如果买不起汽车，就只好将就了。

ex.en: I could do without (= I wish I didn’t have) all this hassle.
ex.zh: 我希望没有发生这些争吵。

senses.en: to tell sb about sth bad that another person has done﹙

ex.en: Kay wasn’t sure who had dobbed her in to the teachers.
ex.zh: 凯搞不准谁向老师们告了她一状。

senses.en: to give money,food, etc. to a group of people﹙

ex.en: She quickly doled out the food.
ex.zh: 她很快把食物发完了。

ex.en: The money was doled out to them on a weekly basis.
ex.zh: 每周给他们发一次钱。

senses.en: to make yourself look attractive by putting on fashionable clothes, doing your hair, etc.﹙

ex.en: Every Friday she dolls herself up and goes out to a nightclub.
ex.zh: 她每到星期五就把自己打扮起来去夜总会。

senses.en: to be/get ready for a special occasion by putting on fashionable clothes, doing your hair, etc.﹙

ex.en: She was all dolled up in a black dress and pearls.
ex.zh: 她穿了一身黑连衣裙，还佩带着珍珠。

ex.en: I got dolled up for the party.
ex.zh: 我打扮好了去参加聚会。

senses.en: to be in a state where you cannot think clearly or act normally because you are under the influence of drugs﹙
senses.zh: 因药物作用﹚神志不清，行为异常:

ex.en: Some of the patients were kept doped up most of the time.
ex.zh: 有些病人大部份时间都用药物维持，迷迷煳煳。

senses.en: to give sb/yourself a large amount of a medicine﹙

ex.en: She dosed him up with aspirin and sent him to bed.
ex.zh: 她让他服用大量阿司匹林然后…床。

senses.en: to spend your time doing nothing or very little

ex.en: Everyone dosses about in geography classes.
ex.zh: 上地理课时大家都不当回事儿。

ex.en: He just dossed around for a year before he got a job.
ex.zh: 他晃荡了一年才找到工作。

senses.en: to sleep on the floor or somewhere uncomfortable because you have nowhere else to sleep﹙
senses.zh: 在地板上或不舒适的地方﹚将就着睡:

ex.en: We dossed down on Tony’s floor after the party.
ex.zh: 聚会后我们凑合着睡在托尼家的地板上。

senses.en: to spread very small amounts of sth in different places on a surface

ex.en: Dot the suncream on your face in tiny quantities and rub it in well.
ex.zh: 在脸上各处点上少量防晒油并揉匀。

ex.en: Dot the top of the cake with small sweets.
ex.zh: 在蛋糕面撒糖粒。

senses.en: to feel or show very great love for sb and ignore their faults

ex.en: They dote on their daughter.
ex.zh: 他们把女儿视为掌上明珠。

senses.en: to have a second function in addition to the main use

ex.en: The garage doubles as his workshop.
ex.zh: 车库兼作他的修理间。

ex.en: The school secretary doubled up as the nurse.
ex.zh: 学校的秘书兼任护理职务。

senses.en: to turn around and go back in the direction you have come from

ex.en: The road ahead was flooded so we had to double back to find another way around.
ex.zh: 前面的路被水淹了，我们只好原路返回再找条路绕过去。

ex.en: The line of trees doubles back on itself at a bend in the river.
ex.zh: 那排树在河道拐弯处折回来。

senses.en: to bend or fold sth in the middle

ex.en: Use an A4 sheet doubled over.
ex.zh: 用一张对摺的A4纸。

senses.en: to bend your body suddenly or quickly because you are in pain, for example; to make sb bend their body in this way﹙
senses.zh: 因疼痛等﹚弓背，弯腰；使…弓背﹙或弯腰﹚:

ex.en: He doubled up in/with pain.
ex.zh: 他痛得蜷起身子。

ex.en: She doubled up with laughter.
ex.zh: 她笑弯了腰。

senses.en: to go to sleep, especially during the day﹙
senses.zh: 尤指日间﹚打瞌睡，打盹儿:

ex.en: He dozed off during the film.
ex.zh: 他看电影时打起盹儿来。

ex.en: I must have dozed off for a few minutes because I didn’t hear her come in.
ex.zh: 我一定是打了几分钟瞌睡，所以没听见她进来。

senses.en: to choose people and send them somewhere for a special task
senses.zh: 选派…，调遣…﹙执行任务或到…等﹚:

ex.en: Extra police are being drafted in to control the crowds.
ex.zh: 当局正在额外抽调警察去控制人群。

ex.en: Williams was drafted into the team to play France.
ex.zh: 威廉斯被徵调到这个队参加对法国队的比赛。

senses.en: to make sb or yourself stop doing sth when they/you do not really want to
senses.zh: 勉强…离开﹙或停止… 等﹚ :

ex.en: She was enjoying herself at the party so much, I couldn’t drag her away.
ex.zh: 她在聚会上玩得兴高采烈，我没法拉她走。

ex.en: I find it difficult to drag myself away from my computer.
ex.zh: 我觉得难以离开我的电脑。

senses.en: to make sb or sth become involved in a difficult or unpleasant situation when they do not want to be involved
senses.zh: 把…牵扯到里头；连累…；把…卷进僵局﹙或事件等﹚:

ex.en: When violence breaks out in the streets, innocent people are always dragged in.
ex.zh: 街头暴力总是殃及无辜。

ex.en: Don’t drag me into your argument!
ex.zh: 别把我卷入你们的争论！

senses.en: to take sb somewhere by force

ex.en: I was dragged off to the head teacher’s office.
ex.zh: 我被拽到校长室。

senses.en: to progress very slowly and take too long

ex.en: The day dragged on interminably.
ex.zh: 那天没完没了地拖延着。

ex.en: Negotiations between the two sides dragged on through the summer.
ex.zh: 双方的谈判拖过了夏天。

senses.en: to make sth last longer than it should
senses.zh: 不必要地拖延；使持续过久:

ex.en: She dragged the meeting out for as long as possible.
ex.zh: 她尽可能地拖延着会议。

senses.en: to make sb give you information they do not want to give you
senses.zh: 强迫某人说出；套某人的话:

ex.en: They eventually dragged a confession out of her.
ex.zh: 他们终于硬迫着她招了供。

senses.en: to mention in a conversation an unpleasant fact from the past that sb would prefer to forget

ex.en: It all happened years ago. There’s no point dragging it up now.
ex.zh: 那都是多年前的事了。现在不必提起了。

ex.en: She’s dragged up that story just to embarrass me.
ex.zh: 她提那件事就是为了使我难堪。

senses.en: or ) to force sb to do sth that they do not want to do
senses.zh: 强迫某人…；勉强人做﹙不愿做的事﹚:

ex.en: We were dragooned into the football team.
ex.zh: 我们迫不得已参加了足球队。

senses.en: (of feelings or colours
senses.zh: 感觉或色彩)to disappear gradually逐渐消失；逐渐退掉:

ex.en: As she lay in the warm bath all the tension drained away.
ex.zh: 她躺在温水浴盆里，一切紧张情绪都慢慢消失了。

ex.en: The colour had drained away from her face.
ex.zh: 她变得脸色苍白。

senses.en: to move away from sb/sth, especially sb/sth that makes you feel frightened﹙
senses.zh: 尤指因害怕﹚移开，后退；畏避:

ex.en: She drew back from the window in case anyone saw her.
ex.zh: 她从窗口退后，免得有人看见她。

senses.en: to reduce the amount of sth, especially money, by using it and spending it

ex.en: Higher production costs will draw down cash gains from rising farm prices.
ex.zh: 生产成本上升会减低来自农产品涨价的现金收益。

senses.en: to get sth from a particular source﹙

ex.en: Many artists and poets have drawn their inspiration from the landscape.
ex.zh: 很多艺术家和诗人的灵感都来自大自然景色。

ex.en: At times of crisis, we drew strength from each other.
ex.zh: 危难时我们彼此鼓劲。

senses.en: to make sb become involved or take part in sth, although they do not want to
senses.zh: 使某人不由自主地投入﹙环境等中﹚；把某人牵涉进去﹙或卷入某事情等﹚:

ex.en: I didn’t like the book when I started it, but the strange story soon drew me in.
ex.zh: 我开始读这本书时并不喜欢它，但那离奇的故事情节很快把我吸引住了。

ex.en: I refuse to be drawn into this argument.
ex.zh: 我拒绝卷入这场争论。

senses.en: to remove some liquid from a larger amount

ex.en: He drew off a glass of beer.
ex.zh: 他倒了一杯啤酒。

senses.en: (of a time or a season
senses.zh: 时光或季节) to slowly pass渐渐过去；荏苒:

ex.en: As night drew on, it became clear he wasn’t coming.
ex.zh: 夜渐深了， 他显然是不会来了。

senses.en: to encourage sb who is shy to talk freely

ex.en: I tried to draw him out on the subject of his life in Africa.
ex.zh: 我设法让他好好谈谈他在非洲的生活。

senses.en: lasting longer than you expect or too long
senses.zh: 拖延的；拉长的；持续很久的:

ex.en: The negotiations were difficult and drawn-out.
ex.zh: 这些谈判进行得艰难且拖沓。

ex.en: It was another long-drawn-out meeting.
ex.zh: 又是一次冗长的会议。

senses.en: to take money out of a bank account﹙

ex.en: How much money did you draw out?
ex.zh: 你取了多少钱？

ex.en: Several thousand pounds had been drawn out of the account.
ex.zh: 有几千英镑从这个账户提走了。

senses.en: to come to a stop; to make sth/sb/yourself stop﹙

ex.en: A taxi drew up outside.
ex.zh: 出租车在外面停了下来。

ex.en: He drew the car up at the front door.
ex.zh: 他把汽车停在前门。

senses.en: to make or write sth that needs careful planning

ex.en: My solicitor is drawing up the contract.
ex.zh: 我的律师正在拟订合同。

ex.en: Clear guidelines need to be drawn up.
ex.zh: 需要拟订明确的指导方针。

senses.en: to stand up very straight so that you are as tall as possible

ex.en: She drew herself up to her full height, hands on hips, and glared at me.
ex.zh: 她双手叉腰站得直挺挺的，对我怒目而视。

senses.en: to spend time in a lazy way thinking about things you would like to do but not actually doing anything﹙
senses.zh: 把时间等用于没有行动的﹚空想:

ex.en: She dreamt her life away, never really achieving anything.
ex.zh: 她一辈子都在幻想，但一事无成。

senses.en: used to emphasize the fact that you would not even think about doing sth
senses.zh: 无论如何也不会做某事:

ex.en: ‘Don’t go without me, will you?’ ‘I wouldn’t dream of it!’
ex.zh: “别扔下我好吗？ ”“我决不会那么做的！ ”

senses.en: much more or much better than you thought was possible
senses.zh: 料想不及的；做梦都没想到的:

ex.en: undreamed-of happiness
ex.zh: 意想不到的幸福

senses.en: used to tell sb that you are certain that what they have just said will not happen
senses.zh: 做梦﹙ 指对方所说的不切实际﹚ :

ex.en: You want a pay rise? Dream on!
ex.zh: 你想加薪？做梦吧！

senses.en: to have an idea or think of a plan, especially one that is not very practical
senses.zh: 凭空想出，虚构出﹙尤指不切实际的事﹚:

ex.en: The scheme was dreamed up by a local businessman.
ex.zh: 这个计划是当地一个商人异想天开地弄出的。

ex.en: Trust you to dream up a crazy idea like this!
ex.zh: 你这个人就是会想出这种荒唐的主意来！

senses.en: to mention sth that sb has forgotten or wants to forget because it is unpleasant or embarrassing
senses.zh: 重提，翻出﹙令人不快的往事﹚:

ex.en: She always dredges up that embarrassing story.
ex.zh: 她老是翻出那件令人尴尬的事。

senses.en: to remember sth or to do sth with difficulty

ex.en: She was dredging up the little she knew about babies.
ex.zh: 她努力回忆自己知道关于婴儿的那点皮毛。

ex.en: He managed to dredge up a smile.
ex.zh: 他勉强笑了笑。

senses.en: to wear clothes that are less formal than those you usually wear or those that are usually worn in a particular situation

ex.en: He deliberately dressed down for the party.
ex.zh: 他有意穿便装参加聚会。

ex.en: More and more people are dressing down for the office these days.
ex.zh: 如今越来越多的人上班着装不讲究。

senses.en: [sing.] (, )an occasion when sb speaks angrily to a person because they have done sth wrong
to put on special clothes in order to pretend to be sb else

ex.en: The kids love dressing up.
ex.zh: 孩子们都喜欢装扮成别人玩儿。

ex.en: They dressed themselves up as cartoon characters.
ex.zh: 他们装扮成了卡通人物。

senses.en: to wear special or more formal clothes than you usually do or than those usually worn in a particular situation

ex.en: Don’t bother to dress up — come as you are.
ex.zh: 用不着穿礼服──就穿平时的衣服来吧。

ex.en: She dressed herself up in a grey suit for the court appearance.
ex.zh: 她穿了一套灰色西装出庭。

senses.en: to make sth seem different or better than it really is by the way that you present it
senses.zh: 把某事物粉饰﹙成…﹚；把事情美化﹙为…﹚:

ex.en: You’re sacking me. Don’t try to dress it up as a career move.
ex.zh: 你是要解雇我。别美其名为工作调动。

senses.en: to become less close or less friendly with sb

ex.en: Over the years we just drifted apart.
ex.zh: 年复一年我们就这么渐渐疏远了。

senses.en: to fall asleep

ex.en: She soon drifted off.
ex.zh: 她很快入睡了。

ex.en: I drifted off to sleep on the sofa while I was watching the football.
ex.zh: 我看足球赛时在沙发上睡着了。

senses.en: to make sb learn or understand sth by repeating it frequently

ex.en: We had multiplication tables drilled into us at school.
ex.zh: 以前我们上学得反复背诵乘法表。

ex.en: There’s no need to drill things into them — they’ll learn as they go along.
ex.zh: 没必要生塞硬灌──他们会边做边学的。

senses.en: to drink all of sth quickly

ex.en: He filled a cup with cold water and drank it down in one gulp.
ex.zh: 他盛了一杯凉水一饮而尽。

senses.en: to look at, listen to or experience sth with great pleasure and interest
senses.zh: 尽情地欣赏某事物；陶醉于…；乐在其中:

ex.en: She wandered the streets, drinking in the atmosphere.
ex.zh: 她漫步街头，乐在其中。

ex.en: We sat gazing at the view, drinking it all in.
ex.zh: 我们坐着尽情地欣赏景色。

senses.en: to wish sb/sth good luck, success or happiness, by raising your glass and then drinking
senses.zh: 为…乾杯﹙或祝酒﹚；举杯祝贺…:

ex.en: They all drank to the couple’s health.
ex.zh: 他们都举杯祝这对夫妇健康。

ex.en: ‘Things can only get better.’ ‘I’ll drink to that!’
ex.zh: “情况只会更好的。”“我举杯赞成！”

senses.en: to finish all of a drink﹙

ex.en: Drink up. It’s time to go.
ex.zh: 喝完吧。该走了。

ex.en: Drink your milk up — it’s good for you.
ex.zh: 把牛奶喝完─牛奶有益。

senses.en: to try to express or say sth
(of a car or a driver
senses.zh: 汽车或开车人) to go away in a vehicle; to take sb away in a vehicle驱车离开；驾车带走:

ex.en: The cab drove slowly away.
ex.zh: 出租车慢慢开走了。

ex.en: There’s someone to drive your car away and park it.
ex.zh: 有人帮你把车开到停车场。

senses.en: to make sb not want to go to a particular place or be with a particular person; to make sb/sth leave a place

ex.en: Rising prices are driving our customers away.
ex.zh: 不断上涨的价格使顾客望而却步。

ex.en: His temper and his violent behaviour have driven all his family away.
ex.zh: 他的脾气和暴力行为把家人全吓跑了。

senses.en: (in golf
senses.zh: 高尔夫球) to hit the ball to begin a game开﹙球﹚

senses.en: to force sb/sth to move away from a particular place

ex.en: The army was driven off by the fierce attacks of the rebels.
ex.zh: 部队被反叛者的激烈进攻打退了。

ex.en: We were driven off the island by the new owner.
ex.zh: 我们给岛上的新主人赶走了。

senses.en: to continue driving either without stopping or after stopping for a short time

ex.en: We drove on until we came to an open square full of cafés.
ex.zh: 我们一直开到一处布满小餐馆的露天广场才停下车。

ex.en: Paula stopped to let Philip out of the car before driving on.
ex.zh: 葆拉停车让菲利普下车之后又继续往前开。

senses.en: to make sb/sth leave or disappear

ex.en: They’re hoping that their competitive prices will drive out the rival company.
ex.zh: 他们希望以具竞争力的价格淘汰对手公司。

ex.en: They tried to drive her out of the village.
ex.zh: 他们试图把她赶出村庄。

senses.en: to talk about sth for a long time in a boring way

ex.en: I nearly fell asleep while he was droning on!
ex.zh: 他囉里囉嗦地讲个没完，我差点睡着！

ex.en: She droned on for hours about the uses of the present tense.
ex.zh: 她花了好几个小时囉嗦现在时的用法。

senses.en: to look at sb/sth in a way that shows you like and admire or want them/it, often in a silly or exaggerated way

ex.en: He was drooling all over you at the party!
ex.zh: 晚会上他一直在痴迷地打量你！

ex.en: The boys drooled over the sports cars in the showroom.
ex.zh: 那些男孩给陈列室里的跑车迷住了。

senses.en: to become less strong or disappear

ex.en: He felt his dark mood dropping away.
ex.zh: 他觉得悲观的情绪渐渐减少了。

senses.en: to pay a short, informal visit to sb, often without arranging this in advance

ex.en: I just dropped by to check you were OK.
ex.zh: 我只是顺便来看看你还好吧。

ex.en: I’m dropping round to Kate’s later.
ex.zh: 我回头要顺便去凯特家一下。

senses.en: to pay a short, informal visit to sb, often without arranging this in advance
senses.zh: 看望一下…；到某处一会儿:

ex.en: Drop in any time you’re passing.
ex.zh: 你路过时就进来坐坐。

ex.en: She drops in on her parents at least once a week.
ex.zh: 她一周至少去看父母一次。

senses.en: [only before noun] used to describe a place where you can go without making an appointment
senses.zh: 无需预约的；可随时去的:

ex.en: a drop-in centre/surgery/clinic
ex.zh: 随时可去的活动中心；无需预约的门诊/诊所

senses.en: to put sb in a difficult or embarrassing situation
senses.zh: 使陷入困境； 使尴尬:

ex.en: She got herself out of trouble by dropping Laura in it.
ex.zh: 她自己甩掉了麻烦却把劳拉扯进去了。

senses.en: (, ) to fall into a light sleep

ex.en: He’s always dropping off in front of the TV.
ex.zh: 他看电视老是打瞌睡。

senses.en: a decrease

ex.en: Managers are concerned by a recent drop-off in sales.
ex.zh: 经理们因新近的销售额下降而担忧。

senses.en: to stop and let sb get out of a car,etc.; to deliver sth to a place, often when you are on the way to somewhere else
senses.zh: 停车让﹙某人﹚下去；﹙顺路﹚递送﹙某物﹚:

ex.en: Could you drop me off at the station?
ex.zh: 你在车站把我放下好吗？

ex.en: I’m going past Jan’s house — I could drop the cake off.
ex.zh: 我要路过简家─可以顺便把蛋糕送去。

senses.en: to stop taking part in an activity, being a member of a group,etc.

ex.en: Several members of the team had to drop out at the last minute.
ex.zh: 有几位队员要临时退出比赛。

ex.en: She had to drop out of the race half way through.
ex.zh: 她不得不半途退出赛跑。

senses.en: to leave school,college, university, etc. without finishing your studies

ex.en: She dropped out of college after only a few weeks.
ex.zh: 她在大学只读了几个星期就退学了。

ex.en: Many students drop out or fail because they’re not enjoying the course.
ex.zh: 很多同学因为不喜欢这门课程而放弃或考试不及格。

senses.en: to reject the accepted ideas, morals and values of society

ex.en: There’s a danger that when people lose their jobs they drop out (of society) altogether.
ex.zh: 失业的人很容易脱离社会。

senses.en: a person who leaves school, college or university before they have finished their studies

ex.en: He might be a college dropout but he’s made a fortune in business.
ex.zh: 他可能中途离开大学，但在商界发了财。

senses.en: , ) a person who rejects the accepted ideas, morals and values of society

ex.en: Many of the town’s dropouts hang around the square.
ex.zh: 这个镇的很多脱离社会传统的人在广场上闲荡。

senses.en: to visit sb for a short time at their home, without arranging a time in advance

ex.en: I think I’ll just drop over to Jim’s for a while.
ex.zh: 我想就去吉姆家小坐会儿。

ex.en: Why don’t you drop over this evening?
ex.zh: 你今晚为什么不来坐坐呢？

senses.en: to deliver sth to sb’s home, etc.

ex.en: I’ll drop those papers round later.
ex.zh: 我过会儿把那些文件送过去。

senses.en: to make sb remember sth by repeating it often
senses.zh: 向某人反复灌输；对某人反复讲述:

ex.en: He drummed road safety into them before letting them out on their bicycles.
ex.zh: 他反复叮嘱他们要注意交通安全，然后才让他们骑自行车出去。

ex.en: Traditional values were drummed into him from an early age.
ex.zh: 他从小就被反复灌输了传统价值。

senses.en: to force sb to leave a group or an organization, usually because they have done sth wrong

ex.en: He was drummed out of the club.
ex.zh: 他被赶出了俱乐部。

senses.en: to work hard to get sth

ex.en: We’re launching a campaign to drum up more business.
ex.zh: 我们正要发起运动以揽到更多生意。

ex.en: We couldn’t drum up enough cash to keep the club going.
ex.zh: 我们无法争取到足够的现金继续办俱乐部。

senses.en: to become dry; to make sb/sth/yourself dry﹙

ex.en: We lay beside the pool to dry off in the sun.
ex.zh: 我们躺在游泳池边在太阳下晒乾。

ex.en: You can use this towel to dry yourself off.
ex.zh: 你可以用这条毛巾擦乾身体。

senses.en: to receive treatment to help you stop drinking alcohol or taking drugs; to cure sb of drinking too much alcohol or of taking drugs﹙

ex.en: She went into a clinic to dry out.
ex.zh: 她到一家诊所戒毒。

senses.en: ) to stop talking suddenly because you cannot remember what to say next or are very nervous

ex.en: She dried up during the second act.
ex.zh: 她在第二幕突然忘台词了。

ex.en: I just dried up halfway through the interview.
ex.zh: 面试进行到一半时我真的张口结舌。

senses.en: ) used to tell sb rudely to be quiet or stop talking
,) to dry dishes after they have been washed

ex.en: I’ll dry up if you wash the dishes.
ex.zh: 你洗盘子，我可以擦乾。

ex.en: He dried all the dishes up and put them away.
ex.zh: 他把所有的碟子抹乾并收起。

senses.en: completely dry

ex.en: They camped in a dried-up river bed.
ex.zh: 他们在一处乾涸的河床上扎营。

senses.en: [only before noun] ()(of a person
senses.zh: 人) old, with many folds and lines on the skin, small and usually bitter or bad-tempered年老乾瘪的﹙且通常尖刻暴躁的﹚ :

ex.en: The librarian was a dried-up, bitter old man.
ex.zh: 图书馆员是个乾瘪尖刻的老头儿。

senses.en: [U] (, ) the act of drying dishes after they have been washed

ex.en: to do the drying up
ex.zh: 把碟子抹乾

senses.en: to avoid a responsibility or duty, especially an unpleasant one

ex.en: She ducked out of visiting him in hospital.
ex.zh: 她找藉口没有去医院看他。

ex.en: You have to go, so don’t try ducking out.
ex.zh: 你必须去，别想逃避。

senses.en: to make yourself more attractive and try to impress people by wearing expensive or special clothes

ex.en: He really duded himself up for the party.
ex.zh: 他为参加聚会着实修饰了一番。

senses.en: to hit or kick sb severely

ex.en: A couple of guys duffed him up.
ex.zh: 几个傢伙把他毒打了一顿。

senses.en: to fight with sb using your hands tightly closed

ex.en: You can’t settle every argument by duking it out.
ex.zh: 你不能靠拳头解决每一次争吵。

ex.en: () You’ll have to duke it out over the last cookie.
ex.zh: 为了最后一块曲奇饼你们只好打一架了。

senses.en: to make sth too simple and therefore less accurate and of poorer quality, by trying to make it easier for people to understand
senses.zh: 为大众化而降低要求﹙或质量等﹚:

ex.en: The programme producers claimed they had to dumb down.
ex.zh: 监制人声称他们不得不使节目通俗些。

ex.en: The new producer has really dumbed the show down.
ex.zh: 监制人确实使演出很通俗。

senses.en: [U] the act or policy of making sth too simple and therefore less accurate and of poorer quality
to say nothing

ex.en: If he dummies up, just try a little persuasion.
ex.zh: 如果他不说话，稍微劝劝他就是了。

senses.en: to treat sb unfairly, especially by giving them too much to do or unpleasant tasks﹙
senses.zh: 以过量的工作或苦差等﹚难为某人:

ex.en: The boss dumps on Jane and she dumps on the junior staff.
ex.zh: 老板和简过不去，简就和底下的职员过不去。

senses.en: ) to criticize sb and make them feel unimportant or stupid

ex.en: Quit dumping on me, I’m trying my best.
ex.zh: 别挑我的毛病了，我尽力了。

senses.en: to tell sb all your problems

ex.en: He dumps on me every time she throws him out.
ex.zh: 他每次给她赶出来就找我诉苦。

ex.en: She keeps phoning me and dumping all her problems on me.
ex.zh: 她不断地给我打电话倾诉她的麻烦。

senses.en: =DUST SB/STH OFF,DUST YOURSELF OFF
=DUST YOURSELF OFF
to remove the dust or dirt from sb/sth/yourself, for example with your hand or a brush
senses.zh: 除去…上的灰尘；掸去；擦去:

ex.en: She stood up and dusted herself down.
ex.zh: 她站起来拍掉了身上的尘土。

senses.en: to bring sth out after it has not been used for a long time and start to use it again

ex.en: The government is dusting off its plans for offshore gas and oil exploration.
ex.zh: 政府重新采用了海上采气和石油勘探计划。

ex.en: Some of their early songs have been brought out and dusted down for re-release.
ex.zh: 他们的一些早期歌曲被发掘出来准备再度发行。

senses.en: to recover after a difficult or unpleasant experience and begin again

ex.en: After every disappointment I just dust myself down and start again.
ex.zh: 每次失望过后我都卷土重来。

senses.en: to think or talk about sth for too long, especially sth unpleasant
senses.zh: 老是想着，唠叨﹙尤指不愉快的事﹚:

ex.en: It’s time you stopped dwelling on the past.
ex.zh: 你该打住了，别唠叨过去的事。

senses.en: ) to look at sth for a long time

ex.en: He smiled, his eyes dwelling on her face.
ex.zh: 他微笑着，久久地端详她的脸。

senses.en: to gradually become familiar again with sth you have not done for some time;to help sb become familiar again with sth they used to do﹙
senses.zh: 让某人或自己﹚重新熟习﹙生疏了的事情﹚ :

ex.en: Smith is gradually easing back into running after his injury.
ex.zh: 史密斯受伤后正慢慢恢复跑步。

ex.en: It’s time to ease the kids back into the school routine.
ex.zh: 该让孩子们逐步恢复上学期间的作息习惯了。

senses.en: to gradually become, or help sb become, familiar with sth new, especially a new job﹙
senses.zh: 让某人或自己﹚逐渐熟悉﹙新事物，尤指新工作﹚:

ex.en: to ease into retirement
ex.zh: 逐步适应退休生活

ex.en: a course for easing people into the world of computing
ex.zh: 帮助学员进入电脑世界的课程

senses.en: to gradually become less strong or unpleasant

ex.en: Eventually the rain started to ease off.
ex.zh: 雨势终于开始减弱了。

ex.en: The pain eased off after a few hours.
ex.zh: 几个小时之后疼痛减轻了。

senses.en: to go slower or make less effort

ex.en: He eased off in the last lap and still won.
ex.zh: 他在最后一圈放慢了速度，还是赢了比赛。

senses.en: to make sb leave their job or position, especially by making it difficult or unpleasant for them over a period of time﹙
senses.zh: 尤指长时期刁难﹚让某人离开﹙工作岗位等﹚:

ex.en: He was eased out of his job as presidential adviser.
ex.zh: 他迫于形势，最终辞去总统顾问的职务。

senses.en: to gradually damage or destroy sth over a period of time

ex.en: Something was eating away the foliage.
ex.zh: 有东西在一点点地侵害叶子。

ex.en: Some of the stone had been eaten away by pollution.
ex.zh: 部份石头被污染物腐蚀了。

senses.en: to worry sb over a long period of time﹙

ex.en: Jealousy is eating away at him.
ex.zh: 嫉妒心折磨着他。

senses.en: to have a meal at home rather than at a restaurant

ex.en: Are you eating in tonight?
ex.zh: 你今晚在家吃饭吗？

senses.en: to gradually damage or destroy sth

ex.en: Woodworm had eaten into most of the furniture.
ex.zh: 木蛀虫把大部份傢具都蛀了。

senses.en: to use or take away a large part of sth valuable, especially money or time
senses.zh: 消耗， 花掉，耗费﹙尤指部份的金钱或时间﹚:

ex.en: My work began to eat into the weekends.
ex.zh: 我的工作开始占用周末。

senses.en: to have a meal in a restaurant, etc. rather than at home

ex.en: We ate out almost every night.
ex.zh: 我们几乎每晚都下馆子。

senses.en: used to tell sb to eat quickly or to eat everything they have been given

ex.en: Eat up! You’ll be late for school.
ex.zh: 快点吃！你上学要迟到了。

senses.en: to gradually become weaker and begin to disappear

ex.en: His confidence ebbed away.
ex.zh: 他渐渐丧失了信心。

senses.en: to gradually move sb out of their job or position,especially by taking their place yourself; to gradually defeat sb﹙
senses.zh: 尤指通过取代其位置﹚把…排除﹙在…外﹚:

ex.en: Be careful he doesn’t edge you out of your job altogether.
ex.zh: 小心别让他乾脆挤掉你，做起你的工作来。

ex.en: She was edged out of the semi-final by her younger rival.
ex.zh: 较年轻的对手取代了她的位置进入半决赛。

senses.en: to remove words or phrases from a book, programme, etc.before it is published or shown
senses.zh: 删除﹙书或节目等中的﹚字句:

ex.en: The swear words were edited out (of the song).
ex.zh: ﹙歌词中的﹚脏话给删掉了。

ex.en: He must have edited a lot of the interview out.
ex.zh: 他一定是大幅度删削了采访内容。

senses.en: a rude way of telling sb to go away, used instead of fuck off
to encourage sb to do sth,especially sth foolish or wrong

ex.en: Egged on by his classmates, he climbed a bit higher.
ex.zh: 他在同学的怂恿下又爬高了一点。

ex.en: The other lads were egging them on to fight.
ex.zh: 其他小伙子煽动他们打架。

senses.en: to make a small supply of sth last longer by using only a little at a time or by adding sth else to it

ex.en: She eked out the stew to make another meal.
ex.zh: 她省出一些炖菜再做一顿饭。

senses.en: to manage to live with very little money
to explain or describe sth in a more detailed way

ex.en: He said he was resigning but did not elaborate on his reasons.
ex.zh: 他说他准备辞职，但没有进一步说明原因。

senses.en: to force sb or sth out of a position or job
senses.zh: 把…排除在﹙某位置等﹚外；把…挤掉:

ex.en: The story was on the front page, elbowing aside the peace talks.
ex.zh: 这件事载于头版，把和谈消息挤到了其他版面。

ex.en: Wrestling elbowed judo out of the 1994 Games.
ex.zh: 摔跤取代了柔道，成为了1994 年奥运会的比赛项目。

senses.en: to start to do sth new, important or difficult
senses.zh: 从事，着手，开始﹙新的、重要的或艰难的事情﹚:

ex.en: The government has embarked upon a programme of reforms.
ex.zh: 政府已开始实施改革计划。

ex.en: He travelled for a year, before embarking on graduate studies.
ex.zh: 他旅行一年之后才开始研究生课程。

senses.en: to remove all the things from inside a container﹙
senses.zh: 从容器中﹚将…全部拿出；腾空﹙容器﹚:

ex.en: He emptied the bag out onto the table.
ex.zh: 他把袋子里的东西全放到桌子上。

ex.en: Don’t empty the bath water out!
ex.zh: 别把洗澡水全倒了！

senses.en: to use up too much of sb’s time,personal life, etc.; to begin to affect sb
senses.zh: 妨碍﹙正常生活或活动等﹚:

ex.en: She tried to prevent her work from encroaching too far on her private life.
ex.zh: 她尽力避免工作过多地影响她的私生活。

senses.en: to have sth as an ending or as a result
senses.zh: 以…结尾﹙或告终﹚；末端是；以…为结果:

ex.en: Many adverbs in English end in -ly.
ex.zh: 很多英语副词以ly结尾。

ex.en: His first attempt to run a marathon ended in disaster.
ex.zh: 他第一次参加马拉松比赛以惨败告终。

senses.en: to reach or come to a particular place or situation that you did not expect or intend to be in
senses.zh: 最终处于﹙意料或意愿之外的境况等﹚；结果做了﹙意料或意愿之外的事﹚:

ex.en: He ended up in prison.
ex.zh: 他最终锒铛入狱。

ex.en: I don’t want to end up worse off than when I started.
ex.zh: 我不想结果比开始时还差。

senses.en: to make sb/yourself loved or liked by sb

ex.en: He managed to endear himself to my entire family.
ex.zh: 他能让我全家人都喜欢他。

ex.en: The government’s record on employment did not endear them to the voters.
ex.zh: 政府促进就业的成绩未能为它赢取选民的支持。

senses.en: to give sb sth, such as a particular quality, responsibility,etc.

ex.en: They endowed their children with remarkable names.
ex.zh: 他们给孩子们取了很独特的名字。

ex.en: The job endows its holder with great prestige.
ex.zh: 做这项工作的人从中得到了很高的威望。

senses.en: to imagine or believe that sb/sth has a particular quality

ex.en: They endowed certain plants with almost magical healing qualities.
ex.zh: 他们认为有些植物具有近乎神奇的疗效。

senses.en: to naturally have a particular skill, quality, feature, etc.
senses.zh: 生来就有…；自然赋予…；天然具有…:

ex.en: He is endowed with both intelligence and good looks.
ex.zh: 他天生才貌双全。

ex.en: machines endowed with amazing powers
ex.zh: 力量惊人的机器

senses.en: to take part in sth; to make sb take part in sth; to be busy doing sth﹙

ex.en: Lecturers engage in teaching and research.
ex.zh: 讲师从事桝学和研究。

ex.en: She tried to engage him in conversation.
ex.zh: 她试图要他跟她谈话。

senses.en: to do sth; to be involved in doing sth

ex.en: He is engaged on a biography of his father.
ex.zh: 他在写关于他父亲的一本传记。

senses.en: to say or write more about sth you have mentioned

ex.en: I’ll enlarge on this point later.
ex.zh: 我过会儿将进一步说明这一点。

senses.en: to ask about sb’s health or about what they are doing

ex.en: My mother enquired after you and the baby.
ex.zh: 我母亲问候你和你的孩子。

senses.en: to try to find out the facts about sth

ex.en: The committee are enquiring into the employment of children.
ex.zh: 委员会正在调查雇用童工的情况。

senses.en: to ask sb sth
senses.zh: 向某人打听﹙或询问、了解﹚…:

ex.en: ‘Are you able to come with us?’ she enquired of Will.
ex.zh: “你能和我们一道来吗？ ”她问威尔。

senses.en: to affect a situation or be an important part of it
to make a start on sth; to begin sth

ex.en: The economy entered on a period of sustained growth.
ex.zh: 经济进入了持续增长阶段。

ex.en: In 1991, he entered upon a turbulent political career.
ex.zh: 他于1991年开始动荡不定的政治生涯。

senses.en: to give sb a right to have or do sth

ex.en: This ticket entitles you to a free meal.
ex.zh: 凭这张票可免费享用一餐。

ex.en: All children are entitled to education.
ex.zh: 所有的孩子都有接受桝育的权利。

senses.en: to make sb responsible for doing sth or for taking care of sb
senses.zh: 委託某人做某事﹙或照看某人﹚:

ex.en: I couldn’t entrust my children to strangers.
ex.zh: 我不能把孩子交给陌生人照看。

ex.en: Can you entrust an assistant with the task?
ex.zh: 你能把这项工作交给助手吗？

senses.en: to be equal to sth

ex.en: Do my qualifications equate to any in your country?
ex.zh: 我的资历在你们国家有相当的吗？

ex.en: Production costs for the movie equated to around 30% of income.
ex.zh: 这部电影的制作成本相当于收益的30%。

senses.en: to consider that sth is the same as sth else, or equal in value or importance
senses.zh: 把﹙一事物﹚ 和﹙另一事物﹚等同看待:

ex.en: He equates success with material wealth.
ex.zh: 他认为成功等同于物质财富。

senses.en: to spread sth equally over a number of people or a period of time

ex.en: She tried to even out the work among the staff.
ex.zh: 她尽量把工作平均分配给职员。

senses.en: to make a situation, a competition,etc. more equal

ex.en: If I give you another ￡5, that will even things up a bit.
ex.zh: 我再给你5英镑的话就拉平些了。

senses.en: to give more information or details about sth you have said or written
senses.zh: 详述；充分论述；详细阐明:

ex.en: Could you expand on your earlier statement?
ex.zh: 把你前面的陈述详细说明一下好吗？

senses.en: to give reasons why you should not be blamed for sth or why sth is not as important or as bad as people think

ex.en: How will you explain away the loss of two cars?
ex.zh: 你将如何为丢了两辆汽车的事进行辩解？

senses.en: to look at sb in a way that shows that you are interested in them, especially in a sexual way
senses.zh: 感兴趣地打量某人；﹙尤指﹚色迷迷地打量着某人:

ex.en: She’s eyeing me up as a potential customer.
ex.zh: 她满怀期待地注视着我，以为我可能买她的东西。

ex.en: He was eyeing up all the women at the party.
ex.zh: 他色迷迷地打量着晚会上所有的女人。

senses.en: to oppose or defeat sb by dealing with them directly and confidently

ex.en: The President is determined to face down his critics.
ex.zh: 总统决心给指责他的人以迎头痛击。

senses.en: ) to start a game such as ice hockey﹙

ex.en: The teams face off at 2.30.
ex.zh: 球队在2点30 分开球。

senses.en: to get ready to argue, fight or compete with sb
senses.zh: 准备好辩论﹙或战斗、比赛﹚:

ex.en: The candidates face off in a Democratic primary today.
ex.zh: 今天候选人准备在民主党初选中进行辩论。

senses.en: a method of beginning a game such as ice hockey﹙
an argument or a fight
to accept and deal with a difficult or unpleasant situation
senses.zh: 敢于面对， 勇于正视﹙困难或不快之事﹚:

ex.en: When is she going to face up to her responsibilities?
ex.zh: 她何时能勇于承担自己的责任呢？

senses.en: to include a particular fact or situation when you are calculating sth, or thinking about or planning sth

ex.en: When you estimated the cost of the repairs, you forgot to factor in the labour.
ex.zh: 你在估算维修成本时忘了把劳务因素考虑进去。

senses.en: to not include a particular fact or situation when you are calculating sth, or thinking about or planning sth
senses.zh: 不把… 因素包括进﹙…﹚去；把…因素排除在﹙…﹚外:

ex.en: When inflation is factored out, the trade deficit fell 12.8%.
ex.zh: 撇开通货膨胀这一因素，贸易赤字下降了12.8%。

senses.en: to gradually become less strong,clear or frequent and disappear
senses.zh: 逐渐变弱﹙或模煳不清﹚；逐渐消逝；逐渐消失:

ex.en: His footsteps gradually faded away.
ex.zh: 他的脚步声渐渐消逝。

ex.en: Her enthusiasm will soon fade away.
ex.zh: 她的热情很快就会消失。

senses.en: [U] [C] an act of gradually making a picture appear at the beginning of a scene in a film/movie﹙
to become quieter,weaker, etc. and gradually disappear
senses.zh: 安静下来；逐渐减弱； 逐渐消失:

ex.en: The protest eventually faded out.
ex.zh: 抗议声终于逐渐消失了。

senses.en: [U] [C] an act of gradually making a picture disappear at the end of a scene in a film/movie﹙
to waste time doing unimportant things and not get very much done

ex.en: Stop faffing about.
ex.zh: 别磨磨蹭蹭的。

senses.en: to deceive or trick sb; to make sb think you are going to do one thing and then do another
senses.zh: 欺骗；蒙骗；以假动作迷惑:

ex.en: He thought I was going to turn left, but I faked him out.
ex.zh: 他以为我要向左拐，可我让他上当了。

senses.en: to laugh a lot
senses.zh: 捧腹大笑；笑得前仰后合:

ex.en: We all fell about at her idea.
ex.zh: 我们听了她的想法都笑得前仰后合。

senses.en: to be old or in bad condition and break or break into pieces

ex.en: If you buy cheap shoes, they’ll fall apart after a few months.
ex.zh: 便宜的鞋子几个月就穿破了。

ex.en: My dictionary is falling apart now, I’ve used it so much.
ex.zh: 我的词典要散架了，我用得太多。

senses.en: to have so many problems that it is no longer possible to exist or operate

ex.en: The whole country’s falling apart.
ex.zh: 整个国家都要分裂了。

ex.en: After my marriage fell apart I moved away.
ex.zh: 我离婚之后搬走了。

senses.en: ) to have so many problems or worries that you can no longer think or behave normally

ex.en: I fell apart when she left.
ex.zh: 她离开之后我崩溃了。

senses.en: to have a lot of problems and be starting to fail
to fail to stay with people at the front in a race﹙

ex.en: Betts had been leading, but fell back with 10 laps to go.
ex.zh: 贝茨原本领先，可还剩10 圈时却落后了。

senses.en: to move or turn back away from sth or sb

ex.en: When the troops moved forward, the crowd fell back.
ex.zh: 部队前进时，人群向后撤退。

senses.en: to use sb/sth when the situation is difficult or other people/things have failed
senses.zh: 求助于；借助于；转而依靠:

ex.en: It’s very hard if you have no family to fall back on.
ex.zh: 没有家人可依靠的生活是很艰难的。

ex.en: He could always fall back on his old jokes.
ex.zh: 他总会搬出他那些老掉牙的笑话。

senses.en: a plan or course of action that you can use if sth else fails

ex.en: a fallback position
ex.zh: 应变方案

senses.en: to fail to stay with other people or things, especially in a race or competition

ex.en: I fell further and further behind.
ex.zh: 我越来越落后。

ex.en: The industry is falling behind the rest of Europe.
ex.zh: 这个行业逐渐落在欧洲其他国家后面。

senses.en: to not do sth or pay sth at the right time

ex.en: She fell behind with the rent.
ex.zh: 她拖欠了租金。

ex.en: He began falling behind in his schoolwork.
ex.zh: 他开始不按时做作业了。

senses.en: to suddenly stop standing

ex.en: I thought the whole house was falling down.
ex.zh: 我以为整个房子要倒塌了。

ex.en: Her legs were so weak that she fell down on her knees.
ex.zh: 她双腿虚弱得突然跪倒在地。

senses.en: to drop to the ground

ex.en: His trousers were falling down.
ex.zh: 他的裤管长及脚跟。

ex.en: A lump of the ceiling fell down.
ex.zh: 天花板掉下了一小块。

senses.zh: 只用于进行时) (of a building建筑物) to be in extremely bad condition破烂不堪:

ex.en: It’s a beautiful house but it’s falling down.
