ex.zh: 房子很漂亮，但摇摇欲坠。

senses.en: the loss of sb’s power, position,money, etc.; the thing that causes this
senses.zh: 衰落；衰败；垮台；衰落﹙或衰败、垮台﹚的原因

senses.en: to fail to do sth correctly or successfully
senses.zh: 没有把… 做好；把…搞糟:

senses.en: to be attracted to sb/sth; to fall in love with sb/sth

ex.en: He fell for a young student.
ex.zh: 他爱上了一个年轻的学生。

ex.en: We fell for the farmhouse as soon as we saw it.
ex.zh: 我们对那所农舍一见倾心。

senses.en: to be tricked into believing sth is true when it is not

ex.en: You didn’t fall for that old trick, did you?
ex.zh: 你没有给那个老花招迷惑住吧？

senses.en: (of soldiers
senses.zh: 士兵) to move into a line集合；列队

senses.en: to join sb; to become involved with sb
senses.zh: 加入；开始与某人有牵连:

ex.en: She fell in with a bad crowd.
ex.zh: 她结交了一帮坏人。

senses.en: to begin to be in a particular state

ex.en: He fell into a deep sleep.
ex.zh: 他陷入沉睡。

ex.en: The tramway fell into disuse in the 1920s.
ex.zh: 有轨电车于20 世纪20年代不用了。

senses.en: to be able to be divided into sth

ex.en: Computer viruses fall into three broad categories.
ex.zh: 计算机病毒可分为三大类。

senses.en: to belong to a particular group or class

ex.en: Only 25% of people fall into this group.
ex.zh: 只有25% 的人属于这一组。

senses.en: to decrease in quantity or quality

ex.en: Attendance has fallen off recently.
ex.zh: 出席人数最近减少了。

ex.en: The standard of cooking fell off when the old chef left.
ex.zh: 原来的厨师走了之后烹饪质量下降了。

senses.en: [sing.] a decrease in the quality of sth﹙

ex.en: a fall-off in attendance/ interest/sales
ex.zh: 出席人数/兴趣/销量的减少

senses.en: to be the responsibility or duty of a particular person or organization﹙
senses.zh: 责任等﹚落在…身上；由…负担:

ex.en: Most of the cost fell on us.
ex.zh: 大部份费用由我们负担。

ex.en: When he died, the responsibility of the business fell on his son.
ex.zh: 他去世以后，企业归他儿子负责管理。

senses.en: to attack sb/sth with energy or enthusiasm

ex.en: The children fell on the food with cries of delight.
ex.zh: 孩子们快活地喊叫着扑向食物。

ex.en: () He fell on the drawings and examined them closely.
ex.zh: 他扑向那些画仔细鉴赏起来。

senses.en: (of hair, teeth, etc.
senses.zh: 毛发、牙齿等) to become loose and drop out掉落； 脱落:

ex.en: The chemotherapy made her hair fall out.
ex.zh: 化疗使她的头发脱落。

senses.en: [sing.] () a quarrel

ex.en: We’ve had a bit of a falling-out.
ex.zh: 我们拌了几句嘴。

senses.en: to be unable to stay standing and fall to the ground

ex.en: () He lost his balance and fell over.
ex.zh: 他没有站稳摔倒了。

ex.en: His bike fell over.
ex.zh: 他的自行车倒了。

senses.en: to hit sb/sth with your foot when you are walking or running and fall or almost fall

ex.en: Mind you don’t fall over the boxes.
ex.zh: 小心别让箱子绊着。

senses.en: to be very eager to do sth
senses.zh: 特别卖力；迫不及待；煞费苦心；不遗余力:

ex.en: Recording companies were falling over themselves to sign the band.
ex.zh: 录制唱片的公司纷纷迫不及待地要和乐队签约。

senses.en: to fail to be completed; to not happen

ex.en: Our travel plans have fallen through.
ex.zh: 我们的旅行计划落空了。

ex.en: The deal fell through.
ex.zh: 交易失败了。

senses.en: to become the duty or responsibility of a particular person﹙
senses.zh: 职责、责任﹚落在…身上；应由…做:

ex.en: The task of telling them the news fell to me.
ex.zh: 把这件事通知他们的差事落在我的头上。

senses.en: to start doing sth

ex.en: Little Red Riding Hood and the wolf fell to talking.
ex.zh: 小红帽和大灰狼交谈起来。

ex.en: They fell to it with gusto.
ex.zh: 他们兴致勃勃地干起来。

senses.en: to belong to or be included in a particular group of things

ex.en: What heading do these items fall under?
ex.zh: 这些项目属于哪一个类目？

senses.en: to teach sb about sth or to learn about sth until you know it well﹙
senses.zh: 使… ﹚ 熟悉， 了解﹙ 某事物﹚ :

ex.en: I familiarized myself with everyone’s name before the meeting.
ex.zh: 我在开会之前熟悉了一下每个人的名字。

senses.en: to spread out over an area from a central point
senses.zh: 展开； 散开； 成扇形散开:

ex.en: Searchers fanned out over the area where the missing child was last seen.
ex.zh: 搜救人员在孩子最后出现的地方散开。

ex.en: Five main roads fan out from the village.
ex.zh: 五条大路从这个村庄通往四面八方。

senses.en: to make sth look more attractive by adding decoration to it

ex.en: I fancied up the dress with some pearls.
ex.zh: 我在连衣裙上缀了一些珍珠。

ex.en: You don’t need to fancy up your web pages.
ex.zh: 不必把网页做得花里胡哨的。

senses.en: to arrange for sb you are responsible for, especially a child, to be cared for by other people

ex.en: When he was little, he was often farmed out to family friends.
ex.zh: 他小时候经常交由他家的朋友照看。

senses.en: to waste time, especially by behaving in a silly way

ex.en: Stop farting around and behave yourself!
ex.zh: 别鬼混了，干点正事吧！

senses.en: to hold sth firmly

ex.en: The cheetah’s jaw fastened on the gazelle’s throat.
ex.zh: 猎豹死死咬住羚羊的喉咙。

senses.en: to choose sth and give it all your attention or interest

ex.en: When she fastens on an idea, there’s no stopping her.
ex.zh: 她一旦拿定主意，就没有什么能阻止她。

senses.en: to direct feelings such as blame, hope, etc. towards sb

ex.en: The blame hasn’t been fastened on anybody yet.
ex.zh: 事情还未有归咎任何人。

senses.en: to close,or to make sth close, with buttons, straps, etc.﹙

ex.en: The dress fastens up at the front.
ex.zh: 这条连衣裙是在前面系扣的。

ex.en: Fasten your jacket up — it’s getting cold.
ex.zh: 把你的短上衣系好—天冷了。

senses.en: to understand how sb thinks and acts; to find an explanation for sth
senses.zh: 理解，弄明白﹙某人的想法和行为﹚；彻底了解；弄清真相:

ex.en: I can’t fathom her out — she says one thing then does another.
ex.zh: 我琢磨不透她─她说的是一套，做的又是一套。

ex.en: Have you fathomed out how to work the video yet?
ex.zh: 你弄清楚如何操作录像机了吗？

senses.en: to become fatter;to give an animal or a person a lot of food so that they become fatter﹙
senses.zh: 使﹚长胖，长肥；﹙把动物﹚育肥:

ex.en: The sheep fattened up quickly.
ex.zh: 羊很快就上膘了。

ex.en: We’re fattening the livestock up for slaughter.
ex.zh: 我们正在催肥牲畜待宰杀。

senses.en: to send a fax (= a message sent using a machine that sends and receives messages or documents along telephone wires and then prints them) to an organization, a company, a television or radio programme, etc.﹙

ex.en: Viewers are invited to fax in with their comments.
ex.zh: 欢迎观众发传真来表达意见。

ex.en: Orders can be either phoned or faxed in to us.
ex.zh: 可给我们打电话或发传真订货。

senses.en: to send a fax (= a message sent using a machine that sends and receives messages or documents along telephone wires and then prints them) that you have received to sb else for them to see or deal with

ex.en: Please email or fax this on to a friend.
ex.zh: 请把此条信息用电子邮件或传真转发给朋友。

senses.en: to send a fax (= a message sent using a machine that sends and receives messages or documents along telephone wires and then prints them) to a large number of people at the same time

ex.en: Draft proposals will be faxed out for comment at the end of May.
ex.zh: 草拟的提案将在五月底一併传真给大家评议。

senses.en: to send sb a fax (= a message sent using a machine that sends and receives messages or documents along telephone wires and then prints them) with details of or information about sth
to be anxious or worried about sb/sth

ex.en: I fear for her safety.
ex.zh: 我担心她的安全。

ex.en: When he’s away at sea, I really fear for him.
ex.zh: 他出海时我十分为他担忧。

senses.en: to give information,advice or opinions about a product, sb’s work,etc., especially so that it can be improved
senses.zh: 将﹙信息、建议或意见﹚反馈给﹙某人﹚:

ex.en: We will feed this information back to the company.
ex.zh: 我们会把这一情况反馈给公司。

ex.en: The results of the tests will be fed back to the schools.
ex.zh: 考试成绩将反馈给各学校。

senses.en: information, advice or opinions about how good a product, sb’s work, etc. is
senses.zh: 反馈的信息﹙或建议、意见﹚:

ex.en: We got a lot of positive feedback about the programme.
ex.zh: 这个节目收到很多正面反馈意见。

senses.en: an unpleasant noise produced by some electrical equipment when some of the power returns to the system﹙
to put sth into a machine

ex.en: You’ll need to feed the paper in by hand.
ex.zh: 你得手动进纸。

ex.en: to feed information into a computer
ex.zh: 将信息输入计算机

senses.en: (of an animal, etc.
senses.zh: 动物等) to use sth as food; to eat sth; to be nourished or strengthened by sth以…为食；从…中得到滋养；靠…长壮:

ex.en: This bat feeds on fruit.
ex.zh: 这种蝙蝠以水果为食。

senses.en: ) to become stronger because of sth else

ex.en: The media feed off each other’s stories.
ex.zh: 媒体靠相互提供报道而运作。

senses.en: to reach sb/sth after going through a process or a system
senses.zh: 逐渐﹙在…身上﹚产生影响﹙或成效﹚:

ex.en: Rises in prices feed through to higher wage claims.
ex.zh: 物价上涨的结果是人们要求加薪。

ex.en: It will take time for the higher rates to feed through to investors.
ex.zh: 需要时日投资者才能因收费提高而受惠。

senses.en: to give extra food to a person or an animal to make them stronger and more healthy﹙

ex.en: You look as if you need feeding up a bit.
ex.zh: 你看上去似乎需要增加点营养。

senses.en: to have sympathy for sb

ex.en: I really felt for her, bringing up her children alone.
ex.zh: 她独力抚养孩子，我确实同情她。

ex.en: I do feel for you, honestly.
ex.zh: 说真的，我确实同情你。

senses.en: to touch sb in a sexual way when they do not want you to
to feel capable of doing sth, physically or mentally
senses.zh: 觉得﹙身体上或心灵上﹚有能力…:

senses.en: to restrict sb’s freedom

ex.en: We’ve been fenced in by rules and regulations for too long.
ex.zh: 我们被规章制度束缚得太久了。

senses.en: to separate one area from another with a fence, often to stop people or animals from entering﹙

ex.en: We’ve fenced off the vegetable patch to stop the rabbits from getting in.
ex.zh: 我们把菜地围了起来，不让兔子进去。

senses.en: to take care of yourself without needing any help from other people

ex.en: We were brought up to fend for ourselves when we were still quite young.
ex.zh: 我们很小的时候就学习自己的事自己做。

senses.en: to defend or protect yourself from sb/sth

ex.en: The minister had to fend off some awkward questions.
ex.zh: 部长不得不迴避一些尴尬的问题。

ex.en: She managed to fend her attackers off for some time.
ex.zh: 她已经把袭击她的人抵挡了一阵。

senses.en: to discover sth by searching thoroughly or asking a lot of questions

ex.en: She’s determined to ferret out the truth.
ex.zh: 她决心查明真相。

senses.en: to admit that you have done sth wrong

ex.en: Come on, fess up. I know there’s something you’re not telling me.
ex.zh: 快点交待吧。我知道你有事瞒着我。

ex.en: How many stolen cars did they fess up to?
ex.zh: 他们承认偷了多少辆汽车？

senses.en: to arrive somewhere by chance

ex.en: The boat finally fetched up on a sandy beach.
ex.zh: 船最后停到了一处沙滩上。

ex.en: He travelled around Europe for a while and finally fetched up in Naples.
ex.zh: 他在欧洲旅行了一段时间，最后不知怎么到了那不勒斯。

senses.en: to spend your time doing nothing or doing sth that is not important

ex.en: He’s fiddling around in the garage.
ex.zh: 他在车库里没事瞎忙。

senses.en: to defend yourself with actions or words when sb attacks you or causes you problems

ex.en: The team fought back to win the game.
ex.zh: 这个队奋力反击以赢得比赛。

ex.en: Don’t let them bully you. Fight back!
ex.zh: 别让他们欺侮你。要还击！

senses.en: to try hard not to show your feelings or not to do sth
senses.zh: 抑制住﹙情感﹚；忍住﹙不做某事﹚:

ex.en: She tried to fight back the tears.
ex.zh: 她强忍住泪水。

senses.en: to try hard not to show an emotion that you are starting to feel
senses.zh: 忍住，抑制住﹙要发作的情绪﹚:

ex.en: He fought down a rush of panic.
ex.zh: 他强压住心头的一阵恐慌。

ex.en: She fought down the anger that was rising in her.
ex.zh: 她压下了胸中燃起的怒火。

senses.en: to resist sb/sth or make them/it go away, by fighting against them/it

ex.en: She managed to fight her attackers off.
ex.zh: 她设法打跑了袭击她的人。

ex.en: The company fought off tough competition.
ex.zh: 公司挫败了强有力的竞争。

senses.en: to fight or argue about sth until it is settled
senses.zh: 以斗争方式解决；辩论出结果:

senses.en: to include sth in your plans; to plan sth
senses.zh: 计划； 打算； 预料到:

ex.en: We hadn’t figured on a long delay at the airport.
ex.zh: 我们没有估计到在机场会耽搁很长时间。

ex.en: I figure on being in New York in January.
ex.zh: 我打算一月份到纽约去。

senses.en: to come to understand sb/sth by thinking carefully

ex.en: I never could figure him out.
ex.zh: 我永远无法理解他。

ex.en: Can you figure out what’s going on?
ex.zh: 你能搞清楚现在的情况吗？

senses.en: to calculate the total amount of sth

ex.en: Have you figured out how much it will cost?
ex.zh: 你算出要花多少钱了吗？

senses.en: to put papers, documents, etc.away in a place where you can find them easily

ex.en: Everything is filed away in drawers.
ex.zh: 所有的文档都存放在抽屉里。

senses.en: to take sb’s place for a short time and do the work they normally do
senses.zh: 暂时代替﹙某人﹚；临时补缺:

ex.en: Who’s filling in for you while you’re away?
ex.zh: 你不在的时候由谁来临时代替？

senses.en: to become larger, rounder or fatter

ex.en: The baby’s filled out a lot recently.
ex.zh: 婴儿最近胖多了。

senses.en: () the action of filling sth, particularly of filling a car with petrol/gas
to give sb a lot of food so that they feel full; to eat as much as you can﹙

ex.en: The meals at school never fill me up.
ex.zh: 学校里的饭菜从未让我吃饱过。

ex.en: Eat lots of pasta to fill yourself up.
ex.zh: 多吃通心粉，吃得饱饱的。

senses.en: to remove sth from a substance by passing it through a special substance or device

ex.en: Use a sun cream to filter out ultraviolet rays.
ex.zh: 用防晒霜滤掉紫外线。

senses.en: to decide in a court of law that sb is guilty
senses.zh: 作出不利于…的裁决；判…败诉﹙或有罪﹚:

ex.en: The court found against the defendant.
ex.zh: 法庭判被告有罪。

senses.en: to decide in a court of law that sb is innocent
senses.zh: 作出有利于…的裁决；判…胜诉﹙ 或无罪﹚ :

ex.en: The jury found for the defendant.
ex.zh: 陪审团作出对被告有利的裁决。

senses.en: to learn a fact, a piece of information, or the truth about sth/sb
senses.zh: 获知，查明，弄清﹙情况或真相﹚:

ex.en: She won’t be happy when she finds out about this.
ex.zh: 她若知道这事会不高兴的。

ex.en: ‘What did she say?’ ‘You’ll find out soon enough.’
ex.zh: “她说了什么？”“你很快就会知道的。”

senses.en: to discover that sb has been dishonest or has done sth wrong

ex.en: If you’re ever found out, you’ll go to prison.
ex.zh: 你一旦被查出来，就会坐牢的。

senses.en: to have sth as the last part of sth; to make sth end by doing one last thing﹙
senses.zh: 以…﹚作结， 使圆满； 完成:

ex.en: After a delicious meal we finished off with coffee and mints.
ex.zh: 吃完美味可口的饭菜之后，我们喝咖啡嚼薄荷糖。

ex.en: The concert finished off with the band’s latest hit.
ex.zh: 音乐会以乐队的最新流行歌曲作压台戏。

senses.en: to make sb so unhappy,tired, etc. that they cannot continue what they are doing
senses.zh: 使垂头丧气；使筋疲力尽:

ex.en: Running in that heat nearly finished him off.
ex.zh: 冒着那种酷热跑步快使他受不了了。

senses.en: to destroy or kill sb/sth, especially sb/sth that is already injured
senses.zh: 杀死，彻底摧毁﹙已严重受伤或受损的人或事物﹚ :

ex.en: He thought the soldiers would come back and finish him off.
ex.zh: 他以为那些士兵会回来打死他。

ex.en: We ought to finish the poor animal off.
ex.zh: 我们应该把这可怜的动物人道毁灭。

senses.en: (in sport
senses.zh: 体育运动) to defeat a person or team that you are competing against打败， 挫败﹙对手﹚:

ex.en: Agassi finished him off in three sets.
ex.zh: 阿加西经过三盘比赛把他击败了。

senses.en: to do the last part of sth; to use what is left of sth
senses.zh: 作最后加工；做﹙或用﹚最后的部份:

ex.en: He stayed home to finish up his assignment.
ex.zh: 他呆在家里完成作业。

senses.en: ) to end a relationship with sb

ex.en: I’ve finished with Antonia.
ex.zh: 我和安东尼娅分手了。

senses.en: used to tell sb to begin asking questions or to begin to speak﹙

ex.en: ‘Can I ask you some questions?’ ‘Fire away!’
ex.zh: “ 我能问几个问题吗？ ”“问吧！”

senses.en: to shoot a bullet from a gun

ex.en: He fired off a volley of shots.
ex.zh: 他举枪扫射。

senses.en: to make sb/sth become excited or enthusiastic about sth

ex.en: The manager fired the team up at half-time.
ex.zh: 经理在中场休息时鼓舞全队的士气。

senses.en: ) to light a fire; to make sth hot

ex.en: I’ll get the burgers — you fire up the grill.
ex.zh: 我去拿汉堡—你把烤架烧热。

senses.en: () to make an engine start operating

ex.en: She fired up the engine.
ex.zh: 她发动了引擎。

senses.zh: 常用于进行时) to try to make sb tell you sth, say sth nice to you, etc. by asking them a question寻求，渴望听到﹙赞扬的话等﹚:

ex.en: Are you fishing for compliments?
ex.zh: 你是在寻求对方的赞扬吧？

senses.en: to take or pull sb/sth out of somewhere﹙

ex.en: He fished some change out of his pocket.
ex.zh: 他从衣兜里摸出一些零钱。

ex.en: Several days later his car was fished out of the river.
ex.zh: 几天之后他的汽车从河里打捞上来。

senses.en: to be the right size or shape to go in a particular place

ex.en: Will all your furniture fit in?
ex.zh: 你的傢具都摆得下吗？

ex.en: The piano wouldn’t fit into the room.
ex.zh: 房间里搁不下这架钢琴。

senses.en: to live or work easily and naturally with a group of people﹙

ex.en: Tim never fitted in at college.
ex.zh: 蒂姆从未适应过大学生活。

senses.en: to find a place for sb/sth, especially when there is not much space
senses.zh: 把…放进﹙有限的空间﹚里；把…置于﹙有限的位置﹚里:

ex.en: We can’t fit a sofa in here.
ex.zh: 这里放不下沙发。

ex.en: We will try to fit you in somewhere in the organization.
ex.zh: 我们将设法把你安排在这个机构里。

senses.en: to manage to find time to see sb or to do sth
senses.zh: 找到时间﹙见某人、做某事﹚:

ex.en: The nurse will fit you in between other appointments.
ex.zh: 护士会在其他预约中安排出见你的时间。

ex.en: How do you manage to fit so much into your day?
ex.zh: 你怎么能在一天中安排下这么多事情？

senses.en: to adapt to what sb else is planning or to sb else’s way of doing things
senses.zh: 与﹙他人的计划或做事方式﹚一致起来；适应:

ex.en: They’ve got to learn to fit in with our methods.
ex.zh: 他们必须学会顺应我们的方法。

ex.en: I’ll fit in with what you want to do.
ex.zh: 我会按你的要求做的。

senses.en: to agree with ideas or information that you already have about sb/sth
senses.zh: 与﹙已有的想法或信息﹚一致；符合:

ex.en: That fits in with everything I’ve heard about her.
ex.zh: 这与我对她的了解完全相符。

senses.en: to supply sb/sth with the clothes, food, equipment,etc. they need
senses.zh: 向…提供所需的东西﹙如衣服、粮食、装备等﹚:

ex.en: The ship had to be fitted out before the voyage.
ex.zh: 轮船出航之前一定要为其提供必需品。

ex.en: the high cost of fitting out offices
ex.zh: 配置办公室设备的高额支出

senses.en: to make sb appear to be guilty of a crime that they have not committed

ex.en: They’re trying to fit me up for the theft.
ex.zh: 他们企图把偷盗的事栽到我头上。

senses.en: to decide to choose sth

ex.en: We haven’t fixed on a date for the meeting yet.
ex.zh: 我们尚未确定会议的日期。

senses.en: to arrange or organize sth; to arrange for sb to have sth

ex.en: Have you fixed your holiday up yet?
ex.zh: 你安排好假期了吗？

ex.en: Shall we fix up a meeting for next week?
ex.zh: 我们把会议定在下个星期好吗？

senses.en: ) to build or make something quickly;to make sth ready
senses.zh: 迅速建起﹙或制作出﹚；准备好:

ex.en: We fixed up a shelter for the night.
ex.zh: 我们匆匆搭了个棚子过夜。

senses.en: to make yourself neat and attractive

ex.en: Can you wait? I’ll just go and fix myself up.
ex.zh: 等一下好吗？我这就去收拾一下。

senses.en: to make arrangements to do sth or for sb to do sth

ex.en: He’s fixed up for her to see the doctor on Thursday.
ex.zh: 他已经安排她星期四看医生。

ex.en: I’ve fixed up with the school to start in September.
ex.zh: 我和学校商定九月份开始。

senses.en: to fail or to end in a weak or disappointing way, often after having started strongly﹙
senses.zh: 顺利开始﹚结果失败，终成泡影；虎头蛇尾:

ex.en: The romance fizzled out after a month.
ex.zh: 这个浪漫故事一个月后就结束了。

ex.en: The coup attempt soon fizzled out.
ex.zh: 政变不久就失败了。

senses.en: to signal to the driver of a moving vehicle to stop, usually by waving your arm﹙
senses.zh: 挥手﹚示意某人停车，示意车子停下:

ex.en: He managed to flag down a passing motorist.
ex.zh: 他挥手招呼一位过路的司机把车停下来。

ex.en: The police were flagging down all heavy goods vehicles.
ex.zh: 警察在挥旗拦挡所有重型货车。

senses.en: to collapse or fall asleep because you are very tired﹙

ex.en: I was so exhausted that I flaked out on the sofa.
ex.zh: 我筋疲力尽地倒在沙发上睡了。

senses.en: ) to begin to behave in a strange way
(of flames, a fire, etc.
senses.zh: 火焰、火等) to suddenly burn more strongly突然旺起来:

ex.en: The fire flared up as I added more wood.
ex.zh: 我添了些木柴，火顿时旺起来。

senses.en: a sudden expression of anger, violent feeling, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 怒火、强烈感情等的﹚爆发:

ex.en: the latest flare-up between the two countries
ex.zh: 两国间新近爆发的不和

senses.en: an occasion when an illness or injury starts again or quickly becomes worse﹙
senses.zh: 疾病的﹚复发；﹙损伤的﹚迅速恶化

senses.en: to show sth valuable,especially money or jewellery to people, or let them see it, to impress them

ex.en: Stop flashing your money around.
ex.zh: 别到处炫耀你的金钱了。

senses.en: [C] [U] a scene in a film/movie,book, etc.which shows sth that happened earlier﹙
senses.zh: 电影、书等的﹚闪回，倒叙，倒叙片段

senses.en: a sudden, very clear, strong memory of sth that happened to you in the past that is so real you feel that you are living through the experience again﹙
senses.zh: 往事的﹚闪回，再现眼前，浮现在脑海:

ex.en: She still has nightmares and vivid flashbacks of the accident.
ex.zh: 她依然做噩梦，那次事故的情景历历在目。

senses.en: to go or pass very quickly; to go very quickly past sb/sth
senses.zh: 急速通过； 飞驰； 飞逝:

ex.en: The days just flashed by.
ex.zh: 日子转眼就过去了。

ex.en: She watched the scenery flash past the train window.
ex.zh: 她看着景色从火车窗外飞掠而过。

senses.en: to press your body or part of your body on or against sb/sth﹙
senses.zh: 把身体或身体部位﹚紧贴…，平贴…:

ex.en: She flattened her nose and lips against the window.
ex.zh: 她把鼻子和嘴唇紧贴着窗户。

ex.en: I flattened myself against the wall to let them pass.
ex.zh: 我身体紧靠着墙让他们通过。

senses.en: to stop growing or going up

ex.en: Sales have flattened out in the last few years.
ex.zh: 过去几年销售额已逐渐停止增长。

senses.en: to make sth completely flat

ex.en: She flattened out the crumpled letter on the desk.
ex.zh: 她在写字台上把皱巴巴的信展平。

senses.en: to add more details or information to an argument, an idea, a drawing,etc.﹙
senses.zh: 以细节或信息﹚充实论据﹙或构思、图像等﹚:

senses.en: to switch sth off quickly﹙
senses.zh: 迅速﹚按开关，按键﹙关电器等﹚:

ex.en: He flicked the light off.
ex.zh: 他啪的一声关了灯。

senses.en: to switch sth on quickly﹙
senses.zh: 迅速﹚按开关，按键﹙开电器等﹚:

ex.en: He flicked on the airconditioning.
ex.zh: 他轻轻一按打开了空调。

senses.en: to turn the pages of a book,etc. quickly, or look through a pile of papers, etc.without reading everything

ex.en: He flicked through a magazine while he waited.
ex.zh: 他边等边浏览一本杂志。

senses.en: to try too hard to show sb that you are interested in them in a sexual way and make them interested in you﹙
senses.zh: 露骨地﹚向某人求爱；向﹙异性﹚献媚

senses.en: to start to do sth with a lot of energy, enthusiasm and effort

ex.en: When they split up she flung herself into her work to try to forget him.
ex.zh: 他们分手之后，她就全身心地投入工作，想忘掉他。

senses.en: to take clothes off quickly and carelessly

ex.en: Flinging off her coat, she sank into an armchair.
ex.zh: 她随手脱掉大衣，一下子坐在扶手椅上。

senses.en: to put clothes on quickly and carelessly

ex.en: Just fling a coat on over your pyjamas.
ex.zh: 在睡衣外面披件外套就行了。

senses.en: to begin to like sb very much; to suddenly become very excited about sth attractive, pleasant, etc.
senses.zh: 开始喜爱﹙某人﹚；对﹙有吸引力、可喜的事物等﹚激动起来:

ex.en: She flipped for his red hair and freckles.
ex.zh: 她对他的红头发和雀斑突然产生了浓厚的兴趣。

senses.en: to raise your middle finger to sb in a very rude gesture
senses.zh: 向某人竖中指﹙很不礼貌的手势﹚

senses.en: to become very angry or excited, or lose control
senses.zh: 情绪失控；变得非常愤怒﹙或激动﹚

senses.en: to turn over, or to turn sth over, onto the other side or upside down﹙

ex.en: The dolphin flipped over onto its back.
ex.zh: 海豚翻转身体肚皮朝上。

ex.en: A huge wave flipped the dinghy over.
ex.zh: 一个巨浪打翻了小艇。

senses.en: to turn over the pages of a book, etc. quickly, or look through a pile of papers, etc. without reading everything

ex.en: He flipped through the photos quickly.
ex.zh: 他匆匆看了那些照片。

senses.en: to think about or be interested in sth for a short time, but not very seriously

ex.en: I flirted briefly with the idea of emigrating.
ex.zh: 我闹着玩似地动过移民的念头。

senses.en: to take risks or not worry about a dangerous situation
senses.zh: 冒险； 不顾危险后果:

ex.en: to flirt with danger/death/disaster
ex.zh: 冒险；玩儿命；不把灾祸当回事

senses.en: to come to or arrive at a place in large numbers or great quantities

ex.en: Letters of support have been flooding in from all over the country.
ex.zh: 全国各地的声援信件像潮水般涌进来。

senses.en: to force sb to leave their home because of a flood
senses.zh: 洪水逼使某人背井离乡:

ex.en: We were flooded out by a burst water main.
ex.zh: 由于自来水总管道破裂，我们被迫离开了家。

senses.en: to send sth somewhere in large numbers or amounts, sometimes more than is necessary
senses.zh: 将﹙ 某物﹚ 大量送往﹙ 某处﹚；某事物充满着某处:

ex.en: The switchboard was flooded with calls after the programme.
ex.zh: 节目播出之后，交换台的电话应接不暇。

ex.en: ()The room was flooded with evening light.
ex.zh: 夜光照得房间通亮。

senses.en: to struggle to move or get somewhere because it is difficult, or because you do not know where you are going

ex.en: People were floundering about in the water, shouting and screaming.
ex.zh: 人们呼喊尖叫着在水里挣扎。

ex.en: () I floundered around trying to decide what I ought to do next.
ex.zh: 我举步维艰，不知道下一步该做什么。

senses.en: to come or result from sth

ex.en: What benefits might flow from having a single European currency?
ex.zh: 欧洲统一货币会带来什么好处呢？

senses.en: to shake or brush feathers, fur,hair, etc. so that they look bigger or softer
senses.zh: 抖松，刷柔软﹙羽毛、毛皮、毛发等﹚:

ex.en: The bird fluffed out its feathers.
ex.zh: 鸟儿抖开羽毛。

ex.en: Let me fluff up your pillows for you.
ex.zh: 我来给你把枕头抖松。

senses.en: to have to leave school or college because your marks/grades are not good enough﹙

ex.en: He flunked out () last year.
ex.zh: 他去年﹙从大学﹚退学了。

senses.en: to get rid of sth with a sudden quick flow of water﹙

ex.en: She flushed the unused tablets away.
ex.zh: 她冲 走了未服用的药片。

senses.en: to force a person or an animal to leave the place where they are hiding

ex.en: The dogs flushed out the deer that were left in the wood.
ex.zh: 狗把树林里剩下的鹿撵了出来。

ex.en: The police flushed the gunmen out of the building.
ex.zh: 警察迫使持枪歹徒离开建筑物。

senses.en: to wash sth out; to get rid of sth with a rush of water

ex.en: Drink lots of water to flush the poisons out of your body.
ex.zh: 多喝水，把体内毒素排泄掉。

senses.en: to move gently through the air to the ground

ex.en: Wind shook the branches and several leaves fluttered down.
ex.zh: 风吹动树枝，几片叶子飘落下来。

senses.en: (of a person or an animal
senses.zh: 人或动物) to attack sb suddenly and violently扑向； 猛烈攻击:

ex.en: She flew at him, hitting and kicking.
ex.zh: 她扑上前去对他拳打脚踢。

senses.en: to arrive/leave a place by plane
senses.zh: 乘飞机来到/离开﹙某地﹚；飞抵；飞离:

ex.en: She’s flying out to join him in Nairobi next week.
ex.zh: 她下个星期将飞往内罗毕和他会合。

ex.en: Several heads of state flew into London last night for talks with the Prime Minister.
ex.zh: 几位国家元首于昨晚飞抵伦敦和首相举行会谈。

senses.en: to bring sb/sth by plane to a place or take them away
senses.zh: 用飞机运来/运走﹙某人或某物﹚；空运:

ex.en: They flew us in by helicopter.
ex.zh: 他们用直升飞机送我们来。

ex.en: Food supplies are being flown out immediately.
ex.zh: 补给食物立刻空运走了。

senses.en: to come off sth suddenly and with force﹙

ex.en: The jolt caused her glasses to fly off.
ex.zh: 那一震把她的眼镜震掉了。

senses.en: to become suddenly very angry
to try to make sb stop asking questions or complaining by giving them answers or excuses that are not true﹙

ex.en: Don’t try to fob me off with excuses.
ex.zh: 休想找藉口骗我。

senses.en: to give sb sth that is different from or not as good as what they want﹙
senses.zh: 把劣质的或不想要的商品﹚ 骗售给:

ex.en: We thought we’d been fobbed off with inferior goods.
ex.zh: 我们以为对方向我们骗售劣质货物。

senses.en: to trick sb into accepting sth that you do not want or sth that is not genuine﹙
senses.zh: 把不想要的商品或假货﹚骗售给:

ex.en: She tried to fob all her junk off onto me.
ex.zh: 她设法向我骗售她的所有旧货。

senses.en: to give all your attention, effort, etc. to a particular problem, subject or person
senses.zh: 集中﹙注意力、精力等﹚于；全力以赴:

ex.en: Suspicion focused on her husband.
ex.zh: 怀疑集中到了她丈夫身上。

ex.en: The programme was intended to focus attention on global warming.
ex.zh: 议程计划集中讨论全球变暖问题。

senses.en: (of eyes, a camera, etc.
senses.zh: 眼睛、摄像机等) to be adjusted so that things can be seen clearly; to adjust sth so that you can see things clearly调节焦距:

ex.en: Rest your eyes by letting them focus on distant objects.
ex.zh: 看远处的景物让眼睛放松一下。

ex.en: The camera was focused on an old woman.
ex.zh: 镜头对准了一位老妇人。

senses.en: to force sb to accept sth that they do not want, or take care of sb that they do not want to

ex.en: He doesn’t try to foist his beliefs on everyone.
ex.zh: 他不会勉强每个人接受他的信念。

ex.en: She resented having the child foisted on her while the parents went travelling abroad.
ex.zh: 她对孩子的父母出国旅行却硬要她来照看孩子这事很反感。

senses.en: to be able to be bent or arranged into a smaller or flatter shape that you can store or carry more easily; to bend or arrange sth in this way
senses.zh: 摺小，叠平﹙以便贮存或携带﹚:

ex.en: The bed can fold away.
ex.zh: 这张床可以摺叠收起。

ex.en: You can fold the table away to make more room.
ex.zh: 你可以把桌子摺叠起来腾出空间。

senses.en: [only before noun] that can be folded so that you can carry it or store it more easily
senses.zh: 摺叠式的； 可摺叠的

senses.en: to fold sth and put it away
senses.zh: 将﹙ 某物﹚ 摺叠 收起:

ex.en: She folded the newspaper away.
ex.zh: 她把报纸叠起收好。

senses.en: to bend sth back, over, down, etc. so that one part of it lies flat on another

ex.en: He folded the corner of the page over to mark his place.
ex.zh: 他摺起书页一角作记号。

senses.en: (in cooking
senses.zh: 烹饪) to mix one substance gently with another,usually with a spoon﹙用勺子等﹚把…调入…，拌入:

ex.en: Gently fold the flour into the mixture.
ex.zh: 轻轻地把麵粉调拌进这一混合物。

ex.en: Fold in two egg whites.
ex.zh: 调入两个鸡蛋的蛋白。

senses.en: to wrap sb/sth in sth

ex.en: She gently folded the baby in a blanket.
ex.zh: 她轻轻地把婴儿裹在毯子里。

ex.en: She folded a blanket round the baby.
ex.zh: 她用毯子把婴儿裹了起来。

senses.en: to bend sth or fold it so that it is smaller

ex.en: The map folds up quite small.
ex.zh: 地图摺起来很小。

ex.en: She folded the letter up and put it in her pocket.
ex.zh: 她把信摺叠起来塞进衣兜。

senses.en: something that continues or results from sth; the action of following on from sth
senses.zh: 后续事物；结果；后续工作:

ex.en: The movie ‘Arthur 2’ was a successful follow-on to ‘Arthur’.
ex.zh: 电影《阿瑟之二》是《阿瑟》的一部成功的续集。

ex.en: follow-on treatment/talks
ex.zh: 后续治疗/会谈

senses.en: to complete a stroke in tennis, golf, etc. by continuing to move the club,etc. after you have hit the ball﹙
senses.zh: 击球后球拍、球棒等﹚完成顺势动作

senses.en: (in tennis, golf, etc.
senses.zh: 网球、高尔夫球等) the final part of a stroke after the ball has been hit﹙击球后的﹚随球动作，顺势动作

senses.en: to complete sth you have begun or already done

ex.en: The store did not follow through with the prosecution.
ex.zh: 商店中途撤回了起诉。

ex.en: He never follows things through.
ex.zh: 他做事从不坚持到底。

senses.en: [usually sing.] something that continues sth

ex.en: The survey is a follow-up to the questionnaire.
ex.zh: 这个调查是问卷的后续工作。

ex.en: follow-up treatment/studies
ex.zh: 继续治疗；追捬研究

senses.en: to try very hard not to show an emotion

ex.en: Forcing back the tears, she nodded and smiled.
ex.zh: 她强忍着眼泪点头微笑。

senses.en: to make yourself eat or drink sth when you do not want to

ex.en: She forced down her breakfast.
ex.zh: 她勉强吃下早餐。

senses.en: to make sb accept sth they do not want to
senses.zh: 强迫某人接受…；把…强加于人:

ex.en: I didn’t want to take the money, but she forced it on me.
ex.zh: 我并不想接那钱，可她硬塞给我。

ex.en: Teachers feel that changes are being forced on them.
ex.zh: 桝师们感觉自己被迫进行变革。

senses.en: to force sb to have sex with you when they do not want to, by using violence or by threatening them
to move forward quickly

ex.en: He forged ahead, panting and breathless.
ex.zh: 他气喘吁吁地向前奔跑。

senses.en: to pay a lot of money for sth, especially when you do not want to﹙
senses.zh: 尤指不情愿地﹚大量花钱，大把掏钱:

ex.en: I had to fork out for a cab home.
ex.zh: 我不得不多掏钱乘出租车回家。

ex.en: I had to fork out $30 for a cab home.
ex.zh: 我不得不花30 元钱乘出租车回家。

senses.en: to pay for sth,especially when you do not want to﹙
senses.zh: 尤指不情愿地﹚ 支付， 出钱:

ex.en: I had to fork over the $10 I owed her.
ex.zh: 我只好把欠她的10 元钱还上。

senses.en: to do sth badly;to spoil sth, especially by making mistakes﹙

ex.en: The team can’t afford to foul up in this game.
ex.zh: 这个队输不起这场比赛。

senses.en: a problem caused by bad organization or a stupid mistake﹙
senses.zh: 因组织不当或愚蠢错误而引起的﹚混乱；差错:

ex.en: an administrative foul-up
ex.zh: 经营混乱

ex.en: There was a computer foul-up at the bank and customers were sent the wrong statements.
ex.zh: 银行的计算机信息出错，给客户发送了错误的结单。

senses.en: to base sth on sth

ex.en: Their conclusions were largely founded on guesswork.
ex.zh: 他们的结论大部份基于猜测。

senses.en: to do sth so that sb is able to do sth else; to make money, time, etc. available for a particular purpose
senses.zh: 让某人脱身﹙做其他事﹚；腾出﹙金钱、时间等﹚:

ex.en: Having a secretary frees me up to work on other things.
ex.zh: 有了秘书我就可以腾出时间处理其他事务。

ex.en: I need to free up more disk space.
ex.zh: 我需要再腾出一些磁盘空间。

senses.en: to prevent sb from being part of a group or taking part in an activity, business, etc.by being very unfriendly or making things very difficult for them

ex.en: My colleagues were freezing me out.
ex.zh: 我的同事们在排挤我。

ex.en: American rice farmers complained that their crops were being frozen out of the market.
ex.zh: 美国大米种植者抱怨说他们的农产品正被挤出市场。

senses.en: [NOTE]This phrasal verb is often used in the passive.
senses.zh: 这个短语动词常用于被动语态。

senses.en: an act of preventing sb from being part of a group or from taking part in an activity, a business, etc.
to become covered by ice

ex.en: The river sometimes freezes over.
ex.zh: 那条河有时全让冰封住。

senses.en: to wash and make yourself look clean and tidy after a journey, before a meeting, etc.

ex.en: I’ll just freshen (myself) up before dinner.
ex.zh: 晚饭前我要去梳洗打扮一番。

senses.en: to make sth look cleaner and more attractive﹙

ex.en: A coat of paint will freshen this room up.
ex.zh: 刷一层油漆会使房间焕然一新。

senses.en: to make a person or an animal go away by making them feel afraid

ex.en: The noise frightened the birds away.
ex.zh: 那声音把鸟儿吓飞了。

ex.en: I sometimes use a gun to frighten dogs away from the hens.
ex.zh: 我有时开枪把狗从母鸡群里吓跑。

senses.en: to make a person or an organization so nervous that they are no longer interested in sth or no longer want to do sth
senses.zh: 把…吓得不敢﹙做某事﹚；让…却步:

ex.en: Investment companies have been frightened off by fear of losing money.
ex.zh: 投资公司由于担心损失资金而却步。

senses.en: to waste time or money on things that are not useful or important﹙
senses.zh: 在…上﹚浪费金钱，浪费时间:

ex.en: He’s frittered away the money his father left him.
ex.zh: 他挥霍掉了父亲留给他的钱财。

senses.en: to represent a group or an organization in order to hide a secret or an illegal activity or protect the person who is controlling it
senses.zh: 为某集体﹙或组织、秘密或非法活动、幕后操纵人等﹚出面:

ex.en: The police could not discover who he was fronting for.
ex.zh: 警方无法查出他挂名代表谁行动。

senses.en: to become covered with frost

ex.en: All the windows frosted up overnight.
ex.zh: 一夜之间窗户全结满了霜。

senses.en: to disapprove of sb/sth
senses.zh: 不赞成； 不同意；不许可:

ex.en: Some restaurants frown on men not wearing jackets.
ex.zh: 有些餐馆不招待没有穿外套的男子。

senses.en: to cook food in oil especially in order to make a meal quickly

ex.en: He fried up some eggs and potatoes.
ex.zh: 他做了些煎蛋和油炸土豆。

senses.en: a meal of fried food,especially bacon, eggs, etc.
senses.zh: 一份油煎食物﹙尤指燻咸肉、鸡蛋等﹚

senses.en: to waste time by behaving in a silly way

ex.en: Stop fucking around and give me a hand.
ex.zh: 别瞎胡闹了，帮帮我吧。

senses.en: used to tell sb very rudely to go away

ex.en: Fuck off and leave me alone!
ex.zh: 磙开，别烦我！

senses.en: to treat sb very badly or unfairly

ex.en: The company promised me a big pay-off but they really fucked me over.
ex.zh: 公司答应给我一大笔酬金，可实际上亏待了我。

senses.en: to spoil sth or do sth badly; to make a stupid mistake
senses.zh: 弄糟；搞坏；犯愚蠢的错误:

ex.en: It was my fault — I fucked up.
ex.zh: 是我的错─我搞砸了。

ex.en: He’s fucked everything up.
ex.zh: 他把整件事搞得一塌煳涂。

senses.en: a problem caused by bad organization or a stupid mistake
to upset or confuse sb so much that they are not able to deal with problems in their life
senses.zh: 使某人的感情受到创伤；完全打乱了某人的生活

senses.en: ) to hit or kick sb hard many times
senses.zh: 接连狠揍﹙ 或踢﹚ 某人

senses.en: thoroughly confused or disturbed
senses.zh: 完全迷乱的；十分困扰的

senses.en: to treat sb badly in a way that makes them annoyed
senses.zh: 苛待，刻薄对待﹙使某人恼怒﹚

senses.en: to put fuel into a vehicle

ex.en: I need to fuel up before I begin the trip.
ex.zh: 我上路前得加加油。

ex.en: () On a cold morning I like to fuel up with a hot breakfast.
ex.zh: 在寒冷的早晨我喜欢吃热早餐加加油。

senses.en: to move awkwardly, especially using your hands to do sth or to find sth
senses.zh: 笨拙地移动；笨手笨脚地做；胡乱摸找:

ex.en: He fumbled around in the dark trying to find the lamp.
ex.zh: 他摸黑找台灯。

senses.en: to supply or provide sb/sth with sth

ex.en: She furnished him with the facts surrounding the case.
ex.zh: 她向他提供了与该案有关的真实情况。

senses.en: to complain to sb about sb/sth very often in an annoying way

ex.en: She’s always fussing at me about my smoking.
ex.zh: 她总唠叨我抽烟的事。

senses.en: to pay a lot of attention, or too much attention, to sb/sth

ex.en: She likes to have someone to fuss over.
ex.zh: 她喜欢对别人瞎操心。

ex.en: When she gets nervous she fusses over unimportant details.
ex.zh: 她一紧张就过多地考虑细枝末节。

senses.en: to spend time doing unimportant things
senses.zh: 闲荡； 瞎混； 虚度光阴:

ex.en: I just futzed around all morning and got nothing done.
ex.zh: 我一上午都无所事事。

senses.en: to talk quickly and for a long time about sth so that people find it difficult to understand you or become bored

ex.en: Someone on the radio was gabbling away in a foreign language.
ex.zh: 收音机里有人在用外语叽里哌啦地讲话。

ex.en: Nicola gabbled on about her boyfriend for hours.
ex.zh: 尼古拉喋喋不休地谈论她的男朋友有好几个小时了。

senses.en: to go to different places looking for fun and excitement, especially when you should be doing sth else

ex.en: It’s about time he stopped gadding about and settled down.
ex.zh: 他该结束游荡生活安顿下来了。

senses.en: to get more of a particular quality

ex.en: The students are slowly gaining in confidence.
ex.zh: 学生们正慢慢地增加信心。

senses.zh: 常用于进行时) to come closer to sb/sth,especially sb/sth that you are chasing接近，逼近﹙所追逐的人或物﹚:

ex.en: We were gaining on the car in front.
ex.zh: 我们快追上前面的汽车了。

senses.en: to do or say sth very quickly

ex.en: Don’t gallop through your speech as if you can’t wait to finish.
ex.zh: 讲话时别匆匆忙忙，好像迫不及待要结束。

senses.en: to lose sth such as money,your possessions, etc. by risking it/them on a card game, horse race, etc.

ex.en: She gambled away all our money.
ex.zh: 她把我们的钱输得精光。

senses.en: to take a risk with sth, hoping that you or it will be successful

ex.en: She’s had two kidney transplants and now her family are gambling on one last operation.
ex.zh: 她做过两次肾移植，现在家人正冒险让她做最后一次手术。

ex.en: We’re gambling on the weather being fine on Saturday.
ex.zh: 我们赌星期六天气会好。

senses.en: to join together, especially to oppose, threaten, hurt or frighten sb
senses.zh: 结伙，联合起来，拉帮结派﹙尤为反对、恐吓或伤害某人﹚:

ex.en: My brothers are always ganging up on me.
ex.zh: 我的兄弟们总是一道儿对付我。

senses.en: to put fuel in a vehicle
senses.zh: 给﹙机动车辆﹚加油，加燃料:

ex.en: I’ll have to gas up before we leave.
ex.zh: 我们出发前我必须加加油。

ex.en: Have you gassed up the car?
ex.zh: 你给汽车加油了吗？

senses.en: to come together in one place, forming a group around sb/sth

ex.en: Everyone gathered around to hear the song.
ex.zh: 所有的人都聚拢过来听这首歌。

ex.en: They all gathered round the table.
ex.zh: 他们全围在桌旁。

senses.en: to collect a quantity of things,especially crops, and put them all together in one place
senses.zh: 收集；收割，收穫﹙尤指庄稼﹚

senses.en: to bring together objects that have been spread around

ex.en: She gathered together her belongings and left.
ex.zh: 她收起自己的行李离开了。

senses.en: to make or change sth so that it is suitable for a particular need or an appropriate level or standard

ex.en: The programme is clearly geared to a teenage audience.
ex.zh: 这个节目显然是针对青少年观众的。

ex.en: We try to gear our services to customers’ requirements.
ex.zh: 我们努力按顾客的要求服务。

senses.en: [NOTE]This phrasal verb is usually used in the passive.
senses.zh: 这个短语动词通常用于被动语态。

senses.en: to be prepared, ready and able to do sth; to become or make sb/sth/yourself ready, prepared or able to do sth﹙

ex.en: The players are gearing up for the big game.
ex.zh: 运动员正在为这场重大比赛做准备。

ex.en: The hospital is gearing itself up to deal with new patients.
ex.zh: 医院正为接诊新病人做准备。

senses.en: used to tell a horse to start moving or to go faster﹙
senses.zh: 用以吆喝马起行或快走﹚叽驾，快跑

senses.en: to find out about sth;to get or give sb information on sth
senses.zh: 了解情况；知道详情；向﹙某人﹚提供情报:

ex.en: I must gen myself up for the interview.
ex.zh: 我必须了解一些情况以参加面试。

senses.en: ) =GET AROUND

senses.zh: (常用于进行时) to havetoo high an opinion of yourself; to behave as ifyou are better than other people自以为了不起；自高自大；自视甚高:

ex.en: She’s been getting a bit above herself since winning that award.
ex.zh: 她得奖之后有点得意扬扬了。

senses.en: to be communicated to sb orunderstood by sb

ex.en: The message is finally getting across to the public.
ex.zh: 这一信息终于传达给了公众。

senses.en: to move fromone side of a river, a bridge, a street, etc. to theother

ex.en: How can we get across to the island?
ex.zh: 我们怎样才能到达那个岛？

ex.en: The only way to get across the lake is by boat.
ex.zh: 渡过这个湖的唯一办法就是乘船。

senses.en: to move sb/sth, or to help sb/sth move, from one side of sth such as a road, river, bridge, wall,etc. to the other
senses.zh: 把﹙某人或某物﹚送过﹙马路、河、桥、墙等﹚；使﹙某人或某物﹚通过:

ex.en: We’ve got to get supplies across the border somehow.
ex.zh: 我们必须想法把供给品运过边界。

ex.en: We got all the injured soldiers across the river.
ex.zh: 我们把所有伤员都送过河了。

senses.en: to keep asking or telling sb to do sth, often in an annoying way

ex.en: She’s been getting after me to take a vacation.
ex.zh: 她一直催着我休假。

ex.en: I had to get after Jack to clean his room.
ex.zh: 我得一再催促杰克打扫他的房间。

senses.en: to try to catch sb, especially after they have committed a crime

ex.en: We need to be tougher on those who commit crime and get after drug users more.
ex.zh: 我们需要更加严厉地对待罪犯，并进一步追捕吸毒者。

senses.en: to make more progress than other people, companies, etc.; to become successful in your life or your career
senses.zh: 走在﹙某人的﹚前面；领先；胜过﹙某人﹚；取得成功:

ex.en: It isn’t easy to get ahead in the movie business.
ex.zh: 想在电影业出类拔萃不是轻而易举的事。

ex.en: By doing extra homework, he soon got ahead of his classmates.
ex.zh: 他额外做家庭作业，很快就在班上名列前茅了。

senses.en: to tell sb sth before you have fully explained the background or the details that they need to know first﹙
senses.zh: 讲话时未经充分说明﹚直奔正题，直接切入主题
常用于进行时) to leave a place离开；离去:

ex.en: It’s late. We’d better be getting along.
ex.zh: 不早了，我们最好离开吧。

ex.en: One more coffee and then I must get along.
ex.zh: 我再喝一杯咖啡就必须走了。

senses.en: )to move from place to place; to go to lots of different places

ex.en: You certainly get around! Paris one minute, Bonn the next.
ex.zh: 你真是个大旅行家啊！一分钟在巴黎，下一分钟又到了波恩。

ex.en: She can use my car to get around while she’s here.
ex.zh: 她在这里逗留期间可以开我的车到各处转。

senses.en: (of news, a piece of information, etc.
senses.zh: 消息、信息等) to become known by a lot of people传播；流传:

ex.en: The news of her resignation soon got around.
ex.zh: 她辞职的消息很快传开了。

ex.en: Word soon got around that they were having an affair.
ex.zh: 很快人们就纷纷传说他们之间关系暧昧。

senses.en: to have an active social life and be aware of what is happening
senses.zh: 积极参加社交活动；关心时事:

ex.en: It’s time you got around more.
ex.zh: 你该多了解社会了。

senses.zh: 通常用于进行时) to keep criticizing sb一再批评，不断指责，老是数落﹙某人﹚ :

ex.en: Sam’s parents are always getting at him.
ex.zh: 萨姆的父母老是责备他。

ex.en: She feels she’s being got at.
ex.zh: 她感到自己总是受人数落。

senses.en: to influence sb, especially illegally, for example by threatening them or offering money, in order to persuade them to say sth untrue or act in an unfair way﹙
senses.zh: 尤指非法地﹚影响某人；胁迫；贿赂；买通；威逼利诱:

ex.en: One of the witnesses had been got at.
ex.zh: 一名证人被买通了。

ex.en: They even tried getting at the judge.
ex.zh: 他们甚至试图给法官施加压力。

senses.en: to reach or obtain sb/sth; to find a way of entering a place, talking to sb, looking at sth, etc.
senses.zh: 接触某人/事物；取得﹙或通往﹚…:

ex.en: The files are locked up and I can’t get at them.
ex.zh: 文件资料锁起来了，我取不到。

ex.en: I can’t get at my inheritance until I’m 21.
ex.zh: 我满21岁时才能得到遗产。

senses.en: to have a holiday/vacation

ex.en: We’re hoping to get away for a few days at Easter.
ex.zh: 我们期待着复活节出去休几天假。

ex.en: Will you manage to get away this year?
ex.zh: 你今年能出去度假吗？

senses.en: [usually sing.]
the act of leaving a place in a hurry, especially after committing a crime﹙
senses.zh: 尤指犯罪后的﹚逃跑，逃走:

ex.en: They made a quick getaway.
ex.zh: 他们迅速逃跑了。

senses.en: a short holiday/vacation; a place for this

ex.en: the popular island getaway of Penang
ex.zh: 热门度假地槟榔屿岛

senses.en: to start doing sth in a different way or talking about a different subject
senses.zh: 改变﹙做事方式﹚；转换﹙话题﹚:

ex.en: The club should get away from its old-fashioned image and try to attract younger people.
ex.zh: 这个俱乐部应该改变过时的形象以吸引年轻人。

ex.en: I tried to get away from the subject of babies.
ex.zh: 我试图转换话题不谈婴儿。

senses.en: to have a short holiday/vacation in a quiet place where you can relax﹙
you have to admit that sth unpleasant is true
senses.zh: 不容否认，只好承认﹙不愉快的事实﹚:

ex.en: There’s no getting away from the fact that his mistake lost the game for his team.
ex.zh: 他的失误导致全队输掉比赛这一事实是无法否认的。

senses.en: to remove sb/sth from somewhere

ex.en: Get that dog away from me!
ex.zh: 把狗从我这儿赶走！

ex.en: Someone was trying to get Angela away from the window.
ex.zh: 有人正在竭力把安杰拉从窗边拉走。

senses.en: to steal sth and escape with it

ex.en: Thieves raided the bank and got away with ￡50 000.
ex.zh: 盗贼抢劫了银行并偷走了5万英镑。

senses.en: to receive a relatively light punishment

ex.en: For such a serious offence he was lucky to get away with a fine.
ex.zh: 他犯了如此大的罪而只交罚款了事，算是万幸。

senses.en: to persuade sb to begin a romantic relationship with you again, after you have been apart for some time
senses.zh: 劝﹙某人﹚恢复恋爱关系；使再续旧情:

ex.en: I’ve done everything I can to get her back.
ex.zh: 我已经尽全力劝她回心转意了。

senses.en: to take sb/sth back to a place after they have been away from it

ex.en: We’ll get her back home before midnight.
ex.zh: 我们将在午夜之前把她送回家。

senses.en: to punish or hurt sb because they have done sth unpleasant to you

ex.en: This is his way of getting back at me for arguing with him.
ex.zh: 这是他因为我和他争论而报复我的方式。

ex.en: I’ll get her back for what she’s done.
ex.zh: 我会为她的所作所为报复她的。

senses.en: to start being interested or involved in a particular activity again
senses.zh: 再度对…产生兴趣；重新参与；重操旧业:

ex.en: She’ll try to get back into journalism when the kids start school.
ex.zh: 孩子们入学之后，她将重新干记者这行。

ex.en: How soon should I get back into serious training?
ex.zh: 我要过多久才应恢复正式训练？

senses.en: to reply to sb or contact them again by letter or by telephone
senses.zh: 以后再答覆﹙或回覆﹚某人:

ex.en: Leave a message and I’ll get back to you as soon as I can.
ex.zh: 留个信儿吧，我尽早答覆你。

ex.en: They never got back to me about my order.
ex.zh: 订单给了他们就杳无音讯。

senses.en: to begin a romantic relationship with sb again,after you have been apart for some time﹙
senses.zh: 和某人﹚恢复恋爱关系，再续旧情:

ex.en: Jack’s getting back with his ex-girlfriend.
ex.zh: 杰克和前女友恢复恋爱关系了。

ex.en: Jack and his girlfriend are getting back together.
ex.zh: 杰克和女朋友恢复恋爱关系了。

senses.en: to not go as fast as is necessary or as other people; to not produce sth at the right time

ex.en: Once I get behind (with my work) it’s very hard to catch up.
ex.zh: 我﹙工作﹚ 一旦落后就很难赶上。

ex.en: We’re getting behind with the rent.
ex.zh: 我们拖欠租金了。

senses.en: to move into a position behind sb/sth

ex.en: If you get behind the tree, she won’t see you.
ex.zh: 你躲到树后面吧，她不会看见你的。

ex.en: He seems to go mad when he gets behind the wheel of a car.
ex.zh: 他走到车子的方向盘前就好像发疯似的。

senses.en: to reveal the person or thing responsible for starting or developing sth
senses.zh: 显露，揭示﹙背后的人或事物﹚:

ex.en: This is a programme that really gets behind the world of pop music.
ex.zh: 这个节目彻底揭示了流行音乐界的幕后情况。

senses.en: ) to support sb/sth and help them to succeed

ex.en: The whole town got behind him/the campaign.
ex.zh: 全镇的人都支持他/这场运动。

senses.en: to become more than sth

ex.en: What if our losses get beyond 10%?
ex.zh: 如果我们亏损超过10% 怎么办？

senses.en: to become annoying and no longer acceptable
senses.zh: 变得令人恼火；变得无法接受﹙或过分﹚:

ex.en: This rain is getting beyond a joke. Let’s go inside.
ex.zh: 这雨越来越烦人了。我们进屋吧。

senses.en: to manage to live or do a particular thing using the money, knowledge, equipment, etc.that you have﹙
senses.zh: 靠…﹚维持生计，设法过活，勉强应付:

ex.en: How does she get by on such a small salary?
ex.zh: 她靠这点微薄的工资怎么过活？

ex.en: ‘Are you earning more money now?’ ‘I get by.’
ex.zh: “你现在赚钱多一些了吗？”“够煳口吧。”

senses.en: to bend downwards from a standing position and sit, kneel or lie on the ground

ex.en: The children got down on their hands and knees and pretended to be lions.
ex.zh: 孩子们四肢着地扮成狮子。

ex.en: He’s going to shoot! Get down!
ex.zh: 他要开枪了！趴下！

senses.en: to move from a higher place to a lower one, for example using stairs, a rope, a ladder, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 用阶梯、绳索、梯子等﹚下来，下去:

ex.en: What are you doing on the table? Get down now!
ex.zh: 你在餐桌上做什么呢？马上下来！

ex.en: Did you get down the hill without any difficulty?
ex.zh: 你下山顺利吗？

senses.en: to make sb feel sad or depressed

ex.en: This weather is really getting me down.
ex.zh: 这天气实在让我觉得压抑。

ex.en: Don’t let it get you down too much.
ex.zh: 别太介意这事。

senses.en: to reduce sth, especially the cost or price of sth
senses.zh: 减少，降低﹙尤指成本或价格﹚:

ex.en: If we bargain, we may be able to get the price down.
ex.zh: 如果我们议价，就有可能把价格压下去。

ex.en: How can I get my blood pressure down?
ex.zh: 我如何能把血压降下来？

senses.en: to manage to move sb/sth from a higher place to a lower one, for example using stairs, a rope, a ladder, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 用阶梯、绳索、梯子等﹚设法把…弄下来:

ex.en: I can’t get the bookcase down the stairs on my own.
ex.zh: 我自己没法把书柜搬下楼梯去。

senses.en: to think that sb/sth is wrong and to criticize them
senses.zh: 认为… 错误而加以指责:

ex.en: She’s always getting down on me for coming in late.
ex.zh: 她总是因我迟到而责骂我。

ex.en: It’s easy to get down on kids from day to day and forget their good points.
ex.zh: 很容易日复一日地数落孩子而忘记他们的优点。

senses.en: to begin to do sth; to give serious attention to sth
senses.zh: 开始做某事；开始认真注意﹙或对待﹚某事:

ex.en: Let’s get down to business straight away.
ex.zh: 咱们马上开始干正事吧。

ex.en: Isn’t it about time you got down to work?
ex.zh: 你是不是该开始工作了？

senses.en: to arrive at a place

ex.en: When do you normally get in (= arrive home) from work?
ex.zh: 你一般什么时间下班回到家？

ex.en: What time do you get into work in the morning?
ex.zh: 你上午什么时间上班？

senses.en: to be elected to a political position

ex.en: They need 326 seats to get in.
ex.zh: 他们需要326个席位才能当选。

ex.en: The Republican candidate got in with a small majority.
ex.zh: 共和党候选人以微弱多数当选。

senses.en: to gain a place at a school, college, university,etc.
senses.zh: 获得学校录取；被接受入学:

ex.en: She’s applied for Cambridge, but doesn’t know if she’ll get in.
ex.zh: 她申请了剑桥大学，但不知道能否被录取。

ex.en: I tried to get into Harvard, but I wasn’t accepted.
ex.zh: 我试图进哈佛大学，但不获接收。

senses.en: to call sb to your home, etc. to do a job for you

ex.en: We’ll have to get a plumber in to mend the pipe.
ex.zh: 我们得找个管子工来修理管子。

senses.en: to attract a large audience

ex.en: A pantomime usually gets the crowds in.
ex.zh: 童话剧通常能吸引大批观众。

senses.en: to manage to say sth,usually when there are lots of people talking﹙
senses.zh: 说话人很多时﹚争取发言:

ex.en: She talks so much that it’s impossible to get a word in.
ex.zh: 她说起话来滔滔不绝，让人一句话都插不进去。

ex.en: ‘Excuse me’, I eventually got in, ‘I think I can help you.’
ex.zh: “对不起，”我最终插进来，“我想我可以帮你。”

senses.en: to make sb/sth more active, interesting or exciting
senses.zh: 使有活力；使活跃；使兴奋:

ex.en: Some dancing would ginger up the party.
ex.zh: 跳跳舞可以使聚会活跃起来。

ex.en: They need some excitement to ginger them up a bit.
ex.zh: 需要来点刺激让他们打起精神。

senses.en: (in a marriage ceremony
senses.zh: 在婚礼上) to lead the woman who is getting married to the man she is going to marry and formally allow her to marry him将新娘交给新郎:

ex.en: Her father gave her away.
ex.zh: 她父亲把她交给新郎。

senses.en: () to give a baby or a child to another person to take care of as their own child
senses.zh: 把﹙ 婴儿或孩子﹚送人；把…给别人抚养:

ex.en: She had never understood why her mother had given her away.
ex.zh: 她一直不理解母亲为什么把她送给了别人。

senses.en: to do or say sth that shows sth about sb/sth/yourself that was a secret

ex.en: It was her eyes that gave her away (= showed how she really felt).
ex.zh: 是她的眼睛流露出她的真实感受。

ex.en: He never gives very much away about himself.
ex.zh: 他从不怎么透露自己的身分。

senses.en: to tell a secret, especially by accident; to show sth that has been hidden

ex.en: I don’t want to give the game away by telling you how the movie ends.
ex.zh: 我不想提前把电影的结尾透露给你。

senses.en: () something that makes you guess the real truth about sth
[only before noun] ()(of prices
to return a child to its parents

ex.en: We love our grandchildren dearly, but we are happy to give them back at the end of the day!
ex.zh: 我们疼爱孙子孙女，但最终还是乐意把他们送回父母身边。

senses.en: to pay or give a particular amount to have or do sth

ex.en: How much did you give for the car?
ex.zh: 你买这辆车花了多少钱？

ex.en: I’d give anything for a cold beer.
ex.zh: 我愿意拿任何东西换瓶冰镇啤酒。

senses.en: to accept that you have been defeated or persuaded by sb﹙

ex.en: I give in — you’ll have to tell me the answer.
ex.zh: 我输了─你得告诉我答案。

ex.en: Eventually I gave in to temptation and had an ice cream.
ex.zh: 我终于经不起诱惑吃了冰激凌。

senses.en: to finally agree to do sth that you do not want to do﹙
senses.zh: 向…﹚低头，作出让步； 屈从… :

ex.en: We mustn’t give in to terrorist demands.
ex.zh: 我们决不能对恐怖分子的要求让步。

ex.en: She gives in to the children all the time to avoid arguments.
ex.zh: 她一直让着孩子们，免得争吵。

senses.en: to give your time or money willingly to help other people without expecting them to do anything for you
senses.zh: 贡献时间﹙或钱财等﹚；奉献；献身:

ex.en: She’s always willing to give of her time to help the homeless.
ex.zh: 她随时愿意为帮助无家的人奉献自己的时间。

senses.en: to produce sth such as heat, light, smoke, etc.

ex.en: Burning apple wood gives off a pleasing smell.
ex.zh: 燃烧苹果木散发出芬芳气味。

senses.en: to look at or read sth very quickly and not very thoroughly

ex.en: Could you glance over this document for me?
ex.zh: 你能帮我把这份文件过目一下吗？

ex.en: I glanced through a magazine while I waited.
ex.zh: 我边等边翻阅杂志。

senses.en: to become very interested in sth such as a new fashion or an idea
senses.zh: 对﹙新款式或想法等﹚产生极大兴趣；入了魔:

ex.en: The whole nation glommed onto the scandal.
ex.zh: 整个国家都开始关注这一丑闻。

senses.en: to get great pleasure or enjoyment from sth
senses.zh: 因某事而喜悦；为某事而欣喜:

ex.en: He gloried in his son’s success.
ex.zh: 他为儿子的成就而自豪。

ex.en: I gloried in the beauty of the scenery.
ex.zh: 美丽的景色使我流连忘返。

senses.en: to take pleasure in sth
senses.zh: 以某事为快；从某事得到快乐:

ex.en: She seemed to glory in his failure.
ex.zh: 她似乎对他的失败幸灾乐祸。

senses.en: to treat sth such as a problem,mistake, etc. as if it was not important and avoid discussing it in detail

ex.en: The manager glossed over the team’s recent defeat.
ex.zh: 经理对这个队最近的失败闪烁其词。

ex.en: The movie glosses over the real issues of the war.
ex.zh: 这部电影掩饰了这次战争的真正问题。

senses.en: to make sb feel gradually more anxious or annoyed over a long period of time﹙

ex.en: These doubts had been gnawing at him for some time.
ex.zh: 这些疑虑已经折磨他一段时间了。

senses.en: to gradually have a harmful effect on sth over a long period of time﹙

ex.en: His attitude towards her gnawed away at her confidence.
ex.zh: 他对她的态度一直在削弱她的自尊心。

senses.en: to continue to do sth in your usualway, especially after sth unusual has happened;to keep busy with sth﹙
senses.zh: 尤指不寻常的事情发生后﹚ 继续做某事； 忙于某事:

ex.en: Everybody was going about their business as usual.
ex.zh: 大家照常忙着自己的事。

senses.en: to start to work at sth; to approach or deal with sth

ex.en: I want to help, but I don’t know how to go about it.
ex.zh: 我想帮忙， 可不知道如何帮。

ex.en: How should I go about finding a job?
ex.zh: 我该怎样着手找工作呢？

senses.en: to cross a room, a road, a river, etc. in order to get to the other side
senses.zh: 通过，穿过﹙房间、道路、河等﹚:

ex.en: We borrowed a boat and went across to the island.
ex.zh: 我们借了条船划到岛上去。

ex.en: Can you go across the road to the store for me?
ex.zh: 你能替我到马路对面的商店去跑一趟吗？

senses.en: to chase or follow a person or an animal to try to catch them
senses.zh: 追赶某人﹙或动物﹚；跟在…后面:

ex.en: He went after the burglars.
ex.zh: 他追赶那些窃贼。

ex.en: Aren’t you going to go after her to see if she’s all right?
ex.zh: 你要不要跟着她看看她是不是没事？

senses.en: to try to get or obtain sb/sth
senses.zh: 追求某人；谋求某事﹙或某物﹚:

ex.en: We’re both going after the same job.
ex.zh: 我们俩都在谋求同一份工作。

senses.en: to resist or oppose sb/sth; to act in a different way from what sb tells you or advises you to do
senses.zh: 反抗﹙或反对﹚某人﹙或某事﹚；与…相背:

ex.en: Anyone who goes against me will be punished.
ex.zh: 任何与我作对的人都将受到惩罚。

ex.en: He was going against his doctor’s advice by continuing to work.
ex.zh: 他没有遵照医嘱，而是继续工作。

senses.en: to be opposed or contrary to sth;to not fit or agree with sth
senses.zh: 违反某事物；与…不符﹙或相反﹚:

ex.en: This goes against everything I believe in.
ex.zh: 这完全违背了我的信念。

ex.en: Paying for my children’s education goes against my principles.
ex.zh: 为孩子们负担桝育费有违我的原则。

senses.en: (of a plan, a project,a deal, etc.
senses.zh: 计划、方案、交易等) to be carried out or happen进行；实行:

ex.en: The building of the new bridge will go ahead as planned.
ex.zh: 新桥的修建将按计划进行。

ex.en: Filming went ahead in spite of the bad weather.
ex.zh: 虽然天气不好，电影拍摄工作照常进行。

senses.en: [sing.] permission or approval for sth to start
[usually before noun] () very ambitious; trying hard to succeed, often by using new methods and ideas
senses.zh: 雄心勃勃的；进取的；有开拓精神的:

ex.en: a go-ahead young designer
ex.zh: 开拓型的年轻设计师

senses.en: to progress; to develop or improve
senses.zh: 进展； 发展； 改进:

ex.en: Things are going along nicely.
ex.zh: 情况进展良好。

senses.en: to move forward or from one end of sth towards the other

ex.en: The bus rattled as it went along.
ex.zh: 公共汽车啷啷地往前开着。

ex.en: I went along a dark narrow passage, past several doors.
ex.zh: 我沿着一条黑暗狭窄的通道向前走，经过了几道门。

senses.en: ) to agree with sb/sth
senses.zh: 赞同某事；和某人观点一致:

ex.en: I can’t go along with you on that point.
ex.zh: 在那一点上我不敢苟同。

senses.en: to accept sth or do sth, especially when you do not really want to﹙

ex.en: They didn’t like the idea, but they went along with it.
ex.zh: 他们不喜欢这个主意，可还是接受了。

ex.en: I didn’t want to make him angry, so I just went along with him (= I didn’t argue with him).
ex.zh: 我不想惹他生气，所以就不同他争辩。

senses.en: to visit a group of people or places, one by one
senses.zh: 逐一见某人﹙或到某处﹚；走遍…:

ex.en: I’ll go around and check all the doors are locked.
ex.zh: 我来挨处看看所有的门都锁上了没有。

ex.en: We spent all afternoon going round the shops.
ex.zh: 我们整整一下午都在四处逛商店。

senses.en: (of a note, etc.
senses.zh: 字条等) to be sent round a group of people so that everyone can read it被传阅:

ex.en: A card’s going around for people to sign.
ex.zh: 传给大家的一张贺卡是供签名的。

ex.en: A memo went around the department.
ex.zh: 部门中传阅了一份便函。

senses.en: to move or be placed in a circle

ex.en: The cyclist was going round the roundabout the wrong way.
ex.zh: 骑自行车的人在环岛处乱拐。

ex.en: The earth goes round the sun.
ex.zh: 地球围绕太阳转。

senses.en: to be enough for everyone to have a share
senses.zh: 足够分给每个人；够每人一份:

ex.en: There aren’t enough chairs to go round.
ex.zh: 椅子不够坐。

ex.en: Is there enough food to go around all the guests?
ex.zh: 食物够分给所有客人吗？

senses.en: to move around the outside of sth in order to get past sth or get to the other side

ex.en: We didn’t go into the city. We went around it.
ex.zh: 我们没有进城。我们绕了过去。

ex.en: Because of the flood, we had to go round by the minor roads to get to school.
ex.zh: 由于发洪水，我们只好择小道绕行去学校。

senses.en: to dress or behave in a particular way; to do sth regularly
senses.zh: 以某种方式穿着﹙或行动﹚；时常做某事:

ex.en: She goes around barefoot most of the time.
ex.zh: 她大部份时间光着脚到处跑。

ex.en: It’s not safe to go about the streets alone.
ex.zh: 独自在大街上行走不安全。

senses.en: to surround or go in a circle around sb/sth

ex.en: I felt his arm going around my shoulder.
ex.zh: 我感觉到他的胳膊搂着我的肩膀。

ex.en: The belt won't go round my waist!
ex.zh: 我的皮带不够长了！

senses.en: to move or travel around a corner

ex.en: The car’s tyres screeched as it went round the bend.
ex.zh: 汽车转弯时轮胎发出尖利的声音。

ex.en: Maggie watched until Jess had gone around the corner and was out of sight.
ex.zh: 玛吉一直目送杰斯绕过拐角处从视线中消失。

senses.en: to go crazy

ex.en: If I have to stay in this place another day, I’ll go round the bend!
ex.zh: 我要是非得在这个地方再呆上一天，我就会疯了！

senses.en: to spend a lot of time with sb or with a group of people
senses.zh: 和某人﹙或一伙人﹚泡在一块儿:

ex.en: Ann goes around with Sue.
ex.zh: 安和休形影不离。

ex.en: Ann and Sue go around together.
ex.zh: 安和休形影不离。

senses.en: to attack sb

ex.en: He went at me like a wild animal.
ex.zh: 他像只野兽一样扑向我。

senses.en: to leave a place with a particular feeling or impression
senses.zh: 带着某种感觉﹙或印象﹚离开:

ex.en: I don’t want people to go away with the wrong idea.
ex.zh: 我不想让人们带着错误的想法离开。

senses.en: to fail to keep a promise; to change your mind about sth
to think about sth again or often﹙

ex.en: I went back over the day’s events in my mind.
ex.zh: 我回想了一下白天发生的事。

senses.en: to start talking about sth again

ex.en: To go back to what you were saying before…
ex.zh: 回到你前面的话题?

senses.en: =GO BACK… 2
=GO BACK…3
to start doing sth again that you had stopped doing

ex.en: Tom turned over and went back to sleep.
ex.zh: 汤姆翻了个身又睡着了。

ex.en: I wouldn’t go back to living in the city.
ex.zh: 我不会回城里居住的。

senses.en: (of a situation
senses.zh: 局势) to return to what it was before sth else happened回到，恢复﹙先前的状况﹚:

ex.en: Things haven’t gone back to normal yet.
ex.zh: 局面尚未恢复正常。

senses.zh: (不用于进行时) to exist or happen in an earlier time居先；先前存在；以往发生:

ex.en: The present crisis is worse than any that have gone before.
ex.zh: 目前的危机比以往任何一次都严重。

senses.en: (of a legal case, a proposal or an issue
senses.zh: 法律案件、提议或议题) to be presented to sb/sth so that they can discuss it or make a decision or a judgement about it提交给…讨论﹙或决定、裁决﹚:

ex.en: When does his case go before the judge?
ex.zh: 他的案子何时提交给法官审理？

senses.en: to be greater, better, etc. than sth

ex.en: The price we got for the painting went beyond all our expectations (= was much better than we had expected).
ex.zh: 我们的画卖得的价钱大大超过我们的预计。

ex.en: The matter has gone beyond a joke (= has become very serious and is no longer amusing).
ex.zh: 这件事已经不是闹着玩的了。

senses.en: (of time
senses.zh: 时间) to pass逝去；过去:

ex.en: As time goes by, my memory seems to get worse.
ex.zh: 随着时间的推移，我的记忆似乎越来越差。

ex.en: The weeks went slowly by.
ex.zh: 时间一周周慢慢地过去了。

senses.en: to pass sb/sth without stopping﹙

ex.en: Did you see a boy go by on a bicycle?
ex.zh: 你见到过一个男孩骑自行车打这儿经过吗？

senses.en: ) to stop somewhere or visit sb for a short time, often on your way to somewhere else﹙
senses.zh: 顺路﹚停在某处，短暂地拜访某人:

senses.en: to fall to the ground

ex.en: She tripped and went down with a bump.
ex.zh: 她绊了一下，重重地摔倒在地上。

senses.en: to become lower or smaller; to fall

ex.en: The price of petrol is going down/Petrol is going down (in price).
ex.zh: 汽油价格正在下跌。

ex.en: The temperature went down by 10 degrees overnight.
ex.zh: 气温一夜间下降了10 度。

senses.en: to get worse

ex.en: The quality of the product has gone down since the company was sold.
ex.zh: 自从公司卖掉之后，产品质量下降了。

ex.en: He’s certainly gone down in my estimation (= I don’t have the good opinion of him that I used to).
ex.zh: 他确实不像我原先印象中那么好了。

senses.en: (of food,a meal, etc.
senses.zh: 食物、饭菜等) to be digested or partly digested被﹙部份﹚消化:

ex.en: Let your food go down before you go swimming.
ex.zh: 先消消食再去游泳。

senses.en: to move from a higher position to a lower one; to go along sth from one end towards the other

ex.en: One end of the see-saw goes up while the other end goes down.
ex.zh: 跷跷板一头起来，另一头就下去。

ex.en: The pain goes down my arm.
ex.zh: 疼痛顺着我的胳膊传下来。

senses.en: to be wasted; to get much worse
senses.zh: 给浪费掉；变得非常糟糕

senses.en: to follow a particular course of action, especially a difficult or harmful one
senses.zh: 采取﹙尤指艰难或有害﹚的做法:

ex.en: He said he’d never used drugs because he’d seen too many talented kids go down that road.
ex.zh: 他说他从没吸毒，因为他见过太多有才华的孩子走上那条歧路。

senses.en: to lower your body towards the ground, especially so that you are kneeling
to go to a place near where you are, or a place you often go to
senses.zh: 去，前往﹙附近或常去的地方﹚:

ex.en: Shall we go down to the beach for a swim?
ex.zh: 我们去海滩游泳吧？

ex.en: I’m going down to the corner shop for some milk.
ex.zh: 我要到拐角处的商店买牛奶。

senses.en: to become ill with sth

ex.en: I think I’m going down with a cold.
ex.zh: 我想我感冒了。

senses.en: to attack sb/sth
senses.zh: 袭击某人；抨击﹙ 或攻击﹚ … :

ex.en: She went for him with a knife.
ex.zh: 她手持尖刀向他刺去。

ex.en: () The newspapers really went for him over his defence of terrorism.
ex.zh: 报章因他为恐怖主义辩护而予以强烈谴责。

senses.en: to apply to sb/sth; to be true of sb/sth
senses.zh: 适用于某人﹙或某事物﹚；…的情况如是:

ex.en: What I said about Tim helping goes for you too, Alex.
ex.zh: 我说的关于让蒂姆帮忙的话也适用于你，亚历克斯。

ex.en: We may have high unemployment, but the same goes for many other countries.
ex.zh: 我们的失业率或许很高， 不过其他许多国家也是如此。

senses.en: to go to get sb/sth
senses.zh: 去带回某人；去取回某物:

ex.en: Shall I go for a doctor?
ex.zh: 要我去请医生吗？

ex.en: She’s gone for some milk.
ex.zh: 她买牛奶去了。

senses.en: to be attracted by sb/sth; to like or prefer sb/sth
senses.zh: 为…所吸引；喜欢﹙或较喜欢﹚…:

ex.en: He’s not the type I usually go for.
ex.zh: 我一般不会找他这种人。

ex.en: Children usually go for colourful packaging.
ex.zh: 儿童一般喜欢色彩鲜艳的包装。

senses.en: to choose sth

ex.en: I think I’ll go for the steak.
ex.zh: 我想要牛排。

ex.en: Which computer system are they going for?
ex.zh: 他们要选哪套计算机系统？

senses.en: to try to get or achieve sth

ex.en: Did you go for that job?
ex.zh: 你争取过那份工作吗？

ex.en: He’s going for the world record.
ex.zh: 他要争取打破世界纪录。

senses.en: to be sold for the price mentioned﹙

ex.en: These computers usually go for under ￡1000.
ex.zh: 这类电脑一般卖不到1 000 英镑。

senses.en: to leave a place and go somewhere,especially in order to do sth good or brave
senses.zh: 动身去某处， 起程﹙ 尤指为做好事或需要勇气的事﹚

senses.en: to make progress; to begin to happen or be successful
senses.zh: 进展；开始发生﹙或有成效﹚:

ex.en: The project is going forward nicely.
ex.zh: 工程进展顺利。

ex.en: Now that we have his agreement, the deal can go forward.
ex.zh: 既然我们得到了他的许可，就可以进行交易了。

senses.en: (of clocks and watches
senses.zh: 钟表) to be set one hour ahead at the beginning of summer﹙夏季开始时﹚被拨快一小时:

ex.en: The clocks go forward tonight. We have an hour less in bed.
ex.zh: 今晚时钟要拨快。我们得少睡一小时。

senses.en: to be suggested as a candidate for a job or an elected position, etc.

ex.en: Her name has gone forward for the job.
ex.zh: 有人提名她负责这项工作。

senses.en: (of the sun or moon
senses.zh: 日、月) to disappear behind a cloud躲进云里:

ex.en: The sun went in and it grew colder.
ex.zh: 太阳躲到云后，天更冷了。

senses.en: (of a piece of equipment, furniture, etc.
senses.zh: 器材、傢具等) to be built or fitted in a place装入；嵌入:

ex.en: The kitchen will be finished once the fridge has gone in.
ex.zh: 冰箱放进去之后厨房就安排停当了。

senses.en: to enter a room, a house, etc.

ex.en: It’s getting cold; let’s go in.
ex.zh: 天冷了；我们进屋去吧。

ex.en: Let’s go in the kitchen — it’s warmer.
ex.zh: 我们进厨房吧─里面暖和些。

senses.en: to fit into a container, etc.

ex.en: The suitcase is full already — those shoes definitely won’t go in.
ex.zh: 箱子已经满了─鞋子肯定放不下了。

ex.en: I’m amazed that all the luggage went in the car.
ex.zh: 行李全都放进车子里了，我很感意外。

senses.en: ) to join an organization,especially one of the armed forces or the police
senses.zh: 加入某组织﹙尤指军队或警察部门﹚:

ex.en: He was 17 when he went in the army.
ex.zh: 他参军时17岁。

ex.en: Ed wants to go into the Marines.
ex.zh: 埃德想加入海军。

senses.en: to go to an office or another place of work in order to work, do a particular task, have some work done for you, etc.
senses.zh: 去办公室，去工作单位﹙工作、从事某任务、找人服务等﹚:

ex.en: I’ve got to work tomorrow, but I can always go in late.
ex.zh: 我明天要工作，但我上班总还可以迟到。

ex.en: The car needs to go in (= into the garage) for a service.
ex.zh: 汽车需要开去﹙汽车修理厂﹚维修了。

senses.en: to go to a hospital to receive treatment, tests, etc.
senses.zh: 去医院﹙接受治疗、检测等﹚:

ex.en: I’m going in on Friday for an X-ray.
ex.zh: 我星期五要去医院照X 光。

ex.en: When is Cara going into hospital?
ex.zh: 卡拉什么时候去医院？

senses.en: (of soldiers,an army, etc.
senses.zh: 士兵、部队等) to go to a place where there is fighting or a war and become involved in it上战场；参战:

ex.en: Troops are going in tonight.
ex.zh: 部队今天夜里上战场。

senses.en: to take part in a competition; to take an exam

ex.en: She goes in for all the competitions in the magazines and never wins anything.
ex.zh: 她参加了杂志里登的所有比赛，然而从未得过奖。

ex.en: Which events are you going in for at the school sports?
ex.zh: 学校运动会上你要参加什么项目？

senses.en: =GO INTO STH 3

ex.en: He decided to go in for politics.
ex.zh: 他决定从政。

senses.en: to like sth and regularly use it, do it, etc.; to have sth as an interest or a hobby
senses.zh: 喜欢用﹙或做﹚…；有…兴趣；以…为业余爱好:

ex.en: She goes in for very bright colours.
ex.zh: 她喜欢鲜艳的色彩。

ex.en: He doesn’t really go in for making long speeches.
ex.zh: 他其实不喜欢做长篇讲话。

senses.en: to join sb in a particular project, activity, business, etc.
senses.zh: 与某人合伙；与某人联合办企业:

ex.en: Jack went in with some friends to start a car hire business.
ex.zh: 杰克和一些朋友做起汽车租赁生意来。

ex.en: I’ll go in with you on (= I’ll give you some money for) Mary’s present.
ex.zh: 我和你凑份子给玛丽买礼物。

senses.en: (of a vehicle
senses.zh: 交通工具) to hit sth violently; to crash into sth猛地撞上某物:

ex.en: The car skidded and went into a tree.
ex.zh: 汽车打滑，猛地撞到树上。

senses.en: (of a vehicle or driver
senses.zh: 交通工具或驾驶员) to start a particular movement开始某种动作；开始以某种方式移动:

ex.en: The truck went into a spin on a patch of ice.
ex.zh: 卡车在一片冰上打起转来。

ex.en: The plane went into a nosedive.
ex.zh: 飞机开始俯冲。

senses.en: to begin to be in a particular state or situation

ex.en: She went into a coma after the accident.
ex.zh: 事故之后她进入了昏迷状态。

ex.en: The country is going into a decline.
ex.zh: 这个国家开始衰落。

senses.en: to begin to act or behave in a particular way﹙
senses.zh: 以某种方式﹚开始做某事；开始某种表现:

ex.en: He went into a long explanation of the affair.
ex.zh: 他开始长篇大论地解释起那件事来。

senses.en: to examine or discuss sth carefully
to start taking part in an exam, a competition,an election, etc.
senses.zh: 参加考试﹙或竞赛、竞选等﹚:

ex.en: I can’t go into the exam unprepared.
ex.zh: 这次考试我不能打无准备之仗。

senses.en: Notice also the example.
to move away from sthlarge or important and go in a different direction
senses.zh: 离开﹙大的或重要的事物﹚；岔开:

ex.en: The road youwant goes off on the right.
ex.zh: 你想走的路从右边分岔。

ex.en: () She’s always going off the point (= not talking about the main topic).
ex.zh: 她讲话动不动就离题。

senses.en: to leave the stage, thesports field, etc. during a play or a game﹙
senses.zh: 演出或比赛中﹚下场，退场:

ex.en: Hamlet goes off in the middle of the scene.
ex.zh: 哈姆雷特在这一场中途退下。

ex.en: Johnson went off at half-time.
ex.zh: 约翰逊中场休息时下场了。

senses.en: to loseinterest in sb/sth; to stop liking sb/sth
senses.zh: 失去对…的兴趣；不再喜欢某人﹙或某事物﹚:

ex.en: I think she’s going off me.
ex.zh: 我觉得她不喜欢我了。

ex.en: He’s gone off his food.
ex.zh: 他不再喜欢他的食物。

senses.en: to leave your husband, wife,partner, etc. in order to have a relationship withsb else

ex.en: Eddie’s gone off with his wife’s best friend.
ex.zh: 埃迪跟他妻子最要好的朋友跑了。

senses.en: to last for a particulartime

ex.en: The meeting went on for hours.
ex.zh: 会开了好几个小时。

ex.en: How much longer will this hot weather go on (for)?
ex.zh: 这样炎热的天气还会持续多久？

senses.en: to continue speaking after a shortpause﹙

ex.en: ‘You know’, he went on, ‘I never liked her.’
ex.zh: “你知道的，”他接着说，“我从未喜欢过她。”

ex.en: Go on then! Tell me what happened!
ex.zh: 那么快说吧！告诉我发生了什么事！

senses.en: (of time
senses.zh: 时间) to pass流逝；过去:

ex.en: Things will improve as time goes on.
ex.zh: 随着时间的推移，情况会好起来的。

ex.en: She became more miserable as the evening went on.
ex.zh: 夜渐深，她越来越难受。

senses.en: to continue to travel in the direction you are going﹙
senses.zh: 按本来的方向﹚继续旅行，继续行进:

ex.en: I’m too tired to go on.
ex.zh: 我太累，走不动了。

ex.en: They had an accident and couldn’t go on.
ex.zh: 他们出了意外，无法继续旅行。

senses.en: to drive and encourage sb to do sth

ex.en: They goaded him on to break the window.
ex.zh: 他们唆使他打破窗户。

ex.en: The boxers were goaded on by the shrieking crowd.
ex.zh: 拳击运动员听见观众的喊叫就来劲儿了。

senses.en: to eat food very quickly

ex.en: I gobbled down my breakfast and ran out of the house.
ex.zh: 我狼吞虎咽地吃早餐就跑出屋子。

senses.en: to use all of sth,especially money, very quickly

ex.en: The rent gobbles up half his earnings.
ex.zh: 租金用去了他一半的收入。

senses.en: to waste your time doing silly or stupid things
senses.zh: 把时间浪费在荒谬无聊的事情上:

ex.en: Come on, quit goofing around — this is serious.
ex.zh: 快点，别浪费时间了—这是正经事。

senses.en: to waste time when you are supposed to be working
a lazy person who does not work hard
to make a mistake; to spoil sth by making a mistake or doing it badly

ex.en: He always goofs up (on exams).
ex.zh: 他总是考砸。

ex.en: He really goofed up his exam.
ex.zh: 他确实考砸了。

senses.en: to remove sth, or form sth, by digging into a surface with a sharp tool, your fingers, etc.﹙

ex.en: I wanted to gouge her eyes out.
ex.zh: 我那时想把她的双眼挖出来。

ex.en: Glaciers gouged out valleys from the hills.
ex.zh: 冰川把丘陵地带冲出一条条山谷。

senses.en: to try to take hold of sb/sth﹙

ex.en: She grabbed at the branch, missed and fell.
ex.zh: 她想抓住树枝，却失手坠落下来。

senses.en: to take advantage of an opportunity to do or have sth

ex.en: He’ll grab at any excuse to avoid doing the dishes.
ex.zh: 他会找任何藉口逃避洗碗的。

senses.en: to try to deal with a difficult situation or solve a difficult problem
senses.zh: 努力应付困境﹙或解决难题﹚:

ex.en: I’ve spent all afternoon grappling with these accounts.
ex.zh: 我用了整整一下午处理这些账目。

senses.en: to try to take hold of sth/sb in your hands

ex.en: She grasped at his coat.
ex.zh: 她使劲抓住了他的上衣。

senses.en: to try to take advantage of an opportunity, especially because you are unhappy with the present situation﹙
senses.zh: 尤因不满现状﹚急切抓住机会:

ex.en: He grasped at any hope of escape.
ex.zh: 任何逃生的希望他都不放过。

senses.en: to try very hard to find a solution to a problem or some hope in a difficult or unpleasant situation, even though this seems very unlikely﹙
senses.zh: 在危难中﹚抓救命稻草，不放过任何渺茫的希望

senses.en: to cover an area of ground with grass

ex.en: The garden had been grassed over.
ex.zh: 花园里长满了草。

senses.en: to inform the police or sb in authority about a crime or sth bad that sb has done﹙
senses.zh: 向警方或当局﹚告密，告发:

ex.en: My girlfriend grassed me up.
ex.zh: 女朋友出卖了我。

senses.en: It is also possible to say

ex.en: My girlfriend grassed (on me).
ex.zh: 女朋友出卖了我。

senses.en: to move towards sb/sth that you are attracted to
senses.zh: 被吸引到；受吸引而转向:

ex.en: Most visitors to New York gravitate to Times Square.
ex.zh: 大多数来纽约的游客都被吸引到时代广场。

senses.en: to treat sb in a harsh way or annoy them for a long time until they can no longer defend themselves or fight back

ex.en: Don’t let your colleagues grind you down!
ex.zh: 别让你的同事亏待你！

ex.en: The villagers had been ground down by years of poverty.
ex.zh: 村民年复一年地受贫穷的折腾。

senses.en: to continue for a long time in a boring or unpleasant way

ex.en: The negotiations ground on for months.
ex.zh: 谈判拖拖拉拉持续了几个月。

senses.en: to produce sth in large quantities over a long period of time, especially sth that is not interesting or of good quality
senses.zh: 大量生产；﹙尤指﹚粗制漤造:

ex.en: He grinds out a novel a month.
ex.zh: 他一个月就胡乱拼凑出一部小说。

senses.en: to try hard to find sth

ex.en: I stepped in the door and groped for the light switch.
ex.zh: 我迈进门去摸索着找电灯开关。

ex.en: ()‘Yes, but….’ He was groping for words.
ex.zh: “是啊，可是…”他努力找词儿。

senses.en: to try to find an agreement, an answer to a problem, etc.
senses.zh: 努力达成一致；试图找到答案﹙等﹚:

ex.en: The two parties are groping towards a compromise.
ex.zh: 双方正在努力寻求妥协。

senses.en: to make sb feel disgusted
senses.zh: 使某人恶心﹙或憎恶、作呕等﹚:

ex.en: His greasy hair really grosses me out!
ex.zh: 他那油乎乎的头发实在使我恶心！

senses.en: to be based on sth

ex.en: Is the story grounded in fact?
ex.zh: 这是真人真事吗？

senses.en: to become less close to sb in a relationship

ex.en: We used to be good friends, but we’ve grown apart.
ex.zh: 我们曾经很要好，可现在疏远了。

senses.en: to come to have a less close relationship with sb; to depend on sb less
senses.zh: 逐渐疏远某人；减少对某人的依赖:

ex.en: She has grown away from her parents.
ex.zh: 她不再那么依赖父母了。

senses.en: to gradually become sth over a period of time

ex.en: She had grown into a beautiful young woman.
ex.zh: 她出落成了一个漂亮的姑娘。

senses.en: to become familiar with and confident in a new job, activity, etc.

ex.en: He needs time to grow into the job.
ex.zh: 他需要时间适应这个工作。

senses.en: to let your hair grow so that the colour or style changes or disappears
senses.zh: 让头发长长以使染色﹙ 或发式﹚ 消失:

ex.en: I’ve decided to grow the layers out.
ex.zh: 我决定把我分层削短的头发留长。

senses.en: mentally and physically an adult

ex.en: He has two grown-up children.
ex.zh: 他有两个已成年的孩子。

senses.en: adult, mature

ex.en: Susie is very grown-up for her age.
ex.zh: 相对她的年龄来说苏西非常成熟。

senses.zh: (尤用于成年人对儿童说话或作儿童用语) an adult person大人；成人:

ex.en: The grown-ups will sit at one table and the children at another.
ex.zh: 大人坐一桌，孩子坐另一桌。

senses.en: to dig sth out of the ground
senses.zh: 掘出， 挖出﹙ 某物﹚ :

ex.en: Thousands of miles of hedgerows have been grubbed up.
ex.zh: 几千英里的树篱被挖了出来。

senses.en: to do sth to prevent sth happening or to protect yourself from sth
senses.zh: 防止，防范，提防﹙某事﹚；避免做某事:

ex.en: Clean the wound to guard against the danger of infection.
ex.zh: 清洗伤口以防感染。

ex.en: We should guard against the possibility of this happening again.
ex.zh: 我们应该提防这事可能再次发生。

senses.en: to try to imagine sth or make a judgement without knowing all the facts

ex.en: We can only guess at the reason for his actions.
ex.zh: 我们只能猜测他行动的原因。

senses.en: to stop yourself showing that you are upset by swallowing hard
senses.zh: 咽下…﹙以防止感情的流露﹚:

senses.en: to swallow sth quickly and noisily
senses.zh: 狼吞虎咽；匆匆吞下﹙或喝下﹚:

ex.en: He gulped down a glass of water.
ex.zh: 他把一杯水一饮而尽。

senses.en: to fill sth with a sticky substance so that it cannot move or work﹙

ex.en: My eyes were all gummed up.
ex.zh: 我的眼皮粘住了。

ex.en: The substance gummed the machine up.
ex.zh: 这东西把机器粘得不能转动。

senses.en: to shoot sb, especially so as to kill or seriously injure them

ex.en: He was gunned down outside his home.
ex.zh: 他在自家门前遭枪杀。

ex.en: Terrorists gunned down six people in the town last month.
ex.zh: 上个月恐怖分子在城里开枪打死了六个人。

senses.zh: (只用于进行时) to try to blame sb or cause trouble for them伺机指责﹙ 或骚扰﹚某人:

ex.en: She’s been gunning for me since I came to work here.
ex.zh: 自从我来这里工作之后她一直伺机找茬。

senses.en: to dress sb/yourself in special, attractive clothes; to decorate sth to make it look attractive
senses.zh: 把…打扮得漂漂亮亮；装饰…:

ex.en: She gussied herself up for the big party.
ex.zh: 她把自己打扮得光彩照人去参加盛大聚会。

senses.en: to cut or change sth in a rough and careless way
senses.zh: 乱砍；乱剪；粗率(或胡乱)地改变:

ex.en: The hairdressers have hacked her hair about a bit.
ex.zh: 理发师把她的头发削得有点乱。

ex.en: () The script was hacked about by several people before the movie was finished.
ex.zh: 电影拍完之前，有几个人大刀阔斧地把脚本删改得面目全非。

senses.en: to try to cut sth using strong rough blows with an axe, a knife, scissors, etc.

ex.en: She’s really hacked at my hair. It’s a complete mess.
ex.zh: 她实在是对我的头发下了狠手，把它剪得一塌煳涂。

ex.en: He was hacking away at the trees with an axe.
ex.zh: 他用斧子对着那些树猛砍。

senses.en: to cut a tree, etc. roughly so that it falls to the ground

ex.en: They are hacking down the forests to sell the timber.
ex.zh: 他们在砍伐森林销售木材。

senses.en: to find a way of looking at or changing the information on sb else’s computer without their knowledge or permission
senses.zh: 非法侵入(他人计算机系统):

ex.en: A teenage girl managed to hack into the bank’s computer.
ex.zh: 一名十几岁的女孩设法侵入了这家银行的计算机。

senses.en: to make sb feel extremely annoyed or irritated
senses.zh: 使极其恼怒；使非常生气:

ex.en: He was hacked off with the whole situation.
ex.zh: 他对整个局面大为恼火。

ex.en: She always wants her jobs done in the next 10 minutes. That really hacks me off.
ex.zh: 她总是要别人10 分钟之内就把活干完。这使我非常气愤。

senses.en: to cut sth off sth with rough heavy blows
senses.zh: 把…(从…上)砍下来；削掉(…上的)…:

ex.en: They hacked off the dead branches.
ex.zh: 他们把枯树枝砍掉了。

ex.en: He hacked the padlock off the door.
ex.zh: 他把门上的挂锁砸掉了。

senses.en: to cut sth very roughly into large pieces

ex.en: He hacked up the meat with a large knife.
ex.zh: 他用大刀大块大块地把肉剁开。

senses.en: to come from or to live in a particular place

ex.en: Which part of Ireland does he hail from?
ex.zh: 他来自爱尔兰的哪个地区？

senses.en: to act in a deliberately artificial or exaggerated way
senses.zh: 夸张表情(或动作)；表演过火:

ex.en: The actors were really hamming it up.
ex.zh: 演员们表演得实在太夸张。

senses.en: to work hard in order to finish or achieve sth; to repeat sth again and again
senses.zh: 努力干；孜孜以求；不断重复:

ex.en: He kept hammering away at the same point all through the meeting.
ex.zh: 他开会自始至终都在反复强调同一点。

senses.en: to force sb to learn sth by repeating it many times

ex.en: I’ll manage to hammer the point in somehow.
ex.zh: 我将设法反复灌输这一点。

ex.en: They have had English grammar hammered into them.
ex.zh: 他们学习英语语法都是通过反复灌输。

senses.en: to discuss a plan, a deal, etc.for a long time and with great effort, until sth is decided or agreed on
senses.zh: 反复讨论出(一致意见)；充分研讨出(决定):

ex.en: It took weeks to hammer out an agreement.
ex.zh: 经过多个星期的反复讨论才达成协议。

senses.en: used by a television or radio reporter at the end of a report from a particular place to show that the main presenter will continue
senses.zh: (电视或电台记者从某地报道结束时示意主持人将继续主持)现在请回到…那里:

ex.en: Now I’ll hand you back to Trevor in the studio.
ex.zh: 现在请回到演播室特雷弗那里。

senses.en: to give sth back to the person, country, etc. who used to have it or who owns it legally
senses.zh: 把…归还(给原先或合法的拥有人、国家等):

ex.en: The territory was handed back to Egypt.
ex.zh: 领土归还给了埃及。

ex.en: We will not press charges if the stolen money is handed back.
