ex.zh: 如果把偷走的钱还回来，我们将不予控告。

senses.en: ) (of a court of law or other official body
senses.zh: 法庭或其他官方团体)to announce an official decision正式宣布；公布:

ex.en: The judge handed down a sentence of six years.
ex.zh: 法官宣布判处六年徒刑。

senses.en: [usually pl.] () clothing that is no longer wanted and is given to sb else, especially a younger brother or sister
senses.zh: 被抛弃(或传给别人)的衣物:

ex.en: I used to hate wearing my brother’s hand-me-downs.
ex.zh: 我以前讨厌穿我哥哥倒下来的旧衣服。

senses.en: to give a piece of work to sb, such as a teacher, so that they can correct,read or deal with it; to give sth to sb in authority because it belongs to them or is lost
senses.zh: 提交， 呈交，上交(书面材料或失物等):

ex.en: Make sure you hand in your homework on time.
ex.zh: 一定要按时交家庭作业。

ex.en: Hand your room keys in by 10 a.m.
ex.zh: 上午10 点之前交房间钥匙。

senses.en: to send or give sth to another person after you have finished with it
senses.zh: 把某事物交给(某人)使用(或处理):

ex.en: Hand on the magazine to your friends.
ex.zh: 把杂志传给你的朋友阅读。

ex.en: The task has been handed on to me.
ex.zh: 这项任务交给了我继续处理。

senses.en: =HAND STH DOWN 1
to give sth to each person in a group

ex.en: She handed textbooks out to the new students.
ex.zh: 她把课本发给新生。

senses.en: to give advice, criticism,a punishment, etc. to sb
senses.zh: 提出，给予(建议、批评、惩罚等) :

ex.en: The courts are handing out tough sentences to frequent offenders.
ex.zh: 法庭正对惯犯予以重判。

senses.en: something that is given free to people, especially food, money or clothes
senses.zh: 免费品(尤指食物、钱或衣物)

senses.en: a document giving information about sth, especially one that is given to a group or a class by a teacher, speaker,etc.
senses.zh: (尤指发给学生、听众等的)讲义

senses.en: to give sb else a turn to speak when you have finished talking
senses.zh: (讲话结束后)请其他人讲话，让某人听另一个人讲话:

ex.en: I’d like to hand over now to our guest speaker.
ex.zh: 现在有请我们的特邀演讲人发言。

ex.en: I’ll hand you over to dad for a chat.
ex.zh: 请你跟我爸爸聊聊。

senses.en: [C] [U] the act of moving power or responsibility from one person or group to another; the period during which this happens
to give sb/sth officially to sb else,especially sb in authority
senses.zh: 把人或物交出(给当局处理) ； 引渡； 自首:

ex.en: They handed him over to the police.
ex.zh: 他们把他交给了警方。

ex.en: He forced me to hand over the keys to the safe.
ex.zh: 他逼我交出保险柜的钥匙。

senses.en: to offer or pass sth (especially food and drink) to each person in a group of people or in a room
senses.zh: 传递，分发(尤指食物或饮料):

ex.en: Could you hand round the sandwiches, please?
ex.zh: 请分发一下三明治好吗？

senses.en: ) =HANG ON 3
=HANG AROUND
to wait

ex.en: Sorry to keep you hanging around for so long.
ex.zh: 对不起让你等了这么久。

ex.en: I won’t hang about for you if you’re late.
ex.zh: 你要是来晚了我就不等你了。

senses.en: to delay doing sth; to be slow to do sth

ex.en: Have you finished already? You don’t hang about, do you?
ex.zh: 你已经完成了？你蛮快呀，是不是？

senses.en: to spend time somewhere, without doing very much

ex.en: We spent most of the day hanging about doing nothing.
ex.zh: 我们那天大部份时间都在闲荡。

ex.en: Children hang around the streets because there’s nowhere for them to play.
ex.zh: 孩子们在街上东游西逛，因为他们没有地方玩。

senses.en: to spend a lot of time with sb or with a group of people
senses.zh: (和某人)常待在一起，泡在一块儿:

ex.en: Bob hangs around with Tim.
ex.zh: 鲍勃和蒂姆形影不离。

ex.en: Bob and Tim hang around together.
ex.zh: 鲍勃和蒂姆形影不离。

senses.en: to not move forwards because you are nervous or afraid

ex.en: She hung back, afraid to go near the dog.
ex.zh: 她站在原地，不敢走近那条狗。

senses.en: to stay behind in a place such as a school or an office after most of the other people have left

ex.en: My friends rushed out, but I hung back to talk to the teacher.
ex.zh: 朋友们急忙跑出去了，可我留下来找老师说话。

senses.en: to be unwilling to do sth; to hesitate

ex.en: This is a great opportunity. We can’t afford to hang back.
ex.zh: 这是个绝好的机会。我们可不能再犹豫了。

senses.en: to hold sb/sth firmly

ex.en: Hang on tight and you won’t fall off.
ex.zh: 你抓紧就不会掉下去。

ex.en: The horse suddenly galloped off and I tried to hang on as best as I could.
ex.zh: 马突然飞奔起来，我拚命抓紧绳。

senses.en: ,) used to ask sb to wait for a short time

ex.en: Hang on a minute — I’m nearly ready.
ex.zh: 请等一下─我快准备好了。

ex.en: The line’s engaged. Would you like to hang on?
ex.zh: 占线。你稍候好吗？

senses.en: to continue trying to do sth, even though it is very difficult

ex.en: Hang on in there! The exams will soon be over.
ex.zh: 坚持下去！考试很快就结束了。

senses.en: to hold sth/sb tightly

ex.en: Hang onto my hand while we cross the road.
ex.zh: 过马路时拉紧我的手。

senses.en: () a place where you live or enjoy spending time with friends
senses.zh: 住所；(和朋友) 常到之处:

ex.en: a popular hang-out for teenagers
ex.zh: 青少年聚首的热门地方

senses.en: to attach things that you have washed to a piece of string or rope outside so that they can dry; to put sth such as a flag, etc. out of a window or in a street by attaching it to a piece of string or rope
senses.zh: 把(衣服) 晾出去；把(旗帜等)挂出去:

ex.en: Have you hung the washing out?
ex.zh: 你把洗好的衣服晾出去了吗？

ex.en: Many houses hung out a banner supporting the march.
ex.zh: 很多住房外悬挂了支持游行的横幅。

senses.en: to be well organized and fit together well; to have parts that all agree with each other

ex.en: The book doesn’t really hang together.
ex.zh: 这本书的结构不很紧密。

ex.en: This account of what happened doesn’t hang together.
ex.zh: 对事情的这一描述前后矛盾。

senses.en: to attach sth from the top to a hook, a piece of string, etc. so that the lower part is free or loose; to be attached in this way

ex.en: My dress is hanging up in the wardrobe.
ex.zh: 我的连衣裙挂在衣柜里。

ex.en: Shall I hang your coat up?
ex.zh: 我帮你把大衣挂起来好吗？

senses.en: to be delayed

ex.en: I got hung up in traffic.
ex.zh: 我遇上了交通阻塞。

ex.en: Sorry I’m late — I got hung up at the office.
ex.zh: 对不起我来晚了─我在办公室脱不开身。

senses.en: to spend a lot of time with sb
senses.zh: (和某人)长时间待在一起，泡在一块儿:

ex.en: Are you still hanging with those guys?
ex.zh: 你还和那些人混在一起吗？

senses.en: to want sth very much

ex.en: He hankered after big city life.
ex.zh: 他嚮往大城市的生活。

senses.en: to arrive or appear unexpectedly

ex.en: A police car happened along just at that moment.
ex.zh: 就在那时一辆警车出乎意料地出现了。

senses.en: to find or meet sb/sth by chance
senses.zh: 偶然发现某物；碰巧遇见某人:

ex.en: I happened upon the book I wanted in a second-hand bookshop.
ex.zh: 我在一家二手书店偶然发现了我想要的那本书。

senses.en: to talk about or remember sth that happened in the past or was mentioned before

ex.en: You can’t keep harking back to the past.
ex.zh: 你不能没完没了地唸叨从前。

senses.en: to keep talking about sth in a way that other people find annoying

ex.en: He’s still harping on about having his bike stolen.
ex.zh: 他还在唠叨自行车失窃的事。

ex.en: He’s always harping on the same theme.
ex.zh: 他总是没完没了地唸叨同一个主题。

senses.en: to discuss sth in detail for a long time in order to reach an agreement

ex.en: They are still hashing out the details of the contract.
ex.zh: 他们还在反复商议合同的细节。

senses.en: to make sb appear in a court of law in order to be judged

ex.en: They were hauled before the courts.
ex.zh: 他们被移交法庭审判。

ex.en: They hauled her up in front of senior officers.
ex.zh: 他们把她送交高级军官究办。

senses.en: to take sb somewhere by force

ex.en: They hauled him off to jail.
ex.zh: 他们押送他去监狱。

senses.en: to make sb appear in a court of law in order to be judged

ex.en: He was hauled up on a charge of dangerous driving.
ex.zh: 他被控危险驾驶已交法院审判。

senses.zh: (不用于进行时) to dislike sb/sth for a particular reason因…而不喜欢…:

senses.en: to allow a husband,wife or partner that you are separated from to return
senses.zh: 允许分手的丈夫(或妻子、伴侣)回头；愿与某人重修旧好:

ex.en: He had his wife back time and time again.
ex.zh: 他一再允许妻子回到身边。

senses.en: to invite sb to your house after you have been somewhere with them
senses.zh: (一起相处后) 邀请某人回自己家:

ex.en: After the cinema we had everybody back for coffee.
ex.zh: 看完电影之后，我们请大家到家里喝咖啡。

senses.en: to think that sb is a particular type of person, especially when in fact they are not
to have sb doing some work in your home or office
senses.zh: 让某人来家里(或办公室)工作:

ex.en: They’ve got the builders in all week.
ex.zh: 他们让建筑工来干了整整一星期了。

ex.en: We had the inspectors in on Tuesday.
ex.zh: 我们星期二接受检查员检查了。

senses.en: to have sex with sb
to joke with sb by pretending sth is true when it is not
senses.zh: 哄骗，欺骗(通常作为玩笑):

ex.en: ‘We’ve won a new car!’ ‘You’re having me on!’
ex.zh: “我们赢了辆新车！”“你是在哄我吧！”

senses.en: to have a piece of electrical equipment switched on

ex.en: I didn’t hear you come in because I had the radio on.
ex.zh: 我开着收音机， 没听见你进来。

senses.en: to know sth bad about someone that can be used against them

ex.en: The police had nothing on him (= no evidence that he had committed a crime).
ex.zh: 警方没掌握他什么证据。

senses.en: to have a tooth or an organ of your body removed

ex.en: I had to have a tooth out.
ex.zh: 我只好拔掉一颗牙。

senses.en: to invite sb to come to your house

ex.en: They had some friends over last night.
ex.zh: 他们昨晚请了些朋友到家里来。

ex.en: We’re having people round for dinner tonight.
ex.zh: 我们今晚有客人来吃饭。

senses.en: to accuse sb of sth and bring them to a court of law to be examined by a judge
senses.zh: 使某人(为某事) 出庭受审:

ex.en: He was had up for dangerous driving.
ex.zh: 他因危险驾驶被送上法庭。

senses.en: to try to sell things by going from place to place asking people to buy them

ex.en: Pirate copies of their CD were being hawked around.
ex.zh: 他们的光碟给盗版后在街上兜售。

ex.en: They hawked their newsletter around student bars.
ex.zh: 他们在学生小卖部推销他们的简讯。

senses.en: to be going in a particular direction or to a particular place
senses.zh: 朝…方向(或地方)行进；前往:

ex.en: It’s time I was heading for home.
ex.zh: 到我该回家去的时候了。

ex.en: Jane headed for the door.
ex.zh: 简走向门口。

senses.en: to be likely to experience sth,especially sth bad
senses.zh: 很可能遭受(尤指不幸)；会招致:

ex.en: They’re heading for trouble.
ex.zh: 他们会惹麻烦的。

ex.en: The country is headed for an economic disaster.
ex.zh: 国家将要陷入经济灾难。

senses.en: to leave a place to go somewhere else or do sth else

ex.en: It’s time we headed off to get the train.
ex.zh: 我们该动身去上火车了。

senses.en: to prevent sth; to stop sb from doing sth
senses.zh: 阻止，防止(某事发生)；阻止(某人做某事):

ex.en: Their attempts to head off criticism have failed.
ex.zh: 他们阻止别人批评的努力失败了。

senses.en: to be in charge of sth such as a department, a company,an organization, etc.
senses.zh: 领导，主管(某部门、公司或机构等):

ex.en: She heads up our finance division.
ex.zh: 她是我们的财务部门主管。

senses.en: to put a lot of sth in a pile on sth

ex.en: She heaped food on my plate.
ex.zh: 她往我的盘子里放了很多食物。

ex.en: The food was heaped on the plate.
ex.zh: 盘子里堆满了食物。

senses.en: to offer or give sb a lot of sth, especially praise or criticism
senses.zh: 大量提供(或送)给某人；(尤指)对某人大加赞扬(或批评) :

ex.en: They heaped scorn upon his proposal.
ex.zh: 他们对他的建议大加嘲讽。

ex.en: Praise was heaped on the police for their handling of the case.
ex.zh: 警方处理这一案件得到了高度赞扬。

senses.en: to put sth into a pile

ex.en: A huge pile of washing was heaped up in a corner.
ex.zh: 角落里攒了一大堆待洗的衣服。

senses.en: to be told news or information about sb/sth
senses.zh: 得知(有关某人的)信息；获悉:

ex.en: I’m so sorry to hear about your mother (=for example, that she is ill).
ex.zh: 获悉你母亲的事我很难过。

ex.en: Have you heard about your job yet (= if you have got it or not)?
ex.zh: 你的工作有消息了吗？

senses.en: to receive news or information from sb, usually by letter or telephone

ex.en: Do you ever hear from any of your school friends?
ex.zh: 你收到过你的校友的信吗？

ex.en: () I look forward to hearing from you.
ex.zh: 盼望着收到你的信。

senses.en: to formally get sb’s opinion about sth or their description of sth that has happened, such as an accident, etc.
senses.zh: 听取某人的意见(或陈述、汇报等):

ex.en: Can we hear from some of the women in the audience?
ex.zh: 我们能否听一些妇女观众的意见？

ex.en: The police would like to hear from anyone who witnessed the accident.
ex.zh: 警方想要听取这次事故的任何目击者的陈述。

senses.en: to know about sb/sth because you have been told about them/it

ex.en: I’ve heard of the Alexander technique, but I don’t know anything about it.
ex.zh: 我听说过亚历山大方法，可我对此一点都不了解。

ex.en: I’ve never heard of him.
ex.zh: 我从未听到过他的消息。

senses.en: to have news of sb/sth

ex.en: I was sorry to hear of your accident.
ex.zh: 获悉你遇到了意外，我很难过。

ex.en: He was last heard of in Liverpool.
ex.zh: 最后一次听到他的消息时，他在利物浦。

senses.en: that has never been known or done; surprising
senses.zh: 前所未闻的；空前的；惊人的:

ex.en: It’s almost unheard-of for it to rain there in July.
ex.zh: 那里七月份下雨很罕见。

senses.en: to not allow something or not allow sb to do sth

ex.en: I offered to go but she wouldn’t hear of it.
ex.zh: 我建议由我去，但她不允许。

ex.en: They wouldn’t hear of us postponing the trip.
ex.zh: 他们就是不同意我们推迟旅行。

senses.en: to listen until sb has finished saying what they want to say

ex.en: I know you don’t believe me, but please hear me out!
ex.zh: 我知道你不相信我，可是请听我说完！

senses.en: to become warm or hot;to make sth warm or hot

ex.en: The pipes will expand as they heat up.
ex.zh: 管子变热就会膨胀。

ex.en: We can heat up the soup in the microwave.
ex.zh: 我们可以把汤放在微波炉里热一热。

senses.en: to surround and limit sth with conditions or restrictions

ex.en: Employment is hedged around with legislation nowadays.
ex.zh: 如今雇工受法律限制。

senses.en: to surround sb/sth with sth;to restrict the freedom of sb to do sth

ex.en: The cathedral is hedged in by other buildings.
ex.zh: 大桝堂四周有建筑物围着。

ex.en: He felt hedged in by all the rules and regulations.
ex.zh: 他感觉被这一切规章制度束缚住了。

senses.en: to try to make sth happen more quickly or easily
senses.zh: 促进，加速(…的发生或发展) :

ex.en: My mother always says that a cup of tea helps things along.
ex.zh: 我母亲总是说喝杯茶效率高。

ex.en: His father’s name helped along his career in the early days.
ex.zh: 他父亲的名字早年助他拓平了事业的道路。

senses.en: to help sb to take off or put on a piece of clothing, such as a coat

ex.en: Can I help you off with your coat?
ex.zh: 我来帮你脱大衣好吧？

ex.en: She helped him on with his dressing gown.
ex.zh: 她帮他穿上了晨衣。

senses.en: to help sb in order to make things easier for them,for example by doing some of their work or by giving them money
senses.zh: (在…上)提供协助，减轻某人的负担:

ex.en: Thank you for helping out.
ex.zh: 感谢你帮我解围。

ex.en: My dad said he’d help me out with money.
ex.zh: 我父亲说他会借钱给我解急的。

senses.en: to give sb/yourself some food or drink
senses.zh: 为某人/自己取用(食物或饮料) :

ex.en: Can I help anyone to more chicken?
ex.zh: 再给哪位来点鸡肉好吗？

ex.en: Please help yourselves to salad.
ex.zh: 用色拉请自便。

senses.en: to surround sb/sth with sth so that they cannot move freely

ex.en: The thick trees hemmed them in on all sides.
ex.zh: 茂密的树木环绕着他们。

ex.en: The ship was hemmed in by the ice.
ex.zh: 船的四周都是冰。

senses.en: to move or make sb/sth move in a particular direction

ex.en: They were herded together into trucks and driven away.
ex.zh: 他们被一起赶上卡车开走了。

senses.en: to go to a place secretly because you do not want anyone to find you

ex.en: She used to hide away in her room when she got depressed.
ex.zh: 她以前心情沮丧就躲在自己房间里。

ex.en: She hid herself away until she felt better.
ex.zh: 她躲起来直到心情好些。

senses.en: a place where sb goes to be alone
to put sb/sth in a secret place so that no one else can find them/it
senses.zh: 把人(或东西) 藏起来:

ex.en: You won’t find your present — I’ve hidden it away!
ex.zh: 你找不到你的礼物的─我藏起来了！

senses.en: to go to a secret place to escape from sb who is trying to find you
senses.zh: 躲藏， 隐匿(避开某人):

ex.en: He hid out in the woods.
ex.zh: 他藏在树林里。

senses.en: a place where sb goes when they do not want to be found
) to lift or pull up a piece of clothing that you are wearing

ex.en: He hiked up his trousers and waded into the water.
ex.zh: 他提起裤子走进水中。

senses.en: to increase a price or rate suddenly and by a large amount
senses.zh: 大幅提高价格(或收费等):

ex.en: They hiked up the price by 40%.
ex.zh: 他们把价格猛增了40%。

senses.en: to suggest in an indirect way that sth is true or likely

ex.en: In his speech the Prime Minister hinted at an early election.
ex.zh: 首相在讲话中暗示会提前选举。

senses.en: to arrange for sb to work for sb else; to arrange to work for sb
senses.zh: 安排聘用某人； 受雇(于… )(为…):

ex.en: The agency hires out cleaning staff.
ex.zh: 这家服务公司安排清洁人员。

ex.en: He hires himself out to farmers at harvest time.
ex.zh: 到了收穫季节他就给农人当雇工。

senses.en: to allow sb to use sth for a short period of time in return for payment

ex.en: The club will hire out tennis rackets to guests.
ex.zh: 俱乐部让访客租用网球拍。

senses.en: to criticize or attack sb who has criticized or attacked you

ex.en: In an interview she hit back at her critics.
ex.zh: 她在访谈中反驳了批评她的人。

senses.en: to ask sb for sth, especially money

ex.en: They hit us for a commission as well.
ex.zh: 他们还向我们索取佣金呢。

ex.en: She’s always hitting me up for the cab fare home.
ex.zh: 她总是要我出打车回家的钱。

senses.en: to talk to sb in a way that shows you are sexually attracted to them

ex.en: He was hitting on my girlfriend!
ex.zh: 他居然在勾引我的女朋友！

senses.en: to attack sb violently, especially sb who is trying to hit or capture you
senses.zh: 猛烈攻击(尤指想打或抓自己的人):

ex.en: She hit out at the policeman as he tried to arrest her.
ex.zh: 她奋力击打想抓捕她的警察。

ex.en: I just hit out blindly in all directions.
ex.zh: 我只是向四方乱击一通。

senses.en: to criticize sb or sth strongly

ex.en: He hit out at the government’s decision.
ex.zh: 他严厉抨击了政府的决定。

senses.en: to separate sth from a larger group; to sell part of a company
senses.zh: 把一部份分离出来；卖掉公司的一部份:

ex.en: Some of the firm’s operations have been hived off into a separate company.
ex.zh: 公司的一些业务已分离出来，成立了一家独立公司。

senses.en: to allow sth bad that sb has done to make you like or respect them less
senses.zh: 对…记仇(或恨等)；对…抱成见:

senses.en: to hesitate, or to make sb hesitate,to act or speak

ex.en: Don’t hold back! This opportunity is too good to miss!
ex.zh: 别犹豫了！机不可失啊！

ex.en: Phil walked forward confidently but something held Ben back.
ex.zh: 菲尔信心十足地走向前去，本却踌躇不定的。

senses.en: to prevent sb/sth from moving forward or from entering or leaving a place

ex.en: The police were unable to hold back the fans.
ex.zh: 警察拦不住那些崇拜者。

senses.en: to prevent the progress or development of sb/sth
to stop yourself from expressing or showing how you feel

ex.en: They couldn’t hold back their laughter.
ex.zh: 他们忍不住大笑起来。

ex.en: He struggled to hold back his tears.
ex.zh: 他竭力没让眼泪流出来。

senses.en: to not tell sb sth that you wish to keep secret

ex.en: I think he’s holding something back; he knows more than he’s admitting.
ex.zh: 我认为他有什么事瞒着；他知道的比他坦白的要多。

senses.en: to try to spend only a little time, money, etc. on sth; to show control in what you do
senses.zh: 节省； 节制； 克制:

ex.en: My grandmother never held back on the tea and cakes when we visited.
ex.zh: 我们去拜访祖母时，她从不吝惜茶点。

ex.en: She held back on her questioning (= she did not ask too many questions).
ex.zh: 她没有提很多问题。

senses.en: to prevent sb from having their freedom or rights
senses.zh: 剥夺某人的自由(或权利)

senses.en: to use force to hold sb/sth in a particular position and stop them/it from moving

ex.en: He was held down and kicked by the two men.
ex.zh: 他被那两个男人按住并踢了几脚。

ex.en: Hold the mouse button down as you move the cursor.
ex.zh: 移动光标时压住鼠标的键。

senses.en: ) to keep sth at a low level

ex.en: The company is trying to hold down costs.
ex.zh: 公司正力图保持低成本。

ex.en: The rate of inflation must be held down.
ex.zh: 通货膨胀率必须控制在低水平上。

senses.en: , ) to limit sth,especially a noise

senses.zh: 通常用于否定句) to be able to eat food without bringing it back out of your mouth吃下…(不吐出来):

ex.en: She hasn’t been able to hold any food down since the operation.
ex.zh: 手术之后她一直是一吃东西就全吐掉。

senses.en: to speak for a long time and often in a boring or annoying way

ex.en: He was holding forth about how successful his business is.
ex.zh: 他滔滔不绝地谈他的公司如何红火。

senses.en: to keep sth inside a place so that it cannot fall out or escape

ex.en: The straps hold the baby in securely.
ex.zh: 带子把婴儿安全地系在里面。

ex.en: I had to hold my stomach in (=pull the muscles flat) to zip up my jeans.
ex.zh: 我得收腹以便拉上牛仔裤的拉锁。

senses.en: to not show or express how you feel

ex.en: I couldn’t hold in my anger any longer.
ex.zh: 我再也忍不住怒火了。

senses.en: to resist an attack by an enemy or an opponent

ex.en: How long do you think you can hold off the attack?
ex.zh: 你认为你对这一攻击能抵抗多久？

ex.en: He held off a late challenge from Davies to win the race.
ex.zh: 他战胜了戴维斯后来居上的威胁，赢了赛跑。

senses.en: to hold sth/sb tightly; to not let go of sth/sb
to keep sth/sb; to not lose sth/sb

ex.en: Hold on to the magazines for as long as you like.
ex.zh: 尽量把杂志保存长一点时间。

ex.en: The party will hold on to its majority at the next election.
ex.zh: 这个党在下次选举中将保持其多数优势。

senses.en: someone who resists an attack, an enemy or an opponent, or who refuses to accept sth
to offer a chance, hope or possibility of sth
senses.zh: 提供机会；给予希望；使有可能:

senses.en: to deliberately delay reaching an agreement in the hope that you will gain sth;to refuse to accept anything less than what you are asking for
senses.zh: (为得到利益)拖延达成协议；拒绝让步:

ex.en: Union leaders are holding out for a better deal.
ex.zh: 工会领导人拖延着，以期达成较优厚的协议。

senses.en: to refuse to tell or give sb sth

ex.en: You promised to give me the money. Stop holding out on me.
ex.zh: 你答应过给我钱的。不许赖。

senses.en: to leave sth to be dealt with later

ex.en: We decided to hold the matter over until the next meeting.
ex.zh: 我们决定把这件事推迟到下次会议。

senses.en: a person who keeps a position of power, for example sb who had a particular position in one government and who still has it in the next
senses.zh: 留任人员；(在下届政府中)留任的官员

senses.en: to make sb keep a promise

ex.en: ‘I promise I’ll take you out to dinner if we win.’ ‘I’ll hold you to that!’
ex.zh: “如果我们赢了，我答应请你出去吃饭。”“你得说话算数啊！ ”

senses.en: ) to stop your opponent in a sports competition winning more points than you
senses.zh: 压住对手；不让对方得分超过自己:

ex.en: Spain held France to a 1-1 draw.
ex.zh: 西班牙队把法国队迫成了1 :1的平局。

senses.en: to remain, or to keep sb/sth, united

ex.en: The coalition has held together for longer than expected.
ex.zh: 联盟坚持的时间超出预料。

ex.en: Strong bonds of loyalty hold the family together.
ex.zh: 绝对的忠诚把全家人连结在一起。

senses.en: to remain in one piece; to stay in good condition

ex.en: It’s a miracle that his car is still holding together.
ex.zh: 他的汽车依然完好真是个奇迹。

ex.en: His trousers were held together by safety pins.
ex.zh: 他的裤子是用安全别针别在一块的。

senses.en: to remain healthy, in good condition or working effectively, especially when there are difficulties
senses.zh: 支持住；承受住；支壠得住:

ex.en: Sales have held up well, in spite of economic difficulties.
ex.zh: 尽管遇到了经济困难，销售额还相当可观。

ex.en: How did your tent hold up in the storm?
ex.zh: 你的帐篷在风暴中是怎样支壠起来的？

senses.en: to raise sb/sth in the air

ex.en: She held up her hand to stop him.
ex.zh: 她抬起手阻挡他。

ex.en: He held up his trophy as the crowd applauded.
ex.zh: 他在众人的欢呼声中举起奖杯。

senses.en: to support sb/sth and prevent it/them from falling

ex.en: Her trousers were held up with string.
ex.zh: 她的裤子是用绳子系着的。

ex.en: The two pillars were holding the ceiling up.
ex.zh: 两根柱子承托着天花板。

senses.en: to block or delay the progress of sb/sth

ex.en: Roadworks on the motorway are holding up traffic.
ex.zh: 高速公路检修造成了交通阻塞。

ex.en: She phoned to say she’d been held up at the office.
ex.zh: 她打电话来说她在办公室脱不开身。

senses.en: to rob a person, a bank, a shop/store, etc. using a gun
senses.zh: 持枪抢劫某人(或银行、商店等):

ex.en: Have they caught the people who held up the bank?
ex.zh: 他们抓到持枪抢劫银行的人了吗？

senses.en: a delay or sth which causes a delay

ex.en: What’s the hold-up?
ex.zh: 遇到什么障碍了？

senses.en: an act of robbing a person, a bank, a shop/store, etc. using a gun
to present sb/sth as an example of sth
senses.zh: 将某人(或某事物)作为…的例子:

ex.en: My mother held up my cousin as an example of a good student.
ex.zh: 我母亲把我表哥看作好学生的代表。

senses.en: to agree with or approve of sth

ex.en: I don’t hold with these new theories on education.
ex.zh: 我不赞成这些新的桝育理论。

senses.en: to hide somewhere

ex.en: The thieves holed up in an empty warehouse.
ex.zh: 盗贼躲在一个空仓库里。

ex.en: The police couldn’t find out where the gang were holed up.
ex.zh: 警方查不到那个团伙的藏身处。

senses.en: to make a space inside sth by removing part of it

ex.en: We hollowed out the pumpkin and put a candle in it.
ex.zh: 我们把南瓜挖空，在里面插了根蜡烛。

ex.en: a hollowed-out tree trunk
ex.zh: 中空的树干

senses.en: to form sth by making a hole in something else

ex.en: The waves have hollowed out caves along the cliff.
ex.zh: 海浪拍击峭壁形成了一个个岩洞。

senses.en: to move or be aimed straight towards sb/sth

ex.en: She homed in on me as soon as she saw me.
ex.zh: 她一看见我就向我直奔过来。

senses.en: to turn all your attention to sth
senses.zh: 把(注意力) 集中于； 全神贯注:

ex.en: The lawyer homed in on the inconsistencies in her story.
ex.zh: 律师集中注意力听她的陈述中前后矛盾的地方。

senses.en: to persuade sb to do sth when they do not want to
senses.zh: 说服某人(做某事)；劝某人改变主意:

ex.en: I didn’t want to be involved but I got hooked into helping.
ex.zh: 我原本不想介入， 可有人劝我帮忙。

ex.en: He tried to hook me into going with them.
ex.zh: 他试图劝我跟他们一道去。

senses.en: ) to agree to work with sb

ex.en: We’ve hooked up with a firm in Ireland.
ex.zh: 我们答应了和爱尔兰的一家公司合作。

senses.en: , ) to meet sb and spend time with them

ex.en: On vacation we hooked up with some Texans.
ex.zh: 我们度假时交往了一些德克萨斯人。

ex.en: Let’s hook up when you get back from your trip.
ex.zh: 等你旅行回来后我们再聚。

senses.en: , ) to start a relationship with sb

ex.en: They hooked up at Kyle’s party.
ex.zh: 他们是在凯尔的聚会上结识的。

senses.en: to connect sb/sth to a piece of electronic equipment or to a power supply
senses.zh: 把…接通电子设备(或电源):

ex.en: All the speakers hook up to a single amplifier.
ex.zh: 所有喇叭都接在单一的扩音器上。

ex.en: The boat was hooked up to the shore power supply.
ex.zh: 船与岸上的电源接通了。

senses.en: a connection between two or more pieces of equipment

ex.en: an international phone hook-up
ex.zh: 国际电话联网

senses.en: to remove dust, dirt, etc.from a carpet or floor with a vacuum cleaner (=an electrical machine that cleans floors and carpets by sucking up dust and dirt)
senses.zh: 用真空吸尘器吸(尘埃等):

ex.en: () The US and Canada usually hoover up all the gold and silver medals at the Olympic Games.
ex.zh: 美国和加拿大常囊括奥运会的金银牌。

senses.en: to play in a noisy and careless way that is likely to damage sth or hurt sb

ex.en: If you two don’t stop horsing around you’ll hurt yourselves.
ex.zh: 你们俩若是继续疯下去的话会把自己弄伤的。

senses.en: to become more lively or exciting

ex.en: Things are hotting up as the election approaches.
ex.zh: 随着选举的临近，渐渐出现了一片热闹的景象。

ex.en: As the pace hotted up, he dropped back into third place.
ex.zh: 随着节奏的加快，他落到了第三名。

senses.en: to force sb to leave a place or their job
senses.zh: 逼迫某人离开某地(或离职):

ex.en: They were hounded out of the town.
ex.zh: 他们被逐出镇子。

ex.en: She was hounded from politics by her rivals.
ex.zh: 她被对手挤出了政坛。

senses.en: to move, stand or sit close to one another for warmth or protection
senses.zh: 靠拢在一起(取暖或寻求保护):

ex.en: We huddled together for warmth.
ex.zh: 我们挤在一块取暖。

senses.en: to press yourself into a small space for warmth or protection
senses.zh: 蜷缩，紧挨着…(以取暖或寻求保护):

ex.en: She huddled up against him to keep warm.
ex.zh: 她缩起身子挨着他以保持温暖。

senses.en: to have a strong desire for sth and try to get it

ex.en: She hungers after wealth and prestige.
ex.zh: 她热中名利。

senses.en: to sit on your heels with your knees bent up in front of you

ex.en: We hunkered down around the fire.
ex.zh: 我们围着炉火蹲坐。

senses.en: to search for sb until you find or catch them

ex.en: He vowed to hunt down the killer.
ex.zh: 他发誓要抓到兇手。

senses.en: to find sth after a long and difficult search
senses.zh: 搜寻到， 寻找到(某物) :

ex.en: I managed to hunt out those files you wanted.
ex.zh: 我想法找到了你要的文件。

ex.en: Can you hunt down his phone number for me?
ex.zh: 你能帮我查到他的电话号码吗？

senses.en: to search for sb/sth, especially sb/sth that is hidden or difficult to find

ex.en: We hunted up anyone who might have known him.
ex.zh: 我们找遍了所有可能认识他的人。

senses.en: to do or say sth to make sb move or work faster; to do sth to make sth happen faster

ex.en: Hurry the kids along or we’ll miss the train.
ex.zh: 让孩子们快点，否则我们就赶不上火车了。

senses.en: to continue speaking, without allowing anyone to interrupt or speak
senses.zh: 喋喋不休；囉嗦得没完没了:

ex.en: She hurried on to the next topic before I could object.
ex.zh: 我还没来得及表示反对她就继续讲下一个话题了。

ex.en: ‘Just leave that to me,’ she hurried on.
ex.zh: “把那个交给我就行了。”她匆忙说道。

senses.en: used to tell sb to move or do sth more quickly

ex.en: Hurry up, we have to leave in five minutes!
ex.zh: 快点，我们五分钟之后必须走！

ex.en: I wish the bus would hurry up and come.
ex.zh: 我希望公共汽车能快点来。

senses.en: to encourage sb to move or work faster; to do sth to make sth happen faster
senses.zh: 催促(某人) ； 加速… 的发生:

ex.en: Hurry your brother up or we’ll be late.
ex.zh: 让你弟弟快点，不然我们要迟到了。

senses.en: to hide information about a situation,especially sth bad or shocking, because you do not want people to know about it

ex.en: The government tried to hush the affair up.
ex.zh: 政府试图隐瞒此事。

senses.en: to advertise or talk about sb/sth in an exaggerated way in order to get a lot of public attention for it
senses.zh: 夸张地宣传(某人或某事物) :

ex.en: His latest movie is being hyped up by the media.
ex.zh: 他新近的电影正被媒体大肆炒作。

senses.en: (of a person
senses.zh: 人)very excited or worried about sth十分兴奋的；很激动的；十分担忧的:

ex.en: She gets very hyped up before a race.
ex.zh: 她一到赛跑前就来了精神。

senses.en: (of a film/movie, a book, an event, etc.
senses.zh: 电影、书、活动等) advertised or talked about in an exaggerated way to get public attention被大肆宣扬(或宣传)的:

ex.en: a hyped-up movie
ex.zh: 被大肆炒作的电影

senses.en: to become covered by a layer of ice

ex.en: The road had iced over during the night.
ex.zh: 夜间公路上结了冰。

ex.en: The windscreen had iced up.
ex.zh: 挡风玻璃上结了一层冰。

senses.en: to feel that you can understand and share the feelings of sb else

ex.en: He’s a character that readers feel they can identify with.
ex.zh: 他是一个读者能与之产生共鸣的人物。

senses.en: to consider sth to be the same as sth else

ex.en: Beauty is often identified with youth.
ex.zh: 人们常常认为美丽就等于青春。

senses.en: to support sb/sth; to be closely connected with sb/sth

ex.en: He refused to identify himself with the new political party.
ex.zh: 他拒绝支持那个新政党。

senses.en: to spend time doing nothing very important

ex.en: They idled away their time watching television.
ex.zh: 他们看电视消磨时光。

senses.en: to fill sb/sth with a strong feeling, quality, etc.
senses.zh: 使充满，灌输，激发(强烈感情或品质等):

ex.en: He managed to imbue his employees with team spirit.
ex.zh: 他成功激发起雇员的团队精神。

ex.en: The painting is imbued with energy and life.
ex.zh: 那幅画充满活力和生命。

senses.en: to become, or to make sb become, completely involved in sth
senses.zh: (使) 醉心于… ， 沉浸在… 中， 投入:

ex.en: He immersed himself in his studies.
ex.zh: 他埋首研究。

ex.en: I was completely immersed in the story.
ex.zh: 我完全沉醉在故事中。

senses.en: to have an effect on sb/sth

ex.en: Government cuts will impact directly on education.
ex.zh: 政府削减资源将直接影响桝育。

ex.en: This decision may impact on the unemployed.
ex.zh: 这个决定可能影响到失业者。

senses.en: to have a strong effect on sb/sth,especially a bad one

ex.en: She didn’t allow her personal problems to impinge on her work.
ex.zh: 她没有让个人问题妨碍自己工作。

senses.en: to expect sb to do sth for you or spend time with you when they do not have much time, or when it may not be convenient for them

ex.en: Tim never says ‘No’, so people are always imposing on him.
ex.zh: 蒂姆从不说“不”，所以别人总是欺负他。

senses.en: to emphasize to sb how important or serious sth is
senses.zh: 向某人强调…重要(或严重):

ex.en: I wanted to impress on him that it was a very serious offence.
ex.zh: 我想让他认识到那是十分严重的罪行。

ex.en: She impressed on her staff the importance of keeping accurate records.
ex.zh: 她向员工强调准确记录的重要性。

senses.en: to have a great effect on sth so that it cannot be forgotten, changed, etc.
senses.zh: 把…印记在心中(或脑海中等)；在…上留下…的印记:

ex.en: The scene was imprinted on my mind.
ex.zh: 那个场面铭刻在我的心中。

ex.en: The picture is imprinted with his own style.
ex.zh: 这幅画深受他个人风格的影响。

senses.en: to print or press a mark or design on sth
senses.zh: 把…印在…上；在…上印上…；压印:

ex.en: T-shirts imprinted with the logos of sports teams
ex.zh: 印着运动队标志的T恤衫

senses.en: to achieve or produce sth of a better standard or quality than sth else
senses.zh: 改进； 做出比…更好的成绩:

ex.en: There are a few points in your work that you could improve on.
ex.zh: 你的工作中有几点可以改进。

ex.en: The Kenyan girl improved on her previous best performance (= in a race).
ex.zh: 那位肯尼亚姑娘超越了自己以往的最佳成绩。

senses.en: to say, often unfairly, that sb/sth is responsible for sth, or has a particular quality
senses.zh: (常指不公正地)把…责任归于…，认…具有…素质:

ex.en: Why do you impute selfish motives to her?
ex.zh: 你为什么说她的动机是自私的？

senses.en: to tend to think or behave in a particular way; to make sb do this

ex.en: I incline to the view that we should take no action.
ex.zh: 我倾向于认为我们不应采取行动。

ex.en: Her love of languages inclined her towards a career as a translator.
ex.zh: 她对语言的热爱使她倾向于从事翻译工作。

senses.en: to allow yourself to have or do sth that you like, often sth that is bad for you

ex.en: She indulged in the luxury of a long bath.
ex.zh: 她在澡盆里泡了半天，尽情享受了一番。

ex.en: He now has time to indulge in his favourite hobby:photography.
ex.zh: 他现在有时间尽情投入他的爱好— 摄影。

senses.en: to take part in an activity, especially sth bad or illegal
senses.zh: 参加，参与(尤指坏事或违法活动) :

ex.en: We shouldn’t indulge in speculation as to what really happened.
ex.zh: 我们不应该对实际发生的事胡乱猜测。

senses.en: to give evidence about sb or make an accusation against sb, to the police or sb in authority

ex.en: One of the gang informed on the rest.
ex.zh: 这团伙中有人告发其他成员。

senses.en: to limit sb’s freedom, rights, etc.
senses.zh: 侵犯，侵害(某人的自由、权益等):

ex.en: The media is accused of infringing on people’s privacy.
ex.zh: 人们指责媒体侵犯了大家的隐私。

senses.en: to fill sb/sth with a particular quality
senses.zh: 把(某种素质)注入…；在…中注入(某种素质):

ex.en: His arrival infused new life and energy into the team.
ex.zh: 他的到来为这支队伍注入了新的生命力和活力。

ex.en: Her work is infused with anger.
ex.zh: 她的作品充满了激愤。

senses.en: to write or draw in ink over sth that has been written or drawn in pencil
senses.zh: 给(铅笔画或底线等)上墨；用墨水加描:

ex.en: I did the answers in pencil first and then inked them in.
ex.zh: 我先用铅笔作答，然后用墨水描出来。

ex.en: () The company has inked in June 1st (= made it definite) for the launch.
ex.zh: 公司已决定于六月一日投产。

senses.en: to get yourself into a position of advantage,especially by clever talk or by gaining the favour or respect of sb important

ex.en: She cleverly insinuated herself into his family.
ex.zh: 她巧妙地混进了他的家庭。

senses.en: to demand sth and refuse to be persuaded to accept anything else

ex.en: They are insisting on a meeting tomorrow.
ex.zh: 他们坚持要在明天开会。

ex.en: I always insist on skimmed milk.
ex.zh: 我始终坚持喝脱脂牛奶。

senses.en: to continue doing sth even though other people find it annoying

ex.en: She will insist on shouting at the top of her voice.
ex.zh: 她会执意一直扯着嗓门喊的。

senses.en: to buy an insurance policy which will pay you money if the event mentioned happens
senses.zh: 投… 保险； 参加… 保险:

ex.en: Everyone needs to insure against fire.
ex.zh: 每个人都需要保火险。

senses.en: to take action to prevent sth unpleasant happening
senses.zh: 采取预防措施；防止…发生:

ex.en: This is to insure against a repetition of previous disasters.
ex.zh: 这是为防止先前的灾难重演而采取的措施。

senses.en: to persuade sb to buy, do or eat sth

ex.en: Could I interest you in this model (= of car), Sir?
ex.zh: 先生，您有兴趣瞧瞧这个车型吗？

senses.en: to touch a child in a sexual way
to make sb/sth get used to sth unpleasant so that they are no longer strongly affected by it
senses.zh: 使习惯于(令人不快的事物):

ex.en: The prisoners quickly became inured to the harsh conditions.
ex.zh: 囚犯们很快就适应了苛刻的条件。

senses.en: to make sb leave a job, especially in the armed forces, because they are ill/sick or injured
senses.zh: 使伤病员退役；使受伤(或生病)的人下岗:

ex.en: He was invalided out of the army because of his injuries.
ex.zh: 他因伤被迫退役。

senses.en: to buy sth or spend money on sth useful, especially sth expensive
senses.zh: 购买有用的东西(尤指昂贵的):

ex.en: It’s time we invested in a new sofa — this one is falling to bits.
ex.zh: 我们该花钱买新沙发了—这套快散架了。

senses.en: to make sb/sth seem to have a particular quality
senses.zh: 使某人/事物似乎具备某性质:

ex.en: Being the boss invests her with a certain glamour.
ex.zh: 当老板似乎给她增添了一定的魅力。

senses.en: to ask sb if they would like to go with you to an event or activity
senses.zh: 邀请某人一道去；请某人同行:

ex.en: Shall I invite Dave along (to the concert)?
ex.zh: 我要不要请戴夫一同前往(音乐会)？

senses.en: to ask sb to go back to your home after you have been out somewhere together

ex.en: She invited me back to her flat for coffee after the movie.
ex.zh: 看完电影后，她邀请我上她住处喝了杯咖啡。

senses.en: to politely ask sb to enter a room, your house, etc.
senses.zh: 邀请某人进房间(或到家里等):

ex.en: Aren’t you going to invite me in for a coffee?
ex.zh: 你不请我进里面喝杯咖啡吗？

senses.en: to ask sb to go out with you, especially as a way of beginning a romantic relationship
senses.zh: 请某人外出约会(尤指为建立恋爱关系):

ex.en: We’ve been invited out for dinner this evening.
ex.zh: 今晚我们应邀出去吃饭。

ex.en: He eventually found the courage to invite Julia out.
ex.zh: 他终于鼓起勇气约朱莉娅外出。

senses.en: to ask sb to come and visit you in your home

ex.en: I’ve invited a few friends round to watch the game with us on TV.
ex.zh: 我请了几个朋友来家里一起看这场电视转播的比赛。

ex.en: We ought to invite the new neighbours over for coffee.
ex.zh: 我们应该邀请新邻居来家里喝咖啡。

senses.en: to make sb experience or do sth, especially sth unpleasant
senses.zh: 让某人经历，让某人做(尤指令人不快的事):

ex.en: The new exams have involved teachers in a lot of extra paperwork.
ex.zh: 新考试让老师们添了一大堆额外的文案工作。

senses.en: to come, go or flow out of sth or somewhere

ex.en: I could see smoke issuing from the window.
ex.zh: 我看得见烟从窗户里冒出来。

senses.en: to want sth very much

ex.en: They were just itching for a fight.
ex.zh: 他们摩拳擦掌就想打架。

senses.en: to push a sharp or pointed object quickly or roughly into sb/sth or in the direction of sb/sth

ex.en: He kept jabbing at the paper cup with his pencil.
ex.zh: 他不断地用铅笔扎着纸杯。

ex.en: She jabbed at the papers with her finger.
ex.zh: 她用手指戳了戳文件。

senses.en: to speak or talk quickly in an excited way

ex.en: She jabbered away, trying to distract his attention.
ex.zh: 她喋喋不休，想分散他的注意力。

ex.en: He was jabbering away in Russian.
ex.zh: 他叽里咕噜地说着俄语。

senses.en: to stop doing sth,especially your job

ex.en: She decided to jack in her job.
ex.zh: 她决定辞职。

senses.en: to make sth more lively or interesting

ex.en: Jazz up that plain dress with some jewellery.
ex.zh: 佩带首饰使那件朴素的连衣裙亮丽起来。

senses.en: to make a piece of music sound more modern, or more like jazz or popular music
senses.zh: 使乐曲现代化(或更具爵士乐或流行音乐风格):

ex.en: jazzed up Bach
ex.zh: 翻新的巴赫作品

senses.en: to treat sb badly and cause them problems, especially by deceiving them
senses.zh: (尤指通过欺骗手段)为难某人:

ex.en: He won’t give us an answer — he keeps jerking us around.
ex.zh: 他不会给我们答覆的—他一直在为难我们。

senses.en: to fly somewhere, especially somewhere far away

ex.en: They’re jetting off to Florida tomorrow.
ex.zh: 他们明天要飞往佛罗里达州。

senses.en: to agree with sth; to be the same as sth or match sth

ex.en: Her story didn’t jibe with the witnesses’ account.
ex.zh: 她的说法和证人的描述有出入。

senses.en: to try very hard to gain an advantage,a favour, etc. for yourself and stop other people getting it

ex.en: Several employees are jockeying for the manager’s position.
ex.zh: 若干雇员正在角逐主管职位。

senses.en: to continue in a steady way, with little or no excitement or progress

ex.en: For years the business just kept jogging along.
ex.zh: 多少年来生意不温也不火。

senses.en: to become involved in sth; to take part in an activity with other people

ex.en: Can I join in (the game)?
ex.zh: 我可以参加(比赛)吗？

ex.en: We all joined in with the singing.
ex.zh: 我们都齐声歌唱。

senses.en: to become a member of the armed forces

ex.en: We both joined up in 1939.
ex.zh: 我俩都是1939年入伍的。

senses.en: to be connected to sth; to connect sth to sth

ex.en: The dots join up to form a solid line.
ex.zh: 小点连接起来形成实线。

ex.en: Join up the dots to see the picture.
ex.zh: 把这些点连接起来就能看出图形了。

senses.en: to do or say sth with sb else or with a group of people

ex.en: I’m sure you’ll join with me in congratulating Isla and Jake.
ex.zh: 我相信你会和我一道祝贺伊斯拉和杰克的。

ex.en: Parents joined with teachers to protest against the closure of the school.
ex.zh: 家长和老师联合起来抗议关闭学校。

senses.en: to keep encouraging sb in a friendly way

ex.en: She tried to jolly him along but he couldn’t forget his problems.
ex.zh: 她一直鼓励他，但他忘不掉自己的问题。

senses.en: to make sb/sth brighter or more cheerful

ex.en: Do you think you can jolly Anthony up a bit?
ex.zh: 你觉得你能让安东尼打起精神吗？

senses.en: to compete strongly and forcefully with other people for sth

ex.en: People in the crowd were jostling for the best positions.
ex.zh: 这群人在竞相抢占最好的位置。

senses.en: to write sth down quickly
senses.zh: 草草记下； 匆匆记下:

ex.en: I’ll jot down their address before I forget it.
ex.zh: 我得赶快把他们的地址写下来，免得忘了。

senses.en: to make sth more lively, exciting or interesting
senses.zh: 增加…的生气(或意思、趣味):

ex.en: Juice up your presentations with colourful graphics.
ex.zh: 用颜色鲜艳的图表使你的演示更活泼。

senses.en: to put petrol in a vehicle

ex.en: We need to juice up the car before we leave.
ex.zh: 我们出发之前要给汽车加加油。

senses.en: to mix things up in a confused way

ex.en: Make sure you don’t jumble everything up.
ex.zh: 一定不要把东西全都弄乱了。

ex.en: The details of the accident were all jumbled together in his mind.
ex.zh: 他把事故细节记得颠三倒四。

senses.en: to accept an opportunity, a chance,etc. with enthusiasm
senses.zh: 迫不及待地接受机会(等):

ex.en: I jumped at the chance of a trip to Italy.
ex.zh: 我急不可待地抓住机会去意大利旅行。

senses.en: to criticize sb sharply
senses.zh: 厉声责备某人；厉声责骂某人:

ex.en: She jumped on me before I had a chance to explain.
ex.zh: 我没来得及解释她便对我破口大骂。

senses.en: to be very easy to see; to be noticeable
senses.zh: 极易引起某人的注意； 显眼:

ex.en: The headline jumped out at me.
ex.zh: 大字标题十分醒目，让我一眼就看到。

ex.en: The mistakes are so obvious they jump out at you.
ex.zh: 错误十分明显，一眼就能看到。

senses.en: to stand quickly and suddenly when you have been sitting

ex.en: He jumped up off the floor.
ex.zh: 他一下子从地板上站起来。

senses.en: [only before noun] (, ,) thinking that you are more important than you really are, particularly when you have risen in social status but do not deserve to
senses.zh: (尤指不具备资格而社会地位提高时)妄自尊大的，自视甚高的:

ex.en: I won’t take orders from a jumped-up office girl!
ex.zh: 我不会听个妄自尊大的办公室女勤习员发号施令的﹗

senses.en: to stand out from sth; to stick out further than the surrounding surface

ex.en: The tops of the flooded houses jutted out of the water.
ex.zh: 一个个遭水淹的房顶突出水面。

senses.en: ) to fall over

ex.en: I’m so tired, all I want to do is keel over and sleep for a week.
ex.zh: 我太累了，我所想做的就是倒头睡上一个星期。

senses.en: to askor tell sb repeatedly to do sth
senses.zh: 一再要求某人，反复提醒某人(…):

ex.en: She keeps after me to fix the TV.
ex.zh: 她总是唠叨着让我修电视。

senses.en: to continueto be more advanced or successful thanother people, groups, etc.

ex.en: We need to keep ahead of our competitors.
ex.zh: 我们得继续领先于我们的对手。

ex.en: If you want to keep ahead in this industry, you have to be ruthless.
ex.zh: 你若想在这个行业一直出人头地就不能手软。

senses.en: to continue towork hard at sth, or to make sb work hard at sth,particularly sth which is difficult or takes a longtime
to not go near sb/sth

ex.en: Keep away fromme!
ex.zh: 离我远点！

ex.en: The police told us to keep well away from the area.
ex.zh: 警察让我们远离那个地区。

senses.en: to preventsb/sth from going near sb/sth

ex.en: Keep him away from the kitchen while we make his birthday cake.
ex.zh: 我们给他做生日蛋糕时不要让他进厨房。

ex.en: We turned off the lights to keep the mosquitoes away.
ex.zh: 我们关掉了电灯，以免招蚊子。

senses.en: to remain at a distancefrom sb/sth

ex.en: Keep back or I’ll shoot!
ex.zh: 不许过来，否则我就开枪！

ex.en: I kept well back from the road.
ex.zh: 我远离公路。

senses.en: to make sb/sthremain at a distance from sb/sth; to prevent sbfrom moving forwards
senses.zh: 使…(与…)保持距离；避免某人走近(… ) :

ex.en: Keep the children back from the fire.
ex.zh: 别让孩子们靠近火炉。

ex.en: The police were trying to keep back the crowds.
ex.zh: 当时警察正设法阻挡人群靠近。

senses.en: ) to keep a partof sth to use later

ex.en: Have you kept some money back to pay the bills?
ex.zh: 你留出支付账单的钱了吗？

ex.en: Keep a piece of cake back for Alex.
ex.zh: 给亚历克斯留块蛋糕。

senses.en: =KEEP SB IN 1
to prevent yourself from doing sth

ex.en: She bit her lip to keep from laughing.
ex.zh: 她咬着嘴唇以免笑出来。

senses.en: to prevent sb from doing sth

ex.en: Don’t let me keep you from your work.
ex.zh: 别让我妨碍你工作。

ex.en: I’ve been trying to keep him from finding out the truth.
ex.zh: 我一直设法不让他找出真相。

senses.en: to avoid telling sb sth
senses.zh: 不将某事告诉某人；瞒着某人:

ex.en: I think he’s keeping secrets from me.
ex.zh: 我想他有秘密不告诉我。

ex.en: Are you keeping something from us?
ex.zh: 你有什么事瞒着我们吗？

senses.en: to stay near the edge of the road or path while you are driving, walking, etc.

ex.en: If you keep in, the van can overtake.
ex.zh: 你往路边靠一下，客货车就能开过去。

senses.en: to give or allow sb/yourself a regular supply of sth
senses.zh: 让某人/自己常有… 的供应:

ex.en: This part-time job keeps me in cigarettes.
ex.zh: 这份兼职工作够我买烟抽了。

senses.en: to continue to be friendly with sb, especially in order to gain some advantage for yourself
senses.zh: 与某人保持友好关系；继续讨好某人:

ex.en: He keeps in with anyone who might be useful to him.
ex.zh: 只要可能对他有用的人他就一直巴结着。

senses.en: to not go onto a particular area

ex.en: Keep off ()!
ex.zh: 勿践踏(草坪)！

ex.en: We kept off the main roads to avoid the traffic.
ex.zh: 我们没有上干线公路，以避开车流。

senses.en: to not eat,drink or smoke sth; to not let sb eat, drink or smoke sth
senses.zh: (使)戒忌食物(或饮料等)；(使)避免吸食…:

ex.en: The doctor’ told me to keep off red meat.
ex.zh: 医生建议我不要吃牛羊肉。

senses.en: to not mention a particular topic; to stop sb talking about a particular topic
senses.zh: 迴避某话题；不让某人谈论某话题:

ex.en: It’s best to keep off the subject of politics with my father.
ex.zh: 最好不要和我父亲谈论政治话题。

ex.en: Keep her off the subject of teenage girls!
ex.zh: 不要让她谈青少年女子这话题！

senses.en: to stop sb/sth from coming near or going into (a place); to stop sb/sth from touching or harming sb/sth
senses.zh: 使…不靠近(或进入某处)；避免…接触(或伤害)…:

ex.en: He covered the sandwiches to keep the flies off.
ex.zh: 他盖上了三明治以免苍蝇贴近。

ex.en: Keep your animals off my land!
ex.zh: 别让你的牲口进我的地！

senses.en: to continue to follow a particular route

ex.en: Keep on until you come to the road.
ex.zh: 一直往前走到公路。

ex.en: Keep on the path until you see a gate.
ex.zh: 沿小路往前走，直到看见一道大门。

senses.en: to continue to employ sb, even though circumstances have changed

ex.en: We can only afford to keep a few workers on.
ex.zh: 我们只能续聘少数几个工友。

senses.en: to stop sth coming or falling off
senses.zh: 避免某物掉落；使固定住:

ex.en: How do you keep that bandage on?
ex.zh: 你怎么缠牢绷带？

senses.en: to continue to rent or be the owner of a house,flat/apartment,etc.
senses.zh: 继续租用，保留(房子、套房等):

ex.en: Can you afford to keep this place on while you’re abroad?
ex.zh: 你出国期间有能力继续租用这个地方吗？

senses.en: used to tell sb not to become angry
to not enter a place; to remain outside

ex.en: There was a sign saying ‘Keep out!’
ex.zh: 告示牌上写着“禁止入内！”

ex.en: Please keep out of the office while I’m working.
ex.zh: 我工作时请不要进办公室。

senses.en: to avoid sth; to prevent sb/yourself from being affected by sth
senses.zh: 避免某事；(使)免受…的影响:

ex.en: The doctor has advised me to keep out of the sun.
ex.zh: 医生建议我不要晒太阳。

ex.en: They always kept their daughter out of the spotlight (= away from the public).
ex.zh: 他们总是不让女儿抛头露面。

senses.en: to avoid becoming involved in sth; to stop sb from becoming involved in sth
senses.zh: 避免(让…)卷入/参与…；使置身于…之外:

ex.en: Keep out of this! It’s got nothing to do with you!
ex.zh: 别参与这事！这不关你的事！

ex.en: Try to keep the kids out of mischief while I’m out.
ex.zh: 我外出时别让孩子们胡闹。

senses.en: to not put sth away that you have taken out of a cupboard, etc.; to keep sth ready to use
senses.zh: 不收走(从橱柜等拿出的东西)；把…预备好:

ex.en: Keep the butter out for your dad’s breakfast.
ex.zh: 把黄油留下让你爸爸吃早餐用。

senses.en: to prevent sb/sth from entering a place
senses.zh: 使…不进入(…)；防止…进入(…)；把…关在(…)外面:

ex.en: We hung a curtain at the door to keep out the cold.
ex.zh: 我们在门上挂了条门帘以防冷气进来。

ex.en: ( ) She tried to keep the anger out of her voice.
ex.zh: 她尽量使自己的声音不流露出怒气。

senses.en: to not leave a path, a road, etc.
senses.zh: 不偏离， 不离开(道路等) :

ex.en: Keep to the footpath.
ex.zh: 顺着道儿走。

ex.en: Keep to the left (= on a road, etc.).
ex.zh: 靠左边走。

senses.en: to avoid meeting people socially or becoming involved in other people’s affairs
senses.zh: 离群索居；不与人往来；不管别人的事:

ex.en: He keeps (himself) to himself and nobody knows very much about him.
ex.zh: 他很少和人交往，所以谁对他都不太了解。

senses.en: to use only one thing or a limited number or amount of sth; to make sure that the number or amount of sth doesn’t become any bigger than a particular size
senses.zh: 仅使用一种(或有限的)…；把数量控制在…内:

ex.en: We’ve decided to keep to pale colours for the bedroom.
ex.zh: 我们决定…室里只用淡颜色。

ex.en: I’m trying to keep the number of guests to a minimum.
ex.zh: 我正设法把来宾人数控制在最少。

senses.en: to not tell anyone about sth or what you think about sth
senses.zh: 对…秘而不宣(或保守秘密)；不将…说出去:

ex.en: I know who’s won, but I’m keeping it to myself.
ex.zh: 我知道谁赢了，但我不会说出去的。

ex.en: Keep your opinions to yourself in future!
ex.zh: 今后不要把你们的意见说出去！

senses.en: to remain together in a group; to make sb/sth do this

ex.en: Keep together, kids, when we cross the road.
ex.zh: 孩子们， 咱们过马路时一起走。

ex.en: Use a paper clip to keep your papers together.
ex.zh: 用纸夹把你的文件夹在一块儿。

senses.en: to control sb

ex.en: The local people are kept under by the army.
ex.zh: 当地居民受军队管制。

senses.en: to work at the necessary speed so that you progress at the same speed as other people
senses.zh: (与其他人)进度相同；跟上进度:

ex.en: She’s having trouble keeping up with the rest of the class.
ex.zh: 她很难跟得上同班同学。

ex.en: Do keep up! I can’t keep repeating everything.
ex.zh: 跟紧些！我不能每句话都重复。

senses.en: the cost or process of keeping a building, piece of land, etc. in good condition

ex.en: Who is responsible for the day-to-day upkeep of the house?
ex.zh: 谁来负责房子的日常养护费？

senses.en: the cost or process of giving a child or an animal the things that they need
to continue to be in contact with sb by writing, phoning or seeing them regularly

ex.en: How many of your old school friends do you manage to keepup with?
ex.zh: 你还和多少老同学保持联系？

senses.en: to put information into a computer, using a keyboard
senses.zh: 键入，输入(信息)；把信息输入(或键入)计算机:

ex.en: Key in your personal number.
ex.zh: 输入你的个人号码。

ex.en: All the information has been keyed into the computer.
ex.zh: 所有信息均已输入电脑。

senses.en: to use a computer or information stored on a computer
senses.zh: 调用计算机(或计算机内存信息):

ex.en: A hacker keyed into a vital database at the newspaper’s office.
ex.zh: 一名黑客窃入了这家报馆的重要数据库。

senses.en: to make sth suitable for sth/sb; to make sth consistent with sth else or to link sth with sth else
senses.zh: 使某事物适合…；使某事物与…一致(或衔接):

ex.en: The farm was keyed to the needs of the local people.
ex.zh: 农场是根据当地人的需要而经营的。

ex.en: The timing of the concerts was keyed to the World Cup soccer games.
ex.zh: 这些音乐会是配合世界杯足球赛来安排时间的。

senses.en: to be present or lying somewhere not being used

ex.en: His letter is kicking about somewhere.
ex.zh: 他的信不知放到哪儿了。

ex.en: The idea has been kicking around for years.
ex.zh: 这个想法多年没提起过了。

senses.en: (of a person
senses.zh: 人) to be somewhere, or to go from one place to another,with no particular purpose(无目的地)四处游荡，闲逛，到处走:

ex.en: I decided to kick around the States for a couple of months.
ex.zh: 我决定在美国各地转悠几个月。

senses.en: to treat sb in a harsh or unfair way
senses.zh: 苛刻(或不公正地)对待某人:

ex.en: Don’t let the boss kick you around.
ex.zh: 别让老板欺负你。

senses.en: to protest about sth or resist sth

ex.en: It’s no use kicking against the system.
ex.zh: 反对这个制度也没有用。

senses.en: to relax

ex.en: I spent the evening kicking back in the hotel’s piano bar.
ex.zh: 我晚上在旅馆的钢琴酒吧轻松了一番。

senses.en: money that is paid to sb in order to get an advantage for yourself
to break sth and make it fall inwards by kicking it

ex.en: If you don’t open up, we’ll kick the door down.
ex.zh: 你若不开门，我们就踹开。

senses.en: [C] [U] the start of a football game

ex.en: It’s an afternoon kickoff.
ex.zh: 足球赛下午开始。

senses.en: to break the connection between sb’s computer and the Internet, so that they can no longer use the Internet
senses.zh: 断开某人的(互联网)连接:

senses.en: to remove sth by kicking

ex.en: She kicked off her shoes and lay down on the bed.
ex.zh: 她把鞋踢掉就躺倒在床上。

senses.en: to kick your foot into the air to try to hit sb, especially because you are angry or upset

ex.en: She kicked out wildly at him as he tried to grab her.
ex.zh: 他想抓住她时，她发疯一般地踢他。

senses.en: to react violently to sb/sth that makes you angry or upset

ex.en: She kicked out against traditional ideas about painting portraits.
ex.zh: 她对画肖像的传统思想强烈质疑。

senses.en: to make sb leave; to send sb away by force

ex.en: His parents kicked him out (= made him leave home) when he was seventeen.
ex.zh: 他十七岁时父母就把他逐出家门。

ex.en: They were kicked out of the nightclub for fighting.
ex.zh: 他们因为斗殴而被逐出夜总会。

senses.en: to make sth fall on its side by kicking it

ex.en: She almost kicked the bucket over.
ex.zh: 她差点把水桶踢翻了。

senses.en: to make dust, sand, etc. rise into the air

ex.en: The horse kicked up a cloud of dust.
ex.zh: 马蹄扬起一片尘土。

senses.en: to behave in a silly way; to joke

ex.en: A lot of what I said was just kidding around, but people took me seriously.
ex.zh: 我说的很多话不过是在开玩笑，可大家都太认真。

senses.en: to make a lot of plants, animals,etc. die
senses.zh: 大量杀死，大量消灭(动植物等):

ex.en: Antibiotics should kill off the bacteria.
ex.zh: 抗生素应能杀死这种细菌。

ex.en: The plant life was killed off by air pollution.
ex.zh: 空气污染导致植物大面积死亡。

senses.en: to get rid of sb/sth; to stop sth

ex.en: The hero is killed off in the last chapter.
ex.zh: 主人公在最后一章被杀死。

ex.en: It is difficult to kill off old traditions or myths.
ex.zh: 很难废除旧传统或神话。

senses.en: to sleep in a place that is not your own bed
senses.zh: 在某处过夜；在(自己的床以外的地方)睡觉:

ex.en: Is there anywhere to kip down for the night?
ex.zh: 夜里有没有什么地方睡觉？

senses.en: to stop sb feeling sad or angry by kissing them

ex.en: Let mummy kiss away your tears.
ex.zh: 让妈妈吻掉你的眼泪吧。

senses.en: to supply sb/sth with the clothes or equipment that they need for a particular purpose
senses.zh: 为…整理行装(或配置设备):

ex.en: The kids are all kitted out for the new school year.
ex.zh: 孩子们都为新学年整理行装。

ex.en: The studio is kitted out with modern sound equipment.
ex.zh: 演播室配备了现代音响设备。

senses.en: to get into a position where one or both knees are resting on the ground

ex.en: He knelt down beside the chair.
ex.zh: 他跪倒在椅子旁。

ex.en: She was kneeling down, looking for something on the floor.
ex.zh: 她跪在地板上找东西。

senses.en: used to say that sb/sthis in a particular place, but is not doing anythingor being used
senses.zh: (某人)在某处闲散；(某物)闲置在某个地方:

ex.en: These chocolates have been knocking around since New Year.
ex.zh: 这些巧克力从新年起就丢在这儿。

ex.en: His book was knocking around the lounge for ages.
ex.zh: 他的书在起居室闲置了几辈子了。

senses.en: to travel and live in various places

ex.en: He spent a few years knocking about Europe.
ex.zh: 他花了几年时间漫游欧洲。

ex.en: Jeff will know what to do — he’s knocked about a bit(= has travelled and had a lot of experience ofdifferent situations).
ex.zh: 杰夫会有办法的─他见多识广。

senses.en: to hit sb again and again

ex.en: Her husband knocks her about.
ex.zh: 她的丈夫虐待她。

senses.en: a period of time spent kicking a ball around with other people

ex.en: We had a knockabout in the park.
ex.zh: 我们在公园里踢了会儿球。

senses.en: to spend a lot of time with sb
senses.zh: (和…)长时间待在一起， 泡在一块儿:

ex.en: She knocks around with Sahan.
ex.zh: 她成天和萨汉在一起。

ex.en: She and Sahan knock around together.
ex.zh: 她和萨汉成天在一起。

senses.en: to prevent sb from achieving sth or making progress, especially by rejecting them or sth that they suggest or ask
senses.zh: 拒绝某人；打击某人的积极性:

ex.en: He had been knocked back twice by the selection committee.
ex.zh: 他曾两度被选举委员会拒绝。

senses.en: to surprise or shock sb

ex.en: The news really knocked me back.
ex.zh: 这消息着实让我大吃一惊。

senses.en: an occasion when sb rejects you or sth that you suggest or ask; a refusal

ex.en: I don’t think I could stand another knock-back.
ex.zh: 我相信要是再遭打击我真的吃不消了。

senses.en: an occasion in boxing when one competitor hits the other so hard that they fall to the ground
to persuade sb to accept a lower price for sth; to make the price of sth lower

ex.en: He knocked Simon down to ￡5.
ex.zh: 他让西蒙把价格降到了5英镑。

ex.en: We knocked the price down to ￡10.
ex.zh: 我们把价格杀到了10 英镑。

senses.en: a much lower price than usual

ex.en: I got these books at a knockdown price.
ex.zh: 我以低价买到这些书。

senses.en: to make sth enter sth by hitting it, for example with a hammer

ex.en: She knocked some nails into the wall.
ex.zh: 她把一些钉子钉在墙上。

senses.en: to make sth go into sth by hitting or kicking it

ex.en: Barnes knocked in two goals.
ex.zh: 巴恩斯踢进了两球。

ex.en: She knocked the ball into the net.
ex.zh: 她击球入网。

senses.en: to make sth such as a hole in sth by hitting

ex.en: They knocked a hole in the wall for the window.
ex.zh: 他们在墙上凿了个洞开窗户。

senses.en: to stop doing sth, especially work
senses.zh: 停止某事；中断某事； (尤指) 下班， 收工:

ex.en: What time do you knock off () today?
ex.zh: 你今天什么时候下班？

senses.en: used to tell sb to stop doing sth annoying

ex.en: Knock it off! I’m trying to concentrate!
ex.zh: 别吵了！ 我要集中注意力！

senses.en: to murder sb
senses.zh: 杀死(或干掉、除掉、结果)某人:

ex.en: He was knocked off by another gang.
ex.zh: 他被另一个团伙干掉了。

senses.en: a copy, often illegal, of a popular product sold at a cheaper price
to remove sth,and usually make it fall to the ground, by hitting it
senses.zh: (从… ) 打落… ， 敲掉… ， 碰掉… :

ex.en: Who knocked that glass off the table?
ex.zh: 谁把桌子上的玻璃杯碰掉了？

ex.en: She knocked my glasses off.
ex.zh: 她把我的眼镜打落了。

senses.en: used to show that you are very angry with sb, by threatening to hit them
to impress or surprise sb very much
senses.zh: 给某人留下深刻印象；使某人感到惊奇

senses.en: (in boxing
senses.zh: 拳击) to hit an opponent so hard that they fall to the ground and cannot get up within a limited time, so losing the fight击败对手

senses.en: () to surprise sb very much; to have a strong emotional effect on sb
senses.zh: 使某人大吃一惊；给某人留下深刻印象:

ex.en: The movie was fantastic. It knocked me out.
ex.zh: 这电影棒极了，着实令我赞叹不已。

senses.en: a person,a piece of clothing, a performance, etc. that is extremely attractive or impressive
senses.zh: 引人注目(或给人留下深刻印象)的人(或衣服、演出等):

ex.en: Her daughter’s an absolute knockout.
ex.zh: 她的女儿简直令人倾倒。

senses.en: (in boxing
senses.zh: 拳击) a blow that is so hard that your opponent falls to the ground and cannot get up within a limited time,so losing the fight击倒对手的一击；击倒对手获胜

senses.en: [pl.] () medicine in liquid form that makes you sleep or feel sleepy
to defeat a person or a team so that they cannot continue in the competition
senses.zh: 把某人(或队伍)淘汰出(比赛):

ex.en: France knocked Belgium out of the European Cup.
ex.zh: 法国队把比利时队淘汰出欧洲杯赛。

senses.en: 1=KNOCK STH OFF 1 ()

ex.en: Can you knock out a quick report for me?
ex.zh: 你能不能给我赶写一份报告？

senses.en: to remove sth with a hard blow

ex.en: She knocked out her front teeth in the fall.
ex.zh: 她摔了一跤，把门牙碰掉了。

senses.en: to make sb lose their breath, because of a fall, a blow, etc.
senses.zh: (由于摔倒、打击等)使喘不上气:

ex.en: The force of the impact knocked the breath out of her.
ex.zh: 她给撞得上不来气了。

senses.en: to push or hit sth, making it fall or turn on its side
senses.zh: 把某物推倒(或推翻)；将某物击倒(或打翻) :

ex.en: You’ve knocked my drink over!
ex.zh: 你把我的饮料打翻了！

ex.en: I’ll put the candle here so that it doesn't get knocked over.
ex.zh: 我把蜡烛放在这里，免得碰倒。

senses.en: ) to join two or more rooms or houses to make a single one

ex.en: They’ve knocked the two rooms together to make one big living room.
ex.zh: 他们把两个房间打通成了一个大起居室。

senses.en: (in tennis, etc.
senses.zh: 网球等)a short practice before a game赛前练习

senses.en: to call sb/sth by a particular name; to think that sb/sth has a particular characteristic or is a particular type of person or thing
senses.zh: 把…称为；认为…具有某特质；把…看成某类人(或事物):

ex.en: She is known to her friends as Beth.
ex.zh: 她的朋友们叫她贝思。

ex.en: It became known as the worst local company to work for.
ex.zh: 它成了雇员公认的最差的本地公司。

senses.en: to be well known because of a particular characteristic, achievement or feature

ex.en: The town is best known for its ancient university.
ex.zh: 这座镇子最出名的是一所古老大学。

ex.en: He is not known for his tact! (= he is often rude)
ex.zh: 他常常出言不逊！

senses.en: to be able to recognize the difference between two things

ex.en: She doesn’t know a Rolls Royce from a Renault.
ex.zh: 她分辨不出劳斯莱斯车和雷诺车。

senses.en: used to say that you think sb is very stupid or completely lacking in skill
to have heard of sb/sth, but not have very much information about or experience of them/it

ex.en: ‘Has he ever been in trouble with the police?’ ‘Not that I know of.’
ex.zh: “他曾被警方抓获吗？”“据我所知没有。”

ex.en: I know of one student who failed the exam twice.
ex.zh: 我听说过一个学生两次没通过这个考试。

senses.en: to begin to work seriously at sth, usually after a period when you have not worked hard

ex.en: It’s time to knuckle down ().
ex.zh: 得开始认真(刻苦工作)了。

senses.en: to accept or admit defeat and do what you are told or what you have to do

ex.en: Those who refused to knuckle under were imprisoned.
ex.zh: 不肯妥协的人被关押起来。

senses.en: to show sb/sth too much respect and be too willing to obey them

ex.en: I refuse to kowtow to anyone.
ex.zh: 我决不屈从任何人。

senses.zh: 常用于进行时) to believe sth that is not true为…所蒙蔽:

ex.en: to be labouring under a delusion
ex.zh: 有错觉

ex.en: She was labouring under the impression that he loved her.
ex.zh: 她以前一直有错觉，以为他爱她。

senses.en: [usually pl.] () shoes fastened with strings

ex.en: As a child, she always wore lace-ups.
ex.zh: 她小时候总是穿系带鞋。

ex.en: lace-up shoes
ex.zh: 系带鞋

senses.en: to put a small amount of sth, such as alcohol, a drug, poison, etc. into a drink
senses.zh: 给(饮料)掺(少许酒、药、毒药等):

ex.en: Someone had laced the cat’s milk with alcohol.
ex.zh: 有人在猫的奶里加了点酒。

senses.en: ) to put a lot of a particular quality into sth such as a speech, a piece of writing, etc.
senses.zh: 把(讲话、文章等)大加润色:

ex.en: The show is laced with black humour.
ex.zh: 这次演出富于黑色幽默。

ex.en: She laces her stories with irony.
ex.zh: 她的故事都运用大量讽刺。

senses.en: to serve food with a large spoon or in large quantities
senses.zh: (用大汤勺)舀出，盛出；盛出(很多食物):

ex.en: He ladled out the soup.
ex.zh: 他用大勺分汤。

senses.en: ) to give sb a lot of sth, especially money or advice
senses.zh: 大量给予，给以一大堆(尤指金钱或建议)

senses.en: to be behind sb/sth because you are walking more slowly

ex.en: Everyone ran down to the beach, but Amy lagged behind.
ex.zh: 大家都向海滩跑去， 只有埃米落在后面。

ex.en: Susie lagged behind the other children.
ex.zh: 苏西落在其他孩子后面。

senses.en: to get sb/yourself into trouble or a difficult situation

ex.en: She landed in court for stealing a car.
ex.zh: 她因为偷车而要出庭。

ex.en: Being too outspoken landed her in trouble.
ex.zh: 她太直率，惹了麻烦。

senses.en: to give sb/yourself an unpleasant or difficult task to deal with
senses.zh: 把重担(或苦差事等)给别人/自己:

ex.en: We’ve landed ourselves with the most boring job of the lot.
ex.zh: 我们承担了其中最枯燥乏味的工作。

ex.en: I got landed with clearing up the mess.
ex.zh: 打扫这片狼藉的活落在了我的头上。

senses.en: to receive sth such as praise or a kind remark with pleasure without thinking about whether it is true or not

ex.en: The baby was lapping up the attention he was getting.
ex.zh: 小孩子发现有人看他就高兴起来。

ex.en: She lapped up his flattery.
ex.zh: 他的恭维话她照单全收。

senses.en: to drink all of sth with great enjoyment

ex.en: The cat lapped up the cream.
ex.zh: 猫把奶油津津有味地舔光了。

senses.en: to pass gradually into a worse or less active state or condition

ex.en: They lapsed into silence.
ex.zh: 他们陷入了沉默。

ex.en: The country lapsed into chaos.
ex.zh: 国家陷入混乱状态。

senses.en: to include a lot of a particular kind of words or expressions in a speech or in a piece of writing
senses.zh: (在讲话或文章中)夹杂大量(某类词语)，大量穿插…:

ex.en: His conversation was larded with Russian proverbs.
ex.zh: 他交谈时夹杂了很多俄国谚语。

senses.en: to enjoy yourself by behaving in a silly way

ex.en: Some kids were larking about in the shopping centre.
ex.zh: 有些孩子在购物中心嬉戏。

senses.en: to make a sudden violent attack on sb

ex.en: He lashed out at us.
ex.zh: 他突然对我们大打出手。

ex.en: Jim lashed out with both fists.
ex.zh: 吉姆突然双手挥拳猛打起来。

senses.en: to criticize sb/sth in an angry way

ex.en: She lashed out at the company for treating her so badly.
ex.zh: 她猛烈抨击公司如此亏待她。

senses.en: to survive for a period of time

ex.en: How long can we last out without water?
ex.zh: 我们不喝水能活多长时间？

ex.en: The doctors thought he might not last out the night.
ex.zh: 医生们以为他可能活不过那晚。

senses.en: to continue in the same situation or manage to do sth for a particular length of time
senses.zh: 坚持下去；坚持(在某段时间内)做某事:

ex.en: He made it to the summit, but at one point I thought he wasn’t going to last out.
ex.zh: 他达到了颠峰，可我一度以为他坚持不下去。

ex.en: She lasted out for a week without smoking.
ex.zh: 她坚持了一个星期不抽烟。

senses.en: to be enough for a particular length of time

ex.en: Our supplies should last out until the end of the month.
ex.zh: 我们的贮备品应足够维持到月底。

senses.en: to follow sb around, often when they do not want you with them

ex.en: He latched onto us and we couldn’t get rid of him.
ex.zh: 他缠着我们，甩也甩不掉。

senses.en: to make sb/yourself seem stupid by making jokes about them/yourself; to not be too serious about sb/yourself
senses.zh: 嘲笑， 讥笑，取笑(某人或自己):

ex.en: They were laughing at him behind his back.
ex.zh: 他们在背后取笑他。

ex.en: We all laughed at Jane when she said she believed in ghosts.
ex.zh: 简说她相信有鬼，我们都笑话她。

senses.en: to show that you find sth funny or amusing

ex.en: You never laugh at my jokes.
ex.zh: 我讲笑话你从来不笑。

ex.en: The whole class was laughing at him clowning around.
ex.zh: 全班同学都给他的滑稽相逗乐了。

senses.en: to make sth seem stupid by making jokes about it

ex.en: He was laughing at my accent.
ex.zh: 他在取笑我的口音。

senses.en: to try to make people think that you do not care about sth, or that it is not serious or important, by making a joke about it
senses.zh: 一笑置之； 付之一笑； 用笑话摆脱:

ex.en: He laughed off suggestions that he had been approached to be manager of the England team.
ex.zh: 传说有人找他当英格兰队的经理，他一笑置之。

ex.en: It was an embarrassing situation, but she managed to laugh it off.
ex.zh: 那个场面很尴尬，可她一笑摆脱了窘境。

senses.en: to start doing sth in a very enthusiastic way; to start to attack sb physically or with words
senses.zh: (热情地)开始做，投入；开始攻击(或抨击)某人:

ex.en: She launched into an explanation of how the machine worked.
ex.zh: 她开始大力讲解机器如何运转。

ex.en: We don’t want to launch ourselves into the wrong enterprise.
ex.zh: 我们不想投入一项我们不应投入的规划。

senses.en: to begin to do sth new or different in a confident way
senses.zh: 拓展，投身于(新的或不同事业):

ex.en: She’s decided she has enough experience to launch out on her own.
ex.zh: 她认为她的经验足以自己创业。

senses.en: to give a lot of sth, often too much, to sb/sth

ex.en: They lavished such care on that house!
ex.zh: 他们把那所房子保养得过于仔细了！

ex.en: He was jealous of the attention lavished on his sister.
ex.zh: 他嫉妒妹妹得到了过多的关爱。

senses.en: to attack sb violently physically or sometimes with words
senses.zh: 袭击(或猛打)某人；猛烈抨击:

ex.en: He started to lay about me with his walking stick.
ex.zh: 他开始用拐杖狠狠揍我。

senses.en: to put sth to one side and not use it or think about it
senses.zh: 把…放在一边(或搁置一旁):

ex.en: I laid my book aside and picked up the letter.
ex.zh: 我把书放在一边，拿起那封信。

ex.en: () They laid aside their differences until the crisis was over.
ex.zh: 他们把分歧搁置起来，直到危机过去。

senses.en: ( ,lay sth 'by )to keep sth to use in the future; to save sth

ex.en: Have you laid anything aside for your old age?
ex.zh: 你有为防老积攒些什么吗？

senses.en: to present a proposal,some information, etc. to sb for them to think about and decide on
senses.zh: 呈交； 提交； 通报:

ex.en: The bill was laid before Parliament.
ex.zh: 议案提交给了国会。

senses.en: to put sth down or stop using it

ex.en: He stopped writing and laid down his pen.
ex.zh: 他停止写字，放下钢笔。

senses.en: to get a supply of sth and store it to use in the future

ex.en: I’ve laid in enough logs for the winter.
ex.zh: 我贮备了足够的木柴过冬。

senses.en: to attack sb/sth violently, with words or blows
senses.zh: (为某事物)(以… ) 痛击， 严厉抨击… :

ex.en: She laid into him with her fists.
ex.zh: 她挥拳狠狠地揍他。

ex.en: He laid into the government for spending millions of pounds on buildings nobody wanted.
ex.zh: 他痛斥政府把几百万英镑耗费在兴建没人想要的建筑物上。

senses.en: used to tell sb to stop doing sth that irritates or annoys you
senses.zh: (让人停止做某事)停止，别再打扰:

ex.en: Lay off! You’re messing up my homework!
ex.zh: 别闹了！你打扰我写作业了！

ex.en: Lay off him, he’s still learning.
ex.zh: 别烦他，他还在学习呢。

senses.en: to stop doing or using sth harmful
senses.zh: 停止做，停止使用(有害的东西):

ex.en: You should lay off alcohol/ drinking for a while.
ex.zh: 你应该暂时别喝酒。

senses.en: to dismiss workers, usually for a short time, because there is not enough work

ex.en: We’ve had to lay off hundreds of workers.
ex.zh: 我们不得不遣散几百名工人。

senses.en: [C] an act of dismissing workers because there is not enough work

ex.en: The crisis has caused thousands of lay-offs.
ex.zh: 这场危机造成了几千人遭解职。

senses.en: [usually sing.] a period of time when sb is not able to take part in an activity or a sport that they usually do
senses.zh: (无法参加活动或运动的)歇工期，歇息期

senses.en: to provide or arrange sth for sb, for example food, transport or entertainment
senses.zh: 提供，安排(食物、运输或娱乐等):

ex.en: Extra buses were laid on during the train strike.
ex.zh: 铁路罢工期间增派了公共汽车。

ex.en: She had laid on tea for the players.
ex.zh: 她为运动员提供茶水。

senses.en: () to talk about sb/sth in a way that makes them seem much better or worse than they really are; to exaggerate sth
senses.zh: 大肆吹捧；过分贬低；夸张:

ex.en: He was laying on the flattery with a trowel.
ex.zh: 他在一个劲儿地拍马屁。

ex.en: Calling him a genius is laying it on a bit thick!
ex.zh: 叫他天才未免有些言过其实了！

senses.en: ) to knock sb unconscious

ex.en: He laid his opponent out with a single blow.
ex.zh: 他一拳就打昏了对手。

senses.en: to prepare a dead body to be buried
[usually sing.] the way in which sth is arranged

ex.en: He still recalled the layout of the house perfectly.
ex.zh: 他依然清晰地记得那所房子的布置。

ex.en: The magazine has a very attractive layout.
ex.zh: 那本杂志的设计非常吸引人。

senses.en: [C] [U] the money that you spend on sth, especially when you start a new project

ex.en: an outlay of $400 000
ex.zh: 40 万元的开支

ex.en: What was your initial outlay on equipment?
ex.zh: 你购置设备的起始费用是多少？

senses.en: to hide somewhere or do nothing for a while

ex.en: They lay up in a cave until it got dark.
ex.zh: 他们在洞里一直躲到天黑。

senses.en: to spend your time relaxing and doing very little
senses.zh: 闲散地打发时间；消磨时光:

ex.en: He lazed about all day.
ex.zh: 他闲散地过了一整天。

ex.en: They lazed around the pool in the afternoon.
ex.zh: 他们下午在游泳池里消磨。

senses.en: to spend a period of time relaxing and doing very little
senses.zh: 闲散地打发时间；消磨时光:

ex.en: We lazed away the summer on the beach.
ex.zh: 我们在沙滩上打发了夏天的时光。

senses.en: an introduction to a subject,a story, etc.
senses.zh: (主题、故事等的)引子，介绍；开场白:

ex.en: We want a striking lead-in to the new programme.
ex.zh: 我们这个新节目需要个精彩的引子。

senses.en: to start a discussion,meeting, etc.

ex.en: Everyone will have a chance to speak. Would you like to lead off?
ex.zh: 大家都有机会发言。你愿意带个头吗？

senses.en: to deceive sb and make them believe sth that is not true, especially that you love them or find them attractive
senses.zh: 误导某人(使其以为受人喜爱等):

ex.en: You shouldn’t have led him on like that.
ex.zh: 你不应该让他产生那样的误解。

senses.en: to result in a particular action or event; to force or persuade sb to take a particular action
senses.zh: 导致；引发；迫使(或劝)某人采取某行动:

ex.en: Living in damp conditions can lead to serious health problems.
ex.zh: 生活在潮湿环境中会引发严重的健康问题。

ex.en: What led you to this conclusion?
ex.zh: 你如何得出这个结论的？

senses.en: to be the introduction to or the cause of sth …

ex.en: The book describes the period leading up to the start of the war.
ex.zh: 这本书描述了战前时期。

ex.en: Police are investigating the chain of events that led up to her death.
ex.zh: 警方正在调查导致她死亡的一连串事情。

senses.en: to prepare to talk about sth or ask a difficult question by gradually introducing the subject you want to talk about
senses.zh: 逐渐引出(话题或难题)；铺埝:

ex.en: What exactly are you leading up to?
ex.zh: 你到底想谈什么？

ex.en: He seemed to be leading up to asking a difficult question.
ex.zh: 他似乎正在为提出难题作铺埝。

senses.en: [sing.] () a period of time or an event or series of events before another event or activity

ex.en: in the lead-up to the election
ex.zh: 在选举前夕

senses.en: to turn over the pages of a book, a magazine etc. quickly without reading them carefully or in detail

ex.en: She picked up a brochure and leafed through it.
ex.zh: 她拿起一本小册子翻阅了一下。

senses.en: to rest against or on sth/sb for support
senses.zh: 倚着人(或物)；靠在…上(或旁)；靠置:

ex.en: Laura leaned weakly against the door.
ex.zh: 劳拉虚弱地靠在门上。

ex.en: We left our bikes leaning up against the wall.
ex.zh: 我们把自行车靠墙放着。

senses.en: to make sth rest against or on sth in a sloping position

ex.en: He leaned his head on his hand and closed his eyes.
ex.zh: 他手托着头闭上眼睛。

ex.en: Maggie leant the broom up against the wall.
ex.zh: 玛吉把扫帚靠在墙上。

senses.en: to try to make sb do sth by threatening them

ex.en: They are leaning on him to make him withdraw his complaints.
ex.zh: 他们正在给他施加压力，让他撤回投诉。

senses.en: to depend on sb/sth

ex.en: It’s good to have someone to lean on.
ex.zh: 有人依赖真好。

ex.en: She was unsure of herself and leaned heavily on her friends for support.
ex.zh: 她对自己没有信心，在很大程度上依靠朋友的支持。

senses.en: to support or tend to prefer a particular idea or political party
senses.zh: 倾向，偏向(某想法或政党):

ex.en: I’m not sure how I’m going to vote but I’m leaning towards the Democrats.
ex.zh: 我没有确定投谁的票，可我倾向于民主党。

senses.en: to accept sth eagerly, without hesitating

ex.en: She leapt at the chance of working in Paris.
ex.zh: 她立刻抓住了去巴黎工作的机会。

senses.en: to suddenly become very interested in an idea or a suggestion, especially because you think it will give you an advantage
senses.zh: (尤指因有利可图，对某想法或建议)突然很感兴趣:

ex.en: The press leapt on the story.
ex.zh: 报界开始对这件事大为关注。

senses.en: to stand quickly and suddenly when you have been sitting

ex.en: He leapt up and ran to answer the door.
ex.zh: 他一下子站起来跑过去开门。

senses.en: to not discuss or consider a particular idea or issue
senses.zh: 把想法(或问题)搁置一边:

senses.en: to make progress much faster than sb else

ex.en: The new car is going to leave the competition far behind.
ex.zh: 新型汽车将把对手远远地甩在后面。

senses.en: to go away from a place without taking sb/sth because you have forgotten them/it

ex.en: Somebody has left their umbrella behind.
ex.zh: 有人忘了取回雨伞。

ex.en: Wait — don’t leave me behind!
ex.zh: 等等─别丢下我！

senses.en: to go away from a place while the result of sth you have done stays there

ex.en: They wore gloves so as not to leave any fingerprints behind (them).
ex.zh: 他们戴着手套，以免留下指纹。

senses.en: to leave a person or place permanently,especially in order to begin a new life
senses.zh: (尤指为开始新生活)永久离开(某人或某地):

ex.en: He was anxious to leave the past behind (him).
ex.zh: 他巴不得永远告别过去。

ex.en: She disappeared a year ago leaving behind a boyfriend and a small baby.
ex.zh: 她一年前抛弃了男友和在襁褓中的孩子消失了。

senses.en: to not remove sth for example from a book, a piece of writing, etc.

ex.en: Make sure you leave that paragraph in.
ex.zh: 一定要保留那个段落。

senses.en: to stop doing sth

ex.en: Lee shouted at him, but he wouldn’t leave off.
ex.zh: 李大声喊他，但他没有停下来。

ex.en: Would you leave off what you are doing for a moment?
ex.zh: 你先放一放手头的事好吗？

senses.en: to not include or mention sb/sth, especially on a list

ex.en: Have I left anyone off the list?
ex.zh: 我有没有漏掉什么人？

senses.en: used to tell sb to stop doing sth silly or annoying
senses.zh: (制止某人做愚蠢或讨厌的事)停下，别干…了

senses.en: used to tell sb that you think what they have said is stupid,or that you do not believe it
senses.zh: 瞎说； 胡说； 不可能:

ex.en: Two million dollars? Leave it out!
ex.zh: 两百万元？不会吧﹗

senses.en: to not include sb deliberately
senses.zh: 不把某人列入(…)；不把某人包括在(…内):

ex.en: It seemed unkind to leave Daisy out, so we invited her too.
ex.zh: 把戴西排除在外似乎不太好，所以我们也邀请了她。

ex.en: There was an outcry when he was left out of the team.
ex.zh: 他被这个队剔除时引起了抗议。

senses.en: unhappy because you have not been included in sth

ex.en: I felt a bit left out.
ex.zh: 我感到有点受到冷落。

senses.en: to not involve sb/sth in sth

ex.en: Leave my brother out of this — he had nothing to do with it.
ex.zh: 别把我弟弟牵扯进去─他与这事没关系。

senses.en: to not include sb/sth either accidentally or on purpose
senses.zh: (偶然或故意地)没有把…包括在(…)内，漏掉:

ex.en: Have I left anyone out?
ex.zh: 我漏掉了什么人吗？

ex.en: You can leave out the gory details.
ex.zh: 你可以删掉那些血腥的细节。

senses.en: [usually pl.] food that has not been eaten and remains after a meal
a custom, tradition, etc. that belongs to an earlier time but still exists
senses.zh: 遗留下来的风俗习惯(或传统等):

ex.en: These narrow roads are a leftover from the days of horse-drawn carriages.
ex.zh: 这些小道是从马车时代沿用下来的。

senses.en: [only before noun] remaining because it has not been eaten or used

ex.en: leftover vegetables/fabric
ex.zh: 剩菜；边角布料

senses.en: to go away from sb so that they can continue what they were doing before you came, or do sth without your help
senses.zh: 离开某人让其继续(或独自) …:

senses.en: to leave sb alone to do as they wish

ex.en: Once I’ve explained things to him I tend to leave him to his own devices.
ex.zh: 我一对他说明了情况，就往往不去干涉他。

senses.en: to allow sb to borrow sth for a period of time

ex.en: The reference books cannot be lent out.
ex.zh: 参考书不得外借。

senses.en: to be suitable for sth

ex.en: Science in elementary schools lends itself well to learning through play.
ex.zh: 小学科学课很适于在游戏中学习。

ex.en: Not all materials lend themselves to scientific dating.
ex.zh: 并非所有材料都能够进行科学鉴定年代。

senses.en: [C, usually sing.] [U] something that is not as good as you thought or hoped it would be

ex.en: The movie was great but the ending was a bit of a let-down.
ex.zh: 这部电影很不错，可是结尾有些不尽人意。

senses.en: to make sb/sth/yourself less successful or impressive than they/it/you should be
senses.zh: (使) 略逊一筹， 美中不足:

ex.en: Her knowledge of Italian is excellent, but her pronunciation lets her down.
ex.zh: 她对意大利语的认识很充分，美中不足的是发音不大好。

ex.en: His clothes let him down.
ex.zh: 他穿着不够得体。

senses.en: to allow sb/sth/yourself to enter a room or a building

ex.en: Let me in! It’s cold out here.
ex.zh: 让我进去！外面很冷。

ex.en: The guard refuses to let anyone in without a security pass.
ex.zh: 警宪不放任何没有安全通行证的人入内。

senses.en: to allow sth such as water or light to enter a place through a hole

ex.en: There was a hole in the roof that let the rain in.
ex.zh: 屋顶有个洞漏雨。

ex.en: I drew the curtains back to let in some light.
ex.zh: 我拉开窗帘透透光。

senses.en: a narrow strip of water which goes from the sea or a lake into the land

ex.en: a narrow/sheltered inlet
ex.zh: 狭窄的/隐蔽的港湾

senses.en: the part of a machine through which air, gas or fuel enters
senses.zh: (气体、液体或燃料进入机器的)入口，进口:

ex.en: a fuel/ power inlet
ex.zh: 燃料入口；充电阀

senses.en: to allow yourself to become involved in sth difficult or unpleasant
senses.zh: 让他人(或自己) 陷入… ， 卷入…，牵涉到…中:

ex.en: If I’d known what I was letting myself in for, I’d never have agreed to help.
ex.zh: 如果我知道要把自己卷进什么事，我决不会同意帮忙的。

ex.en: What have you let me in for?
ex.zh: 你给我招惹了什么麻烦？

senses.en: to allow sb to share a secret
senses.zh: 向某人透露秘密；让某人知道秘密:

ex.en: Are you going to let them in on your plans?
ex.zh: 你是不是打算让他们知道你的计划呀？

ex.en: I wanted to let Chris in on the secret.
ex.zh: 我原打算告诉克里斯这个秘密的。

senses.en: to be put into the surface of sth

ex.en: A large window was let into the wall.
ex.zh: 已经把一个大窗户嵌进墙壁里。

senses.en: to let air from the bowels come out through your bottom
to allow sb not to do sth or not to go somewhere

ex.en: You really ought to help with the shopping, but I suppose I could let you off.
ex.zh: 你真应该帮着买东西，但我想我可以免你不干。

ex.en: Mum let me off the household chores during exams.
ex.zh: 考试期间妈妈免了我的家务活儿。

senses.en: to allow sb to get out of a vehicle, especially a bus
senses.zh: 让某人下车(尤指公共汽车):

ex.en: Can you let me off here?
ex.zh: 让我在这儿下车好吗？

senses.en: to free sb from a difficult or unpleasant task or situation
senses.zh: 让某人免予苦差(或摆脱窘境等):

ex.en: He wasn’t going to let the senator off the hook easily; he kept asking difficult questions.
ex.zh: 他不轻易放过参议员；他不断地质疑问难。

senses.en: to tell sb sth that is supposed to be a secret

ex.en: She doesn’t know I’ve bought her a watch, so don’t let on, will you?
ex.zh: 她并不知道我给她买了块手表，所以请保密，行吗？

ex.en: The children knew he was coming, but they didn’t let on to anyone.
ex.zh: 孩子们知道他要来，但他们对谁都没有说。

senses.en: to allow sb not to do sth they have promised or are expected to do; to free sb from a difficult situation
senses.zh: 让某人免于做…(或摆脱窘境):

ex.en: I’ve got school tomorrow, so that lets me out (of helping).
ex.zh: 我明天上学，因此我不用帮忙了。

senses.en: to allow sb to leave a hospital,prison, etc., especially early or for a short time
senses.zh: 让某人(尤指提前或暂时)出院(或出狱等) :

ex.en: The doctors might let me out tomorrow.
ex.zh: 医生可能让我明天出院。

senses.en: [sing.] () something that allows you to avoid an unpleasant or difficult situation

ex.en: a let-out clause (= in a contract)
ex.zh: 可钻空子的合同条款

ex.en: ‘I think it’s too hot to go jogging today,’ I said, looking for a let-out.
ex.zh: “我觉得今天慢跑太热。”我找藉口说。

senses.en: to allow sb/sth/yourself to go out of a room or a building
senses.zh: 让…(从房间或建筑物)出去:

ex.en: Can you let yourself out?
ex.zh: 你自己可以出去吗？
