ex.en: I was amazed they let her out of hospital so soon.
ex.zh: 我很惊讶他们这么早就让她出院了。

senses.en: to tell a secret carelessly or by mistake

ex.en: I was trying to keep my promotion quiet, but Steve went and let the cat out of the bag.
ex.zh: 我尽量不说我升职的事，可史蒂夫过去说漏了嘴。

senses.en: to give a cry; to make a sound

ex.en: She let out a scream of terror.
ex.zh: 她发出一声恐怖的尖叫。

ex.en: He let out a sigh of relief.
ex.zh: 他松了口气。

senses.en: to make an item of clothing looser or larger

ex.en: I’ve eaten so much I’ll have to let my belt out!
ex.zh: 我吃得太多，只好松一松皮带了！

senses.en: ( ,let sth 'out of sth) to allow air, liquid, etc. to escape or flow out of somewhere
senses.zh: 让空气(或液体等)(从…)透出(或渗漏):

ex.en: We need to let the air out of the radiator.
ex.zh: 我们得给散热器放放气。

senses.en: to allow sb/sth to go past you

ex.en: Can you let me past, please?
ex.zh: 请让我过去好吗？

senses.en: to allow sb/sth to pass or go through sth that is blocking the way

ex.en: The crowd moved aside to let the am bulance through.
ex.zh: 人群退开让救护车通过。

ex.en: Let me through — I’m a doctor.
ex.zh: 让我过一下─我是医生。

senses.en: ) to say that sb/sth is good enough for sth or is correct

ex.en: We were worried the council wouldn’t let the plans for the new building through.
ex.zh: 我们担心议会不会通过兴建新楼房的计划。

senses.en: to become less strong

ex.en: The rain showed no sign of letting up.
ex.zh: 雨没有减小的迹象。

senses.en: to do sth with less effort or energy than before, or stop doing it
senses.zh: 放松(努力) ； 松劲； 停止… :

ex.en: We mustn’t let up, even though we’re winning.
ex.zh: 尽管我们现在领先，我们一定不能松劲。

ex.en: Doesn’t she ever let up? She’s been complaining all day.
ex.zh: 她就不能停一下吗？她抱怨了一整天了。

senses.en: [U] [sing.] a reduction in the strength of something; a period of time when sth unpleasant stops
senses.zh: 减弱；减少；(不愉快的事的)停止期:

ex.en: There can be no let-up in the war against drugs.
ex.zh: 与毒品的斗争是不能松懈的。

ex.en: The rain continued all afternoon with no let-up.
ex.zh: 雨连续下了整整一下午，没有停止过。

senses.en: to point sth, especially a gun, at sb

ex.en: She levelled the pistol at his head.
ex.zh: 她用手枪指着他的脑袋。

senses.en: to make standards,amounts, etc. be the same low/high or lower/higher level
senses.zh: 使(标准、数量等)降低/提高到同等水平:

ex.en: The government is accused of levelling down standards in schools rather than levelling them up.
ex.zh: 政府受到了全面拉低，而非提高各学校标准的指责。

senses.en: to become level or steady after a period of sharp rises and falls
senses.zh: (经过急剧的涨落后)平稳下来:

ex.en: House prices showed no sign of levelling off.
ex.zh: 住房价格没有趋于稳定的迹象。

senses.en: to become level or horizontal after rising or falling

ex.en: The road began to level off as we approached the coast.
ex.zh: 我们接近海岸时，路开始变得平坦。

ex.en: The plane levelled off at 20 000 feet.
ex.zh: 飞机在2万英尺的高空保持水平飞行。

senses.en: to speak or deal with sb in an honest and direct way
senses.zh: 对某人说实话；直言相告:

ex.en: I’m going to level with you now — your work hasn’t been up to standard for some time.
ex.zh: 我跟你说实话吧─你的工作最近一段时间没有达到要求。

ex.en: I’ve got the feeling that he’s not levelling with me.
ex.zh: 我感觉他对我不够坦率。

senses.en: to eat or drink sth by moving your tongue over the surface of it

ex.en: She licked the jam off (the spoon).
ex.zh: 她舔了(小勺上的)果酱。

ex.en: The cat licked up the milk from the dish.
ex.zh: 猫舔了碟子里的牛奶。

senses.en: to be in the future;to be in front of you
senses.zh: 在将来；在某人面前；面对某人:

ex.en: Great opportunities lie ahead.
ex.zh: 将来机会很多。

ex.en: Who knows what problems might lie ahead of us?
ex.zh: 谁知道我们可能遇到什么问题呢？

senses.en: (of a person
senses.zh: 人) to spend time being lazy and not doing anything in particular无所事事地混日子；懒散度日；游手好闲:

ex.en: She’s been lying around the house all day doing nothing.
ex.zh: 她在家里懒散了一整天。

senses.en: (of a number of things
senses.zh: 许多东西) to be left somewhere in a careless or untidy way乱放；乱搁:

ex.en: His clothes lay around all over the floor.
ex.zh: 一地都是他的衣服。

ex.en: ‘Have you seen my purse?’ ‘It was lying about in the kitchen when I last saw it.’
ex.zh: “你看见我的皮夹了吗？”“我上次看见的时候是在厨房里的。”

senses.en: a lazy person who does very little work
senses.zh: 游手好闲的人；懒汉；二流子

senses.en: to rest, relax and do very little

ex.en: Just lie back and enjoy the peace and quiet.
ex.zh: 只管悠闲享受这种宁静好啦。

ex.en: She lay back on the pillows and closed her eyes.
ex.zh: 她安闲地躺在枕头上合上了眼睛。

senses.en: to be in front of sb

ex.en: A terrible sight lay before them.
ex.zh: 可怕的情景出现在他们面前。

senses.en: to be in the future

ex.en: Your whole life lies before you.
ex.zh: 你整个人生还长着呢。

senses.en: to be the real explanation or reason for sth

ex.en: She understood the feelings that lay behind his angry words.
ex.zh: 她明白他愤怒的话语之后的真实感受。

ex.en: We will probably never know what lay behind his decision to resign.
ex.zh: 我们可能永远不会知道他辞职的真正原因。

senses.en: to be or move into a horizontal position on a bed, etc. in order to sleep or rest

ex.en: Go and lie down for a while.
ex.zh: 去躺一会儿吧。

ex.en: He lay down on the sofa and went to sleep.
ex.zh: 他在沙发上躺下睡着了。

senses.en: [sing.] (, ) a short rest,especially in bed

ex.en: to have a lie-down
ex.zh: 躺一会儿

senses.en: to stay in bed after the time you usually get up

ex.en: It’s Saturday tomorrow, so you can lie in.
ex.zh: 明天是星期六，你可以睡懒觉了。

senses.en: [sing.] (, ) an act of staying in bed longer than usual in the morning

ex.en: to have a lie-in
ex.zh: 睡懒觉

senses.en: to hide somewhere

ex.en: The fugitives lay up in the caves until it got dark.
ex.zh: 逃亡者在洞里一直躲到天黑。

senses.en: to be the duty or responsibility of sb/sth
[C] [U] the moment when a rocket or spacecraft leaves the ground and rises into the air
senses.zh: (火箭或航天器的)发射，起飞，升空:

ex.en: We have lift-off!
ex.zh: 我们发射了！

senses.en: to raise sb/sth/yourself to a higher position or level
senses.zh: 举起； 提起； 抬高； 吊起:

ex.en: I can’t lift you up — you’re too heavy!
ex.zh: 我抱不动你─你太重了！

ex.en: She lifted herself up on one elbow.
ex.zh: 她用一只胳膊肘支壠起身体。

senses.en: to suddenly see sb/sth

ex.en: Her gaze lighted on her daughter.
ex.zh: 她一眼瞅见了她的女儿。

senses.en: to suddenly find sb/sth or think of sb/sth

ex.en: The research team has lit upon important new material.
ex.zh: 研究队伍突然找到了重要的新资料。

senses.en: to become or to make sth bright with light or colour

ex.en: She switched the monitor on and the screen lit up.
ex.zh: 她打开显示屏，屏幕上出现了画面。

ex.en: Flashes of lightning lit up the sky.
ex.zh: 闪电照亮了天空。

senses.en: () to begin to smoke a cigarette, etc.

ex.en: She took out a cigarette and lit up.
ex.zh: 她掏出一支香烟点上吸起来。

ex.en: He lit up one cigarette after another.
ex.zh: 他一根接一根地抽着烟。

senses.en: used to tell sb to be less serious or to complain or worry less about sth
senses.zh: 别那么严肃；别抱怨；别担忧:

ex.en: Come on, lighten up! It was only a joke.
ex.zh: 喂，别紧张！这只不过是开玩笑。

senses.en: to compare sb/sth to someone or something else and say that they are similar

ex.en: He has been likened to a young George Best.
ex.zh: 有人把他比作年轻的乔治·贝斯特。

ex.en: She likened the building to a ship.
ex.zh: 她把这座楼房比作一条船。

senses.en: to do exercise to prepare to take part in a sport, a race, etc.; to warm up
senses.zh: (体育运动、比赛等前)做准备活动，做热身运动:

ex.en: The players were limbering up for the game.
ex.zh: 运动员正在为比赛做预备活动。

ex.en: () The candidates are already limbering up for the election campaign.
ex.zh: 各候选人已经在为竞选运动热身了。

senses.en: to make sth exist or happen only in a particular place or within a particular group

ex.en: Violent crime is not limited to big cities.
ex.zh: 暴力犯罪并不局限于大城市。

ex.en: The teaching of history should not be limited to dates and figures.
ex.zh: 桝授历史不应该局限于讲年代和人物。

senses.en: to join with sb in order to do sth

ex.en: Local groups are lining up against the new development.
ex.zh: 当地团体正联合起来反对新的开发项目。

ex.en: Several newspapers lined up to demand his resignation.
ex.zh: 几家报纸联手要求他辞职。

senses.en: [usually sing.] a row of people that is formed so that sb who saw a crime can try to recognize the person who did it
senses.zh: 辨认行列，列队认人(把嫌疑犯同其他人排在一起，让目击罪案者辨认):

ex.en: She picked him out of a line-up (=she recognized him as the person who committed the crime).
ex.zh: 她从辨认行列中把他指认出来。

senses.en: to be, or to put sth, in the correct position in relation to sth else
senses.zh: (使与相关的其他东西)排齐；(使)对齐:

ex.en: The three holes should all line up (with each other).
ex.zh: 这三个孔应该全对齐。

senses.en: to arrange people or things in a line or a row

ex.en: She lined the children up for the photograph.
ex.zh: 她让孩子们站成一排照相。

ex.en: His CDs were lined up on the shelf.
ex.zh: 他的光盘排列在架子上。

senses.en: to remain for a long time

ex.en: The memory of that day lingers on in the minds of local people.
ex.zh: 当地人对那一天久久不能忘怀。

ex.en: The smell lingered on for days after.
ex.zh: 那种气味连续多日不能散尽。

senses.en: to remain alive, but becoming gradually weaker
senses.zh: 奄奄一息； 苟延残喘:

ex.en: We should be thankful that she didn’t linger on.
ex.zh: 她没有一息奄奄地拖延下去，我们应该感到宽慰。

senses.en: to connect sb/sth with someone or something else

ex.en: The alarm is linked up to the police station.
ex.zh: 这个防盗器与警局连接。

ex.en: The new network can link us up to similar organizations around the country.
ex.zh: 新网络能使我们和国内类似的机构相连接。

senses.en: a connection between two systems or machines
senses.zh: (两个系统或机器的)连接，接合:

ex.en: They did a live satellite link-up with the show.
ex.zh: 他们通过宪星实况转播了演出。

senses.en: to be/get drunk

ex.en: We got liquored up on Saturday night.
ex.zh: 星期六晚上我们喝醉了。

senses.en: to listen carefully to see if you can hear sb/sth

ex.en: She lay awake, listening out for the sound of the key in the lock.
ex.zh: 她躺着没睡，一直留心听着是否有钥匙转动锁孔的声音。

ex.en: Will you listen out for the phone while I’m in the bath?
ex.zh: 我洗澡时你注意听电话好吗？

senses.en: used to tell sb to pay attention to what you are going to say

ex.en: Listen up, everyone — this is important!
ex.zh: 大家注意听─这很重要！

senses.en: to follow a particular belief or set of principles
senses.zh: 遵守某种信念(或原则等):

ex.en: Some people live by the rule ‘anything for the sake of peace’.
ex.zh: 有些人的信念是不惜任何代价寻求和平。

ex.en: Women working in a man’s world have to live by men’s rules.
ex.zh: 在男性的圈子里工作的女性要遵守男性的规则。

senses.en: to earn the money that you need by using or doing a particular thing
senses.zh: 靠做某事赚钱为生(或获取所需):

ex.en: people who live by the land (= for example, farmers)
ex.zh: 靠土地为生的人们(如农民)

ex.en: She lived by giving private lessons.
ex.zh: 她靠做家庭桝师赚钱生活。

senses.en: to make people forget sth very embarrassing or bad that you have done in the past
senses.zh: 让人忘记(自己做过的事):

senses.en: to consider sb/sth as the main purpose of or the most important person or thing in your life

ex.en: She lives for her work.
ex.zh: 她活着是为了工作。

ex.en: What have I got to live for now?
ex.zh: 如今我活着是为了什么？

senses.en: to live at the place where you work or study
senses.zh: 住在工作(或学习)的地方:

ex.en: They have a nanny living in.
ex.zh: 他们有个保姆住在家里。

ex.en: () Most students live in during their first year.
ex.zh: 大多数学生第一学年住在学校。

senses.en: [only before noun]
(of an employee
senses.zh: 雇员) living in the house where they work住在工作场所的:

ex.en: a live-in housekeeper/ position
ex.zh: 住在雇主家的管家/工作

senses.en: (of a boyfriend,girlfriend, etc.
senses.zh: 男朋友、女朋友等) living in the same house as their sexual partner同居的:

ex.en: a live-in lover/boyfriend
ex.zh: 同居恋人/男朋友

senses.en: to get the money or the things you need from sb/sth

ex.en: You can’t live off your parents forever!
ex.zh: 你不能一辈子靠父母养！

ex.en: He had to live off his savings.
ex.zh: 他得靠积蓄过活。

senses.en: to eat one type of food very frequently or all the time

ex.en: When I was a student I lived off bread and cheese.
ex.zh: 我当学生时主要吃麵包和黄油。

senses.en: to eat food that you can grow, kill or find yourself
senses.zh: 依靠种地(或养殖、打猎等)为生；靠土地吃饭；自食其力:

ex.en: The army was forced to live off the land.
ex.zh: 军队被迫自给自足。

ex.en: It’s a farming area and most of the people still live off the land.
ex.zh: 那是个农业地区，多数人依然靠土地吃饭。

senses.en: to have enough money to be able to buy expensive food, drink, clothes, etc.

ex.en: It was a time when landlords and merchants lived off the fat of the land.
ex.zh: 那个时代地主和商人穿金戴银，生活阔绰。

senses.en: to continue to live or exist

ex.en: He may be dead but his music lives on.
ex.zh: 他或许不在人世了，但他的音乐经久不衰。

senses.en: to live away from the place where you work or study
senses.zh: 住在工作(或学习)以外的地方:

ex.en: I lived out during my final year at college.
ex.zh: 我唸大学的最后一年住在校外。

senses.en: to do in reality sth that you think about, believe in, dream of,etc.
senses.zh: 将(思想)付诸行动；实践(信念等)；实现(梦想等):

ex.en: On holiday in Texas I lived out my childhood fantasy of being a cowboy.
ex.zh: 我在得克萨斯度假时实现了我想当牛仔的童年梦想。

senses.en: to experience sth difficult or unpleasant and survive
senses.zh: 经历(灾难或困难等)而幸存:

ex.en: He lived through both world wars.
ex.zh: 他经历了两次世界大战。

ex.en: It’s something I never want to live through again.
ex.zh: 那是我永远不想再次经历的事情。

senses.en: to live in the same house, flat/apartment, etc.

ex.en: There are six students living together in the house.
ex.zh: 房子里有六个学生合住。

ex.en: I’m living in a flat with Meg.
ex.zh: 我和梅格合住一个公寓单元。

senses.en: to share a home and have a sexual relationship, but without being married
to have a very exciting and enjoyable time, usually spending a lot of money
senses.zh: 尽情欢乐； 挥霍享乐:

ex.en: I’ve heard that Tom’s living it up in L.A.
ex.zh: 我听说汤姆在洛杉矶市吃喝玩乐。

senses.en: to behave as well as or be as good or successful as people expect

ex.en: The hotel failed to live up to expectations.
ex.zh: 这个旅馆没有期望的好。

ex.en: Mr. Mean lived up to his name and died a millionaire.
ex.zh: 吝啬先生果真名副其实，去世时还是个百万富翁。

senses.en: to accept an unpleasant situation and continue with your life and work

ex.en: You might not like the situation, but you’ll have to learn to live with it.
ex.zh: 你可能不喜欢这种情况，但你必须学会忍受。

ex.en: She wouldn’t be able to live with herself if she hurt him.
ex.zh: 如果她伤害了他，她是无法原谅自己的。

senses.en: to become or to make sb/sth more lively, interesting or exciting

ex.en: She livened up when Alan asked her to dance.
ex.zh: 艾伦请她跳舞她便来了精神。

ex.en: Put some music on to liven things up.
ex.zh: 放些音乐活跃一下气氛吧。

senses.en: to give sb/sth too many things to carry

ex.en: She was loaded down with books.
ex.zh: 她提了很多书。

senses.en: to give sb/sth too much work or too many responsibilities
senses.zh: 给…过多的工作；给…委以过重的任务:

ex.en: We’ve been loaded down with work recently.
ex.zh: 我们最近工作繁忙。

senses.en: to put a lot of things in/on sth, especially a vehicle
senses.zh: (以…)装车(等)；把车辆等装满(…)；把…装车:

ex.en: Bring the car to the door and we’ll help you load up.
ex.zh: 把车开到门前，我们帮你装车。

ex.en: I loaded up the van with all my possessions.
ex.zh: 我把我的东西全塞进了客货车。

senses.en: to spend your time in a lazy way, doing very little
senses.zh: 游手好闲；无所事事；(在…)闲荡:

ex.en: kids loafing about with nothing to do
ex.zh: 四处游荡的孩子们

ex.en: She just loafs around the streets all day.
ex.zh: 她一整天只是逛街。

senses.en: to lend sth/sb to sb,sometimes in return for money
senses.zh: 把…借出(或租出)；把…借给…(或租给…):

ex.en: Several players have been loaned out to other teams.
ex.zh: 有几名运动员借调到其他队。

ex.en: Sometimes we loan out these buses.
ex.zh: 我们有时把这些公共汽车租出去。

senses.en: to shut yourself in a place away from other people so that you are not disturbed
senses.zh: 把自己关起来(不受打扰) :

ex.en: He locked himself away (in his room) until he’d finished his work.
ex.zh: 他把自己关在房间里，直到把活干完。

senses.en: to put sb/sth/yourself in a room or building and lock the door

ex.en: The prisoners are locked in every night.
ex.zh: 犯人每天晚上都给锁在牢房里。

ex.en: He rushed to his bedroom and locked himself in.
ex.zh: 他冲进…室，把自己反锁在里面。

senses.en: () an occasion when customers are locked into a bar or pub after it has closed so that they can continue drinking privately
senses.zh: 顾客留在关门后的酒吧里(继续喝酒)

senses.en: to be involved in a difficult or unpleasant situation, especially an argument or a legal dispute, that seems unlikely to end soon
senses.zh: 陷入，卷入(纷争或困境等中无法摆脱):

ex.en: The parents are locked in a bitter legal battle over the future of the twins.
ex.zh: 父母为双胞胎将来的归属陷入激烈的法律争斗中。

senses.en: to be in a particular situation, or behave in a particular way, that you cannot change
senses.zh: 无法摆脱(某状况)；积习难改:

ex.en: The government is locked into a policy of reducing taxes.
ex.zh: 政府的减税政策欲罢不能。

ex.en: Older horses can get locked into bad habits.
ex.zh: 老马会养成难以改掉的恶习。

senses.en: to prevent workers from entering their place of work until they agree to the conditions given by the employer
senses.zh: (在工人答应雇主的条件前)不准进入工作的地方:

ex.en: The management will lock out anyone who refuses to sign the new contract.
ex.zh: 资方将不允许拒绝签订新合同的人上班。

senses.en: a situation when an employer refuses to let workers enter their place of work until they agree to particular conditions
senses.zh: 停工，闭厂(雇主在工人答应条件前不准其进入工作场所):

ex.en: The strikers faced a lockout.
ex.zh: 罢工者面临着停工闭厂的威胁。

senses.en: to accidentally leave your keys inside a car,building, etc. when you go out, so that you are unable to get inside again

ex.en: I’ve managed to lock myself out of my room three times!
ex.zh: 我已经三次把自己锁在门外了！

senses.en: to make a building safe by locking the doors and windows

ex.en: Make sure you lock up before you leave.
ex.zh: 离开时别忘了锁好门窗。

ex.en: She locked the shop up and went home.
ex.zh: 她锁好商店的门窗后回家了。

senses.en: a small shop that the owner does not live in; a place that the owner does not need and rents to sb else, for example to keep a car in
senses.zh: (店主不住在内的)小商店；(供出租的)车库(等) :

ex.en: a lock-up garage/shop
ex.zh: 出租的车库；不住人的小商店

senses.en: to put sb in prison or in a guarded hospital
senses.zh: 把某人关进监狱(或监管医院) :

ex.en: People like that should be locked up!
ex.zh: 那种人应该坐牢！

ex.en: They should lock her up and throw away the key.
ex.zh: 他们应该把她关起来，丢掉钥匙。

senses.en: to perform the actions that allow you to begin using a computer system
senses.zh: 登录，注册，进入，登入(计算机系统) :

ex.en: I got an error message when I tried to log in/on.
ex.zh: 我想登录时信息提示登录有误。

ex.en: The password allows the user to log into the system.
ex.zh: 用户用密码可进入系统。

senses.en: to perform the actions that allow you to finish using a computer system
senses.zh: 退出， 注销， 登出(计算机系统):

ex.en: Try logging off and logging on again.
ex.zh: 试一试先退出再登录。

senses.en: to sit, lie or stand in a relaxed way, doing very little
senses.zh: 懒洋洋地坐着(或躺着、站着)；无所事事:

ex.en: There were several kids lolling around outside the club.
ex.zh: 有几个小孩在俱乐部外面闲荡。

ex.en: Jim should get a job instead of lolling around the house all day.
ex.zh: 吉姆应该找份工作，不要成天闲在家里。

senses.en: to want sb/sth very much

ex.en: to long for a baby
ex.zh: 盼望要个孩子

ex.en: I was longing for a chat and a good laugh.
ex.zh: 我很想聊聊天开心地笑一笑。

senses.en: [only before noun] that sb has been wanting or hoping for very much

ex.en: a longed-for child
ex.zh: 盼望已久的孩子

senses.en: to look quickly across a room

ex.en: I looked across to where they were sitting.
ex.zh: 我朝他们坐的地方望过去。

ex.en: She knew I was there, but she didn’t look over at me.
ex.zh: 她知道我在那里，可她没往我这边看。

senses.en: to make sure that sb/sth is safe; take care of sb/sth

ex.en: His parents are looking after the children for the weekend.
ex.zh: 他的父母这个周末照看孩子们。

ex.en: She doesn’t look after her clothes.
ex.zh: 她穿得不整洁。

senses.en: to think about what is going to happen in the future

ex.en: The team is looking ahead to next season.
ex.zh: 这支队伍正为下个赛季作准备。

ex.en: Looking ahead to the weekend, the weather will stay fine.
ex.zh: 可以预见好天气将持续到周末。

senses.en: to visit a place or a building as a tourist

ex.en: Take your time looking around.
ex.zh: 慢慢游览吧。

ex.en: They’ve gone to look round the cathedral.
ex.zh: 他们去参观大桝堂。

senses.en: to turn your head in different directions so that you can see sth or see what is there

ex.en: She came into the room, looked around, then went out.
ex.zh: 她进房间里四下察看了一下就出去了。

ex.en: He looked round the classroom angrily.
ex.zh: 他生气地环顾桝室。

senses.en: to turn your eyes towards sb/sth so that you can see them/it

ex.en: Don’t look at me like that!
ex.zh: 别那样看着我！

ex.en: What are you looking at?
ex.zh: 你在看什么呢？

senses.en: to examine sth/sb closely

ex.en: I’d like the doctor to look at him.
ex.zh: 我想找医生给他检查一下。

ex.en: Can you look at this watch for me? I think it might be broken.
ex.zh: 你能帮我看看这块手表吗？我想可能是坏了。

senses.en: to read sth, usually quickly, without reading all the details

ex.en: She sat in the waiting room, looking at a magazine.
ex.zh: 她坐在等候室翻阅杂志。

senses.en: to look in the opposite direction; to turn your eyes away from sb/sth

ex.en: She looked at him then looked away.
ex.zh: 她看了看他，然后移开了视线。

ex.en: He mumbled a reply and looked away from me.
ex.zh: 他支支吾吾回答了一下就不再看我了。

senses.en: to think about sth that has happened in your past
senses.zh: 回首(往事)；回忆； 回顾:

ex.en: Looking back, I’m not surprised she left.
ex.zh: 回头想想，我对她的离开并不感到意外。

ex.en: He looked back on his time in England with a sense of nostalgia.
ex.zh: 他怀恋着自己在英国的时光。

senses.en: to become more and more successful

ex.en: He started work on a market stall in 1970 and he’s never looked back.
ex.zh: 他于1970年开了个集市货摊，从此生意日益兴旺。

senses.en: to turn your eyes downwards to the floor, especially because you are embarrassed,shy, etc.
senses.zh: (尤指因尴尬、害羞等)垂下目光:

ex.en: The little boy blushed and looked down.
ex.zh: 小男孩脸红了， 低头向下看。

ex.en: She looked down at her hands.
ex.zh: 她低头看着自己的双手。

senses.en: to consider sb/sth as less good or important than yourself

ex.en: She tends to look down on people who haven’t been to college.
ex.zh: 她偏向瞧不起没上过大学的人。

ex.en: They looked down on our little house.
ex.zh: 他们对我们的小屋不屑一顾。

senses.en: to search for sb/sth, either because you have lost them/it, or because you need them/it

ex.en: Sue’s been looking for you.
ex.zh: 休一直在找你。

ex.en: ‘Can I help you?’ ‘Yes, I’m looking for this shirt in blue.’ (= in a shop/store)“我能帮你吗？”“是的，我要找这款蓝色衬衣。”

senses.en: to hope for sth or expect sth

ex.en: The examiners will be looking for good grammar and spelling.
ex.zh: 主考人希望语法和拼写正确无误。

ex.en: This could be just the opportunity he’s been looking for.
ex.zh: 这可能就是他一直期待的机会。

senses.en: to search for sth; to try to find sth

ex.en: They were looking for an easy solution to the problem.
ex.zh: 他们正在寻求解决这个问题的简捷途径。

senses.en: not expected

ex.en: unlooked-for success
ex.zh: 意想不到的成功

senses.en: to feel excited about sth that is going to happen because you expect to enjoy it

ex.en: Are you looking forward to your trip?
ex.zh: 你期待着这次旅行吗？

ex.en: I’m not looking forward to going to the dentist.
ex.zh: 我可不希望去看牙医。

senses.en: to make a short visit to a place

ex.en: I asked Sarah to look in on her grandmother on her way home.
ex.zh: 我要萨拉回家时顺便去看看她的祖母。

ex.en: The doctor will look in again this evening.
ex.zh: 医生今晚会再来探视的。

senses.en: to examine sth or consider it carefully

ex.en: The committee is looking into the matter.
ex.zh: 委员会正在调查这件事。

ex.en: The manager is looking into your complaint.
ex.zh: 经理正在处理你们的投诉。

senses.en: to watch an event or an incident without taking part in it yourself

ex.en: People looked on in alarm as the car began to roll down the hill.
ex.zh: 人们惊恐地看着那辆车开始磙下山坡。

ex.en: Passers-by just looked on as he was attacked.
ex.zh: 他遭人袭击，路人只在一边袖手旁观。

senses.en: a person who watches sth without becoming involved in it

ex.en: A crowd of onlookers formed around the fight.
ex.zh: 旁观者聚集起来围观斗殴。

senses.en: used to tell sb to be careful, especially when there is some danger
senses.zh: (表示警告，尤指有危险)小心，当心，留神:

ex.en: Look out! There’s a car coming.
ex.zh: 当心！有车来了。

ex.en: You’re going to burn that food if you don’t look out.
ex.zh: 你要是不看着点就会把食物煮煳。

senses.en: to take care of sb/yourself and think about their/your own interests
senses.zh: 考虑他人(或自己)的利益；关照:

ex.en: Once he was in London he had to look out for himself.
ex.zh: 他一到伦敦就要自己照顾自己。

ex.en: Emily’s brothers always looked out for her.
ex.zh: 埃米莉的哥哥们总是关照她。

senses.en: to try to find sb/sth or meet sb

ex.en: I was looking out for Pete but I didn’t see him.
ex.zh: 我当时一直找皮特，可没有看见他。

ex.en: Look out for this film at your local cinema.
ex.zh: 留意你当地的电影院有没有播放这部影片。

senses.en: to try to avoid sth bad happening or doing sth bad

ex.en: Look out for pickpockets.
ex.zh: 当心扒手。

senses.en: a place where sb watches from to see if there is any danger

ex.en: a lookout post/tower
ex.zh: 了望哨/塔

senses.en: a person who watches for danger

ex.en: The burglars posted a lookout outside the house.
ex.zh: 盗贼在房子外面安排了一人望风。

senses.en: (of a room, etc.
senses.zh: 房间等) to have a view of sth面向；朝向:

ex.en: Our room looked out over the square.
ex.zh: 从我们的房间朝外看可俯视广场。

senses.en: to make a tour of a place

ex.en: We were invited to look over the new classrooms.
ex.zh: 我们应邀参观了新桝室。

senses.en: to read sth quickly

ex.en: I need to look over my notes before the test.
ex.zh: 测验前我得把笔记过一遍。

ex.en: Your tutor will look over your work with you.
ex.zh: 你的导师会和你一道看一遍你的作业。

senses.en: to inspect or examine sb/sth to see how good, big, etc. it is

ex.en: He looked the painting over carefully.
ex.zh: 他仔细查看了那幅画。

ex.en: I’d like the doctor to look him over.
ex.zh: 我想医生给他检查一下。

senses.en: to look at sb and not show that you have seen or recognized them
senses.zh: 对某人视而不见；佯装没有看见某人:

ex.en: I smiled at him, but he just looked straight through me.
ex.zh: 我朝他笑了笑，可他假装没看见我。

senses.en: to rely on sb/sth or expect sb to provide sth or do sth

ex.en: They looked to us for help.
ex.zh: 他们指望得到我们的帮助。

ex.en: We must look to other means to generate the funds we need.
ex.zh: 我们必须通过别的方法筹集我们需要的资金。

senses.en: to think about something that will happen in the future

ex.en: We are looking to the future with confidence.
ex.zh: 我们满怀信心地展望未来。

senses.en: ) to make sure that sth is safe or in good condition; to think about how to improve sth
senses.zh: 注意(确保安全、正常等)；考虑(改进):

ex.en: You should look to your own behaviour before criticizing others.
ex.zh: 正人先要正己。

senses.en: to visit or contact sb when you are in the place where they live, especially when you have not seen them for a long time
senses.zh: (尤指久别之后在所处之地)拜访，看望，接触:

ex.en: Look me up next time you’re in London.
ex.zh: 你下次到伦敦，来看我吧。

senses.en: to admire or respect sb

ex.en: She always looked up to her older sister.
ex.zh: 她一向尊敬她的姐姐。

senses.en: to appear as a large shape that is not clear, often in a way that seems frightening or threatening
senses.zh: 赫然耸现；令人惊恐地隐现:

ex.en: A dark shape loomed up out of the fog.
ex.zh: 一个黑煳煳的物体在雾霭中出现了。

senses.en: to become more relaxed and comfortable

ex.en: He began to loosen up and enjoy the evening.
ex.zh: 他开始轻松下来享受这个夜晚。

senses.en: to relax your muscles or parts of the body, or make them relax,before taking exercise, etc.

ex.en: I swam a short distance to loosen up.
ex.zh: 我游了一小段距离放松放松。

ex.en: A massage will help loosen you up.
ex.zh: 按摩一下会使你得到放松的。

senses.en: to remove sth from sth, especially branches from a tree, by cutting it

ex.en: Several branches had been lopped off ().
ex.zh: (从树上)砍下了几条枝桠。

ex.en: They lopped 20p off the price of each unit.
ex.zh: 他们把单价削减了20 便士。

senses.en: to make sth smaller or less

ex.en: The new rail link has lopped an hour off the journey.
ex.zh: 新铁路连线把旅程缩短了一个小时。

senses.en: to behave in a superior way to sb

ex.en: She likes to lord it over the junior staff.
ex.zh: 她喜欢在初级职员面前摆架子。

senses.en: to become so interested in sth that you are not aware of anything else

ex.en: I soon lost myself in the excitement of the play.
ex.zh: 我很快就沉浸在戏剧激动人心的情节中了。

senses.en: to be unsuccessful in getting sth that you want or think you should have
senses.zh: 得不到(需要或觉得应有的东西):

ex.en: Some youngsters are taking day jobs and losing out on schooling.
ex.zh: 有些年轻人白天工作而荒废了学业。

ex.en: If things go wrong, I’m the one who’ll lose out.
ex.zh: 如果有什么差错，受损失的将是我。

senses.en: to not get the business you expected or hoped to get, because sb else has got it

ex.en: Small stores are losing out to the big supermarkets.
ex.zh: 小商店的生意都转到了大型超市那里。

senses.en: to spend your time in a relaxed way doing very little
senses.zh: 懒散度日； 游手好闲；在… 转悠:

ex.en: She was always lounging about while the rest of us were working!
ex.zh: 我们工作的时候她总是无所事事！

ex.en: They were lounging around the hotel pool.
ex.zh: 他们正在旅馆的游泳池里消磨时间。

senses.en: to spoil or ruin sth

ex.en: He loused up my promotion chances.
ex.zh: 他使我失去了晋升的机会。

senses.en: to get sth you want by chance

ex.en: I lucked into some free tickets.
ex.zh: 我侥幸弄到了几张免费票。

senses.en: to be very lucky

ex.en: We lucked out in a big way.
ex.zh: 我们走鸿运了。

ex.en: We really lucked out with the weather.
ex.zh: 我们真走运，遇上了好天气。

senses.en: to carry or pull sth large, awkward or heavy from one place to another, or everywhere you go
senses.zh: 提着，拉着(笨重的东西)四处走:

ex.en: Can I leave my bag somewhere? It’s very heavy to lug around.
ex.zh: 我能在什么地方存一下包吗？提着它到处走很重。

senses.en: to make sb feel confident and relaxed, especially so that they do not expect it when sth bad happens
senses.zh: 麻醉某人，使某人失去警惕(而…):

ex.en: Don’t let success in the test lull you into thinking you do not need to work hard.
ex.zh: 不要让这次测验的成功冲昏了头脑，以为你不必下工夫。

senses.en: to give sb a responsibility or a problem that they do not want and cannot get rid of
senses.zh: 迫使负担(职责)；给…添麻烦:

ex.en: I’m sorry you’ve been lumbered with driving me home.
ex.zh: 很抱歉麻烦你开车送我回家。

ex.en: The movie was about sb who sees a murder and then gets lumbered with the dead man’s child.
ex.zh: 这部电影描写的是一位兇杀场面的目击者后来担负起了抚养死去男子的遗孤的事。

senses.en: to put or consider two or more people or things together in the same group
senses.zh: 把… 归併一起(或合起来考虑) :

ex.en: A large number of plants are lumped together under the name of ‘herbs’.
ex.zh: 很多植物归于“草本植物”类。

ex.en: You can’t lump the elderly and the disabled together.
ex.zh: 你不能把上年纪的人和残疾人混为一谈。

senses.en: to feel a strong sexual desire for sb
to have a strong desire to possess or have sth
senses.zh: 对(某事物)有极强的慾望:

ex.en: She was lusting after/for revenge.
ex.zh: 她复仇心切。

senses.en: to take great pleasure in sth that is very pleasant and relaxing
senses.zh: 尽情享受；沉浸在(舒适的环境)里:

ex.en: I luxuriated in a long, hot bath.
ex.zh: 我享受了半天热水浴。

senses.en: to use magic to make sb/sth disappear or appear; to make sb/sth disappear or appear so quickly or suddenly that it seems as if you have used magic
senses.zh: 用魔术使消失﹙或出现﹚；变魔术般地使突然消失﹙或出现﹚:

ex.en: I wish my problems could be just magicked away.
ex.zh: 希望我的难题能像变魔术那样一下子就解决了。

ex.en: Sarah magicked up a wonderful meal in a very short time.
ex.zh: 莎拉像变魔术似的一下子就变出一顿丰盛的饭菜。

senses.en: to send sth to sb by post/mail

ex.en: I mailed off an application the next day.
ex.zh: 我第二天寄出了申请。

senses.en: to send sth to a lot of different people or places at the same time

ex.en: Catalogues will be mailed out next week.
ex.zh: 目录将在下周一齐寄出。

senses.en: to study sth as your main subject at a university or college; to get a degree in that subject
senses.zh: 主修；取得﹙某学科的﹚学位:

ex.en: He majored in chemistry.
ex.zh: 他主修化学。

senses.en: to steal sth and take it away with you

ex.en: Thieves made away with a computer and two televisions.
ex.zh: 小偷偷走了一台电脑和两台电视机。

senses.zh: 不用于进行时) to help to make sth possible; to produce a particular result促成；产生﹙某结果﹚:

ex.en: The two-hour journey to work makes for a long day.
ex.zh: 上班的两小时路程使工作日很漫长。

ex.en: The large print makes for easier reading.
ex.zh: 这大字体便于阅读。

senses.en: to change sb/sth into sth

ex.en: They made the extra bedroom into a bathroom.
ex.zh: 他们把多出的教室改成了浴室。

ex.en: You’re trying to make her into something she isn’t.
ex.zh: 你这是在改变她的本性。

senses.en: to have an impression or an understanding of sb/sth
to hurry or rush away, especially when sb is trying to escape or has stolen sth
senses.zh: 匆忙离开；﹙尤指﹚仓惶逃跑，﹙带某物﹚熘走:

ex.en: The youths made off in a stolen car.
ex.zh: 几个年轻人开着偷来的车熘了。

ex.en: Two boys made off with our bags.
ex.zh: 两个男子偷走了我们的包。

senses.en: used to ask sb how they have managed or survived in a particular situation﹙
senses.zh: 询问是否处理得当﹚应付，过:

senses.en: to claim that sth is true that may not be; to try to make people believe sth
senses.zh: 声称；把……说成；努力使人相信:

ex.en: She made out (that) she was earning a fortune.
ex.zh: 她吹嘘说她赚大钱。

ex.en: Things aren’t as bad as he makes out.
ex.zh: 情况并非像他说的那样糟糕。

senses.en: to manage to see sb/sth or read sth
senses.zh: 看清； 分清； 辨认清楚:

ex.en: I could just make out the shape of a house in the darkness.
ex.zh: 黑暗中我隐约看见房子的外形。

ex.en: Can you make out his handwriting?
ex.zh: 你看得清他写的字吗？

senses.zh: 用于否定句和疑问句) to understand sb/sth; to see the reasons why sth happens or why sb behaves in the way that they do理解；明白；弄懂:

ex.en: She couldn’t make out the expression on his face as he spoke.
ex.zh: 她不明白他说话时为什么有这样的表情。

ex.en: I can’t make her out at all.
ex.zh: 我根本摸不透她的性格。

senses.en: to change sb/sth to give them/it a new appearance; to change sth to give it a new use

ex.en: They decided to make over the whole house when they moved in.
ex.zh: 他们搬家时决定把新居彻底整修一下。

senses.en: the process of improving the appearance of a person or a place﹙

ex.en: She won a complete makeover (=new clothes, hairstyle, etc.) in a competition.
ex.zh: 她在比赛中获得革新形象奖。

senses.en: to legally give sth you own to sb else﹙

ex.en: He made his estate over to his eldest son.
ex.zh: 他把财产传给了他的长子。

ex.en: The government has made a lot of its power over to the regions.
ex.zh: 政府将很多权力下放给了各个行政区。

senses.en: to go in the direction of sb/sth

ex.en: I saw them making towards the exit.
ex.zh: 我看见他们向出口走去。

senses.en: to put substances on your/sb’s eyes, lips and face to make them or yourself attractive or to prepare for an appearance in the theatre, on television, etc.

ex.en: It takes her an hour to make up before going on stage.
ex.zh: 她上台演出前用了一个小时化妆。

ex.en: She spends ages making herself up.
ex.zh: 她没完没了地梳理打扮。

senses.en: wearing coloured substances on the face

ex.en: a heavily made-up face
ex.zh: 浓妆艳抹的脸

ex.en: She’s always carefully made-up.
ex.zh: 她总是精心化妆。

senses.en: [U] substances that people put on their eyes, lips and face to make themselves more attractive, or that actors, etc. use

ex.en: to put on your make-up
ex.zh: 化妆

ex.en: a make-up bag
ex.zh: 化妆包

senses.en: to end a quarrel or a dispute with sb
to invent sth, often in order to deceive sb

ex.en: He was making up stories for the children.
ex.zh: 他在给孩子们编故事。

ex.en: She made up an excuse for being late.
ex.zh: 她为迟到找了个藉口。

senses.en: to plan or arrange sth in detail﹙

ex.en: I’ve mapped out a route for you.
ex.zh: 我给你画出了详细路线。

ex.en: She felt as though her future had been mapped out for her.
ex.zh: 她感觉好像有人为她精心规划了前途。

senses.en: to continue marching; to continue walking quickly
senses.zh: 继续行进；继续快速行走:

ex.en: I tried to speak to her but she just marched on.
ex.zh: 我想和她搭话，可她闷头一个劲儿地走。

senses.en: to move on or pass quickly

ex.en: Time marched on and we still hadn’t finished.
ex.zh: 时间过得飞快，我们还没有完成任务。

senses.en: (of soldiers
senses.zh: 士兵) to march past an important person or building在要员﹙或重要建筑﹚前列队经过；作分列式接受检阅:

ex.en: At 11 o’clock the army began to march past.
ex.zh: 部队在11 点钟开始接受检阅。

senses.en: a ceremony in which soldiers formally march past an important person, etc.
senses.zh: 分列式﹙军人列队通过检阅台﹚

senses.en: to reduce the marks given to sb in an examination, etc.

ex.en: She was marked down for poor spelling.
ex.zh: 她因拼写错误被扣了分。

senses.en: to reduce the price of sth

ex.en: All goods have been marked down by 15%.
ex.zh: 所有商品都打八五折。

senses.en: a reduction in price

ex.en: a markdown of 12%
ex.zh: 减价12%

senses.en: to consider sb a particular type of person
senses.zh: 将某人看作；认定某人是:

ex.en: I had him marked down as a promising player from the start.
ex.zh: 我从一开始就觉得他是个有巨大潜力的运动员。

senses.en: to separate sth by marking a line between it and sth else

ex.en: We’ve marked the playing area off with a white line.
ex.zh: 我们用白线划出了运动场地。

senses.en: to write or draw a mark beside a name or an item on a list, for example, for a particular reason﹙
senses.zh: 在名单上或分项旁﹚ 做记号:

ex.en: The students I want to see are marked off on the list.
ex.zh: 我想见的学生已在名单上做了记号。

senses.en: to make sb or sth different from other people or things
senses.zh: 使与众不同；使有别于其他人﹙ 或事物﹚ :

ex.en: There was something about her which marked her out from the other students.
ex.zh: 她有些地方和其他学生不一样。

senses.en: to draw lines to show the edges of sth
senses.zh: 画出界限；画出边界；用线画出范围:

ex.en: She marked out a circle on the ground.
ex.zh: 她在地上画圈为界。

senses.en: to increase the price of sth

ex.en: Shares were marked up by 8%.
ex.zh: 股票价格上涨了8%。

senses.en: to mark or correct a text

ex.en: The text had already been marked up with corrections (= for printing).
ex.zh: 文本已完成修改﹙准备付印﹚。

senses.en: [usually sing.] the difference between the cost of producing sth and the price it is sold at﹙
senses.zh: 成本价与售价间的﹚差价；加成

senses.en: to marry sb who belongs to a lower social class than your own
senses.zh: 和社会地位较低的人结婚； 下嫁:

ex.en: She thought her son was marrying beneath him.
ex.zh: 她觉得她的儿子的婚姻门不当、户不对。

senses.en: to become a part of a family or a group because you have married sb who belongs to it
senses.zh: 因结婚而成为﹙家庭或团体的﹚成员:

ex.en: She married into a wealthy family.
ex.zh: 她嫁到了富裕人家。

senses.en: to get rid of a daughter or a son by finding a husband or wife for them
senses.zh: 让﹙子女﹚结婚以将其摆脱；把……嫁出；让……娶亲:

ex.en: He had married his daughter off to a man twice her age.
ex.zh: 他把女儿嫁给了年纪比她大一倍的男人。

senses.en: to join up or connect successfully; to make two things or two parts do this﹙
senses.zh: 将两个事物或部份﹚接合；﹙使﹚连接上:

ex.en: The two halves of the structure didn’t marry up.
ex.zh: 这个结构的两半部份接合得不好。

ex.en: He couldn’t marry up the two parts of the lock.
ex.zh: 他锁不上锁。

senses.en: to match; to make two things match﹙

ex.en: The two versions of the story don’t quite marry up.
ex.zh: 这件事的两种说法有出入。

ex.en: The lawyers couldn’t marry up her story with the facts.
ex.zh: 律师们无法使她的说法和事实一致起来。

senses.en: to be very surprised or impressed by sb/sth
senses.zh: 感到惊奇； 大为赞叹:

ex.en: Everyone marvelled at his courage.
ex.zh: 人人都赞叹他有这样的勇气。

ex.en: Massimo marvelled at how quickly he had got used to life in Britain.
ex.zh: 马西莫这么快就适应了英国生活，自己也感到意外。

senses.en: to pretend to be sth that you are not

ex.en: commercial advertisers masquerading as private individuals
ex.zh: 以普通百姓姿态出现的商业广告人员

ex.en: The local paper is full of gossip masquerading as news.
ex.zh: 这份地方报纸尽是些包装成新闻的流言蜚语。

senses.en: to make sb/sth compete with another person or thing
senses.zh: 使与……较量； 使与……竞争:

ex.en: Jobson will be matched against a far more experienced player.
ex.zh: 乔布逊将与经验远远超过他的选手比赛。

ex.en: Match your skill against the experts in our weekly quiz.
ex.zh: 和我们的每周问答比赛高手较量吧。

senses.en: to compare sth to sth else to see how the two things are similar or different

ex.en: We are able to match the details he gave us against the information held on the computer.
ex.zh: 我们可以用他提供的资料，对照一下电脑贮存的信息。

senses.en: (with sth) to be the same or similar﹙

ex.en: Do their names match up with any in our database?
ex.zh: 他们的名称和我们数据库中的吻合吗？

ex.en: The two statements don’t match up.
ex.zh: 这两个说法有出入。

senses.en: to find things or people that are suitable for each other or fit well with each other

ex.en: The agency matched me up with a suitable job.
ex.zh: 职业介绍所给我找了份合适的工作。

ex.en: They were unable to match up his tissue type with any of the possible donors.
ex.zh: 他们无法在可捐赠者之中找到类型与他相配的身体组织。

senses.en: to reach the limit at which nothing more is possible

ex.en: The car maxed out at 180 mph.
ex.zh: 汽车达到了每小时180 英里的最快速度。

ex.en: I just maxed out my credit card.
ex.zh: 我刚用尽了信用卡的限定金额。

senses.en: to compare sb/sth/yourself with somebody or something else

ex.en: The quality of the water is measured against EU standards.
ex.zh: 水质是根据欧盟的标准测定的。

ex.en: We have nothing to measure our performance against.
ex.zh: 我们缺乏了衡量表现的准则。

senses.en: to mark out a particular length on sth such as a piece of cloth

ex.en: She measured off two metres of cloth.
ex.zh: 她量了两米布。

senses.en: to measure the quantity of sth that you need from a larger amount

ex.en: He measured out the ingredients for the cake.
ex.zh: 他称好了做蛋糕的配料。

senses.en: to be of a good enough standard

ex.en: The new assistant didn’t measure up (= he was not good enough to do the job), so we had to replace him.
ex.zh: 新来的助手不称职，我们只好把他换掉。

ex.en: The procedures don’t measure up to today’s standards.
ex.zh: 这些程序不符合现在的标准。

senses.en: to have a meeting with sb

ex.en: The Prime Minister met with other European leaders this morning.
ex.zh: 首相今晨与其他欧洲领导人会晤。

senses.en: to be received or treated by sb in a particular way
senses.zh: 引起……反应；受到某种对待:

ex.en: The proposal met with considerable opposition.
ex.zh: 那项建议受到了相当大的反对。

ex.en: My explanation met with a blank stare.
ex.zh: 我的解释换来一脸茫然。

senses.en: to relax and do very little

ex.en: We could just put on some music and mellow out.
ex.zh: 我们可以放点音乐轻松一下。

senses.en: to disappear gradually; to make sth disappear gradually﹙

ex.en: His anger melted away.
ex.zh: 他的怒气慢慢消了。

ex.en: The crowd dispersed, melting away into the side streets.
ex.zh: 人群散了，慢慢消失在小巷里。

senses.en: to heat sth until it is in a liquid state, usually so that it can be made into sth else

ex.en: Aluminium cans can be melted down and recycled.
ex.zh: 铝罐可回炉再用。

senses.en: [U] [C] a serious accident in which the central part of a structure that produces nuclear energy melts, causing harmful rays to escape
senses.zh: 核反应堆核心熔毁﹙导致核辐射泄漏﹚:

ex.en: A meltdown at the reactor had only just been avoided.
ex.zh: 险些发生核反应堆熔毁事故。

ex.en: () The meltdown on Wall Street caused chaos in markets worldwide.
ex.zh: 华尔街股灾引发全球股市震盪。

senses.en: to gradually become part of sth and difficult to see
senses.zh: 逐渐融入；渐渐与某物成为一体:

ex.en: I tried hard to melt into the background.
ex.zh: 我想方设法使自己消失在幕后。

senses.en: (of a person
senses.zh: 人)to behave quietly when you are with a group of people so that they do not notice you在群体中不起眼

senses.en: to treat sb badly, making them waste time, changing your mind a lot, etc.
senses.zh: 不公正地﹙或随便地﹚看待某人； 团弄:

ex.en: They messed us around so much, I wrote to complain.
ex.zh: 他们对我们不公，我已写信去投诉。

ex.en: I don’t like being messed about.
ex.zh: 我讨厌被人愚弄。

senses.en: to have a sexual relationship with sb
senses.zh: 和某人发生性关系；勾搭；调情

senses.en: to spoil sth;to do sth very badly

ex.en: I was so nervous I totally messed up at the interview.
ex.zh: 我面试时紧张得答非所问。

ex.en: She messed up all our arrangements by arriving late.
ex.zh: 她迟到，把我们的安排全毁了。

senses.en: () confused and upset, especially because of sth bad that has happened to you in the past﹙
senses.zh: 因过去的事﹚困惑而苦恼的，心烦的:

ex.en: He’s just a messed-up kid.
ex.zh: 这孩子只是受了惊吓。

senses.en: to do or say sth that might annoy a particular person, as they may react in a violent or dangerous way
senses.zh: 激怒某人；激某人﹙做危险的事﹚:

ex.en: I wouldn’t mess with Frank if I were you.
ex.zh: 我要是你就不会去惹弗兰克。

senses.en: to have or try to have a sexual relationship with sb﹙
senses.zh: 企图﹚和某人发生性关系

senses.en: to give sb a punishment,etc.

ex.en: Schools should not mete out physical punishment to children.
ex.zh: 学校不应该体罚学生。

ex.en: Severe penalties were meted out to the offenders.
ex.zh: 违例者受到了严惩。

senses.en: to prevent sth; to make it difficult for sth to happen

ex.en: Lack of funds militated against the success of the campaign.
ex.zh: 资金短缺使这场运动难以成功。

senses.en: used to warn sb to be careful

ex.en: Mind out! You nearly knocked me off my bike!
ex.zh: 看着点！你差点把我从自行车上撞下来！

ex.en: I’ve got you fish and chips. Mind out for the bones!
ex.zh: 我给你弄了炸鱼薯条。当心鱼刺！

senses.en: ) used to tell sb to move so that you or sb else can pass

ex.en: Mind out Joe — you’re in the way!
ex.zh: 乔，请让一下─你挡路啦！

senses.en: to care for sb; to make sure that sb/sth has everything necessary

ex.en: She felt it was her vocation to minister to the sick.
ex.zh: 她觉得照料病人是她的天职。

ex.en: Servants ministered to his needs.
ex.zh: 仆人们服侍他。

senses.en: to study another subject as well as your main subject at a university or college

ex.en: He minored in Art History.
ex.zh: 他辅修了艺术史。

senses.en: to lose an opportunity to benefit from sth or enjoy yourself, by not doing sth or taking part in an activity

ex.en: I felt I missed out because I didn’t go to college.
ex.zh: 我觉得我因为没有上大学而失去了机会。

ex.en: She missed out on the school trip.
ex.zh: 她错过了学校旅行。

senses.en: to not include sb/sth either deliberately or by accident﹙
senses.zh: 有意或意外地﹚不包括……在内，遗漏:

ex.en: Have I missed anybody out?
ex.zh: 我有没有漏掉谁？

ex.en: You’ve missed out the most important piece of information! (= you haven’t mentioned it)
ex.zh: 你忘了最重要的信息！

senses.en: to cover sth such as glass with small drops of water so that you cannot see through it

ex.en: The inside of the car was beginning to mist up.
ex.zh: 汽车内侧开始蒙上雾气了。

ex.en: The windows were misted up.
ex.zh: 窗户上蒙了一层水气。

senses.en: to think wrongly that sb/sth is sb/sth else

ex.en: I mistook him for his brother.
ex.zh: 我把他当成他兄弟了。

ex.en: The toy could easily be mistaken for a real gun.
ex.zh: 这支玩具枪几可乱真。

senses.en: to combine one substance with others, especially in cooking﹙
senses.zh: 尤指烹调时﹚掺入，和入，使与……混合:

ex.en: Mix the eggs in slowly.
ex.zh: 慢慢地把鸡蛋和进去。

ex.en: Mix a little cream into the sauce.
ex.zh: 在调味酱里掺一点奶油。

senses.en: to make sb unable to think clearly or understand what is happening
senses.zh: 把某人搞煳涂；使弄不清楚:

ex.en: Now you’ve mixed me up completely! I’m really confused.
ex.zh: 你现在把我彻底搞懵了！我实在是弄不懂了。

ex.en: He got mixed up and caught the wrong train.
ex.zh: 他稀里煳涂地上错了火车。

senses.en: () confused because of social or emotional problems

ex.en: She’s a very mixed-up kid.
ex.zh: 这女孩十分迷茫。

senses.en: to think wrongly that sb/sth is sb/sth else; to be unable to distinguish between two or more people or things

ex.en: You’re mixing me up with my brother.
ex.zh: 你把我当成我兄弟了。

ex.en: The hospital was accused of mixing up the babies’ name tags.
ex.zh: 有人指控医院把婴儿的名牌弄混了。

senses.en: to think wrongly that sb/sth is sb/sth else; to be unable to distinguish between two or more people or things

ex.en: My bag got mixed up with somebody else’s at the airport.
ex.zh: 我的包在机场和别人的弄混了。

ex.en: People who are colour-blind usually get red and green mixed up.
ex.zh: 色盲的人通常区分不了红色和绿色。

senses.en: to change the order or arrangement of things in a confused or untidy way

ex.en: I’d sorted those papers out and now you’ve mixed them all up again.
ex.zh: 我本来把文件整理好了，可现在你又弄乱了。

ex.en: My letters have all been mixed up with yours.
ex.zh: 我的信和你的全混在一起了。

senses.en: a mistake that causes confusion; a situation that is full of confusion

ex.en: There was a mix-up over the tickets.
ex.zh: 这些票弄混了。

senses.en: to be/become involved in sth dangerous or illegal
senses.zh: 卷入，牵涉进﹙危险或非法的事﹚:

ex.en: He would never have got mixed up in anything criminal.
ex.zh: 他决不会参与任何犯罪的事的。

ex.en: How did you get mixed up in all this?
ex.zh: 你是如何被牵连进这一切的？

senses.en: to be/become friendly with or involved with sb dangerous or dishonest
senses.zh: 和﹙危险或不诚实的人﹚来往；与……厮混:

ex.en: I’ll never understand how she got mixed up with Phil.
ex.zh: 我永远也搞不明白她是如何跟菲尔鬼混上的。

ex.en: He was mixed up with the wrong crowd for a while.
ex.zh: 他和一些不三不四的人交往过一阵。

senses.en: to compete with sb; to argue or fight with sb
senses.zh: 和……较量；与某人吵架﹙ 或打架﹚ :

ex.en: He’ll be mixing it with the world’s best players.
ex.zh: 他将和世界级好手较量。

ex.en: He can mix it with the best of them.
ex.zh: 他能够和他们中最好的一比高低。

senses.en: to meet and spend time with people in a friendly way

ex.en: She loves mixing it with the rich and famous.
ex.zh: 她喜欢结交上层人物。

senses.en: to produce a copy of sth that is going to be made, so that it can be tested or people can see what it will be like

ex.en: We mocked up the front page to see how it would look.
ex.zh: 我们把头版编排出来以便看一下效果。

senses.en: a copy of sth that is produced to show people what it will be like, or to test it
senses.zh: 实尺寸模型；实物复制品:

ex.en: a mock-up of the next day’s front page
ex.zh: 第二天头版的版面样排

senses.en: to make or create sth that looks or behaves like sth else; to take sb, especially sb you like, as an example and copy them

ex.en: The house was modelled on a French chateau.
ex.zh: 这房子是模仿一座法国大别墅建造的。

ex.en: He modelled the main character on his friend.
ex.zh: 他的这个主要人物是以他的朋友为原型的。

senses.en: to behave in a silly way; to touch or change sth in a careless way

ex.en: They were monkeying around in class.
ex.zh: 当时他们在课堂上捣乱。

ex.en: He’s monkeyed about with the original words of the song.
ex.zh: 他改动歌词闹着玩儿。

senses.en: to spend time doing nothing in particular

ex.en: We went into town and mooched about for a while.
ex.zh: 我们到城里逛了会儿街。

ex.en: They spent an hour mooching around the shops.
ex.zh: 他们花了一个小时逛商店。

senses.en: to spend time doing nothing in particular, often because you are feeling unhappy﹙
senses.zh: 无精打采地﹚闲逛，消磨时光:

ex.en: He mooned around the streets, hoping to see Anna.
ex.zh: 他在街上四处徘徊，希望见到安娜。

senses.en: to spend your time dreamily thinking about sb that you love

ex.en: He spends most of his time mooning over Helen.
ex.zh: 他大部份时间都在痴想着海伦。

senses.en: to clean up liquid or remove liquid from somewhere, using sth that absorbs it

ex.en: I always have to mop up after he’s had a shower.
ex.zh: 他冲完淋浴我总得擦乾净水迹。

ex.en: Can you mop up the water on the bathroom floor?
ex.zh: 请擦掉浴室地板上的水好吗？

senses.en: to use up all of sth

ex.en: The new factory should mop up the pool of surplus labour.
ex.zh: 新工厂应该把剩余的劳动力全用上。

senses.en: to take control of sth

ex.en: The company started mopping up smaller firms.
ex.zh: 这家公司开始兼併较小的公司。

senses.en: to get rid of the last few people who continue to oppose you; to finish tasks that remain
senses.zh: 消灭﹙残敌﹚；完成﹙余下的工作﹚；收尾:

ex.en: The army mopped up some isolated pockets of resistance.
ex.zh: 部队剿灭了一些孤立的抵抗势力。

ex.en: There are a few things to mop up before we go.
ex.zh: 我们走之前还有几件事要做。

senses.en: to walk about a place in an unhappy way, with no particular purpose﹙

ex.en: He’s been moping about all day.
ex.zh: 他百无聊赖地转悠了一整天。

ex.en: You spend too much time moping around the house.
ex.zh: 你闲居的时间太多了。

senses.en: to increase gradually in size or quantity
senses.zh: 逐渐增加，上升﹙至某尺寸或数量等﹚:

ex.en: The paperwork soon mounts up if you don’t deal with it immediately.
ex.zh: 不及时处理，文案工作很快就攒成堆了。

ex.en: My debts have mounted up to over a thousand dollars.
ex.zh: 我积欠债款超过了一千元。

senses.zh: (常用于进行时) to give your opinion about sb/sth loudly; to complain loudly about sb/sth大发议论；大吵大闹:

ex.en: I could hear him mouthing off about how they should have won.
ex.zh: 我听见他大谈特谈他们本应如何取胜的。

ex.en: She was mouthing off at all the other drivers on the road.
ex.zh: 她扯着嗓门责骂所有其他路过的司机。

senses.en: to move from one side of sth to the other
senses.zh: 从一边移到另一边； 横过:

ex.en: He moved across to the window and looked out.
ex.zh: 他走到对面的窗前向外张望。

senses.en: to advance or develop, often after there has been a delay﹙

ex.en: The project is moving ahead again now.
ex.zh: 这个项目现在又继续进行了。

senses.en: to move faster than sb/sth; to develop more quickly than sb/sth else
senses.zh: 比……移动得快；比……进展快；超过:

ex.en: ‘Speed up!’ he said, moving ahead of her.
ex.zh: “快点！”他说着便冲到了她前面。

ex.en: Our foreign competitors are moving ahead of us.
ex.zh: 外国竞争对手走在我们前面。

senses.en: to go forward

ex.en: The convoy of cars was moving slowly along the road.
ex.zh: 车队在公路上缓慢行进。

senses.en: to leave a particular place or go to a new position; tomake sb do this﹙

ex.en: Move along now. You’re blocking the entrance.
ex.zh: 往前走走吧。你挡住门啦。

ex.en: The police arrived to move the demonstrators along.
ex.zh: 警察到场让示威者向前移动。

senses.en: to keep moving from one place toanother

ex.en: Use the mouse to move around the screen.
ex.zh: 用鼠标在屏幕上来回移动。

ex.en: I have to move around a lot with my job.
ex.zh: 我的工作需要经常到处走。

senses.en: to move sb/sth fromone place to another﹙

ex.en: It’s not fair to keep moving the children around from school to school.
ex.zh: 要孩子经常转学不好。

ex.en: The chair is light and easy to move about.
ex.zh: 椅子很轻，便于搬动。

senses.en: to move in a circle around sth that isblocking your path

ex.en: She moved round the table to open the window.
ex.zh: 她绕过桌子去开窗。

senses.en: to put sb/sth to one sideaway from the centre of a place, usually to makeroom for sb/sth else
senses.zh: 把……移到一边﹙ 腾出地方﹚；移开:

ex.en: We moved the tables aside so that we could dance.
ex.zh: 我们把桌子都搬到边上以便跳舞。

senses.en: to leave the place where you live togo and live in another place

ex.en: All her friends have moved away from the area.
ex.zh: 她的朋友都迁离这地区了。

senses.en: to leave the place or position youare in and go to another; to take sth from oneplace or position and put it in another﹙
senses.zh: 使﹚改变位置；离开；把……搬走:

ex.en: Move away from the window in case anyone sees you.
ex.zh: 离开窗户，别让人看见你。

ex.en: Can you move the scissors away from the baby?
ex.zh: 把宝宝那儿的剪刀拿走好吗？

senses.en: to stop doing, followingor believing sth
senses.zh: 停止做；不再顺应﹙或相信﹚:

ex.en: The party seems to be moving away from its original aims.
ex.zh: 这个政党似乎正在背离其原来的宗旨。

senses.en: to go, or tomove sth, to a new position at a distance awayfrom the front or behind sb/sth﹙

ex.en: He moved back a few steps.
ex.zh: 他后退了几步。

ex.en: She moved her chair back from the fire.
ex.zh: 她把椅子从炉火旁往后挪一挪。

senses.en: to go, or to move sth,to the place or position it was in before﹙

ex.en: His eyes moved back to her face.
ex.zh: 他的目光回到了她的脸上。

ex.en: It took a long time to move the furniture back after the party.
ex.zh: 聚会之后花了很长时间才把傢具摆放回原位。

senses.en: (of a level or an amount
senses.zh: 水平或数量) to decrease降低；减少:

ex.en: Prices move up and down according to demand.
ex.zh: 价格随着需求浮动。

senses.en: to movefrom a higher position to a lower one

ex.en: I watched her move nervously down the slope.
ex.zh: 我看着她战战兢兢地下坡。

senses.en: to move sb/sth from a higher position to alower one

ex.en: Move the boxes down from the top of the wardrobe.
ex.zh: 把衣柜顶的那些箱子拿下来。

senses.en: to go,or to make sth go, to a place or position that is infront﹙

ex.en: The car began to move forward slowly.
ex.zh: 汽车开始慢慢向前开动了。

senses.en: todevelop, or to make sth develop, towards a goodresult﹙
senses.zh: 使﹚朝有利方向发展；促进:

ex.en: It’s time to move this project forward.
ex.zh: 是进一步开发这个项目的时候了。

senses.en: to move, or to make sth move,towards the future﹙

ex.en: The company must keep moving forward.
ex.zh: 公司必须不断发展。

ex.en: The story then moves forward to 1999.
ex.zh: 故事情节接着就发展到1999年。

senses.en: (on sb/sth) to move towards sb/sth,especially in a threatening way, or to make a dangeroussituation calm
senses.zh: 向……逼近；进逼；平息﹙危险局势﹚:

ex.en: I moved in close and stuck the gun in his back.
ex.zh: 我逼近他，用枪顶住他的后背。

ex.en: The police moved in to control the crowd.
ex.zh: 警察开了过来控制人群。

senses.en: toarrive and begin work, especially when peopledon’t really want you there﹙
senses.zh: 违背人愿地﹚开进并动工:

ex.en: The developers moved in and built a housing estate in the grounds of the old house.
ex.zh: 开发商开了进来，在旧房子的地皮上建造了一个住宅区。

senses.en: (on sth) to begin to try to have controlof or responsibility for a company, a project, etc.
senses.zh: 试图控制，企图接管﹙公司、项目等﹚:

ex.en: They are moving in on another drugs company.
ex.zh: 他们正试图控制另一家药品公司。

senses.en: to go to a new houseand begin to live there

ex.en: How soon can you move in?
ex.zh: 你多久能搬到新家？

ex.en: When are you moving into your new flat?
ex.zh: 你什么时候搬到新公寓？

senses.en: to startliving with sb, especially a partner
senses.zh: 开始和﹙伴侣等﹚生活；开始同居:

ex.en: They’ve decided to move in together.
ex.zh: 他们决定同居。

senses.en: 1=MOVE IN,MOVE INTO STH
tostart to be involved in a new area of activity orbusiness
senses.zh: 涉足，开始从事﹙新的活动或工作﹚:

ex.en: The company is looking to move into new markets.
ex.zh: 公司正打算打入新市场。

ex.en: After teaching for ten years he moved into publishing.
ex.zh: 执桝十年后他干起了出版工作。

senses.en: to develop or advance into anew position, stage, etc.
senses.zh: 发展到，进入﹙新的位置或阶段等﹚:

ex.en: The project is now moving into its second year.
ex.zh: 这项工程正步入第二个年度。

ex.en: The team has moved into fourth place after their victory.
ex.zh: 这个队获胜后上升到第四名。

senses.en: to take sb/sth and putthem/it in a new place

ex.en: We’ve moved the phone into the hall.
ex.zh: 我们把电话移到了门厅。

ex.en: The doctors at the hospital have moved my father into a room on his own.
ex.zh: 医院里的医生把我父亲转到了单间。

senses.en: (especially of avehicle
senses.zh: 尤指车辆) to start a journey; to begin tomove出发； 开动； 启动:

ex.en: Check your mirrors before you move off.
ex.zh: 开车前注意看看反光镜。

senses.en: to leavethe place where you are; to remove sb/sth from aparticular place

ex.en: Farmers are rapidly moving off the land.
ex.zh: 农民正迅速离开土地。

ex.en: Can you move your car off the pavement please?
ex.zh: 请把你的车开离人行道好吗？

senses.en: to continue your journey after stoppingfor a short while; to leave the place whereyou are and go to a new place﹙
senses.zh: 短暂停留后﹚继续行进；离开；走开:

ex.en: After a few minutes, the bus moved on again.
ex.zh: 几分钟之后，公共汽车又往前开了。

ex.en: The police told them to move on and go home!
ex.zh: 警察令他们离开那里回家去！

senses.en: to leave yourhome and go to live somewhere else

ex.en: The lodger moved out yesterday.
ex.zh: 房客昨天搬走了。

ex.en: He wants to move out of London.
ex.zh: 他想搬出伦敦。

senses.en: to leave a particular place,area or situation

ex.en: We watched the boat moving out of the harbour.
ex.zh: 我们看着那艘船驶离了港湾。

ex.en: The country is moving out of recession.
ex.zh: 这个国家正从衰退中复苏。

senses.en: to stopbeing involved in a particular activity or area ofbusiness
senses.zh: 退出，不再从事﹙某活动或工作﹚:

ex.en: Many people have been forced to move out of farming.
ex.zh: 很多人被迫放弃了耕作。

senses.en: togo forward slowly across a surface; to make sthdo this﹙
senses.zh: 使﹚ 缓慢走过﹙ 平面﹚ :

ex.en: The tank adapts to the ground it is moving over.
ex.zh: 坦克适应了它碾着的地面。

ex.en: Just move the brush lightly over the paper.
ex.zh: 把画笔在纸上轻轻描画就行啦。

senses.en: to pass in front of sb/sth

ex.en: He moved past her into the lounge.
ex.zh: 他在她面前走过，进了候机厅。

senses.en: to approach sb/sth

ex.en: She began to run as the car moved towards her.
ex.zh: 汽车向她开过来时她跑了起来。

senses.zh: (常用于进行时) toprepare to do or achieve sth; to approach or movenearer to sth准备做﹙或取得﹚；接近；靠近:

ex.en: We are moving towards a better understanding of the situation.
ex.zh: 我们正逐渐了解这一状况。

ex.en: Is the group moving towards finding a solution?
ex.zh: 这个团体有望找到解决方法吗？

senses.en: (of a rate, a level or an amount
senses.zh: 比率、水平或数量) to increase增长；上升:

ex.en: What will we do if interest rates move up?
ex.zh: 如果利率上调，我们该怎么办？

senses.en: to move, or to make sb move, to a higher level, grade or class﹙
senses.zh: 使﹚升级，进入较高的班级:

ex.en: She’s been moved up into the Advanced class.
ex.zh: 她被调到了高级班。

senses.en: to move from a lower to a higher position; to make sb/sth do this﹙

ex.en: Hold the ladder tightly and move up a rung at a time.
ex.zh: 抓紧梯子一级一级地往上爬。

ex.en: We watched the group moving up the hill.
ex.zh: 我们看着这队人登上山冈。

senses.en: to kill sb, often large numbers of people, with a gun﹙

ex.en: The demonstrators were mown down by the soldiers.
ex.zh: 示威者被士兵开枪打死了。

senses.en: (of a vehicle or a driver
senses.zh: 车辆或司机) to kill/hit sb,often because the driver has been driving carelessly or dangerously压死；撞倒:

ex.en: A mother and her two children were mown down by joyriders.
ex.zh: 母子三人被偷车兜风的人撞死了。

senses.en: to treat sb badly, making them waste time, changing your mind a lot, etc.

ex.en: I’m sick of being mucked about by employers.
ex.zh: 对于雇主们的耍弄，我觉得很厌倦。

senses.en: to keep touching,moving or changing sth in an annoying way

ex.en: Who’s been mucking about with my computer?
ex.zh: 谁摆弄过我的电脑啦？

ex.en: Don’t muck around with the words of the song — I think they’re fine.
ex.zh: 别再改来改去了─我觉得歌词已经不错。

senses.en: to join in with other people in order to complete a task

ex.en: If we all muck in, we’ll soon get the job finished.
ex.zh: 如果我们大伙一块儿干，很快就能把活儿干完。

senses.en: to share food, accommodation,costs, etc. with other people

ex.en: Money was short, but we all mucked in together.
ex.zh: 钱不够用，但我们都同舟共济。

senses.en: to clean the place where an animal lives, especially a horse

ex.en: It’s your turn to muck out today.
ex.zh: 今天轮到你清扫马了。

senses.en: to do sth very badly; to spoil sth

ex.en: This is your last chance, so don’t muck it up.
ex.zh: 这是你最后的机会，可别弄糟了。

ex.en: Her surprise visit totally mucked up my plans.
ex.zh: 她的意外到访完全破坏了我的计划。

senses.en: to make sth dirty

ex.en: Take your shoes off! You’re mucking up my floor!
ex.zh: 脱掉鞋子！你踩脏我的地板了！

senses.en: to make sth untidy

ex.en: Stop that, you’re mucking up my hair.
ex.zh: 快住手，你把我的头发搞乱了。

senses.en: to continue living or doing sth with no clear purpose or plan

ex.en: We muddle along from day to day.
ex.zh: 我们一天天地混日子。

senses.en: to achieve your aims although you are not efficient, do not know what you are doing, do not have the right equipment,etc.

ex.en: I’ll muddle through somehow.
ex.zh: 我会设法应付过去的。

senses.en: to make sb confused

ex.en: I won’t explain how this works now — it might muddle you up.
ex.zh: 我现在先不讲解工作原理─ 那样会使你摸不着头脑的。

ex.en: You’re muddling me up!
ex.zh: 你把我搞煳涂啦！

senses.en: to confuse one person or thing with another; to think that sb/sth is sb/sth else

ex.en: He muddled up our passports and gave me back the wrong one.
ex.zh: 他把我们的护照搞混了，把别人的发还给了我。

ex.en: I keep muddling her up with her sister.
ex.zh: 我总是把她当成她姐姐。

senses.en: to confuse one person or thing with another

ex.en: I always get the twins muddled up.
ex.zh: 我总是分不清这对双胞胎。

senses.en: to quickly learn sth, especially sth that you should already know, before an exam, etc.
senses.zh: 临时学习；﹙考试前﹚临阵磨枪:

ex.en: He spent the whole night mugging up for the exam.
ex.zh: 考试前他熬了一夜临阵磨枪。

ex.en: I’d better mug up on the subject before I meet her.
ex.zh: 和她见面前我最好赶快了解一下这个课题。

senses.en: to think about or consider sth for a long time before you decide to do sth

ex.en: I’ve been mulling over what you said last night.
ex.zh: 我昨晚一直在琢磨你的话。

senses.en: to get involved in a situation that you have no right to be involved in, especially sth that will give you an advantage or a profit
senses.zh: 强行干涉，粗暴干涉﹙从而为自己谋利﹚；捞﹙好处﹚:

ex.en: I don’t want Matt muscling in on our deal.
ex.zh: 我不想让马特插手我们的交易。

senses.en: to make sth look untidy

ex.en: My skirt got mussed up when I sat down.
ex.zh: 我一坐下就把裙子压皱了。

senses.en: to find the courage, strength,etc. that you need in order to do sth difficult or unpleasant

ex.en: She could barely muster up the strength to get out of bed.
ex.zh: 她几乎连起床的力气都没有了。

senses.en: , , )used by some people to tell sb rudely to go away and stop annoying them

ex.en: Just naff off and leave me alone!
ex.zh: 磙蛋，别烦我！

senses.en: to keep complaining to sb about their behaviour; to keep asking sb to do sth
senses.zh: 无休止地抱怨；不断指责；唠叨:

ex.en: He keeps nagging at me to get more exercise.
ex.zh: 他没完没了地叫我多做运动。

senses.en: to worry or irritate you continuously

ex.en: The suspicion that she was lying continued to nag at me.
ex.zh: 我怀疑她撒谎，这使我烦闷不已。

senses.en: to force sb to state exactly what they think,what they intend to do, etc.
senses.zh: 迫使准确说出﹙想法或想做之事等﹚:

ex.en: He says he’ll come, but I can’t nail him down to a date.
ex.zh: 他说要来，但我无法让他敲定日期。

senses.en: to give sb/sth the name of sb/sth else that you like or admire, for example a family member or a famous person or place

ex.en: We named her after her grandmother.
ex.zh: 我们给她取了她祖母的名字。

ex.en: The Miller fire was named for the canyon in which it began.
ex.zh: “米勒大火”是以那条起火的峡谷命名的。

senses.en: to gradually reduce the number of possibilities
senses.zh: 逐渐把﹙可能性﹚减小﹙到﹚；缩小范围:

ex.en: I’ve narrowed the list of candidates down to three.
ex.zh: 我把候选人名单缩减到三人。

senses.en: to make yourself warm and comfortable by moving close to sb

ex.en: Jamie nestled up to his mother on the sofa.
ex.zh: 杰米在沙发上偎依着母亲。

senses.en: to eat sth by taking very small bites

ex.en: The mouse nibbled at the peanuts.
ex.zh: 老鼠一点一点地啃着花生。

ex.en: You’ve only nibbled at your lunch.
ex.zh: 你午饭只吃了几口。

senses.en: to show a slight interest in sth

ex.en: Several companies have nibbled at our offer.
ex.zh: 若干公司表示对我们的出价有兴趣。

senses.en: to gradually reduce or use up the total amount of sth

ex.en: Inflation began to nibble away at their savings.
ex.zh: 通货膨胀开始蚕食他们的存款。

senses.en: to remove a part of sth by squeezing it with your fingers, cutting it quickly with scissors,etc.

ex.en: She nipped off the dead leaves.
ex.zh: 她剪掉了枯叶。

senses.en: to fall asleep

ex.en: She nodded off in front of the television.
ex.zh: 她在电视机前睡着了。

senses.en: to go around trying to find out sth about sb/sth, particularly when you should not do this

ex.en: I’m just nosing about for clues.
ex.zh: 我正在寻找线索。

senses.en: to defeat sb by a small amount, for example in a race or an election

ex.en: She was nosed out of first place by her old rival.
ex.zh: 她被老对手以微弱优势击败丢掉了冠军。

senses.en: to achieve a win or a high score

ex.en: He notched up ten points in the first five minutes of the game.
ex.zh: 他在比赛开始后的五分钟里得了十分。

senses.en: to write sth down so that you will remember it

ex.en: The class noted down every word she said.
ex.zh: 全班学生把她说的每个字都记了下来。

senses.en: to include sb/sth in a particular group

ex.en: I number her among my closest friends.
ex.zh: 我把她当成我最亲密的朋友之一。

ex.en: He is numbered among the world’s top experts.
ex.zh: 他被归入世界顶尖高手的行列。

senses.en: to press your head, face, etc. against sb/sth to show affection or keep warm, etc.﹙

ex.en: He nuzzled up to his mother with a happy sigh.
ex.zh: 他依偎着母亲满意地舒了口气。

senses.en: to say that you disagree with, disapprove of or oppose sth
senses.zh: 不同意；不赞成； 反对:

ex.en: Many local people object to the building of the new airport.
ex.zh: 很多当地的居民反对修建新机场。

ex.en: I really object to being charged for parking at the hospital.
ex.zh: 我坚决反对医院收取停车费。

senses.en: to go against what people believe is morally right

ex.en: The film offends against good taste.
ex.zh: 这部电影品位不高。

senses.en: to give sth to God

ex.en: She offered up a prayer for her husband’s safe return.
ex.zh: 她祈求上帝保佑丈夫平安回来。

senses.en: (into/onto sth) to become wider or bigger; to become more open and not enclosed by anything
senses.zh: 变宽； 变大； 变得开阔:

ex.en: The valley opened out in front of us.
ex.zh: 宽阔的山谷在我们面前展开。

ex.en: The narrow lane opened out into a field.
ex.zh: 狭窄的小路尽头是一大片地。

senses.en: to become or to make sth possible, available or able to be reached﹙
senses.zh: 使某事物﹚ 成为可能， 可得到， 可达到:

ex.en: If you have good qualifications, a whole range of possibilities open up for you.
ex.zh: 如果资历足够，发展的机会就会很多。

ex.en: The whole region has been opened up for trade by the new rail link.
ex.zh: 新铁路线把整个地区的贸易搞活了。

senses.en: to start a new business

ex.en: The company are opening up a new factory in Wales.
ex.zh: 公司将在威尔士开一家新工厂。

senses.en: to begin business for the day﹙

ex.en: If you’re feeling tired this morning, I’ll open up (the store).
ex.zh: 你今天早上要是觉得累，就由我来开店吧。

senses.en: (usually in sport
senses.zh: 通常用于体育运动) to develop or start to happen; to produce sth or make sth start to happen发展；﹙使﹚开始发生，出现:

ex.en: An increasing gap is opening up between the achievements of girls and boys in exams.
ex.zh: 女生和男生的考试成绩差距开始拉远。

ex.en: United have opened up a three-point lead after five games.
ex.zh: 联队在五局比赛后以三分领先。

senses.en: to become wider; to make sth wider, especially sth that has been closed﹙

ex.en: Coughing might open up your wound.
ex.zh: 咳嗽有可能震裂你的伤口。

ex.en: She wished the floor would open up and swallow her (= for example, because she felt very embarrassed about sth).
ex.zh: 她恨不得地上开个口子把她吞下去﹙因受窘为难等﹚。

senses.en: to choose sth; to make a decision about sth

ex.en: More students are now opting for computer science courses.
ex.zh: 现在有较多的学生选修计算机科学课程。

ex.en: You can stay in the main hotel or opt for one of the bungalows near the beach.
ex.zh: 你可以住在旅馆主楼或海滩附近其中一座平房。

senses.en: to choose to take part in sth

ex.en: We offer a pension plan, and all staff have the chance to opt in.
ex.zh: 我们实行养老金计划，所有职员均可参加。

ex.en: The government decided to opt into the new European treaty.
ex.zh: 政府决定加入新的欧洲条约。

senses.en: to choose not to take part in sth

ex.en: You can opt out of the company’s pension plan.
ex.zh: 你可以选择不参加公司的养老金计划。

senses.en: (of a school or a hospital in Britain
senses.zh: 英国学校或医院) to choose not to be under the control of the local authority选择不受地方当局管理:

ex.en: A majority of parents were in favour of opting out.
ex.zh: 大多数家长赞成脱离地方当局管理。

senses.en: the act of choosing not to take part in sth
(in Britain
senses.zh: 英国) the action of a school or a hospital that decides to manage its own money and is therefore no longer controlled by a local authority﹙学校或医院从地方当局管理的﹚退出，脱离:

ex.en: Nurses and health workers voted against the opt-out.
ex.zh: 护士和保健员表决反对脱离地方当局管理。

senses.en: to keep on telling sb to do things in an unpleasant way﹙

ex.en: Stop ordering me around!
ex.zh: 别再使唤我了！

ex.en: Even as a child he ordered his friends about.
ex.zh: 他从小就爱支使朋友。

senses.en: to telephone and buy a meal from a restaurant that cooks the food and brings it to your home
senses.zh: 打电话让餐馆等送外卖食物；电话订餐:

ex.en: I’m too tired to cook — let’s order in.
ex.zh: 我累得不想做饭了─我们叫外卖吧。

ex.en: Let’s order in Chinese tonight.
ex.zh: 咱们今晚打电话要中餐外卖吧。

senses.en: to tell sb to leave sth such as a bus, a train, etc.

ex.en: The driver ordered the boys off for messing around on the bus.
ex.zh: 几个男孩在公共汽车上捣乱被司机赶了下去。

senses.en: to telephone and buy a meal from a restaurant that cooks the food and brings it to you
senses.zh: 打电话让餐馆等送外卖食物；电话订餐； 叫外卖:

ex.en: We could order out for a Chinese.
ex.zh: 我们可以打电话要份外卖中餐。

senses.en: to admit that you are the person responsible for sth that has happened
senses.zh: 承担﹙事故等的﹚责任；承认﹙错误﹚:

ex.en: Nobody owned up to breaking the window.
ex.zh: 没有人承认把窗户打破了。

senses.en: to measure sth by taking regular steps across it

ex.en: She paced out the length of the room.
ex.zh: 她步测了屋子的长度。

senses.en: to put sth into a box,cupboard, etc. when you are no longer using it﹙
senses.zh: 用后﹚收拾好；把东西装进盒子里﹙或柜子里等﹚:

ex.en: We packed away the picnic things and put them in the car.
ex.zh: 我们把野餐用品装好放到车里。

senses.en: ) to eat a lot of sth
to attract large numbers of people to a show, a play, etc.

ex.en: The film is still packing in the crowds.
ex.zh: 这部电影依然吸引着大批观众。

senses.en: to do a lot of things, see a lot of people, etc. in a limited period of time
senses.zh: 把要做的事情﹙或要见的人等﹚挤在﹙有限的时间里﹚:

ex.en: She managed to pack a lot of sightseeing into three days.
ex.zh: 她设法用三天时间游览了许多地方。

ex.en: We packed in a lot yesterday afternoon.
ex.zh: 我们昨天下午做了很多事情。

senses.en: to put a lot of things or people into a limited space
senses.zh: 把大量的东西﹙或人﹚挤在﹙有限的空间里﹚ :

ex.en: Somehow we managed to pack everyone in.
ex.zh: 我们设法让所有的人都挤了进去。

senses.en: to send sb away,especially because you do not want them with you

ex.en: She was packed off to boarding school at the age of eight.
ex.zh: 她八岁时就被送到寄宿学校。

ex.en: He packed the children off to bed.
ex.zh: 他打发孩子们去睡觉了。

senses.en: () very full

ex.en: The town is packed out with tourists in the summer.
ex.zh: 夏天城里游人如织。

ex.en: a packed-out stadium
ex.zh: 挤得水泄不通的体育场

senses.en: to put your possessions,equipment, etc. into bags or boxes before you leave a place

ex.en: It’s time to pack up and go home now.
ex.zh: 该收拾行李回家了。

ex.en: All our things were packed up waiting to be moved.
ex.zh: 我们把所有的东西都打包好了等着运走。

senses.en: to wrap sth and make it into a parcel so that you can send it somewhere

ex.en: She packaged up his books and mailed them to him.
ex.zh: 她把他的书包好，邮寄给了他。

senses.en: to put soft material into a piece of clothing in order to change its shape
senses.zh: 给﹙衣服﹚加衬埝﹙或软填料﹚:

ex.en: She padded the costume out with foam.
ex.zh: 她给戏装填衬了泡沫塑料。

senses.en: to make sth, such as a book, an article,a speech, etc., longer by adding unnecessary material﹙
senses.zh: 用多余的话﹚拉长﹙书、文章、讲话等﹚；充篇幅:

ex.en: I padded out the article with lots of quotations.
ex.zh: 我用大量引文扩充了文章。

senses.en: to turn the pages of a book, a magazine, etc. and look at them without reading them in detail

ex.en: She paged through the report looking for her name.
ex.zh: 她翻阅报告查找自己的名字。

senses.en: ) to cover sth, such as a mark, part of a picture, etc. by putting paint on top of it so that no one can see it

ex.en: The markings on the plane had been hurriedly painted out.
ex.zh: 飞机上的标志被匆匆涂抹掉了。

senses.en: to cover sth with a layer of paint

ex.en: We’ll have to paint over the dirty marks on the wall.
ex.zh: 我们得用油漆把墙上的污斑涂抹掉。

ex.en: I don’t like the way the painting has turned out so I’ll just paint over it.
ex.zh: 我不喜欢这幅画的效果，我就乾脆在上面再画。

senses.en: to paint sth, decorating it in a bright, attractive way

ex.en: Their house had been painted up in amazing colours.
ex.zh: 他们把房子刷得绚丽无比。

ex.en: The bus was painted up with advertisements.
ex.zh: 公共汽车上涂满了广告。

senses.en: to form a pair or pairs, especially in order to have a romantic relationship; to bring two people together in this way﹙

ex.en: By the end of the course, everyone had paired off.
ex.zh: 课程结束时大家都成双结对了。

ex.en: (especially BrE) They tried to pair their daughter off with the neighbour’s son.
ex.zh: 他们尝试把女儿与邻居的儿子配成一对。

senses.en: to form a pair or pairs (with sb/sth) in order to work, play a game, etc. together; to bring two people together for this purpose

ex.en: The job is a lot easier if you pair up with someone else.
ex.zh: 你如果找人搭档，这活儿就轻松多了。

ex.en: Writers have been paired up with artists to write articles on paintings.
ex.zh: 作家和艺术家联手作画赋文。

senses.en: to become friends with sb and spend time with them﹙

ex.en: I used to pal around with Brad.
ex.zh: 我以前常和布拉德一起玩儿。

senses.en: to become friends with sb

ex.en: They palled up at college.
ex.zh: 他们是在大学结识的。

senses.en: to persuade sb to believe an explanation for sth that is not true, in order to stop them asking questions or complaining﹙
senses.zh: 藉口某事﹚搪塞某人，骗过某人:

ex.en: Don’t let him palm you off with an excuse.
ex.zh: 别听他找藉口搪塞你。

senses.en: to persuade sb to accept sth that has little value or is not what they really want

ex.en: Make sure he doesn’t palm you off with faulty goods.
ex.zh: 当心别让他以残次品假充正品卖给你。

senses.en: to persuade sb that sth is better than it really is, or is sth different,especially in order to sell it
senses.zh: 以﹙次品﹚假充﹙正品﹚；以假乱真:

ex.en: She was trying to palm copies off as original paintings.
ex.zh: 她企图以复制品假冒原画作出售。

senses.en: to get rid of sb/sth that you do not want by persuading sb else to accept them/it
senses.zh: 劝说……接受﹙自己不想要的人或事物﹚:

ex.en: He tried to palm his uncle off on me for the whole afternoon.
ex.zh: 他整整花了一下午时间把他叔叔推给我。

ex.en: I think she palmed off the stolen necklace on some unsuspecting old lady.
ex.zh: 我想她已经把偷来的项链脱了手给一位没有防备的老妇人。

senses.en: (of events or a situation
senses.zh: 事情或局面) to develop in a particular way发展成…:

ex.en: I don’t know why things panned out the way they did.
ex.zh: 我搞不明白事情怎么会这样发展。

ex.en: How do you see your career panning out?
ex.zh: 你设想你的工作前程会是怎样的？

senses.en: to try to please sb by doing or providing what they want although you know it is probably wrong to do so

ex.en: He panders to her every whim.
ex.zh: 他对她的性子百依百顺。

ex.en: His films never pandered to public taste.
ex.zh: 他的电影从不迎合公众的口味。

senses.en: to make sb do sth too quickly because they are afraid
senses.zh: 使仓惶行事；使仓促行动:

ex.en: Don’t let them panic you into a decision.
ex.zh: 别因为害怕他们而匆忙作决定。

senses.en: to cover sth such as a wall with thick paper in order to hide sth
senses.zh: 用墙纸裱煳；用厚纸遮盖:

ex.en: We papered over the stains on the wall.
ex.zh: 我们用墙纸把墙上的污斑煳上了。

senses.en: to hide sth such as a problem, a disagreement, etc.,especially quickly or not very well
senses.zh: 暂时掩盖，权且掩饰﹙问题、分歧等﹚:

ex.en: The divisions in the party had been papered over during the election campaign.
ex.zh: 竞选运动期间该党的内部分歧被掩盖了。

senses.en: to divide sth into parts or portions
senses.zh: 把某物分成若干部份； 划分:

ex.en: They parcelled out the land into small plots.
ex.zh: 他们把地分成了若干小块。

ex.en: The work was parcelled out among the staff.
ex.zh: 那工作分派给了各个职员。

senses.en: to wrap sth and make it into a parcel

ex.en: She parcelled up the books ready to send.
ex.zh: 她把书包起来准备寄走。

senses.en: to remove the thin outer layer from sth in thin strips

ex.en: Pare off the rind from the orange using a sharp knife.
ex.zh: 用锋利的刀子削去橙子皮。

ex.en: () Their rights had been pared away under the last three kings.
ex.zh: 前三任国王统治期间他们的权利被一层一层地剥夺了。

senses.en: to gradually reduce sth considerably in size or amount
senses.zh: 逐步进行﹙大幅度的﹚缩减:

ex.en: We’ve pared our expenses down to a minimum.
ex.zh: 我们已把开支削减到最低限度。

senses.en: to use an advantage that you have, such as money or a skill, in order to get sth or make it worth more

ex.en: He parlayed his relationship with his boss into an important job.
ex.zh: 他利用和老板的关系得到了一份重要工作。

senses.en: to give sth away that you would prefer to keep
senses.zh: 割捨﹙ 事物﹚ ； 割爱:

ex.en: It was my grandmother’s necklace and I’ll never part with it.
ex.zh: 那是我祖母的项链，我决不会割爱。

ex.en: (humorous) We won’t be sorry to part with that old sofa.
ex.zh: 把旧沙发扔了我们不会捨不得的。

senses.en: to separate one area, one part of a room, etc. from another with a wall or screen﹙
senses.zh: 用隔板墙或屏风等把地方、房间等﹚分隔，隔开:

ex.en: The dining area is partitioned off with screens.
ex.zh: 吃饭的地方是用屏风隔出的。

senses.en: to offer sth to each person in a group

ex.en: Would you mind passing the sandwiches round?
ex.zh: 请您把三明治递给大家吃好吗？

ex.en: A picture was passed around the class.
ex.zh: 班上的同学传看一幅画。

senses.en: to disappear

ex.en: Many of these customs have passed away.
ex.zh: 这些风俗有很多已失传了。

senses.en: to go past sb/sth without stopping

ex.en: He saw the procession pass by.
ex.zh: 他看见队伍走过。

ex.en: The boat passed close by the island.
ex.zh: 那艘船紧挨着岛驶过。

senses.en: a road that goes around a town, etc.and which is intended to keep traffic out of the town centre
senses.zh: 旁道，外环道﹙绕过市中心等﹚

senses.en: a medical operation on the heart in which blood is directed along a different route so that it does not flow through a part that is damaged or blocked;the new route that the blood takes﹙
senses.zh: 给心脏接旁通管的﹚分流术，搭桥术；旁通管:

ex.en: a bypass operation
ex.zh: 分流手术

senses.en: a person who is walking past sb/sth, especially when sth unexpected happens﹙
senses.zh: 尤指出现意外事情时的﹚ 过路人； 路人:

ex.en: Several passers-by stopped to help.
ex.zh: 几位过路人停下来帮忙。

senses.en: to happen without affecting sb/sth

ex.en: She feels that life is passing her by (= that she is not enjoying the opportunities and pleasures of life).
ex.zh: 她觉得所有人生的机遇欢乐都与她无缘。

ex.en: The whole business passed him by (= he was hardly aware that it was happening).
ex.zh: 他没有察觉到发生了什么事。

senses.en: to give sth or teach sth to your children or people who are younger than you, who will then give or teach it to their children,etc.

ex.en: These stories were passed down from one generation to the next.
ex.zh: 这些故事世代相传。

ex.en: Some of the furniture has been passed down through the family.
ex.zh: 有些傢具是一代代传下来的。

senses.en: used to say that although sth is said to be a particular thing, you do not think it is good enough to be called that

ex.en: I got used to drinking what passes for tea in that part of the world.
ex.zh: 我习惯了喝那个地方的所谓的茶。

senses.en: to be so much like another person,or another type of person, that people could easily think you were that person or type﹙
senses.zh: 因相似﹚被当作某人，被看成为某类人:

ex.en: He speaks French well enough to pass for a Frenchman.
ex.zh: 他说法语很流利，很容易被当作法国人。

ex.en: She’s in her forties but she could pass for ten years younger.
ex.zh: 她四十多岁了，但看上去要年轻十岁。

senses.en: to become a part of sth
senses.zh: 成为其中一部份；溶入；纳入:

ex.en: Many foreign words have passed into English.
ex.zh: 许多外来词语已被英语吸收过来。

senses.en: to act as if a difficult or awkward remark or situation is less important than you really think it is
senses.zh: 对﹙ 困难或尴尬的话语或状况﹚加以淡化，从容应付:

ex.en: He had really upset her, but she smiled and tried to pass it off.
ex.zh: 他着实让她难过，但她笑了笑就算了。

ex.en: He managed to pass the question off lightly.
ex.zh: 他把那个问题轻轻带过就应付下去了。

senses.en: to pretend that sb or sth is something that they are not

ex.en: She tried to pass the picture off as an original.
ex.zh: 她企图把那张画冒充成原作。

ex.en: He succeeded in passing himself off as a doctor.
ex.zh: 他成功地装扮成医生。

senses.en: to give sth to sb else, especially after receiving or using it yourself

ex.en: I’ll pass this book on to you when I’ve finished with it.
ex.zh: 我看完这本书后就给你。

ex.en: I’ll pass on your news to the rest of the family.
ex.zh: 我会把你的消息带给家里人的。

senses.en: to arrange for sb else to help or deal with a particular person
senses.zh: 把某人交给他人；安排他人接手:

ex.en: I’m afraid I can’t answer your question, but I’ll pass you on to my colleague.
ex.zh: 恐怕我不能回答你的问题，不过我可以请我的同事回答你。

senses.en: to lose consciousness

ex.en: He almost passed out with the pain.
ex.zh: 他痛得快要昏了。

senses.en: to not consider sb for a better job,especially when they deserve it or think they deserve it﹙
senses.zh: 考虑提职等时﹚跳过某人:

ex.en: I was passed over for promotion again.
ex.zh: 晋升又没有考虑我。

ex.en: He was passed over in favour of a younger man.
ex.zh: 他未被擢升，却提拔了一个比他年轻的人。

senses.en: to move over the top of sb/sth

ex.en: The planes pass directly over the hospital.
ex.zh: 飞机都从医院的正上方飞过。

ex.en: The eye of the storm was passing over us.
ex.zh: 那时风暴眼正从我们上方通过。

senses.en: to ignore or avoid sth

ex.en: They chose to pass over her rude remarks.
ex.zh: 他们决定不理会她的粗鲁言辞。

ex.en: For years this painting was passed over by experts.
ex.zh: 这幅画有很多年都被专家冷落在一边。

senses.en: () a bridge that carries one road or railway above another; a bridge over a road for people who want to cross

ex.en: Don’t try to cross the highway — use the overpass.
ex.zh: 别横穿公路—从天桥上走。
