senses.en: to give sth to sb, especially when they ask for it or you do not want it any more; to give sb, or the responsibility for sb,to sb else

ex.en: Jeff passed the phone over so that I could speak to Clare.
ex.zh: 杰夫把电话递给我，让我和克莱尔讲话。

ex.en: The doctor passed the baby over to the nurse.
ex.zh: 医生把婴儿交给护士照料。

senses.en: to let sb listen or speak to sb else when you have finished talking﹙
senses.zh: 讲话之后﹚让……听﹙别人﹚讲话，让……找﹙ 别人﹚ 谈话:

ex.en: If there are no more questions, I’ll pass you over to Ted.
ex.zh: 如果没有其他问题问我，现在请听特德讲话。

senses.en: to go or travel through a place, only stopping for a short time

ex.en: We’re not staying here, we’re just passing through.
ex.zh: 我们只是路经此地，不会久留的。

ex.en: We passed through Pompeii on our way to Naples.
ex.zh: 我们去那不勒斯时途经庞贝。

senses.en: to experience a particular kind of situation or period of time, especially a difficult or unpleasant one,and develop during it

ex.en: She passed through a difficult period after her divorce.
ex.zh: 她离婚之后一度倍受煎熬。

ex.en: The industry is passing through a period of change.
ex.zh: 该行业正经历着一场变革。

senses.en: to begin to be owned by sb new

ex.en: When she died, the house passed to her niece.
ex.zh: 她去世后，房子归她的姪女所有。

senses.en: to decide not to take advantage of an opportunity, an offer, etc.

ex.en: She passed up the chance of a trip to Rome.
ex.zh: 她放弃了去罗马旅游的机会。

ex.en: Imagine passing up an offer like that!
ex.zh: 真想不到居然放弃人家提供的大好机会！

senses.en: to connect telephone or electronic equipment temporarily﹙
senses.zh: 临时把电话、电子设备﹚接通，连通:

ex.en: The radio was patched through to army headquarters
ex.zh: 无线电和部队司令部接通了。

senses.en: to arrange sth quickly,especially by putting several different parts together, without taking any care over it

ex.en: An interim government was quickly patched together.
ex.zh: 匆匆组建了临时政府。

senses.en: to give quick or temporary medical treatment to someone who is injured
senses.zh: 匆忙处理，临时包扎﹙伤员或伤口﹚:

ex.en: They patched him up and sent him back onto the field (=for example in a game of football).
ex.zh: 他们给他上了点药就让他回到了赛场。

ex.en: The doctor did the best he could to patch up their wounds.
ex.zh: 医生尽最大努力很快给他们包扎了伤口。

senses.en: to repair sth, especially quickly or temporarily

ex.en: The car was patched up and resold.
ex.zh: 汽车草草修理一下又卖掉了。

ex.en: We patched up the hole in the roof and got it repaired the next day.
ex.zh: 我们堵了堵顶部的洞，第二天找人把它修好了。

senses.en: to end a quarrel or dispute with sb and be friends again

ex.en: They patched up their differences.
ex.zh: 他们弥合了分歧。

senses.en: to punish sb because they have made you or sb else suffer

ex.en: I’ll pay him back for getting me into trouble!
ex.zh: 他给我惹了麻烦，我非治治他不可！

senses.en: [C] [U] a reward or a punishment that sb receives for sth they have done
to return money that you have borrowed from sb

ex.en: I’ll pay you back next week.
ex.zh: 我下周把钱还给你。

ex.en: She’s trying to pay the loan back over 5 years.
ex.zh: 她在争取5年内分期归还贷款。

senses.en: to suffer or be punished for sth wrong that you have done or said, or for sth you believe
senses.zh: 为﹙做错的事或说错的话、相信的事﹚吃苦头；为……受惩罚:

ex.en: Someone’s going to pay for this!
ex.zh: 一定得有人为这事付出代价！

senses.en: to put money into a bank account

ex.en: I had to go to the bank to pay a cheque in.
ex.zh: 我得去银行存入一张支票。

ex.en: Her wages are paid directly into her account.
ex.zh: 工资直接存入她的账户。

senses.en: () a reward or a benefit that you receive as a result of sth you do

ex.en: What are the pay-offs of working at home?
ex.zh: 在家工作有什么好处？

senses.en: to give sb money to persuade them not to do sth or not to tell sb about sth illegal or dishonest you have done
senses.zh: 用钱封某人的口；买通某人:

ex.en: She refused to be paid off.
ex.zh: 她拒绝被收买。

senses.en: to finish paying money that you owe for sth﹙

ex.en: I used the money to pay off my overdraft.
ex.zh: 我把钱用来付清透支。

ex.en: They’re still paying off their mortgage.
ex.zh: 他们还在偿还按揭贷款。

senses.en: ) to pay the fare for a taxi journey

ex.en: She paid the taxi off and walked the rest of the way.
ex.zh: 她付了打车的钱，然后步行。

senses.en: to pay a large amount for sth

ex.en: The insurance company refused to pay out.
ex.zh: 保险公司拒绝支付巨额。

ex.en: The government pays out millions of pounds in benefits.
ex.zh: 政府支出几百万英镑救济金。

senses.en: a large amount of money that is given to sb

ex.en: People injured in the crash won record payouts from the rail company.
ex.zh: 撞车事故中的伤员得到了铁路公司空前高额的赔款。

senses.en: to release or pass a length or rope, etc. through your hands﹙
senses.zh: 从手中﹚徐徐放出﹙绳索等﹚:

ex.en: He started paying out the rope.
ex.zh: 他开始一点一点地放开绳子。

senses.en: [only before noun]
having paid all the money necessary to be a member of a club or an organization
senses.zh: 已付清会费的；已缴款的

senses.en: () strongly supporting sth
senses.zh: 坚决支持的； 全情投入的:

ex.en: a fully paid-up football fan
ex.zh: 痴心的足球迷

senses.en: to eat only very small amounts of sth, because you are not hungry﹙
senses.zh: 一口一口﹚啃； 一点一点吃:

ex.en: He was so nervous he only pecked at his lunch.
ex.zh: 他紧张得只吃了一丁点儿午饭。

senses.en: to come off the surface of sth;to remove a thin layer from the surface of sth

ex.en: The wallpaper had started to peel away.
ex.zh: 壁纸开始脱落。

ex.en: The paint was peeling away from the wood.
ex.zh: 木头上的油漆一片一片地剥落。

senses.en: to come away from the surface of sth

ex.en: The wallpaper was peeling off.
ex.zh: 壁纸正在脱落。

senses.en: to remove a thin layer from the surface of something

ex.en: He peeled off the sweet wrapper.
ex.zh: 他剥掉糖纸。

ex.en: She peeled all the wallpaper off the bathroom ceiling.
ex.zh: 她把浴室天花板的壁纸全撕掉了。

senses.en: to continue to work hard at or try to achieve sth difficult
senses.zh: 坚持不懈地工作﹙或努力﹚:

ex.en: He keeps pegging away at his novel.
ex.zh: 他毫不懈怠地撰写着小说。

senses.en: (especially in sport
senses.zh: 尤用于体育运动) to stop sb/sth from winning or from increasing the amount by which they are ahead扼止；止住；拖住:

ex.en: Italy were winning 2-0, but were pegged back to a draw by Spain’s late goal.
ex.zh: 意大利队以2 :0 领先，但西班牙队后来的入球使比分拉平。

senses.en: to die

ex.en: I thought she was going to peg out right in front of me!
ex.zh: 我还以为她就要死在我面前呢！

senses.en: to rain very heavily

ex.en: It’s pelting down (with rain) outside.
ex.zh: 外面下着倾盆大雨。

senses.en: to shut sb/sth in a small space with walls or fences, etc. all around﹙

ex.en: We penned the sheep in the yard.
ex.zh: 我们把绵羊关在院子里。

ex.en: The trouble makers were penned in by the police.
ex.zh: 警方关押了那些惹是生非的傢伙。

senses.en: [NOTE]This phrasal verb is often used in the passive.
senses.zh: 这个短语动词常用于被动语态。

senses.en: ) to shut sb/sth in a place with walls, fences, etc. all around, and not let them leave﹙

ex.en: It was good to go outside after being penned up in the house all day.
ex.zh: 在屋子里关了一整天，出去走走真好。

ex.en: They penned us up in a little room and wouldn’t let anyone leave.
ex.zh: 他们把我们关在一个小房间里，不许任何人离开。

senses.en: to write down sb’s name for an appointment, or the details of an arrangement, although you know that this might have to be changed later
senses.zh: 临时记下﹙约会的人名或细节安排﹚:

ex.en: Let’s pencil in the third of May for the meeting.
ex.zh: 我们暂定五月三号开会吧。

senses.en: to make sb/sth more interesting; to make sb feel more lively or full of energy
senses.zh: 增加……的趣味；使兴致勃勃；激励；使活跃:

ex.en: The company needs to pep up its image.
ex.zh: 这家公司有必要改善其形象。

senses.en: to hit sb/sth with lots of small things such as bullets﹙
senses.zh: 以小物体﹚频繁击打；向……不断射击:

ex.en: They said they were peppered with shotgun pellets as they walked in the forest.
ex.zh: 他们说在森林行走时遭到了猎枪铅弹的连续射击。

ex.en: () The interviewer peppered her with questions.
ex.zh: 主持面试的人连珠炮般地向她发问。

senses.en: to include a large number of sth in sth

ex.en: She peppers her conversation with references to famous people.
ex.zh: 她在交谈中提到了很多名人。

ex.en: Her hair is peppered with grey.
ex.zh: 她头发花白。

senses.en: to become, or make sb, more lively or more cheerful, especially after they have been ill/sick﹙

ex.en: You’ve perked up since this morning.
ex.zh: 你今天上午精神就好多了。

ex.en: A shower would soon perk you up.
ex.zh: 冲个淋浴你很快就会打起精神的。

senses.en: to make sth more interesting or more attractive

ex.en: Perk up a dark kitchen with a coat of paint.
ex.zh: 把昏暗的厨房油漆一下使它更亮堂。

ex.en: A vegetable stew can be perked up with a dash of chilli sauce.
ex.zh: 给炖菜加点辣椒酱能使味道更佳。

senses.en: to make sth possible; to allow sth to happen

ex.en: The situation does not permit of any delay.
ex.zh: 情势刻不容缓。

senses.en: to be connected with a particular subject, person, event or situation

ex.en: The committee was reviewing all the laws pertaining to adoption.
ex.zh: 委员会在复查所有有关收养的法律。

senses.en: to decrease or fade gradually before coming to an end
senses.zh: 逐渐减少；逐渐减弱；慢慢消失:

ex.en: The road petered out into a dirt track.
ex.zh: 大道延伸到一条泥土小径。

ex.en: By midday their enthusiasm had petered out.
ex.zh: 他们的热情到中午就烟消云散了。

senses.en: to introduce sth gradually or in stages

ex.en: The government will phase in the new tax.
ex.zh: 政府将逐步推出新税种。

senses.en: to stop using sth gradually or in stages

ex.en: They agreed to phase out chemical weapons.
ex.zh: 他们同意逐步废除化学武器。

senses.en: to make phone calls to several different people or places, usually to try to find out some information
senses.zh: 给各人﹙或到处﹚打电话﹙询问等﹚:

ex.en: I spent the morning phoning round hotels, trying to book a room.
ex.zh: 我一上午都在给各家旅馆打电话想订个房间。

ex.en: He phoned around to tell everyone about the meeting.
ex.zh: 他打电话通知大家开会。

senses.en: to telephone sb again or to telephone sb who telephoned you earlier﹙
senses.zh: 给某人﹚ 再打电话， 回电话:

ex.en: I left a message but they never phoned back.
ex.zh: 我留言了，可他们从没回过电话。

ex.en: Tom called while you were out. He asked if you could phone him back.
ex.zh: 你外出时汤姆来电话了，他请你给他回电话。

senses.en: to telephone your place of work

ex.en: I’ll phone in to say I won’t be in until lunchtime.
ex.zh: 我会给单位打电话说我到午饭时才到。

senses.en: to phone a television or radio programme
senses.zh: 给电视﹙或电台﹚节目打电话；打﹙观众或听众﹚热线电话:

ex.en: Hundreds of listeners phoned in to complain.
ex.zh: 有几百名听众打热线电话表示不满。

senses.en: () a radio or TV programme in which people can phone and ask questions, give their opinions, etc. as the programme is being broadcast﹙
senses.zh: 电台或电视台的﹚热线电话节目:

ex.en: He hosts a radio phone-in.
ex.zh: 他在电台主持热线电话节目。

ex.en: a phone-in programme
ex.zh: 热线电话节目

senses.en: to phone sb with details of or information about sth

ex.en: Phone your order through to the store.
ex.zh: 给商店打电话详细说明你订购的货物。

senses.en: to make a telephone call to sb/sth﹙

ex.en: I’ll phone up and cancel my appointment.
ex.zh: 我将打电话取消约会。

ex.en: Phone Mike up and ask him if he wants to come.
ex.zh: 给迈克打电话，问问他想不想来。

senses.en: to eat very small amounts of food because you are not hungry﹙

ex.en: She picked at her food for a while, then left the table.
ex.zh: 她吃了几小口东西就离开了餐桌。

senses.en: to shoot a person, an animal, a bird, an aircraft, etc. especially one of a group,after aiming carefully

ex.en: One of our men was picked off by a sniper.
ex.zh: 狙击手射中了我们的一个人。

senses.en: to choose the best people or things for your own use
senses.zh: 挑选﹙ 优秀人才或事物﹚ :

ex.en: The company continues to pick off the brightest young graduates.
ex.zh: 这家公司继续物色最优秀的年轻大学毕业生。

senses.en: to remove sth from sth with your fingernails or a tool﹙
senses.zh: 用指甲或工具﹚去除，剪除:

ex.en: She watered the plants and picked off the dead leaves.
ex.zh: 她浇了花草并摘掉了枯叶。

senses.en: to treat sb badly or unfairly, especially repeatedly﹙
senses.zh: 一再对某人﹚刁难挑剔，找彆扭:

ex.en: You’re always picking on me!
ex.zh: 你总是在跟我过不去！

ex.en: The manager was accused of picking on a member of the department.
ex.zh: 有人指责经理总刁难这个部门中的一名职员。

senses.en: )to choose sb for a task, especially an unpleasant one

ex.en: The teacher always picked on Tom to answer the difficult questions.
ex.zh: 老师总是点汤姆回答难题。

senses.en: to choose sb/sth from a number of people or things

ex.en: He picks out people from the audience to come up on stage.
ex.zh: 他叫一些听众到台上来。

ex.en: The brightest students were picked out for special training.
ex.zh: 最优秀的学生被选出来接受专门的培训。

senses.en: to recognize sb/sth from among people or things

ex.en: Can you pick me out in this old school photo?
ex.zh: 你能在这张旧学校照片中认出我来吗﹖

ex.en: The suspect was picked out at an identity parade.
ex.zh: 嫌疑犯在列队认人时被认出了。

senses.en: to manage to see sb/sth

ex.en: We could just pick out a car in the distance.
ex.zh: 我们只能隐隐约约看见远处有一辆车。

senses.en: to discover or recognize sth after careful study﹙
senses.zh: 经仔细研究﹚找出，认识到:

ex.en: It was difficult to pick out the important points from the mass of facts.
ex.zh: 很难从这一大堆资料中理出要点。

ex.en: They were asked to pick out exactly what it was that made his style so distinctive.
ex.zh: 他们被问到到底是什么使他的风格如此鲜明。

senses.en: ) to examine or analyse sth carefully

ex.en: We spent the meeting picking over last month’s results.
ex.zh: 我们开会详细研究了上个月的成绩。

senses.en: to become better; to improve

ex.en: The market always picks up in the spring.
ex.zh: 市面总是在春季好转。

ex.en: The game started very slowly but picked up in the second half.
ex.zh: 比赛开始时进行缓慢，但在下半场越来越激烈。

senses.en: to start again; to continue
an improvement

ex.en: There are no signs of a pickup in consumer spending.
ex.zh: 没有迹象显示消费开支会增长。

senses.en: () the ability of a vehicle to increase its speed﹙
() something that makes you feel better or happier, etc.
senses.zh: 提神之物；振奋精神的事物:

ex.en: The country air was the perfect pick-me-up.
ex.zh: 乡下的空气让人神清气爽。

senses.en: the part of a record player or musical instrument that changes electrical signals into sound, or sound into electrical signals
to get to your feet, especially after a fall﹙

ex.en: She picked herself up and stumbled on.
ex.zh: 她爬起来踉踉跄跄地继续走。

ex.en: () We have to pick ourselves up after yesterday’s defeat and start again.
ex.zh: 我们必须从昨天的失败中振作起来重新开始。

senses.en: to notice sth

ex.en: He picked up on her feelings of unease.
ex.zh: 他意识到她的不安。

ex.en: Children soon pick up on tensions between their parents.
ex.zh: 父母关系紧张，孩子很快就察觉到。

senses.en: to return to a point in order to talk about it in more detail
senses.zh: 回到﹙某课题等﹚；重提﹙要点等﹚:

ex.en: I’d like to pick up on Mr Finlay’s point.
ex.zh: 我想再谈一下芬利先生提到的那一点。

senses.en: to discover a story, etc.by putting together separate facts or pieces of evidence
senses.zh: 组合资料﹙以便了解情况﹚；厘清:

ex.en: Detectives are piecing together the events of the last hours of his life.
ex.zh: 侦探正在理清他死亡之前数小时发生的事。

ex.en: Investigators are still trying to piece together the evidence to find out what caused the crash.
ex.zh: 调查人员仍然在努力厘清证据，以找出撞车原因。

senses.en: to eat too much or a lot of food

ex.en: We pigged out at lunch for four bucks each.
ex.zh: 午餐时我们每人出四块钱大吃一通。

ex.en: It isn’t a good idea to pig out on sugar.
ex.zh: 大量吃糖不太好。

senses.en: an occasion on which you eat too much or a lot of food

ex.en: We had a real pig-out last night.
ex.zh: 我们昨晚吃得真够多的。

ex.en: a pig-out party
ex.zh: 吃喝聚会

senses.en: to go in or out of somewhere without order or control
senses.zh: 蜂拥； 拥挤； 涌出:

ex.en: The taxi arrived and we all piled in.
ex.zh: 出租车一到，我们一拥而上。

ex.en: Crowds of children piled out of the building.
ex.zh: 一群群孩子闹哄哄地从楼里跑出来。

senses.en: to crash into sb/sth

ex.en: She stopped dead in the middle of the pavement and we all piled into her.
ex.zh: 她突然在路中心停下来，我们全撞了她。

ex.en: As many as 30 cars and trucks piled into each other in the fog this morning.
ex.zh: 在今天上午的大雾中有多达30 辆汽车和货车连环相撞。

senses.en: to express a feeling in a much stronger way than is necessary

ex.en: I admit I’m piling on the drama a bit, but I’m trying to make a serious point.
ex.zh: 我承认我有点夸大，但我是想认真说明问题。

senses.en: to give sb a lot or too much of sth
senses.zh: 给以大量﹙或过量﹚的……；过度施加:

senses.en: to form a pile; to make a lot of things into a pile﹙

ex.en: Snow was piling up against the windows.
ex.zh: 雪堆积到了窗户上。

ex.en: They piled the stones up in a corner of the yard.
ex.zh: 他们把石头堆在院子的一角。

senses.en: to increase or to make sth increase in quantity or amount﹙

ex.en: Rubbish was piling up in the streets.
ex.zh: 街上的垃圾越来越多。

ex.en: The bills were piling up and we had no money to pay them.
ex.zh: 账单越积越多，我们没钱支付。

senses.en: a road accident in which several vehicles crash into each other
senses.zh: 几辆车相撞；连环撞车事故:

ex.en: Eleven cars were involved in a pileup on the motorway.
ex.zh: 有十一辆车在高速公路上相撞。

ex.en: Three people were killed in a multiple pile-up.
ex.zh: 在连环撞车事故中有三人死亡。

senses.en: to make sb unable to move, especially by holding them firmly﹙

ex.en: The older boy had pinned Jimmy down on the floor.
ex.zh: 大些的男孩把吉米死死地摁在地板上。

ex.en: The rebels were pinned down (= they could not move from their position) just south of the border.
ex.zh: 反叛者就钳制在边境以南。

senses.en: to make sb seem responsible or take the blame for sth they have not done
senses.zh: 让﹙无辜的人﹚受过；冤枉﹙某人﹚:

ex.en: They tried to pin the blame on me!
ex.zh: 他们居然想让我背黑锅！

senses.en: to fasten sth to a wall, etc. with pins

ex.en: He pinned up a notice on the board.
ex.zh: 他把通告钉在布告板上。

ex.en: Can I pin this poster up?
ex.zh: 我可不可以把海报钉起来？

senses.en: to fix your hair in place with pins

ex.en: She was pinning her hair up in front of the mirror.
ex.zh: 她在镜子前面往头发上别发卡。

senses.en: a picture of an attractive person,designed to be put up on the wall for people to look at﹙
senses.zh: 可钉在墙上的﹚美人画像，名人挂图:

ex.en: The walls of his room were covered in pin-ups.
ex.zh: 他房间的墙壁上挂满了美人像。

ex.en: He was football’s first pin-up boy.
ex.zh: 他是海报上的第一位足球偶像。

senses.en: a person who appears in a pin-up
to become very sad, and sometimes ill or weak because sb has died or gone away﹙
senses.zh: 因忧伤而﹚憔悴，形容枯槁，病病歪歪:

ex.en: After his wife died, he just pined away.
ex.zh: 妻子死后，他日渐憔悴。

ex.en: He seemed to be pining away from love.
ex.zh: 他好像得了相思病。

senses.en: to want or miss sb/sth very much
senses.zh: 怀念； 思念； 渴望:

ex.en: She wasn’t really pining for Brazil at all.
ex.zh: 她并不十分怀念巴西。

ex.en: a dog pining for its master
ex.zh: 想念主人的狗

senses.en: used to tell sb to be less noisy or to stop talking

ex.en: OK, everybody pipe down!
ex.zh: 好了，大家安静啦！

senses.en: to begin to speak

ex.en: Debbie suddenly piped up with ‘I’ve seen this film before!’
ex.zh: 戴比突然叫起来：“我以前看过这部电影！”

senses.en: , !, ) to act in a silly or unhelpful way and waste time

ex.en: We haven’t got time to piss about.
ex.zh: 我们没有时间混下去了。

senses.en: to rain very heavily

ex.en: It’s still pissing (it) down out there.
ex.zh: 外面依然大雨如注。

senses.en: used to tell sb rudely to go away

ex.en: I told him to piss off.
ex.zh: 我让他磙开。

ex.en: Piss off and leave me alone!
ex.zh: 磙开，别管我！

senses.en: to test sb/sth/yourself in a struggle or competition with sb/sth﹙
senses.zh: 使﹚与……竞争，与……较量，经受考验:

ex.en: It’s a chance to pit yourself against the champion.
ex.zh: 这是一次与冠军较量的机会。

senses.en: to join in willingly with sb to help with an activity

ex.en: We all pitched in and soon finished the job.
ex.zh: 我们都上手帮忙，很快便完成了工作。

ex.en: Lots of people pitched in with advice.
ex.zh: 很多人主动献计献策。

senses.en: to attack or criticize sb

ex.en: They really pitched into me when I refused to cooperate.
ex.zh: 我拒绝合作后他们便对我大肆攻击。

senses.en: to depend on a central point; to develop from a central idea or point
senses.zh: 以……为核心；围绕﹙主旨﹚展开:

ex.en: The success of the project pivots on investment from abroad.
ex.zh: 这个工程的成功主要依靠外来投资。

ex.en: The novel pivots around a long conversation between two characters.
ex.zh: 这部小说是以两个人物的对话为中心展开的。

senses.en: to make arrangements in advance

ex.en: It’s impossible to plan ahead when things keep changing!
ex.zh: 情势变化无常，不可能提前计划好。

ex.en: We need to plan ahead for our retirement.
ex.zh: 我们得为退休做准备。

senses.en: to intend to do sth

ex.en: We’d planned on having a quiet evening at home tonight.
ex.zh: 今天晚上我们想安静地呆在家里。

ex.en: I’m not planning on going to bed yet.
ex.zh: 我还没打算睡觉呢。

senses.zh: 常用于否定句) to expect sth to happen预料；料想:

ex.en: We hadn’t planned on a storm!
ex.zh: 我们没料到会有风暴！

ex.en: They hadn’t planned on so many people visiting the exhibition.
ex.zh: 他们没想到有这么多人来参观展览。

senses.en: to plan carefully and in detail sth that you are going to do in the future

ex.en: to plan out your time/route
ex.zh: 仔细安排时间/设计路线

ex.en: I knew exactly where I was going — I’d got it all planned out.
ex.zh: 我完全明白我的目标—我已经精心规划了一切。

senses.en: to put plants in the ground so that they have enough room to grow
senses.zh: 均匀栽植﹙彼此保持适当距离以利生长﹚

senses.en: to pretend to agree with sb/sth, to believe sb/sth, etc., to gain an advantage for yourself, amuse yourself, avoid trouble,etc.

ex.en: He realized they’d mistaken him for the gardener, but decided to play along.
ex.zh: 他意识到他们误以为他是园丁，但决定将错就错。

ex.en: I knew he was lying, but I decided to play along with him for a while.
ex.zh: 我知道他在撒谎，但我想还是先不戳穿他。

senses.en: to test or try new ideas, methods, etc. to see how good or effective they are before you make a final decision
senses.zh: 检验，尝试﹙新想法、新方法等﹚:

ex.en: Play around with the spreadsheet until you find the best way to display the data.
ex.zh: 试用电子制表，摸出演示这些数据的最好方法。

ex.en: We’re still playing around with ideas for a new programme.
ex.zh: 我们仍然在构思新计划。

senses.en: to do sth without any effort or real interest

ex.en: He’s just playing at being in love.
ex.zh: 他谈恋爱只不过是玩玩而已。

senses.en: used to tell sb who has played a trick on you that you can do the same to them﹙
senses.zh: 表示也会对方耍的花招﹚游戏可以两个人玩，我照样能以牙还牙

senses.en: used to ask in an angry way about what sb is doing﹙

ex.en: What do you think you’re playing at?
ex.zh: 你以为你在搞什么鬼名堂？

senses.en: to play music, sound, film,etc. that has been recorded on a tape or video﹙

ex.en: Can you play back what we’ve just recorded?
ex.zh: 把我们刚录制的播放一下好吗？

senses.en: [U] [C] the act of playing music,showing a film/movie or listening to a telephone message that has been recorded before; a recording that you listen to or watch again
senses.zh: 录音﹙或录像、电话留言等的﹚播放；播放的录音﹙或录像﹚ :

ex.en: A TV playback showed exactly what had happened.
ex.zh: 电视播放的录像原样显示了所发生的事。

senses.en: to try to make sth appear less important than it is
senses.zh: 减少……的重要性；贬低；淡化:

ex.en: The government is trying to play down its involvement in the affair.
ex.zh: 政府正极力淡化与此事的关系。

senses.en: a game or games between two players or teams with equal points in a competition to decide who the winner is﹙
senses.zh: 平分后决出胜负的﹚附加赛:

ex.en: We’re unlikely to reach the playoffs.
ex.zh: 我们不大可能进入加赛。

ex.en: The title was decided by a sudden-death play-off.
ex.zh: 冠军是由突然死亡法的加时赛决定的。

senses.en: to make two people or groups oppose each other,especially in order to gain an advantage for yourself
senses.zh: 挑拨离间，引起……间的矛盾﹙以便渔利﹚:

ex.en: () He tries to play one parent off against the other.
ex.zh: 他试图挑拨父母不和。

ex.en: () The children played their parents off each other.
ex.zh: 孩子们搞得他们父母闹不和。

senses.en: () to continue to play; to start playing again

ex.en: They claimed a penalty but the referee told them to play on.
ex.zh: 他们要求判罚，但裁判却要他们继续比赛。

senses.en: to continue to play music

ex.en: Despite the uproar, the musicians played on.
ex.zh: 乐师们不顾喧闹继续奏乐。

senses.en: to develop and come to an end or be no longer useful or important

ex.en: The crisis has yet to play out.
ex.zh: 危机尚待消除。

ex.en: The revolution soon played itself out.
ex.zh: 革命很快便垮掉了。

senses.en: [NOTE]This phrasal verb is usually used in written English.
senses.zh: 这个短语动词通常用于书面语。

senses.en: completely finished; too tired or weak to continue

ex.en: She was played out — too exhausted even to cry.
ex.zh: 她疲惫不堪—累得连哭的力气也没有了。

senses.en: ) to continue to play sth until it finishes

ex.en: We’ll play out this game and then go to bed.
ex.zh: 我们完成这一局就去睡觉。

senses.en: to let a length of rope pass through your hands bit by bit﹙
if children play up or play sb up, they behave very badly﹙

ex.en: The kids have been playing up all day.
ex.zh: 孩子们胡闹了一整天。

ex.en: All kids play new teachers up.
ex.zh: 所有孩子都戏弄新老师的。

senses.en: to try to make sth appear more important than it really is
senses.zh: 夸大……的重要性；渲染；吹嘘；炒热:

ex.en: She played up her achievements in an attempt to impress us.
ex.zh: 她吹嘘自己的成就，好让我们觉得她了不起。

senses.en: to behave towards sb in a way that you think they will like and will bring you an advantage

ex.en: She always played up to her father.
ex.zh: 她总是讨好她的父亲。

senses.en: to behave towards sb in a way that is not serious, especially by pretending to feel sth you do not feel
senses.zh: 轻率对待；玩弄；对……虚情假意:

ex.en: She was just playing with my emotions.
ex.zh: 她只不过是在玩弄我的感情。

senses.en: to touch your sexual organs in order to give yourself pleasure
to continue doing sth, especially difficult or boring work, at a very slow rate
senses.zh: 缓慢进行﹙尤指艰难枯燥的工作﹚:

ex.en: Keep plodding on — you’ll soon be finished!
ex.zh: 坚持干吧—就快做完啦！

ex.en: They’re still plodding along with their investigation.
ex.zh: 他们仍然在不厌其烦地进行调查。

senses.en: to work steadily but slowly at a difficult or boring task
senses.zh: 坚持不懈地做﹙困难或枯燥的事﹚ :

ex.en: He plodded away all night at his project to get it finished.
ex.zh: 他通宵埋头苦干以便做完专题研究。

senses.en: to sit down heavily and quickly

ex.en: She plonked herself down in front of the telly.
ex.zh: 她一屁股坐在了电视机前。

senses.en: to drop sth or put sth down heavily without taking great care

ex.en: She plonked the food down in front of them.
ex.zh: 她把食物啪的一声扔在他们面前。

ex.en: Don’t just plonk the baby down on the floor.
ex.zh: 别粗手粗脚地把孩子往地板上随便一扔。

senses.en: to put profits back into the business that produced them

ex.en: All the profits are ploughed back into the company.
ex.zh: 所有的利润都再投资到了公司。

ex.en: The director confirmed that every penny had been ploughed back in.
ex.zh: 董事确认所有的钱都进行了再投资。

senses.en: (of a vehicle or a driver
senses.zh: 车辆或司机) to crash violently into sb/sth猛撞；撞车:

ex.en: The car hit a lamp post before ploughing into a wall.
ex.zh: 汽车碰了灯柱后就撞上一堵墙。

senses.en: to invest a large amount of money on a project, a business etc.
senses.zh: 把﹙巨额资金﹚投入；大量投资于:

ex.en: $50 million will be ploughed into the area over the next five years.
ex.zh: 在今后的五年中将有5千万元投放到这个地区。

senses.en: to continue to say or do sth even though it becomes difficult
senses.zh: 坚持说，继续做﹙困难的事﹚:

senses.en: to force a way through sth
senses.zh: 费劲地穿越﹙ 或通过﹚ :

ex.en: The car ploughed its way through the snow and ice.
ex.zh: 汽车在冰雪中艰难地行驶。

ex.en: The journey involved ploughing through 50 miles of swamp land.
ex.zh: 旅途中需要穿行50 英里的沼泽地。

senses.en: (of a vehicle or an aircraft
senses.zh: 车辆或飞机) to crash violently through sth猛冲过:

ex.en: The car ploughed through the hedge.
ex.zh: 汽车猛地冲破了树篱。

senses.en: to slowly do, read or eat all of sth even though it is difficult or boring
senses.zh: 缓慢地做完﹙或读完、吃完﹚；艰难地进行；埋头苦干:

ex.en: It took me hours to plough through all the mail.
ex.zh: 我花了几小时埋头读完了所有信件。

ex.en: I had to plough my way through a mountain of pasta because I didn’t want to appear rude.
ex.zh: 我不想让人觉得我不礼貌，于是硬着头皮吃下了一大盘意大利麵食。

senses.en: to take hold of sth with your fingers and pull it towards you in a quick, sharp movement

ex.en: He plucked at my sleeve.‘’
ex.zh: 他拉了拉我的衣袖说：“来坐下吧。

senses.en: to work hard and steadily at sth for a long time, especially sth difficult or boring
senses.zh: 坚持不懈地做﹙尤指困难或乏味的工作﹚:

ex.en: Scientists have been plugging away at the problem for years.
ex.zh: 科学家多年来一直在钻研这个难题。

senses.en: to be able to be connected to a source of electricity or another piece of electrical equipment
senses.zh: 能与﹙电源或其他电器﹚连接:

ex.en: Where does the TV plug in?
ex.zh: 电视机的电源在哪里？

ex.en: The guitar plugs into this amplifier.
ex.zh: 这把吉他能接到这个扬声器上。

senses.en: to become involved with a particular activity or group of people

ex.en: The company hopes to plug into new markets in Asia.
ex.zh: 这家公司希望打入亚洲新市场。

senses.en: [only before noun] that can be connected to an electricity supply with a plug (= a small plastic object with two or three metal pins)
senses.zh: 带﹙电源﹚插头的；插入式的:

ex.en: a plug-in kettle
ex.zh: 电源插入式水壶

senses.en: () a piece of software (=programs used to operate a computer) that can be added to a computer system to give extra features

ex.en: plug-ins for a palmtop computer
ex.zh: 掌上电脑的软插件

ex.en: a plug-in graphics card
ex.zh: 插入式显卡

senses.en: =PLUG STH IN,PLUG STH INTO STH
to connect a computer to a computer system
to fill or block a hole with a substance or a piece of material that fits tightly into it

ex.en: We plugged up all the holes around the window to stop the wind coming in.
ex.zh: 我们堵上了窗隙挡风。

senses.en: to connect a washingmachine,a bath, etc. to a water system
senses.zh: 把﹙洗衣机、浴缸等﹚与水管连接:

ex.en: He’s plumbed in the new washing machine for me.
ex.zh: 他帮我给新洗衣机接上了水管。

senses.en: () to sit down quickly and heavily

ex.en: She plumped herself down in the armchair.
ex.zh: 她一屁股坐到扶手椅上。

senses.en: to put sth down suddenly and carelessly

ex.en: He plumped his books down on the table.
ex.zh: 他的一声把书丢在桌子上。

senses.en: to choose or vote for sb/sth after thinking about it carefully

ex.en: I think I’ll plump for the steak.
ex.zh: 我想我要牛排。

senses.en: to become rounder or fatter

ex.en: Soak the raisins until they plump up.
ex.zh: 把葡萄乾泡在水里发好。

senses.en: to jump or fall in to sth, usually with some force﹙

ex.en: He plunged into the pool.
ex.zh: 他猛地跳进了游泳池。

ex.en: The car plunged into a gorge.
ex.zh: 汽车坠入了峡谷。

senses.en: to begin doing sth or talking about sth without preparing for it or thinking carefully

ex.en: He plunged into the task of clearing the office.
ex.zh: 他二话没说就开始清理办公室。

ex.en: I plunged in and started telling him all about it.
ex.zh: 我冒冒失失地把这事给他和盘托出。

senses.en: to put sth quickly and with force into sth else

ex.en: She plunged the knife into his leg.
ex.zh: 她把刀子刺进他的腿。

ex.en: He opened the sack and plunged his arm in.
ex.zh: 他打开袋子将胳膊一下子插进去。

senses.en: to be or to make sb/sth suddenly be in a bad situation or state﹙
senses.zh: 使﹚突然陷入﹙糟糕的境地或状况﹚:

ex.en: The country plunged into recession.
ex.zh: 国家经济急剧衰退。

ex.en: The city was plunged into chaos as a result of the strike.
ex.zh: 罢工使城市骤然陷入一片混乱。

senses.en: to keep giving sb large amounts of sth, especially food and drink
senses.zh: 持续大量提供﹙食物和饮料﹚:

ex.en: They plied us with tea and cakes.
ex.zh: 他们一个劲儿地让我们喝茶、吃糕饼。

senses.en: to keep asking sb question

ex.en: They plied me with questions about my visit to England.
ex.zh: 他们不断地询问我的英国之行。

senses.en: to show sb which person or thing you are referring to, for example by moving your head, by describing them/it, etc.

ex.en: Will you point his wife out to me if you see her?
ex.zh: 你如果看见他的妻子就指给我看好吗﹖

ex.en: He drove them around Beverley Hills pointing out where the stars lived.
ex.zh: 他开车带他们在贝弗利希尔斯各处转，把明星的住所指给他们看。

senses.en: to mention sth in order to give sb information about it or make them notice it﹙

ex.en: He thanked me for pointing out the mistakes in his report.
ex.zh: 他感谢我指出了他报告中的错误。

ex.en: I must point out that my part in the rescue was very small.
ex.zh: 我必须说明，我在这次营救行动中的作用非常小。

senses.en: to mention sth that you think is important and/or the reason why a particular situation exists
senses.zh: 提出， 指出﹙ 重要的事或理由﹚:

ex.en: She pointed to unemployment as a reason for rising crime.
ex.zh: 她强调失业导致了犯罪率上升。

senses.en: to give special emphasis to one particular aspect of a problem, fact or opinion; to show sth very clearly

ex.en: This incident points up the hostility between the two sides.
ex.zh: 此次事件显明了双方的敌意。

senses.en: to try to find out information, especially secret or hidden information; to get involved in sth that does not concern you

ex.en: A reporter had been poking around, trying to discover something in my past.
ex.zh: 有位记者一直试图探听我过去的事。

senses.en: to move or do things slowly, without hurrying
senses.zh: 闲逛；从容做事；闲散地移动﹙或做﹚ :

ex.en: I was just poking around in town all morning.
ex.zh: 我一个上午都在城里闲逛。

senses.en: to push your finger, a stick, etc. into sth, often several times﹙
senses.zh: 用手指、棍子等反复地﹚捅，戳，扎:

ex.en: She poked at her salad with her fork.
ex.zh: 她用叉子拨弄着色拉。

senses.en: to move sth suddenly forwards or out of sth

ex.en: The door opened and Max poked his head out.
ex.zh: 门开了，马克斯猛地探出头来。

ex.en: The pony poked its nose out of the door as I went past.
ex.zh: 我经过时，小马一下子把鼻子伸出门来。

senses.en: to become visible because a small part is coming through a hole, etc.

ex.en: The grass had begun to poke up through the snow.
ex.zh: 草开始破雪而出了。

senses.en: to kill someone

ex.en: She hired an assassin to polish him off.
ex.zh: 她雇了杀手除掉他。

senses.en: to make changes to sth in order to improve it
senses.zh: 修改； 润色； 润饰:

ex.en: The college needs to polish up its image.
ex.zh: 这所学院得改变一下形象了。

senses.en: to do silly things in a way that looks ridiculous, especially to attract attention; to waste time﹙
senses.zh: 尤指为引人注意﹚ 无事忙， 做无聊的事:

ex.en: He ponces around on the show, interviewing members of the audience.
ex.zh: 他装模作样地采访着观众。

ex.en: I could have finished that job while you’ve been poncing around!
ex.zh: 你胡闹的时候我就可以把那活干完。

senses.en: to make sb very tired

ex.en: A long day at the office poops me out.
ex.zh: 在办公室忙了一整天把我累垮了。

senses.en: [not before noun] (,) very tired

ex.en: I was pooped out after a long day at the office.
ex.zh: 办公室的漫长一天让我疲乏极了。

senses.en: to visit sb/sth for a short time﹙

ex.en: She often pops in for coffee.
ex.zh: 她常来小坐，喝杯咖啡。

ex.en: I’ll pop in to see you at the weekend.
ex.zh: 周末我要去看看你。

senses.en: to deliver sth to sb on your way to another place

ex.en: I’ll pop the library books in on my way home.
ex.zh: 我回家时会捎带把图书馆的书还了。

ex.en: Could you pop those photos round later?
ex.zh: 回头请顺便把那些照片带来好吗?

senses.en: to go or leave somewhere, especially for a short time﹙
senses.zh: 尤指暂时﹚ 前往， 离开:

ex.en: I’m going to pop off early tonight (= leave work early), if it’s all right with you.
ex.zh: 如果你不介意，我今晚要早点下班。

ex.en: They just pop off to France whenever they feel like it.
ex.zh: 他们一高兴就去法国。

senses.en: ) to die

ex.en: When I pop off, all my money goes to you.
ex.zh: 我死后，我的钱全都归你。

senses.en: to put on a piece of clothing quickly﹙

ex.en: He popped on his jacket and went out.
ex.zh: 他披上短上衣就出去了。

senses.en: to turn on a piece of electrical equipment

ex.en: I’ll pop the kettle on and we’ll have some tea.
ex.zh: 我来烧壶水，咱们泡茶喝。

senses.en: ) to leave somewhere for a very short time

ex.en: John’s just popped out to get a newspaper.
ex.zh: 约翰刚刚出去取份报纸。

senses.en: to visit sb’s home for a short time

ex.en: Pop over if you feel lonely.
ex.zh: 你要是觉得寂寞就来家里坐坐。

senses.en: to appear or happen when you do not expect it

ex.en: He seems to pop up in the most unlikely places.
ex.zh: 他好像神出鬼没。

ex.en: When you click with the mouse, a menu pops up.
ex.zh: 点击鼠标，菜单就弹出。

senses.en: (of a book, etc.
senses.zh: 书籍等) having pictures that stand up when you open the pages有立体活动图的:

ex.en: a pop-up book
ex.zh: 立体图书

senses.en: to study sth by looking at it or thinking about it very carefully

ex.en: She was poring over an old map.
ex.zh: 她全神贯注地看一张旧地图。

senses.en: to send sth to sb by post/mail﹙

ex.en: I posted a letter off to you this morning.
ex.zh: 我今天上午给你寄了封信。

senses.en: to put a notice, etc. up on a wall so that people can see it

ex.en: The exam results will be posted up in the hall.
ex.zh: 考试成绩将在礼堂张榜公布。

senses.en: to do things or move without hurrying, especially when you are doing sth that you enjoy and that is not important
senses.zh: 从容做事；欣然从事；漫步；闲荡:

ex.en: They spent the day pottering about by the river.
ex.zh: 他们在河边逍遥了一天。

ex.en: She was happy just pottering around the house.
ex.zh: 她就乐意在家里晃悠。

senses.en: to quickly notice sth that sb has said or done, and criticize it or use it for your own advantage
senses.zh: 一眼看出；抓住机会﹙进行抨击﹚:

ex.en: As soon as I opened my mouth, the teacher pounced on me.
ex.zh: 我一张嘴就被老师抓住嗬斥了。

ex.en: He said something silly and the other boys pounced on it at once.
ex.zh: 他说了句傻话，马上遭到了其他男孩的嘲笑。

senses.en: to accept an opportunity, etc. with enthusiasm
senses.zh: 热中于接受， 抓紧﹙ 机会等﹚ :

ex.en: She pounced on the opportunity to work with them.
ex.zh: 有机会同他们一起工作她乐不可支。

senses.en: to play a tune on a musical instrument very loudly﹙

ex.en: Cole was pounding out a tune on the piano.
ex.zh: 科尔正在用力弹奏一首钢琴曲。

ex.en: () She pounded out her poems on an old typewriter.
ex.zh: 她用一台旧打字机噼噼啪啪打出她的诗歌。

senses.en: to get rid of a liquid by emptying it out of its container

ex.en: He poured the water away after he finished washing the car.
ex.zh: 他擦洗完车就把水倒掉了。

senses.en: to rain heavily

ex.en: It’s pouring down.
ex.zh: 大雨滂沱。

ex.en: The rain poured down all weekend.
ex.zh: 大雨下了整整一个周末。

senses.en: a heavy shower of rain
to appear or to produce sth from somewhere in large numbers or amounts

ex.en: The doors opened and a crowd of people poured forth.
ex.zh: 门开了， 一群人蜂拥而进。

ex.en: He poured forth a stream of bitter accusations.
ex.zh: 他连珠炮般地进行了严厉谴责。

senses.en: to arrive somewhere in large numbers or amounts

ex.en: Complaints poured in after last night’s programme.
ex.zh: 昨晚的节目播出之后，不满意见纷至沓来。

ex.en: Sunlight poured in through the windows.
ex.zh: 阳光从窗户照射进来。

senses.en: to provide a large amount of money for sth
senses.zh: 向……投入大量金钱；大量投资于:

ex.en: The council has been pouring money into the area.
ex.zh: 议会一直在向这个地区投入大量金钱。

senses.en: to remove some of the liquid from a container, cooking pot, etc. by pouring

ex.en: When the fish is cooked, pour off the water.
ex.zh: 鱼煮熟之后就把水滗出去。

senses.en: [usually pl.] a strong and sudden expression of feeling﹙

ex.en: She hated having to listen to his passionate outpourings.
ex.zh: 她讨厌他那赤裸裸的表白。

senses.en: a large amount of sth produced in a short time

ex.en: a remarkable outpouring of scholarship
ex.zh: 学术成就的涌现

senses.en: to do or say sth before the main thing that you want to do or say
senses.zh: 在﹙正事﹚前做；在﹙正题﹚前说；以……开始﹙或引导﹚:

ex.en: They often precede their performances with a short talk or display.
ex.zh: 他们常在演出前说几句话或进行花絮表演。

senses.en: to make sb more likely to do something or to suffer from a particular illness
senses.zh: 使倾向于做；使易于患﹙病﹚:

ex.en: Cigarette advertising predisposes children to smoking.
ex.zh: 烟草广告会引导儿童抽烟。

ex.en: His lifestyle predisposed him to high blood pressure.
ex.zh: 他的生活方式容易使他患高血压。

senses.en: to say sth before you start making a speech, answering a question, etc.

ex.en: It is helpful if an interviewer prefaces each group of questions with a brief explanation.
ex.zh: 面试主持人最好在每组提问前进行简要讲解。

senses.en: to add letters,numbers or words to the beginning of a number or word
senses.zh: 在……前面加﹙字母、数字或字词﹚:

ex.en: Prefix 020 to the number you want to call.
ex.zh: 在你要拨打的号码前加020。

ex.en: Prefix the number you want to call with 020.
ex.zh: 在你要拨打的号码前加020。

senses.en: to lead or be in charge of a meeting, ceremony, etc.
senses.zh: 主持﹙ 会议、仪式等﹚；担任﹙会议等﹚的主席:

ex.en: She presided over the meeting.
ex.zh: 她主持了会议。

ex.en: The court is presided over by a single judge.
ex.zh: 该法庭只有一名法官主持。

senses.en: to continue moving forward quickly; to continue to do a task in a determined way
senses.zh: 匆忙前进；坚持不懈地做；加紧进行:

ex.en: He pressed on, even though it was now dark.
ex.zh: 他不顾夜幕降临，继续工作。

ex.en: They decided to press ahead with their plans.
ex.zh: 他们决定坚持推行他们的计划。

senses.en: to make repeated and urgent requests for sth

ex.en: The unions are pressing for a pay rise.
ex.zh: 工会正强烈要求增加工资。

ex.en: I must press you for a reply.
ex.zh: 我得催你给一个答覆。

senses.en: to move nearer to sb in a way that seems likely to cause harm

ex.en: He felt as if the walls were pressing in on him.
ex.zh: 他彷彿觉得四周的墙壁向他压过来。

senses.en: to try to make sb accept sth,even though they may not want it

ex.en: She pressed cake and tea on us.
ex.zh: 她非要我们吃蛋糕、喝茶。

senses.en: to use sb’s friendship or kindness for your own advantage in an unfair way
senses.zh: 利用﹙交情等，给自己好处﹚:

ex.en: I felt it would be presuming on our friendship to keep asking her for help.
ex.zh: 我觉得不断要她帮忙是利用了我们的交情。

senses.zh: (通常用于否定句和疑问句) to claim to be or have sth, especially when it is not true声称；自称；自诩:

ex.en: I don’t pretend to any great knowledge of the situation.
ex.zh: 我不敢说自己对局势了解得很多。

senses.en: to persuade sb to do sth

ex.en: Can I prevail on you to play the piano for us?
ex.zh: 可以请你为我们弹一首钢琴吗？

senses.en: to treat sb who is weaker than you in an unfair or dishonest way in order to get sth or gain an advantage for yourself

ex.en: The thieves have been preying on elderly people living alone.
ex.zh: 窃贼一直在偷独居老人的东西。

senses.en: to be proud of sth such as a personal quality or a skill

ex.en: She had always prided herself on her appearance.
ex.zh: 她总是对自己的外表感到得意。

senses.en: to produce a document or information from a computer in printed form﹙

ex.en: I’ll print off enough copies for everyone to have one.
ex.zh: 我会给每人打印一份的。

ex.en: I’m waiting for the results to be printed out.
ex.zh: 我等着把结果打印出来。

senses.en: a printed copy of information in a computer file﹙
senses.zh: 计算机﹚打印件，打印资料:

ex.en: She asked for a printout of the previous year’s accounts.
ex.zh: 她索要了一份去年账目的打印件。

senses.en: to obtain some information, etc. from sb with great difficulty﹙
senses.zh: 向某人﹚逼问情况；强迫……透露消息:

ex.en: I finally managed to prise his new address out of her.
ex.zh: 我最终从她口中套出了他的新住址。

ex.en: She had a way of prising secrets from people.
ex.zh: 她善于打探秘密。

senses.en: to start a court case against sb

ex.en: I shall instruct my solicitor to proceed against you for trespass.
ex.zh: 我要委託我的律师控告你非法侵入他人土地。

senses.en: to be caused by or be the result of sth
senses.zh: 由……引起；起因于；是……的结果:

ex.en: The dispute proceeded from a wrong interpretation of the law.
ex.zh: 争执的起因是对法律的错误解释。

senses.en: to press sth with your finger or with a pointed object, especially to see what it is, or what it is made of, etc.﹙

ex.en: He prodded at the plate of fish with his fork.
ex.zh: 他拿叉子戳弄着那盘鱼。

senses.en: to give a judgement in a court of law for or against sb/sth
senses.zh: 作有利﹙或不利﹚于……的判决；判……胜诉﹙或败诉﹚

senses.en: to express an opinion or give a judgement on sth

ex.en: The minister will pronounce on the situation today.
ex.zh: 部长今天将对这一局面发表讲话。

senses.en: to support a person by putting sth under or behind them

ex.en: We propped her up with a pillow.
ex.zh: 我们给她埝一个枕头。

ex.en: He tried to prop himself up on his elbow.
ex.zh: 他努力用胳膊肘壠起身子。

senses.en: to keep sth upright or stop sth from falling by putting sth under or behind it

ex.en: A family photo was propped up against some books on her desk.
ex.zh: 她的书桌上有一张全家福靠着书立着。

ex.en: The tree had to be propped up with thick posts.
ex.zh: 那棵树得用粗棍子顶住。

senses.en: to support sth that is having financial,political, etc. difficulties
senses.zh: 支持； 扶持； 救济:

ex.en: The regime is being propped up by foreign aid.
ex.zh: 这个政权靠外援扶持着。

ex.en: The government will no longer prop up inefficient industries.
ex.zh: 政府将不再贴补无效益的产业。

senses.en: to make plans in order to deal with or prevent a bad or unpleasant situation

ex.en: Does your insurance provide against loss of income?
ex.zh: 你的保险是否赔付收入损失？

senses.en: to give sb the things that they need to live, such as food, money and clothing

ex.en: How will she provide for six children?
ex.zh: 她将如何供养六个孩子？

ex.en: My family will be well provided for if I die.
ex.zh: 我死后，我的家人将衣食无忧。

senses.en: to move quietly and carefully around an area, often with the intention of committing a crime

ex.en: There was someone prowling around outside.
ex.zh: 外面有个人蹑手蹑脚的。

ex.en: Why were you prowling about the building so late?
ex.zh: 那么晚了你还在楼周围转悠什么？

senses.en: to walk around a room, a building, etc.,because you are worried, bored or unable to relax﹙
senses.zh: 因焦躁、无聊等﹚徘徊，走来走去:

ex.en: Her husband prowled about restlessly.
ex.zh: 她的丈夫焦躁不安地来回踱步。

ex.en: She got up and prowled around the room.
ex.zh: 她站起来在房间里踱来踱去。

senses.en: to make an opponent feel less confident by saying or doing things that make you seem better, stronger, etc. than them

ex.en: The other team tried to psych us out before the game started.
ex.zh: 对方运动队试图在比赛开始前就把我们吓倒。

senses.en: to prepare sb/yourself mentally for sth difficult or unpleasant, such as a game, an exam, an interview, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 为困难或不快的事﹚作好思想准备:

ex.en: Boxers need to psych themselves up for the fight.
ex.zh: 拳击手得为比赛作好心理准备。

ex.en: I’d got psyched up for the interview but then it was cancelled at the very last minute!
ex.zh: 我为面试作好了心理准备，可最后临时取消了。

senses.zh: (通常用于进行时) to smoke a pipe, cigarette, etc., often when you are thinking deeply吸，抽﹙烟斗、香烟等﹚:

ex.en: He stood looking out of the window, puffing away at his pipe.
ex.zh: 他站在那里一边看着窗外一边吸着烟斗。

senses.en: to make sth larger and rounder by filling it with air

ex.en: She puffed out her cheeks in anger.
ex.zh: 她气得鼓起了腮帮子。

ex.en: Her hair was puffed out round her face.
ex.zh: 她披头散发。

senses.en: to swell or to make sth swell and increase in size﹙

ex.en: He could feel his face puffing up where Mark had hit him.
ex.zh: 他能感觉到脸上被马克打的地方肿胀起来。

ex.en: He puffed up his chest like an exotic bird.
ex.zh: 他像只奇异的鸟一样鼓起了胸脯。

senses.en: to be too full of pride, self-importance, etc.

ex.en: She was so puffed up with conceit she didn’t notice people were avoiding her.
ex.zh: 她太自以为是了，没有注意到人们都在躲着她。

senses.en: to move infront of sb/sth, especially suddenly or unexpectedly﹙
senses.zh: 突然或出人意料地﹚抢先，领先:

ex.en: I pulled ahead of the other runners on the last straight.
ex.zh: 我在直道冲刺时一下子超过了其他选手。

senses.en: to separate sb/sth, oftenpeople or animals that are fighting
senses.zh: 分开，拉开﹙打斗的人或动物﹚:

ex.en: It took several of us to pull them apart.
ex.zh: 我们上了几个人拉架。

senses.en: to severely criticizesb/sth

ex.en: She pulled my work apart and made me do it again.
ex.zh: 她把我的工作批得一无是处，并且令我返工。

senses.en: to destroy sth or separate sthinto pieces by pulling parts of it in different directions

ex.en: I pulled the machine apart, but couldn’t find what was wrong with it.
ex.zh: 我卸开机器，但没找到毛病。

ex.en: The fox was pulled apart by the dogs.
ex.zh: 几条狗把狐狸撕成了碎片。

senses.en: to take sb to a quiet corner orplace to talk to them privately

ex.en: I pulled him aside to warn him not to say anything.
ex.zh: 我把他拉到一边，警告他什么也别说。

senses.en: to pull sth lightly several timesespecially to gain attention﹙

ex.en: The little boy pulled anxiously at her sleeve.
ex.zh: 小男孩焦急地拉了拉她的袖子。

senses.en: =PULL ON/ATSTH
to gradually move further in frontof sb/sth; to start to win a game or competitionby getting more points than your opponent
senses.zh: 逐渐超出； 开始赢分； 赢得比赛:

ex.en: The British boat began to pull away from the Italians (= in arace).
ex.zh: 英国赛艇渐渐甩开了意大利赛艇。

ex.en: The German pair pulled away to finish three games ahead (= in tennis).
ex.zh: 德国双打选手最后领先三局。

senses.en: (from sb/sth) to move quickly away fromsb/sth

ex.en: She pulled away from him in horror.
ex.zh: 她惊恐地挣脱了他。

senses.en: to make sb/sth move away from sb/sth

ex.en: I pulled her away from the edge.
ex.zh: 我把她从边缘上拉了回来。

senses.en: (from sb/sth) to move backwards away from sb/sth

ex.en: He pulled back and stared at her in disbelief.
ex.zh: 他倒退一步，用怀疑的目光盯着她。

ex.en: The camera then pulled back to a wider view.
ex.zh: 然后摄影机镜头缩回使取景变宽。

senses.en: to decide not to do sth you were intending to do, usually because of possible problems

ex.en: Their sponsors pulled back from financing the movie.
ex.zh: 赞助人打了退堂鼓，不再赞助该影片。

senses.en: to move back from a place; to make an army move back from a place
, )to improve a team’s position in a game
senses.zh: 挽回局势； 翻盘； 扳回:

ex.en: Rangers pulled back to 4–3.
ex.zh: 流浪者队以4 :3反败为胜。

ex.en: They pulled back a goal in the last few minutes of the game.
ex.zh: 他们在比赛结束前几分钟扳回一球。

senses.en: to hold sb/sth and move them/it backwards, sideways or away from sth

ex.en: I pulled the child back from the edge.
ex.zh: 我把孩子从边缘上拉回来。

ex.en: He pulled back the curtain.
ex.zh: 他拉开窗帘。

senses.en: to have a bad effect on sb’s health or happiness

ex.en: The strain is really pulling me down.
ex.zh: 压力太大，我实在支壠不住了。

senses.en: [only before noun] used to describe a list of possible choices that appears on a computer screen below a title

ex.en: a pull-down menu
ex.zh: 下拉式菜单

senses.en: to support and encourage sb/sth and hope they will be successful

ex.en: Hang in there, we’re all pulling for you to win!
ex.zh: 坚持下去，我们都在为你加油，希望你取胜。

senses.en: (, ) an area at the side of a road where drivers can stop; a restaurant for drivers at the side of a road
senses.zh: 路边停车区；路边小餐馆

senses.en: ) to bring sb to a police station in order to ask them questions

ex.en: The police have pulled him in for questioning.
ex.zh: 警方把他扣起来讯问。

senses.en: (of a vehicle or its driver
senses.zh: 车辆或司机) to leave the road in order to stop for a short time驶离﹙马路﹚短暂停车:

ex.en: He pulled off onto the verge.
ex.zh: 他把车开到路边停下。

ex.en: I pulled off the main road and stopped.
ex.zh: 我把车驶离大路然后停下。

senses.en: to forcefully pull away sb/sth attacking sb/sth else
senses.zh: 用力拉开﹙进攻的人或动物﹚:

ex.en: They tried to pull off the dogs with their hands.
ex.zh: 他们试图徒手把那些狗拽开。

ex.en: He had to be pulled off the older man by two policemen.
ex.zh: 要由两位警察把他从年纪较大的男子身上拉开。

senses.en: to remove an item of clothing quickly or with difficulty

ex.en: She pulled off her hat and gloves.
ex.zh: 她一把摘下帽子和手套。

senses.en: () to succeed in doing or achieving sth difficult

ex.en: The goalie pulled off a terrific save.
ex.zh: 守门员来了个漂亮的救球。

senses.en: to take long deep breaths from a cigarette, etc.

ex.en: She pulled on her cigar.
ex.zh: 她狠抽着雪茄。

senses.en: to move or to make sb/sth move away from sth or stop being involved in it﹙

ex.en: They are pulling their troops out of the war zone.
ex.zh: 他们正从战区撤出军队。

senses.en: an act of taking an army away from an area; an act of taking an organization out of a system, a deal, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 军队的﹚转移，撤退；﹙机构的﹚撤出，退出:

ex.en: their unexpected pullout from the competition
ex.zh: 他们出人意料的退出比赛

senses.en: to take sth out of somewhere by pulling﹙

ex.en: He pulled an envelope out of his pocket.
ex.zh: 他从衣兜里掏出信封。

ex.en: The woman suddenly pulled out a knife.
ex.zh: 那女子突然拔刀。

senses.en: to remove sth from sth else; to separate sth from sth else﹙

ex.en: I pulled out the middle page of the magazine to show him.
ex.zh: 我抽出杂志的中页给他看。

senses.en: to move or to make sb/sth move, to the side of the road and stop﹙

ex.en: He pulled over and jumped out of the car.
ex.zh: 他把车停在路边，然后跳下车。

ex.en: I pulled over to let the ambulance pass.
ex.zh: 我开车到路边给救护车让路。

senses.en: to get better after an illness; to help sb get better after an illness﹙

ex.en: Few people expected him to pull through after the accident.
ex.zh: 那场事故之后很少人认为他会康复。

ex.en: She has pulled through the operation remarkably well.
ex.zh: 她手术后恢复得非常好。

senses.en: to succeed in doing sth very difficult or in dealing with difficult problems; to help sb do this﹙
senses.zh: 协助…﹚完成﹙困难的事﹚，渡过难关:

ex.en: He’s got his problems at school, but with help he’ll pull through.
ex.zh: 他在学校遇到困难，但帮他一把他就能克服的。

ex.en: It’s going to be tough but we’ll pull through it together.
ex.zh: 这事会很棘手，但我们将齐心协力渡过难关。

senses.en: to make all the different parts of an organization, an activity, etc. work together in a successful way
senses.zh: 使﹙组织等﹚齐心协力；使﹙行动等﹚协调一致:

ex.en: His inspired leadership pulled the party together.
ex.zh: 他的英明领导使该党团结一心。

senses.en: to organize a variety of ideas,etc. in a logical and careful way﹙

ex.en: This lecture pulls together several recent theories.
ex.zh: 这次讲座系统地介绍了几个新理论。

senses.en: to gain control of your feelings and start to act in a calm and sensible way
senses.zh: 使自己镇定自若﹙或冷静﹚:

ex.en: She made a great effort to pull herself together.
ex.zh: 她咬紧牙关保持冷静。

ex.en: Stop crying and pull yourself together!
ex.zh: 别哭了，振作起来！

senses.en: to make sb/sth become completely covered in water

ex.en: He felt the waves pulling him under.
ex.zh: 他觉得波浪要把他吞没了。

senses.en: (of a vehicle, or its driver
senses.zh: 车辆或司机) to stop, especially for a short time﹙尤指临时﹚停车，停止:

ex.en: He pulled up alongside me at the traffic lights.
ex.zh: 他在红绿灯处把车停在我旁边。

ex.en: A taxi pulled up outside.
ex.zh: 一辆出租车停在了外面。

senses.en: an exercise in which you hold onto a high bar above your head and pull yourself up towards it

ex.en: She does 50 pull-ups and 100 sit-ups every morning.
ex.zh: 她每天早晨做50 次引体向上和100次仰卧起坐。

senses.en: to move your body into an upright position, especially by holding sth firmly and using force﹙
senses.zh: 尤指抓住某物用力﹚站起来:

ex.en: Julia pulled herself up from the sofa.
ex.zh: 朱莉娅使劲地从沙发上站起来。

senses.en: to stop doing or saying sth very suddenly
to give large amounts of money or resources to sth
senses.zh: 把﹙资金或资源﹚大量投入；大量注入:

ex.en: Millions have been pumped into this industry.
ex.zh: 已经对这个产业投资几百万。

senses.en: (of a liquid
senses.zh: 液体) to come out of somewhere or to be produced from somewhere with force and in large amounts涌出；涌流；排放:

ex.en: Blood was pumping out of the wound.
ex.zh: 鲜血正从伤口中喷涌出来。

ex.en: Cars are pumping out tons of pollutants every year.
ex.zh: 汽车每年排放成吨的污染物。

senses.en: to remove a gas, liquid, etc. from inside sth with a pump

ex.en: The fire brigade pumped out the basement.
ex.zh: 消防队把地下室的水抽出来。

ex.en: The fire brigade pumped the water out of the basement.
ex.zh: 消防队把地下室的水抽出来。

senses.en: to make sb feel more excited or determined about sth

ex.en: I was really pumped up for the race.
ex.zh: 那次赛跑我真是鼓足了劲。

senses.en: to fill a tyre, etc. with air using a pump

ex.en: Pump your tyres up before you set off.
ex.zh: 出发前给你的轮胎打打气。

senses.en: , ) to increase the amount, value or volume of sth
senses.zh: 增加数量﹙或价值、体积等﹚；提高:

ex.en: They always pump their prices up before Christmas.
ex.zh: 他们总是在圣诞节之前提价。

senses.en: to record the time that you arrive at or leave work,by putting a card into a machine; to do this for sb else﹙
senses.zh: 替某人﹚用计时卡登录﹙上、下班﹚时间；﹙替某人﹚刷计时卡:

ex.en: He punched in ten minutes late.
ex.zh: 他上班刷卡迟到了十分钟。

ex.en: I was in such a hurry to leave that I forgot to punch out.
ex.zh: 我下班时过于匆忙，忘了刷卡。

senses.en: to put information into a computer, etc. by pressing keys

ex.en: She punched in the security code and the door opened.
ex.zh: 她输入密码，门开了。

senses.en: to hit sb repeatedly

ex.en: Touch my car and I’ll punch you out.
ex.zh: 你敢动一下我的车，我就让你嚐嚐我的拳头。

senses.en: to continue with a plan in a determined way

ex.en: They pushed ahead with the modernization programme.
ex.zh: 他们坚定地推行现代化计划。

senses.en: to order sb to do things ina threatening or unpleasant way

ex.en: Don’t let him push you around.
ex.zh: 别让他对你指手画脚。

senses.en: to move sb/sth to a positionwhere they do not prevent you from goingsomewhere or doing sth
senses.zh: 移开，推开﹙阻挡前进的人或物﹚:

ex.en: He pushed her aside and went into the room.
ex.zh: 他推开她，自己进了房间。

ex.en: I pushed the curtain aside to get a better view.
ex.zh: 我拉开窗帘开阔视野。

senses.en: to treat sb/sth as if they/it are notimportant; to avoid thinking about sb/sth﹙
senses.zh: 将人或事物﹚置之不理，抛诸脑后:

ex.en: When his sister brought home a school friend, he felt pushed aside and abandoned.
ex.zh: 他妹妹带了一位同学回家，他觉得自己被扔在一边，无人理会。

ex.en: Emma immediately pushed the unpleasant thought aside.
ex.zh: 埃玛立刻把这不愉快的想法抛到脑后。

senses.en: to remove sb/sth from infront of you with your hands or arms, to showthat you do not want them/it
senses.zh: 把﹙不需要的人或物﹚推开:

ex.en: He offered to help, but she pushed him away.
ex.zh: 他主动来帮忙，却被她推开了。

ex.en: She pushed her plate away. ‘I’m not hungry.’
ex.zh: 她把盘子推到一边说：“我不饿。

senses.en: to use force to make sb movebackwards, especially by using your hands orarms

ex.en: The police pushed the protesters back.
ex.zh: 警察把示威者压了回去。

senses.en: to use force to go past other people, rudely making them move to one side﹙

ex.en: She pushed by without saying a word.
ex.zh: 她一言不发地挤了过去。

ex.en: He followed me to the door and pushed past me into the house.
ex.zh: 他跟随我来到门口，把我推到一边，进了屋子。

senses.en: to keep asking for sth, or asking sb to do sth, because you think it is very important
senses.zh: 催促﹙ 某人﹚ …… ； 不断要求；争取:

ex.en: We are pushing hard for electoral reform.
ex.zh: 我们强烈要求选举改革。

ex.en: They’re pushing me for a decision on the matter.
ex.zh: 他们在催促我就此事做出决定。

senses.en: to move forward through a group of people until you are near the front

ex.en: She pushed forward through the crowd.
ex.zh: 她挤到了人群前面。

senses.en: =PUSH AHEAD/FORWARD/ON
to try to make sb notice sb/yourself, especially in order to obtain sth such as a job or a move to a more important job﹙
senses.zh: 使﹚引人注目，出风头，突显:

ex.en: He’s not the sort of person who pushes himself forward.
ex.zh: 他不是那种想方设法表现自己的人。

senses.en: to move in front of other people who are waiting in a line

ex.en: They thought I was trying to push in at the head of the queue.
ex.zh: 他们以为我想插到队列前面。

senses.en: , ) used to tell sb rudely to go away

ex.en: Push off and leave me in peace!
ex.zh: 磙开，让我安静点！

senses.en: to leave sb/a place, especially in order to go home

ex.en: It’s time I pushed off and did some work.
ex.zh: 那时候我该回家干活儿。

senses.en: to try to make sb accept or buy sth they do not really want

ex.en: He keeps pushing his attentions on her.
ex.zh: 他没完没了地向她献殷勤。

senses.en: to make sb leave a place or an organization

ex.en: He refused to resign, so his colleagues pushed him out.
ex.zh: 他不肯辞职，于是他的同僚把他赶下了台。

ex.en: Patients are being pushed out of hospital before they are really ready.
ex.zh: 病人们现在还没好利索就要被逐出医院。

senses.en: to make sb/sth less important than before; to replace sb/sth with sb/sth else
senses.zh: 减少……的重要性； 使失势； 替换:

ex.en: My parents didn’t want me to feel pushed out by my younger brother.
ex.zh: 父母不想让我因为我弟弟而觉得失宠。

ex.en: ‘Harry Potter’ is pushing out more traditional children’s stories.
ex.zh: 《哈利波特》正取代更多的传统童话。

senses.en: to make sb/sth fall to the ground; to make sth fall onto its side or turn over

ex.en: I was pushed over in the playground.
ex.zh: 我在运动场上被撞倒了。

senses.en: a task that is easy to do; a contest that you win easily
senses.zh: 简易的事；轻易取胜的比赛:

ex.en: The game against Sheffield will be a pushover.
ex.zh: 和谢菲尔德队的比赛将易如反掌。

senses.en: a person who is easy to influence or persuade
senses.zh: 容易说服的人；好说话的人；耳软心活的人

senses.en: to use force to cross a barrier, especially one formed by a crowd of people
senses.zh: 冲过﹙障碍物﹚；挤过﹙ 人群﹚ :

senses.en: to make progress towards achieving an aim

ex.en: We are pushing towards full monetary union in Europe.
ex.zh: 我们正向全欧洲货币联盟的方向迈进。

senses.en: to make sb try to do or achieve sth

ex.en: The need for aid finally pushed them towards cooperation with the USA.
ex.zh: 为了得到援助，他们最终还是得与美国合作。

senses.en: to make sth rise or increase

ex.en: A shortage of land pushed property prices up.
ex.zh: 土地短缺推高了房地产价格。

senses.en: to spread information, stories, etc. among a group of people
to communicate your ideas, feelings, etc. to sb clearly and successfully

ex.en: The campaign failed to put the message across.
ex.zh: 这次运动未能把信息传递开来。

ex.en: She’s very good at putting across her ideas.
ex.zh: 她很善于表达思想。

senses.en: to make sb understand your ideas,your personality, etc.
senses.zh: 表明自己的想法；使﹙别人﹚ 了解自己:

ex.en: She puts herself across well at interviews.
ex.zh: 她面试表达得很好。

senses.en: to place sth to one side

ex.en: She put the newspaper aside and stood up.
ex.zh: 她把报纸放在旁边站了起来。

senses.en: to calculate or estimate something to be a particular size, amount, etc.

ex.en: I’d put his age at about sixty.
ex.zh: 我估计他大约六十岁。

ex.en: I’d put him at about sixty.
ex.zh: 我估计他大约六十岁。

senses.en: to send sb to prison, to a hospital for people who are mentally ill, etc.
senses.zh: 把某人送进监狱﹙或精神病院等﹚:

ex.en: He was put away for 15 years.
ex.zh: 他被关押了15 年。

ex.en: If you’re found guilty, they’ll put you away for a long time.
ex.zh: 如果你被判有罪，你就要长期坐牢。

senses.en: ) to eat or drink large quantities of sth

ex.en: They put away five bottles of wine between them!
ex.zh: 他俩共喝了五瓶酒！

ex.en: I don’t know how he manages to put it all away!
ex.zh: 我真不知道他怎么吃得下这么多！

senses.en: ) =PUT STH DOWN 4
to move the hands of a clock back to give the correct earlier time, especially at the end of summer﹙
senses.zh: 尤指夏时制结束时﹚向后拨，拨慢﹙钟表指针﹚:

ex.en: We forgot to put the clocks back last night.
ex.zh: 我们昨晚忘记把时钟指针拨回去。

senses.en: to give sb/sth more importance than sb/sth else

ex.en: He puts his children before anyone else.
ex.zh: 他把子女看得比谁都重要。

ex.en: They have always put business before pleasure.
ex.zh: 他们一直是正事在先，享乐在后。

senses.en: to present sth to sb/sth

ex.en: She will be able to put her arguments before the committee.
ex.zh: 她将能够向委员会提出自己的论据。

ex.en: The new evidence was put before the court.
ex.zh: 新的证据被呈交给法庭。

senses.en: to try to forget about sth unpleasant that has happened and not allow it to affect your future

ex.en: She wanted to put the past behind her.
ex.zh: 她想忘掉过去。

senses.en: ) (of a bus, etc.
senses.zh: 公共汽车等) to allow sb to get off让某人下车:

ex.en: The bus stopped to put down some passengers.
ex.zh: 公共汽车停下来让乘客下车。

ex.en: Ask the driver to put you down outside the City Hall.
ex.zh: 告诉司机让你在市政厅外下车。

senses.en: () a remark or an action that is intended to make sb look stupid
senses.zh: 令人难堪的话﹙或行为﹚；噎人的话:

ex.en: She produces some wonderful put-downs.
ex.zh: 她巧妙地奚落了几句。

senses.en: =PUT SB DOWN 1
=PUT SB/STH DOWN,PUT YOURSELF DOWN
to place sb/sth that you are holding onto the floor or another surface

ex.en: She put her bag down by the door.
ex.zh: 她把背包放在门旁。

ex.en: Put me down!
ex.zh: 把我放下来！

senses.en: to pay part of the cost of sth

ex.en: I’ve put down a deposit on our trip.
ex.zh: 我已经付了我们旅行的订金。

senses.en: to spread sth on the floor or ground
senses.zh: 在地板上铺；在地面上撒:

ex.en: We decorated the room and put a new carpet down.
ex.zh: 我们装饰了房间，铺了张新地毯。

ex.en: I’m going to put some poison down for the rats.
ex.zh: 我要往地上撒些老鼠药。

senses.en: (in a game of cards
senses.zh: 纸牌游戏中) to play a card出牌；打出:

ex.en: She put down the ace of spades.
ex.zh: 她打出了黑桃幺。

ex.en: Each player puts down a card in turn.
ex.zh: 打纸牌的人轮流出牌。

senses.en: to go to sleep

ex.en: Why don’t you put your head down for a while?
ex.zh: 你干吗不睡一会儿呢？

senses.en: to think that sb is a particular type of person, especially when you do not know them very well
senses.zh: 把某人看作﹙ 或视为﹚……:

ex.en: I put the boy down as a troublemaker as soon as I saw him.
ex.zh: 我一看见这孩子就以为他很调皮。

ex.en: I would never have put you down as an athlete!
ex.zh: 我怎么也想不到你是个运动员！

senses.en: to write down that sb is willing or wishes to buy sth, give an amount of money, etc.

ex.en: Put me down for three tickets for the Saturday show.
ex.zh: 给我登记预订三张星期六的演出门票。

senses.en: to consider that sth is caused by sth

ex.en: She tends to put everything down to fate.
ex.zh: 她总是把一切归于命运的安排。

senses.en: =PUT STH OUT 9

ex.en: The plant put forth new leaves.
ex.zh: 植物长出了新叶子。

senses.en: ) =PUT STH FORWARD3
) to make a strong physical or mental effort to do sth

ex.en: He isn’t putting forth the necessary effort.
ex.zh: 他没有尽力。

senses.en: to suggest somebody or yourself as a candidate for a job, a position, etc.

ex.en: Can I put your name forward for the job?
ex.zh: 我推荐你来做这份工作好吗？

ex.en: Only one woman has put herself forward as a candidate.
ex.zh: 只有一名女性毛遂自荐。

senses.en: to find the solution to a difficult problem by thinking carefully about it
senses.zh: 琢磨出……的答案；找到……的解决方法:

ex.en: She couldn’t puzzle out where her keys could have gone.
ex.zh: 她怎么也想不起她的钥匙去哪儿了。

ex.en: I spent hours trying to puzzle out an explanation for his behaviour.
ex.zh: 我琢磨了好几个小时想弄明白他的行为。

senses.en: to think hard about something because you want to understand it

ex.en: Police are still puzzling over the incident.
ex.zh: 警方仍然在追查这件事的来龙去脉。

ex.en: She puzzled over the postmark on the letter.
ex.zh: 她想弄明白信封上的邮戳。

senses.zh: (通常用于否定句) to disagree with sth/sb不赞同；反对:

ex.en: Few would quarrel with the principle of free education for all.
ex.zh: 很少人会反对普及义务桝育这原则。

senses.en: to wait or stand in a line with other people in order to get sth or do sth

ex.en: They spent four hours queueing up for tickets.
ex.zh: 他们花了四个小时排队买票。

ex.en: We had to queue up to get our visas.
ex.zh: 我们得排队领取签证。

senses.en: to become, or to make sb, calmer, less noisy or less active﹙
to stop helping,working with or supporting sb when they need you most
senses.zh: 离开﹙需要帮助或合作等的人﹚；撇下﹙某人﹚不管:

ex.en: I can’t believe he quit on the team after only two games!
ex.zh: 我无法相信他只打了两场比赛就离队了！

ex.en: You can’t quit on me now, we’re almost there!
ex.zh: 你不能现在丢下我，我们快到了！

senses.en: to talk about sth for a long time in a boring way

ex.en: What’s he rabbiting on about?
ex.zh: 他瞎唠叨些什么？

senses.en: ,) to get or collect a large amount or quantity of sth, such as profits or losses in a business or points in a competition
senses.zh: 累积﹙ 盈利、亏损等﹚；聚集﹙某物﹚；累计﹙得分﹚:

ex.en: The company racked up $20 billion in sales.
ex.zh: 公司销售额累计达到200 亿元。

ex.en: Bush has racked up victories in another five states.
ex.zh: 布什在另外五个州又获得了胜利。

senses.en: to offer sth as a prize in a raffle (=a way of making money when people buy tickets with a number on and some of the numbers are later chosen to win prizes)﹙

ex.en: The cake will be raffled off to raise money for the school.
ex.zh: 抽奖活动是为学校筹款。奖品是这个蛋糕。

senses.en: to protest about sb/sth in an angry or bitter way
senses.zh: 强烈抗议；愤怒谴责；怒叱:

ex.en: to rail against the government/ authorities
ex.zh: 愤怒抗议政府/当局

ex.en: There’s no point railing against the decision.
ex.zh: 强烈反对这一决定也没用。

senses.en: to fall or to make sth fall on sb/sth in large quantities﹙
senses.zh: 使﹚ 散落， 撒落﹙在…﹚:

ex.en: Huge boulders rained down on us.
ex.zh: 巨石不断地朝我们砸来。

ex.en: He rained blow after blow down on my skull.
ex.zh: 他接二连三地打我的脑袋。

senses.en: to earn large amounts of money without difficulty

ex.en: The company rakes in about ￡190 million.
ex.zh: 公司轻松地赚了大概1.9 亿英镑。

senses.en: to examine sth that happened in the past in great detail and keep talking about it, when it should be forgotten
senses.zh: 翻开﹙前尘旧事﹚；在﹙往事﹚上纠缠:

ex.en: There’s no point in raking over the events of the past.
ex.zh: 活在往事里是没有意义的。

senses.en: to criticize sb severely because they have done sth wrong
to talk about sth unpleasant that has happened in the past, which people would like to forget

ex.en: I didn’t come here to rake up old arguments.
ex.zh: 我来这里不是要重提以前的争吵。

senses.en: to hit sth violently; to make sth hit sth violently﹙

ex.en: He was going too fast and rammed into the car in front.
ex.zh: 他速度太快，猛地撞上了前面的车。

ex.en: The thieves rammed their truck into the jeweller’s window.
ex.zh: 窃贼的货车撞了珠宝行的橱窗。

senses.en: to talk or write a lot about sb/sth in a confused and boring way

ex.en: What is she rambling on about?
ex.zh: 她在东拉西扯些什么呢？

ex.en: There’s me rambling on, and you haven’t told me your news yet.
ex.zh: 我一个劲地说，你还没有把你的事告诉我呢。

senses.en: to join with other people to oppose sb/sth﹙

ex.en: He felt as though the whole family was ranged against him.
ex.zh: 他觉得好像全家人合在一起对付他。

ex.en: She ranged herself more with her parents than with her brother.
ex.zh: 她多数是站在父母而不是哥哥一边。

senses.en: to say sth quickly and sharply
senses.zh: 迅速厉声说出； 喝﹙ 令﹚ :

ex.en: The officer rapped out orders.
ex.zh: 军官大声命令。

senses.en: to give information to people in authority, causing trouble for sb

ex.en: Say what you like about Ali but he has never ratted on his friends.
ex.zh: 随便你怎么说阿里，但他从未打朋友的小报告。

senses.en: to make prices, etc. increase a little at a time

ex.en: The interest rates have been ratcheted up sharply.
ex.zh: 利率渐渐提得很高。

ex.en: The hormone rushes around the brain, ratcheting the heart rate up from 60–80 to about a hundred.
ex.zh: 荷尔蒙在脑髓中四处窜，把心率从60-80 逐渐提高到大约一百。

senses.en: to divide sth that there is not very much of between a group of people in such a way that everyone gets a small share
senses.zh: 把﹙有限的东西﹚分配；配给:

ex.en: They rationed the water out among the survivors.
ex.zh: 他们把水分给了幸存者。

senses.en: to live,work, etc. somewhere that is much too big for your needs
senses.zh: 在空荡荡的地方居住﹙或工作等﹚:

ex.en: There are only two of us, rattling around in this massive office.
ex.zh: 这么大的办公室空落落的，只有我们两个人。

ex.en: They’re rattling around that house now that the children have left.
ex.zh: 孩子们走了之后，就剩下他们住在空荡荡的房子里。

senses.en: to say or repeat sth from memory,quickly and without any effort
senses.zh: 脱口而出；不假思索地说出:

ex.en: She rattled off the names of the movies Hitchcock had directed.
ex.zh: 她一口气说出了希区柯克导演的电影名称。

senses.en: to talk quickly and for a long time about sth that is not important or interesting
senses.zh: 喋喋不休地说﹙无谓的话﹚:

ex.en: He rattled on about his job for over an hour.
ex.zh: 他用了一个多小时喋喋不休地聊他的工作。

senses.en: to do something very quickly

ex.en: He rattled through his homework then went out.
ex.zh: 他急急忙忙写完作业就出去了。

senses.en: to get sth down from a high place﹙

ex.en: Could you reach that vase down for me?
ex.zh: 请帮我把那个花瓶拿下来好吗？

ex.en: She reached down a box from the top shelf.
ex.zh: 她把箱子从架子最上层拿了下来。

senses.en: to stretch your arm or your hand in order to touch or get something

ex.en: He reached out to switch on the light.
ex.zh: 他伸手开灯。

senses.en: to show sb that you are interested in them and/or want to help them; to try to get people’s interest or attention
senses.zh: 表示对某人感兴趣；伸出援助之手；试图吸引注意力:

ex.en: The organization is trying to reach out to people of all ages and from all levels of society.
ex.zh: 这个组织正尝试惠及各个年龄段以及社会各阶层的人。

ex.en: The party has failed to reach out to young people.
ex.zh: 这个政党未能成功接触年轻人。

senses.en: [U] the activity of an organization that provides a service or advice to people in the community, especially those who cannot or are unlikely to come to an office, a hospital, etc. for help
senses.zh: 外展服务﹙在服务机构以外的场所提供的社区服务等﹚:

ex.en: a rural outreach programme
ex.zh: 农村外展活动

ex.en: outreach work
ex.zh: 外展工作

senses.en: to read a message, a letter etc.aloud in order to check that it is correct

ex.en: I got her to read the message back to me to make sure it was right.
ex.zh: 我让她把便条给我读了一遍，以确保没什么错。

senses.en: to think that something has a meaning or an importance that it probably does not have
senses.zh: 认为有更深层含义；作过多的理解:

ex.en: It’s a mistake to read too much into the results of one opinion poll.
ex.zh: 凭一次民意调查结果作过多的推想是不对的。

ex.en: You can read anything you want into horoscopes.
ex.zh: 占星术算命任你诠释。

senses.en: to look at the measurement shown on a machine or other measuring device

ex.en: The speed can be calculated or read off from the graph.
ex.zh: 可以计算速度， 或从图表读取。

ex.en: I looked at the thermometer and read off the temperature.
ex.zh: 我看了看温度计上的读数。

senses.en: to continue reading

ex.en: The book was so exciting he read on until dawn.
ex.zh: 那本书太精彩了，他一口气读到天亮。

ex.en: The idea is to make the reader want to read on.
ex.zh: 目的是吸引读者继续读下去。

senses.en: to read sth aloud, especially to other people

ex.en: She read out the names of the winners.
ex.zh: 她宣读了获胜者的名字。

ex.en: The teacher read my poem out to the class.
ex.zh: 老师在班上朗读了我的诗。

senses.en: , ) to get back information that is stored on a computer; to produce a display of the information on a screen
() a record or display of information on a computer screen﹙

ex.en: The computer will work out the best route for you and give you a read-out on the screen.
ex.zh: 计算机会为你设计出最佳路线并显示在屏幕上。

senses.en: to read something from the beginning to the end, usually in order to find any mistakes

ex.en: I read through my translation, checking for mistakes.
ex.zh: 我从头到尾核对我的译文。

ex.en: When she read her letter through the next day, she decided not to send it.
ex.zh: 第二天她把信通读之后便决定不发了。

senses.en: to read a lot about a particular subject in order to learn about it﹙
senses.zh: 就某课题﹚广泛阅读，博览群书:

ex.en: Have you been reading up on the history of the island?
ex.zh: 你是不是一直在阅读有关这个岛的历史？

ex.en: I’ve been reading this place up in the library.
ex.zh: 我一直在图书馆查阅有关这个地方的资料。

senses.en: to give a person or an animal a particular type of food, entertainment, etc.when they are young﹙

ex.en: I was reared on jazz, but later discovered rock.
ex.zh: 我小时候听的都是爵士乐，后来才发现了摇磙乐。

senses.en: to think carefully about something in a logical way in order to understand it

ex.en: Let’s try to reason out why he behaved as he did.
ex.zh: 我们来想一想，他为什么会有这种行为。

ex.en: Reason it out for yourself — why do you think she didn’t say where she was going?
ex.zh: 你自己想想─她为什么不说她上哪儿去。

senses.en: to talk to sb in order to persuade them to be more sensible

ex.en: It’s impossible to reason with her when she’s in this mood.
ex.zh: 她情绪不好，不可能听得进劝告。

senses.en: to rely on sb/sth or on sth happening; to expect sb to do sth or sth to happen
senses.zh: 指望；依赖；把希望寄託在……:

ex.en: We were reckoning on a profit of about half a million.
ex.zh: 我们希望大约有五十万的赢利。

ex.en: You can reckon on my support.
ex.zh: 你可以指望我会支持你。

senses.en: to add figures or numbers together

ex.en: That’ll be ￡20.50, if I’ve reckoned it up correctly.
ex.zh: 如果我没合计错的话，应该是20.50 英镑。

senses.zh: 通常用于否定句) to consider sb/sth as a possible problem that you should be prepared for考虑到﹙可能出现的问题﹚；顾及:

ex.en: Unfortunately, we hadn’t reckoned with Emily.
ex.zh: 可惜我们忘了考虑埃米莉。

ex.en: We must reckon with the possibility of failure.
ex.zh: 我们必须考虑到有可能失败。

senses.en: to consider or deal with sb/sth as a serious opponent or problem

ex.en: He had to reckon with a great deal of opposition.
ex.zh: 他不得不认真对待诸多的反对。

senses.en: to not consider sb/sth as a possible problem and therefore not be prepared for it

ex.en: We allowed an hour to get there, but we’d reckoned without the traffic (= it took us much longer).
ex.zh: 我们原打算用一个小时赶到那里，并没有顾及交通情况。

senses.en: to make sb/yourself accept an unpleasant situation because there is nothing you can do to change it

ex.en: They were reconciled to the fact that he wouldn’t be coming back.
ex.zh: 他们无可奈何地接受了他不会回来的事实。

ex.en: I’ve reconciled myself to having no money while I’m a student.
ex.zh: 我在学生时代已经适应了没有钱用的日子。

senses.en: to bring sb to a particular state, especially a worse one
senses.zh: 使陷入﹙更坏的﹚境地； 使陷入窘境:

ex.en: She was reduced to tears by their criticism.
ex.zh: 他们的批评使她流泪。

ex.en: The building was reduced to a heap of rubble.
ex.zh: 这座建筑物化成了残垣断壁。

senses.en: to make sb do something they do not approve of or are ashamed of because there is no other choice for them

ex.en: I was reduced to borrowing money from friends.
ex.zh: 我被迫沦落到了向朋友借钱的地步。

senses.en: to change sth into a simpler or more general form

ex.en: His arguments can be reduced to four points.
ex.zh: 他的论据可以概括成四点。

senses.en: to smell very strongly of sth unpleasant

ex.en: His breath reeked of tobacco.
ex.zh: 他满嘴烟臭味。

senses.en: to say a long list of things quickly and without having to think about it
senses.zh: 一口气说出；滔滔不绝地讲:

ex.en: He reeled off the names of the people he’d invited.
ex.zh: 他一口气说出了他邀请的人的名字。

senses.en: (as sth) to mention or talk about somebody or something

ex.en: She never referred to the incident again.
ex.zh: 她再也没有提起过这件事。

ex.en: Passengers are now referred to as ‘customers’.
ex.zh: 乘客现在都称为“顾客”。

senses.en: to describe or be connected to sb/sth

ex.en: This paragraph refers to the events of last year.
ex.zh: 这一段说的是去年发生的事。

ex.en: This phenomenon is referred to in detail in chapter nine.
ex.zh: 第九章详细描述了这一现象。

senses.en: to look at sth for information

ex.en: You don’t need to refer to a dictionary for this exercise.
ex.zh: 做这个练习不必查词典。

senses.en: to send sb/sth to a different place or person in order to get help, advice or a decision
senses.zh: 将……送交﹙或转介﹚……处理；让……去﹙ 找﹚ :

ex.en: The case was referred to the Court of Appeal.
ex.zh: 该案已提交上诉法院审理。

ex.en: My tutor referred me to a counsellor.
ex.zh: 我的导师让我去找辅导员。

senses.en: to make sb have a particular opinion of sb/sth

ex.en: When the department performs badly, it reflects on me as manager (= it makes people think I am a bad manager).
ex.zh: 部门表现欠佳会反映我作为经理的能力。

senses.en: to entertain sb with stories,jokes, etc.

ex.en: She was regaling us with tales of her youth.
ex.zh: 她给我们讲她年轻时的事，逗着我们开心。

senses.en: to pull on the reins of a horse (= the leather bands that go around its neck) to make it go more slowly or stop

ex.en: Felipe reined back and rode beside her.
ex.zh: 费利普勒了勒马和她并驾齐驱。

ex.en: She reined in her horse and waited for John to catch up.
ex.zh: 她勒住马等着约翰赶上来。

senses.en: to control sb or sth more strictly

ex.en: We need to rein in public spending.
ex.zh: 我们需要严格控制公共开销。

ex.en: The new President is faced with the task of reining in the military.
ex.zh: 新总统面临着在军事上保持克制的任务。

senses.en: to feel that you can understand a person, a situation, sth that sb does or feels, etc. and have sympathy with them/it
senses.zh: 能够理解并同情；谅解；体恤:

ex.en: She was unable to relate to her youngest child.
ex.zh: 她无法和她最小的孩子沟通。

ex.en: I find him very difficult to relate to.
ex.zh: 我发现他这人难以琢磨。

senses.en: to be connected to sb/sth; to refer to sb/sth

ex.en: All the documents relating to the matter were destroyed.
ex.zh: 所有与这件事有关的文件都给销毁了。

ex.en: The new law relates only to children born after 1996.
ex.zh: 新法规只涉及1996年之后出生的儿童。

senses.en: ( ) to carry out a difficult or unpleasant task for sb else, or instead of them
senses.zh: 替……做﹙艰难困苦的工作﹚；减轻……的负担:

ex.en: Robots can relieve people of dull and repetitive work.
ex.zh: 单调重复的工作，机器人可以代劳。

ex.en: Can I relieve you of some of your bags (= carry them for you)?
ex.zh: 我帮你提其中几个包好吗？

senses.en: ( ) to dismiss sb from a job or responsibility

ex.en: He was relieved of his post as manager.
ex.zh: 他被解除了经理职务。

senses.en: (for sth) to need or be dependent on sb/sth

ex.en: She still has to rely on her parents for money.
ex.zh: 她仍然得向父母要钱花。

ex.en: He hasn’t got a car, and relies on public transport to get around.
ex.zh: 他没有汽车，出外都得靠公交。

senses.zh: (不用于进行时) used to ask sb to give your greetings and good wishes to sb else代我问候﹙某人﹚:

ex.en: Remember me to your mother.
ex.zh: 代我向你的母亲问好。

senses.en: to allow something that you own to be used by someone else in return for payment

ex.en: They rented the house out to students.
ex.zh: 他们把房子租给了学生。

ex.en: Most of these houses are rented out.
ex.zh: 这些房子大多数都租出去了。

senses.en: to go to a place

ex.en: After dinner, they repaired to the lounge for coffee.
ex.zh: 饭后他们到休息室喝咖啡。

senses.en: (to…) to return to a place, especially in order to start work again

ex.en: When do you have to report back for duty?
ex.zh: 你什么时候归队？

senses.en: to contact sb to let them know where you are or what you are doing
senses.zh: 报告，汇报﹙方位或工作情况﹚:

ex.en: The officer briefly reported in (to the police station).
ex.zh: 那位警察向警察局简单报告了情况。

senses.en: to be in sb/sth; to be caused by sth

ex.en: The attraction of the book resides in its illustrations.
ex.zh: 这本书的魅力在于它的插图。

ex.en: The interests of the child reside in getting the best possible education.
ex.zh: 孩子的权益是得到尽可能好的桝育。

senses.en: to be present in or belong to sb/sth
senses.zh: 存在于； 属于； 隶属于:

ex.en: Supreme authority resides with the President.
ex.zh: 最高权力属于总统。

ex.en: Political power seems to reside increasingly in the South of England.
ex.zh: 英国南部的政治力量似乎与日俱增。

senses.en: to be ready to accept sth unpleasant because you cannot avoid it
to separate or to be separated into its parts

ex.en: The design resolved into a number of different patterns.
ex.zh: 设计图分成若干不同的图案。

ex.en: a lawyer’s ability to resolve facts into their legal categories
ex.zh: 律师按照法律将事实分门别类的能力

senses.en: to gradually become or be understood as sth
senses.zh: 逐步变成；逐渐被理解为:

ex.en: The discussion eventually resolved itself into two main issues.
ex.zh: 讨论后来集中在两大主要议题上。

ex.en: The question resolves itself into whether individuals should be allowed to choose such a course of action.
ex.zh: 问题逐步被解释为是否应该允许个人选择这种做法。

senses.en: to make use of something, especially something bad or unpleasant, as a way of achieving sth, often because no other course of action is possible
senses.zh: 不得已而诉之于﹙或采用某种方法﹚:

ex.en: They should be able to settle their differences without resorting to violence.
ex.zh: 他们应该能够解决分歧，无须诉诸暴力。

ex.en: They resorted to bribery to get what they wanted.
ex.zh: 他们最后靠贿赂达到目的。

senses.en: to depend on sb/sth
senses.zh: 寄託在某人身上﹙或某事物上﹚:

ex.en: Britain’s hopes of a medal now rest on Henderson.
ex.zh: 现在英国把得奖的希望寄託在亨德森身上。

senses.en: to be based on sth

ex.en: The whole case rests on one man’s evidence.
ex.zh: 整个论据都基于一名男子提供的证明。

ex.en: His argument seemed to rest on a false assumption.
ex.zh: 他的论点似乎基于错误的假设。

senses.en: , ) to rest after an illness or injury﹙
senses.zh: 因病或受伤﹚休息；养病；养伤:

ex.en: He was advised to rest up for a week after his fall.
ex.zh: 他摔了一跤，要遵嘱休息一个星期。

senses.zh: (不用于进行时) to be sb’s responsibility﹙责任﹚落在……身上:

ex.en: The decision rests entirely with you.
ex.zh: 这个决定完全得由你来作。

ex.en: The responsibility for bringing up children rests with the parents.
ex.zh: 养育子女是父母的责任。

senses.en: to have a particular effect; to make sth happen

ex.en: The accident resulted in 67 deaths.
ex.zh: 这场事故造成了67人死亡。

ex.en: The agreement will result in employers working more closely with students and teachers.
ex.zh: 协议将促使雇主更紧密地和师生合作。

senses.en: ) to be sold at a particular price

ex.en: The videos retail at ￡15 each.
ex.zh: 录像带每盘售价15英镑。

senses.en: to become, or to make sb/sth, more active or excited﹙

ex.en: The team are revving up for next week’s game.
ex.zh: 这个队伍对下周的比赛跃跃欲试。

ex.en: It’s his job to rev up the audience before the show starts.
ex.zh: 他要负责在表演开始前鼓动观众的热情。

senses.en: to enjoy a situation or an experience very much

ex.en: I think he’s secretly revelling in all the attention.
ex.zh: 我觉得他对于能够引起广泛的注意心里感到飘飘然。

ex.en: She seems to revel in annoying her parents.
ex.zh: 她似乎以惹父母生气为乐。

senses.en: (of property and land
senses.zh: 财产或土地) to return legally to the owner复归，归还﹙合法主人﹚:

ex.en: After his death the house reverted to its original owner.
ex.zh: 他死后房子归还给了原先的主人。
