senses.en: to go back to a previous condition or activity,especially a worse one
senses.zh: 回复，退回﹙尤指较差的状况﹚:

ex.en: When the pressure is on, players revert to bad habits.
ex.zh: 遇到压力，运动员就恢复坏习惯。

senses.en: to start talking or thinking again about a subject you were considering earlier
senses.zh: 回到，恢复﹙先前的话题或思路﹚ :

ex.en: To revert to your earlier question . . .
ex.zh: 回到你前面提出的问题……

senses.en: to have sb/sth as the main subject or interest
senses.zh: 围绕； 以……为中心；将……作为主要兴趣﹙或主题﹚:

ex.en: His whole life revolved round cars.
ex.zh: 他一生都在和汽车打交道。

ex.en: You think the whole world revolves around you.
ex.zh: 你以为整个世界都以你为中心呢。

senses.en: to move around sth in a circle

ex.en: The earth revolves around the sun.
ex.zh: 地球绕太阳公转。

senses.en: to remove sth/sb unpleasant from a person, a place or an organization

ex.en: The government pledged to rid the country of nuclear weapons.
ex.zh: 政府承诺清除这个国家的核武器。

ex.en: How could she rid herself of Charles?
ex.zh: 她如何能摆脱查尔斯？

senses.en: [NOTE]This phrasal verb is used mainly in written English.
senses.zh: 这个短语动词主要用于书面语。

senses.en: to fill sb/sth with bullets or with holes

ex.en: His body was riddled with bullets.
ex.zh: 他被子弹打得体无完肤。

ex.en: wooden beams riddled with holes
ex.zh: 千疮百孔的木梁

senses.en: to be full of sth, especially sth unpleasant or bad

ex.en: The whole organization is riddled with corruption.
ex.zh: 整个组织腐败透顶。

senses.zh: 通常用于进行时) to depend on sth决定于:

ex.en: My whole future is riding on this interview.
ex.zh: 我的未来全押在这场面试上。

ex.en: There’s a lot of money riding on this deal.
ex.zh: 这宗交易关系到一大笔钱。

senses.en: to manage to survive a difficult period or situation without suffering serious harm

ex.en: Do you think the president will be able to ride out this latest crisis?
ex.zh: 你认为总统能挺过最近这次危机吗？

senses.en: to search quickly through sth such as drawers, cupboards or papers, in order to find or steal sth

ex.en: Sally rifled through her wardrobe looking for something to wear.
ex.zh: 萨莉翻腾着衣柜找穿的。

ex.en: The room looked as if a burglar had rifled through it (= it was very untidy).
ex.zh: 房间看上去像是被劫掠过。

senses.en: to provide sb/sth with clothes or equipment

ex.en: They took the kids to a big store and rigged them out from top to bottom (= bought them a set of new clothes,shoes, etc.).
ex.zh: 他们把孩子们带到一家大商店，给他们从头到脚穿戴一新。

ex.en: The ship had been rigged out with state-of-the-art equipment.
ex.zh: 这艘轮船安装了最先进的设备。

senses.en: to fix a piece of equipment into place

ex.en: We’ve rigged up lights in the garden for the party.
ex.zh: 我们在花园里安了开晚会的灯。

ex.en: He was rigged up to a machine so that the nurses could check his heartbeat.
ex.zh: 他身上连接了机器让护士检查心跳。

senses.en: to make or build sth quickly, using whatever materials are available﹙
senses.zh: 用现有材料﹚匆匆做成，草草搭建:

ex.en: He had rigged up a sort of tent, using his jacket and shirt.
ex.zh: 他用外衣和衬衫匆忙搭了个类似帐篷的东西。

senses.en: to phone several people or places to find out information or discuss sth
senses.zh: 到处打电话；打电话给各方:

ex.en: I’ve spent the morning ringing round travel agents to find a flight.
ex.zh: 我一上午都在打电话向各旅行社询问航班。

senses.en: to telephone sb again or to telephone sb who telephoned you earlier﹙
senses.zh: 给某人﹚再打电话，回覆电话:

ex.en: I’ll ring you back later with more details.
ex.zh: 我过会儿再给你打电话细说。

ex.en: Your mother called while you were out. She wants you to ring back.
ex.zh: 你外出时你母亲打来电话了。她让你回电话。

senses.en: to telephone the place where you work

ex.en: She felt so exhausted she rang in sick (= to say she could not come to work).
ex.zh: 她感觉筋疲力尽，于是给单位打电话请病假。

ex.en: The boss rings in several times a day, even when he’s on holiday.
ex.zh: 老板一天打来几次电话，即使他休假也不例外。

senses.en: to telephone a radio,television programme, etc.
senses.zh: 给电台﹙或电视节目等﹚打电话:

ex.en: Listeners were asked to ring in with their opinions.
ex.zh: 欢迎听众打电话来提意见。

senses.en: to end a telephone conversation,and put the telephone down

ex.en: He rang off before I could explain.
ex.zh: 我还没来得及解释他就把电话挂了。

senses.en: to be heard loudly and clearly
senses.zh: 清晰可闻；发出响亮的声音:

ex.en: His clear voice rang out across the hall.
ex.zh: 他那清亮的嗓音在大厅中回响。

ex.en: Suddenly shots rang out nearby.
ex.zh: 附近突然响起一阵枪声。

senses.en: to make a telephone call to sb, especially within the same building
senses.zh: 打电话﹙给同一栋大楼内的人﹚:

ex.en: Reception rang through to say my visitor had arrived.
ex.zh: 服务打电话来说我的客人到了。

senses.en: to telephone sb/sth

ex.en: He rang up to apologize.
ex.zh: 他打电话来道歉。

ex.en: We must ring Jenny up tonight.
ex.zh: 我们今天晚上一定得给珍妮打电话。

senses.en: to make sth clean by washing it in water

ex.en: Ruth finished her coffee and rinsed out her cup under the tap.
ex.zh: 鲁思喝完咖啡就到水龙头把杯子冲乾净。

ex.en: Rinse your mouth out to get rid of the taste.
ex.zh: 漱漱口除掉嘴里的味道。

senses.en: to attack sth violently and tear it or cut it

ex.en: The bird ripped at its rival’s throat.
ex.zh: 那只鸟猛啄敌人的喉咙。

ex.en: ()The hurricane tore at their skin and ripped at their clothes.
ex.zh: 飓风打在他们的皮肤上，撕扯着他们的衣服。

senses.en: to criticize sb in an angry way for sth they have done or said﹙

ex.en: He ripped into me for being late.
ex.zh: 我因为迟到而受到他训斥。

senses.en: to go very quickly or violently into or through sb/sth﹙

ex.en: An explosion ripped through a four-storey apartment building.
ex.zh: 猛烈的爆炸穿过一座四层楼公寓。

senses.en: to cheat sb, for example by charging them too much for sth, selling them sth of poor quality, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 以次货等﹚欺诈某人；敲竹杠:

ex.en: The bank was accused of ripping off its customers.
ex.zh: 银行被指责欺诈顾客。

ex.en: The tickets were very expensive, but the play was terrible.We felt we’d been ripped off.
ex.zh: 票很贵，可演出糟糕透了。我们觉得上当受骗了。

senses.en: [usually sing.] () a situation where you pay too much for sth; sth that is not worth what you pay for it

ex.en: They charged you ￡25 for a T-shirt? What a ripoff!
ex.zh: 一件T恤衫开价25英镑？真会敲竹杠！

ex.en: The meal was a total rip-off.
ex.zh: 那顿饭完全不合算。

senses.en: to copy sb/sth, by stealing ideas, designs, etc. especially in order to make money for yourself

ex.en: Another band has ripped off our song.
ex.zh: 另一个乐队剽窃了我们的歌。

ex.en: She was accused of ripping off other people’s ideas.
ex.zh: 她被控抄袭他人的构想。

senses.en: to remove sth,especially clothing, very quickly by pulling sharply
senses.zh: 猛地拉下﹙或拽下﹚；迅速脱下:

ex.en: The fans were trying to rip his clothes off.
ex.zh: 追随者试图拉掉他的衣服。

ex.en: She ripped the poster off the wall.
ex.zh: 她把海报从墙上一把撕下来。

senses.en: to tear sth to pieces

ex.en: I ripped the letter up without reading it.
ex.zh: 我没看信就把它撕碎了。

senses.en: to pull sth quickly or violently from the floor or ground﹙
senses.zh: 从地上﹚迅速拉起来，猛地拔起:

ex.en: A gang of teenagers ripped up fences and plants.
ex.zh: 一帮青少年拔掉围栏和花草。

ex.en: We’ve ripped up the old carpets and painted the walls.
ex.zh: 我们把旧地毯拽了起来，刷了墙壁。

senses.en: to not be affected or limited by problems, insults, etc.; to be able to deal with problems
senses.zh: 克服﹙障碍﹚；超越﹙界限﹚；战胜﹙困难﹚:

ex.en: She was able to rise above her disability.
ex.zh: 她能够战胜自身残疾。

senses.en: to be too wise or good to do sth wrong or to think or behave in the way other people do

ex.en: He had an unusual ability to rise above the prejudices of his generation.
ex.zh: 他有一种不寻常的能力，能够超脱同代人的偏见。

ex.en: There will always be gossip. You have to try and rise above it.
ex.zh: 流言蜚语总是会有的。你必须尽量置之不理。

senses.en: to be better than other similar things

ex.en: Her articles never rise above the level of a gossip column.
ex.zh: 她的文章从未超出过漫谈栏的水平。

senses.en: to deal successfully with a situation or problem that you do not expect or do not usually have to face
senses.zh: 成功处理﹙突发情况、问题等﹚:

senses.en: to react when sb is deliberately trying to make you angry or get you interested in sth

ex.en: I refuse to rise to that sort of comment.
ex.zh: 我拒绝对那样的评论作出反应。

senses.en: a situation in which a group of people join together to fight against or to refuse to obey people in authority

ex.en: The uprising was ruthlessly suppressed.
ex.zh: 起义被残酷地镇压下去。

senses.en: (of a regular event
senses.zh: 定期活动) to arrive; to happen at the usual time举行；进行:

ex.en: We have to be ready when election time rolls around again.
ex.zh: 我们必须为下次选举作好准备。

senses.en: to reduce the amount of influence,power or importance that sth has; to change sth so that it is the opposite of what it was
senses.zh: 减少﹙影响、力量或重要性﹚；扭转:

ex.en: They were determined to roll back union power.
ex.zh: 他们决心削减工会的权力。

senses.en: to reduce prices,wages, etc.

ex.en: We must roll back inflation.
ex.zh: 我们必须减低通胀。

senses.en: ) a reduction or decrease in sth

ex.en: a 2% rollback in taxes
ex.zh: 减税2%

senses.en: ) a return to the condition that existed before there was an error in a computer system
to open out a piece of clothing, etc. that has been folded over and over

ex.en: She rolled down her sleeves.
ex.zh: 她放下了衣袖。

senses.en: to arrive in great numbers or quantities

ex.en: Offers of help continue to roll in.
ex.zh: 不断有人表示愿意提供援助。

senses.en: to arrive somewhere, usually late and without being worried or sorry

ex.en: Rob finally rolled in at lunch time.
ex.zh: 到午饭时分，罗布终于慢吞吞地来了。

senses.en: (of time
senses.zh: 时间) to pass steadily流逝:

ex.en: As the years rolled on the painful memories began to fade.
ex.zh: 一年年过去了，痛苦的回忆开始淡忘。

senses.en: to continue without changing very much

ex.en: For the next few weeks the debate rolled on.
ex.zh: 在随后的几周里，争论一如既往地进行着。

senses.en: to use sb/sth to help you achieve sth

ex.en: He rolled out all his old friends to help him win the election.
ex.zh: 他发动了所有的老朋友帮他赢得选举。

ex.en: The Moscow Circus rolled out dancing bears to announce its arrival in North America.
ex.zh: 莫斯科马戏团出动跳舞熊来宣布他们来到了北美洲。

senses.en: to make a substance such as pastry flat and thin by rolling sth over it

ex.en: Roll out the pastry with a clean rolling pin.
ex.zh: 用乾净的麵杖把油酥麵糰平。

senses.en: to officially make a new product available to the public
senses.zh: 正式推出﹙新产品﹚；将……公之于世:

ex.en: The Air Force will roll out its new planes in November.
ex.zh: 空军的新型飞机将于十一月面世。

senses.en: an occasion when a company introduces a new product﹙

ex.en: a roll-out ceremony
ex.zh: 新产品上市仪式

senses.en: (of a person
senses.zh: 人)to turn from lying on one side of your body to the other side; to move sb in this way﹙使﹚躺着时转动身体:

ex.en: She rolled over onto her back.
ex.zh: 她翻了个身仰……着。

ex.en: I rolled the baby over and sat up.
ex.zh: 我把婴儿翻过来， 自己坐直身子。

senses.en: (of a vehicle, a boat, etc.
senses.zh: 车辆、船等) to turn onto its side or upside down; to move sth in this way﹙使﹚翻侧，翻转:

ex.en: The car rolled over into a ditch.
ex.zh: 汽车翻进了沟里。

senses.en: ) to allow money that sb owes to be paid at a later date
senses.zh: 准许﹙将欠款﹚延期偿还； ﹙ 将债项﹚ 转期:

ex.en: The government agreed to roll over the debt.
ex.zh: 政府批准延期还债。

senses.en: [C] () a prize of money in a competition that is formed by adding the prize from one week when no one has won it to the prize for the next week

ex.en: This week there is a rollover of $14 million.
ex.zh: 本周的累积奖金是1 400 万元。

ex.en: a rollover jackpot/week
ex.zh: 累积头奖；有累积奖金的一周

senses.en: [U] () the act of allowing money that is owed to be paid at a later date﹙
(, ) a cigarette that you make yourself by rolling tobacco in special paper

ex.en: Simon lit a roll-up.
ex.zh: 西蒙点了根烟卷。

senses.en: to make progress,increase or win quickly and easily
senses.zh: 进步神速；快速增加；轻易取胜:

ex.en: The home team romped away to win by 3 goals.
ex.zh: 主队轻而易举地以3分取胜。

senses.en: [NOTE]This verb is mostly used in newspapers.
senses.zh: 这个动词主要用于报章。

senses.en: to do sth easily and quickly

ex.en: She romped through the exam questions.
ex.zh: 她很快就答完了考试题。

senses.en: [NOTE]This verb is mostly used in newspapers.
senses.zh: 这个动词主要用于报章。

senses.en: to move things around or turn them over to try to find sth

ex.en: He was rooting around in the drawer for his keys.
ex.zh: 他翻抽屉找他的钥匙。

ex.en: Something or someone had been rooting through the piles of rubbish.
ex.zh: 垃圾堆被翻动过了。

senses.zh: (通常用于进行时):to support or encourage sb in a sports competition or when they are in a difficult situation给﹙参加比赛或遭遇困难者﹚助威，加油:

ex.en: Good luck — I’ll be rooting for you!
ex.zh: 祝你好运─我会为你加油的！

senses.en: to find the person or thing that is causing a problem and remove or get rid of them
senses.zh: 铲除﹙有害的人或事物﹚；斩草除根；根除:

ex.en: The government has promised to root out police corruption.
ex.zh: 政府承诺要杜绝警务人员贪污。

ex.en: The trouble makers seem to have been rooted out.
ex.zh: 惹是生非的人似乎都已经被揪出来了。

senses.en: to dig or pull up a plant, tree, etc.with its roots

ex.en: Kids have been rooting up plants and carving their names on the trees.
ex.zh: 孩子们一直在拔花草，在树上刻名字。

senses.en: to persuade sb to take part in an activity or to help you, even when they do not want to
senses.zh: 劝说某人加入；说服某人帮忙:

ex.en: We’ll rope Colin in to help us.
ex.zh: 我们要游说科林来帮助我们。

ex.en: I got roped into washing all the dirty dishes.
ex.zh: 我被说服洗所有的脏盘子。

senses.en: [NOTE]This phrasal verb is often used in the passive.
senses.zh: 这个短语动词常用于被动语态。

senses.en: to separate one area from another with ropes, in order to stop people from entering it

ex.en: The scene of the crime had been roped off.
ex.zh: 犯罪现场用绳子圈起了。

senses.en: to gradually decay

ex.en: The window frame had rotted away.
ex.zh: 窗框已经烂了。

senses.en: to draw or write the main parts of sth without including all the details

ex.en: She roughed out the design on the back of an envelope.
ex.zh: 她在信封背面勾画设计草图。

ex.en: I’ve roughed out a few ideas for the book.
ex.zh: 我给这本书草拟了几个构想。

senses.en: to hurt sb by hitting or kicking them, especially in order to frighten or warn them
senses.zh: 殴打， 施以暴力﹙ 以示恐吓或警告﹚:

ex.en: They didn’t want to kill him, just rough him up a little.
ex.zh: 他们并不想杀他，只是让他吃了点皮肉之苦。

ex.en: Demonstrators claimed they had been roughed up by the police.
ex.zh: 示威者声称他们遭到警察殴打。

senses.en: to give a smooth curved shape to the edge of sth
senses.zh: 除去……的稜角；使……的边缘光滑:

ex.en: I rounded off the corners with sandpaper.
ex.zh: 我用砂纸把稜角打磨光滑。

senses.en: to suddenly speak angrily to sb and criticize or attack them

ex.en: He rounded on her angrily and told her to keep her mouth shut.
ex.zh: 他突然怒气冲冲地嗬斥了她并让她闭嘴。

senses.en: to bring together a number of people, animals or objects in one place

ex.en: to round up cattle/sheep
ex.zh: 圈起牛/羊

ex.en: The gang were rounded up and put in jail.
ex.zh: 这个帮派被逮捕并且投进了监狱。

senses.en: [usually sing.]
a brief summary of the most important points of news or sport,for example on a television or radio news programme

ex.en: a news round-up
ex.zh: 综合新闻报道

ex.en: a round-up of the day’s events
ex.zh: 今日赛事综述

senses.en: an act of bringing people or animals together in one place

ex.en: a round-up of wild ponies
ex.zh: 对野生矮马的圈起

ex.en: a round-up of suspects
ex.zh: 嫌疑犯的集中拘押

senses.en: to increase/decrease a number to the next highest or lowest whole number﹙
senses.zh: 把数字﹚上捨入，下捨入；﹙将数字调高或调低﹚使成为整数:

ex.en: He rounded the price down to $900.
ex.zh: 他把价格捨为900 元。

ex.en: Totals should be rounded up to the nearest whole number.
ex.zh: 总数应该捨为最接近的整数。

senses.en: to live or work together with sb in a satisfactory way﹙

ex.en: We rub along all right with the neighbours.
ex.zh: 我们和邻居处得很融洽。

senses.en: to rub the skin of a person, an animal, etc. with sth such as a towel, to make it clean and dry

ex.en: She rubbed herself down with a towel.
ex.zh: 她用毛巾擦乾身体。

ex.en: After exercise each horse must be rubbed down.
ex.zh: 训练之后必须把每匹马都擦乾净。

senses.en: [usually sing.] an act of rubbing sb/sth yourself with a towel, for example﹙
) to make sth clean by wiping it with a cloth, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 用布等﹚将……擦乾净，揩乾净:

ex.en: Rub the walls down well before painting them.
ex.zh: 上漆之前先把墙壁擦乾净。

senses.en: to make the surface of sth smooth by rubbing it with special paper, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 用专用的纸等﹚将某物打磨光滑:

ex.en: He rubbed the woodwork down with sandpaper.
ex.zh: 他用砂纸把木结构的部份打磨光滑。

senses.en: to say sth to sb which reminds them of sth that they feel embarrassed or guilty about and would like to forget
senses.zh: 提及令人尴尬﹙或愧疚﹚的事； 触及痛处:

senses.en: to spread a substance over a surface while pressing firmly with your fingers, a cloth, etc.

ex.en: Rub the lotion into your skin with your fingers.
ex.zh: 用手指将润肤液揉进皮肤里。

ex.en: Spray on the polish and rub it in well.
ex.zh: 喷上上光蜡并打匀。

senses.en: to be removed from sth by rubbing; to remove sth from sth by rubbing﹙

ex.en: Somebody’s used the wrong kind of pen on the whiteboard and it won’t rub off.
ex.zh: 有人在白写字板上用错了笔，擦不掉了。

ex.en: He quickly rubbed mud off his face.
ex.zh: 他迅速擦掉了脸上的泥。

senses.en: to murder sb

ex.en: He was rubbed out before he could give evidence.
ex.zh: 他还没来得及作证就被人做了。

senses.en: to form untidy folds; to make sth do this﹙

ex.en: Your blouse has rucked up at the back.
ex.zh: 你的衬衫后面起褶儿了。

ex.en: Her skirt was rucked up.
ex.zh: 她的裙子皱了。

senses.en: to decide you do not want to or are not able to do sth; to decide that you are not suitable for sth
senses.zh: 认为自己不想做﹙或没有能力、不适合等﹚ :

ex.en: Smith has not ruled himself out of Saturday’s game.
ex.zh: 史密斯没排除自己参加星期六的比赛的可能。

senses.en: a small car, boat or aircraft, used mainly for short journeys﹙
senses.zh: 短途﹚小汽车，小船，小飞机

senses.en: ) a person who moves from place to place
to meet sb or find sth by chance

ex.en: I ran across Mary in town yesterday.
ex.zh: 我昨天在城里遇见玛丽了。

senses.en: to try to persuade sb to have a romantic or sexual relationship with you

ex.en: He’s always running after younger women.
ex.zh: 他总在追求年轻女子。

senses.en: to run to try to catch sb/sth; to chase sb/sth

ex.en: They ran after the thief but he got away.
ex.zh: 他们追赶小偷，可他跑掉了。

senses.en: , ) used to tell sb, especially a child, to go away and not disturb you﹙
senses.zh: 尤用以命令儿童﹚走开，一边去:

ex.en: Run along now, children, I’m busy.
ex.zh: 孩子们，都走开吧，我忙着呢。

senses.en: to run in different directions, especially in an excited way﹙
senses.zh: 兴奋地﹚各处跑，东奔西跑:

ex.en: It’s a lovely park to run around in.
ex.zh: 这个公园不错，可以到处跑。

ex.en: The children were running round the house with no clothes on.
ex.zh: 孩子们光着身子在房子里各处跑。

senses.en: to move very quickly from place to place, being very busy

ex.en: I ran around like a mad thing all day.
ex.zh: 我一整天像疯了一样跑来跑去。

ex.en: He’s been running about the place organizing the party.
ex.zh: 他一直在这里四处奔走组织聚会。

senses.en: to be very busy doing a lot of things for sb,when they should be able to do them for themselves
senses.zh: 替﹙某人﹚做他力所能及的事；替……忙活:

ex.en: His mother shouldn’t have to run around after him.
ex.zh: 他的母亲不该替他忙活。

ex.en: She spends all her time running round after the children.
ex.zh: 她所有的时间都无谓地花在照料孩子上。

senses.en: to spend a lot of time with sb

ex.en: Their son is running around with a bad crowd.
ex.zh: 他们的儿子与一帮坏人混在一起。

senses.en: to run towards sb to attack them or as if you were going to attack them

ex.en: He ran at me with a knife.
ex.zh: 他拿着刀朝我冲过来。

senses.en: (from sb/sth) to move quickly away from sb/a place; to escape from sb/a place

ex.en: A man was seen running away from the shop.
ex.zh: 有人看见一名男子从商店里跑出去了。

ex.en: ‘Bye then,’ she said, and ran away without looking back.
ex.zh: “再见吧。”她说完头也不回拔腿就走。

senses.en: (from sth)to leave the place where you are living or staying suddenly and secretly because you are unhappy

ex.en: She ran away from home on several occasions.
ex.zh: 她几次离家出走。

ex.en: He ran away and joined a circus.
ex.zh: 他离家出走后进了马戏团。

senses.en: to leave a person or a place to try to avoid doing sth﹙
senses.zh: 为免做某事而﹚离开某人，离开某地；避开；躲避:

ex.en: Don’t run away — I want your advice.
ex.zh: 别跑开─你得帮我出主意。

senses.en: [only before noun]
(of a situation or an event
senses.zh: 情况或事情) happening quickly and easily and not able to be controlled迅猛的；急骤的:

ex.en: The movie has been a runaway success.
ex.zh: 这部电影一炮打响。

ex.en: The game was a runaway victory for Liverpool.
ex.zh: 利物浦队这场比赛赢得乾净利落。

senses.en: (of an animal or a vehicle
senses.zh: 动物或车辆) moving, but no longer under the control of the rider or driver失去控制的；失控的:

ex.en: a runaway horse
ex.zh: 脱繮的马

senses.en: a person who has left their home or the place where they are staying suddenly and secretly because they are unhappy there

ex.en: a 16-year-old runaway
ex.zh: 离家出走的16 岁少年

senses.en: to leave your home, husband,wife, etc. secretly with sb else in order to marry them or have a sexual relationship with them

ex.en: They ran away to Scotland.
ex.zh: 他们私奔到了苏格兰。

ex.en: We think John and Susie have run off together.
ex.zh: 我们认为约翰和苏西一起私奔了。

senses.en: to try to avoid dealing with or thinking about sth because it is difficult or unpleasant

ex.en: He is running away from his responsibilities.
ex.zh: 他在逃避责任。

ex.en: You can’t just run away from difficult situations — you must face up to them.
ex.zh: 你不能只是迴避─必须直接面对困难。

senses.en: to win sth clearly or easily

ex.en: Their team are running away with the championship.
ex.zh: 他们队即将轻松获得冠军。

ex.en: She ran away with the show (= she was easily the best performer).
ex.zh: 她轻而易举地成为最佳演员。

senses.en: ) to believe sth that is not true
to show sb sth or tell them about an idea, a proposal, etc. in order to get their reaction to it
senses.zh: 给某人看，说给某人听﹙以观察其反应﹚:

ex.en: I’ve got a few ideas I’d like to run by you.
ex.zh: 我有几个主意想说给你听听。

ex.en: Run that past me again.
ex.zh: 把它再给我看看。

senses.en: to lose power or stop working; to make sth do this﹙

ex.en: I think the batteries are running down.
ex.zh: 我想电池没电了。

ex.en: If you leave your headlights on, you’ll run the battery down.
ex.zh: 让前灯亮着就会耗尽电池的。

senses.en: [usually sing.] ()
a reduction in the size, number, amount or importance of sth

ex.en: The public are complaining about the rundown of health services.
ex.zh: 公众抱怨医疗宪生服务紧缩。

senses.en: a description or an explanation of sth, especially the main points
senses.zh: 解释； 要略； 综述:

ex.en: a rundown of the history of each team
ex.zh: 各队历史概略

senses.en: (of a building or an area
senses.zh: 建筑或地区) in poor condition; that has not been looked after破旧的； 疏于管理的； 失修的:

ex.en: a run-down area of East London
ex.zh: 伦敦东部破败的地区

senses.en: (of a business, etc.
senses.zh: 商业机构等) not as busy or as active as it used to be衰微的；衰落的

senses.en: [not before noun] (of a person
senses.zh: 人) tired, weak and not in good health after having worked too hard, etc.衰弱；虚弱:

ex.en: I’m feeling a bit run-down.
ex.zh: 我觉得有点虚弱。

senses.en: to look quickly at a list; to quickly read and mention the items on it

ex.en: Her eyes ran down the figures on the page.
ex.zh: 她浏览了一下这一页的数字。

ex.en: She ran her eyes down the page.
ex.zh: 她迅速浏览了这一页。

senses.en: to pass, or to make sth pass, downwards over a surface﹙

ex.en: She ran her finger down the page.
ex.zh: 她用手指往下抹了抹那一页。

senses.en: (of a vehicle or its driver
senses.zh: 车辆或司机) to hit a person or an animal and knock them/it to the ground把……撞倒:

ex.en: The cyclist was run down by a lorry.
ex.zh: 骑自行车的人被一辆货车撞倒了。

ex.en: You nearly ran down that pedestrian.
ex.zh: 你差点撞了那个行人。

senses.en: to criticize yourself, often unfairly

ex.en: You’re always running yourself down!
ex.zh: 你总是贬低自己！

senses.en: to visit sb for a short time in an informal way; to go somewhere quickly on your way to somewhere else
senses.zh: 顺便探望﹙某人﹚；串门子；顺路去﹙某处﹚:

ex.en: I’ll run in on my way home.
ex.zh: 我回家时顺便去看看。

ex.en: Can you run into the dry-cleaner’s on your way to work?
ex.zh: 你上班时顺路到乾洗店去一下好吗？

senses.en: , ) to arrest sb and take them to a police station

ex.en: She was run in for shoplifting.
ex.zh: 她因为到商店里偷东西被抓到局子里了。

senses.en: to take sb by car to the centre of town, etc.
senses.zh: 用车送某人去﹙市中心等﹚:

ex.en: I need to go into town. Can you run me in?
ex.zh: 我需要进一次城。你开车送我好吗？

senses.en: to meet sb by chance

ex.en: Guess who I ran into today?
ex.zh: 猜猜我今天碰见谁了？

ex.en: You rarely run into people you know in London.
ex.zh: 在伦敦很难遇见熟人。

senses.en: to accidentally crash into sb/sth; to make a vehicle do this

ex.en: The car went out of control and ran into a tree.
ex.zh: 汽车失控撞了一棵树。

ex.en: The lorry behind ran into the back of me(= my car).
ex.zh: 后面的大货车撞了我的汽车后尾。

senses.en: to experience difficulties or problems
senses.zh: 遭遇， 遇到﹙ 困难或问题﹚ :

ex.en: We ran into problems right from the beginning of the project.
ex.zh: 从这个项目一开始我们就遇到问题。

senses.en: to move quickly away from sb/a place;to escape from sb/a place

ex.en: The thief ran off down a side street.
ex.zh: 小偷从小巷逃跑了。

ex.en: They ran off laughing.
ex.zh: 他们大笑着跑掉了。

senses.en: to leave a place secretly

ex.en: She ran off in the middle of the night.
ex.zh: 她是半夜离开的。

senses.en: to drain or flow from sb/sth

ex.en: Water runs off the fields into the valley.
ex.zh: 水从地里流进了峡谷。

ex.en: Sweat was running off her.
ex.zh: 她汗流浃背。

senses.en: [C] () rain, water or other liquid that runs off land and into rivers, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 雨、水或其他液体的﹚径流，径流量

senses.en: (of a machine,etc.
senses.zh: 机器等) to use a particular type of power in order to operate a machine以……为动力:

ex.en: The outboard motor runs off an ordinary car battery.
ex.zh: 舷外发动机以一个普通汽车蓄电池来推动。

senses.en: to continue to run in the same direction﹙
senses.zh: 向相同方向﹚继续跑，接着跑:

ex.en: I’ll stop here, you run on ahead.
ex.zh: 我在这儿打住了，你接着往前跑吧。

senses.en: to continue longer than is necessary or expected

ex.en: I don’t want the meeting to run on.
ex.zh: 我不想延长会议。

senses.en: to use a particular type of power or fuel to make a machine or a vehicle work
senses.zh: 用﹙某种动力或燃料﹚使运转:

ex.en: You can run the car on any type of unleaded petrol.
ex.zh: 这辆汽车可使用任何类型的无铅汽油做燃料。

senses.en: () to force sb to leave a place

ex.en: He vowed to run them out of town.
ex.zh: 他发誓把他们赶出这座城。

senses.en: to leave sb that you live or work with, especially when they need your help

ex.en: She ran out on him as soon as things got difficult.
ex.zh: 情况一变得艰难她就离他而去。

senses.en: to move over a surface; to make sth do this﹙

ex.en: I let the cold water run over me.
ex.zh: 我把凉水浇在身上。

ex.en: She ran her eye over the figures on the page.
ex.zh: 她浏览了那一页上的数字。

senses.en: to read through or think about sth quickly; to practise sth
senses.zh: 快速阅读﹙ 或思索﹚；练习:

ex.en: Let’s run over the plans again.
ex.zh: 我们再把计划很快地过一遍吧。

ex.en: I ran over the possibilities in my mind.
ex.zh: 我在脑子里合计了一下这些可能性。

senses.en: (of a vehicle or its driver
senses.zh: 车辆或司机) to knock a person or an animal down and often pass over their body or part of it撞倒并碾过﹙人或动物﹚:

ex.en: Two children were run over by a truck and killed.
ex.zh: 两名儿童被一辆卡车轧死了。

ex.en: I ran over a cat last night.
ex.zh: 我昨晚轧了一只猫。

senses.en: to be present in every part of sth

ex.en: There is a common theme running through all of her novels.
ex.zh: 有一个共同主题贯穿她所有的小说。

ex.en: The English title picks up a thread running through the film.
ex.zh: 英文标题和贯穿影片的线索相呼应。

senses.en: to discuss, examine or read sth quickly
senses.zh: 匆匆讨论﹙或检查﹚；快速阅读:

ex.en: He ran through his check list one more time.
ex.zh: 他再浏览了一下清单。

ex.en: Can you run through some of these figures with me?
ex.zh: 和我一起核对一下这里的一些数据好吗？

senses.en: to perform, act or practise sth

ex.en: Could we run through Act 3 again, please?
ex.zh: 请大家再来排练一下第3幕好吗？

senses.en: a practice for an event or a performance

ex.en: We’re having the main technical run-through of the play tonight.
ex.zh: 我们今晚进行这部戏的主要技术连排。

senses.en: to go to sb for help, advice, protection,etc.
senses.zh: 向某人寻求帮助﹙或建议、保护等﹚:

ex.en: If you get hurt, don’t come running to me.
ex.zh: 你要是伤害到自己，可别来找我。

senses.en: to move quickly towards sb/sth

ex.en: She ran up to me, smiling.
ex.zh: 她向我跑来，脸上带着微笑。

senses.en: (in cricket and other sports
senses.zh: 板球和其他体育运动) to run in order to gain speed before you throw a ball, jump a long distance, etc.助跑:

ex.en: Gough is now running up to bowl.
ex.zh: 高夫正在助跑投球。

senses.en: ) the act of running or the distance you run in order to gain speed before you throw a ball, jump a long distance, etc.

ex.en: She took a run-up and kicked the ball.
ex.zh: 她通过助跑踢球。

senses.en: to experience a difficulty or a problem

ex.en: The project keeps running up against the problem of lack of funds.
ex.zh: 这个项目不断地遇到缺乏资金的问题。

ex.en: In this round, he will run up against the previous year’s champion.
ex.zh: 他在这一轮将和去年的冠军交手。

senses.en: to move very quickly from place to place, being very busy

ex.en: I’ve been rushing around all day.
ex.zh: 我整整一天忙得团团转。

ex.en: He rushed about the room tidying.
ex.zh: 他跑来跑去收拾着房间。

senses.en: to do or decide sth very quickly, often without thinking about it for long enough

ex.en: He’s very wary of rushing in and making changes.
ex.zh: 他十分慎重， 不肯贸然改变。

senses.en: used to say that people with little experience will try to do the difficult or dangerous things that people with more experience would not do
to do or decide sth quickly without thinking about it carefully; to make sb do this﹙

ex.en: Don’t go rushing into anything.
ex.zh: 不要贸然采取任何行动。

ex.en: You shouldn’t rush into getting married.
ex.zh: 你不应该仓促结婚。

senses.en: to leave quickly

ex.en: Don’t rush off, I haven’t finished.
ex.zh: 别忙着走，我还没说完呢。

senses.en: to produce sth very quickly

ex.en: They rushed out the posters in time for the festival.
ex.zh: 他们及时为庆祝活动赶制出海报。

ex.en: The book was rushed out by the publishers.
ex.zh: 出版商匆匆发行了这本书。

senses.en: to make sth become official policy, etc. much quicker than normal
senses.zh: 赶快通过﹙ 使成为政策等﹚ :

ex.en: The legislation has been rushed through.
ex.zh: 这条法规匆匆通过了。

ex.en: They rushed the bill through Parliament.
ex.zh: 他们使议案在议会仓促通过。

senses.en: to prepare or provide sth for sb very quickly without planning; to find sb very quickly
senses.zh: 仓促准备﹙或提供﹚；迅速找到﹙某人﹚:

ex.en: I’ll rustle up some lunch up for you.
ex.zh: 我给你马上弄些午饭来。

ex.en: I rustled up a few helpers to hand out leaflets.
ex.zh: 我仓促拉了几个帮手来分发传单。

senses.en: to lie down to rest or relax

ex.en: We sacked out on the couch and watched a video.
ex.zh: 我们躺在沙发上看录像。

senses.en: to give sb/yourself a difficult or unpleasant task or responsibility to deal with
senses.zh: 使某人﹙或自己﹚担负重活儿﹙或讨厌的工作、责任﹚:

ex.en: I’ve been saddled with my brother’s kids for the weekend (= I have to take care of them).
ex.zh: 我这个周末要照看我哥哥的孩子。

ex.en: He had saddled himself with huge debts.
ex.zh: 他背上了巨大的债务

senses.en: to prevent sth bad from happening to sth; to keep sth safe from harm or damage﹙
senses.zh: 保护别人/某物/自己﹚使免受…的伤害﹙或损失等﹚:

ex.en: Safeguard against theft by installing a burglar alarm.
ex.zh: 安装防盗警报器以防盗窃。

ex.en: The leaflet shows you how to safeguard your home against electrical dangers and accidents.
ex.zh: 宣传单上说明如何防止家里发生与电力有关的危险和事故。

senses.en: to succeed in an examination, a test, etc. very easily

ex.en: She sailed through her final exams.
ex.zh: 她顺利通过了期终考试。

senses.en: to leave a place in a determined or enthusiastic way

ex.en: After lunch she sallied forth for a short walk.
ex.zh: 午饭后她赶忙出去散步了。

senses.en: to save money, etc. for the future,often secretly or dishonestly﹙
senses.zh: 常指秘密地或以欺瞒手段﹚ 贮存， 储蓄:

ex.en: He claimed she had salted money away in Brazil.
ex.zh: 他声称她把钱偷偷存到了巴西。

ex.en: $10 billion had been salted away in banks.
ex.zh: 秘密存入银行的有100 亿元。

senses.en: to make sth smooth by rubbing it with strong, rough paper﹙

ex.en: Sand the doors down before you paint them.
ex.zh: 油漆之前把门打磨光滑。

senses.en: to fit sth/sb into a very small space between two other things or people

ex.en: I was sandwiched between two large men on the back seat.
ex.zh: 我在后排座位上被两个高大的男子挤在中间。

ex.en: The shop is sandwiched between a bank and a café.
ex.zh: 铺子就夹在一家银行和一家小餐馆中间。

senses.en: to put sth between two things to join them﹙

ex.en: Sandwich the cakes together with cream.
ex.zh: 用奶油把蛋糕粘在一起。

senses.en: to use less of sth or not more than necessary﹙

ex.en: He saved on electricity by using candles.
ex.zh: 他使用蜡烛以便省电。

ex.en: Get your tickets early and save $5 on the cost of an adult ticket.
ex.zh: 早点买票，成人票可少花5元钱。

senses.en: to keep your money instead of spending it, especially because you want to buy a particular thing﹙

ex.en: She’s saving up for a new computer.
ex.zh: 她在攒钱买新电脑。

ex.en: I saved up all my wages to buy my parents a present.
ex.zh: 我省下了全部工资给父母买礼物。

senses.en: to keep sth to use or enjoy in the future

ex.en: I save up the week’s newspapers to read at weekends.
ex.zh: 我把一周的报纸攒到周末看。

senses.en: to reduce sth in size or importance
senses.zh: 减少，缩小﹙规模或重要性﹚:

ex.en: The company has scaled down its training programmes this year.
ex.zh: 公司缩小了今年的培训计划。

ex.en: Police are scaling down the search for the attacker.
ex.zh: 警方正在缩小对攻击者的搜寻规模。

senses.en: to increase the size or importance of sth
senses.zh: 增加，扩大﹙规模或重要性﹚:

ex.en: We’re deciding how to scale up our operation.
ex.zh: 我们正在考虑如何扩大我们的行动。

senses.en: to make sb/sth leave or stay away by frightening them

ex.en: She used a whistle to scare away her attacker.
ex.zh: 她吹响哨子吓跑了攻击她的人。

ex.en: The noise scared the birds off.
ex.zh: 响声惊飞了鸟儿。

senses.en: to make sb do sth by frightening them
senses.zh: 威胁，恐吓﹙使某人做某事﹚:

ex.en: Her threats finally scared him into action.
ex.zh: 她的威胁最终使他采取了行动。

ex.en: He was scared into signing a confession.
ex.zh: 他迫于威胁在供状上签了字。

senses.en: to accidentally make sb afraid of or nervous about sth they were planning to do

ex.en: Many investors were scared off by the rumours.
ex.zh: 很多投资者都给传闻吓跑了。

ex.en: Don’t act too interested or you’ll scare him off (= a boyfriend).
ex.zh: 别表现得太投入，否则你会把他吓跑的。

senses.en: to find sb/sth or to make sth by using whatever is available﹙

ex.en: I’ll see if I can scare up enough chairs for us all.
ex.zh: 我来看看能不能给大家凑够椅子。

ex.en: I’ll try to scare up some friends to come and help us.
ex.zh: 我尽量拉些朋友来帮帮忙。

senses.en: ( ,scoop sth 'out of sth) to remove sth from the inside of sth else using a curved tool, such as a spoon, or your hand﹙
senses.zh: 用勺子、手等从…中﹚挖出，舀出… :

ex.en: Scoop all the seeds out of the fruit.
ex.zh: 把果实里的籽全挖出来。

senses.en: to move or lift sb/sth using a quick continuous movement﹙

ex.en: I scooped up a handful of sweets.
ex.zh: 我抓起一把糖果。

ex.en: She scooped the baby up into her arms.
ex.zh: 她一下子把孩子抱到怀里。

senses.en: to win or get sth easily, especially a large sum of money or a prize
senses.zh: 轻松赢得，轻易得到﹙ 巨款或大奖等﹚ :

ex.en: The Democrat party scooped up four fifths of the seats.
ex.zh: 民主党没费吹灰之力便赢得了五分之四的席位。

senses.en: to move along on a seat to make room for another person﹙

ex.en: Scoot over and make room for your sister.
ex.zh: 往里挪一下，给你妹妹腾个座儿。

ex.en: ( ) Scoot over, men! Women golfers are on the increase.
ex.zh: 让位吧，男士们！打高尔夫的女士越来越多了。

senses.en: to look for sb/sth interesting or attractive; to search out sb/sth

ex.en: We scoped out a place to spend the weekend.
ex.zh: 我们找到了一个地方过周末。

senses.en: ) to show that you are better than sb, especially by making clever remarks, for example in an argument

ex.en: He’s always trying to score off his colleagues.
ex.zh: 他总是和同事抬杠。

senses.en: to draw a line or lines through sth in a text to show that you do not want it

ex.en: The last paragraph had been scored out.
ex.zh: 最后一段给画掉了。

ex.en: He neatly scored through the word ‘impossible’.
ex.zh: 他在impossible一词上画了一条笔直的线。

senses.en: to search an area or different places to try to find sb/sth﹙
senses.zh: 在某处﹚侦察，搜索，勘察﹙以找寻人或物﹚:

ex.en: I’ll go and scout around for some water.
ex.zh: 我去找些水来。

senses.en: to find out what sth is like or where sth is, by searching﹙

ex.en: A team travelled to Moscow to scout out possible places for a meeting.
ex.zh: 一个小组去了莫斯科寻找可以开会的地方。

ex.en: The company is scouting out business opportunities in Vietnam.
ex.zh: 公司正在越南寻找商机。

senses.en: to use your fingers to search for sth quickly or with difficulty﹙
senses.zh: 用手指迅速或困难地﹚摸索着找:

ex.en: She scrabbled around in her bag for her glasses.
ex.zh: 她在包里摸来摸去找眼镜。

senses.en: to scratch at sth with small,hurried movements

ex.en: She was scrabbling at the earth with her fingers.
ex.zh: 她用手指不断抓挠着泥土。

senses.en: to manage to live on the money you have, although you do not have much﹙
senses.zh: 靠…﹚勉强维持生计，煳口，艰难度日:

ex.en: I can just scrape by on what my parents give me.
ex.zh: 我靠父母给我的那点钱只能勉强度日。

senses.en: to manage to get a job, a position, a place at college, etc., but with difficulty
senses.zh: 勉强获得﹙工作、职位、入学资格等﹚:

ex.en: I just managed to scrape into university.
ex.zh: 我勉强升入了大学。

ex.en: He scraped in with 180 votes.
ex.zh: 他以180票勉强当选。

senses.en: to remove sth from a surface by moving sth sharp and hard like a knife across it﹙

ex.en: He spent all day scraping paint off the walls.
ex.zh: 他一整天都在刮墙壁上的漆。

senses.en: ) to just manage to make enough money to live
to succeed with difficulty in doing sth, especially in passing an exam
senses.zh: 艰难完成；勉强通过﹙考试﹚:

ex.en: I might scrape through () if I’m lucky.
ex.zh: 要是走运的话，我也许可以勉强及格。

ex.en: She just scraped through law school.
ex.zh: 她勉强从法学院毕业。

senses.en: to obtain or collect sth such as an amount of money with difficulty
senses.zh: 勉强凑集；费力聚拢； 艰难筹措:

ex.en: They managed to scrape together $1 200 and printed 3 000 copies of the comic.
ex.zh: 他们勉强凑了1 200 元印了3 000 份连环画册。

senses.en: to search for sth in a way that is not very organized, by looking at different things, looking on the ground, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 茫无头绪地﹚搜寻，查寻， 查找:

ex.en: He was scratching around on the ground for clues.
ex.zh: 他在地面上寻找线索。

senses.en: to remove sth from a surface by rubbing with your nails, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 用指甲等﹚ 刮掉， 擦去:

ex.en: She scratched the paint off to see what was underneath.
ex.zh: 她刮开油漆看看下面是什么。

senses.en: to remove a word, especially a name, from sth written, usually by putting a line through it

ex.en: Their names had been scratched out.
ex.zh: 他们的名字被勾掉了。

senses.en: to be very obvious or noticeable; to demand attention

ex.en: The mistakes just scream out at you.
ex.zh: 这些错误显而易见。

ex.en: The cake was screaming out to be eaten.
ex.zh: 那块蛋糕令人馋涎欲滴。

senses.en: to separate or hide an area of a room etc. from another area by putting a tall piece of furniture or equipment in front of it or around it﹙

ex.en: Part of the room had been screened off with a curtain.
ex.zh: 房间的一部份用帷幔隔开了。

senses.en: to decide not to include sb/sth, or not to allow sb to join an organization,enter a country, etc. because you think they may not be suitable or may cause trouble
senses.zh: 把…排除在外；不准某人参加﹙组织﹚；拒绝某人入境:

ex.en: Unsuitable candidates were screened out.
ex.zh: 不合格的候选者给淘汰了。

ex.en: His job is to screen out inquiries unlikely to result in a sale.
ex.zh: 他的工作是排除不是旨在买东西的咨询。

senses.en: to prevent sth harmful from entering or going through sth

ex.en: It is essential to screen out ultraviolet rays.
ex.zh: 挡住紫外线是很有必要的。

ex.en: A window blind will screen out too much light.
ex.zh: 窗帘能遮挡过强的光线。

senses.en: to have sex with a lot of different people
senses.zh: 乱搞男女关系；漤交异性

senses.en: ) to waste time doing silly or useless activities

ex.en: Stop screwing around and do some work!
ex.zh: 别瞎晃荡了，干点正事吧！

senses.en: to attach sth firmly to sth else using screws

ex.en: Screw the lid of the box down securely.
ex.zh: 用螺丝钉把箱子盖拧牢。

senses.en: to fasten the top on a container by twisting it around
senses.zh: 将﹙容器的盖子﹚拧紧；旋紧:

ex.en: Is the top screwed on tightly?
ex.zh: 盖子拧紧了吗？

senses.en: to cheat sb and prevent them from having sth that they should have

ex.en: She tried to screw him out of his winnings.
ex.zh: 她试图把他赢的钱骗走。

senses.en: to trick sb in order to obtain sth valuable from them; to treat sb badly, especially by deceiving them

ex.en: He screwed her over and took all her money.
ex.zh: 他骗走了她所有的钱。

senses.en: to do sth badly or spoil sth﹙

ex.en: I was trying to be helpful, but I screwed up again.
ex.zh: 我本来想帮忙，却又一次搞砸了。

ex.en: She screwed up all the arrangements.
ex.zh: 她把计划全毁了。

senses.en: a situation that has been dealt with very badly; a bad mistake

ex.en: There was a screw-up over the bookings.
ex.zh: 预订情况一片狼藉。

senses.en: to make sb so upset or confused that they are unable to deal with problems in life
senses.zh: 使烦恼得不能正常生活；使神经不正常:

ex.en: Her parents have really screwed her up.
ex.zh: 她的父母实在是把她逼疯了。

senses.en: upset and anxious,especially because of sth bad that has happened to you in the past﹙
senses.zh: 因经历所致﹚焦虑而紧张的:

ex.en: a screwed-up kid
ex.zh: 神经紧张的孩子

senses.en: to write sth quickly and carelessly

ex.en: She scribbled down the directions on her pad.
ex.zh: 她在拍纸簿上潦草地记下了指示。

senses.en: to move down/ up or backwards/forwards in the text on a computer screen so that you can read different parts of it﹙

ex.en: She scrolled down to the end of the document.
ex.zh: 她把屏幕磙动到了文件末尾。

senses.en: to search around in different places for sth, especially if it is difficult to find or there is not much available

ex.en: He scrounged around in his desk drawer for a paper clip.
ex.zh: 他在书桌抽屉里翻来翻去找纸夹。

senses.en: to remove sth from the surface of sth by rubbing it hard with a brush, etc.﹙

ex.en: Scrub all that mud off the walls.
ex.zh: 把墙壁上的泥全刷掉。

senses.en: to clean the inside of sth by rubbing it hard with a brush and usually with soap and water﹙
senses.zh: 用刷子、肥皂等﹚把某物从里到外擦洗乾净:

ex.en: He scrubbed out the pans and left them to drain.
ex.zh: 他把锅刷乾净，放在那儿烘乾。

ex.en: The cupboards are scrubbed out every week.
ex.zh: 每周都要清洁碗柜。

senses.en: (of a doctor, nurse, etc.
senses.zh: 医生、护士等) to wash your hands and arms very thoroughly before performing a medical operation﹙手术前﹚擦洗手和臂:

ex.en: The surgeon scrubbed up and put on his gloves.
ex.zh: 外科医生洗乾净手臂后戴上手套。

ex.en: He asked to scrub in for surgery.
ex.zh: 他要求擦洗手臂准备做手术。

senses.en: to squeeze sth into a small round shape in your hands

ex.en: He scrunched up the piece of paper and threw it at me.
ex.zh: 他把那张纸揉成一个小团，朝我扔过来。

senses.en: to keep sth inside a container so that none of it can escape

ex.en: The foil packet seals in the flavour.
ex.zh: 锡纸盒保存了味道。

senses.en: to close an envelope, etc. by sticking the edges of the opening together

ex.en: He sealed up the envelope and wrote the address on it.
ex.zh: 他粘好信封然后写上地址。

senses.en: to close sth completely so that nothing can get in or out

ex.en: I sealed up the windows to keep out the fumes.
ex.zh: 我关上窗户挡住烟。

senses.en: to look for sb/sth until you find them

ex.en: He’s searching out some old pictures to show us.
ex.zh: 他在找些旧照片给我们看。

ex.en: She wanted to search out her real parents.
ex.zh: 她想找亲生父母。

senses.en: to deal with sth; to make arrangements for sth to be done

ex.en: I’ll go and see about lunch.
ex.zh: 我去安排一下午餐。

ex.en: I must see about getting someone to help you with the kids.
ex.zh: 我一定得找人来帮你照看孩子。

senses.en: to go with sb into a room, building, etc. to make sure that they get there safely

ex.en: After seeing her in (= into her home), he rode off without a word.
ex.zh: 把她送到家之后，他一句话都没说就开车走了。

senses.en: to believe that sb/sth has a particular quality or characteristic, especially a good one
senses.zh: 认为…有﹙某种品质或特徵﹚:

ex.en: I don’t know what she sees in him (= I can’t understand why she likes him or finds him attractive).
ex.zh: 我弄不明白她看上了他哪儿了。

ex.en: He sees good in everyone.
ex.zh: 他觉得每个人都有善良的一面。

senses.en: to go to a station, an airport,etc. to say goodbye to sb who is going on a journey

ex.en: We all went to the airport to see her off.
ex.zh: 我们全都去机场给她送行。

senses.en: )to force sb to leave a place, for example by chasing them

ex.en: The dogs soon saw off the burglars.
ex.zh: 几条狗不一会儿就撵走了窃贼。

senses.en: to defeat sb

ex.en: She saw off her opponent and now goes into the final.
ex.zh: 她击败对手进入了决赛。

senses.en: to be strong enough to resist sth

ex.en: The company saw off the threat of a takeover.
ex.zh: 公司经受住了被收购的威胁。

senses.en: to go with sb out of a building, etc. to make sure that they find the way

ex.en: Jay saw the last guests out and locked the door.
ex.zh: 杰伊送走最后几位客人就锁上了门。

ex.en: Don’t get up. I’ll see myself out.
ex.zh: 别起来。我自己会出去的。

senses.en: to stay in the same place, do the same things, or survive, until the end of sth

ex.en: She promised to see out the rest of her contract.
ex.zh: 她答应坚持干到合同期满。

senses.en: to last until the end of sth

ex.en: We have enough fuel to see the winter out.
ex.zh: 我们有足够的燃料过冬。

senses.en: to visit and look at a place carefully

ex.en: We’d like to see over the flat again before we rent it.
ex.zh: 我们想再好好看看这个单元之后才租用。

senses.en: to realize the truth about sb/sth so that you are not deceived

ex.en: We saw through him straight away.
ex.zh: 我们一下子就识破他了。

ex.en: I can see through your little game (= trick).
ex.zh: 我看透了你的小把戏。

senses.en: to give sb support to enable them to survive a difficult experience or a particular period of time

ex.en: His courage and good humour saw him through.
ex.zh: 他靠勇气和乐观的性格挺了过来。

ex.en: She saw him through the months after his accident.
ex.zh: 在他出事故之后的几个月中，她一直陪伴着他。

senses.en: to not give up a task, project, etc. until it is completed
senses.zh: 把﹙任务、工程等﹚进行到底；坚持完成:

ex.en: She’s determined to see the job through.
ex.zh: 她决心完成这项工作。

senses.en: to deal with sb/sth that needs attention

ex.en: I’ll see to the kids.
ex.zh: 我来照看孩子。

ex.en: Lin was great and saw to everything.
ex.zh: 林真了不起，把一切都包了。

senses.en: to make sure that sth happens

ex.en: Can you see to it that everyone knows the date of the meeting?
ex.zh: 你保证把会期通知到每个人，可以吗？

senses.en: to look for and find sb/sth,especially when this means using a lot of effort
senses.zh: 寻求，挑选，物色﹙人或事物﹚:

ex.en: He sought her out to ask her advice.
ex.zh: 他找到她讨主意。

ex.en: She’s always seeking out new business opportunities.
ex.zh: 她不断发掘新的商机。

senses.en: to flow away slowly and in small quantities

ex.en: Water had been slowly seeping away from the pond.
ex.zh: 池塘里的水一直在慢慢渗漏。

ex.en: ( ) My anger began to seep away.
ex.zh: 我的怒火开始消下去了。

senses.en: to move smoothly from one song, subject, place, etc. to another﹙
senses.zh: 顺利﹚转到，接入﹙另一首歌、话题、地方等﹚:

ex.en: a spiritual that segued into a singalong chorus
ex.zh: 后面紧接合唱曲的灵歌

ex.en: He then segued into a discussion of children’s rights.
ex.zh: 他接着转到了对儿童权利的讨论。

senses.en: to suddenly show a lot of interest in sth, especially because you can use it to your advantage
senses.zh: 突然大为关注，抓住﹙可利用的事物﹚:

ex.en: The scandal was immediately seized upon by the press.
ex.zh: 报章立即对这件丑闻抓住不放。

ex.en: Peter seized eagerly on all opportunities for conversation.
ex.zh: 彼得逮谁跟谁聊。

senses.en: to sell all or part of an industry, a company or a piece of land
senses.zh: 售出，卖掉﹙产业、公司或土地﹚:

ex.en: Unwanted land next to the farm was sold off.
ex.zh: 农场附近闲置的那片地给卖掉了。

ex.en: The government decided to sell off state companies.
ex.zh: 政府决定出售国有公司。

senses.en: the sale by the government of an industry or a service to individual people or private companies﹙
senses.zh: 国有企业的﹚出售；私有化:

ex.en: the proposed sell-off of the rail company
ex.zh: 建议的铁路公司私有化

ex.en: sell-off plans
ex.zh: 私有化计划

senses.en: , ) the sale of a large number of shares in a company, after which their value usually falls﹙
to sell sth to sb else that you have bought not long before, usually in order to make a profit

ex.en: She managed the business for a year and then sold it on.
ex.zh: 她把公司经营了一年，然后转卖了。

senses.en: to be convinced that sth is very good

ex.en: I could see she was sold on the idea.
ex.zh: 我看得出她非常赞同这个主意。

ex.en: I’m not really sold on American music.
ex.zh: 我并不怎么喜欢美国音乐。

senses.en: [usually sing.] a play, concert, etc.for which all the tickets have been sold

ex.en: The gig is a sell-out.
ex.zh: 这次演奏会座无虚席。

ex.en: a sell-out tour/crowd
ex.zh: 场场爆满的巡迴演出/观众

senses.en: to ignore or change your principles or beliefs, especially to gain an advantage for yourself

ex.en: The rest of the gang accused him of selling out to the law.
ex.zh: 这个团伙的其他人指责他告发了他们。

ex.en: a talented British movie director who’s sold out to Hollywood
ex.zh: 一位卖身到好莱坞的有才华的英国电影导演

senses.en: to sell your business or a part of your business

ex.en: The company sold out to its rival.
ex.zh: 公司卖给了对手。

senses.en: to betray sb﹙

ex.en: They discovered who had sold them out to the enemy.
ex.zh: 他们弄清了是谁把他们出卖给了敌人。

senses.en: to sell your home, possessions,business, etc., usually because you need the money, are moving to another place or stopping work

ex.en: They sold up and moved to France.
ex.zh: 他们把家卖了，移居到法国。

ex.en: We decided to sell up everything and buy a farm.
ex.zh: 我们决定卖光所有财产，然后买个农场。

senses.en: to arrange for sb/sth to go or be taken to the place you are going to, before you arrive there
senses.zh: 提前运送某人﹙或物﹚；派某人打头阵:

ex.en: The rest of the equipment was sent ahead by air.
ex.zh: 其余的设备用飞机提前运走了。

senses.en: to tell sb to leave

ex.en: The reporters were sent away empty-handed (= without any news).
ex.zh: 记者都被要求离开，空手而回。

senses.en: (to…) to arrange for sb to go somewhere away from home
senses.zh: 安排某人离开家﹙去某处﹚:

ex.en: He was sent away to boarding school at the age of 7.
ex.zh: 他7岁时就被送到了寄宿学校。

senses.en: to return sb/sth to where they/it came from

ex.en: The refugees were sent back to their own country.
ex.zh: 难民被遣送回国。

ex.en: You can send the goods back if you’re not satisfied.
ex.zh: 不满意可退货。

senses.en: ) to send sb to prison

ex.en: He was sent down for ten years.
ex.zh: 他给判了十年监禁。

senses.en: to send a message to sb to ask them to come and see you, especially in order to help you

ex.en: Send for a doctor.
ex.zh: 请大夫来吧。

senses.en: to order sb to go to a place to deal with a difficult situation

ex.en: Troops were sent in to restore order.
ex.zh: 已派部队前去恢复秩序。

senses.en: to write to sb and ask them to send you sth by post/mail

ex.en: If you save enough packets, you can send off and get a free toy.
ex.zh: 攒够包装纸可来信免费索取玩具。

ex.en: You can send off for a free booklet.
ex.zh: 可来信免费索取小册子。

senses.en: () (in a sports game
senses.zh: 体育运动) a situation when a player is told to leave the field because they have broken the rules判罚下场；罚出场外:

ex.en: It’s his third sending-off this year.
ex.zh: 这是他今年第三次被罚下场了。

ex.en: The match saw three penalties and two sendings-off.
ex.zh: 比赛有三次罚球，两人罚下场。

senses.en: () an occasion when people come together to say goodbye to sb who is leaving

ex.en: She was given a good send-off by all her colleagues.
ex.zh: 她受到了所有同事的热情欢送。

senses.en: (to…) to send a letter, etc. that has arrived at sb’s old address to their new one

ex.en: I’ve asked a neighbour to send on any important letters.
ex.zh: 我已经请一位邻居帮忙转寄重要信件。

senses.en: to send sb somewhere for a particular purpose
senses.zh: 派某人到别处﹙担负任务等﹚；派遣:

ex.en: I’ll ask them to send someone out straightaway to fix the car.
ex.zh: 我会请他们马上派人修理汽车的。

ex.en: If I’m not back by midnight, send out a search party!
ex.zh: 如果我半夜还回不来，就派出搜索队！

senses.en: to ask a restaurant or shop/store to deliver food to you at home or at work

ex.en: We could send out for a takeaway.
ex.zh: 我们可以订一份外卖。

senses.en: to make people laugh, especially by copying them/it in an amusing way

ex.en: a TV programme that sends up politicians
ex.zh: 模仿取笑政治人物的电视节目

ex.en: Everyone was sending her up.
ex.zh: 大家都在模仿取笑她。

senses.en: (, ) an act of making sb/sth look silly by copying them in an amusing way﹙
senses.zh: 对人或事物的﹚滑稽模仿:

ex.en: The movie is a hilarious send-up of the Hollywood western.
ex.zh: 这部电影是对好莱坞西部片的滑稽模仿。

senses.en: to remove sth from a larger thing or group; to keep sth apart

ex.en: The property agency has been separated off from the main business.
ex.zh: 房地产经销处从主公司分离出来了。

senses.en: to divide into different parts; to divide sb/sth into different parts or groups﹙

ex.en: The mixture separates out into layers.
ex.zh: 混合物分出了层次。

ex.en: Plastics must be separated out into different types for recycling.
ex.zh: 回收塑料必须先行分类。

senses.en: to be used instead of sth else when there is nothing better available

ex.en: An old box served as a table.
ex.zh: 当时就用一个旧箱子凑合着充当桌子。

ex.en: Small temporary buildings had to serve for offices.
ex.zh: 狭小的临时建筑权且作办公室用。

senses.en: to give or send sb an official document, especially one that orders them to appear in a court of law
senses.zh: 将传票﹙等﹚送达某人；给某人发出传票﹙等﹚:

ex.en: The police have served a summons on Mr Jackson.
ex.zh: 警方已向杰克逊先生发传票。

ex.en: The police have served him with a summons.
ex.zh: 警方已经把传票送交给他。

senses.en: to continue doing sth until the end of a fixed period of time

ex.en: She served out the rest of her sentence in an open prison.
ex.zh: 她在一座开放式监狱服满了刑期。

senses.en: ( ,serve sth 'out )
to put food onto plates and give it to people

ex.en: He served up a delicious meal.
ex.zh: 他端上一顿可口的饭菜。

senses.en: ) to give or offer sth

ex.en: All the TV channels served up the usual old movies during the holidays.
ex.zh: 假期时所有电视频道都播放老掉牙的影片。

senses.en: to attack sb

ex.en: He set about me with a stick.
ex.zh: 他用棍子打我。

senses.en: tobegin a task or an activity, especially withenergy or enthusiasm

ex.en: We set about the task of cleaning the apartment.
ex.zh: 我们动手打扫起公寓来。

senses.en: to approach aproblem or task in a particular way
senses.zh: 着手处理﹙问题﹚；展开﹙工作﹚:

ex.en: You’ve set about this problem the wrong way.
ex.zh: 你处理这个问题的方式错了。

ex.en: How should I set about finding a job?
ex.zh: 我该怎样着手找工作呢？

senses.en: to make sb oppose a friend,relative, etc.
senses.zh: 使某人反对﹙朋友、亲人等﹚:

ex.en: The civil war set brother against brother.
ex.zh: 内战造成骨肉相残。

senses.en: to change a clock or watch to show the correct later time

ex.en: Don’t forget to set your clocks ahead tonight (=because the time has officially changed).
ex.zh: 今晚别忘了把时钟拨快。

senses.en: to make sb/sth different from or better than others
senses.zh: 使某人﹙或事物﹚与其他的不同；使突出；使优于﹙…﹚:

ex.en: His confidence sets him apart from his classmates.
ex.zh: 他的自信心使他有别于同班同学。

ex.en: It’s the service at the restaurant that sets it apart.
ex.zh: 这家餐馆的服务独具特色。

senses.en: to keep sth such as money or time for a special use or purpose
senses.zh: 留出金钱﹙或时间等﹚；拨出﹙专用﹚:

ex.en: A room was set apart for quiet reading.
ex.zh: 留出了一个房间作为安静的读书室。

senses.en: to place sth to one side
senses.zh: 把…放到一旁﹙或搁到一边﹚:

ex.en: I set her letter aside, meaning to read it later.
ex.zh: 我把她的信放在一边等以后读。

senses.en: [U] a system in which the government pays farmers not to use some of their land for growing crops; the land that the farmers are paid not to use
senses.zh: 退耕补贴制度，退耕地﹙由政府补贴，鼓励农民退耕部份耕地﹚:

ex.en: 750 acres of setaside
ex.zh: 750 英亩的退耕土地

senses.en: to delay the progress of sb/sth
senses.zh: 耽搁某人﹙或事物﹚的进展；耽误；使延误:

ex.en: The rain set the building programme back by several weeks.
ex.zh: 建筑计划因雨延误了几周。

ex.en: He was starting to play very well, but his injury has really set him back.
ex.zh: 他正开始表现非常好，但受伤着实把他耽误了。

senses.en: a problem or difficulty that delays the progress of sb/sth

ex.en: Parry’s broken ankle was a major setback for the team.
ex.zh: 帕里脚腕受伤对于这个队是一大打击。

senses.en: (of a plane, a pilot,passengers, etc.
senses.zh: 飞机、飞行员、乘客等) to land着陆:

ex.en: We set down on the beach.
ex.zh: 我们在沙滩上着陆了。

ex.en: The pilot tried to set the plane down in a field.
ex.zh: 飞行员试图把飞机降落在一块田里。

senses.en: (of a vehicle or its driver
senses.zh: 车辆或驾驶员) to stop and allow sb to get off/out让人下车；停车谢客:

ex.en: The taxi set me down at the end of the road.
ex.zh: 出租车在路尽头让我下了车。

senses.en: to start a journey

ex.en: They set forth for Crete.
ex.zh: 他们动身前往克里特岛。

senses.en: to state sth clearly; to make sth known

ex.en: The President set forth his views in a long television broadcast.
ex.zh: 总统在一次很长的电视讲话中阐述了自己的观点。

senses.en: This phrasal verb can be used in the passive.
senses.zh: 这个短语动词可用于被动语态:

ex.en: Her beliefs have been clearly set forth.
ex.zh: 她已经表明自己的信念。

senses.en: to fix sth in a space so that it does not stick out beyond the surface

ex.en: A small safe had been set into the wall.
ex.zh: 墙壁里安装了个小保险箱。

senses.en: a small picture, map, etc. inside a larger one﹙
senses.zh: 套印在大图片、地图等中的﹚小图，小地图:

ex.en: Brad Pitt at the premiere, and his wife (inset) (= about a photograph in a newspaper)
ex.zh: 首次公演时的布雷德·皮特，以及他的妻子﹙插图﹚

senses.en: a piece of material, a small stone,etc. that is added on to sth else or put inside sth else

ex.en: a silver brooch with ruby insets
ex.zh: 镶嵌红宝石的银胸针

senses.en: to begin a journey

ex.en: I set off for work at seven.
ex.zh: 我七点钟动身上班。

ex.en: Check your oil before setting off on a long journey.
ex.zh: 长途旅行出发前要检查一下燃油。

senses.en: to make sb start doing sth such as laughing, crying or talking
senses.zh: 使……笑起来﹙或哭起来、说起话来﹚:

ex.en: Those photos always set her off (crying).
ex.zh: 她每次看那些照片就哭。

ex.en: Just seeing him laughing sets me off! (= makes me start laughing)
ex.zh: 看到他笑我忍不住也笑了。

senses.en: to make sth appear more attractive by being placed near it
senses.zh: 衬托；使显得更突出﹙或更漂亮﹚:

ex.en: That scarf sets off the blue of her eyes.
ex.zh: 围巾衬托出她的蓝眼睛。

senses.en: to attack sb

ex.en: I was set upon by a gang of youths.
ex.zh: 我遭到一伙青年袭击。

senses.en: to make a person or an animal attack sb

ex.en: The farmer threatened to set his dogs on us if we didn’t leave at once.
ex.zh: 农夫威胁说，如果我们不马上离开，他就放狗咬我们。

senses.en: to leave a place and begin a journey,especially a long journey
senses.zh: 出发，动身，启程﹙尤指长途旅行﹚:

ex.en: They set out on the last stage of their journey.
ex.zh: 他们踏上最后一段行程。

ex.en: We set out at dawn.
ex.zh: 我们是拂晓时分出发的。

senses.en: the beginning of sth
to begin doing sth in a busy or determined way
senses.zh: 起劲地干起来；毅然开始做:

ex.en: She set to with a scrubbing brush (= she started cleaning).
ex.zh: 她拿起刷子起劲地擦洗。

senses.en: to begin fighting

ex.en: They took off their jackets and set to.
ex.zh: 他们脱掉外衣就打了起来。

senses.en: a fight or an argument

ex.en: He had a set-to with one of his workmates.
ex.zh: 他和一位工友干了一架。

senses.en: to make a machine, some equipment, etc. ready to use
senses.zh: 安装好，装配好，调试好﹙设备或机器﹚:

ex.en: He helped me to carry my equipment in and set up.
ex.zh: 他帮我把设备搬进来并调试好。

ex.en: It took hours to set up all the equipment.
ex.zh: 花了很长时间才把所有的设备安装好。

senses.en: to start running your own business

ex.en: He left the firm and set up in business on his own.
ex.zh: 他离开了公司自己开业。

ex.en: She set herself up as a hairdresser.
ex.zh: 她自己开了个理发店。

senses.en: to provide sb with the money they need, for example to start a business, buy a home, etc.

ex.en: A bank loan helped to set her up in business.
ex.zh: 她靠一笔银行贷款做起了生意。

ex.en: He set his daughter up in her own apartment.
ex.zh: 他资助女儿买了她自己的公寓。

senses.en: ) to trick sb, especially by making them appear to be guilty of sth that they have not done
senses.zh: 诬陷，冤枉﹙某人﹚；给某人栽﹙罪名﹚:

ex.en: He claimed he had been set up by the police.
ex.zh: 他说警方冤枉了他。

senses.en: ) to make sb feel healthier, stronger, more active, etc.
senses.zh: 使更健康﹙或强壮、活泼等﹚:

ex.en: A good breakfast will set you up for the day.
ex.zh: 早餐吃好一天都精力充沛。

senses.en: (with sb) () to arrange for sb to meet sb so that they can have a romantic or sexual relationship
senses.zh: 介绍某人﹙ 和… ﹚ 约会；给…当红娘；为…搭桥:

ex.en: He set me up with his sister.
ex.zh: 他介绍我和他妹妹约会。

senses.en: a situation in which sb tricks you or makes it seem as if you are guilty of sth that you have not done

ex.en: I didn’t do it, this is a set-up!
ex.zh: 我没干那事，这是诬陷！

senses.en: a situation when sb arranges for you to meet sb in order to begin a romantic or sexual relationship

ex.en: a set-up date
ex.zh: 经人介绍的约会

senses.en: [usually sing.] () the way sth is organized or arranged; a system

ex.en: I’ve only been here a week so I don’t really know the set-up.
ex.zh: 我来这里才一个星期，所以还不太清楚这里的组织情况。

senses.en: to claim to be very important, know a lot about sth, etc.

ex.en: He set himself up as an authority on modern art.
ex.zh: 他自我标榜为现代艺术权威。

senses.en: to start to have a calmer or quieter way of life,without many changes, especially living in one place﹙
senses.zh: 在某地﹚定居下来，过安定的生活:

ex.en: He got married and settled down.
ex.zh: 他成了家并安定下来。

senses.en: to become relaxed and confident in a new situation; to get used to a new way of life, job, etc.
senses.zh: 安顿下来；习惯于﹙新生活﹚；适应﹙新环境﹚:

ex.en: She’s settling down well at her new school.
ex.zh: 她在新学校很习惯。

ex.en: He just couldn’t settle down in the city.
ex.zh: 他就是不能适应城里的生活。

senses.en: to become calmer and less active

ex.en: I’ve been really busy at work, but things should settle down again soon.
ex.zh: 我确实一直忙于工作，但情况很快就会再平静下来的。

ex.en: Their speed settled down to a steady fifty miles an hour.
ex.zh: 他们减低车速，稳定在每小时五十英里。

senses.en: to become or to make sb become calmer, less excited, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 使某人﹚ 安静下来， 平静下来:

ex.en: The children finally settled down and started work.
ex.zh: 孩子们终于安静下来开始干活了。

ex.en: The teacher had trouble settling the class down.
ex.zh: 老师没法让班上的同学安静下来。

senses.en: to begin to think about sth or give your attention to doing sth
senses.zh: 开始认真对待；定下心来做:

ex.en: They had just settled down to dinner when the phone rang.
ex.zh: 他们刚刚开始吃饭，电话铃就响了。

ex.en: I’m so worried that I can’t settle to anything.
ex.zh: 我忧心忡忡，做什么事都静不下心来。

senses.en: to accept sth that is not quite what you wanted but is the best that you can get

ex.en: Both teams were happy to settle for a draw.
ex.zh: 两个队都愿意接受平局的结果。

ex.en: He’d hoped to get ￡8 000 for the car but had to settle for a lot less.
ex.zh: 他本想把车卖上8 000 英镑，可只得接受低得多的价格。

senses.en: to become used to something new, such as a new home, school or job
senses.zh: 安顿下来；习惯于，适应﹙新事物或新环境﹚:

ex.en: She soon settled in at school.
ex.zh: 她在学校很快便习惯了。

ex.en: It took her a while to settle into her new job.
ex.zh: 她过了一段时间才适应了新工作。

senses.en: to choose sth ; to make a decision about sth

ex.en: We couldn’t decide where to go but we eventually settled on Italy.我们定不下来去哪儿，可最终决定去意大利。

senses.en: to arrange to give property or money to sb, for example after your death
senses.zh: 指定把财产等授与﹙或分配给﹚某人:

ex.en: He settled his entire estate on his son.
ex.zh: 他把全部财产都传给了儿子。

senses.en: to pay sb the money you owe them﹙

ex.en: We need to settle up with them for the hire of the room.
ex.zh: 我们得跟他们结清房租。

ex.en: I’ll pay now — we can settle up later.
ex.zh: 我来付钱吧—我们以后再算。

senses.en: to join or mend sth using a needle and thread

ex.en: Sew up the tear before it gets any worse.
ex.zh: 把撕破的地方及时补好。

ex.en: They cleaned the wound and sewed it up.
ex.zh: 他们清洗了伤口， 然后缝合。

senses.en: to live with sb you are having a sexual relationship with but are not married to

ex.en: He’s shacked up with some girl he met in Berlin.
ex.zh: 他跟一个在柏林结识的女子同居。

senses.en: to make part of a picture darker,either with colours or using black

ex.en: He shaded in part of the graph.
ex.zh: 他把曲线图的一部份涂了阴影。

senses.en: to gradually change into sth else so that you cannot tell where one thing ends and the other begins﹙

ex.en: The blue gradually shades into purple.
ex.zh: 蓝色逐渐变成了紫色。

ex.en: Sometimes nervousness can shade into fear.
ex.zh: 有时紧张可能慢慢转变为恐惧。

senses.en: to become comfortable and confident in a new situation
senses.zh: 融入新环境；适应新情况:

ex.en: Once the team shakes down, results should improve.
ex.zh: 整个队伍熟悉了情况，成绩应该可以提高的。

senses.en: the test of a vehicle or an aircraft before it is generally used,to see if there are any problems and to make the crew familiar with it﹙
senses.zh: 车辆或飞行器的﹚最后测试，试用，试航:

ex.en: a shakedown flight
ex.zh: 试飞

senses.en: to search a person or place in a very thorough way

ex.en: Police shook down the club, looking for drugs.
ex.zh: 警察彻底搜查俱乐部，想找毒品。

senses.en: to escape from sb; to get rid of sb who is following you

ex.en: He twisted and turned in a desperate attempt to shake off his pursuer.
ex.zh: 他左拐右转拚命想甩掉追他的人。

ex.en: I think we’ve shaken them off.
ex.zh: 相信我们已经甩开他们了。

senses.en: to escape from sb who is holding you and will not let go

ex.en: She clung to him, but he shook her off.
ex.zh: 她拥抱着他，可他挣脱了。

senses.en: to shake hands with sb in order to show that you agree to sth

ex.en: Let’s shake on it.
ex.zh: 咱们握手庆贺取得一致。

senses.en: to open or spread sth by shaking it

ex.en: He shook the blanket out and spread it on the grass.
ex.zh: 他把毯子抖开铺在草地上。

senses.en: to open sth by shaking it in order to get rid of bits of dirt, dust, etc.

ex.en: She went outside to shake out the tablecloth.
ex.zh: 她到外面把桌布抖乾净。

senses.en: to shock or upset sb

ex.en: She has been badly shaken up by the experience.
ex.zh: 那次经历让她大受刺激。

senses.en: a major change to a company or an organization in order to improve it﹙
senses.zh: 公司、机构的﹚大改革，重组:

ex.en: The police force is facing the biggest shake-up in its history.
ex.zh: 警察队伍面临有史以来最重大的改革。

senses.en: to persuade sb to do sth by making them feel ashamed not to do it
senses.zh: 使某人羞愧不得不﹙ 做某事﹚:

ex.en: They shamed him into apologizing.
ex.zh: 他们弄得他很惭愧，只好道歉。

senses.en: to divide something such as money, food or work and give an amount to each person

ex.en: The work was shared out equally.
ex.zh: 工作平均分配给大家了。

ex.en: How can we share out the pizza between the five of us?
ex.zh: 我们五人怎么平分这个比萨饼呢？

senses.en: to become,or to make sb/sth, better, more skilful, more effective, etc. than before﹙
senses.zh: 使﹚变得更好﹙或技术更高、更有效等﹚；提高某人﹙或事物﹚的水平﹙或技术、效率等﹚:

ex.en: She needs to sharpen up before next month’s competition.
ex.zh: 下个月比赛之前，她的水平需要提高一下。

ex.en: This exercise will help students sharpen up their reading skills.
ex.zh: 这个练习将帮助学生提高阅读能力。

senses.en: to remove hair from your face,head, etc.

ex.en: Dad’s shaved his beard off.
ex.zh: 爸爸刮掉了鬍子。

ex.en: She shocked everyone by shaving all her hair off.
ex.zh: 她剃光了头发，让大家吃了一惊。

senses.en: to cut very thin pieces from the surface of a piece of wood, etc.﹙

ex.en: I had to shave a bit off the door to make it shut.
ex.zh: 我把门刨去了一点才能关上。

ex.en: Use a sharp knife to shave off thin rolls of chocolate.
ex.zh: 用锋利的刀子片下薄薄的巧克力卷儿。

senses.en: to make something smaller or lower by a very small amount﹙

ex.en: We managed to shave 5% off the cost.
ex.zh: 我们设法把成本减少了5%。

ex.en: He shaved half a second off the world record.
ex.zh: 他把世界纪录缩短了半秒。

senses.en: to have sth important taken away from you

ex.en: a political party shorn of power
ex.zh: 被剥夺了权力的政党

senses.en: ) (especially of sth metal
senses.zh: 尤指金属) to break under pressure; to cut through sth and make it break受压断裂；剪切:

ex.en: The bolts holding the wheel in place sheared off.
ex.zh: 固定轮子的螺栓压断了。

senses.en: to suddenly move away in a different direction, especially to avoid hitting sth

ex.en: The car sheered wildly away, just missing the truck.
ex.zh: 汽车猛地一转，正好避开了卡车。

ex.en: Her mind sheered away from images she did not wish to dwell on.
ex.zh: 她有意不去想那些她不愿多想的事情。

senses.en: to pay for sth, especially when it is a lot of money or you do not really want to﹙
senses.zh: 为某事物﹚花很多钱，破费:

ex.en: I’m not shelling out for another computer.
ex.zh: 我不会花钱再买一台电脑的。

ex.en: I had to shell out $500 for the air fare.
ex.zh: 我只得拿出500 元买飞机票。

senses.en: () to climb down or up sth, using your hands and legs to hold it tightly

ex.en: He shinned down the drainpipe.
ex.zh: 他顺着排水管爬下来。

ex.en: You might be able to see if you shin up that tree.
ex.zh: 爬上那棵树你就有可能看见了。

senses.en: to shine brightly

ex.en: A light shone out across the field.
ex.zh: 地那边有光在闪耀。

senses.en: to be seen clearly and easily

ex.en: In the last game her talent really shone through.
ex.zh: 在最后一场比赛中，她真正展露了才华。

ex.en: His love of life shines through the pages of his book.
ex.zh: 他的书字里行间流露出对生命的热爱。

senses.en: to send sb away somewhere, especially when they do not want to go

ex.en: They shipped the children off to summer camp.
ex.zh: 他们把孩子们送到了夏令营。

senses.en: to send goods or people somewhere by ship

ex.en: They shipped all their possessions off to Australia.
ex.zh: 他们把所有财产都海运到了澳大利亚。

senses.en: to send goods or people somewhere, especially by ship﹙

ex.en: They shipped the sculpture out to the States.
ex.zh: 他们把雕塑海运到了美国。

senses.en: to shoot at sb/sth and make them/it fall to the ground

ex.en: They were shot down in cold blood.
ex.zh: 他们被残酷地击毙了。

ex.en: They shot down a civilian aircraft by mistake.
ex.zh: 他们不小心击落了一架民用飞机。

senses.en: ) to strongly criticize sb or their ideas, etc.
senses.zh: 批驳，驳倒，彻底推翻﹙观点等﹚:

ex.en: When I made a suggestion they shot me down in flames.
ex.zh: 我提了个建议，却被他们彻底推翻了。

ex.en: My ideas were shot down one by one.
ex.zh: 我的观点被逐一批驳了。

senses.zh: (通常用于进行时) to try to get or achieve sth difficult力争达到；努力获取:

ex.en: They’re shooting for another victory this season.
ex.zh: 他们力争这个赛季再赢一场。

senses.en: to leave somewhere very quickly

ex.en: She had to shoot off to meet someone.
ex.zh: 她得赶去见个人。

ex.en: I’m sorry, I’ve got to shoot off.
ex.zh: 抱歉，我必须马上离开。

senses.zh: 澳大利亚英语) to leave, especially in order to avoid sb/sth离去；躲避:

ex.en: I was only five when my Dad shot through.
ex.zh: 我才五岁爸爸就离开了。

senses.en: (to sth) to rise or increase very quickly

ex.en: The inflation rate has shot up to 20%.
ex.zh: 通货膨胀率激增到20%。

senses.en: to grow taller in a short time

ex.en: She’s shot up in the last few months.
ex.zh: 她在过去的几个月中个头一下子蹿上来了。

senses.en: to inject an illegal drug
to injure sb or damage sth severely by shooting

ex.en: An armed gang shot up the nightclub.
ex.zh: 一个武装团伙开枪把夜总会打得千疮百孔。

senses.en: to look at different shops/stores to compare the prices of goods or services so that you can buy the ones that are the best value﹙
senses.zh: 就某种商品或服务﹚比较…的价格；货问三家而后买:

ex.en: If you’re buying a new hi-fi, shop around for the best price.
ex.zh: 你要是买新高保真音响，要货比三家买最合算的。

ex.en: It’s worth shopping around the travel agents to find the best deal.
ex.zh: 比较各家旅行社，找最划算的服务是很值得的。

senses.en: to support part of a building or other large structure by placing large pieces of wood or metal against or under it so that it does not fall down

ex.en: Engineers shored up the tunnel with wooden beams.
ex.zh: 工程师用木梁支撑隧道。

ex.en: The building was shored up to make it safe.
ex.zh: 这座建筑物被支撑起来以保持稳固。

senses.en: to strengthen or support sth that is weak or failing

ex.en: to shore up the economy/ dollar/pound
ex.zh: 稳定经济/美元/英镑

senses.en: to shout to prevent sb who is speaking from being heard, because you do not like them, or you disagree with what they are saying
senses.zh: 用喊叫声盖过某人的讲话:

ex.en: I tried to explain but they just shouted me down.
ex.zh: 我试图解释，可他们把我的声音压下去了。

ex.en: The speaker was shouted down by angry protesters.
ex.zh: 愤怒的抗议者大叫大嚷，盖过了讲话人的声音。

senses.en: to suddenly say sth in a loud voice﹙

ex.en: I shouted out to them but they didn’t hear me.
ex.zh: 我朝他们大喊一声，可他们没听见。

ex.en: She shouted out a warning.
ex.zh: 她大声发出警告。

senses.en: , ) used to tell sb rather rudely to go away

ex.en: Just shove off and leave me alone!
ex.zh: 磙开，别烦我！

senses.en: , ) used to ask sb to move to make a space for sb else to sit down

ex.en: We can get one more in if you shove up.
ex.zh: 你挪动一下我们就能再坐下一个。

ex.en: Shove up a bit!
ex.zh: 稍挪一挪！

senses.en: to go with sb when they visit a place for the first time, showing them what is interesting
senses.zh: 领某人参观；带某人巡视……:

ex.en: There are guides in the palace who will show visitors around.
ex.zh: 宫殿里会有导游带访客参观。

ex.en: I’ll arrange for someone to show you around the school.
ex.zh: 我会安排人领你参观学校的。

senses.en: to lead a visitor to a place where they can wait, or to the room where sb is waiting to see them
senses.zh: 把﹙客人﹚带到﹙等候处或会客室﹚:

ex.en: Sarah showed the visitors in.
ex.zh: 萨拉把客人们领了进来。

ex.en: I was shown into a waiting room.
ex.zh: 有人把我带到候客室。

senses.en: to try to impress other people with your abilities,wealth,intelligence, etc.

ex.en: Stop showing off!
ex.zh: 别卖弄了！

ex.en: Bonnie was showing off to her friends, doing handstands on the grass.
ex.zh: 邦尼向朋友们炫耀，在草地上拿大顶。

senses.en: (, ) a person who likes to impress other people with their abilities, wealth, etc.

ex.en: You’re such a show-off!
ex.zh: 你真会卖弄！

senses.en: to try to make people pay attention to sb/sth because you are proud of them/it﹙
senses.zh: 向人﹚炫示，夸示﹙人或事物﹚:

ex.en: He was showing his CD collection off to his friends.
ex.zh: 他在向朋友展示他所有的光盘。

ex.en: She brought her new boyfriend along to show him off.
ex.zh: 她把新男友带来炫耀一番。

senses.en: to make sb/sth look attractive or seem interesting or exciting by showing their best features
senses.zh: 使﹙人或物﹚显得漂亮；使夺目；衬托:

ex.en: The black sweater showed off her figure to full advantage.
ex.zh: 那件黑毛衣完全衬托出她的身材。

ex.en: The music shows the band off in their best light.
ex.zh: 这音乐展现了乐队最出色的一面。

senses.en: to lead a visitor to the door out of a room, a building, etc.

ex.en: I’ll show you out.
ex.zh: 我来送送你。

senses.en: to take sb around a place they are visiting and show them what is interesting
senses.zh: 带某人查看； 带某人参观:

ex.en: They showed me over the house.
ex.zh: 他们带我看了房子。

senses.en: to be visible through something or behind sth﹙
senses.zh: 从某事物中﹚ 透出， 显出， 透视:

ex.en: This paper is so thin the ink shows through.
ex.zh: 这纸薄得能透过墨迹。

ex.en: His skull showed through his thin hair.
ex.zh: 他的脑壳在稀疏的头发下清晰可见。

senses.en: to arrive or appear at the place you have arranged

ex.en: She finally showed up at lunchtime.
ex.zh: 午饭时分她终于赶到了。

ex.en: I arranged to meet him but he didn’t show up.
ex.zh: 我约了和他见面，可他没来。

senses.en: to become or to make sth easy to see﹙
senses.zh: 使﹚容易看见，变得明显，显现出来:

ex.en: His striped tie showed up well against his dark red shirt.
ex.zh: 他那条纹领带在深红色的衬衫下十分醒目。

ex.en: Something odd has shown up on the X-ray.
ex.zh: X光照片显示有些不寻常。

senses.en: to show what sb/sth is really like, when this is worse than people thought
senses.zh: 暴露；揭示某人﹙或事物﹚为…:

ex.en: The book shows her up for what she really is : a fraud.
ex.zh: 这本书揭示出她的真面目——一个骗子。

ex.en: We were shown up as the second-rate team that we were.
ex.zh: 我们暴露了二流球队的水平。

senses.en: to fall onto sb/sth, especially in a lot of small pieces﹙
senses.zh: 雨点般﹚ 落在… 上； 洒落:

ex.en: Volcanic ash showered down on the town after the eruption.
ex.zh: 火山喷发之后，小城落了一层火山灰。

ex.en: The bottle broke and showered glass fragments on us.
ex.zh: 瓶子炸了，玻璃碎片溅到我们身上。

senses.en: to drop a lot of small things onto sb

ex.en: The bride and groom were showered with rice as they left the church.
ex.zh: 新娘新郎离开教堂时大家向他们身上撒大米。

ex.en: The roof collapsed, showering us with dust and debris.
ex.zh: 房顶塌了，灰尘和瓦砾洒落在我们身上。

senses.en: to move backwards or away from sb/sth, especially because you are frightened or disgusted
senses.zh: 躲避﹙人或事物﹚；退避；畏缩:

ex.en: She shrank away from him in horror.
ex.zh: 她因恐惧而躲避他。

senses.zh: (常用于否定句) to be unwilling to do or accept sth that you find frightening, unpleasant or immoral畏避，迴避﹙可怕、讨厌或邪恶的事情﹚:

ex.en: She recognized her responsibility and did not shrink from it.
ex.zh: 她意识到自己的责任，没有退缩。

ex.en: He shrank from confronting his son face to face.
ex.zh: 他迴避和儿子正面交锋。

senses.en: to become dry and wrinkled (= having many small lines or folds) because of heat,lack of water, etc.

ex.en: The apples left on the tree had shrivelled up.
ex.zh: 留在树上的苹果都蔫了。

senses.en: dry and wrinkled (= with many small lines or folds)

ex.en: shrivelled-up apples
ex.zh: 乾瘪的苹果

senses.en: to be covered or hidden by sth
senses.zh: 被…覆盖； 被… 掩藏:

ex.en: The city was shrouded in mist.
ex.zh: 城市笼罩在雾霭中。

ex.en: furniture shrouded in dust sheets
ex.zh: 蒙着防尘罩的傢具

senses.en: if information, etc. is shrouded in mystery, it is hidden or kept secret﹙
to put sb/sth in a place where other people cannot see or find them/it

ex.en: He shut the files away in the safe.
ex.zh: 他把文件锁在了保险柜里。

ex.en: prisoners shut away in jail for a long time
ex.zh: 长期监禁的犯人

senses.en: to stay in your room or go somewhere where you will be completely alone

ex.en: He shut himself away in his study to finish the book.
ex.zh: 他独自躲进书房把书看完。

ex.en: You can’t just shut yourself away from the world.
ex.zh: 你不能与世隔绝。

senses.en: to stop opening for business; to stop sth from opening﹙

ex.en: The mine shut down last month.
ex.zh: 煤矿上个月关闭了。

ex.en: The club was shut down by the police.
ex.zh: 俱乐部给警方查封了。

senses.en: the act of closing a factory or business, either temporarily or permanently﹙
senses.zh: 工厂或商店的﹚关闭，停工，歇业:

ex.en: The shutdown has put hundreds out of work.
ex.zh: 倒闭造成了几百人失业。

senses.en: the act of stopping a large machine from working, either temporarily or permanently﹙

ex.en: There was a fault in the nuclear reactor’s emergency shutdown procedures.
ex.zh: 核反应堆的紧急停堆程序有错误。

senses.en: to put sb/sth in a room, a vehicle, etc. and keep them there; to go into a room, a building, a vehicle, etc.and stay there
senses.zh: 把…关在﹙房间、车辆等﹚里面； 在… 里呆着:

ex.en: They shut the animals in at night.
ex.zh: 他们夜间把牲畜圈起来。

ex.en: Liz rushed out of the kitchen and shut herself in her room.
ex.zh: 利兹冲出厨房，然后把自己关在房间里。

senses.en: (, ) a person who cannot leave their home because they are ill/sick or cannot move easily
senses.zh: 因病﹙或行动不便﹚不能离家的人；卧病在家的人

senses.en: to trap or injure sth by closing sth tightly around it

ex.en: I shut my finger in the car door.
ex.zh: 我让车门夹住了手指。

senses.en: a device that stops sth working or stops power, water, gas, etc. from flowing

ex.en: a shut-off valve
ex.zh: 关闭用阀门

senses.en: a period when power, water, gas, etc. is prevented from flowing

ex.en: a shutoff of the water supply
ex.zh: 停水

senses.en: to keep sb/sth separate from other people or things

ex.en: A range of mountains shuts Bosnia off from the Adriatic.
ex.zh: 波斯尼亚和亚得里亚海之间有山脉相隔。

ex.en: The kitchen area could be shut off from the rest of the room.
ex.zh: 做饭的地方可以和房间的其他部份隔开。

senses.en: to deliberately separate yourself physically or socially from other people
senses.zh: 躲避﹙ 人或事物﹚ ； 离群独处:

ex.en: After her son died, she just wanted to shut herself off from the world.
ex.zh: 儿子死后，她只想遁世离群。

senses.en: a game in which one team does not score
to stop sb/sth from entering a place
senses.zh: 使…不能进入﹙某处﹚；挡住；遮住:

ex.en: He closed the door firmly, shutting us out of the room.
ex.zh: 他用力关上门，不让我们进屋里。

ex.en: I drew the curtains to shut out the light.
ex.zh: 我拉上窗帘遮挡光线。

senses.en: to stop yourself from having particular feelings or from thinking about particular things

ex.en: She tried to shut out all the painful memories.
ex.zh: 她尽力避免想起这一切痛苦的回忆。

senses.en: to be unable to enter your home because you have closed the door and left your keys inside
senses.zh: 把自己锁在门外﹙进不了家﹚:

ex.en: I’ve shut myself out of the house again!
ex.zh: 我又把自己锁在门外了！

senses.en: used to tell sb rudely to stop talking or making a noise

ex.en: Shut up and go away!
ex.zh: 闭嘴，磙开！

ex.en: If you’d shut up, I could hear what she’s saying.
ex.zh: 你要是闭上嘴，我就能听清楚她说的话了。

senses.en: to keep sb/sth in a place and prevent them from going anywhere; to stay in a room and not go out

ex.en: He had been shut up in a cell for ten years.
ex.zh: 他被关在牢房里十年了。

ex.en: Shut the dog up in the shed.
ex.zh: 把狗关在棚子里。

senses.en: to avoid doing sth because you are nervous or frightened
senses.zh: 因畏惧﹙或畏怯﹚而躲避；迴避:

ex.en: She shies away from close friendships.
ex.zh: 她不愿跟人深交。

ex.en: Don’t shy away from saying what you think.
ex.zh: 别吞吞吐吐的，说出你的想法吧。

senses.en: to tell a dog to attack sb

ex.en: Back off or I’ll sic the dog on you.
ex.zh: 走开，否则我就放狗咬你。

senses.en: to bring food up from the stomach

ex.en: The baby sicked up her milk.
ex.zh: 婴儿吐奶了。

senses.zh: (通常用于进行时) to show signs that you may be becoming ill/sick表现出将要患病的迹象；像是要得病:

ex.en: I feel as if I’m sickening for something.
ex.zh: 我感觉好像得了什么病。

ex.en: You look as if you’re sickening for flu.
ex.zh: 你看上去像是要患流感。

senses.en: to support sb in an argument, a dispute, etc.
senses.zh: 支持某人﹙反对…﹚；和某人站在一起﹙ 反对… ﹚ :

ex.en: The children always sided with their mother ().
ex.zh: 孩子们总是站在妈妈一边┓磳Π职蜘w。

senses.en: to approach sb in a shy,uncertain or secret way
senses.zh: 羞怯﹙或犹豫、悄悄﹚地走向﹙某人﹚:

ex.en: She sidled up to him and whispered in his ear.
ex.zh: 她不动声色地走到他旁边，对着他的耳朵低语。

senses.en: to separate sth, usually sth you want, from a group of things
senses.zh: 从﹙ 众多东西中﹚ 选取﹙ 拟保留的﹚；筛选；挑选:

ex.en: to sift () the good from the bad
ex.zh: 去粗取精

senses.en: to separate sth, usually sth you do not want, from a group of things﹙
senses.zh: 从众多东西中﹚去掉﹙不适合的﹚；剔除；淘汰:

ex.en: We need to sift out unsuitable applications.
ex.zh: 我们需要剔出不合资格的申请。

ex.en: He helped me sift out the bad songs I’d written.
ex.zh: 他帮我筛除了我那些写得不好的歌。

senses.en: to carefully examine a large amount of sth in order to find sth important or decide what is useful and what is not
senses.zh: 详细审查…， 仔细检查… ﹙ 以寻找… ﹚ :

ex.en: I sifted through his papers for clues.
ex.zh: 我认真推敲了他的文件寻找线索。

ex.en: The judges sifted through 8 000 entries and finally picked the winner.
ex.zh: 裁判详细查看了8 000 份参赛作品，最后选了获奖者。

senses.en: to give up your rights, property,etc. by signing a document
senses.zh: 签字放弃，签字让与﹙权利或财产等﹚:

ex.en: The artist lost millions by signing away his rights to the cartoon character he created.
ex.zh: 这位艺术家签字放弃了他创作的卡通人物的所有权，因此损失很大。

senses.en: to sign a form, etc. as proof that you have received sth

ex.en: The postman asked me to sign for the packet.
ex.zh: 邮递员要我签收小包裹。

senses.en: to write your name or the name of a guest when you arrive at an office, a club, etc.﹙

ex.en: All visitors must sign in on arrival.
ex.zh: 来客均须签到。

ex.en: You have to be signed in by a member.
ex.zh: 你必须由会员帮你签到。

senses.en: ) to end a letter, a postcard, etc.
senses.zh: 结束写信﹙或写明信片等﹚:

ex.en: I’ll sign off now and post this.
ex.zh: 我马上就把这个写完并寄出去。

senses.en: to end a broadcast by saying goodbye or playing a piece of music﹙
senses.zh: 以说再见或播放音乐的形式﹚结束播送:

ex.en: I’ll sign off with a reminder to tune in again tomorrow.
ex.zh: 现在结束播音，明天请继续收听。

senses.en: to express your approval of sth formally and definitely

ex.en: The President hasn’t yet signed off on this report.
ex.zh: 这份报告总统还没有批准。

senses.en: , ) to sign a form stating that you are unemployed so that you can receive payment from the government
senses.zh: 办理失业登记﹙以领取失业救济金﹚:

ex.en: He had to sign on when the factory closed.
ex.zh: 工厂倒闭他不得不办理失业登记。
