senses.en: , ) to announce the start of broadcasting for the day

ex.en: This is Jack Grainger signing on.
ex.zh: 我是杰克·格兰杰，现在开始播音。

senses.en: to write your name or the name of a guest when you leave an office, a club,etc.﹙

ex.en: Don’t forget to sign out when you go.
ex.zh: 离开时别忘了签退。

ex.en: You must sign your guests out when they leave the club.
ex.zh: 客人离开俱乐部，你必须替他们签退。

senses.en: to sign a document to say officially that sth can be removed from a place or that you have taken it
senses.zh: 签字﹙同意﹚取用﹙或借用等﹚:

ex.en: There is no record of the file being signed out again.
ex.zh: 又一次欠签借阅文件记录。

senses.en: to give your rights or property to sb else by signing a document

ex.en: He signed the house over to his daughter.
ex.zh: 他签署了转让手续，把房子过到女儿名下。

senses.en: (with/for sb) to sign a document saying that you agree to work for sb, play for their team, etc.; to persuade sb to do this﹙

ex.en: She’s signed up with an employment agency.
ex.zh: 她已签约受雇于一家职介所。

ex.en: We’ve signed up three new players.
ex.zh: 我们签约聘用了三个新队员。

senses.en: (for sth) to arrange to do a course of study by adding your name or sb else’s name to the list of people doing it﹙
senses.zh: 帮某人﹚报名，注册﹙上某课程﹚:

ex.en: I’ve signed up for a pottery course.
ex.zh: 我已经报名上陶艺班。

ex.en: Shall I sign you up for the workshop too?
ex.zh: 我要不要也替你报名参加讲习班？

senses.en: to agree to become a member of the armed forces; to persuade sb to do this﹙

ex.en: He tried to sign up when he was only fifteen.
ex.zh: 他才十五岁就想签合同服役。

senses.en: to become blocked with sand, mud, etc. that has been brought by flowing water; to block sth in this way﹙

ex.en: The old harbour has silted up.
ex.zh: 老港口已经淤塞。

ex.en: Mud is silting up the stream.
ex.zh: 泥沙把小河淤塞了。

senses.en: to become calm after a period of anger, excitement, violence, etc.

ex.en: Just simmer down and we’ll discuss this calmly.
ex.zh: 先平静一下，然后我们心平气和地谈谈这件事。

senses.en: (to sth)to sing together with sb who is already singing or while a record, radio, or musical instrument is playing

ex.en: He sang along with the CD.
ex.zh: 他跟着光盘唱歌。

ex.en: We sang along to all the songs.
ex.zh: 我们跟唱了所有的歌。

senses.en: an informal occasion at which people sing songs together

ex.en: We had a great singalong in the pub last night.
ex.zh: 我们昨晚在酒吧齐声跟唱，妙极了。

senses.en: to sing or say sth clearly and loudly

ex.en: Sing out so that everyone can hear.
ex.zh: 亮开嗓门唱， 让大家都能听见。

ex.en: If you need anything, just sing out.
ex.zh: 需要什么就喊一声。

senses.en: to sing more loudly
senses.zh: 更大声地唱；放开嗓门唱:

ex.en: Sing up, I can’t hear you.
ex.zh: 大点声唱，我听不见。

senses.en: to choose sb/sth from among a group for special comment or treatment﹙
senses.zh: 为某事﹚ 单独挑出﹙ 人或事物﹚；单独挑出……﹙作为…﹚:

ex.en: They singled her out for particular praise.
ex.zh: 她给点名特别加以表扬。

ex.en: He was singled out as the best student.
ex.zh: 他被评选为最优秀的学生。

senses.en: to move or fall backwards,or lie down, especially when you are feeling tired

ex.en: She sank back into her chair.
ex.zh: 她向后一仰靠在椅子上。

ex.en: He sank back against the pillows, exhausted.
ex.zh: 他筋疲力尽地靠到枕头上。

senses.en: (of liquids
senses.zh: 液体) to go down into another substance渗透；渗入…中:

ex.en: Apply the moisturiser and let it sink in.
ex.zh: 擦上润肤霜，让它渗进皮肤。

ex.en: The rain sank into the dry ground.
ex.zh: 雨水渗进了乾地里。

senses.en: (of words, etc.
senses.zh: 话语等) to be fully understood or realized被完全理解；消化；被吸收:

ex.en: It took a while for the news to sink in.
ex.zh: 人们过了一段时间才完全明白这则消息。

ex.en: He paused to let his words sink into her brain.
ex.zh: 他停了一下，好让她充分领会他的意思。

senses.en: to go gradually into a less active,happy or pleasant state
senses.zh: 渐渐进入﹙消极、不快等的﹚状态:

ex.en: She sank into a deep sleep.
ex.zh: 她沉沉地睡去。

ex.en: He sank deeper into depression.
ex.zh: 他越来越消沉。

senses.en: to go deep into sth solid; to make sth sharp do this﹙

ex.en: Sharp teeth sank into his arm.
ex.zh: 锋利的牙齿刺入了他的胳膊。

ex.en: The dog sank its teeth into my leg.
ex.zh: 狗猛咬我的腿。

senses.en: to drink sth slowly, taking a very small amount each time

ex.en: She sipped at her coffee.
ex.zh: 她一点一点地抿咖啡。

senses.en: to move money or resources from one place to another,usually illegally﹙
senses.zh: 非法﹚将﹙钱或资源﹚抽走，转移:

ex.en: She siphoned off profits into her own bank account.
ex.zh: 她私自将赢利转到了她本人的银行账户上。

senses.en: to spend time sitting down doing very little

ex.en: I’m far too busy to sit around here all day.
ex.zh: 我忙得很，没空在这儿成天闲坐着。

ex.en: We sat about talking for most of the morning.
ex.zh: 今天我们大半上午都坐着闲聊。

senses.en: to sit or lean comfortably in a chair
senses.zh: 舒服地坐﹙或靠在椅子上﹚:

ex.en: He sat back in his chair and closed his eyes.
ex.zh: 他安稳地坐在椅子上闭上眼睛。

senses.en: (and do sth) to relax, especially by not getting too involved in or anxious about sth
to do nothing to stop sth bad or unpleasant happening

ex.en: I’m not going to sit by and let an innocent man go to jail.
ex.zh: 我不会坐视一个无辜的人去坐牢的。

senses.en: to lower your body until you are sitting on a chair, etc.

ex.en: Please sit down!
ex.zh: 请坐！

ex.en: We sat down on the sofa.
ex.zh: 我们在沙发上坐下。

senses.en: (and do sth) to give time and attention to sth in order to try to solve a problem or achieve sth
[C] a strike, demonstration, protest,etc. involving people sitting down and refusing to leave a place
senses.zh: 静坐罢工﹙或示威、抗议等﹚:

ex.en: to stage a sit-down
ex.zh: 发起静坐请愿

ex.en: a sitdown protest
ex.zh: 静坐抗议

senses.en: [sing.] (, )a short rest while sitting

ex.en: I need a sit-down.
ex.zh: 我需要坐着休息一下。

senses.en: to lower your body until you are sitting on a chair, etc.

ex.en: Come in and sit yourself down.
ex.zh: 进来坐下吧。

senses.en: to be a model for an artist or a photographer

ex.en: She sat for some of the most famous artists of her day.
ex.zh: 她为她那个时代一些最知名的艺术家当过模特。

senses.en: to attend a meeting, a class, etc. to watch it, not to take part

ex.en: I was allowed to sit in on the meeting.
ex.zh: 我获准列席会议。

ex.en: I sat in on some English classes.
ex.zh: 我旁听了一些英语课。

senses.en: a form of protest in which people refuse to leave a factory, a building, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 拒绝离开工厂、某建筑物等的﹚静坐示威，静坐抗议:

ex.en: Workers decided to stage a sit-in.
ex.zh: 工人们决定发起静坐罢工。

senses.en: to do sb’s job or perform sb’s duties while they are away

ex.en: The chief reporter often sat in for George as editor.
ex.zh: 主任记者常顶替乔治作编辑。

senses.en: to be a member of a group of people such as a committee

ex.en: How many people sit on the committee?
ex.zh: 委员会有多少成员？

ex.en: My mother sat on the jury during a famous murder trial.
ex.zh: 我母亲曾经当过一宗有名的谋杀案的陪审员。

senses.en: to sit outside somewhere rather than inside

ex.en: It’s too cold now to sit out.
ex.zh: 这会儿在外面坐着太冷了。

ex.en: Let’s sit out on the balcony.
ex.zh: 咱们坐到阳台上吧。

senses.en: to have a meal or a drink in a slow relaxed way

ex.en: We sat over breakfast and planned the day ahead.
ex.zh: 我们慢悠悠地吃着早餐，安排着一天的事。

senses.en: to stay until the end of a performance,speech, meeting, etc. that you think is boring or too long
senses.zh: 坐到﹙表演、演讲、会议等﹚结束:

ex.en: We had to sit through a whole dinner without a cigarette.
ex.zh: 我们一根烟都不能抽，一直等到宴会结束。

ex.en: I can’t sit through four hours of Shakespeare!
ex.zh: 我可没耐心看完四个小时的莎士比亚剧！

senses.en: to be or to move yourself into a sitting position, for example, from lying down

ex.en: He sat up, turned the light on, and looked at his watch.
ex.zh: 他坐起来打开灯，看了看表。

ex.en: Do you feel well enough to sit up yet?
ex.zh: 你感觉怎么样，能坐起来了吗？

senses.en: to not go to bed until later than usual

ex.en: We sat up late watching a movie.
ex.zh: 我们熬夜看了场电影。

senses.en: (and do sth) to suddenly give your attention to sth
an exercise in which you move from lying down to a sitting position

ex.en: I do about sixty sit-ups a day.
ex.zh: 我每天做大约六十个仰卧起坐。

senses.en: to form a judgement or an opinion of sb/sth

ex.en: The two opponents were sizing each other up.
ex.zh: 两个对手相互打量着。

ex.en: I sized up the situation very quickly.
ex.zh: 我很快对形势作出了判断。

senses.en: to talk about sth difficult or embarrassing quickly, without giving attention to details﹙
senses.zh: 把困难或尴尬的事﹚轻轻带过；避重就轻；轻描淡写:

ex.en: She skated over the next part of her story.
ex.zh: 她把自己的故事的下一个片段一带而过。

senses.en: to give more information or details about sth

ex.en: He sketched in the background to the case.
ex.zh: 他补充说明了这件事的背景。

ex.en: I’ll sketch in the details later for you.
ex.zh: 我以后给你补上细节。

senses.en: to draw all the main features of sth without showing exact details

ex.en: He sketched out some preliminary designs.
ex.zh: 他简单地勾了几个初步的设计。

senses.en: to give a brief general description of a plan or an idea

ex.en: She sketched out the plots of her novels in an exercise book.
ex.zh: 她在练习本里勾勒了她的小说的情节。

senses.en: to remove a substance such as fat from the surface of a liquid
senses.zh: 撇去﹙液体表面的油脂等﹚:

ex.en: Skim off the fat and reheat the stew.
ex.zh: 把油撇掉后再把炖菜热一热。

senses.en: to take the best part of sth for yourself, often in an unfair or dishonest way
senses.zh: 攫取﹙最好的部份﹚；捞取﹙精华部份﹚:

ex.en: She’s been skimming off a percentage of the profits for years.
ex.zh: 她多年来一直在捞取一定百分比的利润。

senses.en: to read sth very quickly in order to get a general impression or to find a particular point

ex.en: I only had time to skim through the report.
ex.zh: 我只来得及粗略看一遍报告。

ex.en: He skimmed through the article trying to find his name.
ex.zh: 他浏览了一下文章想找自己的名字。

senses.en: to spend less money or time on sth than is normal or necessary
senses.zh: 节省﹙ 钱或时间﹚；省吃俭用:

ex.en: Older people shouldn’t skimp on food or heating.
ex.zh: 老年人不应过分吝惜食物或取暖方面的开销。

senses.en: to leave a place secretly or suddenly, especially for a dishonest reason, for example to avoid paying for sth﹙
senses.zh: 出于不正当的原因﹚熘走，突然离去:

ex.en: They skipped off without paying.
ex.zh: 他们没付钱就熘了。

senses.en: to leave sb,especially when they need you, or when you have a responsibility towards them; to try to avoid a difficult situation by leaving a place﹙
senses.zh: 尤指不顾某人或责任而﹚ 离开， 熘走， 逃避:

ex.en: He just skipped out on his wife leaving her with four kids to take care of.
ex.zh: 他撇下妻子就走了，还留下四个孩子让她照看。

ex.en: He was found 12 years after he skipped out on drugs charges.
ex.zh: 他在逃脱了贩毒指控12 年之后被找到了。

senses.en: to be or move around the edge
senses.zh: 环绕…的边缘；位于…的四周:

ex.en: We skirted around the pond and crossed the bridge.
ex.zh: 我们绕着池塘边走， 然后过桥。

senses.en: to avoid discussing or dealing with a difficult or embarrassing subject

ex.en: She tactfully skirted around the subject of money.
ex.zh: 她巧妙地避而不谈钱的事。

senses.en: to avoid work or school by staying away or leaving early

ex.en: I can skive off for a few hours.
ex.zh: 我可以提前几个小时熘出来。

ex.en: I decided to skive off school and tell my mum I had a bad headache.
ex.zh: 我决定不去上学，告诉妈妈我的头很疼。

senses.en: to do sth more slowly or work less hard than before

ex.en: We can’t slack off until everything is finished.
ex.zh: 等一切都完成了我们才可以放松。

senses.en: to become less busy or active

ex.en: We’ve been really busy, but things are starting to slacken off now.
ex.zh: 我们忙极了，不过现在事情开始减少了。

senses.en: to criticize sb/sth in a cruel, unkind way
senses.zh: 诋毁； 贬损； 辱骂:

ex.en: He’s always slagging his brother off.
ex.zh: 他老损他的弟弟。

senses.en: to put sth down with a lot of force, especially when you are angry

ex.en: She slammed the book down on the table.
ex.zh: 她把书摔在桌子上。

ex.en: I slammed down the phone (= put the receiver down and ended the phone conversation) in a rage.
ex.zh: 我愤怒地摔了电话。

senses.en: to crash, or to make sth crash, into sth with a lot of force﹙

ex.en: The jeep slammed into the wall.
ex.zh: 吉普车轰隆一声撞到墙上。

ex.en: In the crash she was slammed against the back of the seat.
ex.zh: 撞车时她被甩到了座位靠背上。

senses.en: to hit sb regularly or often, used especially of a man hitting a woman
senses.zh: 常常打，动辄殴打﹙尤指男性打女性﹚:

ex.en: He used to come back drunk and slap his wife around.
ex.zh: 他过去经常醉醺醺地回家打他的妻子。

senses.en: to criticize sb or their ideas or suggestions in an unfair way, often in public

ex.en: He tried to object, but was immediately slapped down.
ex.zh: 他想申辩，可立即遭到了喝止。

ex.en: If you ask a question, she just slaps you down.
ex.zh: 你要是提问题，她就把你批一通。

senses.en: to announce suddenly that sb must have a punishment,obey a new rule etc., often when this is unfair
senses.zh: 突然强制实行﹙惩罚﹚；突然强迫遵守﹙ 新规则等﹚ :

ex.en: Judges have been slapping on longer prison sentences.
ex.zh: 法官们一直判处较长的刑期。

ex.en: The government slapped a new tax on high earners.
ex.zh: 政府突然对高收入者强制实行新税种。

senses.en: to spread a substance on a surface quickly and carelessly﹙
senses.zh: 在…上﹚胡乱涂抹，随意涂抹:

ex.en: I’d better slap some make-up on before I go out.
ex.zh: 我出门以前最好是简单化化妆。

senses.en: to increase the price of sth suddenly
senses.zh: 突然把…的价格提高…；忽然提价:

ex.en: They’ve slapped 50p on the price of cigarettes.
ex.zh: 他们把香烟的价格一下子提高了50 便士。

senses.en: to attack sb violently with a knife, etc. and try to cut them/it﹙

ex.en: He slashed at his opponent’s face with a knife.
ex.zh: 他用刀子猛划对手的脸。

senses.zh: (通常用于进行时) used to emphasize how hard you are working, especially when you think people do not recognize this or feel grateful﹙默默地﹚辛勤劳作，做苦力:

ex.en: I’ve been slaving away all day trying to get this work finished.
ex.zh: 我忙了一整天想把这活儿干完。

senses.en: to remain in bed longer than usual in the morning﹙

ex.en: She usually sleeps in on Sundays.
ex.zh: 她星期天通常睡懒觉。

senses.en: to get better after sth, especially drinking too much alcohol, by sleeping
senses.zh: 靠睡觉来消除；睡一觉熬过﹙酒劲﹚:

ex.en: He’s still sleeping off yesterday’s hangover.
ex.zh: 他还在睡觉消除昨天的宿醉呢。

senses.en: to delay making a decision about sth until the next day so that you can think about it
senses.zh: 把…留待第二天决定；把…拖延到第二天再说:

ex.en: Sleep on it and let me know tomorrow.
ex.zh: 晚上考虑考虑，明天给我个答覆。

senses.en: to sleep outdoors

ex.en: We slept out most nights when we were in Greece.
ex.zh: 我们在希腊时大部份时间露宿。

senses.en: to stay the night at sb else’s home

ex.en: The kids are sleeping over with friends.
ex.zh: 孩子们在朋友家过夜。

ex.en: It’s very late now — why don’t you sleep over?
ex.zh: 现在已经很晚了——为什么不就睡这儿呢？

senses.en: a party for children or young people when a group of them spend the night at one house﹙
senses.zh: 儿童或年轻人在某人家里的﹚过夜聚会

senses.en: to not be woken up by sth such as a loud noise or a lot of activity
senses.zh: 不被﹙吵闹声或混乱﹚吵醒；睡觉不受…影响:

ex.en: She slept right through the thunderstorm.
ex.zh: 她完全没被暴风雨吵醒。

ex.en: I’m afraid I slept through the alarm.
ex.zh: 或许闹钟没把我叫醒。

senses.en: to have sex with sb, especially sb you are not married to
senses.zh: 和某人﹙尤指非配偶﹚发生性关系:

ex.en: They have been sleeping together for months now.
ex.zh: 他们一块儿睡觉已经有几个月了。

senses.en: to remove a thin piece of sth from sth larger by cutting﹙

ex.en: The top of his finger was sliced off in an accident.
ex.zh: 他的指尖在一次事故中被切掉了。

ex.en: She sliced a piece of meat off the joint.
ex.zh: 她从大块烤肉上切下一片。

senses.en: to reduce sth by a particular amount

ex.en: He sliced two seconds off the world record.
ex.zh: 他把世界纪录缩短了两秒。

senses.en: to pass through sth very easily

ex.en: The axe sliced through the wood like butter.
ex.zh: 这把斧子噼木柴如同切黄油一样轻松。

ex.en: () He sliced through all my objections.
ex.zh: 他轻而易举地避开了我的一切反对。

senses.en: to cut sth into flat thin pieces

ex.en: Would you slice the cucumber up?
ex.zh: 请把黄瓜切成片好吗？

senses.en: to become thinner, for example as a result of eating less﹙

ex.en: She slimmed down to 60 kilos before her wedding.
ex.zh: 她在婚礼前把体重减到了60 公斤。

senses.en: to make sth, such as an organization or a company, smaller by employing fewer people, reducing the amount of work done, etc.
senses.zh: 精简﹙机构﹚；裁减﹙人员﹚；减少﹙岗位等﹚:

ex.en: The coal industry has had to slim down.
ex.zh: 煤炭工业还得压缩。

ex.en: The firm had to slim down its workforce.
ex.zh: 公司不得不裁减职工。

senses.en: (from sb) to disappear; to die or to stop existing
senses.zh: 消失； 消亡； 死去:

ex.en: He slipped away (= died) peacefully during the night.
ex.zh: 他夜间安详地去世了。

ex.en: I felt the game was slipping away from me (= I was losing).
ex.zh: 我感觉我要输掉比赛了。

senses.en: 1=SLIP AWAY 2

ex.en: Time just seemed to slip by.
ex.zh: 时间好像悄悄地就过去了。

senses.en: to add sth to a speech, conversation or written text quickly or secretly﹙
senses.zh: 在说话或文字中﹚插入﹙几句话等﹚:

ex.en: He usually slips a couple of jokes into his lectures.
ex.zh: 他讲课时常捎带插进几个笑话。

ex.en: She slipped in a few comments about her boyfriend.
ex.zh: 她插话讲了讲她的男友。

senses.en: to put clothes on quickly and easily

ex.en: I’ll just slip into something more comfortable.
ex.zh: 我套件舒服点的衣服就行了。

senses.en: to pass into a particular state or situation, especially a difficult or unpleasant one
senses.zh: 进入，陷入﹙尤指困难或不快的状况﹚:

ex.en: The patient slipped into a coma.
ex.zh: 病人陷入了昏迷。

ex.en: The economy has slipped into recession.
ex.zh: 经济开始衰退。

senses.en: to take clothes or shoes off quickly and easily
senses.zh: 迅速轻易地脱下﹙ 或脱掉﹚ :

ex.en: She slipped her shoes off by the door.
ex.zh: 她在门旁一下子踢掉了鞋子。

ex.en: Slip off your coat and I’ll make some tea.
ex.zh: 快把外衣脱了，我去沏茶。

senses.en: to put clothes or shoes on quickly and easily

ex.en: Hold on, I’ll just slip my coat on, then I’ll be ready.
ex.zh: 等一下，我披上外衣就好了。

senses.en: [usually pl.] a shoe that you can put on and take off quickly and easily without having to tie or fasten anything﹙

ex.en: a pair of cheap slip-ons
ex.zh: 一双便宜的无带便鞋

ex.en: slip-on shoes
ex.zh: 无带便鞋

senses.en: to slide a short distance and fall

ex.en: He slipped over on the ice and broke his leg.
ex.zh: 他在冰上滑了一跤摔断了腿。

senses.en: when sb/sth slips through the net, an organization or a system fails to find them and deal with them
senses.zh: 被漏掉；得不到处理；漏网:

ex.en: We tried to contact all the former students, but some slipped through the net.
ex.zh: 我们尝试和所有校友取得联系，可有一些找不到。

senses.en: to make a careless mistake

ex.en: I slipped up over the date of the meeting.
ex.zh: 我不小心把开会日期搞错了。

ex.en: He slipped up in his calculations.
ex.zh: 他的计算有粗心错误。

senses.en: () a careless mistake

ex.en: One small slip-up could cost us the election.
ex.zh: 一个小小的失误就会让我们选举失败。

senses.en: to spend time being lazy and doing nothing

ex.en: We just slobbed out in front of the telly last night.
ex.zh: 我们昨晚就看了看电视打发时间。

ex.en: Are you going to slob around in your pyjamas all morning?
ex.zh: 你是不是要穿着睡衣晃荡一上午？

senses.en: to work hard and steadily at sth, especially a boring or difficult task, for a long time

ex.en: He slogged away at that report for weeks.
ex.zh: 他埋头苦干了几个星期写那份报告。

senses.en: to work hard and steadily at sth, especially a boring or difficult task, for a long time

ex.en: I seem to have been slogging through this book for weeks.
ex.zh: 我好像用了好几个星期啃这本书了。

senses.en: (in sth) (of a liquid
senses.zh: 液体)to move around in a container, often so that some liquid comes over the edge晃盪；﹙常指﹚溢出，溅出:

ex.en: Water was slopping about in the bottom of the boat.
ex.zh: 水在船底晃来晃去。

senses.en: (in sth) to move around in water,mud, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 在水、泥等里﹚趟来趟去，走动:

ex.en: She slopped around in the cooling water.
ex.zh: 她在凉爽的水里走来走去。

senses.en: (of a liquid
senses.zh: 液体) to move around in a container so much that some liquid comes out over the edge晃出； 溅出:

ex.en: Some tea had slopped over into the saucer.
ex.zh: 一些茶水晃到了茶托上。

ex.en: Water slopped over the edge of the bath.
ex.zh: 水从浴缸边上溅出了。

senses.en: to go away, especially without being noticed, in order to avoid doing work, talking to sb, etc.﹙

ex.en: He always slopes off if there’s any work to be done.
ex.zh: 一到要干活时他就开熘。

ex.en: Where are you trying to slope off to?
ex.zh: 你要躲到哪里去？

senses.en: (of a liquid
senses.zh: 液体) to move around noisily in a container﹙在容器里﹚晃盪作响:

ex.en: The water was sloshing about in the bucket.
ex.zh: 水在桶里哗啦哗啦地晃着。

senses.en: to manage to find a time to see sb or to do sth
senses.zh: 为…安排时间；抽时间﹙见某人、做某事﹚:

ex.en: I can slot you in tomorrow at four.
ex.zh: 我可以把你安排在明天四点钟。

senses.en: to put something into a space that is available or designed for it
senses.zh: 把…投入﹙已有的或设计好的空隙﹚:

ex.en: He slotted a coin into the machine.
ex.zh: 他往机器里投了一枚硬币。

senses.en: to spend time relaxing or being lazy

ex.en: He slouches around all day reading comics.
ex.zh: 他闲散地看了一整天的连环画。

ex.en: She wasted the day slouching about the house.
ex.zh: 她在屋子里晃悠了一天。

senses.en: to remove or get rid of a layer of dead skin, etc.

ex.en: Slough off dry skin once a week.
ex.zh: 每周除一次乾皮。

senses.en: to go, or to make sb/sth go, at a slower speed﹙

ex.en: Slow down, I can’t keep up with you.
ex.zh: 慢点，我跟不上你。

ex.en: The bus slowed up as it approached the junction.
ex.zh: 公共汽车在驶近交叉路口时放慢了速度。

senses.en: to be less active or develop more slowly; to make sb/sth do this﹙
senses.zh: 使某人﹚松弛；﹙使发展﹚减缓:

ex.en: He looks ill, he should slow down.
ex.zh: 他看上去不太舒服，应该放松一下。

ex.en: The economy has slowed down.
ex.zh: 经济放缓了。

senses.en: a decrease in the rate of activity or production﹙
senses.zh: 活动或生产的﹚ 减速:

ex.en: a slowdown in the economy
ex.zh: 经济放缓

senses.en: ) a protest that workers make by doing their work more slowly than usual

ex.en: The union threatened a slowdown if their demands were not met.
ex.zh: 工会威胁说如果不答应他们的要求，他们就怠工。

senses.en: to fight; to compete until sb has won
senses.zh: 斗争；比出胜负；一决雌雄:

ex.en: The two companies slugged it out for their share of the market.
ex.zh: 两家公司为争夺市场一较高下。

ex.en: The Democrats and the Republicans will be slugging it out in November.
ex.zh: 民主党和共和党将于十一月一决雌雄。

senses.en: to wash or clean the surface of sth with large amounts of water
senses.zh: 冲 洗， 洗净﹙ 表面﹚ :

ex.en: They sluice the streets down every morning.
ex.zh: 他们每天早晨冲洗街道。

ex.en: An attendant was sluicing out the changing rooms.
ex.zh: 一位服务员正在冲洗更衣室。

senses.en: to seem to contain an unpleasant attitude or quality
senses.zh: 有﹙否定的﹚态度；带有﹙消极的﹚意味:

ex.en: His comments smack of racism.
ex.zh: 他的评论带有种族主义的味道。

senses.en: ) to become more clever and aware of things

ex.en: You’ll have to smarten up if you want to pass those exams.
ex.zh: 你要是想通过考试，思维就必须更加敏捷。

senses.en: to make a person or a place neater, tidier or more attractive
senses.zh: 使﹙人或地方﹚整洁起来；使变得光鲜亮丽:

ex.en: The hotel has been smartened up by the new owners.
ex.zh: 新业主把旅馆修葺一新。

ex.en: She did her best to smarten her husband up.
ex.zh: 她尽最大努力把丈夫打扮得更英俊。

senses.en: to make sth fall by hitting it very hard and breaking it﹙

ex.en: The police decided to smash the door down.
ex.zh: 警察决定破门而入。

senses.en: to make a hole in sth or destroy it by hitting it very hard﹙

ex.en: The doll’s face had been smashed in.
ex.zh: 玩具娃娃的脸被打瘪了。

senses.en: to damage or destroy sth by hitting it very hard

ex.en: A bunch of thugs broke in and smashed the place up.
ex.zh: 一帮恶棍闯进来把这个地方砸了个乱七八糟。

ex.en: He smashed his car up last week (= he had a crash).
ex.zh: 他上个星期把汽车撞毁了。

senses.en: to have the smell of sth

ex.en: The baby smelled of soap and milk.
ex.zh: 孩子身上散发着肥皂味和奶味。

ex.en: Can you put your cigarette out? I don’t want my room smelling of smoke.
ex.zh: 把烟灭了好吗？我不希望我的房间里有烟味儿。

senses.en: to still have a good reputation, even though you have been involved in sth that might have given people a bad opinion of you
senses.zh: 虽卷入…而好名声依旧；事后于名誉无损

senses.en: to be aware of fear, danger,trouble, etc. in a situation
senses.zh: 觉察到，意识到﹙危险、麻烦等﹚:

ex.en: He could smell out weakness in others.
ex.zh: 他能够抓住他人的弱点。

senses.en: (of dogs
senses.zh: 狗) to detect sb/sth, by smelling嗅出；闻出:

ex.en: The dogs are trained to smell out drugs.
ex.zh: 这些狗是经训练用于缉毒的。

senses.en: to fill a place with an unpleasant smell

ex.en: That fish smelt the whole house out.
ex.zh: 那鱼让整个房子充满腥味。

senses.en: to make sb/sth come out of a place by filling it with smoke

ex.en: The fire is used to smoke the bees out.
ex.zh: 用火把蜜蜂燻出来。

senses.en: to find sb/sth that is causing a problem;to make sth that is secret publicly known
senses.zh: 找到﹙坏人或问题根源﹚；揭露﹙秘密﹚:

ex.en: The police are determined to smoke out the leaders of the gang.
ex.zh: 警方决心揪出犯罪团伙的头目。

senses.en: to reduce or remove problems and difficulties
senses.zh: 减少， 消除， 克服﹙问题或困难﹚:

ex.en: The group was set up to smooth away local difficulties.
ex.zh: 成立这个组的目的是解决当地的困难。

ex.en: His anxieties were quickly smoothed away.
ex.zh: 他的担心很快就消除了。

senses.en: to make your hair or your clothes smooth and flat with your hands
senses.zh: 用手将﹙头发或衣服﹚弄光滑平整:

ex.en: He smoothed down his hair.
ex.zh: 他把头发抚平。

senses.en: to make sth such as a piece of paper or cloth smooth and flat with your hands
senses.zh: 将﹙纸张、布等﹚抚平；使光滑平整:

ex.en: She tried to smooth out the crumpled letter.
ex.zh: 她试着把皱巴巴的信抻平。

senses.en: to make a problem or difficulty seem less serious or easier to deal with,especially by talking to the people involved
to eat small amounts of food between or instead of meals

ex.en: It’s healthier to snack on fruit rather than chocolate.
ex.zh: 以水果当零食比吃巧克力更有益于健康。

senses.en: to say sth in a sharp or unpleasant way

ex.en: The sergeant snapped out an order.
ex.zh: 中士厉声下达命令。

senses.en: to make yourself, or help sb else, stop feeling upset, in a bad mood, etc.; to wake up from a day dream﹙
senses.zh: 帮某人﹚ 消除烦恼﹙或坏心情等﹚；从白日梦中醒来:

senses.en: used to tell sb to start working harder or more quickly

ex.en: This place has to be clean by this evening so snap to it!
ex.zh: 这个地方到晚上必须乾乾净净，加紧干吧！

senses.en: to buy or seize sth quickly and eagerly

ex.en: Fans quickly snapped up the tickets.
ex.zh: 球迷很快就把门票抢购一空。

ex.en: ( ) He was snapped up by United.
ex.zh: 他被联队抢去了。

senses.en: (, ) a situation in which traffic is unable to move
to try to take hold of sth

ex.en: She snatched at the letter in his hand.
ex.zh: 她伸手去抓他手里的信。

senses.en: ) to take an opportunity to do sth eagerly and quickly

ex.en: They snatched at the chance to be happy.
ex.zh: 他们抓住机会开心一下。

senses.en: to approach sb very quietly, so that they do not see or hear you until you reach them

ex.en: He loves sneaking up on me to scare me.
ex.zh: 他就爱偷偷熘到我身边吓唬我。

ex.en: She snuck up behind them and suddenly shouted.
ex.zh: 她蹑手蹑脚地走到他们身后，然后突然大喊一声。

senses.en: to go somewhere to try to find secret information about sth/sb or to look for a particular person or thing
senses.zh: 探查， 打探， 访查﹙ 秘密信息﹚:

ex.en: Representatives from the studio were sniffing around for new talent.
ex.zh: 电影公司的代表在四处物色新秀。

ex.en: It won’t be long before the press come sniffing around the club.
ex.zh: 记者们很快就会来这个俱乐部访查的。

senses.en: to show a lack of interest in or respect for sth
senses.zh: 对…嗤之以鼻﹙或不屑一顾﹚:

ex.en: At first he sniffed at her foreign ways.
ex.zh: 起初他对她的外国作风嗤之以鼻。

senses.en: good enough to be accepted or considered seriously
senses.zh: 值得认真对待； 不容轻视:

ex.en: Her achievement is not to be sniffed at.
ex.zh: 不可小看她的成绩。

senses.en: (especially of dogs
senses.zh: 尤指狗) to find sb/sth by smelling嗅出；闻出:

ex.en: These dogs can sniff out explosives.
ex.zh: 这些狗能闻出炸药。

senses.en: to be unable to go anywhere or leave a place because of heavy snow

ex.en: We got snowed in for three days.
ex.zh: 我们被大雪困了三天。

senses.en: to have so much work that you have problems dealing with it﹙

ex.en: We’re snowed under with work at the moment.
ex.zh: 我们现在让工作压得直不起腰。

senses.en: 1=BE/GET SNOWED IN/UP
2(of a road, etc.
senses.zh: 道路等) to be/become blocked with snow被雪封住:

ex.en: The driveway was still snowed up.
ex.zh: 车行道依然被雪封着。

senses.en: to kill sb

ex.en: He was snuffed out by the Mafia.
ex.zh: 他被黑手党杀了。

senses.en: to make yourself warm and comfortable in your bed

ex.en: He snuggled down and went to sleep.
ex.zh: 他舒舒服服地躺在床上睡着了。

senses.en: to get into a warm and comfortable position close to sb/sth or in sth﹙
senses.zh: 温暖舒适地﹚偎依，挨近﹙人或物﹚，蜷伏在:

ex.en: She snuggled up to him on the sofa.
ex.zh: 她依偎着他坐在沙发上。

ex.en: I’d love to snuggle up in bed right now!
ex.zh: 我真想立刻舒舒服服地躺到床上！

senses.en: (of a liquid
senses.zh: 液体) to pass into sth渗入； 渗进:

ex.en: Apply the oil to the wood and leave it to soak in.
ex.zh: 把油涂在木头上让它渗进去。

ex.en: The wine had soaked into the carpet.
ex.zh: 葡萄酒渗进了地毯。

senses.en: (of a liquid
senses.zh: 液体) to pass into or through sth渗入；渗透:

ex.en: Blood had soaked through the bandage.
ex.zh: 血透过绷带渗了出来。

senses.en: to take in or absorb sth, especially a liquid

ex.en: Use a paper towel to soak up the excess oil.
ex.zh: 用厚纸巾把多余的油吸去。

senses.en: to become, or to make sb, no longer drunk﹙

ex.en: I decided to walk home to sober up.
ex.zh: 我决定步行回家醒醒酒。

ex.en: I need a black coffee to sober me up.
ex.zh: 我需要一杯黑咖啡醒酒。

senses.en: to save money by putting it in a bank or by buying shares in a company, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 通过存银行或买股票﹚存，积攒﹙钱﹚:

ex.en: She already has $500 socked away for college.
ex.zh: 她已经存了500 元用于上大学。

ex.en: He socks away half his salary every month for the house.
ex.zh: 他每个月将工资的一半攒起来用于买房子。

senses.en: or ) used to encourage sb to do or say sth that will have a strong effect, for example before an interview, a sports game, etc.
senses.zh: 尽最大努力做某事；有力地对某人说…:

ex.en: You’ll be fine. Just get in there and sock it to them.
ex.zh: 没事的。只要进去好好发挥就行了。

senses.en: ,!, ) used to tell sb to go away

ex.en: Just sod off and leave me in peace!
ex.zh: 磙开，让我安静会儿！

senses.en: to try to make sb more willing to do sth for you by being very nice to them first

ex.en: I know you, you’re just trying to soften me up!
ex.zh: 我了解你，你只不过是在拉拢我！

ex.en: They softened the voters up with promises they had no intention of keeping.
ex.zh: 他们为拉拢选民，作出了他们无意兑现的承诺。

senses.en: to make an enemy weaker and easier to attack

ex.en: It’ll take more than a few bruises to soften him up.
ex.zh: 要把他制伏可不是件轻而易举的事。

ex.en: The artillery was used to soften up the advancing enemy.
ex.zh: 用了大炮来遏制向前挺进的敌人。

senses.en: to continue with sth you are doing although it is difficult or unpleasant

ex.en: She soldiered on with the course in spite of her personal problems.
ex.zh: 尽管她有些个人困难，她还是坚持上课。

ex.en: I’m having to soldier on alone since Bill left.
ex.zh: 比尔离开后，我不得不独自撑着。

senses.en: to deal with sb who has been causing trouble

ex.en: They sent the lads round to sort him out.
ex.zh: 他们派小伙子们去收拾他。

senses.en: to find a solution to sb’s/your own problems, etc.
senses.zh: 解决某人﹙或自己﹚的问题:

ex.en: It took her months to sort herself out after the divorce.
ex.zh: 离婚后，她过了好几个月才恢复正常生活。

ex.en: He was so upset it took us an hour to calm him down and sort him out.
ex.zh: 他十分难过，我们用了一个小时才让他平静下来并帮他解决问题。

senses.en: to organize sb or yourself
senses.zh: 组织某人，安顿某人﹙或自己﹚:

ex.en: You load the car and I’ll sort the kids out.
ex.zh: 你装车，我把孩子们安顿好。

ex.en: She’s in her room sorting herself out for the trip (=packing clothes, etc.).
ex.zh: 她在房间里打点行装。

senses.en: to provide sb with something they need
senses.zh: 给某人提供﹙ 所需物品﹚ :

ex.en: I’m sure we can sort you out with some dry clothes.
ex.zh: 我想我们一定能给你找几件乾衣服的。

senses.en: (, ) an act of arranging or organizing things in a neat and tidy way and getting rid of things you don’t want
to look through a number of things either in order to find a particular thing or to put them in groups

ex.en: She sorted through her wardrobe for something to wear.
ex.zh: 她翻遍衣柜找件穿的。

ex.en: They sorted through thousands of old photos.
ex.zh: 他们归整了几千张旧照片。

senses.en: to express your opinions loudly or in an aggressive way

ex.en: He should check his facts before sounding off like that.
ex.zh: 他应该先核实一下实情再那样高谈阔论。

senses.en: to try to discover sb’s views, opinions, etc. on sth, especially in an indirect way
senses.zh: 试探某人﹙对某事﹚的看法；探口风:

ex.en: I want to sound him out about a possible job.
ex.zh: 我想探探他的口风看看能不能得到那份工作。

ex.en: We should sound out opinions on these changes.
ex.zh: 我们应该试探一下人们对这些变革的看法。

senses.en: to be confused, unable to think clearly, or not aware of what is happening around you, for example as a result of taking drugs; to put sb in a state like this﹙
senses.zh: 药物等导致﹚精神恍惚，神志迷蒙:

ex.en: I was supposed to meet her for lunch but I spaced out and forgot.
ex.zh: 我本应该和她共进午餐，可我昏昏沉沉地忘记了。

ex.en: The drugs I was taking for my illness spaced me out so I couldn’t think clearly.
ex.zh: 我为治病吃的药把我弄得头晕脑胀，神志不清。

senses.en: () confused, unable to think clearly and not completely conscious of what is happening around you, for example because of taking drugs﹙
senses.zh: 药物等导致﹚精神恍惚的，神志迷蒙的:

ex.en: He sat in the corner looking completely spaced out.
ex.zh: 他坐在角落里，显得完全神色迷离。

senses.en: to arrange things with a regular distance or time between them, especially a fairly large amount
senses.zh: 使拉开﹙空间或时间上的﹚间距；使隔开:

ex.en: Try spacing the words out more on the page.
ex.zh: 把页面上的字间距再拉大些。

ex.en: Should I space out the baby’s feeds over 24 hours?
ex.zh: 我要不要把餵宝宝的时间按24小时平均分开？

senses.en: to cause something to suddenly happen or develop
senses.zh: 使突然发生﹙或发展﹚；引发；导致:

ex.en: The incident sparked off riots across the country.
ex.zh: 这件事引起了全国各地的骚乱。

ex.en: His resignation sparked off a political crisis.
ex.zh: 他辞职触发了一场政治危机。

senses.en: to add interest or excitement to sth
senses.zh: 给…增添趣味﹙ 或兴味﹚ :

ex.en: Spark up pasta dishes with fresh herbs.
ex.zh: 用新鲜香草给麵食调味。

ex.en: Send a card and spark up someone’s day.
ex.zh: 寄张贺卡，为人打打气。

senses.en: to state the wishes or views of sb;to act as a representative for sb

ex.en: I can’t speak for the others, but I’d love to come.
ex.zh: 我不能代表其他人讲话，但我很想来。

ex.en: She speaks for a whole generation of disillusioned youngsters.
ex.zh: 她代表着整整一代幻想破灭的青年。

senses.en: to express your own opinion,although you know that others might not agree with you
senses.zh: 表达自己的观点；按照个人的意见:

senses.en: to express your opinion yourself, rather than sb else doing it for you

ex.en: I can speak for myself, thank you!
ex.zh: 我自己能说清楚的，谢谢你！

senses.en: used to tell sb that sth they have said is not true of you﹙
senses.zh: 表示对方说的话只能代表他自己﹚:

ex.en: ‘We’re all tired.’ ‘Speak for yourself — I’m fine!’
ex.zh: “我们都累了。”“你说的是你自己吧─我可不累！”

senses.en: to be married or to have a partner already

ex.en: You can forget about him, he’s spoken for!
ex.zh: 你别去想他了，他是有妇之夫！

senses.en: to be set aside for a particular purpose

ex.en: Half the money is already spoken for.
ex.zh: 半数的钱已经留出来了。

senses.en: to be evidence of sth; to suggest sth

ex.en: The pictures and ornaments in the room spoke of dreams of faraway places.
ex.zh: 房间里的图画和摆设表明了对遥远地方的嚮往。

senses.en: to say what you think clearly and publicly, often criticizing or opposing sb/sth, in a way that needs courage
senses.zh: 挺身而出，站出来﹙表示反对、支持等﹚:

ex.en: People are no longer afraid to speak out.
ex.zh: 人们再也不惧怕站出来说话了。

ex.en: She spoke out against the regime.
ex.zh: 她公开表示反对这一政权。

senses.en: saying openly exactly what you think, even if you know other people will disagree or be offended

ex.en: Her outspoken views often get her into trouble.
ex.zh: 她坦率的观点常常给她惹麻烦。

senses.en: used to ask sb to speak louder

ex.en: Please speak up — we can’t hear you at the back.
ex.zh: 请大点声讲——我们在后面听不见。

senses.en: (for sb/sth/yourself) to say what you think clearly and freely, especially to support or defend sb/sth
senses.zh: 明确表态；﹙尤指为…﹚说好话，辩护:

ex.en: Several players spoke up for their manager.
ex.zh: 有几个运动员为他们的经理辩护。

ex.en: She’s learned to speak up for herself.
ex.zh: 她学会了据理力争。

senses.en: to leave very quickly, usually in a vehicle of some kind﹙

ex.en: The car sped away from the house.
ex.zh: 那辆车嗖地一声离开了那所房子。

ex.en: She sped off on her bike to get help.
ex.zh: 她飞快地骑着自行车去找人帮忙。

senses.en: to start to move or happen faster; to make sth do this﹙

ex.en: The train started to speed up.
ex.zh: 火车开始加速了。

ex.en: Parking restrictions were introduced to try to speed up the traffic.
ex.zh: 推行限制停车的规定以使交通提速。

senses.en: to make sth clear and easy to understand; to explain sth in detail
senses.zh: 解释明白；讲清楚；详细解释:

ex.en: His reasons for leaving are spelt out in detail in his letter.
ex.zh: 他在信中详细解释了他离开的原因。

ex.en: Surely I don’t have to spell it out? (= it should be obvious)
ex.zh: 我肯定不需要作进一步解释吧？

senses.en: to say or write the letters of a word in the correct order

ex.en: Could you spell that word out for me again? 你能不能把那个字再给我拼一次？

senses.en: to flow out quickly in large amounts; to make sth do this﹙

ex.en: lava spewing out from a volcano
ex.zh: 从火山中喷出的熔岩

ex.en: fumes spewed out by cars and trucks
ex.zh: 汽车和货车排放的废气

senses.en: to bring food from the stomach back out through the mouth

ex.en: He spewed up all over my jacket.
ex.zh: 他把我的上衣吐得到处都是。

senses.en: to add spice to food in order to give it more flavour and make it more interesting﹙

ex.en: Casseroles can be spiced up with a dash of tabasco sauce.
ex.zh: 炖锅菜里可加一点塔巴斯科辣椒酱调调味。

ex.en: () He exaggerated the details to spice up the story.
ex.zh: 他夸大了细节，把故事讲得更生动。

senses.en: to make sb/sth/yourself look more attractiv
senses.zh: 将…收拾得更漂亮；打扮；装扮:

senses.en: to accidentally flow out of a container﹙
senses.zh: 从容器中意外地﹚流出，洒出，溢出:

ex.en: The contents of her bag spilled out everywhere.
ex.zh: 她袋子里的东西洒得到处都是。

ex.en: Water had spilled out onto the floor.
ex.zh: 水流到了地板上。

senses.en: to come out in large numbers or amounts

ex.en: The theatre crowds spilled out onto the pavement.
ex.zh: 剧院的观众纷纷涌上人行道。

ex.en: The children spilled out into the yard.
ex.zh: 孩子们蜂拥到院子里。

senses.en: to tell sb a secret, your fears, worries, etc. in a hurried and unplanned way
to start in one situation or area and then have an effect on another situation or in another area
senses.zh: 波及，影响到﹙另一范围﹚；蜕变﹙成另一局面﹚:

ex.en: Unrest has spilt over into areas outside the city.
ex.zh: 骚乱已经波及城市的周边地区。

ex.en: Anger spilled over into violence at yesterday’s demonstration.
ex.zh: 在昨天的示威游行中，愤怒的人群后来采取了暴力。

senses.en: [U] [sing.] () people who move from a town or city because it is too crowded and go and live somewhere else

ex.en: These towns were built to house overspill populations from the big cities.
ex.zh: 兴建这些小镇是为了容纳从大城市迁出的过剩人口。

senses.en: something that is too large or too much for the place where it starts and spreads to other places
senses.zh: 容纳不下的部份；溢出部份:

ex.en: a spillover of riots
ex.zh: 其他地区引致的骚乱

ex.en: a spillover room for guests and friends (= a room where extra guests and friends can go)
ex.zh: 给客人和朋友使用的空闲房间

senses.en: the results and effects of sth that have spread to other situations or areas﹙
senses.zh: 波及其他情况或地区的﹚伴随结果，影响:

ex.en: Other resorts could benefit from the spillover (of tourists).
ex.zh: 其他度假胜地可以从游客带来的影响中间接受益。

ex.en: spillover effects/benefits
ex.zh: 间接影响/利益

senses.en: to flow over the edge of a container that is too full

ex.en: The water spilled over the rim of the glass.
ex.zh: 水从玻璃杯口溢出。

ex.en: Her tears suddenly spilled over (=she started to cry).
ex.zh: 她突然哭了起来。

senses.en: to turn very quickly to face in the opposite direction; to turn sb/sth in this way﹙

ex.en: She jumped when she heard her name and spun around to see the speaker.
ex.zh: 她听到自己的名字时吓了一跳，猛地回过身去看说话的人。

ex.en: He spun her round to face him.
ex.zh: 他拉她转过身面对着自己。

senses.en: to turn round and round quickly; to make sth do this﹙

ex.en: The propeller started to spin around.
ex.zh: 螺旋桨开始飞快地旋转起来。

ex.en: The room seemed to be spinning round.
ex.zh: 房间彷彿在不停地旋转。

senses.en: to produce a new product,material, service, etc. that is connected with sth successful that already exists; to be produced in this way﹙
senses.zh: 从成功的产品、服务等﹚派生，衍生:

ex.en: Calendars and diaries spinning off from familiar books and TV shows are always popular.
ex.zh: 根据喜闻乐见的书和电视节目生产的日历和日记本始终受欢迎。

ex.en: ‘A Different World’ was spun off from ‘The Cosby Show’.
ex.zh: 《与众不同的世界》是《科斯比节目》成功后的派生作品。

senses.en: an unexpected but useful result of an activity that is designed to produce sth else﹙
senses.zh: 意外但有用的﹚副产品，派生物:

ex.en: commercial spin-offs from medical research
ex.zh: 医学研究的商业副产品

ex.en: spin-off effects
ex.zh: 副作用

senses.en: a product or a book, film/movie, etc. that is based on a very successful book, film/movie or television series﹙
senses.zh: 根据成功的书、电影或电视系列剧制作的﹚派生作品，搭车产品:

ex.en: ‘The Cosby Show’ and its spinoff ‘A Different World’
ex.zh: 《科斯比节目》及其派生作品《与众不同的世界》

ex.en: a spin-off movie
ex.zh: 一部派生电影

senses.en: , ) to separate part of a company or an organization from the main part in order to form a new one﹙
senses.zh: 从公司或机构中﹚分拆出…:

ex.en: The fast food chain could be spun off as a separate company.
ex.zh: 这个快餐连锁店可以分拆出来作为独立公司。

senses.en: to make sth last as long as possible

ex.en: I managed to spin my talk out to an hour.
ex.zh: 我设法把讲话拖长到一个小时。

ex.en: She had to spin out her money until pay day.
ex.zh: 她得一分钱掰作两半花，坚持到发工资日。

senses.en: to remove sb/sth quickly, secretly or as if by magic
senses.zh: 迅速地﹙或秘密地﹚弄走；像变魔术般地转移…:

ex.en: He was spirited away by his friends before the police arrived.
ex.zh: 朋友们赶在警察到来之前把他悄悄转移了。

ex.en: An enormous amount of money had been spirited away in only two months.
ex.zh: 一笔巨款仅用了两个月就被神秘地转走了。

senses.en: used to tell sb to reveal a piece of information or to say sth when they are feeling nervous or unwilling to speak
senses.zh: 说出来吧； 有什么尽管说出来:

ex.en: Come on, spit it out! Who did it?
ex.zh: 快点说出来吧！是谁干的？

senses.en: to force sth out of your mouth

ex.en: It tasted so horrible he had to spit it out.
ex.zh: 那东西味道差极了，他只好吐了出来。

senses.en: to say sth very angrily

ex.en: ‘Men!’ She spat the word out.
ex.zh: “老兄们！”她愤怒地说。

senses.en: [U] the milk that a baby brings back out of its mouth
to spend money freely or carelessly
senses.zh: 无节制地花钱； 挥霍:

ex.en: He splashes his wages about just to impress her.
ex.zh: 他大手大脚地花工资只是为了引起她注意。

senses.en: to publish a photograph, a news story, etc. in a place where a lot of people will see it, especially in a newspaper
senses.zh: 把﹙照片、新闻报道等﹚安排在﹙报纸等的﹚显着位置；在突出位置刊载:

ex.en: The next day her name was splashed across all the front pages.
ex.zh: 第二天，她的名字出现在所有报纸的头版。

ex.en: I don’t want my private life splashed all over the tabloids.
ex.zh: 我不想让我的私生活刊载在所有小报的显着位置。

senses.en: to move about in water making it fly everywhere﹙

ex.en: The children splashed about in the river all afternoon.
ex.zh: 孩子们整个下午都在河里嬉水。

senses.en: [C] [U] the return of a spacecraft to earth when it lands in the sea/ocean
senses.zh: 溅落﹙指航天器坠入海洋﹚:

ex.en: Splashdown is expected 300 kilometres west of Valparai so.
ex.zh: 溅落位置预定在瓦尔帕来索以西300 公里。

senses.en: to spend a lot of money on sth

ex.en: She splashed out on a new pair of shoes.
ex.zh: 她花很多钱买了双新鞋。

ex.en: Why don’t we splash out and go out for a meal?
ex.zh: 我们为什么不潇洒一把出去吃顿饭呢？

senses.en: to separate from, or be separated from, a large object or a group﹙
senses.zh: 从……中﹚脱离，分裂出去， 分离:

ex.en: The branch had split away from the main trunk.
ex.zh: 那根树枝是从树干上折下的。

ex.en: The wind split the door away from its frame.
ex.zh: 强风把门从门框上颳了下来。

senses.en: to tell sb in authority about sth bad or wrong that sb has done﹙

ex.en: Promise you won’t split on me.
ex.zh: 你要答应不出卖我。

senses.en: to end a relationship or a marriage; to make two people stop having a relationship with each other﹙
senses.zh: 使和某人﹚断绝关系，分手:

ex.en: He told me he had split up with his girlfriend.
ex.zh: 他告诉我他和女友分手了。

ex.en: The band split up at the height of their fame.
ex.zh: 乐队在最红的时候散伙了。

senses.en: to divide sth into smaller parts

ex.en: The day was split up into 6 one-hour classes.
ex.zh: 一天分作6节课，每节课一小时。

ex.en: We split the profits up between us.
ex.zh: 我们把利润分了。

senses.zh: (只用于进行时) to be very eager to fight sb按捺不住想﹙和某人﹚打架:

ex.en: He was spoiling for a fight.
ex.zh: 他攒足了劲儿想打架。

senses.en: to wash sb/sth with a wet cloth or a soft material
senses.zh: 用湿布﹙或软材料﹚清洗人﹙或物﹚:

ex.en: I sponged the coat down to remove the mud.
ex.zh: 我用湿布擦洗掉外套上的泥。

ex.en: She tried sponging the baby down to lower his temperature.
ex.zh: 她试着用湿毛巾给孩子降体温。

senses.en: to get money, food, etc.from other people, without doing anything for them or offering to pay
senses.zh: 从某人处白拿钱﹙或食物等﹚ ； 揩油； 蹭﹙ 饭等﹚:

ex.en: He’s constantly sponging off his friends.
ex.zh: 他时常揩朋友的油。

senses.en: to remove a mark, some dirt, etc. with a wet cloth or a piece of a soft material
senses.zh: 用湿布﹙或软材料﹚除掉污迹﹙或尘土等﹚:

ex.en: It was impossible to sponge the mark off.
ex.zh: 这块污斑擦不掉。

ex.en: I couldn’t sponge the stain off my dress.
ex.zh: 我擦不掉我连衣裙上的污迹。

senses.en: to talk about sth in a boring or annoying way

ex.en: He’s always spouting off about the behaviour of young people today.
ex.zh: 他总是没完没了地数落如今年轻人的行为。

ex.en: What are you spouting on about now?
ex.zh: 你在囉嗦什么呢？

senses.en: to sit or lie down with your arms and legs spread out in a relaxed or awkward way

ex.en: He came home and just sprawled out on the sofa.
ex.zh: 他回到家就四肢舒展地倒在沙发上。

senses.en: to gradually cover a wider area

ex.en: The city has spread out into what used to be countryside.
ex.zh: 城市渐渐延伸到了从前的乡村。

ex.en: The ripples spread out across the water.
ex.zh: 波纹在水面上扩散开。

senses.en: [NOTE]When this phrasal verb is used with a reflexive pronoun, the pronoun is always plural: ourselves,yourselves or themselves.
senses.zh: 这个短语动词和反身代词连用时，这个代词用复数形式：ourselves、yourselves或themselves。

senses.en: to cover a wide area

ex.en: The valley spread out beneath us.
ex.zh: 开阔的山谷出现在我们脚下。

ex.en: We looked down at the city spread out below us.
ex.zh: 我们鸟瞰着下面宽广的城市。

senses.en: This verb is often used in descriptions of cities, views, etc.
senses.zh: 这个动词常用于形容城市、景色等。

senses.en: to pay for sth for other people

ex.en: I’ll spring for lunch.
ex.zh: 午饭我来买单。

senses.en: ) to be caused by sth;to start from sth
senses.zh: 由某事物造成；起源于﹙或来自﹚某事物:

ex.en: The idea for the novel sprang from a trip to India.
ex.zh: 这部小说的灵感来自一次印度旅行。

ex.en: Aggression often springs from fear.
ex.zh: 侵略行为常常是由恐惧引起的。

senses.zh: (通常用于疑问句) to appear suddenly or unexpectedly from somewhere突如其来地从﹙某处﹚出现:

ex.en: Where on earth did you spring from?
ex.zh: 你究竟是从哪儿冒出来的？

senses.en: to suddenly do, say or suggest sth that people do not expect
senses.zh: 突如其来地做﹙或说、提起﹚某人意想不到的事:

ex.en: I hate to spring this on you at such short notice.
ex.zh: 我不想如此突然地让你知道这件事。

ex.en: They were planning to spring a surprise on us.
ex.zh: 他们计划着给我们来个惊喜。

senses.en: to appear, develop, grow, etc. quickly or suddenly
senses.zh: 迅速出现﹙或发展、生长等﹚；突然兴起:

ex.en: Weeds were springing up everywhere.
ex.zh: 到处杂草丛生。

ex.en: Several new cafés sprang up in the area.
ex.zh: 这个地区突然冒出了几家新的小餐馆。

senses.en: to make sb/sth/yourself tidy and clean

ex.en: We spruced up the room with a coat of paint.
ex.zh: 我们把房间刷了一层涂料，令其整洁一新。

ex.en: He spruced himself up for the interview.
ex.zh: 他为参加面试打扮了一番。

senses.en: to encourage sb to act in a particular way, especially to work harder or to try to achieve sth

ex.en: Her difficult childhood spurred her on to succeed.
ex.zh: 她艰难的童年激励着她去争取成功。

ex.en: His parents’ encouragement spurred him on to greater efforts.
ex.zh: 父母的鼓励促使他更加努力。

senses.en: to come out of sth in a sudden or fast stream; to pour out a sudden fast stream of liquid or flames﹙
senses.zh: 从…中﹚ 喷出，冒出，涌出﹙…﹚:

ex.en: Water spurted out of the hole.
ex.zh: 水从小孔中喷出来。

ex.en: The volcano was spurting out rivers of molten lava.
ex.zh: 火山喷涌着熔岩。

senses.en: to watch sb/sth secretly
senses.zh: 暗中监视，窥探﹙某人或事﹚:

ex.en: He hired a detective to spy on his wife.
ex.zh: 他雇了侦探暗中监视他的妻子。

senses.en: to go somewhere secretly to try to find out information﹙
senses.zh: 去某处﹚暗中查明，秘密了解清楚﹙某事﹚:

ex.en: I arrived early to spy out the land (= collect information before deciding what to do).
ex.zh: 我很早便到了，以便摸清情况。

ex.en: He studied the map and spied out the quickest route.
ex.zh: 他研究了一下地图，发现了一条最快捷的路径。

senses.en: to finish dealing with sth; to put sth in order

ex.en: We need to get everything squared away before you leave.
ex.zh: 我们在你走之前得把一切整理好。

senses.en: to fight or to prepare to fight sb﹙
senses.zh: 和某人﹚打斗；摆好架势﹙和某人﹚打斗:

ex.en: The two candidates will square off in a TV debate tomorrow.
ex.zh: 两名候选人将在明天的电视辩论中交锋。

ex.en: Protesting students squared off against police.
ex.zh: 抗议的学生和警察发生了冲突。

senses.en: to agree with another fact, idea or situation; to make two facts, ideas or situations agree with each other﹙

ex.en: This doesn’t square with what you told us earlier.
ex.zh: 这与你先前告诉我们的有出入。

ex.en: How do you square your profession with your religious beliefs?
ex.zh: 你怎样使你从事的职业和你的宗教信仰协调一致呢？

senses.en: to get sb’s approval before you do sth
senses.zh: 就……徵得某人同意﹙或认可﹚:

ex.en: You’d better square it with the boss if you want to leave early.
ex.zh: 你要是想提前下班， 最好徵得老板的同意。

senses.en: to press people or things tightly together in a small space

ex.en: people living squashed together in terrible conditions
ex.zh: 拥挤地生活在恶劣环境中的人

senses.en: to achieve a successful result with great difficulty
senses.zh: 费力﹙ 或勉强﹚ 取得成功:

ex.en: We just squeaked by in the semi-final.
ex.zh: 我们好不容易在半决赛中取胜。

senses.en: to manage to achieve sth or get a successful result with great difficulty﹙

ex.en: Andrew squeaked through the qualifying rounds of the championship.
ex.zh: 安德鲁勉强通过了锦标赛的资格赛。

senses.en: to just manage to fit into a small space

ex.en: The bus was so full not one more passenger could have squeezed in.
ex.zh: 公共汽车上拥挤得连一个乘客也再塞不下了。

senses.en: to just manage to fit sb/sth into a short period of time
senses.zh: 挤出时间见某人﹙或做某事﹚:

ex.en: The doctor can squeeze you in on Tuesday morning.
ex.zh: 大夫星期二上午可以挤出时间看你。

ex.en: All my classes are squeezed into four days a week.
ex.zh: 我每周上四天课，挤得满满的。

senses.en: to prevent sb/sth from doing sth or from doing business

ex.en: Small firms are being squeezed out by larger companies.
ex.zh: 小公司逐渐被较大的公司挤垮。

ex.en: One candidate has already been squeezed out of the leadership race.
ex.zh: 一名候选人已从领导人竞选中被淘汰。

senses.en: to move closer towards sb so that you are pressed tightly together﹙

ex.en: There’ll be enough room if we all squeeze up a bit.
ex.zh: 大家稍稍挤一挤，地方就够了。

ex.en: I’ll walk — it’s better than being squeezed up in the back of the car.
ex.zh: 我要步行——这总比挤在车的后座上要好。

senses.en: to put sth, especially money,in a safe place so that you can use it later

ex.en: She had money squirrelled away in various bank accounts.
ex.zh: 她把钱存在几个不同的银行账户上。

senses.en: to increase gradually until there is a large pile, a long line, etc.
senses.zh: 积聚成一大堆﹙或一长排等﹚:

ex.en: Over the months he just let the paperwork stack up.
ex.zh: 几个月过去了，他就那么让文案工作积压成堆。

ex.en: The traffic quickly stacked up behind the bus.
ex.zh: 公共汽车后面的车辆很快排成了长龙。

senses.en: to risk money or sth very important on the result of sth or on sth happening﹙
senses.zh: 就某事﹚拿钱﹙或十分重要的东西﹚ 冒险； 以…打赌:

ex.en: He staked twenty pounds on the favourite (= in horse racing,for example).
ex.zh: 他在那匹众人看好的马上押了二十英镑。

ex.en: Several journalists staked their reputation on Bush winning the election.
ex.zh: 有几个记者拿名誉担保布什能赢得选举。

senses.en: to mark the position and the limits of a piece of land or an area to show that you own it
senses.zh: 界定属于自己的地区；划出自己的势力范围；圈地:

ex.en: The male stakes out his territory and defends it from other birds.
ex.zh: 雄鸟清楚标出自己的地盘，保护它不受别的鸟侵犯。

senses.en: to state your position or opinion on sth clearly

ex.en: The President staked out his position on the issue.
ex.zh: 总统明确阐述了他在这个问题上的立场。

senses.en: a situation when police watch a building continuously and secretly because they think sth illegal is happening there

ex.en: The stake-out at the house produced nothing.
ex.zh: 监视这所房子没有什么收获。

senses.en: to bring your foot down on sth with force

ex.en: The child stamped on the spider.
ex.zh: 小孩使劲踩那只蜘蛛。

ex.en: She stamped on his foot as hard as she could.
ex.zh: 她使出全身力气踩他的脚。

senses.en: ) to control sth or stop sth from happening by force

ex.en: This kind of disobedience must be stamped on at once.
ex.zh: 必须立刻镇压此类违抗行为。

senses.en: to destroy or get rid of sth bad or unpleasant by force or with a lot of effort﹙
senses.zh: 通过武力或不懈努力﹚消除，消灭，镇压:

ex.en: They aim to stamp out drug dealing in schools.
ex.zh: 他们旨在消灭校园里的毒品交易。

ex.en: The party chairman is determined to stamp out corruption.
ex.zh: 党主席决心杜绝腐败现象。

senses.en: to stand in a place doing nothing, either waiting for sb/sth or with no particular purpose﹙
senses.zh: 在某人旁或在某处﹚ 闲站着， 站着等:

ex.en: Don’t just stand around watching me, give me a hand.
ex.zh: 别光站着看，帮帮我嘛。

ex.en: There were a few people standing around the square.
ex.zh: 广场四周站了几个人。

senses.en: to move to one side to let sb/sth pass

ex.en: Stand aside please and let her through.
ex.zh: 请站到一边让她过去。

senses.en: to take no part in events; to do nothing

ex.en: I can’t stand aside and let you waste an opportunity like that.
ex.zh: 我不能不管不问，让你把机会那样浪费掉。

senses.en: to stop doing a job so that sb else can do it
senses.zh: 退居一旁；让位于他人；靠边:

ex.en: It’s time he stood aside and let somebody younger take his place.
ex.zh: 现在他该退出职位，让给较年轻的人了。

senses.en: to move a short distance away from sb/sth
to be situated at a distance from sth

ex.en: The house stands back from the road.
ex.zh: 房子离公路有一段距离。

senses.en: to think about a situation as if you are not involved in it

ex.en: She found it hard to stand back from the situation.
ex.zh: 她觉得很难把自己当成局外人。

ex.en: This is an opportunity to stand back and think about what you have achieved.
ex.zh: 这是一个客观思考自己成绩的机会。

senses.en: to prevent sb from doing or having sth, or being in a particular situation

ex.en: Only three people stood between him and the crown (= becoming king).
ex.zh: 在他与王位之间只有三个人。

ex.en: Your lack of confidence is all that stands between you and a much better job.
ex.zh: 缺乏自信是你得到更好工作的唯一阻碍。

senses.en: to be present when sth bad or unpleasant is happening, but not become involved
(for sth) to be ready to take appropriate action
senses.zh: 做好随时行动的准备； 候命:

ex.en: The pilot was instructed to stand by for take-off.
ex.zh: 飞行员接到指示，做好随时起飞的准备。

ex.en: Fire crews are standing by in case of an explosion.
ex.zh: 消防队严阵以待，若有爆炸立刻出动。

senses.en: a person who is present but is not involved in sth

ex.en: Two innocent bystanders were hit by stray bullets.
ex.zh: 两名无辜的旁观者被流弹击中。

senses.en: [C] a person or a thing that can be used if sb/sth else is not available
senses.zh: 后备﹙或候补﹚人员；备用品:

ex.en: Keep some candles as a standby in case the power fails.
ex.zh: 预备一些蜡烛以防断电。

ex.en: Mia made a delicious meal from standbys in the store cupboard.
ex.zh: 米娅用储藏柜里的备用食物做了一顿可口的饭。

senses.en: [U] a state of being ready to act if necessary
[only before noun]
that can be used if other things are not available

ex.en: standby supplies
ex.zh: 备用物资

ex.en: Two divers work together while a standby diver remains on the surface.
ex.zh: 两名潜水员协同工作，同时有一名候补潜水员留在水面上。

senses.en: (in a court of law
senses.zh: 法庭) to leave the place where you stand to give evidence离开证人席:

ex.en: The witness was allowed to stand down.
ex.zh: 证人获准离开证人席。

senses.zh: 不用于进行时) to be an abbreviation of sth﹙指缩写﹚是…意思，代表:

ex.en: What does DVD stand for?
ex.zh: DVD代表什么？

senses.en: to support sth; to be in favour of sth

ex.en: Our party stands for racial harmony.
ex.zh: 我们的党主张种族和谐。

ex.en: I hated him and all he stood for.
ex.zh: 我讨厌他，也讨厌他的一切主张。

senses.zh: 用于否定句和疑问句) to allow sth to happen or sb to do sth容忍；忍受:

ex.en: I won’t stand for this behaviour.
ex.zh: 我无法容忍这种行为。

senses.en: to take sb’s place

ex.en: We’ll need someone to stand in for you while you’re away.
ex.zh: 你不在期间，我们需要有个人代替你。

senses.en: a person who does sb’s job for a short time while they are away or not available﹙
senses.zh: 暂时担任某种职务的﹚代理:

ex.en: Tom acted as my stand-in while I was abroad.
ex.zh: 我出国期间由汤姆代职。

ex.en: a stand-in captain/goalkeeper (= for example, in a football game)
ex.zh: 代理船长；临时守门员

senses.en: a person who replaces an actor in some scenes in a film/movie, especially dangerous ones﹙
senses.zh: 尤指影视中危险动作的﹚ 替身演员:

ex.en: rehearsing with stand-ins
ex.zh: 和替身一起排练

senses.en: (against/from sth) to be clearly visible

ex.en: His yellow jacket stood out clearly against the grey hillside.
ex.zh: 灰色的山坡把他黄色的上衣衬托得十分鲜明。

ex.en: The church tower stands out against the sky.
ex.zh: 教堂的尖塔在天空映衬下格外突出。

senses.en: (as/from sb/sth) to be much better or more important than other people or things

ex.en: This building stands out from the rest because of its superior design.
ex.zh: 这座建筑物由于设计优良而鹤立鸡群。

senses.en: to be very noticeable in an unpleasant way

ex.en: Dressed like that, you’ll stand out like a sore thumb.
ex.zh: 你穿戴成那样会很扎眼。

senses.en: excellent

ex.en: an outstanding young actress
ex.zh: 杰出的年轻女演员

senses.en: [usually before noun] very obvious or important

ex.en: Lake Baykal is one of earth’s outstanding features.
ex.zh: 贝加尔湖是世界上最引人注目的景色之一。

senses.en: (of payment,work, problems, etc.
senses.zh: 款项、工作、困难等) not yet paid, done, solved, etc.未支付的；未完成的；未解决的:

ex.en: to repay outstanding debts
ex.zh: 清偿欠债

ex.en: I don’t have any urgent work outstanding.
ex.zh: 我没有什么未做完的紧要工作。

senses.en: used to emphasize the good quality of sth

ex.en: outstandingly beautiful/successful
ex.zh: 特别美丽/成功

senses.en: extremely well

ex.en: Owen has played outstandingly this season.
ex.zh: 欧文在这个赛季表现极佳。

senses.en: to remain close to sb and watch them, usually to make sure that they behave or do sth correctly

ex.en: She won’t do her homework unless I stand over her.
ex.zh: 除非我看着她，否则她不肯做作业。

ex.en: I can’t concentrate with you standing over me.
ex.zh: 你盯着我，我无法集中精神。

senses.en: to rise to your feet from a sitting or lying position; to be on your feet

ex.en: Darcy stood up when Emma came into the room.
ex.zh: 埃玛一进房间，达西就站起来。

ex.en: There was silence when the President stood up to speak.
ex.zh: 总统起身讲话，会场就寂静下来。

senses.en: (to sth) to remain true or correct even when tested, examined closely, etc.

ex.en: Your theory doesn’t stand up to close examination.
ex.zh: 你的理论经不起仔细推敲。

ex.en: His story won’t stand up under crossexamination.
ex.zh: 他的陈述经不起严密诘问。

senses.en: [only before noun]
to support or defend sb/sth/yourself, especially when sb is criticizing them/it/you
senses.zh: 支持，维护﹙某人、某事、自己﹚:

ex.en: She’s always stood up for her friends.
ex.zh: 她常常为朋友辩解。

ex.en: You should stand up for what you believe in.
ex.zh: 你应该维护自己的信念。

senses.en: to resist sb/sth; to defend your position against a more powerful person or organization that is treating you badly or unfairly
senses.zh: 抵抗；勇敢维护；反抗某人的欺负﹙或不公平对待﹚:

ex.en: If you don’t stand up to him he’ll treat you like dirt.
ex.zh: 你如果俯首帖耳，他就根本不会尊重你。

ex.en: It was difficult for Paul to stand up to his father’s rage.
ex.zh: 保罗很难不屈服于他父亲的暴怒。

senses.en: (of a product, material, etc.
senses.zh: 产品、材料等) to be able to stay in good condition even though it is treated roughly能承受；经受得住；耐用:

ex.en: Will your china and glass stand up to family wear and tear?
ex.zh: 你的瓷器和玻璃器皿在家里耐用吗？

senses.en: to begin to return somewhere

ex.en: It’s time we started back.
ex.zh: 我们该回去了。

senses.en: to leave one place to go to another

ex.en: We started for home.
ex.zh: 我们动身回家去了。

senses.en: to begin to do sth

ex.en: Let’s start in now and get the job done quickly.
ex.zh: 咱们现在就动手快点把活干完吧。

ex.en: It’s time you started in on your homework.
ex.zh: 你该做家庭作业了。

senses.en: to attack sb physically or with words﹙
senses.zh: 使用暴力或言语﹚对……进行攻击:

ex.en: He hit me first and then he started () on my friend.
ex.zh: 他先打了我，然后就打我的朋友。

ex.en: Don’t start on me, I’m tired.
ex.zh: 别跟我找茬了，我累了。

senses.en: to begin to deal with sth; to begin to do sth

ex.en: When she’d finished cleaning the kitchen, she started on the bathroom.
ex.zh: 她把厨房打扫完就动手清洁浴室。

senses.en: to begin a journey

ex.en: Check the engine before you start out.
ex.zh: 出发之前检查一下发动机。

ex.en: What time did they start out?
ex.zh: 他们什么时间动身的？

senses.en: to begin doing sth again, especially because you were not successful the first time
senses.zh: 重新开始；从头开始再做:

ex.en: I messed up and had to start over.
ex.zh: 我弄得一团糟，不得不返工。

ex.en: She spelled my name wrong and had to start over.
ex.zh: 她把我的名字拼错了， 只好再来一次。

senses.en: to begin happening

ex.en: After a moment’s silence, the music started up again.
ex.zh: 片刻沉寂过后，又扬起了音乐声。

senses.en: to start operating; to make sth start operating﹙

ex.en: The engine started up with a roar.
ex.zh: 引擎轰隆隆地发动起来。

ex.en: It took me a while to start up the generator.
ex.zh: 我费了点时间启动发电机。

senses.en: (in sth) to start operating or trading; to establish a business

ex.en: When I started up in business, I needed a lot of help.
ex.zh: 我创业时需要很多帮助。

ex.en: There are a lot of small businesses starting up in the area.
ex.zh: 区内小企业涌现。

senses.en: connected with beginning a new business
senses.zh: 创业有关的； 创办阶段的:

ex.en: the new company’s start-up costs
ex.zh: 这家公司的开业成本

senses.en: a company that is just beginning to operate, especially an Internet company
senses.zh: 新成立的公司；新网络商:

ex.en: This is just one of the problems facing start-ups in this highly competitive area.
ex.zh: 这只是新互联网公司在这个竞争激烈的领域中所面临的问题之一。

senses.en: to feel you do not have something that you really need; to prevent sb/sth from having sth necessary or very important

ex.en: Sam was starving for a kind word from Clare.
ex.zh: 萨姆渴望听到克莱尔的一句好话。

ex.en: The children were starved for affection.
ex.zh: 这些孩子严重缺乏爱。

senses.en: to force sb to do sth or accept sth by preventing them from getting food or money
senses.zh: 断绝食物﹙或资金﹚来源以迫使某人做某事:

senses.en: to prevent sb/sth from having sth that they want or need

ex.en: The project is being starved of funds.
ex.zh: 这个项目正苦于缺少资金。

ex.en: The baby had been starved of oxygen at birth.
ex.zh: 这个婴儿出生时缺氧。

senses.en: to force sb to leave a place by not allowing them to get food
senses.zh: 以断绝食物来源迫使某人出来:

ex.en: It took a month to starve them out.
ex.zh: 给他们断绝食物一个月才把他们迫了出来。

ex.en: A few rebels remain in the area. The rest have been starved out.
ex.zh: 少数反叛者还留在那个地区，其余的都饿得跑出来了。

senses.en: to store sth in a secret or safe place

ex.en: She has a fortune stashed away in various bank accounts.
ex.zh: 她在不同的银行账户上秘密储存了一大笔钱。

senses.en: to break sth by hitting it with force and making part of it fall inwards

ex.en: The side of the boat was staved in when it hit the rocks.
ex.zh: 船触礁把船舷撞扁了。

senses.en: to prevent sth unpleasant from happening for a period of time; to delay sth unpleasant
senses.zh: 暂时挡住，避开﹙某事﹚；延缓，推迟﹙令人不快的事物﹚:

ex.en: to stave off hunger/illness
ex.zh: 暂时解飢/缓解病情

ex.en: desperate attempts to stave off civil war
ex.zh: 孤注一掷地避免内战的努力

senses.en: to succeedin remaining further forward in space,time, development, success, etc.

ex.en: We need to keep an eye on our competitors if we want to stay ahead.
ex.zh: 我们要保持领先地位，就得对竞争对手时刻留神。

ex.en: He stayed ahead of me throughout the race.
ex.zh: 整个赛跑中他一直冲在我前面。

senses.en: to not leave somewhere

ex.en: I’ll stay around in case you need me.
ex.zh: 我就待在这儿， 也许你用得着我。

ex.en: I don’t know if he’ll be angry with us or not, but I’m not staying around to find out!
ex.zh: 我不知道他会不会生我们的气，不过我不会傻等着弄清楚的！

senses.en: to not go near sb/sthdangerous or unpleasant; to have nothing to dowith sb/sth
senses.zh: 离开，不接近﹙危险或讨厌的人或事物﹚；不去﹙某处﹚；不沾染﹙某物﹚:

ex.en: Stay away from the edge!
ex.zh: 不要靠近边缘！

ex.en: He advised us to stay away from drugs.
ex.zh: 他告诫我们远离毒品。

senses.en: to remain in a place and not move forward
senses.zh: 待在原地﹙ 不向前移动﹚ :

ex.en: The police shouted to the crowd to stay back.
ex.zh: 警方向群众喊叫，要他们待在原地。

senses.en: to remain in a place atthe end of an event after other people have left﹙

ex.en: I had to stay behind after class.
ex.zh: 课后我要留下来。

ex.en: She stayed behind after the meeting for a chat.
ex.zh: 会议结束之后，她留下来闲谈。

senses.en: to remain in a low position

ex.en: The blind won’t stay down.
ex.zh: 窗帘总不向下垂。

ex.en: Get down and stay down or he’ll see you!
ex.zh: 趴下别起来，不然他就看见你了！

senses.en: to remain in a position inside sth

ex.en: This nail won’t stay in.
ex.zh: 这颗钉子就是钉不牢。

senses.en: to remain at home or inside a building

ex.en: I was ill and had to stay in all week.
ex.zh: 我生病了，只好在家里休息了整整一周。

ex.en: Let’s stay in this evening.
ex.zh: 咱们今晚待在家里吧。

senses.en: to keep away; to not return

ex.en: If the rain stays off, we’ll go out for a walk.
ex.zh: 雨要是不再下了，我们就出去散散步。

ex.en: She’s always dieting, but she can never get the weight to stay off.
ex.zh: 她总是在节食，然而体重老反弹。

senses.en: to not go to work,school, etc., especially because you are ill/sick﹙

ex.en: He injured his back and stayed off for a week.
ex.zh: 他背部受伤，一个星期没上班。

ex.en: Can I stay off school today?
ex.zh: 我今天可以不上学吗？

senses.en: to remain in position on top of sth﹙

ex.en: The lid won’t stay on.
ex.zh: 这个盖子就是盖不上。

senses.en: to not leave a job, school, place,etc. when you are expected to, or when otherpeople do
senses.zh: 留下来继续﹙学习、工作等﹚:

ex.en: We hope he will stay on as manager at the end of his contract.
ex.zh: 我们希望他合同期满之后能留下来继续当经理。

ex.en: We couldn’t persuade Jane to stay on at school for an extra year.
ex.zh: 我们无法说服简留在学校继续学习一年。

senses.en: to continue operating

ex.en: The light stays on until dawn.
ex.zh: 灯一直亮到拂晓。

senses.en: to remain out of the house or outdoors,especially at night﹙
senses.zh: 尤指晚上﹚待在户外，不在家:

ex.en: Sam was allowed to stay out until 11.30 on a Saturday.
ex.zh: 有个星期六萨姆获准在外待到11 :30。

ex.en: I don’t like you staying out so late. Try to come home earlier next time.
ex.zh: 我不喜欢你在外面待到这么晚。下次要早一点回家。

senses.en: toremain on strike

ex.en: The miners stayed out for fifteen months.
ex.zh: 矿工连续罢工十五个月。

senses.en: to remain outside a place

ex.en: Stay out, the floor’s wet.
ex.zh: 在外面待着，地板湿着呢。

ex.en: Stay out of the kitchen, I’m busy.
ex.zh: 别到厨房来，我忙着呢。

senses.en: to not become involved in sth that does not concern you

ex.en: I try to stay out of their little quarrels.
ex.zh: 他们斗嘴我尽量不掺和。

ex.en: Stay out of this, it’s none of your business.
ex.zh: 别插手，这事与你无关。

senses.en: to avoid sth

ex.en: Try to stay out of trouble!
ex.zh: 尽量别惹麻烦！

senses.en: to sleep at sb’s house for a night

ex.en: It got late, so we stayed over.
ex.zh: 当时已经很晚，我们就留下过夜。

ex.en: Can I stay over at Gareth’s () tonight?
ex.zh: 我今晚可以在加雷思家过夜吗？

senses.en: to not go to bed
to continue to do sth, especially when it is difficult or you do not really want to; to wait until sb has finished sth
senses.zh: 坚持做﹙困难或不想做的事﹚；等某人﹙做完某事﹚ :

ex.en: Several students said they weren’t enjoying the course, but they stayed with it.
ex.zh: 有几个学生说他们不喜欢这个课程，只是硬着头皮继续下去。

ex.en: Stay with me, I’ve nearly finished this list.
ex.zh: 等等我吧，我快要列完这份单子了。

senses.en: to go away from a place quietly and secretly

ex.en: He stole away under cover of darkness.
ex.zh: 他在夜幕的掩护下熘掉了。

senses.en: to approach sb silently so that they do not see or hear you coming

ex.en: She stole up on him in the dark.
ex.zh: 她在黑暗中悄悄地靠近他。

senses.en: to remove a piece of paper from another piece using steam to soften the glue that is holding them together

ex.en: He steamed the stamp off the envelope.
ex.zh: 他用蒸汽嘘了嘘，使邮票脱离了信封。

senses.en: to become, or to make sth become, covered with steam﹙

ex.en: The windows had steamed up.
ex.zh: 窗户上蒙了一层雾。

ex.en: The warmth in the room steamed all the windows up.
ex.zh: 房间里的热气使所有的窗户都起了一层雾。

senses.en: to be/become very angry or excited about sth﹙
senses.zh: 对某事变得﹚非常愤怒，非常激动:

ex.en: I realized I had got all steamed up over nothing.
ex.zh: 我意识到我净发了些无名火。

senses.en: to put food in a liquid and leave it for some time so that it becomes soft and flavoured by the liquid

ex.en: Raspberries are delicious steeped in brandy.
ex.zh: 悬鈎子用白兰地浸泡味道很好。

senses.en: to spend a lot of time doing sth or thinking about sth and learn a lot about it

ex.en: teenagers steeping themselves in pop culture
ex.zh: 沉迷于通俗文化的青少年

ex.en: He was steeped in the family business from an early age.
ex.zh: 他从早年起就潜心经营家族企业。

senses.en: [NOTE]This phrasal verb is mainly used in written English.
senses.zh: 这个短语动词主要用于书面语。

senses.en: to have a lot of a particular quality

ex.en: a city steeped in history and tradition
ex.zh: 有着悠久历史和丰富传统的一个城市

senses.en: to avoid discussing sth or becoming involved with sb/sth, because it may cause problems
senses.zh: 避免谈论某事；把话题引开；避开某人﹙或某物﹚:

ex.en: I tried to steer away from the subject of divorce.
ex.zh: 我设法避开离婚这个话题。

ex.en: Jane tends to steer away from sugary foods.
ex.zh: 简一般不吃甜食。

senses.zh: (不用于进行时) to be caused by sth; to be the result of sth起源于；根源是；是……的结果:

ex.en: Many of her problems stem from the fact that her parents are famous.
ex.zh: 她的很多问题根源于她的父母是名人这一现实。

ex.en: Their opposition stems from fear and ignorance.
ex.zh: 他们反对是出于惧怕和无知。

senses.en: to leave an important job or position in order to let sb else take your place

ex.en: After 10 years as party leader, it’s time for him to step aside.
ex.zh: 他当了10 年的党领导，现在该让贤了。

ex.en: He decided to step aside as company director to make way for his son.
ex.zh: 他决定把公司董事的位置让给儿子。

senses.en: (from sth) to try to think calmly about a situation in which you have been closely involved, as if you are not involved in it
senses.zh: 跳出﹙某事物的﹚圈子看问题；旁观:

ex.en: You should try to step back from the problem and look for a new way to deal with it.
ex.zh: 你应该试着从旁观者的角度看待这个问题，寻找新的处理方法。

senses.en: to offer to help sb, give information,money, etc.
senses.zh: 主动站出来﹙帮忙、提供信息、出钱等﹚:

ex.en: A soft drinks company has stepped forward to sponsor the team.
ex.zh: 一家软饮料公司提出赞助这个队。

senses.en: to help in an argument or a difficult situation
senses.zh: 援之以手；居间调停；居中斡旋:

ex.en: When my mum was ill, my aunt stepped in to help.
ex.zh: 我妈妈生病时，姨妈前来帮忙。

ex.en: The Youth Club was going to close, but a local bank stepped in with a generous donation.
ex.zh: 青年俱乐部即将关闭时，当地一家银行出来捐了一大笔款。

senses.en: used especially to tell sb to drive faster﹙
senses.zh: 尤用以要求加速驾驶﹚开快些，赶快:

ex.en: Step on it! We’re late already!
ex.zh: 开快点！我们都迟到了！

ex.en: We’ll have to really step on it to be there by noon.
ex.zh: 我们要想中午赶到那里，就真的得加速了。

senses.en: to leave a place for a short period

ex.en: He’s just stepped out for ten minutes.
ex.zh: 他就出去了十分钟。

senses.en: to come forward

ex.en: He stepped up to receive his award.
ex.zh: 他走上前去领奖。

ex.en: The runners stepped up to the line.
ex.zh: 赛跑运动员走向起跑线。

senses.en: to stay in or near a place, waiting for sth to happen, sb to arrive, etc.

ex.en: Stick around, we need all the help we can get.
ex.zh: 别走开，我们需要任何可能得到的帮助。

ex.en: I’ll stick around here in case Maya arrives.
ex.zh: 我就待在这儿，说不定马娅会来呢。

senses.en: to work continuously at sth in a determined way

ex.en: If we stick at it, we should finish the job today.
ex.zh: 我们只要不停地干，今天应该能把活干完。

ex.en: She never sticks at anything for very long.
ex.zh: 她做任何事都缺乏恒心。

senses.en: to return sth to its usual place; to return sth to the place it was before

ex.en: Stick the cake back in the oven for ten minutes.
ex.zh: 把蛋糕放回烤箱里烤十分钟。

ex.en: When you’ve finished with the dictionary, just stick it back on the shelf.
ex.zh: 你用完词典就把它放回书架上。

senses.en: to be loyal to sb and continue to support them in difficult times

ex.en: She stuck by him through thick and thin.
ex.zh: 在任何情况下她都对他忠贞不渝。

senses.en: to fix a piece of paper, etc. to sth else using glue﹙

ex.en: I can’t stick the corners of this wallpaper down.
ex.zh: 我没法粘住墙纸的角。

ex.en: The envelope hadn’t been stuck down properly.
ex.zh: 信封没粘好。

senses.en: () to place sth that you are holding onto the floor or another surface

ex.en: Stick your coat on the chair and come and sit down here.
ex.zh: 把你的外套放在椅子上，过来坐这儿吧。

senses.en: )to put sth into sth

ex.en: I stuck the letter in my pocket to read later.
ex.zh: 我把信塞进衣兜，等以后再看。

ex.en: He saw the hole and stuck his finger in.
ex.zh: 他看见那个小孔就把手指伸了进去。

senses.en: to put sth sharp into sth, making a small hole

ex.en: Ouch! I’ve stuck the needle in my finger!
ex.zh: 哎哟！我的手指被针扎了！

senses.en: to start doing sth in an enthusiastic way; to become very interested and involved in sth
senses.zh: 热情地开始﹙做某事﹚；热切地参与﹙某事﹚:

ex.en: You must be hungry. Get stuck in! (= start eating)
ex.zh: 你一定饿了。快吃吧！

ex.en: I was too tired to get really stuck into the debate.
ex.zh: 我疲乏得没法真正投入这场争辩。

senses.en: to switch on a piece of electrical equipment
senses.zh: 打开﹙ 电器﹚ 开关:

ex.en: I’ll stick the kettle on for a cup of tea.
ex.zh: 我来烧壶水，沏杯茶。

senses.en: to put on clothes

ex.en: I’ll just stick a jacket on, and I’m ready.
ex.zh: 我套件上衣就行了。

senses.en: to begin to cook food

ex.en: I’ll stick the potatoes on and then I’ll make us a coffee.
ex.zh: 我来把土豆做上，然后给咱们弄杯咖啡。

senses.en: to attach sth firmly to a surface, using glue, tape,etc.

ex.en: I stuck the label on with adhesive tape.
ex.zh: 我用黏胶带贴上标籤。

ex.en: He sealed the envelope, and stuck a stamp on it.
ex.zh: 他封上信封，在上面贴了一枚邮票。

senses.en: [only before noun] a stick-on object has glue on one side so that it can be attached to sth
senses.zh: 可粘贴的；一面带黏胶的:

ex.en: stickon badges/labels
ex.zh: 带黏胶的标记/标籤

senses.en: to be very different from others, especially in an unpleasant way

ex.en: The red house stuck out like a sore thumb among the old stone cottages.
ex.zh: 那所红房子在陈旧的小石屋中间很扎眼。

senses.en: to be further out than sth else; to be partly outside sth such as a container
senses.zh: 突出；﹙从容器等中﹚伸出，探出:

ex.en: His ears stick out.
ex.zh: 他长着一对招风耳。

ex.en: There was a newspaper sticking out of her coat pocket.
ex.zh: 她外衣兜里露出了一截报纸。

senses.en: to do or say sth when there is a risk you may be wrong
senses.zh: 做有风险的事；冒险说没有把握的话:

ex.en: I’m going to stick my neck out and say that we’ll have a dry summer.
ex.zh: 我不一定对，但我还是要说这个夏天会乾旱的。

senses.en: to continue doing sth difficult or boring until it is finished

ex.en: I don’t like being on my own, but I’ll stick it out until my parents come back.
ex.zh: 我不喜欢独自在家，但我会坚持等到父母回来的。

ex.en: I’m amazed that she’s stuck the course out.
ex.zh: 我觉得很意外，她居然耐着性子把课学完了。

senses.en: to refuse to give up until you get what you want
senses.zh: 坚持要求；得不到……不罢休:

ex.en: They’re sticking out for a higher pay rise.
ex.zh: 他们坚持要求更大幅度地提高工资。

senses.en: to continue doing sth even if it is difficult or you have problems

ex.en: He found it difficult to stick to a diet.
ex.zh: 要经常按规定饮食，他觉得很困难。

senses.en: to continue doing or using sth and not want to change it
senses.zh: 坚持； 维持；固守；坚持保留:

ex.en: I’m sticking to my previous statement.
ex.zh: 我坚持我先前所说的话。

ex.en: That’s her story and she’s sticking to it.
ex.zh: 那是她本人的叙述，并且她坚持那么说。

senses.en: to keep inside the limits of a particular subject,etc.

ex.en: I’m not interested in your opinions — just stick to the facts.
ex.zh: 我对你的看法不感兴趣——只讲事实就行了。

senses.en: to remain friendly and loyal to one another; to support each other
senses.zh: 彼此友好忠诚；团结在一起:

ex.en: The family should stick together at a time like this.
ex.zh: 在这样的时期，全家人应该团结一致。

ex.en: The children from the village tended to stick together.
ex.zh: 这个村的孩子喜欢抱团。

senses.en: ) to stay physically close to each other

ex.en: Let’s all stick together until we find the way out.
ex.zh: 找到出路之前我们大家不要分开。

senses.en: to point upwards; to be upright

ex.en: The branch was sticking up out of the water.
ex.zh: 树枝从水下伸了出来。

ex.en: Is my hair sticking up?
ex.zh: 我的头发翘起来了吗？

senses.en: an act of robbing sb/sth using a gun

ex.en: This is a stick-up, nobody move!
ex.zh: 抢劫，都不许动！

senses.en: to place sth in a high position; to move sth upwards,especially inside sth
senses.zh: 举起；擎起；使﹙在某物内部﹚向上移动:

ex.en: Stick your hand up if you know the answer.
ex.zh: 知道答案就举手。

ex.en: Jeff stuck his hand up the pipe to see what was blocking it.
ex.zh: 杰夫用手顺着管子往上摸，看有什么堵塞了。

senses.en: to support or defend sb, yourself or sth, when they are being criticized
senses.zh: 支持，维护，捍宪﹙某人、自己、某事物﹚ :

ex.en: She always sticks up for her little sister.
ex.zh: 她总是护着她的妹妹。

ex.en: You must stick up for what you believe in.
ex.zh: 你一定要捍宪你的信念。

senses.en: ) to stay physically close to sb

ex.en: Stick with me until we get out of the forest.
ex.zh: 走出森林之前跟紧我。

senses.en: ) to remain in sb’s memory

ex.en: His words will stick with me forever.
ex.zh: 他的话会永远铭刻在我的记忆里。

senses.en: to continue doing or using sth and not want to change it
senses.zh: 持续不变地做﹙或使用﹚；坚持；维持:

ex.en: I’ve decided to stick with my usual method.
ex.zh: 我决定沿用我惯用的方法。

senses.en: to be forced to do sth, take care of sb/sth, etc. that you do not want to
senses.zh: 被迫做某事﹙或照料某人、某事等﹚；摆脱不了:

ex.en: How did I get stuck with all the cleaning?
ex.zh: 怎么非得让我来打扫这一切呢？

ex.en: If we’re stuck with each other for the next two weeks, we might as well be polite.
ex.zh: 如果我们今后两个星期必须一起共事，我们还是客气点比较好。

senses.en: to trick or cheat sb into paying more money than they should or than they expected to﹙
senses.zh: 抬高价﹚骗某人的钱；敲某人的竹杠:

ex.en: Motorists are being stung for another ￡25 road tax.
ex.zh: 开车的人又遭索取25英镑的公路税。

senses.en: ) to borrow money from sb,especially when they are unwilling to give it to you﹙
senses.zh: 尤指强人所难﹚向某人借钱:

ex.en: Can I sting you for a fiver (= five pounds)?
ex.zh: 能借给我五英镑吗？

senses.en: to mix one substance into another by moving a spoon or sth similar in circles

ex.en: Stir in the cream.
ex.zh: 把奶油调和进去。

ex.en: Stir the pasta into the sauce.
ex.zh: 把麵条加到调味汁里调拌。

senses.en: to encourage sb to do sth; to make sb feel they must do sth

ex.en: He was accused of stirring up the slaves against their masters.
ex.zh: 有人指责他鼓动奴隶反抗主人。

senses.en: to cause trouble, especially by making people feel strong emotions
senses.zh: 煽风点火；煽动别人；挑起事端:

ex.en: I don’t want to stir up any more trouble.
ex.zh: 我不想再挑起更多麻烦了。

ex.en: The government has been accused of stirring up racial hatred.
ex.zh: 有人谴责政府煽动种族仇恨。

senses.en: to make sb have a particular feeling or attitude

ex.en: Her story stirred up a lot of old memories for me.
ex.zh: 她的故事唤起了我对过去的很多回忆。

ex.en: I can’t seem to stir up any interest in the campaign.
ex.zh: 我似乎对这个运动唤不起任何兴趣。

senses.en: to make sb appear to be guilty of sth they have not done, for example by giving false information; to cheat sb
senses.zh: 诬陷某人； 欺骗某人:

ex.en: I didn’t do it! I’ve been stitched up!
ex.zh: 我没干那事！有人诬陷我！

senses.en: to buy or get a lot of sth so that you can use it later

ex.en: The shops are very busy with people stocking up for the holidays.
ex.zh: 商店里到处是忙于为节日大采购的人们。

ex.en: I need to stock up on food before all the family arrive.
ex.zh: 我得赶在全家人到来之前备足食物。

senses.en: to eat a lot of sth so that you will not feel hungry later

ex.en: We’d better stoke up now — we’ve got a long journey in front of us.
ex.zh: 我们现在最好吃得饱饱的——前面的路还很长呢。

senses.en: to do sth bad or unpleasant in order to gain an advantage for yourself﹙
senses.zh: 为私利﹚不择手段；卑鄙﹙或堕落﹚到做某事:

ex.en: I can’t believe he would stoop to blackmail.
ex.zh: 我没法相信他会下作到勒索的地步。

ex.en: He’s the kind of person who would stoop to making personal attacks on a rival.
ex.zh: 他是那种能卑鄙到对竞争对手进行人身攻击的人。

senses.en: to make a short visit to sb, usually at their home
senses.zh: 去看看﹙某人﹚；去﹙某人家﹚坐坐:

ex.en: I’ll stop around this evening when I finish work.
ex.zh: 我今晚下班后要去拜访一下。

ex.en: Let’s stop around the Smiths’ house for a quick drink.
ex.zh: 咱们去史密斯家坐坐喝点东西吧。

senses.en: to deliberately decide not to go somewhere

ex.en: Many of the people invited to the dinner had stopped away in protest.
ex.zh: 很多受到邀请的人都故意不赴宴以示抗议。

senses.en: to return to somewhere that you have visited earlier
senses.zh: 返回，回到﹙先前去过的地方﹚:

ex.en: I’ll stop back on my way home.
ex.zh: 我回家时会再来一下的。

senses.en: to remain somewhere at the end of an event after other people have left﹙

ex.en: She stopped behind after the meeting to talk to him.
ex.zh: 会后她留下来和他谈话。

senses.en: to make a short visit to sb/somewhere, especially when you are on the way to somewhere else

ex.en: Stop by for a chat on your way home.
ex.zh: 你回家时顺路过来聊聊吧。

ex.en: Could you stop by the store for some milk?
ex.zh: 你能不能顺路进那家店里买点牛奶？

senses.en: to stay at home rather than go out

ex.en: We’ve decided to stop in tonight because it’s raining.
ex.zh: 下雨了，我们打算今晚留在家里。

senses.en: to stop somewhere for a short time when you are on the way to somewhere else

ex.en: We stopped off for lunch just north of Paris.
ex.zh: 我们就在巴黎的北面中途停下来吃了午饭。

ex.en: I stopped off at the supermarket on the way home.
ex.zh: 我回家时去了超市一趟。

senses.en: a short stay somewhere during a trip﹙

ex.en: a stop-off in Sydney
ex.zh: 在悉尼的短暂停留

senses.en: a place where you stop for a short time during a trip﹙
senses.zh: 旅程中的﹚ 中途停留地

senses.en: to stay somewhere longer than you planned or after other people have left

ex.en: I’ll be late home tonight — the boss wants me to stop on an hour after work and help tidy up after the meeting.
ex.zh: 我今晚要晚回家——老板要我加班一小时，会后帮忙收拾一下。

senses.en: to stay out late at night or all night instead of going home
senses.zh: 夜里很晚不回家；夜不归宿:

ex.en: He often stops out till three in the morning.
ex.zh: 他常常在外面呆到凌晨三点。

senses.en: to stop somewhere for a short time when you are on a long journey, especially a journey by plane﹙
senses.zh: 尤指乘飞机、长途旅行在某处﹚中途停留:

ex.en: I stopped over in Mérida on the way to Havana.
ex.zh: 我去哈瓦那途中在梅里达停留了一下。

senses.en: a short stay somewhere during a long journey﹙

ex.en: We had a three-day stopover in Hawaii.
ex.zh: 我们在夏威夷停留了三天。

senses.en: a place where you stay for a short time during a long journey﹙
senses.zh: 长途旅行的﹚中途停留地

senses.en: to not go to bed until later than usual

ex.en: She stopped up to see the football match.
ex.zh: 她熬夜看足球赛。

senses.en: to put sth in a safe place and keep it there so that you can use it later

ex.en: We stored away the baby clothes until we had another child.
ex.zh: 我们把婴儿服装全都收好了，等再生孩子时又用上了。

ex.en: It’s amazing how much knowledge he’s got stored away in his memory.
ex.zh: 他记忆里贮存的知识多得令人吃惊。

senses.en: to not express strong feelings or deal with problems when you have them, often making trouble for yourself in future﹙
senses.zh: 把强烈的感情或问题﹚郁积，憋在心里；当断不断:

ex.en: Smokers may be storing up health problems for their unborn children.
ex.zh: 吸烟的人可能给他们的胎儿留下健康隐患。

ex.en: Children who store up their bad feelings often develop headaches or stomach pains.
ex.zh: 孩子郁积坏心情常常造成头痛或腹痛现象。

senses.en: to keep sth so that it can be used later
