ex.en: animals storing up food for the winter
ex.zh: 贮藏食物准备过冬的动物

ex.en: The batteries store up enough energy for a week.
ex.zh: 电池可存储足够一周用的能量。

senses.en: to leave a place or a person suddenly because you are very angry

ex.en: We had a big argument and he stormed off.
ex.zh: 我们大吵一架，然后他愤怒地冲了出去。

senses.en: to hide on a vehicle, especially a ship or a plane, in order to travel without paying or without being seen
senses.zh: 无票偷乘﹙交通工具，尤指船或飞机﹚:

ex.en: He stowed away on a ship bound for Vigo.
ex.zh: 他偷偷地上了一艘开往维哥的船。

senses.en: a person who hides on a ship or a plane in order to travel without paying or without being seen
senses.zh: 无票偷乘船﹙或飞机﹚的人

senses.en: to become or to make sth straight﹙

ex.en: After the bridge, the road straightens out.
ex.zh: 过了桥之后，路就直了。

ex.en: attempts to straighten out the river
ex.zh: 将河道改直的尝试

senses.en: to help sb deal with problems or understand a difficult situation which may be making them behave badly; to help yourself in this way
senses.zh: 帮人﹙或自行﹚解决问题；﹙使某人﹚重回正轨:

ex.en: A few sessions talking to a counsellor should straighten him out.
ex.zh: 跟辅导员谈几次就会使他改正过来的。

senses.en: to deal with problems or a difficult situation; to organize things that are confused
senses.zh: 解决问题﹙或困难﹚；清理；整顿:

ex.en: I was left to straighten out the mess.
ex.zh: 只留下我来收拾这个烂摊子。

ex.en: He’s trying to straighten out his finances.
ex.zh: 他正试图理清他的财务。

senses.en: to stand up straight from a bent position
senses.zh: 挺直身子； 站立起来:

ex.en: She slowly straightened up and rubbed her back.
ex.zh: 她慢慢站起来揉了揉背。

senses.en: to pull very hard on sth

ex.en: The dog was straining at its lead.
ex.zh: 那狗用力拖拽着牵狗绳。

senses.en: () to want to do sth very much, especially when sb/sth is trying to stop you
senses.zh: 迫不及待，急于摆脱束缚﹙做某事﹚ :

ex.en: He’s straining at the leash to get on with his research.
ex.zh: 他急于摆脱束缚继续搞研究。

senses.en: to separate a liquid from sth solid by pouring it through sth that has very small holes in it

ex.en: Strain off any excess liquid.
ex.zh: 把多余的液体都滤掉。

senses.en: to fasten sb/yourself in a seat, etc. using straps
senses.zh: 给某人﹙或自己﹚系上安全带:

ex.en: All passengers in the plane must be securely strapped in.
ex.zh: 飞机上的所有乘客必须把安全带系牢。

ex.en: Make sure you strap the baby firmly into the high chair.
ex.zh: 孩子坐高脚椅一定要系牢。

senses.en: to attach sth to sth else with straps
senses.zh: 用带子把…捆﹙或系、绑﹚﹙在…上﹚:

ex.en: He strapped on his helmet and rode away.
ex.zh: 他系好头盔就开车走了。

ex.en: She strapped the suitcases onto the roof of the car.
ex.zh: 她把手提箱绑在车顶上。

senses.en: to make sb very anxious and tired so that they are unable to relax
senses.zh: 使某人过度焦虑﹙或劳累﹚；使心力交瘁:

ex.en: My job really stresses me out.
ex.zh: 我的工作实在使我心力交瘁。

ex.en: My Dad stressed me out by criticizing me all the time.
ex.zh: 爸爸没完没了地数落我，都快把我逼疯了。

senses.en: too anxious and tired to be able to relax

ex.en: When I’m stressed out, I try to go for a long walk.
ex.zh: 我压力过大时，就抽出时间往远处散步。

ex.en: stressed-out executives
ex.zh: 心力交瘁的行政人员

senses.en: to spread over a large area of land, especially away from where you are﹙

ex.en: The mountains stretched away into the distance.
ex.zh: 山脉延伸向远方。

ex.en: Banana plantations stretched away as far as the eye could see.
ex.zh: 极目远望，只见一片香蕉种植园。

senses.en: to lie down, with your arms or legs out straight, especially in order to relax or sleep
senses.zh: 舒展四肢躺下﹙尤指为休息或睡觉﹚:

ex.en: He stretched out on the floor and fell asleep.
ex.zh: 他摊开四肢躺在地板上睡了。

senses.en: to put your arm or leg out straight, especially in order to reach sth

ex.en: She stretched out a hand to touch his face.
ex.zh: 她伸手去摸他的脸。

ex.en: He leant back and stretched his legs out in front of him.
ex.zh: 他靠后仰，把腿伸向前面。

senses.en: to be covered with a lot of things

ex.en: The floor was strewn with clothes.
ex.zh: 满地都是衣服。

ex.en: () The way ahead is strewn with difficulties.
ex.zh: 前面的路困难重重。

senses.en: to try to hit sb/sth, especially with a weapon﹙

ex.en: She screamed and struck at the wolf with a stick.
ex.zh: 她尖叫着用棍子朝那只狼打去。

senses.en: to cause damage or have a serious effect on sb/sth
senses.zh: 损害；有损于；严重影响到:

senses.en: to criticize or attack sb who has criticized or attacked you

ex.en: Sarah used the article to strike back at her critics.
ex.zh: 萨拉借这篇文章反击批评她的人。

senses.en: to hit sb very hard so that they fall to the ground; to kill sb

ex.en: Fights broke out near the shop and one girl was struck down by a handbag.
ex.zh: 商店附近发生了打斗，一名女孩被一只手提包击倒。

ex.en: the spot where Kennedy was struck down
ex.zh: 肯尼迪遇刺的地点

senses.en: to reject sth;to make sth no longer valid

ex.en: Only the Supreme Court has the power to strike down this legislation.
ex.zh: 只有最高法院有权废除这项法规。

ex.en: Parents tried to have the dance ban struck down.
ex.zh: 父母们试图使跳舞禁令得以取消。

senses.en: to remove sb’s name from the list of members of a profession so that they can no longer work in that profession
senses.zh: 把某人﹙从某专业中﹚除名；取消…资格:

ex.en: She was struck off for professional misconduct.
ex.zh: 她因为渎职被除名了。

ex.en: These doctors should be struck off the medical register.
ex.zh: 这些医生应该被取消行医资格。

senses.en: to remove sth with a sharp blow; to cut sth off

ex.en: They struck off his head with a sword.
ex.zh: 他们用剑削掉了他的脑袋。

senses.en: (in baseball
senses.zh: 棒球) to fail to hit the ball successfully three times and so finish your turn; to make sb do this﹙使﹚三击不中出局:

ex.en: He struck out in the third inning.
ex.zh: 他在第三局三击不中出局了。

ex.en: The pitcher struck out three batters.
ex.zh: 投手使三名击球员三击未中出局。

senses.en: to remove sth from a text or a list by drawing a line through it

ex.en: I struck out some words to make the telegram shorter.
ex.zh: 我删掉一些字，把电报压缩了一下。

ex.en: He insisted that I strike out all references to his family.
ex.zh: 他坚持要我删掉所有提及他的家庭的内容。

senses.en: to begin a friendship,a relationship, a conversation, etc. with sb﹙
senses.zh: 和某人﹚建立友谊，开始来往，交谈起来:

ex.en: My mother will strike up a conversation with anyone she meets.
ex.zh: 我母亲逮谁跟谁聊。

ex.en: Children of the same age don’t always strike up friendships ().
ex.zh: 同龄的孩子不一定会成为朋友。

senses.en: to go somewhere or do sth with sb else, especially because you have nothing else to do﹙

ex.en: I’m free this morning. Can I string along with you when you go to the shops?
ex.zh: 我今天上午有空。能跟你去商店吗？

senses.en: to spread out in a line

ex.en: As we climbed, we tended to string out, with the fittest people taking the lead.
ex.zh: 我们爬山时一般会拉长阵线，由最强壮的人领头。

senses.en: to combine words,phrases, sentences, etc. to form sth that has some meaning
senses.zh: 把﹙单词、短语、句子等﹚联成有意义的单位:

ex.en: I can barely string together two words of German.
ex.zh: 我勉强懂得说一两句德语。

ex.en: The report should be written by somebody who can string two sentences together.
ex.zh: 这份报告应该让会摆弄文笔的人来写。

senses.en: to join a series of things together
senses.zh: 把﹙一系列事物﹚连接起来:

ex.en: pearls strung together on a necklace
ex.zh: 穿在项链上的珍珠

ex.en: The student of kung fu learns various movements that are then strung together.
ex.zh: 学功夫的人先学会各种基本动作，然后组合成一套一套的动作。

senses.en: to kill sb by hanging them, especially illegally﹙

ex.en: They’ll string him up if they catch him.
ex.zh: 他们一抓住他，就会把他吊死。

senses.en: to separate a machine or an engine into parts, especially in order to clean or repair it

ex.en: We had to strip down the engine and replace the worn parts.
ex.zh: 我们得拆开引擎更换磨损了的部件。

ex.en: The car was stripped down and sold for parts.
ex.zh: 车子已拆成零件卖了。

senses.en: to take off your clothes until you are only wearing the items mentioned

ex.en: I stripped down to my underwear for the massage.
ex.zh: 我脱得只剩下内衣，等着按摩。

senses.en: to take away a right, a privilege,property, etc. that sb has, as a punishment
senses.zh: 取消…的权利﹙或特权、财产等﹚；使…丧失权利等﹙作为惩罚﹚:

ex.en: He was stripped of his title for refusing to fight in Britain (= for example, in boxing).
ex.zh: 他因为拒绝在英国比赛而被取消了头衔。

ex.en: They stripped me of my citizenship and deported me.他们剥夺我的公民资格，将我驱逐出境。

senses.en: to remove a layer of sth﹙

ex.en: It was hard work stripping the old wallpaper off.
ex.zh: 那些旧墙纸很不容易揭掉。

ex.en: All the leaves had been stripped off the branches.
ex.zh: 树枝上的叶子落光了。

senses.en: to completely remove things you do not want; to remove everything from a place and leave it empty
senses.zh: 将﹙不需要的东西﹚全部挪走；清空﹙某处的东西﹚:

ex.en: They had stripped out all the original features of the house.
ex.zh: 他们把房子本来的面目全毁了。

senses.en: to manage to continue in spite of great difficulties
senses.zh: 在困难中坚持；勉力维持:

ex.en: The country’s economy is still struggling along.
ex.zh: 国家的经济还在艰难地维持着。

ex.en: The government struggled on with a tiny majority.
ex.zh: 政府以微弱多数勉力维持着。

senses.en: to stop a cigarette, etc. burning

ex.en: He stubbed the cigarette out with his foot.
ex.zh: 他用脚把香烟踩灭了。

senses.en: to do sth very badly; to fail at sth﹙

ex.en: I’m afraid I stuffed up again.
ex.zh: 恐怕我又砸锅了。

ex.en: I’m not having them stuff up my plans.
ex.zh: 我不会让他们破坏我的计划的。

senses.en: to find sb/sth unexpectedly or by chance

ex.en: We stumbled on the solution by accident.
ex.zh: 我们是偶然发现了这个解决方法的。

ex.en: I stumbled across an old school friend today.
ex.zh: 我今天碰到了一位老校友。

senses.en: to become involved in sth by chance

ex.en: She stumbled into engineering because of her love of maths.
ex.zh: 她因为喜欢数学，巧逢机遇搞起了工程。

senses.en: to pay the amount of money for sth that sb asks, often when you do not want to﹙
senses.zh: 不情愿地为…﹚付钱，掏腰包:

ex.en: He had no money so I had to stump up for his ticket.
ex.zh: 他没带钱，于是我只好替他出钱买票。

ex.en: We had to stump up an extra five hundred pounds for insurance.
ex.zh: 我们不得不又付了五百英镑买保险。

senses.en: to make sb/sth/yourself experience, suffer or be affected by sth, usually sth unpleasant

ex.en: to subject sth to scrutiny/analysis
ex.zh: 对某事物进行认真审查/分析

ex.en: All our products are subjected to thorough tests.
ex.zh: 我们的所有产品都要经过全面检测。

senses.en: to agree with an opinion, a theory, etc.

ex.en: It’s not an opinion I tend to subscribe to.
ex.zh: 这个观点我不太赞同。

ex.en: The company subscribe to the view that if you can encourage children to use your products, they will continue to use them when they are adults.
ex.zh: 公司赞成这样的观点，即如果能够鼓励儿童使用你的产品，他们长大后就会继续使用这些产品。

senses.en: to take the place of sb/sth else

ex.en: Can you substitute for me at the meeting?
ex.zh: 你能代我去开一下会吗？

ex.en: Nothing can substitute for the advice your doctor is able to give you.
ex.zh: 没有什么可以取代医生所能给你的医嘱。

senses.en: to achieve sth that you have been trying to do or get; to have the result or effect that was intended
senses.zh: 做成某事；获取某物；实现目标；达到目的:

ex.en: He succeeded in getting top marks in chemistry.
ex.zh: 他拿到了化学课的最高分。

ex.en: The Labour Party succeeded in capturing the female vote (= they persuaded women to vote for them).
ex.zh: 工党成功地说服了女性投他们的票。

senses.en: to gradually involve sb in an activity, a situation, etc., especially one that they do not at first want to be involved in

ex.en: There is a danger we could be sucked into a war.
ex.zh: 我们有被卷入战争的危险。

ex.en: Don’t let yourself get sucked in.
ex.zh: 别让自己牵扯进去。

senses.en: to try to please sb by helping them, saying nice things to them, etc. in order to gain an advantage for yourself

ex.en: He’s always sucking up to the teacher.
ex.zh: 他总是讨好老师。

ex.en: We don’t suck up to anyone!
ex.zh: 我们不对任何人卑躬屈膝！

senses.en: to persuade sb to do sth they do not really want to do, especially by using their lack of knowledge or experience
senses.zh: 蒙骗某人使﹙做某事﹚；诱使﹙做某事﹚:

ex.en: He got suckered into the scheme.
ex.zh: 他进了圈套。

ex.en: I was suckered into helping.
ex.zh: 我上了当去帮忙。

senses.en: [NOTE]This phrasal verb is usually used in the passive.
senses.zh: 这个短语动词通常用于被动语态。

senses.en: to formally ask for sth, especially in a court of law
senses.zh: 提出请求；﹙尤指在法院﹚起诉:

ex.en: to sue for divorce
ex.zh: 正式要求离婚

ex.en: The rebels were forced to sue for peace.
ex.zh: 反叛者被迫求和。

senses.en: to make sth appropriate for sb/sth
senses.zh: 使适合﹙或适应﹚某人﹙或事物﹚:

ex.en: He can suit his conversation to whoever he’s with.
ex.zh: 无论跟谁在一起，他都能说到一块儿。

senses.en: to give the main points of sth in a few words

ex.en: Before we conclude the meeting, let me sum up.
ex.zh: 会议结束之前，我来总结一下。

ex.en: To sum up, there are three main ways of tackling the problem…
ex.zh: 概括起来说，这一问题主要有三种处理办法…

senses.en: a speech made by the judge to the jury near the end of the trial, giving the main points of the evidence and the arguments in the case
senses.zh: 证据概述﹙法官综述证据，提请陪审员注意﹚:

ex.en: The judge will begin her summing-up on Monday.
ex.zh: 法官将于周一开始进行概述。

senses.en: an occasion when sb states the main points of an argument, etc.

ex.en: There was a final summing-up by each of the speakers.
ex.zh: 每位演讲者都作了最后总结。

ex.en: The speakers gave brief summings-up of their talks.
ex.zh: 演讲者对他们的讲话进行了简要总结。

senses.en: to describe or show the most typical characteristics of sb/sth, especially in a few words
senses.zh: 扼要描述人﹙或事物﹚；简而言之:

ex.en: His speech summed up the mood of the whole country.
ex.zh: 他的讲话简要描述了整个国家的气氛。

ex.en: Totally lazy — that just about sums him up.
ex.zh: 懒到家了——这大体上就是他的真实写照。

senses.en: (as sb/sth) to decide or express what you think about sb/sth
senses.zh: 估量，判断﹙人或事物﹚；视某人﹙或事物﹚为……:

ex.en: The two of them stood there, summing each other up.
ex.zh: 他们俩站在那儿，相互打量着。

ex.en: He had already summed her up as someone who hated to admit defeat.
ex.zh: 他已经把她归为那种不愿认输的人。

senses.en: to manage to produce a particular feeling in yourself, although this is difficult
senses.zh: 设法激起﹙感情﹚；鼓起﹙勇气﹚；振作﹙ 精神﹚:

ex.en: She eventually summoned up the courage to knock at the door.
ex.zh: 她最终鼓起勇气敲了门。

ex.en: He managed to summon up a smile.
ex.zh: 他挤出了一个笑容。

senses.en: [sing.] a sudden great increase in sth

ex.en: There has been a recent upsurge of violence in the area.
ex.zh: 近日区内暴力事件急增。

ex.en: an upsurge of interest in science and technology
ex.zh: 对科学技术的兴趣倍增

senses.en: to stop trying to resist a feeling,a particular person, etc. and let them control what you do
senses.zh: 任随别人﹙或感觉等﹚控制:

ex.en: He surrendered to his natural instinct to run away.
ex.zh: 他克制不住，本能地逃跑了。

ex.en: She surrendered to Leo’s charm.
ex.zh: 她抵挡不住利奥的魅力。

senses.en: to find out what sb/sth is really like; to understand the important things about sb/sth
senses.zh: 发现…的真相；了解…的本质:

ex.en: My classmates were sussing me out, seeing how tough I was.
ex.zh: 我的同学开始了解我，看出我有多坚强。

ex.en: We’ll need to suss out our opponents before the game.
ex.zh: 我们在比赛前要摸清对手的底细。

senses.en: to completely cover sb/sth or absorb them/it, so that they can no longer be seen or do not exist separately

ex.en: He watched them walk away until the darkness swallowed them up.
ex.zh: 他目送他们走远，直到消失在黑夜里。

ex.en: She was so embarrassed she wished that the ground would open and swallow her up.
ex.zh: 她尴尬极了，简直希望地面裂开把她吞没。

senses.en: to use sth such as money or resources completely﹙
senses.zh: 把钱或资源等﹚用光，用尽，耗尽:

ex.en: Practising the piano swallows up all her free time.
ex.zh: 练钢琴占用了她的所有闲暇时间。

ex.en: Pay rises were quickly swallowed up by price increases.
ex.zh: 工资的增长很快就被物价的提高抵消了。

senses.en: to move around or go from one place to another enjoying yourself, but with no real purpose﹙

ex.en: Stop swanning about pretending to be clever.
ex.zh: 别自以为是地晃荡了。

ex.en: She’s swanning around Europe for the summer.
ex.zh: 她夏天要在欧洲转悠。

senses.en: to go off to enjoy yourself with no real purpose

ex.en: He’s always swanning off to Spain on holiday!
ex.zh: 他一有假期就去西班牙悠闲作乐！

senses.en: to replace sb/sth with sb/sth else

ex.en: At half-time the manager swapped some of the players around.
ex.zh: 经理在半场时把几名队员换下了场。

senses.en: to change from one situation, position, etc. to another; to make sb do this﹙
senses.zh: 使…﹚从一种情况﹙或位置等﹚转换到另一种:

ex.en: We swapped over from an electric cooker to a gas cooker.
ex.zh: 我们从电炉灶具换到了煤气炉。

ex.en: Have you been swapped over to the new computer system yet?
ex.zh: 有人给你换上新计算机系统了吗？

senses.en: (not used in the progressive tenses
senses.zh: 不用于进行时) to name sb in order to show that you are making a serious promise以… 名义发誓；起誓；立誓:

ex.en: I swear by Almighty God that I will tell the truth (= for example, said in a British court of law).
ex.zh: 我向全能的上帝起誓，我以下所说句句属实。

senses.zh: 不用于进行时) to believe strongly that sth/sb is very useful and helpful极信赖；对…推崇备至:

ex.en: My brother swears by lemon and honey drinks as a cold remedy.
ex.zh: 我哥哥深信柠檬加蜂蜜饮料能治疗感冒。

ex.en: Why don’t you go and see Dr. Nash? My mother swears by him.
ex.zh: 你干吗不去看纳什医生呢？我母亲对他十分推崇。

senses.en: to introduce sb publicly to a new position, responsibility, etc.by getting them to promise that they will do the job correctly, be loyal to the organization, their country, etc.
senses.zh: 使某人宣誓就职；使某人宣誓忠于某组织﹙ 或国家等﹚ :

ex.en: He was sworn in as President in January.
ex.zh: 他于一月份宣誓就任总统。

ex.en: The new President was hurriedly sworn into office.
ex.zh: 新总统急急忙忙宣誓就职。

senses.en: [U] [sing.] the act of getting sb to promise publicly to do their job correctly, be loyal to their organization or country, etc. before they begin a new job or responsibility

ex.en: The swearing-in of the new president will take place tomorrow.
ex.zh: 新总统将于明天宣誓就职。

ex.en: a swearing-in ceremony
ex.zh: 宣誓就职典礼

senses.en: to make a serious promise that you will give sth up,especially sth that is bad or harmful
senses.zh: 发誓放弃﹙ 尤指坏的或有害事物﹚ :

ex.en: He’s intending to swear off alcohol.
ex.zh: 他有意发誓戒酒。

ex.en: Ever since her boyfriend left she has sworn off men.
ex.zh: 自从她的男友离开之后，她发誓不再和男性来往。

senses.en: to say that sth is definitely true
to lose weight by doing a lot of hard exercise to make yourself hot and produce sweat

ex.en: I sweated off the extra weight by playing squash every day.
ex.zh: 我每天靠打壁球出一身汗减掉多余的体重。

senses.en: to get rid of a cold, fever, etc. by staying warm so that you produce sweat
senses.zh: 通过发汗治好感冒﹙或发烧等﹚:

ex.en: Whenever I get a bad fever I go to bed and sweat it out.
ex.zh: 我一发高烧就卧床发发汗把它治好。

senses.en: to work very hard on sth; to spend a lot of time doing sth or worrying about sth
senses.zh: 努力做某事；耗费时间做﹙或操心﹚某事:

ex.en: I’ve been sweating over my letter of resignation for several days.
ex.zh: 我已经花了几天时间写辞职信了。

senses.en: to make sb feel very enthusiastic about sth or involved in sth; to affect sb so much they forget everything else

ex.en: Anna was swept along by her father’s enthusiasm.
ex.zh: 父亲的热情使安娜也激动起来。

senses.en: to defeat sb easily

ex.en: United swept Liverpool aside with ease.
ex.zh: 联队轻而易举地把利物浦队打败。

senses.en: to destroy or get rid of sth completely
senses.zh: 消灭；彻底消除；完全打消:

ex.en: The President’s speech swept away all our doubts.
ex.zh: 总统的讲话消除了我们的一切疑虑。

ex.en: Poverty will be swept away!
ex.zh: 贫穷将被消灭！

senses.en: to remove sth from somewhere, especially by brushing with your hands, a brush, etc.﹙

ex.en: He swept the crumbs off the table.
ex.zh: 他把桌上的麵包屑扫掉。

ex.en: () The wind swept her hat off.
ex.zh: 风把她的帽子吹走了。

senses.en: to make sb fall suddenly and deeply in love with you
senses.zh: 使某人一见倾心；使某人立刻迷上自己:

ex.en: Maria was swept off her feet by Mark’s charm.
ex.zh: 马克的魅力使玛丽亚一见倾心。

senses.en: to lift sb with a sudden smooth movement

ex.en: He ran forward and swept her up in his arms.
ex.zh: 他跑上前去一把将她抱在怀里。

senses.en: to make sb become very involved in sth so that they are unable to think clearly

ex.en: The whole country was swept up in the excitement.
ex.zh: 全国上下都沉浸在兴奋的气氛中。

senses.en: to remove dust,dirt, etc. from a floor with a brush

ex.en: We had to sweep up before we left.
ex.zh: 我们临走之前得清扫地板。

ex.en: We’d better sweep up all the bits of broken glass quickly.
ex.zh: 我们最好快点把玻璃碴子扫乾净。

senses.en: to try to persuade sb to help you, agree to sth, etc. by giving them gifts,being very nice to them, etc.

ex.en: If you sweeten him up he’ll do the work for you.
ex.zh: 你要是哄哄他，他就会帮你干活。

ex.en: They sweeten up customers with special offers.
ex.zh: 他们用特别优惠吸引顾客。

senses.en: to drink a large amount of sth quickly

ex.en: He just swilled down his beer and walked out.
ex.zh: 他一口气把啤酒灌下肚，然后走了出去。

senses.en: to turn around fast to face the other way; to make sb/sth do this﹙
senses.zh: 使某人﹚猛地转身；猛地掉转﹙ 某物﹚:

ex.en: Luke suddenly swung round and glared at me.
ex.zh: 卢克突然转过身来瞪着我。

ex.en: I swung the car round and drove back down the road.
ex.zh: 我猛地掉转车头沿路开车返回。

senses.en: to change from one idea, opinion, etc. to another,especially the opposite one﹙
senses.zh: 使﹚改变主意﹙或想法等﹚；﹙使﹚改弦易辙:

ex.en: The Labour Party has now swung round to supporting Europe.
ex.zh: 工党现在已经改弦更张，转而支持欧洲了。

ex.en: You should be able to swing people round to your point of view.
ex.zh: 你应该有能力扭转人们的想法，接受你的观点。

senses.en: to try to hit sb﹙

ex.en: She swung at me with the iron bar.
ex.zh: 她抡着根铁棍向我打过来。

senses.en: to visit a person or place for a short time, especially when you are going somewhere else
senses.zh: 进某处一会儿；短暂拜访；看望一下:

ex.en: She swung by (=came here) on her way home.
ex.zh: 她回家路过时进来了一下。

ex.en: Let’s swing by Dave’s house after the movie.
ex.zh: 咱们看完电影后顺便到戴夫家去坐坐吧。

senses.en: to stop an electrical device, a machine or an engine working by pressing a switch, a button,etc.
senses.zh: 关﹙ 电器、机器或引擎﹚ :

ex.en: The heating switches off at 10.00 p.m.
ex.zh: 晚上10 点停止供暖。

ex.en: Shall I switch the lights off?
ex.zh: 我要不要关了灯？

senses.en: to start an electrical device, a machine or an engine by pressing a switch, a button, etc.

ex.en: She walked in and switched on the light.
ex.zh: 她走进来打开了灯。

ex.en: The machine switches () on automatically.
ex.zh: 这台机器能自动开启。

senses.en: ) to change from one television station to another

ex.en: I switched over to watch the news.
ex.zh: 我换了个频道看看新闻。

senses.en: to turn or move your body, eyes or head around quickly to face another direction﹙
senses.zh: 把身子或脸等﹚转向另一方:

ex.en: He swivelled around to look at her.
ex.zh: 他猛地转过头去看她。

senses.en: to turn or make sth turn around a fixed central point﹙

ex.en: She swivelled the chair around to face them.
ex.zh: 她把椅子转过来面向他们。

senses.en: to study a subject very hard, especially when you are preparing for an exam﹙
senses.zh: 尤指为准备考试﹚刻苦学习﹙某门课程﹚:

ex.en: I have to swot up on phrasal verbs for a test tomorrow.
ex.zh: 我不得不为明天的测验努力温习短语动词。

ex.en: It’s time to start swotting up for the exam.
ex.zh: 现在该开始好好复习准备考试了。

senses.en: to add sth as an extra item, especially in a careless way﹙
senses.zh: 不经意地﹚ 附加， 增补， 添加:

ex.en: The last paragraph seems to have been tacked on at the last minute.
ex.zh: 最后一段像是在最后一分钟加上的。

ex.en: An extra day has been tacked onto the New Year holiday.
ex.zh: 新年休假额外增加了一天。

senses.en: to go somewhere with sb, especially when you have not been invited﹙
senses.zh: 尤指未经邀请﹚跟随，尾随:

ex.en: The children tagged along behind their mother.
ex.zh: 孩子们跟在妈妈后面。

ex.en: Can I tag along () when you go to the shops?
ex.zh: 我跟着你去商店好吗？

senses.en: to follow sb closely and go somewhere with them,although you have not been invited﹙

ex.en: Kate’s friend tagged on and spoiled the day.
ex.zh: 凯特的朋友黏着她，弄得大家一天都扫兴。

ex.en: We tagged on to the end of the procession.
ex.zh: 我们紧紧地跟在游行队伍的末尾。

senses.en: to add sth as an extra item to the end of sth, especially in a careless way﹙

ex.en: An apology was tagged on to the end of the letter.
ex.zh: 信的结尾顺便附了一句抱歉的话。

ex.en: Online security is being built in to the system, not tagged on.
ex.zh: 联机安全措施正被内置在系统中，不是外加的。

senses.en: () a long line of traffic that moves very slowly or does not move at all﹙

ex.en: The crash caused a six-mile tailback.
ex.zh: 撞车事故使受阻车辆排了六英里长。

senses.en: to become smaller, fewer, weaker, etc.
senses.zh: 变得越来越小﹙或少、弱等﹚；逐渐消失:

ex.en: Sales tailed off in the autumn/fall.
ex.zh: 进入秋季，销售开始下滑。

ex.en: The number of tourists starts to tail off in September.
ex.zh: 从九月份起，游客人数开始逐步减少。

senses.en: to make or adapt sth for a particular purpose, a particular person, etc.

ex.en: Special programmes of study are tailored to the needs of specific students.
ex.zh: 针对具体学生的需要安排了特别的课程。

senses.en: to shock or surprise sb

ex.en: I was taken aback by his rudeness.
ex.zh: 我对他的粗鲁无礼感到吃惊。

senses.zh: 不用于进行时) to look like or behave likean older member of your family﹙外貌或举止﹚像﹙长辈﹚:

ex.en: I’m told I take after my grandmother.
ex.zh: 有人说我长得像外婆。

ex.en: Your daughter doesn’t ake after you at all.
ex.zh: 你女儿一点儿都不像你。

senses.en: ) to begin to follow sb quickly inorder to catch them

ex.en: A man rushed out of the bank and two men took after him.
ex.zh: 一名男子冲出银行，另两名男子追了出来。

ex.en: She ran out into the night and he took after her.
ex.zh: 她冲入了夜幕，他紧随其后赶了出去。

senses.en: , ) tobegin to dislike sb/sth

ex.en: Why have you suddenly taken against Laura?
ex.zh: 你为什么突然讨厌劳拉了？

senses.en: to take sb or sth withyou when you go somewhere

ex.en: Tom took his sister along to the party.
ex.zh: 汤姆带着妹妹去参加晚会。

ex.en: When you travel with young children, take along some favourite toys or a book.
ex.zh: 和孩子们旅行要带些他们喜欢的玩具或一本书。

senses.en: (in sport
senses.zh: 体育运动) to defeat sb easily轻易打败；把…打得一败涂地:

ex.en: He took the American apart in the third set (= in a game of tennis).
ex.zh: 他在第三盘轻松地打败了美国选手。

ex.en: We took the other team apart.
ex.zh: 我们把另一个队打得一败涂地。

senses.en: to attack or criticize sb/sthseverely

ex.en: Her second novel was taken apart by the critics.
ex.zh: 她的第二部小说被评论家批得体无完肤。

senses.en: to separate a machine, a piece ofequipment, etc. into its parts

ex.en: She took the clock apart and couldn’t put it back together.
ex.zh: 她把钟拆了却装不到一块儿。

ex.en: You can take the mixer apart to clean it.
ex.zh: 你可以把搅拌器拆开来清洁。

senses.en: to visita place with sb; to show sb the interesting orimportant parts of a place
senses.zh: 带﹙某人﹚游览；领﹙ 某人﹚ 参观:

ex.en: If you’d like to see the town, I could take you around.
ex.zh: 你要是想看看城里，我可以带你转转。

ex.en: We got a guide to take us round the temples.
ex.zh: 有一位导游带我们参观了那些寺庙。

senses.en: to separate sb from the rest of agroup in order to talk to them privately
senses.zh: 把……带到一边﹙ 私下谈话﹚ :

ex.en: She took me aside and explained the situation.
ex.zh: 她把我拉到旁边解释情况。

senses.en: to remove sb fromsomewhere; to lead or move sb to another place
senses.zh: 把…送走；带…去别处；将…转到别处:

ex.en: The injured were taken away by ambulance.
ex.zh: 伤员被救护车送走了。

ex.en: I can take you away from all this (= all this trouble).
ex.zh: 我可以带你离开这一切烦扰。

senses.en: to remove sb, especially a child, from sb’scare

ex.en: The children were taken away from them and put into a children’s home.
ex.zh: 孩子们从他们身边被带走，送到了儿童之家。

ex.en: My father took me away from school and taught me himself.
ex.zh: 我父亲给我退了学亲自教我。

senses.en: to take sb with you on a trip or holiday/vacation

ex.en: He takes the whole family away for two weeks in the summer.
ex.zh: 他夏天带全家旅游两个星期。

senses.en: a restaurant that cooks and sells food that you eat somewhere else

ex.en: a Chinese/Indian takeaway
ex.zh: 中国/印度外卖餐馆

ex.en: a takeaway restaurant
ex.zh: 外卖餐馆

senses.en: 'takeout, 'carry-out) a meal that you buy from this type of restaurant

ex.en: We could get a takeaway tonight.
ex.zh: 我们今天可以吃外卖晚餐。

ex.en: a takeaway pizza
ex.zh: 外卖的比萨饼

senses.en: to make the effect or value of sth seem less﹙
senses.zh: 使效果、价值等﹚减少，减弱；贬低﹙意义等﹚:

ex.en: I don’t wish to take away from his achievements, but he couldn’t have done it without our help.
ex.zh: 我不想贬低他的成绩，但是如果没有我们的帮助，他是做不成的。

senses.en: to go with sb/sth to a lower level, to a more southern part of a country, etc., or to a different part of a building, town, country, etc.
senses.zh: 带…去﹙下一层、南方或别处﹚:

ex.en: The nurse will take you down in the lift.
ex.zh: 护士将带你乘电梯下去。

ex.en: The injured climbers were taken down the mountain on a sledge.
ex.zh: 受伤的登山者用雪橇送下山去。

senses.en: to remove sth from a high level

ex.en: She took a book down from the top shelf.
ex.zh: 她从书架最上层拿下一本书。

senses.en: to remove sth that is hanging on a wall, etc.
senses.zh: 摘掉，取下﹙墙上悬挂的东西等﹚:

ex.en: Will you help me take the curtains down?
ex.zh: 请帮我摘下窗帘好吗？

senses.en: to remove a structure by separating it into pieces

ex.en: They were taking their tent down as we left.
ex.zh: 我们离开时他们正在拆帐篷。

senses.en: [C] [U] the number of people who join a college or other organization at a particular time
senses.zh: 接受﹙入学或入会等﹚的人数:

ex.en: a new intake of students
ex.zh: 新入学的学生人数

senses.en: ) a first test, meeting, etc. that you have when you go to a hospital or have an interview for a job or school, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 入院的﹚初次检查；﹙求职或申请入学等的﹚ 初次面试， 初次见面

senses.en: to go with sb or to take sth into a building or another place

ex.en: I’m going into town, so I’ll take you in if you like.
ex.zh: 我要去城里，你要是想去我就带上你。

ex.en: I took Jack into the kitchen for a quiet chat.
ex.zh: 我把杰克带进厨房悄悄地聊天。

senses.en: ) to do particular kinds of work for other people in your home, in order to earn money
senses.zh: 领﹙ 活﹚ 到家里做:

ex.en: My grandmother used to take in washing.
ex.zh: 我祖母从前把洗衣活揽回家做。

senses.en: to absorb sth into the body by breathing or swallowing it

ex.en: Fish take in oxygen through their gills.
ex.zh: 鱼用鳃吸氧气。

ex.en: She took in deep breaths of sea air.
ex.zh: 她深深地吸着海边的空气。

senses.en: to accept sb into an institution,an organization, etc.
to bring sb/sth into a particular situation, activity, period of time, etc.
senses.zh: 将…带进﹙某状况、活动、时期等﹚:

ex.en: Improved graphics took computer games into a new era.
ex.zh: 经改进的制图技术将电脑游戏带进了一个新时代。

ex.en: Owen’s goal took England into the lead (=they were winning).
ex.zh: 欧文的进球让英格兰队取得了领先地位。

senses.en: the moment when an aircraft,etc. leaves the ground﹙

ex.en: The plane is ready for take-off.
ex.zh: 飞机准备起飞。

ex.en: take-off point/speed/run
ex.zh: 起飞点/速度/滑行

senses.en: the moment when your feet leave the ground when you jump
to leave somewhere suddenly or in a hurry

ex.en: Whenever things get tough, she takes off.
ex.zh: 每当遇到困难，她就熘走。

ex.en: He stayed for a year, then took off for a job in New York.
ex.zh: 他呆了一年，就匆匆到纽约找了份工作。

senses.en: an act of copying sb in an amusing way
to rescue sb from a ship, a mountain, etc.﹙

ex.en: The injured men were taken off the boat by helicopter.
ex.zh: 受伤的人被直升机从船上救走了。

senses.en: [NOTE]This phrasal verb is often used in the passive.
senses.zh: 这个短语动词常用于被动语态。

senses.en: to make sb go with you to another place ; to take sth to another place

ex.en: They took him off to the police station.
ex.zh: 他们把他带到了警察局。

ex.en: She collected our passports and took them off somewhere.
ex.zh: 她收集我们的护照拿走了。

senses.en: to remove sb from a job, position, etc.and not allow them to continue

ex.en: One of the lawyers has been taken off the case.
ex.zh: 其中一名律师已被禁止继续参与此案。

senses.en: to begin to have a particular quality,appearance, etc.

ex.en: Lisa’s voice took on a more serious tone.
ex.zh: 莉萨说话的语气变得严肃起来。

ex.en: His words suddenly took on a different meaning.
ex.zh: 他的话突然弦外有音了。

senses.en: (of a bus, plane, ship, etc.
senses.zh: 公共汽车、飞机、船只等) to allow sb/sth to enter or come on board接载﹙乘客﹚；装载:

ex.en: The bus stopped to take on more passengers.
ex.zh: 公共汽车停下让其他乘客上车。

ex.en: The plane was taking on fuel from a tanker.
ex.zh: 飞机正在从加油飞机上加油。

senses.en: to decide to do sth without asking permission or talking to anyone else
senses.zh: 自行决定，主动﹙做某事﹚；自作主张:

ex.en: She took the responsibility for what had happened upon herself.
ex.zh: 她主动为所发生的事承担责任。

senses.en: to invite sb to go with you to the theatre, a restaurant, etc.
senses.zh: 请某人一同做某事﹙ 或到某处﹚ :

ex.en: He took Susie out for a meal.
ex.zh: 他请苏茜出去吃饭了。

senses.en: to remove sb from a place; to take sb outside a building
senses.zh: 把﹙某人﹚弄走；带某人出去﹙或离开﹚:

ex.en: The prisoners were taken out and shot.
ex.zh: 囚犯被带出去枪毙了。

senses.en: to kill sb or destroy sth; to injure or damage sb/sth so that they cannot work or be used
senses.zh: 杀死； 毁灭； 摧残:

ex.en: Enemy missiles took out two of our planes.
ex.zh: 敌人的导弹击落了我们其中两架飞机。

ex.en: Police think he was taken out by a rival gang.
ex.zh: 警方认为他是被一个敌对团伙杀害的。

senses.en: to remove an amount of money from a larger amount to pay for sth

ex.en: ￡20 will be taken out of your wages to pay for the damage.
ex.zh: 将从你的工资中扣除20 英镑赔偿损失。

ex.en: Contributions to your pension will be taken out of your salary.
ex.zh: 养老金的交款将从薪金中扣除。

senses.en: to stop your career, studies, etc.for a period of time in order to do sth else﹙

ex.en: She took a year out of college to work abroad.
ex.zh: 她大学休学一年到国外工作。

ex.en: He took a year out between school and college.
ex.zh: 他中学毕业后在上大学之前休学一年。

senses.en: to make sb feel very tired

ex.en: That flu really took it out of me.
ex.zh: 那次流感使我病得一塌煳涂。

ex.en: Looking after three young children really takes a lot out of you.
ex.zh: 照看三个小孩子能把你累死。

senses.en: to make sb forget their worries, thoughts, concerns,etc.

ex.en: Seeing his old friends again took him out of himself.
ex.zh: 再次见到老朋友使他忘掉了很多烦恼。

senses.en: to behave in an unpleasant way towards sb/sth because you feel angry, disappointed, etc.

ex.en: When he’s had a bad day, he always takes it out on me.
ex.zh: 他哪天不顺心就拿我当出气筒。

ex.en: You shouldn’t take your frustrations out on the kids.
ex.zh: 你别拿孩子们出气。

senses.en: to go with sb around a building and show them what is interesting or important

ex.en: A guide took us over the house.
ex.zh: 导游带我们参观了这所房子。

senses.en: to look at or discuss sth with sb and explain important points

ex.en: Would you mind taking us over the procedure again?
ex.zh: 请给我们再讲解一下程序好吗？

senses.en: to affect sb so strongly that they are unable to think of anything else or do anything else
senses.zh: 充塞着思想﹙或生活等﹚；使满脑子… :

ex.en: His ambition had taken him over.
ex.zh: 他的野心左右着他。

ex.en: My job is starting to take over my life.
ex.zh: 我的工作开始支配我的生活。

senses.en: an act of gaining control of a company by buying most of its shares
senses.zh: 收购； 接管； 接收:

ex.en: The company have abandoned their takeover bid.
ex.zh: 这家公司已经放弃了收购建议。

senses.en: an act of gaining control of a country,region or city, especially by force﹙
senses.zh: 对国家、地区或城市的﹚控制，强行接管:

ex.en: a military takeover
ex.zh: 军事接管

senses.en: to take sb/sth with you to another place, sb else’s home, etc.

ex.en: I’m taking the photos straight round to Phil’s to show him.
ex.zh: 我要把这些照片直接带到菲尔家给他看看。

ex.en: Joe took us round to see his mother.
ex.zh: 乔带我们去看他母亲。

senses.en: to lead or carry a person or a thing through one place to another
senses.zh: 把人﹙或物﹚一直带到…；带着人﹙ 或物﹚ 经过… :

ex.en: Let’s take our tea through to the lounge.
ex.zh: 咱们把茶端到休息室吧。

ex.en: The journey takes you through some beautiful scenery.
ex.zh: 旅途中将穿越一些美丽的风景地带。

senses.en: to discuss sth with sb or explain it to them so that they know what to do
senses.zh: 帮助…熟悉了解； 给… 讲解:

ex.en: Your solicitor will take you through the contract.
ex.zh: 你的律师会向你解释合同。

ex.en: The director took us through the play scene by scene.
ex.zh: 导演一幕一幕地给我们说戏。

senses.en: to start liking sb/sth

ex.en: I didn’t take to Elena’s husband at all.
ex.zh: 我从来没有喜欢过埃琳娜的丈夫。

ex.en: He hasn’t taken to his new school.
ex.zh: 他对新学校还没有产生兴趣。

senses.en: to not like sb/sth
senses.zh: 不喜欢，厌烦﹙某人或某事物﹚:

ex.en: I don’t take kindly to being told how to run my life.
ex.zh: 我讨厌别人对我的生活指手画脚。

senses.en: to go away to a particular place, especially to escape from sth difficult or dangerous﹙
senses.zh: 尤指为逃避困难或危险﹚逃往，躲到:

ex.en: She felt so ill that she took to her bed.
ex.zh: 她感觉很不舒服，只好上床休息了。

ex.en: The rebels took to the hills.
ex.zh: 反叛者逃进了山里。

senses.en: to start running

ex.en: They took to their heels and fled.
ex.zh: 他们撒腿就跑，逃走了。

senses.en: to develop an ability for sth

ex.en: He took to tennis as if he’d been playing all his life.
ex.zh: 他网球学得很快，好像一生都在从事这项运动似的。

senses.en: to go with sb or take sth to a higher place or to another part of a building, country, etc.
senses.zh: 和﹙某人﹚去较高处﹙或别处﹚；把﹙某物﹚带到较高处﹙或别处﹚:

ex.en: Someone will take you up to your room.
ex.zh: 有人会带你去你的房间的。

ex.en: Why don’t we take our picnic up the hill?
ex.zh: 我们为什么不到山上去野餐呢？

senses.en: to move into a particular position

ex.en: We took up our positions by the door.
ex.zh: 我们把住了门口。

senses.en: the process by which sth is taken into a body or system; the rate at which this happens

ex.en: The experiment measured the uptake of oxygen by the muscles.
ex.zh: 这个实验测量了肌肉对氧气的吸收速度。

senses.en: an act of making or starting sth; the number of people who do this
senses.zh: 制作某物﹙的人数﹚；开始某事﹙的人数﹚:

ex.en: There has been an increase in the uptake of these courses.
ex.zh: 听这些课的人数有所增长。

senses.en: to question sb or argue with sb about sth because you do not agree

ex.en: I thought he was wrong but I didn’t take him up on it.
ex.zh: 我认为他错了，但我没有和他澄清。

ex.en: I’d like to take you up on what you said about unemployment.
ex.zh: 我想就你对失业问题发表的谈话提几个问题。

senses.en: to become friendly with sb; to start a relationship with sb, especially sb who might have a bad influence on you
senses.zh: 开始结交﹙尤指会产生坏影响的人﹚:

ex.en: I heard Tom has taken up with a supermodel!
ex.zh: 我听说汤姆傍上了个超级模特儿！

ex.en: She’s taken up with a bunch of losers (= people who will never be successful).
ex.zh: 她结交了一帮碌碌无为的人。

senses.en: to be very busy with sb or with doing sth
senses.zh: 致力于；专心于；对…一心一意:

ex.en: She is very taken up with the children.
ex.zh: 她整天忙着照料孩子。

ex.en: I’ve been completely taken up with preparing for exams.
ex.zh: 我一直在全力以赴准备考试。

senses.en: to find sb/sth attractive or interesting

ex.en: We were all very taken with Zoe.
ex.zh: 我们都觉得佐伊非常讨人喜欢。

senses.en: to talk in a general way about a subject or a problem without discussing the difficult or important parts of it
senses.zh: 拐弯抹角地谈；不着边际地谈:

ex.en: We talked around the subject for some time before coming to the real issue.
ex.zh: 我们围绕这个主题闲扯了一会之后才进入正题。

senses.en: to speak to sb without listening to what they say in reply
senses.zh: 对…大发议论；滔滔不绝地对…说:

ex.en: My father always listened to our point of view — he never just talked at us.
ex.zh: 我父亲总是听取我们的观点——他从不搞一言堂。

senses.en: to talk without stopping for a period of time

ex.en: They were soon talking away to each other as if they’d known each other for years.
ex.zh: 他们很快就像老相识一般聊个没完。

senses.en: to reply rudely to sb in authority﹙

ex.en: She was sent out for talking back to the teacher.
ex.zh: 她因为顶撞老师而被赶了出去。

senses.en: [U] (, ) a rude reply or comment

ex.en: I said no, and don’t give me any more back talk.
ex.zh: 我说过不行， 不要再顶嘴了。

senses.en: to talk to sb who is threatening to kill themselves and persuade them not to jump from a tall building, a bridge, etc.

ex.en: The police were trying to talk down a youth threatening to jump from the roof of the car park.
ex.zh: 警察正通过谈话制止一名要从停车场顶跳下的青年。

senses.en: to prevent sb from speaking by talking loudly or without stopping
senses.zh: 以高声﹙或连续﹚讲话盖过﹙某人的话﹚；不让…插话:

ex.en: I tried to argue but they talked me down.
ex.zh: 我想争辩，可他们不给我说话的机会。

senses.en: to help a pilot bring a plane to the ground by giving detailed instructions from the ground

ex.en: The pilots were talked down through the fog by the Ground Controllers.
ex.zh: 地面导航人员引导飞行员穿过雾霭降落。

ex.en: to talk a plane down
ex.zh: 引导飞机降落

senses.en: to persuade sb to lower their prices

ex.en: He’s asked for $1 000. Can we talk him down any further?
ex.zh: 他要1 000 元。咱们能不能和他再压压价？

senses.en: to talk about sth in a way that makes it seem less important or successful than it really is

ex.en: The opposition was attacked for talking the country down.
ex.zh: 反对派因贬损国家而遭到抨击。

ex.en: He tends to talk his achievements down.
ex.zh: 他常常贬低自己的成绩。

senses.en: to speak to sb as if they are younger or less intelligent than you or than they really are
senses.zh: 以高人一等﹙或不尊重﹚的口气说话:

ex.en: He makes the mistake of talking down to his students.
ex.zh: 他不该以高高在上的态度跟学生说话。

senses.en: to persuade sb/yourself to do/not to do sth
senses.zh: 说服别人﹙或自己﹚做/不做某事:

ex.en: Why did you let James talk you into this crazy scheme?
ex.zh: 你为什么听信了詹姆斯作出此等荒唐的计划？

ex.en: I talked myself into believing I was happy.
ex.zh: 我让自己相信自己身在福中。

senses.en: to make excuses and give reasons for not doing sth;to manage to get yourself out of a difficult situation
senses.zh: 找藉口﹙或理由﹚不做某事；以话解围:

ex.en: I managed to talk my way out of having to give a speech.
ex.zh: 我设法逃避了讲话。

ex.en: His wife’s found out about everything! I’d like to see him talk his way out of this one!
ex.zh: 他的妻子什么都知道了！我倒想看看他怎么逃过这次！

senses.en: to discuss sth thoroughly until you find a solution, an agreement, etc. or make a decision
senses.zh: 把…谈透；协商做出决定﹙或解决问题、达成协议等﹚ :

ex.en: to talk out your thoughts/ feelings/problems with sb
ex.zh: 对某人说出想法/倾吐感情；与某人协商解决问题

ex.en: It might help to talk things out.
ex.zh: 把事情好好谈谈也许有助益。

senses.en: to talk until you have nothing left to say

ex.en: They spent all the evening discussing the problem until they talked themselves out.
ex.zh: 他们用了一晚上尽情讨论这个问题。

senses.en: to discuss sth thoroughly with sb in order to find a solution, make a decision,etc.
senses.zh: 详细讨论，详谈﹙以解决问题或做出决定等﹚ :

ex.en: I need to talk it over with my parents.
ex.zh: 我得和父母好好商量。

ex.en: You’ll find it helpful to talk things over with a friend.
ex.zh: 把情况和朋友畅谈，你会觉得大有帮助。

senses.en: to persuade sb to accept sth or to agree to sth

ex.en: My parents didn’t want me to go to study in Britain, but I managed to talk them round ().
ex.zh: 我父母不想让我去英国学习，但我总算说服了他们。

senses.en: to explain sth to sb in detail so that they understand it

ex.en: The technical support staff will talk you through any difficulties you have with the software.
ex.zh: 技术支持人员将给你详细讲解使用软件时遇到的困难。

ex.en: I can talk you through the application form.
ex.zh: 我可以详细告诉你如何填写申请表。

senses.en: to speak to sb seriously, especially about sth wrong that they have done, or sth that they have not done

ex.en: I’d like to talk to you in my office now.
ex.zh: 我想现在请你来我的办公室好好谈谈。

senses.en: [sing.] () a serious talk with sb who has done sth wrong

ex.en: to give sb a good talking-to
ex.zh: 狠狠责骂某人一通

senses.en: to praise sb/sth in order to make other people interested in them/it; to describe sb/sth in a way that makes them sound better or more successful than they really are
senses.zh: 过分夸奖；吹捧； 炒作:

ex.en: They talked up the tourist attractions to encourage more visitors.
ex.zh: 他们对这些旅游胜地大肆炒作以吸引更多游客。

ex.en: He was being talked up as a future presidential candidate.
ex.zh: 他被吹捧成未来的总统候选人。

senses.en: to do something to sth to change it without permission
senses.zh: 篡改；擅自改动；胡乱摆弄:

ex.en: Two policemen were accused of tampering with the evidence.
ex.zh: 有两名警察被控篡改证据。

senses.en: to twist sth into an untidy mass; to become twisted in this way

ex.en: My long skirt got tangled up in the wheel of my bike.
ex.zh: 我的长裙缠进了自行车轮子里。

ex.en: () Kurt didn’t want to get tangled up with a girl while he was trying to study.
ex.zh: 库尔特不想在求学期间和女孩子谈恋爱。

senses.en: to become involved in an argument or a fight with sb

ex.en: You’ve chosen the wrong man to tangle with.
ex.zh: 你吵架找错人了。

senses.en: to fill a vehicle with fuel

ex.en: We’d better tank up before we get on the thruway.
ex.zh: 上直达高速公路前我们最好加满油。

senses.en: to drink a lot of alcohol

ex.en: The lads had spent all evening tanking up on scotch.
ex.zh: 小伙子们整晚都在狂饮苏格兰威士忌。

senses.en: very drunk
senses.zh: 喝得烂醉的；烂醉如泥的:

ex.en: She got totally tanked up and couldn’t drive home.
ex.zh: 她喝得酩酊大醉，没法开车回家。

senses.en: , ) to persuade sb to give you sth, especially money

ex.en: Can’t you tap your father for a loan?
ex.zh: 你不能找你父亲借钱吗？

ex.en: to tap sb for information
ex.zh: 向某人索取资料

senses.en: , ) to choose sb for a particular role or job

ex.en: A British actress has been tapped for a part in the movie.
ex.zh: 已挑选一名英国女演员参与这部电影的演出。

senses.en: to put information, numbers,letters, etc. into a machine by pressing buttons
senses.zh: 输入，输出﹙信息、数字、字母等﹚:

ex.en: Tap in your password.
ex.zh: 请输入密码。

ex.en: I picked up the phone and tapped out Joe’s number.
ex.zh: 我抓起电话拨了乔的号码。

senses.en: to use a computer to obtain information from another computer﹙

ex.en: He had managed to tap into the company’s database.
ex.zh: 他设法进入了公司的数据库。

senses.en: to use sth from a supply of energy, knowledge,etc. for your own advantage

ex.en: Schools should tap into the knowledge and experience of people in the local community.
ex.zh: 学校应该利用当地社区的人们的知识和经验。

ex.en: His talk about bullying tapped into parents’ anxieties.
ex.zh: 他的关于霸道行为的讲话是利用了父母的担忧。

senses.en: to hit a surface lightly, making a rhythm

ex.en: He tapped out the rhythm with his foot.
ex.zh: 他用脚轻轻打着节拍。

senses.en: 2=TAP STH IN/OUT
to fasten tape around sth firmly

ex.en: Put it in a box and tape it up securely.
ex.zh: 把它装进盒子捆扎牢固。

senses.en: to gradually become smaller in size,volume, amount, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 规模、体积、数量等﹚逐渐减少:

ex.en: Our profits have begun to taper off.
ex.zh: 我们的利润开始逐步减少了。

senses.en: to decorate or improve the appearance of sth, often in a way that other people do not think is attractive
senses.zh: 把…装饰得俗气；把…弄得花里胡哨:

ex.en: They’ve tarted up the restaurant but the food hasn’t improved.
ex.zh: 他们把餐馆整得花里胡哨，然而食物却没有改进。

senses.en: to give sb a task to do

ex.en: forces tasked with keeping the peace
ex.zh: 执行维和任务的部队

senses.en: to accuse sb of doing sth wrong﹙

ex.en: Critics taxed the government with not acting quickly enough.
ex.zh: 评论家指责政府行动不够迅速。

senses.en: to work together with another person or group in order to do sth﹙

ex.en: The two companies have teamed up to produce new software.
ex.zh: 两家公司联手生产新软件。

ex.en: We’ve teamed up with XL Records to give away 25 pairs of tickets for the live concert.
ex.zh: 我们和唱片合作，送出25套现场音乐会双人门票。

senses.en: to make sb/yourself suffer very much or feel very unhappy
senses.zh: 使别人﹙或自己﹚痛苦，使难过:

ex.en: Being separated from the children was tearing her apart.
ex.zh: 与子女分离令她痛不欲生。

ex.en: Don’t tear yourself apart thinking about the past.
ex.zh: 别想过去的事了，那只会使自己难受。

senses.en: ( ,tear itself, themselves, etc. a'part) to separate people in a family,an organization, a country, etc. and make them argue with or fight against each other
senses.zh: 使四分五裂；使分崩离析:

ex.en: The civil war is tearing the country apart.
ex.zh: 内战把这个国家搞得四分五裂。

ex.en: The family was torn apart by conflicting loyalties.
ex.zh: 这个家庭因家人政见不和而破裂。

senses.en: to destroy or defeat sb/sth; to criticize sb/sth severely
senses.zh: 摧毁； 打败； 严厉抨击:

ex.en: We tore the other team apart in the second half.
ex.zh: 我们在下半场把对方打得片甲不留。

ex.en: You can’t write that — you’ll be torn apart.
ex.zh: 你不能写那个─他们会毁了你。

senses.en: to destroy sth by pulling it violently so that it breaks into pieces

ex.en: The dogs tore the fox apart.
ex.zh: 几条狗把那只狐狸撕成了碎片。

senses.en: to destroy a building, etc.

ex.en: Hundreds of homes were torn apart by the hurricane.
ex.zh: 飓风毁掉了几百所住房。

ex.en: The police tore the room apart looking for drugs.
ex.zh: 警察为了寻找毒品把房间翻了个底朝天。

senses.en: to attack sth violently, especially by pulling pieces off it﹙

ex.en: The brambles tore at her legs.
ex.zh: 荆棘挂破了她的腿。

ex.en: He tore at the meat with his bare hands.
ex.zh: 他乾脆用手把肉撕开。

senses.en: to make sb/yourself stop doing sth they/you enjoy in order to do sth else﹙
senses.zh: 使﹚依依不捨地停止；﹙使﹚忍痛离去:

ex.en: I can’t tear myself away from this book.
ex.zh: 我对这本书简直爱不释手。

ex.en: Come and visit us, if you can tear Bill away from his computer!
ex.zh: 你要是能说服比尔离开电脑，就来看看我们吧！

senses.en: () a young person who behaves in a wild way or who is not responsible or reliable
senses.zh: 放荡不羁的年轻人；无责任心﹙或不可靠﹚的年轻人:

ex.en: Her son’s a bit of a tearaway.
ex.zh: 她儿子有点鲁莽。

ex.en: The 11-year-old tearaway had burgled several houses.
ex.zh: 那个11 岁的小阿飞已经盗窃了几家了。

senses.en: to pull sth violently from the thing it is attached to

ex.en: The floods had torn away the base of the bridge.
ex.zh: 洪水把桥墩冲走了。

senses.en: to have to make a very difficult choice between two things, people,etc.﹙
senses.zh: 在两者间﹚难以选择，左右为难:

ex.en: I was torn between my parents and my friend.
ex.zh: 我在父母和朋友之间左右为难。

ex.en: Jenni was torn between staying at school or going to music college.
ex.zh: 珍妮在继续留在学校和去音乐学院之间难以取捨。

senses.en: to pull or knock down a building,a wall, etc.
senses.zh: 拆毁， 拆除﹙ 建筑物、墙等﹚ :

ex.en: They’re tearing down some old houses to build a new office block.
ex.zh: 他们正在拆除旧房，以建造新的办公楼。

senses.en: to attack sb/sth physically or with words

ex.en: He tore into Jed with his fists.
ex.zh: 他给了杰德几拳。

ex.en: She tore into the students if they were late.
ex.zh: 学生要是迟到，她就训斥他们。

senses.en: to remove sth quickly by pulling violently﹙

ex.en: Alice tore off her ring and threw it on the ground.
ex.zh: 爱丽丝一把摘下戒指摔到了地上。

ex.en: The door was nearly torn off its hinges.
ex.zh: 门几乎要从铰链上被拽掉了。

senses.en: to speak angrily to sb you think has done sth wrong

ex.en: The boss tore him off a strip.
ex.zh: 老板把他痛骂了一通。

senses.en: to separate sth from sth it is attached to, especially with your hands﹙

ex.en: Several pages had been torn out of the book.
ex.zh: 这本书有几页给撕掉了。

senses.en: to show that you are very angry or very worried about sth

ex.en: I was tearing my hair out trying to work out what to do.
ex.zh: 我为了想清楚该干什么而大伤脑筋。

senses.en: to destroy a piece of paper, a letter,etc. by pulling it into pieces

ex.en: She tore up all the letters he had sent her.
ex.zh: 她把他寄来的信都撕了。

ex.en: () The union accused the management of tearing up (=ignoring) the agreement.
ex.zh: 工会谴责资方破坏协议。

senses.en: to try to find some information or the meaning of sth when this is hidden or not clear﹙
senses.zh: 从…中﹚找出；深入研究；梳理清楚:

ex.en: teasing out meanings from texts
ex.zh: 弄清楚课文的含义

ex.en: to tease information/the truth out of somebody
ex.zh: 从某人处打探消息/实情

senses.en: to start a game of golf by hitting the ball for the first time﹙
senses.zh: 高尔夫球比赛﹚开赛，发球， 开球:

ex.en: The players eventually teed off two hours late.
ex.zh: 推迟两个小时之后，运动员终于开球了。

senses.en: (, ) annoyed or angry

ex.en: Her friend was teed off about what she said.
ex.zh: 她的话把她朋友激怒了。

senses.en: to rain hard

ex.en: It was absolutely teeming down.
ex.zh: 大雨真是滂沱而下。

senses.zh: (通常用于进行时) to have large numbers of people or things moving around充满，遍布，到处都是﹙移动着的人、事物等﹚ :

ex.en: cities teeming with life/people
ex.zh: 充满生机/人流如潮的城市

ex.en: The lake was teeming with fish.
ex.zh: 湖里的鱼穿梭游弋。

senses.en: , ) to be a serious disadvantage to sb

ex.en: Her lack of experience told against her.
ex.zh: 她缺乏经验对她十分不利。

senses.en: to be able to distinguish sb/sth from other similar people or things

ex.en: I can never tell the twins apart.
ex.zh: 我从来分不清这对双胞胎。

senses.en: to distinguish sb/sth from another person or thing

ex.en: It needs skill to tell a real diamond from a fake.
ex.zh: 识别真假钻石需要技巧。

ex.en: Can you tell Tom from his twin brother?
ex.zh: 你能分得出汤姆和他的孪生弟弟吗？

senses.en: ( or ) to make sth known; to give an account of sth

ex.en: The report told of a series of design errors.
ex.zh: 这份报告公布了一系列设计上的错误。

ex.en: The story tells of the love between a prince and a young girl.
ex.zh: 故事讲的是王子和一个姑娘之间的爱情。

senses.en: to speak angrily to sb, especially a child, because they have done sth wrong
senses.zh: 责备，斥责，责骂，数落﹙尤指儿童﹚:

ex.en: I told the boys off for making so much noise.
ex.zh: 孩子们太吵，我把他们训斥了一顿。

ex.en: You’ll get told off if you’re caught doing that.
ex.zh: 你做那事要是被抓住了就要挨骂。

senses.en: [C, usually sing.] (, ) an act of speaking angrily to sb, especially a child, because they have done sth wrong﹙
senses.zh: 尤指对儿童的﹚责备，责骂， 数落， 嗔怪:

ex.en: You’ve already had one telling-off today!
ex.zh: 你今天已经挨了一次骂了！

ex.en: How many tellings-off have you had this week?
ex.zh: 你这个星期挨了几次训？

senses.zh: (主要是儿童用语) to tell a teacher or sb in authority that sb has done sth wrong告发；打…的小报告；告…的状:

ex.en: Don’t tell on me, will you?
ex.zh: 别告我， 好吗？

senses.en: ) to have a bad effect on sb/sth

ex.en: The long wait was telling on his nerves.
ex.zh: 长久的等待让他心烦。

senses.en: to care for sb/sth, especially when there is a problem﹙
senses.zh: 尤指有问题时﹚照看，照料:

ex.en: I’ll look after the child — you tend to the mother.
ex.zh: 我来看着孩子——你照料这位母亲吧。

ex.en: The injured were already being tended to.
ex.zh: 已经有人在看护伤员了。

senses.en: ) to take a particular direction or have a particular opinion; to have a lot of a particular quality
senses.zh: 趋向； 倾向； 趋于:

ex.en: We’re tending towards the view that all students should study English.
ex.zh: 我们倾向于认为所有的学生都应该学习英语。

ex.en: His views tend towards the extreme.
ex.zh: 他的观点趋于偏激。

senses.en: to examine sb/sth to see if a particular substance, etc.is present
senses.zh: 验﹙成分等﹚；对人﹙或物﹚做……检测﹙或化验、测试等﹚:

ex.en: They are testing for oil in the area.
ex.zh: 他们正在这个地区勘探石油。

ex.en: She was tested for hepatitis.
ex.zh: 她接受过肝炎检查。

senses.en: to try to find out what qualities sb has, how they will react in a particular situation,etc.

ex.en: My new boss gave me the most difficult clients to deal with. I felt he was really testing me out to see if I would cope.
ex.zh: 新老板让我去对付那些最棘手的客户。我觉得他在考验我能否应付。

senses.en: to show or be evidence that sth is true
senses.zh: 作为某事的证明； 表明； 说明:

ex.en: Vijay’s school reports testified to his ability.
ex.zh: 维杰伊的学校成绩报告说明了他的能力。

senses.en: to become, or to let frozen food become, soft and ready to cook﹙

ex.en: He took the meat out of the freezer and left it to thaw out.
ex.zh: 他把肉从冰箱里拿出来解冻。

ex.en: to thaw out meat/fish
ex.zh: 把肉/鱼解冻

senses.en: to make a liquid less thick or strong, for example by adding water to it﹙

ex.en: The paint needs to be thinned down with water before you use it.
ex.zh: 颜料使用之前需要用水调稀。

senses.en: to become fewer in number, or less thick

ex.en: The crowd had thinned out and only a few people were left.
ex.zh: 人群渐渐散去，只剩下几个人。

ex.en: Once they were clear of the city, the traffic started to thin out.
ex.zh: 他们一出城， 来往车辆就开始减少。

senses.en: to have ideas or images in your mind; to remember sb/sth

ex.en: I can’t stop thinking about her.
ex.zh: 我没法不想她。

ex.en: All he ever thinks about is money.
ex.zh: 他满脑子都是钱。

senses.en: ( 'think of sb/sth) to consider sb/sth
senses.zh: 考虑； 顾及； 替…着想:

ex.en: It’s time you stopped being so selfish and started thinking about other people!
ex.zh: 你现在该别这么自私了，为别人想想吧！

senses.en: used to draw attention to a fact that is not obvious or has not been mentioned before
senses.zh: 如果仔细想想； 如果三思:

ex.en: It must have been terrible when you think about it.
ex.zh: 你想想看，这事一定很可怕。

senses.en: to use your mind to consider sth, such as your future plans, to try to solve problems, etc.

ex.en: I’ll think about it and let you know tomorrow.
ex.zh: 我先考虑一下， 明天再告诉你。

ex.en: She’s thinking about changing her job.
ex.zh: 她在考虑换工作。

senses.en: to think carefully before you decide to do sth
senses.zh: 认真考虑后再决定； 三思而后行:

ex.en: I’d think twice about calling him if I were you.
ex.zh: 我要是你，给他打电话之前会先考虑考虑。

senses.en: to think carefully about what might happen in the future; to plan for the future

ex.en: Even whe their children are very young, parents are thinking ahead to exams and jobs.
ex.zh: 孩子年纪还很小，父母就在想什么考试呀、工作呀，实在太早了。

ex.en: Pilots are trained to think ahead.
ex.zh: 飞行员接受预见情况的训练。

senses.en: to remember or think about sth that happened in the past

ex.en: She thought back to the day they first met.
ex.zh: 她回想起他们第一次见面的那一天。

ex.en: Thinking back, I’m sure I noticed there was something strange.
ex.zh: 回想起来，我敢说我注意到有些不寻常。

senses.en: to make your own decisions,form your own opinions, etc. without depending on other people

ex.en: You need to learn to think for yourself.
ex.zh: 你需要学会独立思考。

ex.en: Our parents always encouraged us to think for ourselves.
ex.zh: 父母总是鼓励我们自己拿主意。

senses.en: to have an image or idea of a particular person or thing in your mind

ex.en: When I said that, I wasn’t thinking of anyone in particular.
ex.zh: 我说那话时，并没有想到任何具体的人。

ex.en: He thought of how happy his parents would be to see him.
ex.zh: 他想着父母见到他会有多高兴。

senses.en: 2=THINK ABOUT SB/STH 2

ex.en: Just think of the consequences if you give up your job.
ex.zh: 想一想你放弃工作的后果吧。

senses.en: to create an idea in your imagination

ex.en: Who first thought of the idea?
ex.zh: 这是谁想出来的主意？

ex.en: Can you think of anyone who could help?
ex.zh: 你能想到有谁可以帮忙吗？

senses.en: to consider that you might do sth

ex.en: They’re thinking of moving to America.
ex.zh: 他们正在考虑移居美国。

ex.en: I did think of resigning, but I decided against it.
ex.zh: 我确实考虑过辞职，可后来决定放弃这个念头。

senses.en: to consider all the details of sth carefully, especially in order to find an answer or a solution to a problem
to consider sth carefully especially before making a decision﹙
senses.zh: 在做出决定前﹚仔细考虑，慎重思考:

ex.en: Please think over what I’ve said.
ex.zh: 请把我的话仔细思考一下。

senses.en: to consider a problem fully
senses.zh: 充分考虑；全盘考虑；想透:

ex.en: Careers advisers can help you think through your choices.
ex.zh: 职业顾问能帮你把各种选择考虑清楚。

senses.en: to create an idea, a plan,a story, etc. in your mind

ex.en: We need to think up a new name for the group.
ex.zh: 我们得给这个团体想出个新名字。

ex.en: Can’t you think up a better excuse than that?
ex.zh: 难道你就想不出一个更好的藉口﹖

senses.en: to be eager for sth; to want sth very much

ex.en: Our opponents were thirsting for revenge.
ex.zh: 我们的对手迫不及待地想还击。

senses.en: to move about in a violent, uncontrolled way

ex.en: He thrashed around in the water, gasping for breath.
ex.zh: 他在水里挣扎，急促地喘着气。

senses.en: to discuss sth thoroughly and in an open and honest way to try to find a solution
senses.zh: 彻底讨论，反复讨论﹙寻求解决方法﹚:

ex.en: He called a meeting to thrash out the problem.
ex.zh: 他召开了会议研究这个问题。

ex.en: Eventually they thrashed out an agreement.
ex.zh: 他们通过讨论最终达成了协议。

senses.en: to feel very excited at sth
senses.zh: 对… 感到非常兴奋﹙ 或激动﹚ :

ex.en: Audiences thrilled to his performance in Macbeth.
ex.zh: 观众看到他在《麦克佩斯》中的演出感到十分兴奋。

senses.en: to enjoy or be successful in a situation or condition that other people would not like
senses.zh: 在﹙某种环境等﹚中自得其乐；以﹙令人不快的事﹚ 取乐:

ex.en: He thrives on hard work.
ex.zh: 他以苦干为乐事。

ex.en: Sue and Jack seem to thrive on arguments.
ex.zh: 休和杰克似乎专爱吵架。

senses.en: to control the supply of fuel or power to an engine in order to reduce the speed of a vehicle

ex.en: The pilot got very low before he throttled back.
ex.zh: 飞行员减速之前下降得很低。

senses.en: to control the supply of fuel or power to an engine in order to increase the speed of a vehicle
to make sb/yourself move about suddenly and violently, often causing injury﹙
senses.zh: 使人﹚大力摇晃；﹙指人﹚横冲直撞:

ex.en: The passengers were thrown around in the crash.
ex.zh: 撞车时乘客给抛到不同的位置。

ex.en: The child was screaming and throwing himself around.
ex.zh: 那孩子尖叫着跑来跑去。

senses.en: to say sth, discuss sth, etc. in a general way

ex.en: You can’t just throw accusations around like that!
ex.zh: 你不能只是那样不着边际地指责！

ex.en: Let’s have an initial meeting to throw some ideas about.
ex.zh: 我们先开个会简单讨论一下某些想法吧。

senses.en: to spend time throwing sth such as a ball from one person to another, in a not very serious way
senses.zh: 随便地相互抛﹙或传球等﹚ :

ex.en: They were in the yard throwing a ball around.
ex.zh: 他们在院子里抛球玩。

senses.en: to send sth from your hand in different directions, often because you are angry﹙
senses.zh: 常因生气﹚四处扔，到处撒:

ex.en: How do you stop babies throwing their food around?
ex.zh: 怎样才能制止小孩子把食物撒得到处都是呢？

ex.en: Jeff got so angry that he started throwing furniture about.
ex.zh: 杰夫气愤得动手乱摔傢具。

senses.en: to put sth quickly to one side, often because you are angry or in a hurry﹙
senses.zh: 常因生气或匆忙﹚把……搁在一边:

ex.en: She read the letter and immediately threw it aside.
ex.zh: 她读完信便立刻把它扔到一边。

senses.en: to reject sth such as an attitude, an idea, a way of life, etc.
senses.zh: 拒绝接受﹙某种看法、想法、生活方式等﹚:

ex.en: All loyalties were thrown aside once the competition started.
ex.zh: 竞争一开始，所有的效忠义务都抛弃了。

ex.en: to throw aside sentimentality/nervousness
ex.zh: 抛开感伤/紧张的心情

senses.en: to direct sth such as a remark,a question, etc. at sb, often in an aggressive way
senses.zh: 针对某人说话﹙或提问等﹚:

ex.en: She threw a look of contempt at me.
ex.zh: 她鄙视地看了我一眼。

ex.en: to throw insults/accusations at somebody
ex.zh: 侮辱/指责他人

senses.en: to throw an object in the direction of sb/sth, trying to make it hit them
senses.zh: 向人或物掷﹙或扔﹚；以…砸向人或物:

ex.en: He threw stones at the window to try to catch their attention.
ex.zh: 他朝窗户扔石头， 想吸引他们的注意。

senses.en: to punish sb who has committed an offence very severely
()to try to solve a difficult situation or problem by spending lots of money on it rather than considering other ways of dealing with it
senses.zh: 企图靠花大钱解决问题:

ex.en: You can’t solve the problem by throwing money at it.
ex.zh: 这个问题不是靠花大钱可以解决的。

senses.en: (usually of a woman
senses.zh: 通常指女性) to be too eager to try to attract sb, because you want to have a romantic relationship with them撒娇；献媚；勾引:

ex.en: He was flattered that such an attractive woman as Nell was throwing herself at him.
ex.zh: 有内尔这样漂亮的女子向他献媚，他心里飘飘然起来。

senses.en: to rush or jump violently towards or onto sb/sth
senses.zh: 冲向﹙ 人或物﹚；向……猛扑过去:

ex.en: The dogs threw themselves at the gate.
ex.zh: 几条狗扑向大门。

senses.en: [only before noun]
to have a relationship with sb, or work for sb, who is not good enough for you or does not deserve you﹙
senses.zh: 和不相配的人﹚ 交往； 屈就:

ex.en: Don’t throw yourself away on somebody like him.
ex.zh: 不要屈尊和他这种人来往。

senses.en: to return sth with a sharp movement of your arm or wrist

ex.en: Can you throw the ball back to me?
ex.zh: 帮我把球扔回来好吗？

senses.en: to put sth quickly and carelessly in the place where it was before﹙

ex.en: Just throw those papers back in the drawer when you’ve finished with them.
ex.zh: 你用完那些文件后就放回抽屉里吧。

senses.en: [C, usually sing.] sb/sth that is very similar to sb/sth that existed a long time ago
senses.zh: 有返祖现象的人﹙或事物﹚:

ex.en: This music is a real throwback to the seventies.
ex.zh: 这音乐确实像七十年代的音乐。

senses.en: to remind sb of sth they have said or done in the past, especially to upset or annoy them﹙
senses.zh: 尤指为使人烦恼﹚使想起， 提醒， 重提:

ex.en: His unwise remark was frequently thrown back at him by his colleagues.
ex.zh: 他的同事经常重提他的蠢话。

senses.en: to refuse to listen to sb’s complaints,comments, etc.

ex.en: All our objections were thrust aside.
ex.zh: 我们所有的异议都被置之不理。

senses.en: to force sb to accept sb/sth or do sth that they do not want to
senses.zh: 把……强加于某人；强迫某人接受……；强人所难:

ex.en: Responsibility for the family was thrust upon him at an early age.
ex.zh: 他年龄不大的时候就担负起家庭的责任。

ex.en: She was annoyed at having three extra guests suddenly thrust upon her.
ex.zh: 突然又来了三位不速之客要她接待，她感到很恼火。

senses.en: to turn the pages of a book, a magazine, etc. looking at them quickly

ex.en: She thumbed through her diary.
ex.zh: 她迅速地翻阅她的日记。

senses.en: (of time
senses.zh: 时间) to pass, especially when you feel it is passing too quickly or too slowly过去，流逝﹙尤其使人感觉太快或太慢﹚:

ex.en: The seconds ticked by as I tried to think of something to say.
ex.zh: 时间一秒一秒地过去，我努力想找话说。

ex.en: Two long minutes ticked past.
ex.zh: 漫长的两分钟过去了。

senses.en: , ) to annoy sb

ex.en: This type of thing really ticks me off.
ex.zh: 这种事着实让我生气。

senses.en: (, )annoyed

ex.en: I was really ticked off about it.
ex.zh: 我对这事十分恼火。

senses.en: [sing.] (,, ) the act of speaking to somebody angrily because they have done sth wrong

ex.en: He gave me a ticking off for being late for class.
ex.zh: 他因为我上课迟到把我训斥了一通。

senses.en: to put a mark next to sth on a list to show that it has been dealt with

ex.en: Al ticked off the names of the people who had replied.
ex.zh: 阿尔在已回覆者的姓名旁打鈎。

ex.en: Everything on the list had been ticked off.
ex.zh: 单子上的东西都做了记号。

senses.en: to help sb through a difficult period by providing what they need
senses.zh: 帮助某人渡过﹙困难时期﹚；协助某人克服﹙困难﹚:

ex.en: We’ve got enough money to tide us over until next month.
ex.zh: 我们有足够的钱让我们凑合到下个月。

ex.en: Our savings should tide us over the next couple of months.
ex.zh: 我们的积蓄应该够我们挺过以后几个月。

senses.en: to put things in a particular place where they cannot be seen so that a room, etc. appears tidy

ex.en: Harry was busy tidying away his papers in the office.
ex.zh: 哈里在办公室忙着整理他的文件。

senses.en: to make a room, a cupboard,etc. tidy by removing things you do not want and arranging the rest neatly

ex.en: It’s time to tidy out the kitchen cupboards.
ex.zh: 该清理厨房里的橱柜了。

senses.en: to make a room, a group of things, etc. tidy by arranging things neatly in the correct places

ex.en: Don’t forget to tidy up when you’ve finished.
ex.zh: 你干完之后别忘了收拾好。

ex.en: The whole place needs tidying up.
ex.zh: 这个地方需要彻底整理。

senses.en: to make sb/yourself look cleaner and smarter
senses.zh: 使更整洁帅气；梳理打扮:

ex.en: How about tidying yourself up a bit before we go out?
ex.zh: 我们出去前你打扮一下好吗？

senses.en: to finish sth such as a piece of written work by dealing with the last details well or correctly
senses.zh: 修饰好，润色好﹙书面材料等﹚:

ex.en: My lecture still needs tidying up.
ex.zh: 我的讲稿还需要最后加工一下。

senses.en: to do sth so that an enemy force is kept busy and has to stay in a particular area

ex.en: Guerrilla activity kept the army tied down in the mountains.
ex.zh: 游击队的活动把军队牵制在了山区。

senses.en: to become or to make sth tight or tighter﹙

ex.en: His face muscles tightened up in anger.
ex.zh: 他生气地紧绷着脸。

ex.en: to tighten up a screw/ wheel/muscle
ex.zh: 拧紧螺丝；上紧轮子；绷紧肌肉

senses.en: to make small changes to sth in order to repair or improve it, especially in a way that may not be helpful﹙
senses.zh: 尤指不起作用地﹚修修补补，小修理:

ex.en: He’s outside tinkering around with his bike.
ex.zh: 他在外面捣鼓他的自行车。

ex.en: They haven’t made any real changes to the system — they’ve just been tinkering around a bit.
ex.zh: 他们对系统没有做出任何真正的改进—只不过是一点修修补补。

senses.en: to give sb a warning about sth which will affect them and which they should know about, especially sth illegal
senses.zh: 暗中警告，私下告诫，密报﹙尤指非法的事情﹚:

ex.en: The police were tipped off about the bank robbery.
ex.zh: 警方获得了有关抢劫银行的密报。

senses.en: () a piece of useful or secret information that sb gives, for example to the police, to warn them about an illegal or unexpected activity

ex.en: The police received an anonymous tip-off about the attack.
ex.zh: 警方收到了有关这次攻击的匿名密报。

senses.en: to become unstable and fall over; to make sth do this﹙

ex.en: The bottle tipped over and all the water spilled out.
ex.zh: 瓶子倒了，水全洒了。

ex.en: Watch you don’t tip the jug over.
ex.zh: 小心点，别把罐子打翻。

senses.en: to become unsteady and fall forwards, backwards or sideways; to make sth do this﹙

ex.en: One after another the canoes tipped up.
ex.zh: 独木舟一艘接一艘地翻了。

ex.en: The pile of books on the end of the table nearly tipped it up.
ex.zh: 桌子一头的一摞书几乎把桌子压翻。

senses.en: to change the angle of sth so that it leans to one side

ex.en: She tipped her glass up and drained it.
ex.zh: 她倾斜玻璃杯把水倒掉。

ex.en: He tipped his face up towards the light.
ex.zh: 他朝灯光侧过脸。

senses.en: to become bored with sb/sth or begin to enjoy them/it less

ex.en: They soon tired of the beach and went for a walk.
ex.zh: 他们很快对海滩腻烦了，便去散步。

senses.en: to do sth a lot, especially in a way that annoys people

ex.en: Jack travelled all over the world when he was a student, as he never tires of telling us.
ex.zh: 杰克在学生时代就周游世界，他总是不厌其烦地跟我们说这事。

senses.en: to make sb/yourself feel very tired
senses.zh: 使别人﹙或自己﹚筋疲力尽；感疲惫不堪:

ex.en: I took the children to the beach to tire them out.
ex.zh: 我把孩子们带到海滩去让他们玩得筋疲力尽。

ex.en: Try not to tire yourself out too soon in the race.
ex.zh: 赛跑时尽量不要过早地把力气用光。

senses.en: very tired
senses.zh: 筋疲力尽的；疲乏不堪的:

ex.en: We finally reached home tired out.
ex.zh: 我们终于回到家了，疲惫不堪。

senses.en: to leave; to depart

ex.en: It’s late — it’s time you toddled off to bed.
ex.zh: 不早了—你该去睡觉了。

senses.en: to be wearing clothes for a particular activity or occasion
senses.zh: 穿着﹙适合某场合﹚的服装；专门穿戴:

ex.en: He got togged up in a suit and tie for the interview.
ex.zh: 他穿着西装打着领带去参加面试。

ex.en: We were all togged out in our best clothes.
ex.zh: 我们都穿上了最漂亮的衣服。

senses.en: to work extremely hard at sth difficult or boring
senses.zh: 辛勤地做﹙ 困难或乏味的事﹚ :

ex.en: He toiled away at his homework all the evening.
ex.zh: 他一晚上都在费力地做作业。

senses.en: to make sth such as a speech, an opinion, etc. less offensive, critical or harsh than it was originally
senses.zh: 使﹙讲话、意见等﹚缓和；使温和:

ex.en: He had to tone down his article before it was published.
ex.zh: 他得在文章发表之前把措辞缓和一下。

senses.en: to make sth, especially your clothes, less bright, colourful and noticeable
senses.zh: 使﹙衣服等﹚暗淡些；使不太艳丽；使不太扎眼:

ex.en: She toned down her style of dress when she started her new job.
ex.zh: 她开始新工作时穿得庄重了些。

senses.en: to make a colour less bright

ex.en: We toned down the yellow paint with a little white.
ex.zh: 我们掺了一点白色使黄漆显得柔和些。

ex.en: Petra used powder to tone down her rosy cheeks.
ex.zh: 佩特拉在红红的面颊上搽了些粉遮盖一下。

senses.en: to match or fit with the colour or style of sth else﹙

ex.en: The cushions tone in well with the carpet.
ex.zh: 那些埝子和地毯的颜色很协调。

ex.en: The new bridge doesn’t tone in with the buildings around it.
ex.zh: 新桥和周围的建筑物不谐调。

senses.en: to make your muscles or a part of your body firmer, stronger, and healthier
senses.zh: 使﹙肌肉或身体﹚更结实；使更强壮；使更健康:

ex.en: It’s time I toned up and slimmed down.
ex.zh: 我应该练得健美些了。

ex.en: This exercise will tone up your stomach muscles.
ex.zh: 这项运动有助于增强你的腹肌。

senses.en: to get or provide sb/sth with the equipment,machines, etc. necessary to do or produce sth
senses.zh: 获得﹙或提供﹚必要的设备；给……配置装备:

ex.en: It took several months to tool up to produce the new model.
ex.zh: 配置生产新型产品的设备用了几个月的时间。

ex.en: A new plant in Scotland is being tooled up to produce these screws.
ex.zh: 苏格兰的一家新工厂正在装置生产这些螺钉的设备。

senses.en: having the equipment necessary for a particular job﹙
senses.zh: 做某工作﹚设备齐全的；全套装备的

senses.en: ) carrying a gun
to complete sth in a successful or pleasant way, especially by adding one final thing

ex.en: Jane was wearing a very colourful outfit, topped off with a dramatic hat.
ex.zh: 简身穿鲜艳的套服，再加上引人注目的帽子，十分好看。

senses.en: to stop increasing after reaching a high level

ex.en: Your annual salary will top out at seventy thousand dollars.
ex.zh: 你的年薪最高是七万元。

senses.en: to fill sb’s glass or cup by adding some more liquid
senses.zh: 给某人的杯子斟满﹙饮料﹚；满上某人的杯:

ex.en: Can I top you up?
ex.zh: 给你把杯子加满好吗？

senses.en: an amount of liquid that you add to some already in a glass, cup or other container﹙

ex.en: Can I give you a top-up?
ex.zh: 给你把杯子加满好吗？

senses.en: a card that you buy for a mobile phone that enables you to make calls to the value of the card
senses.zh: 移动电话卡；手机储值卡

senses.en: to become unsteady and fall over

ex.en: The vase wobbled and then toppled over.
ex.zh: 花瓶摇晃了几下就倒了。

senses.en: to put sth quickly to one side because you are angry or in a hurry﹙
senses.zh: 因生气或匆忙﹚把……扔﹙或丢﹚到一边:

ex.en: He tossed aside the newspaper angrily and stood up.
ex.zh: 他生气地把报纸往旁边一扔，站了起来。

ex.en: ( ) When he’s bored with people he just tosses them aside.
ex.zh: 他要是对别人感到厌烦了就置之不理。

senses.en: to reject sth such as an attitude, an idea, a way of life, etc.
senses.zh: 拒绝接受， 摒弃， 排除﹙ 态度、想法、生活方式等﹚:

ex.en: The idea of buying a new car was quickly tossed aside.
ex.zh: 买新车的想法很快就被抛到一边。

senses.en: to throw sth away carelessly

ex.en: She finished her drink and tossed the can away.
ex.zh: 她喝完饮料就随手把罐子扔了。

ex.en: () He’s tossed away so many opportunities.
ex.zh: 他丢失了这么多机会。

senses.en: to make a decision about sth by spinning a coin in the air and seeing which side is on top when it lands﹙

ex.en: We can’t both go, so why don’t we toss for it?
ex.zh: 既然咱俩不能都去，为什么不掷硬币决定谁去呢？

ex.en: There’s only one ticket left — I’ll toss you for it.
ex.zh: 只剩一张票—我要和你掷硬币决定给谁。

senses.en: (, !, ) to give yourself sexual pleasure by rubbing your sex organs; to give sb else sexual pleasure in this way
to do sth quickly,easily and often with little care or effort﹙
senses.zh: 不加审慎或不费力﹚很快做好:

ex.en: He tossed this novel off in two months.
ex.zh: 他用了两个月就把小说匆匆写完了。

senses.en: [sing.] () a situation where it is difficult to decide between two things, or where there are two possible results
senses.zh: 两难的局面；难以取捨的事；机会均等的事:

ex.en: It was a tossup between spending the night in the van and walking ten miles for help.
ex.zh: 在客货车里睡一晚还是走上十英里求援，当时实在是进退两难。

senses.en: to add together several numbers or amounts in order to get a total

ex.en: Can you tot up how much I owe you?
ex.zh: 你能算一下我总共欠你多少钱吗？

senses.en: to reach a particular total

ex.en: The costs total up to over a million.
ex.zh: 费用总计超过一百万。

senses.en: (of a plane, a spacecraft, etc.
senses.zh: 飞机、航天器等) to land着陆；降落:

ex.en: The plane touched down safely at Kennedy Airport at about midday.
ex.zh: 飞机中午时分安全降落在肯尼迪机场。

ex.en: () A tornado touched down in Colorado, injuring five people.
ex.zh: 龙卷风在科罗拉多登陆，导致五人受伤。

senses.en: the moment when a plane or a spacecraft lands﹙
senses.zh: 飞机或宇宙飞船的﹚着陆，降落， 接地

senses.en: (in rugby
senses.zh: 橄榄球) an act of scoring points by putting the ball down on the area of ground behind the other team’s goal line﹙在对方球门线后的﹚持球触地

senses.en: (in American football
senses.zh: 美式足球) an act of scoring points by crossing the other team’s goal line while carrying the ball, or receiving the ball when you are over the other team’s goal line持球越过对方球门线；在对方球门线上接球

senses.en: to persuade sb to give or lend you money

ex.en: He tried to touch me for twenty pounds.
ex.zh: 他想向我要二十英镑。

senses.en: to make sth begin, especially an explosion or a violent or difficult situation
senses.zh: 触发，引发，引起﹙爆炸、暴力或困难的局面﹚:

ex.en: The explosion was touched off by a single spark.
ex.zh: 爆炸是由一个火星引起的。

ex.en: His arrest touched off a riot.
ex.zh: 他被逮捕触发了一场暴乱。

senses.en: to mention or deal briefly with a topic, a problem, etc.

ex.en: He touched on the need for increased funding.
ex.zh: 他提到有必要增加资金。

ex.en: Some of these issues were touched on in Chapter 7.
ex.zh: 这些问题有的在第7章涉及过。

senses.en: to touch sb in an unpleasant sexual way﹙
to stay firm and determined in a difficult situation
to become stronger and better able to deal with difficult situations; to make sb stronger in this way﹙

ex.en: He had toughened up during military service.
ex.zh: 他服役期间变得坚强起来。

ex.en: His parents sent him away to boarding school to toughen him up.
ex.zh: 父母把他送到寄宿学校经受锻炼。

senses.en: to make sth such as a law or a rule more strict

ex.en: The legislation on this trade needs to be toughened up.
ex.zh: 这一行业的法规需要加强。

senses.en: to take sth to many different places or companies in the hope of selling it

ex.en: He’s been touting his novel around publishers for years.
ex.zh: 他几年来一直到处找出版商兜售自己的小说。

senses.en: to try to get business,work, etc. by asking people directly

ex.en: cab drivers touting for business at the airport
ex.zh: 在机场拉客的出租车司机

senses.en: to remove sth, especially a vehicle, from a place, by pulling it behind another one
senses.zh: 拖走，拉走，拽走﹙尤指车辆﹚:

ex.en: They’ll tow your car away if you park it here.
ex.zh: 你要是在这里停放汽车，人家就会把它拖走。

senses.en: to be much higher or taller than other things or people that are near
senses.zh: 高于，超过﹙附近的人或物﹚:

ex.en: The new offices tower above the rest of the town.
ex.zh: 新的办公楼耸立于城中。

ex.en: Amy towers over her mother.
ex.zh: 埃米比母亲高出了一大截。

senses.en: to be much better, more famous, etc. than other people or things
senses.zh: 比﹙其他人或事物﹚优越；胜过……:

ex.en: He towers above all other poets of his generation.
ex.zh: 他在同时代的诗人中卓然独立。

senses.en: to play with sth; to move sth around carelessly without really thinking about it

ex.en: Stop toying with your food!
ex.zh: 别瞎拨弄食物！

ex.en: () He accused the young man of toying with his daughter’s affections.
ex.zh: 他指责那个年轻人玩弄他女儿的感情。

senses.en: to find the origin or cause of sth by following clues or evidence backwards from the present time
senses.zh: 探究事物的本源；追溯﹙到…﹚:

ex.en: Many different childhood illnesses can be traced back to certain foods.
ex.zh: 多种儿童疾病的起因都可追溯到某些食物。

ex.en: Boston has a large population that traces its roots back to Ireland.
ex.zh: 波士顿拥有一大批祖先在爱尔兰的人。

senses.en: to draw a shape or a mark clearly

ex.en: I traced out our route on the map.
ex.zh: 我在地图上描出我们的路线。

ex.en: ( )She traced out how working patterns had changed in the last 50 years.
ex.zh: 她描绘了过去50 年中工作模式的变化情况。

senses.en: to find sb/sth after a long and difficult search﹙
senses.zh: 到某处﹚搜寻，追踪，追查﹙某人或物﹚:

ex.en: We finally tracked Sam down to his parents’ house.
ex.zh: 我们终于在萨姆父母的房子中找到了萨姆。

ex.en: It has taken ten years to track down the wreckage of the plane.
ex.zh: 用了十年时间才搜寻到飞机的残骸。

senses.en: to spend less money on things than you used to

ex.en: People are trading down and buying cheaper food.
ex.zh: 人们都降低消费，购买廉价食物。

senses.en: to sell sth large or expensive and buy sth smaller or less expensive
senses.zh: 卖好买次；卖大的买小的，卖高价的买低价的﹙…﹚:

ex.en: They traded down to a house with fewer bedrooms.
ex.zh: 他们卖掉房子，买了座少几间卧室的。

senses.en: to give sth that you have used to sb you are buying sth new from as part of your payment
senses.zh: 以旧物折价﹙换新物﹚；折价贴换﹙…﹚:

ex.en: He traded his motorbike in for a new van.
ex.zh: 他把摩托车折价添钱买了辆新客货车。

senses.en: a method of buying something by giving a used item as part of the payment for a new one; the used item that you give
senses.zh: 折价贴换；以旧折价换新；折价旧物:

ex.en: the trade-in value of a car
ex.zh: 一辆汽车的折价价值

ex.en: Do you have a tradein?
ex.zh: 你有折价的旧东西吗？

senses.en: to balance two things or situations that are opposed to each other
senses.zh: 权衡； 平衡； 使协调:

ex.en: The government were attempting to trade off inflation against unemployment.
ex.zh: 政府正力求在通货膨胀和失业之间取得平衡。

ex.en: They were willing to trade off information to keep the hostages alive (= to give information in exchange for their lives).
ex.zh: 他们愿意交出信息以换取人质的性命。

senses.en: the act of balancing two things that you need or want but which are opposed to each other﹙
senses.zh: 在需要而又相互对立的两者间的﹚权衡，协调:

ex.en: a trade-off between inflation and unemployment
ex.zh: 通货膨胀和失业之间的平衡

ex.en: There is a trade-off between the benefits of the drug and the risk of side effects.
ex.zh: 这种药既有好处又有产生副作用的危险。

senses.en: to unfairly make use of sth for your own advantage

ex.en: He traded on his father’s name to get himself a job.
ex.zh: 他利用他父亲的名义为自己弄到了份工作。

senses.en: to sell sth small or not expensive in order to buy sth larger or more expensive
senses.zh: 卖次买好；卖小的买大的，卖低价的买高价的﹙……﹚ :

ex.en: He traded up to a larger car.
ex.zh: 他卖掉汽车，买了辆较大的。

senses.en: to buy and sell sth, especially drugs or weapons, illegally﹙

ex.en: He was accused of trafficking in stolen works of art.
ex.zh: 他被控买卖盗窃艺术品。

senses.en: to point sth such as a gun, a camera, a light, etc. at sb/sth
senses.zh: 把﹙枪口、照相机、灯光等﹚瞄准，对准:

ex.en: The police marksmen trained their weapons on the building.
ex.zh: 警方的射手用武器瞄准那座楼房。

ex.en: She trained the camera on the bride and groom.
ex.zh: 她把照相机对准了新娘和新郎。

senses.en: to make sb ready to do a job or an activity by teaching them the skills they need

ex.en: We need to train up extra staff for the Christmas period.
ex.zh: 我们得培训额外的职员，以应付圣诞节期间的需要。

senses.en: to walk from place to place slowly because you are tired and unwilling
senses.zh: 疲惫地走；拖沓地行走；磨蹭:

ex.en: I’ve been traipsing around all day with Jenny trying to buy a coat for her.
ex.zh: 我一整天都疲乏地陪着珍妮四处转悠，想给她买件大衣。

ex.en: We spent the afternoon traipsing around the town.
ex.zh: 我们拖着疲惫的身子在城里转了一下午。

senses.en: to ignore sb’s feelings or rights and treat them as if they are not important

ex.en: The government is trampling on the views of ordinary people.
ex.zh: 政府在践踏民意。

senses.en: to entertain sb with sth special

ex.en: Visitors will be treated to a spectacular show.
ex.zh: 届时会让参观者看一场精彩的演出。

ex.en: () We were treated to (= we had to suffer) a two-hour lecture.
ex.zh: 我们接受了两小时的讲座。

senses.en: to manage to get sb to do sth by deceiving them or not telling them the truth

ex.en: She felt she’d been tricked into marriage.
ex.zh: 她觉得自己结婚是被人骗了。

ex.en: He tricked me into lending him ￡100.
ex.zh: 他骗我借给了他100 英镑。

senses.en: to take sth away from sb by deceiving them

ex.en: An 80-year old woman was tricked out of her life savings.
ex.zh: 一位80 岁老妇一生的积蓄被骗走了。

senses.en: (especially of money
senses.zh: 尤指钱) to spread from rich to poor people through the economic system of a country﹙ 经国家经济体制﹚由富人向贫者滴流:

ex.en: If the wealthy pay less tax, the benefits should trickle down to people on lower incomes.
ex.zh: 如果富人减少纳税，低收入者应该可以受惠。

senses.en: [U] the theory that if the richest people in society become richer this will have a good effect on poorer people as well, for example by creating more jobs
senses.zh: 滴入论，垂滴论﹙富者愈富应能惠及贫者﹚
尤用于否定句) to treat sb/sth without respect as if they are not very important怠慢；小看；轻视﹙人或事物﹚:

ex.en: He is not a man to be trifled with.
ex.zh: 他这个人怠慢不得。

ex.en: He was a man who trifled with women’s affections.
ex.zh: 他是个玩弄女性感情的人。

senses.en: to cut off a small part of sth because it is not needed
senses.zh: 切去，修剪﹙不必要的部份﹚:

ex.en: My hair is too long now. Can you trim off about two centimetres?
ex.zh: 我的头发太长了。你给我剪掉大约两公分好吗？

senses.en: to become, or to make sth, smaller in size

ex.en: He’s trimmed down from 90 kilos to 70.
ex.zh: 他的体重从90千克减到了70 千克。

ex.en: The movie was trimmed down to 21/2 hours.
ex.zh: 电影被剪辑成了两个半小时。

senses.en: to fall or almost fall because you have accidentally hit your foot against sth while you are walking or running

ex.en: I tripped over the rug and fell heavily.
ex.zh: 我给小地毯绊了一下，重重地摔倒了。

ex.en: He kept tripping over.
ex.zh: 他不断地绊倒。

senses.en: ) to fall or almost fall because you have accidentally hit your foot against sth while walking or running;to make sb fall or almost fall by catching their foot while they are walking or running﹙
senses.zh: 将某人﹚绊倒，绊趔趄；﹙使﹚跌倒:

ex.en: I tripped up as I ran across the room.
ex.zh: 我跑过房间时绊倒了。

ex.en: She tripped him up with her stick.
ex.zh: 她用拐杖把他绊了一跤。

senses.en: to make a mistake; to deliberately make sb do this﹙

ex.en: I knew I had to think carefully in the interview or I might trip up.
