ex.zh: 我知道面试时我必须思想清晰，否则就会出错。

ex.en: She was trying to trip me up with her questions.
ex.zh: 她试图把我问倒。

senses.en: to go somewhere, walking quite quickly
senses.zh: 快步走， 小跑﹙ 去某处﹚:

ex.en: She trotted off to school happily with her new lunch box.
ex.zh: 她带着新午饭盒高高兴兴地跑去学校了。

senses.en: to say or repeat sth such as an excuse, an explanation, etc.without thinking about it or being sincere about it
senses.zh: 随口说出﹙常用的託词、解释等﹚:

ex.en: The airline trotted out the same old excuses to explain the delays.
ex.zh: 航空公司又用那老一套的藉口来解释延误。

ex.en: He’s just trotting out the party line again(= in politics).
ex.zh: 他又搬出了党的路线。

senses.en: to make up a false story about sb/sth, especially accusing them of doing sth wrong

ex.en: Several of his colleagues trumped up a complaint to get him removed from the job.
ex.zh: 他的几位同事诬告他，使他丢掉了工作。

senses.en: to mention sb/sth or do sth that you have often mentioned or done before

ex.en: The government trundled out the same old clichés to justify their actions.
ex.zh: 政府搬出一堆老掉牙的理由为自己的做法辩护。

senses.en: to tie a person or an animal up very tightly so that they cannot move or escape

ex.en: The victims had been trussed up with rope and beaten.
ex.zh: 受害人被人用绳子捆绑起来进行殴打。

senses.en: to have confidence in sb/sth; to rely on sb completely
senses.zh: 相信，信任，信赖﹙人或事物﹚:

ex.en: I was scared before the operation, but I trusted in the skill of the doctors and nurses.
ex.zh: 手术之前我很害怕，但我相信医生和护士的技术。

ex.en: He urged them to trust in God.
ex.zh: 他鼓励他们相信上帝。

senses.en: to leave the result or progress of events to be decided by luck, chance, etc.,because there is nothing or no one else to help you
to give sb/sth to a person to take care of because you believe they will be careful with them/it
senses.zh: 託付；託交；把……委託给某人照管:

ex.en: Would you trust her with the children?
ex.zh: 你把孩子们交给她照看好吗？

ex.en: I’d trust him with my life.
ex.zh: 他是我可以託付终身的人。

senses.en: to telephone sb again when you have already telephoned them but have not managed to speak to them﹙

ex.en: Can you try back later?
ex.zh: 你过会儿再打过来好吗？

ex.en: She’s not there. I’ll have to try her back after lunch.
ex.zh: 她不在。我只好等午饭之后再给她打电话。

senses.en: to make an attempt to get or win sth
senses.zh: 试图获得； 力争赢得:

ex.en: Are you going to try for that job?
ex.zh: 你打算争取那份工作吗？

ex.en: They’ve been trying for a baby for several years now (= the woman has been trying to become pregnant).
ex.zh: 他们试了几年时间想怀上孩子。

senses.en: (, , ) to behave badly towards sb or try to get sth from them just to see what you can do before they become angry or stop you

ex.en: The kids sometimes try it on with a new babysitter.
ex.zh: 小孩子有时会摸摸新保姆的脾气。

senses.en: () an act of trying to behave badly and hoping that no one will stop you﹙
senses.zh: 对别人脾气的﹚摸底，探索

senses.en: to put on a piece of clothing to see if it fits and how it looks

ex.en: Can I try on the blue one?
ex.zh: 我能试试那件蓝色的吗？

ex.en: If you like it, why don’t you try it on?
ex.zh: 你如果喜欢，为什么不试穿一下呢？

senses.en: to compete for a place in a sports team, a part in a play, etc.
senses.zh: 参加﹙……的﹚选拔；参加﹙……的﹚试演:

ex.en: He tried out for the school band.
ex.zh: 他参加了学校乐队的甄选。

ex.en: It’s a pretty good team. I think I’ll try out.
ex.zh: 那个队很不错。我想我要去参加选拔。

senses.en: () a test, etc. to choose players for a team, actors for a play, etc.

ex.en: The team is holding try-outs this Thursday.
ex.zh: 这个队将于本周四进行选拔。

ex.en: Did you have a try-out for the school play?
ex.zh: 你参加学校戏剧演员甄选了吗？

senses.en: to test sb/sth to see how good and useful they are or how suitable for a particular task or purpose before you decide to use them/it

ex.en: We’ve been trying out some new musicians for our band.
ex.zh: 我们一直在为我们的乐队试用一些新乐手。

ex.en: He couldn’t wait to try out his new invention.
ex.zh: 他迫不及待地想试验一下他的新发明。

senses.en: to eat food, especially quickly or with enthusiasm
senses.zh: 痛快地吃；狼吞虎咽地吃:

ex.en: We tucked in hungrily.
ex.zh: 我们狼吞虎咽地大吃一通。

ex.en: He was tucking into a huge plateful of pasta.
ex.zh: 他在狼吞虎咽地吃一大盘通心粉。

senses.en: to cover sb, especially a child,comfortably in bed by pulling the covers around them
senses.zh: 把﹙孩子等﹚的被子掖好；给……盖好被子:

ex.en: Will you come and tuck me in, Mummy?
ex.zh: 妈妈，来给我掖掖被子好吗？

ex.en: The children were all tucked up in bed by 8 p.m.
ex.zh: 孩子们到晚上8点钟就全给掖进被窝了。

senses.en: to move or put sth in a small space, especially to hide it or keep it safe or comfortable
senses.zh: 将……收起；将……放在﹙狭小而安全或舒适的位置﹚:

ex.en: She kicked off her shoes and tucked her feet up under her.
ex.zh: 她踢掉鞋子，盘起腿。

senses.en: to give sth a quick, strong pull

ex.en: Daniel tugged at my sleeve.
ex.zh: 丹尼尔拽了拽我的衣袖。

senses.en: to fall suddenly to the ground in a dramatic way

ex.en: One push and the wall came tumbling down.
ex.zh: 那堵墙一推就倒塌了。

ex.en: Her long dark hair tumbled down around her face.
ex.zh: 她那黑油油的长发垂在她的脸庞周围。

senses.en: to fall to the ground

ex.en: She knocked the statue and it tumbled over.
ex.zh: 她碰到塑像上，塑像就翻倒了。

senses.en: to suddenly realize, understand, or become aware of what sb/sth is really like
senses.zh: 一下子了解某人﹙或事情等﹚；顿悟；突然意识到:

ex.en: I’ve tumbled to Isabel now.
ex.zh: 我现在突然明白了伊莎贝儿的为人。

ex.en: I’ve tumbled to what he is trying to do.
ex.zh: 我赫然意识到他的意图。

senses.en: to turn on the radio or television in order to listen or watch a particular programme or channel
senses.zh: 收听﹙收音机广播节目﹚；收看﹙电视节目﹚:

ex.en: We tuned in to watch the football.
ex.zh: 我们收看了足球节目。

ex.en: Tune into (= watch) next week’s exciting episode!
ex.zh: 请收看下星期激动人心的一集。

senses.en: to be aware of or understand other people’s thoughts, feelings or needs
senses.zh: 理解，体谅﹙他人的思想、感情或需要﹚:

ex.en: You must tune into the needs of the people you love.
ex.zh: 你必须体察你所爱的人的需要。

senses.en: to adjust the controls on a radio or television so that you can hear or see a particular programme or channel clearly﹙
senses.zh: 给收音机、电视﹚调谐，调频道:

ex.en: The radio isn’t properly tuned in.
ex.zh: 收音机没有调好台。

ex.en: I keep the radio tuned in to the BBC World Service.
ex.zh: 我把收音机调定在英国广播公司国际广播电台的频道。

senses.en: () to turn on the radio or television in order to listen to or watch a particular programme
senses.zh: 收听﹙收音机广播节目﹚；收看﹙电视节目﹚:

ex.en: Tune in our TV special tonight at nine.
ex.zh: 今晚九点请收看我们的特别节目。

senses.en: to be aware of or understand sth, especially other people’s feelings
senses.zh: 明白，理解，体谅﹙尤指他人的感情﹚:

ex.en: Parents should be tuned in to the needs of their child.
ex.zh: 父母应该理解孩子的需要。

ex.en: I’m tuned in to what I have to do.
ex.zh: 我明白我需要做什么。

senses.en: to stop listening to sb/sth; to ignore sb/sth
senses.zh: 不用心听；不理睬；﹙对…﹚听而不闻:

ex.en: When Lee started talking about her job, Tim just tuned out.
ex.zh: 李开始谈她的工作，蒂姆就走神了。

senses.en: to adjust the controls of a radio or television so that you can listen to or watch a particular programme
senses.zh: 把收音机﹙或电视机﹚调到﹙某频道﹚上:

ex.en: All the TVs in the store were tuned to the same channel.
ex.zh: 这店里所有的电视机都调在同一频道。

senses.en: to force sb/sth to leave a particular place or an organization
senses.zh: 把……赶出，驱逐出﹙地方、组织等﹚:

ex.en: We need to turf the Democratic party out.
ex.zh: 我们应该把民主党赶走。

ex.en: Several families have been turfed out of their homes.
ex.zh: 有几家人被逐出了家园。

senses.en: to get rid of sth you do not want
senses.zh: 丢弃，扔掉﹙不需要的东西﹚:

ex.en: The shop is full of beautiful clothes that people have turfed out.
ex.zh: 这家商店里面全是人们处理掉的漂亮衣服。

senses.en: to turn around quickly so as to face in the opposite direction
senses.zh: 急向后转；突然转身；回头:

ex.en: She turned about and went into the kitchen.
ex.zh: 她一转身进了厨房。

senses.en: an act of turning around quickly so as to face in the opposite direction
senses.zh: 向后转； 急转身； 回头:

ex.en: He did a rapid about-turn when he saw me and went back inside.
ex.zh: 他一见到我就连忙转过身回到里面。

senses.en: a complete change of opinion, plan or behaviour﹙
senses.zh: 看法、计划、态度的﹚彻底转变；改弦易辙:

ex.en: Hours later the management did an about-turn and agreed to our demands.
ex.zh: 几个小时之后，资方彻底转变了态度，同意了我们的要求。

ex.en: a dramatic about-turn in government policy
ex.zh: 政府政策的突然重大改变

senses.en: an act of turning around quickly so as to face in the opposite direction
senses.zh: 向后转； 急转身； 回头

senses.en: a sudden and complete change in attitude or opinion﹙
senses.zh: 态度或看法的﹚彻底转变；突变；变卦

senses.en: to stop, or to make sb stop, being friendly towards sb; to stop, or to make sb stop,supporting sb/sth﹙
senses.zh: 使﹚与……反目成仇，变得敌对，不再支持:

ex.en: Her old friends were turning against her.
ex.zh: 她的老朋友都跟她翻脸了。

ex.en: He’s trying to turn his family against me.
ex.zh: 他试图令他的家人反对我。

senses.en: to move your head and shoulders or your whole body so that you face in the opposite direction; to make sb/sth change position in this way﹙

ex.en: She turned around to stare at the man behind her.
ex.zh: 她转身盯着后面的男子。

ex.en: He walked away without turning round.
ex.zh: 他头也不回地走了。

senses.en: the amount of time it takes to unload a plane or ship at the end of a journey and load it ready for the next one﹙
senses.zh: 飞机或船的﹚终点装卸时间

senses.en: the amount of time that it takes to do a piece of work that you have been given and return it﹙
senses.zh: 接活到交活之间的﹚周转期，时限

senses.en: a complete change in sb’s opinion, plans,behaviour, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 看法、计划、态度等的﹚彻底转变；改弦易辙

senses.en: a sudden improvement in a business, an economy, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 企业、经济等的﹚好转，复苏，转机:

ex.en: The predicted economic turnaround failed to happen.
ex.zh: 预期的经济复苏没有出现。

senses.en: to deliberately understand sth that sb says in the wrong way, especially for your own advantage
senses.zh: 故意错误理解，曲解﹙某人的话﹚:

ex.en: You turn everything I say around to make me look stupid.
ex.zh: 你成心曲解我的话，让我看上去像个傻瓜。

senses.en: to change direction and go to one side, especially in order to avoid sb/sth

ex.en: He turned aside in embarrassment.
ex.zh: 他尴尬地转过脸去。

senses.en: to make sb/sth move to one side, especially in order to avoid sth difficult or dangerous
senses.zh: 使闪开；使避开；使转向一边:

ex.en: As he bent to kiss her, she turned her head aside.
ex.zh: 他弯腰去亲吻她时，她把头转向了一边。

ex.en: ( ) He cleverly turned all her questions aside (= he did not answer them).
ex.zh: 他机灵地迴避了她的所有提问。

senses.en: to move or to move your head to face in a different direction, often to avoid sth difficult or dangerous
senses.zh: 转身，转头﹙以避开困难或危险﹚:

ex.en: Will turned quickly away and walked out of the door.
ex.zh: 威尔连忙掉头走出门去。

ex.en: He turned away from her with a sigh.
ex.zh: 他叹了口气，转身离开了她。

senses.en: to stop, or to make sb stop, supporting sb/sth or being interested in sth﹙
senses.zh: 使某人﹚不再支持……，对……失去兴趣:

ex.en: Younger voters are turning away from the party.
ex.zh: 较年轻的选民渐渐不支持这个党了。

ex.en: The recent scandals have turned many people away from politics.
ex.zh: 最近的丑闻使很多人不愿再过问政治。

senses.en: to return in the direction that you have come from; to make sb/sth do this﹙

ex.en: The weather got so bad that we turned back.
ex.zh: 天气变得非常恶劣，我们不得不折返。

ex.en: We were turned back at the border.
ex.zh: 我们在边境被挡了回来。

senses.en: to return to a situation that existed in the past; to return to oldfashioned methods or ideas

ex.en: This new law is an attempt to turn the clock back.
ex.zh: 这项新法律目的在于恢复旧秩序。

senses.en: to fold sth back on itself

ex.en: She straightened the bedclothes and turned back the top sheet.
ex.zh: 她整理了床铺，把床罩掀开。

senses.en: to reject or refuse sb/sth

ex.en: Why did Clare turn down your invitation?
ex.zh: 克莱尔为什么谢绝你的邀请？

ex.en: He asked her to marry him, but she turned him down.
ex.zh: 他向她求婚，但是她回绝了。

senses.en: to adjust the controls on a piece of equipment in order to reduce the amount of heat, noise, light, etc. produced

ex.en: Turn that radio down, I can’t sleep.
ex.zh: 把收音机音量调低些，我没法入睡。

ex.en: I t ’ s warmer today. I’ll turn down the heating.
ex.zh: 今天暖和了些。我要把暖气关小些。

senses.en: [C, usually sing.] a fall in economic activity or profits﹙
senses.zh: 经济或收益的﹚衰退，下降:

ex.en: a downturn in sales
ex.zh: 销售额的下降

senses.en: , ) to go to bed

ex.en: It’s time for me to turn in.
ex.zh: 我该去睡觉了。

senses.en: to fold sth so that it bends or faces inwards; to be folded in this way﹙

ex.en: Her feet turn in as she walks.
ex.zh: 她走路时两脚呈内八字。

senses.en: to give sb or yourself to sb in authority because they/you have done sth wrong

ex.en: He turned his own brother in to the police.
ex.zh: 他把自己的亲兄弟交给了警方。

ex.en: Things will be better for you if you turn yourself in.
ex.zh: 如果你自首，情况会好一些的。

senses.en: to become very concerned with your own problems and stop communicating with others
senses.zh: 关心自己的困难而不与人交往；闭门谢客:

ex.en: He completely turned in on himself after his wife left him.
ex.zh: 妻子离开之后，他就完全闭门谢客了。

senses.en: to make the inside of sth face outwards
senses.zh: 把﹙……的﹚内部翻到外面； 翻出:

ex.en: It was so windy my umbrella turned inside out.
ex.zh: 风很大，把我的伞吹翻了。

ex.en: She pulled off her jumper, turning the sleeves inside out.
ex.zh: 她脱下套衫，把袖子翻了过来。

senses.en: to make great changes in sb’s life
senses.zh: 使某人﹙或其生命﹚产生巨大变化:

ex.en: The shock turned her world inside out.
ex.zh: 这一打击完全改变了她的一切。

senses.en: to change, or to make sth change, into sth different﹙

ex.en: We need to stop this problem from turning into a crisis.
ex.zh: 我们应该制止这个问题演化成一场危机。

ex.en: The house had been turned into three apartments.
ex.zh: 房子被改建成了三间公寓套房。

senses.en: to stop listening to or thinking about sb/sth

ex.en: I couldn’t understand the lecture so I just turned off.
ex.zh: 我听不懂讲课，所以也就不听了。

senses.en: to leave one road in order to travel on another
senses.zh: 拐弯﹙离开…﹚；转入另一条路:

ex.en: She turned off onto a side street.
ex.zh: 她拐进一条小巷。

ex.en: The car turned off the main road.
ex.zh: 汽车驶离了大路。

senses.en: a place where one road leads off a larger or more important road

ex.en: the turn-off for the airport
ex.zh: 通往机场的岔道

senses.en: )to make sb lose interest or become bored
senses.zh: 使﹙对某人或事物﹚失去兴趣；使厌烦:

ex.en: People had been turned off by both candidates in the election.
ex.zh: 大选中的两位候选人都让人觉得扫兴。

ex.en: His political views turned her off him.
ex.zh: 他的政见使她对他产生了反感。

senses.en: ) to stop sb feeling attracted to sb/sth; to make sb feel disgusted
senses.zh: 使﹙对某人或事物﹚失去兴趣；使厌恶:

ex.en: If I tell her I’m only 17 it might turn her off.
ex.zh: 如果我告诉她我才17 岁，她也许会扫兴。

ex.en: The sight of all that raw meat turned me off.
ex.zh: 一看到那些生肉我就觉得恶心。

senses.en: something or somebody that people do not find interesting or attractive
senses.zh: 扫兴的人﹙或事物﹚；厌烦的人﹙或事物﹚:

ex.en: Unlike many other women she found his beard a real turn-off.
ex.zh: 她觉得他的鬍鬚实在难看，这和其他许多女性的看法不同。

senses.en: to attack sb suddenly and unexpectedly

ex.en: The dog turned on him and bit his finger.
ex.zh: 那条狗突然扑过去咬他的手指。

ex.en: She suddenly turned on me and started shouting.
ex.zh: 她突然冲着我喊叫起来。

senses.en: [C, usually sing.] () a person,a thing, a situation, etc. that sb finds sexually exciting
senses.zh: 引起性慾的人﹙或环境等﹚:

ex.en: Being the centre of attention for four or five guys was a real turn-on.
ex.zh: 有四五个小伙子注视着真令人兴奋。

senses.en: to point sth such as gun, a camera,a light, etc. at sb/sth
senses.zh: 用﹙枪、照相机、灯光等﹚瞄准，对准:

ex.en: Officers turned hoses on the demonstrators.
ex.zh: 警察用水龙对准示威者。

senses.en: to make sb interested in sb/sth or use sth for the first time
senses.zh: 引起……对人﹙或事物﹚的兴趣；激发……作出尝试:

ex.en: What was it that first turned you on to jazz?
ex.zh: 是什么引发你对爵士乐的兴趣？

senses.en: to be present at an event; to attend sth or to go somewhere

ex.en: The whole village turned out to welcome us.
ex.zh: 全村人都出来欢迎我们。

ex.en: Only half the team turned out for the practice.
ex.zh: 只有一半队员参加训练。

senses.en: the number of people who come to take part in or watch an activity
senses.zh: 参加﹙或出席、到场等﹚的人数:

ex.en: There was a good turnout for the concert.
ex.zh: 参加音乐会的人很多。

senses.en: the number of people who vote in a particular election

ex.en: a high/low/poor turnout
ex.zh: 投票的人多/少/很少

senses.en: to point, or to make sth point, outwards﹙

ex.en: His feet turn out as he walks.
ex.zh: 他走路时脚向外撇。

ex.en: She turns her toes out when she walks.
ex.zh: 她走路时脚趾向外撇。

senses.en: to force sb to leave or go out of a place

ex.en: The landlord turned them out of their house just before the New Year.
ex.zh: 房东就在临近新年时把他们赶出了房门。

ex.en: You can’t turn us out in this storm!
ex.zh: 你不能在这种风暴下把我们赶走！

senses.en: to produce sth/sb

ex.en: The factory turns out 900 cars a week.
ex.zh: 这家工厂每周生产900 辆汽车。

ex.en: This school has turned out several well-known engineers.
ex.zh: 这所学校培养了几个赫赫有名的工程师。

senses.en: [NOTE]This phrasal verb is always used in the passive.
senses.zh: 这个短语动词总是用于被动语态。

senses.en: to change your position, or the position of sb/sth, so that the other side is facing outwards or upwards﹙

ex.en: He turned over onto his back.
ex.zh: 他翻了个身仰……着。

ex.en: The van skidded and turned over.
ex.zh: 客货车打滑向一侧翻倒了。

senses.en: a small piece of pastry filled with fruit or jam, folded over and baked
senses.zh: 三角馅饼，半圆馅饼﹙以水果或果酱作馅﹚

senses.en: (of an engine
senses.zh: 发动机) to run steadily at a low speed; to start转动；慢速运转；发动:

ex.en: I turned the key and the engine turned over quietly.
ex.zh: 我转动钥匙，引擎轻声发动起来。

ex.en: The engine was turning over too fast.
ex.zh: 发动机运转得太快。

senses.en: to move a page or a piece of paper so that you can see the other side

ex.en: Turn over (the page) for more details.
ex.zh: ﹙此页﹚背面有更详细的说明。

senses.en: the rate at which employees leave a company and are replaced by others﹙
senses.zh: 公司的﹚人事变更率，人员调整率:

ex.en: a high turnover of staff
ex.zh: 职员的高速变动

senses.en: the rate at which goods are sold in a shop/store and are replaced by others﹙
senses.zh: 商店的﹚货品周转率，销售比率:

ex.en: a fast turnover of stock
ex.zh: 存货的快速周转

senses.en: to deliver sb/sth to the control and care of sb in authority, especially the police
senses.zh: 移交，送交﹙当局，尤指警方﹚:

ex.en: He was turned over to the Belgian police at the border.
ex.zh: 他在边境被移交给了比利时警方。

senses.en: to think about sth carefully

ex.en: Diana turned over what James had said in her mind.
ex.zh: 黛安娜的脑子里不断琢磨詹姆斯的话。

ex.en: He lay in the dark, turning over the day’s extraordinary events.
ex.zh: 他躺在黑暗中，反复思考着那天里不寻常的事。

senses.en: , ) to enter a place illegally and steal valuable things from it

ex.en: The burglars had turned the house over.
ex.zh: 盗贼把房子洗劫一空。

senses.en: () to search a place very thoroughly, making it very untidy
senses.zh: 彻底搜查；把某处翻得凌乱不堪:

ex.en: His room had been turned over by the police.
ex.zh: 他的房间被警察翻了个底朝天。

senses.en: to move your head or body so as to face sb
senses.zh: 把脸转向，转身朝向﹙某人﹚:

ex.en: He turned to me and smiled.
ex.zh: 他转过身对我笑了。

senses.en: to turn your attention,your thoughts, etc. to a new subject﹙
senses.zh: 将注意力、思路等﹚转到新课题上:

ex.en: Our conversation soon turned to the kind of music that we liked.
ex.zh: 我们的谈话很快就转到我们喜欢的那种音乐。

ex.en: Let’s turn our attention to next week’s conference.
ex.zh: 我们集中看看下个星期的会议吧。

senses.en: something surprising or unexpected that happens
senses.zh: 奇异的事；意想不到的事:

senses.en: an improvement or an increase in sth

ex.en: an upturn in the economy
ex.zh: 经济改善

senses.en: to point, or to make sth point, upwards﹙

ex.en: Her nose turns up at the end.
ex.zh: 她是个翘鼻子。

ex.en: She turned her face up towards him.
ex.zh: 她对他仰起脸。

senses.en: [only before noun] pointing upwards

ex.en: a turned-up nose
ex.zh: 翘鼻子

senses.en: [only before noun] pointing or facing upwards

ex.en: an upturned nose
ex.zh: 翘鼻子

ex.en: upturned faces
ex.zh: 仰起的脸

senses.en: the bottom of the leg of a pair of trousers/pants that has been folded over on the outside﹙

ex.en: Turnups seem to be coming back into fashion.
ex.zh: 裤脚外翻边似乎又时兴起来了。

senses.en: to move sth so that the bottom is facing upwards﹙

ex.en: The car hit a wall, turned upside down, and ended up in a field.
ex.zh: 汽车撞到墙上，翻了过来，最后停在一块田里。

ex.en: I turned the box upside down and everything fell out.
ex.zh: 我把盒子扣过来，东西全掉出来了。

senses.en: to make a place very untidy while you are searching for sth

ex.en: The burglars turned the flat upside down.
ex.zh: 窃贼把这个单元房翻得一片狼藉。

senses.en: to make large changes and confusion in sb’s life
to remove sth or break sth off by turning and pulling it with your hand

ex.en: He twisted off the lid and looked inside.
ex.zh: 他拧开盖子往里面看。

ex.en: She twisted the cap off the bottle and took a mouthful of water.
ex.zh: 她拧开瓶盖，喝了一口水。

senses.en: to put data into a document using a computer or a typewriter
senses.zh: 将数据输入，键入﹙计算机或打字机﹚:

ex.en: Type in the file name then press return.
ex.zh: 键入文件名，然后按回车键。

ex.en: Type the relevant details into the boxes provided.
ex.zh: 把相关细节输入预设的方框内。

senses.en: to encourage sb; to support sb so that they can do sth better
senses.zh: 鼓励…，激励…﹙做某事﹚；为…加油:

ex.en: The supporters were urging the team on.
ex.zh: 助威者在为这个队加油。

ex.en: Urged on by the Prime Minister the police tried to end the strike.
ex.zh: 在首相的敦促下，警方力图终止罢工。

senses.en: to use all of sth until no more is left

ex.en: I’ve used up all the milk.
ex.zh: 我把牛奶全喝了。

ex.en: These eggs need to be used up quickly.
ex.zh: 这些鸡蛋得赶快吃完。

senses.en: to mark or be the start of sth new

ex.en: The elections ushered in a new period of change in the country.
ex.zh: 随着这些选举，国家进入了一个新的改革时期。

ex.en: Firework displays ushered in the New Year.
ex.zh: 烟火表演标志着新年的开始。

senses.en: to suddenly change direction﹙
senses.zh: 从…﹚突然改变方向，猛然转向:

ex.en: The car suddenly veered off to the left.
ex.zh: 汽车突然拐向左边。

ex.en: The truck veered off the road and crashed into a tree.
ex.zh: 卡车突然驶离公路撞上了一棵树。

senses.en: (of a conversation or a way of behaving or thinking
senses.zh: 谈话、行为或思想) to change in the way it develops离开主题﹙或常轨等﹚:

ex.en: The conversation veered off into more personal matters.
ex.zh: 谈话转到了更私人的话题。

ex.en: Throughout his career, he’s veered away from jazz into other areas.
ex.zh: 在整个职业生涯中，除了爵士乐他也不断涉猎其他领域。

senses.en: to relax and do very little

ex.en: All she does is veg out in front of the telly.
ex.zh: 她成天清闲地泡在电视前。

senses.en: to dare to do sth that could be dangerous or involve risk

ex.en: As soon as he arrived in the country, he ventured on a trip up the Amazon.
ex.zh: 他一到这个国家就沿亚马孙河溯流而上冒险旅行去了。

ex.en: This is the first time the company has ventured into movie production.
ex.zh: 这是本公司首次涉足电影制作。

senses.en: to be very close or similar to an extreme state or condition

ex.en: I was treated with suspicion that verged on hostility.
ex.zh: 我受到了几近敌意的猜疑。

ex.en: Her hair was dark brown, verging on black.
ex.zh: 她的头发深棕色，近乎黑色。

senses.en: to officially or legally give sb the power or authority to do sth
senses.zh: 授予，赋予，给予﹙正式或合法权力﹚:

ex.en: It is unwise to vest absolute power in a single institution.
ex.zh: 将绝对权力赋予单一机构是不明智的。

ex.en: The court is vested with certain rights.
ex.zh: 法庭拥有某些权力。

senses.en: to make sb the legal owner of land or property
senses.zh: 使合法拥有﹙土地或财产﹚
(常用于进行时) to compete strongly with sb/sth﹙为某事物﹚与…激烈竞争:

ex.en: There’ll be a lot of people vying for those posts.
ex.zh: 会有很多人争夺这些职位的。

ex.en: The children were vying for the teacher’s attention.
ex.zh: 孩子们都较着劲想得到老师的注意。

senses.en: , ) to spend time with sb talking in an informal and casual way

ex.en: I visited with my neighbour while the kids were playing.
ex.zh: 孩子们玩的时候我和邻居聊天。

senses.en: to be punished with sth

ex.en: He listed the horrors visited upon the region during the conflict.
ex.zh: 他列举了冲突期间这个地区的悲惨状况。

ex.en: Each new indignity visited on her was worse than the previous one.
ex.zh: 她受到的侮辱一次比一次严重。

senses.en: to reject or defeat a candidate or a proposal by voting

ex.en: The Senate has voted down efforts to raise taxes.
ex.zh: 参议院投票否决了增加税收的努力。

ex.en: If Mr Smith demands too much, the unions will vote him down.
ex.zh: 如果史密斯先生提出过高的要求，工会将不投他的票。

senses.en: to choose sb for a particular position by voting

ex.en: I was voted in as treasurer.
ex.zh: 我当选为司库。

ex.en: When was this government voted into office?
ex.zh: 这个政府是何时获选当政的？

senses.en: to make a decision about sth by voting

ex.en: The committee is voting on the proposal tonight.
ex.zh: 委员会将于今晚对该提议进行投票表决。

ex.en: Workers have begun voting on whether to hold a series of one-day strikes.
ex.zh: 工人们已经开始进行投票，决定是否举行一连串的逐日罢工。

senses.en: to decide as a group to remove sb from a particular position by voting

ex.en: The government may be voted out of office at the next election.
ex.zh: 这个政府在下次大选时可能落选。

ex.en: What will he do if he gets voted out?
ex.zh: 他如果落选会做什么呢？

senses.en: to approve sth or bring a proposal,etc. into force by voting for it

ex.en: Congress voted the bill through without a debate.
ex.zh: 国会未经辩论就投票通过了法案。

senses.en: to say that you know sb, that you believe they have a good character and that you are prepared to be responsible for their actions
senses.zh: 替… 担保﹙ 或保证﹚ :

ex.en: They asked whether I was prepared to vouch for him.
ex.zh: 他们问我是否愿意为他作担保。

ex.en: You should give the names of two people who can vouch for your honesty and reliability.
ex.zh: 你应该提供两个能担保你诚实可信的人的名字。

senses.en: to get involved in a discussion, an argument, a difficult situation, etc. in a forceful and not very sensitive way
senses.zh: 强行加入，介入，插手﹙讨论、争论、困局等﹚:

ex.en: She waded in with an attack on company policy.
ex.zh: 她插了一杠子，对公司的政策进行了抨击。

ex.en: The Senator waded into a new argument over defence spending.
ex.zh: 参议员强行加入了关于国防开支的新一轮争论。

senses.en: to attack sb physically or with words

ex.en: Marty was terrific — he just waded into the skinheads without a thought.
ex.zh: 马蒂太棒了─他毫不含煳地揍了那些光头仔。

ex.en: She waded straight into her critics with her opening remarks.
ex.zh: 她在开场白里直截了当地反驳了批评她的人。

senses.en: to spend a lot of time and effort reading sth or dealing with sth
senses.zh: 费时费力地阅读； 艰难地处理:

ex.en: I had to wade through pages and pages of statistics.
ex.zh: 我不得不硬着头皮研读一页页的统计数字。

senses.en: to talk or write a lot about sth without giving any useful information

ex.en: He waffled on for ages about his garden.
ex.zh: 他没完没了地瞎扯他的花园。

senses.en: to stay after other people have gone, especially in order to speak to sb privately
senses.zh: 等到他人走后留下来﹙尤指为私下谈话﹚ :

ex.en: He asked her to wait behind after the meeting.
ex.zh: 他要她会议结束后留下来。

senses.en: to stay at home because you are expecting sb to arrive or telephone

ex.en: I’ve got to wait in for the TV repair man.
ex.zh: 我必须在家等维修电视的人来。

ex.en: She waited in all day in case he called.
ex.zh: 她一整天都守在家里，因为他可能打电话来。

senses.en: ) to serve customers in a shop/store

ex.en: Is anybody waiting on you?
ex.zh: 有人招呼你吗？

ex.en: There is no one in the furniture department to wait on me.
ex.zh: 傢具部没人接待我。

senses.en: to wait until sb arrives or until sth is available

ex.en: Judd was late and she was sick of waiting on him.
ex.zh: 贾德迟到了，她讨厌一直等着他。

ex.en: I’m still waiting on the result of the blood test.
ex.zh: 我还在等验血结果。

senses.en: to stay in a place until sth difficult or unpleasant has passed or finished
senses.zh: 等待﹙困难或令人不快的事情﹚结束:

ex.en: We sheltered in a doorway to wait out the storm.
ex.zh: 我们躲在一个门口等候暴风雨过去。

ex.en: It was difficult to wait out the hours until I could phone her to hear the news.
ex.zh: 很难熬上几个小时一直等到能给她打电话听取消息。

senses.en: to stop sleeping; to make sb stop sleeping

ex.en: How many times does the baby wake up in the night?
ex.zh: 婴儿夜里醒几次？

ex.en: I usually wake up early in the summer.
ex.zh: 我夏天通常醒得早。

senses.en: to become, or to make sb, more lively and interested﹙

ex.en: You need to wake up and start paying attention.
ex.zh: 你得清醒点并集中注意力了。

ex.en: Wake up! I don’t want to have to repeat all this.
ex.zh: 打起精神！我不想再得重复这一切了。

senses.en: [only before noun] that is intended to wake you up

ex.en: What time would you like your wake-up call (= for example, in a hotel)?
ex.zh: 你想什么时间给你打催醒电话？

senses.en: to become aware of sth; to realize sth
to leave a difficult or unpleasant situation in order to avoid it, instead of staying to deal with it
senses.zh: 丢下﹙某人﹚；﹙从困难或不愉快的处境中﹚脱身，一走了之:

ex.en: to walk away from a situation/deal
ex.zh: 脱离某情形；放弃一项协议

ex.en: You can’t just walk away from the problem.
ex.zh: 你不能就这么甩手不管这个问题了。

senses.en: to win sth very easily

ex.en: The team walked away with the championship.
ex.zh: 这个队轻松地获得了冠军。

senses.en: to steal sth; to take sth without the owner’s permission

ex.en: The thief walked away with jewellery worth ￡24 000.
ex.zh: 窃贼偷走了价值24 000 英镑的珠宝。

senses.en: to go into a room and see what sb is doing when they did not expect you and did not want anyone to see them

ex.en: Sorry, I didn’t mean to walk in on you.
ex.zh: 对不起，我没想到你在这儿。

ex.en: I’d obviously walked in on a very serious conversation.
ex.zh: 我显然是猝不及防地进去撞见了十分严肃的交谈。

senses.en: to crash into sb/sth while you are walking
senses.zh: 走路时撞到﹙ 人或东西﹚ :

ex.en: Look where you’re going! You walked straight into me.
ex.zh: 看着点路！ 你把我撞了个正着。

ex.en: He keeps bumping into things and walking into walls.
ex.zh: 他不断地碰着东西撞着墙。

senses.en: to become caught in sth that you are not expecting, especially because you are not careful
senses.zh: 不意落入，不小心陷入﹙不愉快的境地﹚:

ex.en: He realized he’d walked into a trap.
ex.zh: 他意识到自己稀里煳涂落入了陷阱。

senses.en: to succeed in getting a job without having to make an effort

ex.en: She walked straight into a job in publishing.
ex.zh: 她轻易获得了一份出版行业的工作。

senses.en: to leave a place or a person suddenly because you are angry or upset

ex.en: She turned and walked off without a word.
ex.zh: 她二话没说，转身离去。

ex.en: The rest of the team walked off the field in protest.
ex.zh: 其他队员气愤地离开了场地以示抗议。

senses.en: to go for a walk in order to get rid of the feeling that you have eaten too much or an emotion such as anger

ex.en: I need to walk off that lunch.
ex.zh: 我要散散步把午饭消化一下。

ex.en: It’ll do her good to walk some of her temper off.
ex.zh: 散散步消消气会对她有好处。

senses.en: 1=WALK AWAY/OFF WITH STH 1

ex.en: They’ve walked off with most of the film awards.
ex.zh: 他们轻易获得了大部份电影奖项。

senses.en: )=WALK AWAY/OFF WITH STH 2

ex.en: Who’s walked off with my pen?
ex.zh: 谁顺手牵羊拿走了我的笔？

ex.en: That dog’s just walked off with our ball!
ex.zh: 那狗刚刚叨走了我们的球！

senses.en: (of workers
senses.zh: 工人) to stop working and go on strike罢工:

ex.en: The cameramen have walked out over working conditions.
ex.zh: 摄影师们因不满意工作条件而罢工。

senses.en: a sudden strike by workers﹙
to treat sb badly and not consider their wishes or feelings
to defeat sb easily in a competition
() an easy victory in a game or competition; a situation in which you are considered to have won a game although you did not in fact play
senses.zh: 轻易获得的胜利；不战而胜:

ex.en: The race was no walkover (= it was not easy to win).
ex.zh: 那场比赛的胜利得来不易。

ex.en: The other team didn’t turn up so we had a walkover into the final.
ex.zh: 对手没有出场，因此我队不战而胜，进入了决赛。

senses.en: to practise or perform a play in a simple way, just using basic moves and positions
senses.zh: 简单地排练，初排﹙ 戏剧﹚ ； 走过场

senses.en: to practise a television programme without the cameras
senses.zh: 排练﹙电视节目﹚；拍摄前排练

senses.en: [usually sing.]
a practice of a play without costumes or the objects you need,to practise basic moves and positions﹙
a practice of a television programme without the cameras﹙
senses.zh: 电视节目的﹚开拍前排练，初拍

senses.en: to approach sb/sth in a confident way﹙
senses.zh: 自信地﹚ 向… 走去， 走近:

ex.en: She walked straight up to the desk and asked to see the manager.
ex.zh: 她直接走到服务台前要求见经理。

senses.en: to put a wall or a barrier around sth
senses.zh: 把﹙某物﹚围到屏障等里面:

ex.en: Apartment blocks walled in the playground completely.
ex.zh: 公寓大楼把操场围得严严实实。

senses.en: to build a wall or a barrier around an area to separate it from another area

ex.en: Part of the yard had been walled off.
ex.zh: 院子的一部份已经隔开了。

senses.en: to keep sb as a prisoner in a place surrounded by walls

ex.en: a story of a woman who was walled up in a small room and left to die
ex.zh: 一个被关在小屋子里等死的女子的故事

senses.en: to enjoy sth that gives you pleasure, especially when it is sth unpleasant and you do it in a way that makes other people think you enjoy being unhappy or want sympathy from them
senses.zh: 热中于，沉湎于﹙尤指不愉快或惹人同情的事﹚:

ex.en: Stop wallowing in self-pity.
ex.zh: 不要一味地自怜了。

ex.en: She wallows in nostalgia for the past.
ex.zh: 她沉湎于对过去的怀恋。

senses.en: to leave a person or place in an annoying way, often taking sth without the owner’s permission
senses.zh: 令人讨厌地离开﹙常擅自带走东西﹚:

ex.en: The tenants waltzed off with half our possessions.
ex.zh: 房客顺手牵羊把我们的东西带走了一半。

ex.en: He just waltzed off and left me!
ex.zh: 他甩掉我，自己熘了！

senses.en: to leave the place where you ought to be, or the person or group of people you are with, without thinking about it

ex.en: Don’t wander off and get lost.
ex.zh: 别乱走迷了路。

ex.en: The child had wandered away from her mother.
ex.zh: 那孩子和她妈妈走散了。

senses.zh: 通常与否定词连用) to suffer because you do not have sth因缺少某物而受苦:

ex.en: I work hard so that my children want for nothing.
ex.zh: 我努力工作为的是让我的孩子什么也不缺少。

senses.en: , ) to want to come inside a place

ex.en: The cat wants in. Can you open the door?
ex.zh: 猫要进来。你开一下门好吗？

senses.en: ) to no longer want to be involved in sth, especially a business deal
senses.zh: 想要退出﹙ 尤指商业交易﹚ :

ex.en: I want out before we get into difficulties.
ex.zh: 我想在我们遇到麻烦之前退出。

ex.en: I want out of this mess.
ex.zh: 我不想再理这个烂摊子了。

senses.en: , )to want to go out of a place

ex.en: I want out of here.
ex.zh: 我想出去了。

senses.en: to prevent sb/sth dangerous or unpleasant from affecting or harming you
senses.zh: 抵御﹙人或事物带来的﹚不良影响；避开…人﹙或事物﹚:

ex.en: She put up a hand to ward off the blows.
ex.zh: 她抬起一只手阻挡击打。

ex.en: I’m taking vitamin C to ward off a cold.
ex.zh: 我在服用维生素C抗感冒。

senses.en: to start to like a person

ex.en: I warmed to the teacher immediately.
ex.zh: 我立即喜欢上了那位老师。

senses.en: (of the weather, the earth, etc.
senses.zh: 天气、地球等) to become warmer变暖:

ex.en: Research shows that the sea is warming up.
ex.zh: 研究显示海洋在变暖。

ex.en: When spring comes the earth begins to warm up.
ex.zh: 春天到来时大地开始回暖。

senses.en: to do gentle exercise or practice to prepare for an athletic activity or a performance﹙
senses.zh: 为体育活动或表演﹚做适应性练习，做准备活动；热身:

ex.en: I’m always careful to warm up before I go jogging.
ex.zh: 我慢跑之前总是注意热身。

ex.en: Peter was warming up with a few scales.
ex.zh: 彼得在稍微做做准备活动。

senses.en: [usually sing.] a series of gentle exercises or a short practice to prepare for an athletic activity or a performance﹙
senses.zh: 体育运动或表演前的﹚准备活动，适应性练习；热身:

ex.en: What do you do as a warm-up?
ex.zh: 你准备活动做什么？

ex.en: warm-up exercises
ex.zh: 热身练习

senses.en: to become, or to make sb or a part of sb’s body, feel warmer﹙
senses.zh: 使某人或身体部位﹚暖和，变暖:

ex.en: Come and warm up by the fire.
ex.zh: 来炉子旁暖和一下吧。

ex.en: They stamped their feet to warm them up.
ex.zh: 他们跺着脚取暖。

senses.en: to become, or to make sb/sth, more lively or enthusiastic﹙

ex.en: By midnight the party was only just warming up.
ex.zh: 到半夜时聚会才刚开始活跃起来。

ex.en: His role is to warm up the audience before the main event.
ex.zh: 他的任务是在正式演出之前活跃观众的气氛。

senses.en: to tell a person, a ship, an aircraft, etc. not to come near a place because it is dangerous
senses.zh: 警告﹙人、船、飞机等﹚不要靠近:

ex.en: The male birds sing to warn other males away.
ex.zh: 雄鸟鸣叫着警告其他雄鸟走开。

ex.en: An electric fence warned away anyone who came too close.
ex.zh: 电篱笆使过于接近的人不敢再靠前。

senses.en: to tell sb to leave or not to come near a place, often in a threatening way﹙
senses.zh: 常指以威胁的方式﹚叫某人离开，叫某人不要靠近，告诫某人不要…:

ex.en: The farmer warned us off his land when we tried to camp there.
ex.zh: 我们想在那里露营时，农场主警告我们不得靠近他的土地。

senses.en: to advise sb not to do sth or to stop doing sth
senses.zh: 劝某人不要…；建议某人停止…:

ex.en: He was warned off smoking after his first heart attack.
ex.zh: 他心脏病初次发作之后，别人就劝他戒烟。

ex.en: She warned him off a career in acting.
ex.zh: 她建议他放弃演艺生涯。

senses.en: to use water to remove a mark,dirt, etc. from sth

ex.en: She tried to wash away some of the dirt and blood from the boy’s face.
ex.zh: 她试着洗掉男孩脸上的一些尘土和血迹。

ex.en: () A hot bath soon washed my tiredness away.
ex.zh: 我洗了个热水澡，很快就解乏了。

senses.en: to be removed from the surface of sth or from a fabric by washing; to remove sth in this way﹙

ex.en: However hard you rub, an ink stain won’t wash off.
ex.zh: 无论怎样用劲揉搓，墨水渍是洗不掉的。

ex.en: Wash off the dirt with soap and water.
ex.zh: 用肥皂和水把污垢洗刷掉。

senses.en: to be removed from a fabric, hair, etc. by washing; to remove sth in this way﹙

ex.en: The hair colour isn’t permanent. It will wash out in a few weeks.
ex.zh: 这种染发剂不会持久。过几个星期就会洗掉。

ex.en: Take care to wash all the shampoo out of your hair.
ex.zh: 注意把头发上的洗发水都冲乾净。

senses.en: (of fabric, clothes or colours
senses.zh: 织物、衣服或颜色) no longer brightly coloured,often as a result of frequent washing﹙洗后﹚退色的，不再鲜艳的:

ex.en: Washed-out jeans were very fashionable at that time.
ex.zh: 那时退色牛仔裤很时髦。

senses.en: to make sb very tired

ex.en: That long walk has washed me out.
ex.zh: 走那么长的路把我累得疲惫不堪。

senses.en: (of water, a wave, etc.
senses.zh: 水、浪头等) to carry sb/sth away from their/its original position将人或物﹙从…﹚冲走﹙到…﹚:

senses.en: , ) to end sth

ex.en: Baltimore washed out the Indians’ six-game win streak with an 8-3 win.
ex.zh: 巴尔的摩队以8 :3结束了印地安队连赢六场的好运。

senses.en: an event that stops early or does not happen, because of rain
senses.zh: 因雨中止﹙或取消﹚的赛事:

ex.en: The game was a washout.
ex.zh: 这场比赛因雨提前结束。

senses.en: an event that is a complete failure

ex.en: The party was a total washout.
ex.zh: 聚会完全是个失败。

senses.en: ) to happen all around sb without affecting them﹙
senses.zh: 周围发生的事情﹚对…无多大影响:

ex.en: All their criticism seems to wash over him.
ex.zh: 他们所有的批评似乎都对他没有丝毫影响。

senses.en: to wash your hands and face

ex.en: I went to the men’s room to wash up.
ex.zh: 我到男洗手间去洗了洗手和脸。

senses.en: ) to wash dirty plates, glasses, etc. after a meal﹙

ex.en: It’s your turn to wash up.
ex.zh: 轮到你洗碗了。

ex.en: Don’t forget to wash up the glasses as well.
ex.zh: 别忘了捎带洗洗玻璃杯。

senses.en: to be carried along in the water and then left on land; to carry sth along and leave it in this way﹙

ex.en: A number of dead dolphins have washed up on the shore.
ex.zh: 有一些死海豚被冲到了岸上。

ex.en: His body was washed up on the beach two days later.
ex.zh: 两天后，他的尸体被冲上海滩。

senses.en: (, ) to be no longer successful and unlikely to succeed again in the future﹙

ex.en: a washed-up cabaret singer
ex.zh: 不再走红的卡巴莱歌手

senses.en: the act of washing dirty dishes, glasses, etc. after a meal﹙

ex.en: Don’t forget to do the washing-up before you go out.
ex.zh: 你出去之前别忘了洗碗。

ex.en: washingup liquid
ex.zh: 餐具洗涤液

senses.en: the dirty dishes, glasses,etc. that have to be washed after a meal﹙

ex.en: a sink full of washing-up
ex.zh: 堆满脏碗碟的洗涤槽

senses.en: (of a person, part of the body, etc.
senses.zh: 人、身体部位等) to grow thin or weak in an unhealthy way﹙不健康地﹚变得瘦弱:

ex.en: He was clearly wasting away.
ex.zh: 他明显消瘦了。

ex.en: The muscles in her arm had wasted away.
ex.zh: 她手臂上的肌肉退化了。

senses.en: to look and wait for sth to happen or for sb to come
senses.zh: 观察等待﹙发生某事或某人出现﹚:

ex.en: My parents were watching for me coming off the plane.
ex.zh: 父母翘首等待着我下飞机。

ex.en: Watch for the sign.
ex.zh: 注意观察信号。

senses.en: 2=WATCH OUT FOR SB/STH 1

ex.en: There are several points to watch for.
ex.zh: 有几点需要注意。

senses.en: to take care of sb/sth, by being near them; to protect or guard sb/sth

ex.en: The child needed to be watched over 24 hours a day.
ex.zh: 那孩子需要每天24小时看护。

ex.en: He believed his mother was still watching over him, even though she had died when he was very young.
ex.zh: 尽管母亲在他很小的时候就去世了，他相信她依然在保护着他。

senses.en: to watch sb/sth carefully to make sure that everything is done or happens correctly

ex.en: There is a committee to watch over each different area of government policy.
ex.zh: 政府政策的每一个范畴都有委员会监督。

senses.en: to make a liquid weaker by adding water
senses.zh: 加水冲淡﹙液体﹚；掺水稀释:

ex.en: The beer had been watered down.
ex.zh: 啤酒掺水了。

senses.en: made weaker because water has been added
senses.zh: 加水冲淡的；掺水稀释的:

ex.en: watered-down beer
ex.zh: 掺水的啤酒

senses.en: made less strong or critical in order not to offend people

ex.en: watered-down language
ex.zh: 温和些的语言

ex.en: It’s a watered-down version of the original proposal.
ex.zh: 这份提议比最初的语气缓和些。

senses.en: to not accept sth because you think it is not important or necessary

ex.en: Their protests were waved aside.
ex.zh: 他们的抗议未被理会。

ex.en: He waved away my question without trying to answer it.
ex.zh: 他根本没打算回答我的问题。

senses.en: to signal to sb/sth to stop, by waving your hand
senses.zh: 对… 挥手示意停下； 挥手叫停:

ex.en: We waited while Richard waved down a taxi.
ex.zh: 我们等着，由理查德招手叫出租车。

ex.en: The police had set up a roadblock and waved several drivers down.
ex.zh: 警方设下路障并挥手示意几位司机停车。

senses.en: to wave goodbye to sb as they leave

ex.en: I waved the children off to school and went back inside.
ex.zh: 我挥手与上学的孩子们告别，然后就回到屋里。

senses.en: to signal to sb/sth to go forwards,by waving your hand or arm

ex.en: The police waved the traffic on.
ex.zh: 警察招手让车辆向前开。

ex.en: We stopped, but the cab driver waved us on.
ex.zh: 我们停下了，但出租车司机招手让我们往前走。

senses.en: to signal to sb to continue forwards through a gate or a barrier, by waving your hand or arm
senses.zh: 打手势让…通过﹙门或障碍物﹚ :

ex.en: The soldier gave us back our passports and waved us through.
ex.zh: 士兵把护照还给我们，然后打手势示意我们通过。

senses.en: to have learned about or experienced sth from an early age﹙

ex.en: I was weaned on a regular diet of Hollywood fantasy.
ex.zh: 我从小就时常看好莱坞幻想片。

senses.en: to make sb/yourself gradually stop doing sth or using sth that is bad or harmful﹙
senses.zh: 使﹚逐渐戒除恶习﹙或避免依赖…﹚:

ex.en: The hospital managed to wean her off the drug.
ex.zh: 医院已让她逐步减少依赖这种药。

ex.en: The patch enables smokers to wean themselves off cigarettes very gradually.
ex.zh: 这张贴片能使吸烟者很缓慢地把烟戒掉。

senses.en: to become, or to make sth become thinner, smoother, etc. by continually using or rubbing it﹙
senses.zh: 因重复使用而﹚变薄，变光滑；磨薄；磨光:

ex.en: The picture on the coin had worn away.
ex.zh: 硬币上的图画已经磨没了。

ex.en: The steps had been worn away by the feet of thousands of visitors.
ex.zh: 成千上万的游客把台阶踏得很光滑。

senses.en: to slowly and gradually make sth thinner or smoother﹙

ex.en: a drop of water wearing away at a stone
ex.zh: 渐渐磨损石头的水滴

ex.en: () Stress can wear away at your ability to think straight.
ex.zh: 压力会逐步破坏你的逻辑思维能力。

senses.en: to become or to make sth become, gradually smaller, thinner,etc. by continuously using or rubbing it﹙
senses.zh: 因重复使用而﹚ 变小， 变光滑； 磨短； 磨薄:

ex.en: The tyres had worn right down.
ex.zh: 轮胎完全磨损了。

ex.en: The path has been worn down in places to bare rock.
ex.zh: 这条小路有些地方已经磨得露出了石头。

senses.en: to make sb/sth weaker or less determined, especially by continuously attacking or putting pressure on them/it over a period of time﹙
senses.zh: 尤指通过不断攻击或施加压力﹚使衰弱，使意志薄弱:

ex.en: Constantly being criticized was wearing her down.
ex.zh: 她因为不断受到指责而意志消沉。

ex.en: to wear down sb’s patience/ resistance
ex.zh: 消磨耐心；削弱抵抗力

senses.en: to become, or to make sth become, thin or no longer able to be used,usually because it has been used too much

ex.en: Our carpets always seem to wear out quickly.
ex.zh: 我们的地毯似乎总是很快就磨坏了。

ex.en: I wore out two pairs of boots on the walking trip.
ex.zh: 我这次徒步旅行穿坏了两双靴子。

senses.en: badly damaged and no longer useful because it has been used a lot
senses.zh: 彻底损坏的； 破旧不堪的:

ex.en: worn-out clothes/equipment
ex.zh: 破烂不堪的衣服；老掉牙的设备

senses.en: to make sb/yourself extremely tired
senses.zh: 使疲乏；使筋疲力尽； 使厌烦:

ex.en: It’s no good wearing yourself out by working so late.
ex.zh: 熬夜把自己累垮是不可取的。

ex.en: The kids have worn me out today.
ex.zh: 孩子们今天把我累坏了。

senses.en: to lose your interest in or enthusiasm for sb/sth
senses.zh: 对…失去兴趣﹙或热情﹚；厌倦:

ex.en: As the day went on, we wearied of the long journey.
ex.zh: 随着那一天的过去，我们对漫长的旅行失去了兴趣。

senses.en: to avoid keeping a promise, doing your duty, etc.

ex.en: What I did was wrong and I should be punished. I’m not going to try and weasel out.
ex.zh: 我错了， 应受惩罚。我不会设法逃避的。

ex.en: He’s trying to figure out a way to weasel out of the deal.
ex.zh: 他正设法逃避根据协议应承担的义务。

senses.en: to remove or get rid of sb/sth that you do not want from a group of people or things
senses.zh: 清除，剔除，淘汰﹙不需要的人或物﹚:

ex.en: a plan intended to weed out poor teachers
ex.zh: 淘汰不称职桝师的计划

ex.en: Weak or sick animals were weeded out.
ex.zh: 病弱的动物已经处理掉。

senses.en: to make sb less likely to achieve sth or to be successful
senses.zh: 妨碍，阻碍某人﹙做成某事﹚:

ex.en: The fact that he’s had five jobs in two years will weigh against his application.
ex.zh: 他两年之内做过五份工作，这将妨碍他的申请。

senses.en: to consider the importance or the advantages of sth compared to sth else

ex.en: Potential benefits need to be weighed against the obvious risks.
ex.zh: 需要对潜在的利益和明显的风险进行权衡。

senses.en: to make sb feel anxious or depressed﹙
senses.zh: 某事物﹚使人烦恼﹙或焦虑、忧心、沮丧等﹚:

ex.en: The responsibilities of the job are weighing her down.
ex.zh: 工作上的责任压得她喘不过气来。

ex.en: He was weighed down with grief.
ex.zh: 他悲伤过度。

senses.en: to put a heavy weight on sb/sth so that it is difficult for them to move easily﹙
senses.zh: 某物﹚把…压得难以移动，把…压弯:

ex.en: We were weighed down with bags of shopping.
ex.zh: 一袋袋买来的东西把我们压得走不动路。

ex.en: The snow was weighing down the branches of the fir trees.
ex.zh: 雪把杉树枝压弯了。

senses.en: the occasion when the weight of a sports person such as a boxer is measured just before a fight, a race, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 赛前对拳击手等的﹚量体重:

ex.en: The champion arrived five minutes late for the weigh-in.
ex.zh: 冠军在赛前量体重时迟到了五分钟。

senses.en: to make sb feel worried or depressed; to be a difficult duty or task for sb/sth
senses.zh: 加重…的思想负担；使担忧；使沮丧；对…是艰难的任务:

senses.en: to measure a quantity of sth by weight

ex.en: Weigh out all the ingredients before you start making the cake.
ex.zh: 做蛋糕之前要先把配料都量好。

senses.en: to form an opinion of sb by watching them or talking to them﹙
senses.zh: 通过观察或谈话﹚形成对…的看法，品评:

ex.en: She stared at him, weighing him up.
ex.zh: 她一边注视一边掂量着他。

ex.en: The two women weighed each other up for a few moments.
ex.zh: 两个女人相互揣摩了一会儿。

senses.en: to add a weight to sth so that it feels very heavy, bends down, sinks,etc.﹙
senses.zh: 某物﹚加重…的负荷﹙以致其向下弯曲、下沉等﹚:

ex.en: The canvas sheet was weighted down to stop it blowing away.
ex.zh: 帆布用东西压住了，以免被风颳走。

ex.en: My pockets were weighted down with lots of small coins.
ex.zh: 我的衣袋里装了很多小硬币，沉甸甸的。

senses.en: to unite sb/sth into an effective whole

ex.en: The manager has welded the players into a strong team.
ex.zh: 经理把运动员组织成了一支强劲的队伍。

ex.en: The crisis helped to weld the community together.
ex.zh: 这场危机促使整个集体紧密团结起来。

senses.en: to not do sth that you have promised to do, for example to not pay money that you owe a person

ex.en: ‘I’m not in the habit of welshing on deals,’ said Don.
ex.zh: “我不习惯违背协议。”唐说道。

senses.en: to attack sb by hitting them again and again with great force

ex.en: Jo really whaled on Steve and was surprised he was still standing afterwards.
ex.zh: 乔确实狠狠地揍了史蒂夫，可她感到吃惊的是揍完之后史蒂夫居然还站着。

ex.en: I was so angry, I simply whaled into him.
ex.zh: 我气愤极了，就那么揍了他一通。

senses.en: to turn around very quickly to face the opposite direction; to make sb/sth do this﹙

ex.en: I wheeled around to scream at Miles.
ex.zh: 我猛地转过去对着迈尔斯尖叫。

senses.en: to produce sb/sth and use them to help you do sth, even though they have often been used before

ex.en: He wheels out the same old arguments every time he makes a speech.
ex.zh: 他又弹起了他每次讲话都弹的老调。

senses.en: to take sth out quickly and suddenly﹙

ex.en: He whipped out his camera and started taking photos.
ex.zh: 他突然拿出相机开始照相。

senses.en: to do sth very quickly

ex.en: She whipped through the routine paperwork.
ex.zh: 她迅速处理了日常的文案工作。

senses.en: to deliberately make sb feel strong emotions or get excited about or interested in sth
senses.zh: 鼓动﹙某人、情绪等﹚；激发﹙热情等﹚:

ex.en: The studio audience was whipped up into a frenzy.
ex.zh: 录制现场的观众被鼓动得十分痴狂。

ex.en: They’re trying to whip up support for their candidate.
ex.zh: 他们正竭力鼓动大家支持他们的候选人。

senses.en: to prepare a meal or some food very quickly

ex.en: I can easily whip up an omelette.
ex.zh: 我马上就能做好煎蛋卷。

senses.en: to remove sb/sth from a place very quickly
senses.zh: 迅速移走，匆匆带走﹙人或物﹚ :

ex.en: The president was whisked away by his bodyguards.
ex.zh: 总统立刻由保镖护送走了。

ex.en: The food was whisked away before we had finished.
ex.zh: 还没等我们吃完，食物就给匆忙端走了。

senses.en: to gradually reduce the size,importance or value of sth
senses.zh: 削减，减少，降低﹙…的大小、重要性或价值﹚:

ex.en: Inflation has been whittling away their savings.
ex.zh: 通货膨胀使他们的积蓄不断减少。

senses.en: to reduce the size or number of sb/sth gradually
senses.zh: 逐渐减少，逐渐缩减﹙…的大小或数目﹚:

ex.en: The government’s majority has been whittled down to eight.
ex.zh: 政府多数票减少到了八票。

senses.en: to do, read sth, etc. very quickly

ex.en: She whizzed through the work and was finished before lunch.
ex.zh: 她麻利地赶在午饭前把活干完了。

senses.en: to enjoy yourself in a noisy and excited way

ex.en: I’ve been working hard while you’ve been whooping it up in Berlin.
ex.zh: 我一直埋首工作，你却在柏林狂欢作乐。

senses.en: ) to try to make people excited or enthusiastic about sb/sth
to become,or to make sb, very excited or very anxious about sth; to go, or to make sb, crazy, often as a result of the effect of drugs﹙
senses.zh: 使﹚十分激动﹙或焦虑﹚；﹙使﹚亢奋

senses.en: to decide not to do sth you had intended to do because you are too frightened
senses.zh: 畏缩而不敢做；怯而不做:

ex.en: Did you wimp out on any of the tests?
ex.zh: 你有没有因害怕而放弃过哪门考试？

ex.en: Dave wimped out and refused to dive off the top board.
ex.zh: 戴夫畏缩不前，不肯从顶层跳板跳水。

senses.en: to get again by your own efforts sb/sth that you had before

ex.en: I’m hoping to win back my place in the team soon.
ex.zh: 我希望很快恢复我在队里的位置。

ex.en: Jack had tried everything to win Martha back.
ex.zh: 杰克尽一切努力要夺回马莎。

senses.en: to gain sb’s support or approval, especially by persuading them that you are right﹙
senses.zh: 尤指通过劝说﹚获得某人的支持﹙或赞成﹚:

ex.en: My dad’s against the idea, but I’m sure I can win him over.
ex.zh: 我爸爸反对这个想法，但我相信我能说服他。

ex.en: Jenny’s parents were soon won over by Anthony’s easy charm.
ex.zh: 珍妮的父母很快就被安东尼潇洒自如的风度征服了。

senses.en: to finally succeed after trying very hard

ex.en: We are faced with a lot of problems but we’ll win through in the end.
ex.zh: 我们面临很多问题，但我们终将成功。

ex.en: United won through to the final in an exciting game.
ex.zh: 联队在一场激动人心的比赛中赢得了决赛权。

senses.en: to relax, after a period of stress or excitement

ex.en: It takes a while for me to wind down after work.
ex.zh: 我下班之后要过一会儿才能松下心来。

senses.en: to find yourself after a long time in a particular place or situation

ex.en: I always said she would wind up in jail.
ex.zh: 我以前一直说她终归要入狱。

ex.en: Bill wound up marrying the girl next door!
ex.zh: 比尔最后娶了隔壁的女孩！

senses.en: to bring sth such as a speech, a meeting or a discussion to an end

ex.en: Before I wind up, I’d like to make one final point.
ex.zh: 讲话结束之前， 我想说明最后一点。

ex.en: If we all agree, let’s wind up the discussion.
ex.zh: 如果大家都同意，咱们就结束讨论吧。

senses.en: to make sth mechanical work by turning a handle several times﹙
senses.zh: 给机械物品﹚上弦，上发条；﹙通过转动把手﹚操作:

ex.en: Does this clock have a battery or does it wind up?
ex.zh: 这个钟使用电池还是靠上弦？

ex.en: This is a great little toy.You just wind it up and off it goes!
ex.zh: 这个小玩具很棒。只要上一下发条它就动起来！

senses.en: to deliberately make sb very angry or annoyed﹙

ex.en: Are you deliberately winding me up?
ex.zh: 你是不是在故意气我？

ex.en: Ignore them. They’re just trying to wind you up.
ex.zh: 别理他们。他们只不过是想惹你生气。

senses.en: sth that sb says or does in order to annoy sb or to make a joke
senses.zh: 故意气人的话﹙或做法﹚；戏弄人的话﹙或做法﹚:

ex.en: It sounded so crazy I thought it was a wind-up.
ex.zh: 那听上去十分荒唐，我觉得是骗人的。

senses.en: the act of officially closing a business, a company, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 企业、公司等的﹚正式关闭， 歇业:

ex.en: a voluntary winding-up of the company
ex.zh: 公司的自愿正式停业

ex.en: a winding-up order/petition
ex.zh: 停止营业指令/申请

senses.en: to pretend that you have not noticed sth, especially sth bad or illegal﹙
senses.zh: 尤指对坏事﹚视而不见；睁一只眼闭一只眼:

ex.en: The authorities have chosen to wink at the illegal trade.
ex.zh: 当局决定不过问这种非法贸易。

senses.en: to get sb/sth out of somewhere slowly and with difficulty﹙
senses.zh: 从…﹚挖出，掏出；逼使…﹙从…﹚离开:

ex.en: The bird uses its sharp beak to winkle insects out of tree trunks.
ex.zh: 这种鸟用尖喙从树干里啄出虫子。

ex.en: The terrorists have been winkled out of their hiding place.
ex.zh: 恐怖分子被迫从藏身地跑了出来。

senses.en: to get sth such as information, money, etc. from sb with difficulty
senses.zh: 从…套出﹙实情等﹚；从…索取﹙金钱﹚:

ex.en: She’s very good at winkling out secrets.
ex.zh: 她很善于打探秘密。

ex.en: He wouldn’t tell you? Don’t worry, I’ll winkle it out of him.
ex.zh: 他不肯告诉你？别担心，我会让他吐露的。

senses.en: to remove sth, such as dirt or tears, with a cloth or your hand
senses.zh: 擦掉， 抹去﹙污迹、眼泪等﹚:

ex.en: Wipe away mud splashes with a wet cloth.
ex.zh: 用湿布把溅的泥点擦乾净。

ex.en: He wiped away a tear.
ex.zh: 他抹掉了一滴眼泪。

senses.en: to clean a surface with a cloth

ex.en: I’ll just wipe the table down before you put your books there.
ex.zh: 我这就把桌面擦乾净，你再把书放在上面。

senses.en: to remove sth from a surface with a cloth﹙
senses.zh: 从… 上﹚ 抹掉…，擦掉…:

ex.en: Wipe off any surplus glue with a rag before it dries.
ex.zh: 用碎布把多余的胶水擦掉，以免乾结。

ex.en: Tom had carefully wiped his fingerprints off the glass.
ex.zh: 汤姆小心地擦去自己留在玻璃杯上的指纹。

senses.en: to remove sth that has been recorded on a tape or a video tape﹙
senses.zh: 从磁带或录像带上﹚抹掉…，清除…:

ex.en: He wiped the conversation off the tape.
ex.zh: 他把磁带上的谈话录音抹掉了。

senses.en: to reduce the value of sth, especially shares

ex.en: Over ￡5 billion was wiped off share values worldwide today.
ex.zh: 今天全球股票价格下挫了五十多亿英镑。

senses.en: ) to defeat sb easily in a sports competition﹙
senses.zh: 体育比赛中﹚轻松打败，轻易战胜:

ex.en: The Welsh side was wiped out 24-3.
ex.zh: 威尔士队被对方以24 :3轻而易举地打败了。

senses.en: (, ) to make sb very tired

ex.en: All that travelling wiped her out.
ex.zh: 整个旅程让她舟车劳顿。

senses.en: ) to murder sb
[not before noun] ()very tired
to kill large numbers of people or animals

ex.en: The whole village was wiped out by the flood.
ex.zh: 全村人都死于那场大水。

ex.en: Pollution has wiped out half the species of fish in the river.
ex.zh: 污染已使河中半数鱼种灭绝。

senses.en: to dry dishes with a cloth

ex.en: You wash and I’ll wipe up.
ex.zh: 你洗碗，我来擦乾。

senses.en: to clean a substance, especially a liquid, from a surface with a cloth

ex.en: Keep a cloth handy to wipe up any mess.
ex.zh: 备好抹布，以便随时擦掉脏东西。

senses.en: to connect sb/sth to a piece of electrical equipment by using electrical wires
senses.zh: 用导线将某人﹙或某物﹚连接到﹙电气设备﹚:

ex.en: You will be wired up to a machine which will record your heartbeat.
ex.zh: 你会被连接到记录心搏的仪器上。

ex.en: The police suggested I should be wired up (= to record the conversation) before I met the dealer.
ex.zh: 警察建议我应该在见到毒品贩子之前接好录音设备。

senses.en: to understand sth better; to become aware of the unpleasant truth about a situation
senses.zh: 加深﹙对情况的﹚理解；意识到，觉察﹙令人不愉快的实情﹚:

ex.en: Employees should wise up about how the industry works.
ex.zh: 雇工应该进一步理解这个行业的运作。

ex.en: You need to wise up to the fact that he’s never coming back.
ex.zh: 你得明白他永远不会回来这一事实。

senses.en: to try to get rid of sth by wishing it did not exist; to wish that sb was somewhere else
senses.zh: 从心里竭力摆脱；希望﹙某事物﹚不存在；希望﹙某人﹚在别处:

ex.en: These complications can’t just be wished away, you know.
ex.zh: 这些麻烦事并不是想让它们消失就能消失的，你知道。

ex.en: Don’t wish your life away (= said to sb who spends a lot of time looking forward to sth that is going to happen in the future).
ex.zh: 不要成天空等着将来。

senses.en: to become less or weaker, especially before disappearing completely
senses.zh: 萎缩；﹙尤指渐渐﹚破灭，消失:

ex.en: All our hopes just withered away.
ex.zh: 我们的一切希望就这样渐渐破灭了。

ex.en: They predicted that the bad schools would wither away.
ex.zh: 他们预言劣等学校将逐步消失。

senses.en: to eat sth very quickly, especially in large quantities﹙
senses.zh: 尤指大量地﹚快速吃；狼吞虎咽:

ex.en: He wolfed down his breakfast and rushed out of the house.
ex.zh: 他狼吞虎咽地吃了早餐就冲出房门。

senses.en: to be very surprised by sth
senses.zh: 感到诧异； 非常惊奇； 惊叹:

ex.en: He wondered at her beauty.
ex.zh: 他对她的美貌赞叹不已。

ex.en: She wondered at her own stupidity.
ex.zh: 她没想到自己会这么笨。

senses.en: to find a way of doing what you want to in spite of situations, rules, etc. that could prevent you doing it
senses.zh: 绕过﹙有妨碍的状况、规则等﹚；绕道走:

ex.en: If we can’t get rid of the problem, we’ll just have to work round it.
ex.zh: 如果我们不能解决这个问题， 就只好绕过它了。

ex.en: He urged the two sides to work around their disputes and reach an agreement.
ex.zh: 他敦促双方避开他们的纠纷达成协议。

senses.en: to gradually turn a conversation towards a particular topic

ex.en: I wondered when he would work around to the subject of money.
ex.zh: 我不知道他何时会绕到钱的主题上来。

senses.en: to make great efforts to achieve sth or do sth well

ex.en: She worked hard at her French and passed the exam.
ex.zh: 她刻苦学习法语，通过了考试。

ex.en: You’ve got to work at losing weight.
ex.zh: 你必须下工夫减肥。

senses.zh: (常用于进行时) to continue to work hard for a period of time继续努力﹙…﹚:

ex.en: I’ve been working away in the gym, trying to get fit.
ex.zh: 我一直在健身房锻炼以保持健康。

ex.en: Ruth spends hours in the library, working away at Japanese.
ex.zh: 鲁思在图书馆一待就是好几个小时，刻苦温习日语。

senses.en: to add one substance to another and mix them together

ex.en: Work the butter in with your fingers.
ex.zh: 用手指掺进黄油。

ex.en: Use plenty of polish and work it well into the wood.
ex.zh: 涂上足够的光蜡并使它充分渗入木料。

senses.en: to try to include sth in a piece of writing, a speech, etc.
senses.zh: 设法把…加进﹙文章、讲话等中﹚；尽量包括:

ex.en: Try and work in something about your own experience.
ex.zh: 尽量穿插讲点你本人的经验。

ex.en: He usually manages to work something topical into his act.
ex.zh: 他通常设法在他的节目中加插些热门话题。

senses.en: to become very angry,excited, etc.
senses.zh: 变得十分气愤﹙或非常激动等﹚:

senses.en: (of a machine, a piece of electrical equipment, etc.
senses.zh: 机器、电气设备等) to use a supply of power or another machine in order to operate靠电源﹙或其他机器﹚运行:

ex.en: The lighter works off the car battery.
ex.zh: 引燃器利用汽车蓄电池打火。

senses.en: to try to persuade sb to agree to sth or to do sth
senses.zh: 努力劝说…同意﹙或做某事﹚；尽力说服:

ex.en: My father hasn’t said he will lend me the car yet, but I’m working on him.
ex.zh: 父亲还没说他会把汽车借给我，但我正在竭力说服他呢。

senses.en: to happen or develop in a particular way, especially a successful way

ex.en: I’m glad my plan worked out (= was successful).
ex.zh: 我很高兴我的计划成功了。

ex.en: Their marriage didn’t work out (= was not successful).
ex.zh: 他们的婚姻不美满。

senses.en: a period of physical exercise

ex.en: I did a two-hour workout in the gym.
ex.zh: 我在健身房锻炼了两个小时。

senses.en: to attack sb physically and injure them, either as a punishment or to get information from them

ex.en: They sent the boys round to work him over.
ex.zh: 他们派出了几个兄弟去拷问他。

senses.en: to work without stopping for a particular period of time﹙
senses.zh: 一段时间内﹚连续工作， 不停地干活:

ex.en: At harvest time we work through until it gets dark.
ex.zh: 收穫季节里，我们一直干到天黑。

senses.en: to start to have an effect somewhere
senses.zh: 开始影响； 对…发挥作用:

ex.en: These pressures have worked through to the staff.
ex.zh: 这些压力影响到了员工。

ex.en: The full effects of the change will take time to work through the system.
ex.zh: 这项改革对整个体系全面发挥效用是指日可待的事。

senses.en: to move or pass through sth gradually until you reach a particular point
senses.zh: 逐渐移动到；慢慢过渡到:

senses.en: to follow a plan, etc.
senses.zh: 按照﹙ 计划等﹚；根据…行事:

ex.en: We’re working to a very tight schedule.
ex.zh: 我们的日程安排很满。

ex.en: They have to work to a budget.
ex.zh: 他们必须按照预算办事。

senses.en: to try to reach or achieve a goal
senses.zh: 努力达到，设法完成﹙目标﹚:

ex.en: She’s working towards her PhD.
ex.zh: 她在攻读博士学位。

ex.en: The two groups are working towards the same end.
ex.zh: 两个组正向同一目标努力。

senses.en: to gradually make sb/yourself become very upset,angry or excited about sth﹙

ex.en: She had worked herself up into a rage.
ex.zh: 她发起了怒火。

ex.en: He worked the crowd up into a frenzy.
ex.zh: 他把人群煽动得疯狂起来。

senses.en: [not before noun]() very excited, upset or angry about sth﹙
senses.zh: 对某事﹚非常兴奋，惴惴不安，大怒:

ex.en: What was Ben so worked up about?
ex.zh: 本对什么事如此激动？

ex.en: I can’t get at all worked up about cars (= I am not interested in or excited by cars).
ex.zh: 我对汽车根本不感兴趣。

senses.en: to gradually develop or increase sth until you have enough
senses.zh: 逐步发展，逐渐增加﹙到足量﹚:

ex.en: We jogged up the hill to work up an appetite.
ex.zh: 我们为了增加食慾就慢跑上山了。

ex.en: I can’t work up much enthusiasm for this subject.
ex.zh: 我对这个话题提不起多大热情。

senses.en: to gradually prepare for and move towards sth that is more exciting or extreme
senses.zh: 逐步发展到，逐渐达到﹙更高或更深的程度﹚:

ex.en: He started slowly and worked up to running ten miles a day.
ex.zh: 他开始时慢跑，后来逐渐增加到一天跑十英里。

ex.en: The tension works up to a climax towards the end of the film.
ex.zh: 电影快结束时，紧张气氛达到了高潮。

senses.en: to prepare yourself to do sth difficult or unpleasant
senses.zh: 为﹙困难或不愉快的事情﹚做准备:

ex.en: I haven’t told him yet but I’m working up to it.
ex.zh: 我还没告诉他呢，但我正准备告诉他。

senses.en: to gradually make sb like or trust you, especially in order to gain an advantage for yourself
senses.zh: 逐渐赢得欢心，渐渐骗取信任﹙以获利﹚:

senses.en: to manage to obtain information from sb, often by asking them questions in a clever way for a long period of time﹙
senses.zh: 慢慢地﹚从某人处套出话来；不断套问:

ex.en: It took me days to worm the truth out of my daughter.
ex.zh: 我用了好几天时间才从女儿口中探听出真相。

senses.en: to think or talk a lot about a problem and try to find a solution
senses.zh: 思考，苦想，反复谈论﹙以寻求解决办法﹚:

ex.en: He lay awake all night, worrying at the problem.
ex.zh: 他醒着躺了一夜，苦想着这个问题。

senses.en: to put sth firmly around sth/sb

ex.en: He wrapped his arms tightly around my waist.
ex.zh: 他双臂紧紧搂住了我的腰。

ex.en: A long scarf was wrapped round her neck.
ex.zh: 她脖子上围了一条长围巾。

senses.en: used to tell sb rudely to stop talking and be quiet

ex.en: Oh wrap up and let somebody else say something!
ex.zh: 喂，闭上嘴让别人说话吧！

senses.en: to put warm clothes, etc.on yourself/sb﹙

ex.en: Wrap up warm— it’s really cold outside.
ex.zh: 穿暖和点─外面非常冷。

ex.en: I wrapped the twins up before letting them go out.
ex.zh: 我把这对双胞胎穿暖和了才让他们出去。

senses.en: a short summary of what has gone before, especially at the end of a news broadcast
senses.zh: 简要回顾；摘要；概述；﹙尤指新闻广播之后的﹚新闻提要:

ex.en: And to close, here is a wrap-up of today’s developments.
ex.zh: 最后是关于今天进展情况的提要。

senses.en: the final actions that complete sth

ex.en: the wrap-up of the campaign
ex.zh: 这场运动的最后阶段

senses.en: to be so involved in a person or an activity that you do not notice other people or what is happening around you
senses.zh: 注意力集中于某人身上﹙或某事情上﹚:

ex.en: He was so wrapped up in his book that he didn’t notice me leaving.
ex.zh: 他专心地看着书，居然没有注意到我离开了。

ex.en: Julia is completely wrapped up in her children.
ex.zh: 朱莉娅把全部精力都花在孩子身上。

senses.en: to remove sth from sth by force with a strong twisting movement﹙
senses.zh: 从…上﹚猛扭下，用力撇掉﹙某物﹚:

ex.en: The tug of the rope nearly wrenched my arm off.
ex.zh: 绳子差点把我的胳膊拽脱臼。

ex.en: He wrenched the picture off the wall and threw it to the ground.
ex.zh: 他从墙上一把撕下那张画并摔到地上。

senses.en: to take sth such as power or control from sb/sth with great effort﹙

ex.en: The rebels tried to wrest control of the town from government forces.
ex.zh: 反叛者企图从政府军手中夺取这个城镇的控制权。

senses.en: to take sth from sb that they do not want to give, suddenly or violently﹙

ex.en: The officer managed to wrest the gun from his grasp.
ex.zh: 警官最终把枪从他手中夺走了。

senses.en: to struggle to deal with sth difficult

ex.en: Farmers are wrestling with the problem of the wet weather.
ex.zh: 农民正努力抵御多雨的天气。

ex.en: He spent several more weeks wrestling with his conscience and then finally decided to resign.
ex.zh: 他和自己的良心又搏斗了几个星期，最终决定辞职。

senses.en: to avoid doing sth unpleasant or sth that you do not want to do by making clever excuses
senses.zh: 耍滑不做，逃避﹙应做的事等﹚:

ex.en: to wriggle out of your responsibilities
ex.zh: 找藉口逃避责任

ex.en: I’ve got an appointment I can’t wriggle out of.
ex.zh: 我有个推脱不掉的约会。

senses.en: to remove water or other liquid from a cloth, etc. by twisting it tightly and squeezing it
senses.zh: 拧，绞﹙某物﹚；拧出，绞出﹙水或其他液体﹚:

ex.en: Rinse the cloth and wring it out well.
ex.zh: 把布冲洗净并拧乾。

ex.en: My clothes got so wet I could wring the water out!
ex.zh: 我的衣服湿得能拧出水来！

senses.en: to obtain sth from sb with difficulty, especially by putting pressure on them

ex.en: She eventually wrung an apology out of him.
ex.zh: 她最终逼他道歉了。

ex.en: A few concessions were wrung from the government.
ex.zh: 政府逼于压力作出了一些让步。

senses.en: to write in reply to sb’s letter﹙
senses.zh: 给某人﹚ 写回信， 覆信:

ex.en: I wrote and apologized, but he never wrote back.
ex.zh: 我写了信道歉，可他从未回覆。

ex.en: The school wrote back to me saying that all the courses were full.
ex.zh: 学校给我覆信说所有的课程都满额了。

senses.en: to write sth on paper so that you do not forget it

ex.en: I wrote her address down in my notebook.
ex.zh: 我把她的住址记在我的笔记本上。

ex.en: There is a handout so you needn’t write all this down.
ex.zh: 有一份讲义发给你们，不必把这些全记下来。

senses.en: () a reduction in the value of what a company owns, etc.﹙
senses.zh: 资产账面值的﹚减记，划减

senses.en: to write a letter to an organization to state an opinion or to ask a question
senses.zh: 致函﹙某机构﹚ ﹙表达意见或咨询﹚:

ex.en: Write in to the programme and tell us your own opinion on this.
ex.zh: 欢迎来函表达有关本节目的意见。

ex.en: 500 viewers wrote in to complain about the advertisement.
ex.zh: 500 名电视观众写信来投诉这个广告。

senses.en: to add an extra name to a list of candidates in an election so that you can vote for them﹙
senses.zh: 在选票上﹚写上非原定候选人姓名:

ex.en: She wrote Carrasco in on the ballot paper.
ex.zh: 她在选票上加上卡拉斯科的名字。

ex.en: Workers were handing out sample ballots with their candidate’s name written in.
ex.zh: 工人们正在散发模拟选票，上面加了他们所选的非原定候选人名字。

senses.en: a vote for sb who is not an official candidate in an election, in which you write their name on your voting paper
senses.zh: 投给非原定候选人的票:

ex.en: He qualified as a write-in in 15 states.
ex.zh: 他在15 个州获得了非原定候选人的资格。

ex.en: a write-in candidate/vote
ex.zh: 非原定候选人；非原定候选人选票

senses.en: to add a character or a scene to a play, a film/movie,a regular series, etc.
senses.zh: 把某角色﹙或情节﹚加进戏剧﹙ 或电影、系列电视剧等﹚ :

ex.en: Why did you write the plane crash in?
ex.zh: 你为什么要把飞机坠毁的一幕加进去？

ex.en: It was the first time a disabled child had been written into a TV soap.
ex.zh: 那是电视肥皂剧里首次出现残疾儿童这种角色。

senses.en: to include sth such as a special rule or a condition in a document, a contract, an agreement, etc.
senses.zh: 把…写入﹙文件、合同、协议等﹚:

ex.en: A yearly visit to both families was written into their marriage contract.
ex.zh: 他们在婚约里订明每年都去两家拜访。

senses.en: to write to an organization or a company, asking them to send you sth
senses.zh: 致函﹙ 某机构或公司﹚ ﹙索取资料等﹚；函索﹙…﹚:

ex.en: She wrote off to an agency for advice.
ex.zh: 她去信代理行查询。

senses.en: to consider that sb/sth is a failure or not important

ex.en: Don’t write John off too soon — he may surprise you!
ex.zh: 不要过早认为约翰完蛋─他会出乎你意料的！

ex.en: I wrote off my symptoms as tiredness.
ex.zh: 我以为我的症状是疲劳所致。

senses.en: [sing.] () a failure; a time when you do not achieve anything

ex.en: Today has been a write-off as far as work is concerned.
ex.zh: 今天的工作毫无进展。

senses.en: () to cancel a debt; to recognize that sth is a failure, has no value, etc.
senses.zh: 注销，销记﹙账项、资产等﹚；认定…失败﹙或无价值等﹚:

ex.en: All outstanding Third World debts should now be written off.
ex.zh: 所有未偿清的第三世界债务现在都应该注销了。

senses.en: ) to damage a vehicle so badly that it is not worth spending money to repair it

ex.en: That’s the third car he’s written off this year.
ex.zh: 这是他今年报废的第三辆汽车。

senses.en: to remove a character, a scene, etc. from a play, a film/movie, a regular series, etc.
senses.zh: 去掉﹙戏剧、电影、系列电视剧等中的﹚角色﹙或情节等﹚:

ex.en: He got bored and asked to be written out of the series.
ex.zh: 他厌烦了，于是要求退出这个系列剧。

ex.en: The censor demanded that the scene be written out.
ex.zh: 审查员要求把这个情节抹掉。

senses.en: to write sth on paper clearly,including all the details

ex.en: Use symbols and abbreviations instead of writing things out in full.
ex.zh: 用符号和缩写，不要都用全写。

ex.en: I wrote out the poem in my best handwriting.
ex.zh: 我尽可能把整首诗写得工工整整。

senses.en: to report sb in writing because they have done sth illegal

ex.en: He wrote me up for illegal parking.
ex.zh: 他因为我违章停车给我开了罚单。

senses.en: a review of a concert, a play, a book,etc. in a newspaper or magazine﹙
senses.zh: 报刊上对音乐会、戏剧、书等的﹚评述，评论，评介:

ex.en: The concert got a good write-up in all the papers.
ex.zh: 音乐会获得报章一致的好评。

senses.en: to pull at sth hard and quickly

ex.en: Someone yanked at my hair.
ex.zh: 有人猛拉我的头发。

senses.en: to remove sth by pulling it quickly and hard

ex.en: He yanked off his shoes.
ex.zh: 他猛地扒下鞋子。

ex.en: She yanked the lid off the tin.
ex.zh: 她猛一下拉掉了金属盒的盖子。

senses.en: to remove sb/sth from somewhere by pulling hard and quickly

ex.en: He was yanked out of the house and bundled into a car.
ex.zh: 他被人从房子里拽了出来塞进一辆汽车。

senses.en: to want sb/sth very much, especially when this is difficult to get
senses.zh: 渴望，渴求﹙尤指难以企及的人或事物﹚:

ex.en: Mira yearned for a child.
ex.zh: 米拉渴想着要个孩子。

senses.en: to suddenly shout sth in a loud voice

ex.en: She was yelling out in terror.
ex.zh: 她吓得喊叫起来。

ex.en: He yelled out the names of the winners.
ex.zh: 他高声报出优胜者的名字。

senses.en: to be replaced by sth
senses.zh: 被…替代； 为… 所取代:

ex.en: Barges yielded to road vehicles for transporting goods.
ex.zh: 在货物运输方面，驳船让位给了公路车辆。

senses.en: to allow sb else to take sth that you own and feel is very important for you
senses.zh: 交出，让出﹙自己看重的东西﹚:

ex.en: He swore he would never yield up the castle to the English.
ex.zh: 他发誓永远不会把城堡交给英国人。

senses.en: to reveal sth that has been hidden

ex.en: A thorough search of the site yielded up only a few ancient coins.
ex.zh: 彻底搜查了这个地方之后只发现了几枚古代的硬币。

senses.en: to aim weapons at sb/sth﹙

ex.en: They zeroed in on the target.
ex.zh: 他们瞄准了目标。

ex.en: () Clare zeroed in on Craig (= went to talk to him) as soon as he entered the room.
ex.zh: 克雷格一进房间，克莱尔就迳直去和他说话。

senses.en: to fix all your attention on sb/sth

ex.en: Wasting no time she zeroed in on the main topic.
ex.zh: 她一开始就直截了当地切入主题。

senses.en: to do, read, etc. sth very quickly

ex.en: Could you zip through my report and check it’s OK?
ex.zh: 你能不能快速检查一下我的报告是否可以？

senses.en: to be fastened with a zip/zipper (= a device consisting of two rows of metal or plastic teeth that you can pull together or pull apart); to fasten sth with a zip/zipper

ex.en: The skirt zips up at the side.
ex.zh: 这条裙子的拉链在侧面。

ex.en: Will you zip me up (= my dress), please ?
ex.zh: 请帮我拉上拉链好吗？

senses.en: [only before noun] fastened with a zip/zipper

ex.en: a zip-up jacket
ex.zh: 拉链夹克服

senses.en: to keep an area of land to be used for a particular purpose﹙
senses.zh: 为某目的﹚留出，划出﹙一片地﹚:

ex.en: The city centre has been zoned off for pedestrians.
ex.zh: 市中心已划为行人区。

senses.en: to stop thinking or noticing what is going on around you
senses.zh: 不再想，不再注意﹙ 周围的事﹚ ； 入静:

ex.en: Relax your muscles, take a deep breath, and zone out for a while.
ex.zh: 放松肌肉，深吸一口气，然后入静。

senses.en: a time when you stop thinking or noticing what is going on around you
unable to think or to notice what is going on around you because of the effects of drugs or alcohol﹙
senses.zh: 由于药物或酒精作用﹚精神恍惚的，神志不清的

senses.en: to fall asleep, become unconscious or unable to think, either because you are very tired or because of the effects of drugs or alcohol; to make sb do this﹙
senses.zh: 劳累或药物、酒精作用使﹚睡着，失去知觉，精神恍惚:

ex.en: He zonked out after the big exam.
ex.zh: 他大考结束之后就倒头睡了。

ex.en: I usually zonk out about 11 p.m.
ex.zh: 我通常在晚上11点左右睡觉。

senses.en: sleeping,unconscious, or unable to think, especially from the effects of drugs or alcohol﹙
senses.zh: 尤指因药物或酒精作用﹚睡着，失去知觉，精神恍惚:

ex.en: I feel totally zonked out after the day’s work.
ex.zh: 工作了一天之后我觉得头昏脑胀。

senses.en: to hurry away

ex.en: He jumped into his car and zoomed off.
ex.zh: 他跳进他的车里急匆匆地开走了。
